mus|Abdominal part of pectoralis major m.origen: Anterior layer of the rectus sheath of the rectus abdominis m.
mus|Abdominal part of pectoralis major m.insercion: Crest of the greater tubercle of the humerus (lateral lip of the intertubercular sulcus)
mus|Abdominal part of pectoralis major m.irrigacion: Thoracoacromial a. (pectoral branch) and lateral thoracic a.
mus|Abdominal part of pectoralis major m.accion: Adduction and medial rotation of the arm; depresses the shoulder; extension of the flexed arm
mus|Abdominal part of pectoralis major m.prueba: Supine, shoulder flexed ~135° and internally rotated, elbow extended. Stabilize the opposite iliac crest. Oblique adduction toward the contralateral hip. Resistance on the forearm upward and outward (grades 4–5); grade 3 is full movement without resistance.
mus|Abdominal part of pectoralis major m.biomecanica: Shoulder extension from flexion and oblique adduction (sagittal plane, frontal axis); adduction and internal rotation of the humerus; depression of the shoulder girdle.

mus|Abductor digiti minimi of foot.es: Abductor digiti minimi m. of foot
mus|Abductor digiti minimi of foot.origen: Medial and lateral processes of the calcaneal tuberosity and plantar aponeurosis
mus|Abductor digiti minimi of foot.insercion: Lateral surface of the base of the proximal phalanx of the 5th toe
mus|Abductor digiti minimi of foot.accion: Abduction and flexion of the 5th toe; supports the lateral longitudinal arch
mus|Abductor digiti minimi of foot.clinica: The branch of the lateral plantar n. that supplies it (Baxter's n.) can become entrapped and cause chronic medial heel pain.
mus|Abductor digiti minimi of foot.prueba: Supine or sitting, ankle neutral. Stabilize the calcaneus and metatarsals. Abduction of the fifth toe. Resistance on the lateral surface of the proximal phalanx of the 5th toe; many patients cannot isolate it, so it is assessed by palpation.
mus|Abductor digiti minimi of foot.biomecanica: Abduction and flexion of the metatarsophalangeal joint of the 5th toe (transverse plane of the foot, vertical axis); support of the lateral longitudinal arch.

mus|Abductor digiti minimi of hand.es: Abductor digiti minimi m. of hand
mus|Abductor digiti minimi of hand.origen: Pisiform bone and tendon of the flexor carpi ulnaris m.
mus|Abductor digiti minimi of hand.insercion: Medial surface of the base of the proximal phalanx of the 5th finger
mus|Abductor digiti minimi of hand.accion: Abduction of the 5th finger; flexion of the metacarpophalangeal joint
mus|Abductor digiti minimi of hand.clinica: Its atrophy (hypothenar eminence) suggests ulnar n. injury.
mus|Abductor digiti minimi of hand.prueba: Sitting, forearm supinated and dorsum of the hand resting. Stabilize the metacarpals. Abduction of the little finger. Resistance on the ulnar border of the proximal phalanx of the 5th finger (grades 4–5).
mus|Abductor digiti minimi of hand.biomecanica: Abduction of the 5th finger at the metacarpophalangeal joint (frontal plane, anteroposterior axis); assists MCP flexion.

mus|Abductor hallucis.origen: Medial process of the calcaneal tuberosity, flexor retinaculum and plantar aponeurosis
mus|Abductor hallucis.insercion: Medial surface of the base of the proximal phalanx of the great toe (via the medial sesamoid)
mus|Abductor hallucis.accion: Abduction and flexion of the great toe; supports the medial longitudinal arch
mus|Abductor hallucis.clinica: It can compress the tibial n. and its branches in the tarsal tunnel.
mus|Abductor hallucis.prueba: Sitting or supine, foot resting. Stabilize the first metatarsal and the calcaneus. Abduction of the great toe away from the second. Resistance on the medial surface of the proximal phalanx of the hallux; frequently assessed by palpation.
mus|Abductor hallucis.biomecanica: Abduction and flexion of the 1st metatarsophalangeal joint (transverse plane of the foot, vertical axis); support of the medial longitudinal arch.

mus|Abductor pollicis brevis.origen: Flexor retinaculum and tubercles of the scaphoid and trapezium
mus|Abductor pollicis brevis.insercion: Lateral surface of the base of the proximal phalanx of the thumb
mus|Abductor pollicis brevis.accion: Abduction of the thumb; assists opposition
mus|Abductor pollicis brevis.clinica: Its weakness and thenar atrophy are typical signs of carpal tunnel syndrome.
mus|Abductor pollicis brevis.prueba: Sitting, forearm supinated, wrist neutral. Stabilize the metacarpals and wrist. Palmar abduction of the thumb (moving it perpendicular to the palm). Resistance on the lateral surface of the proximal phalanx toward adduction (grades 4–5).
mus|Abductor pollicis brevis.biomecanica: Palmar abduction of the thumb at the trapeziometacarpal joint (sagittal plane, frontal axis); participates in opposition.

mus|Abductor pollicis longus.origen: Posterior surface of the ulna, radius and interosseous membrane
mus|Abductor pollicis longus.inervacion: Posterior interosseous n., from the radial n. (C7–C8)
mus|Abductor pollicis longus.accion: Abduction and extension of the thumb at the carpometacarpal joint; radial abduction of the wrist
mus|Abductor pollicis longus.clinica: Its tendon, together with the extensor pollicis brevis, is affected in De Quervain tenosynovitis (Finkelstein test).
mus|Abductor pollicis longus.prueba: Sitting, forearm neutral or supinated, wrist neutral. Stabilize the wrist. Radial abduction of the thumb in the plane of the palm. Resistance on the distal lateral surface of the first metacarpal toward adduction (grades 4–5).
mus|Abductor pollicis longus.biomecanica: Radial abduction and extension of the thumb at the trapeziometacarpal joint (frontal plane, anteroposterior axis); radial deviation and weak flexion of the wrist.

mus|Acromial part of deltoid muscle.irrigacion: Posterior circumflex humeral a. and deltoid branch of the thoracoacromial a.
mus|Acromial part of deltoid muscle.accion: Abduction of the arm (principal between 15° and 90°)
mus|Acromial part of deltoid muscle.clinica: Injury to the axillary n. (fracture of the surgical neck, shoulder dislocation) prevents abduction and causes anesthesia in the 'regimental badge' area.
mus|Acromial part of deltoid muscle.prueba: Sitting, arm at the side, elbow slightly flexed. Stabilize the scapula over the acromion. Shoulder abduction up to 90°. Resistance on the lateral surface of the arm, proximal to the elbow, toward adduction (grades 4–5).

mus|Adductor brevis.origen: Body and inferior ramus of the pubis
mus|Adductor brevis.insercion: Upper third of the linea aspera and pectineal line of the femur
mus|Adductor brevis.irrigacion: Obturator a. and deep femoral a.
mus|Adductor brevis.accion: Adduction of the thigh; assists hip flexion
mus|Adductor brevis.prueba: Side-lying on the side to be tested; the examiner supports the upper leg in abduction. Stabilize the pelvis. Adduction of the lower leg until it touches the upper one. Resistance on the distal medial surface of the thigh (grades 4–5); tested together with the adductor group.
mus|Adductor brevis.biomecanica: Hip adduction (frontal plane, anteroposterior axis); assists in flexion (sagittal plane, frontal axis) and external rotation.

mus|Adductor longus.origen: Body of the pubis, inferior to the pubic crest
mus|Adductor longus.insercion: Middle third of the medial lip of the linea aspera
mus|Adductor longus.irrigacion: Deep femoral a. and obturator a.
mus|Adductor longus.accion: Adduction of the thigh; assists hip flexion
mus|Adductor longus.clinica: It is the adductor most often injured in athletic groin strain; it forms the medial border of the femoral triangle.
mus|Adductor longus.prueba: Side-lying on the side to be tested; upper leg supported in abduction. Stabilize the pelvis. Adduction of the lower leg without rotation or flexion. Resistance on the distal medial surface of the thigh, over the femoral condyle (grades 4–5); adductor group test.
mus|Adductor longus.biomecanica: Hip adduction (frontal plane, anteroposterior axis); hip flexion (sagittal plane, frontal axis).

mus|Adductor magnus.origen: Inferior ramus of the pubis, ramus of the ischium and ischial tuberosity
mus|Adductor magnus.insercion: Gluteal tuberosity, linea aspera, medial supracondylar line and adductor tubercle of the femur
mus|Adductor magnus.inervacion: Adductor part: obturator n. (L2–L4); hamstring part: tibial n. of the sciatic n. (L4)
mus|Adductor magnus.irrigacion: Deep femoral a., obturator a. and femoral a.
mus|Adductor magnus.accion: Adduction of the thigh; the adductor part flexes and the hamstring part extends the hip
mus|Adductor magnus.clinica: The adductor hiatus, between its insertions, transmits the femoral vessels to the popliteal fossa.
mus|Adductor magnus.prueba: Side-lying on the side to be tested; upper leg supported in abduction. Stabilize the pelvis. Adduction of the lower leg, lifting it. Resistance on the distal medial surface of the thigh (grades 4–5); tested together with the adductor group.
mus|Adductor magnus.biomecanica: Hip adduction (frontal plane, anteroposterior axis); ischial part: hip extension (sagittal plane, frontal axis).

mus|Adductor minimus.insercion: Upper part of the linea aspera, inferior to the gluteal tuberosity
mus|Adductor minimus.irrigacion: Deep femoral a. (perforating branches) and obturator a.
mus|Adductor minimus.accion: Adduction and lateral rotation of the thigh
mus|Adductor minimus.clinica: It is the proximal part, often independent, of the adductor magnus m.
mus|Adductor minimus.prueba: Side-lying on the side to be tested; upper leg supported in abduction. Stabilize the pelvis. Adduction of the lower leg. Resistance on the distal medial surface of the thigh; cannot be isolated, tested together with the adductor group.
mus|Adductor minimus.biomecanica: Hip adduction (frontal plane, anteroposterior axis); external rotation (transverse plane, longitudinal axis).

mus|Anconeus muscle.origen: Posterior surface of the lateral epicondyle of the humerus
mus|Anconeus muscle.insercion: Lateral surface of the olecranon and upper part of the posterior surface of the ulna
mus|Anconeus muscle.irrigacion: Recurrent interosseous a. and middle collateral a.
mus|Anconeus muscle.accion: Assists the triceps in elbow extension; tenses the joint capsule; stabilizes the ulna in pronation
mus|Anconeus muscle.prueba: Cannot be isolated; tested with the triceps brachii: prone, shoulder abducted 90°, forearm hanging. Stabilize the arm. Elbow extension. Resistance on the distal forearm toward flexion (grades 4–5). Palpation lateral to the olecranon.
mus|Anconeus muscle.biomecanica: Elbow extension (sagittal plane, frontal axis); stabilization of the humeroulnar joint during pronation–supination.

mus|Anterior belly of digastric muscle.insercion: Intermediate tendon attached to the body and greater horn of the hyoid by a fibrous loop
mus|Anterior belly of digastric muscle.inervacion: Mylohyoid n., from the mandibular n. (V3)
mus|Anterior belly of digastric muscle.accion: Elevates the hyoid; depresses the mandible (mouth opening) with the hyoid fixed
mus|Anterior belly of digastric muscle.clinica: It bounds the submental and submandibular triangles of the neck.
mus|Anterior belly of digastric muscle.prueba: Clinical assessment: mouth opening against gentle resistance applied under the chin, with submandibular palpation. Tested together with the mandibular depressors.
mus|Anterior belly of digastric muscle.biomecanica: Mandibular depression / mouth opening (sagittal plane, frontal axis); hyoid elevation during swallowing.

mus|Ary-epiglottic part of oblique aryte.origen: Apex of the arytenoid cartilage (continuation of the oblique arytenoid)
mus|Ary-epiglottic part of oblique aryte.insercion: Lateral border of the epiglottis, within the aryepiglottic fold
mus|Ary-epiglottic part of oblique aryte.inervacion: Recurrent (inferior) laryngeal n., from the vagus n. (X)
mus|Ary-epiglottic part of oblique aryte.accion: Closes the laryngeal inlet by approximating the aryepiglottic folds (sphincter during swallowing)
mus|Ary-epiglottic part of oblique aryte.prueba: Cannot be assessed manually; assessment by laryngoscopy of closure of the laryngeal vestibule during swallowing.

mus|Ascending part of trapezius muscle.origen: Spinous processes of T4–T12 (approx.) and supraspinous ligaments
mus|Ascending part of trapezius muscle.insercion: Tubercle of the spine of the scapula (medial end)
mus|Ascending part of trapezius muscle.inervacion: Accessory n. (XI); proprioceptive fibers from C3–C4
mus|Ascending part of trapezius muscle.irrigacion: Dorsal branches of the posterior intercostal a.; dorsal scapular a.
mus|Ascending part of trapezius muscle.accion: Depresses the scapula; together with the descending part, rotates the scapula upward
mus|Ascending part of trapezius muscle.prueba: Prone, arm abducted ~145° (aligned with the fibers), thumb up. Stabilize the thorax. Lift the arm off the table with adduction and scapular depression. Resistance on the distal forearm toward the floor (grades 4–5); on the scapula if the shoulder is weak.
mus|Ascending part of trapezius muscle.biomecanica: Depression and adduction of the scapula (frontal plane); upward rotation of the scapula (frontal plane, anteroposterior axis).

mus|Brachialis muscle.origen: Distal half of the anterior surface of the humerus
mus|Brachialis muscle.insercion: Coronoid process and tuberosity of the ulna
mus|Brachialis muscle.inervacion: Musculocutaneous n. (C5–C6); lateral part by the radial n. (C7)
mus|Brachialis muscle.irrigacion: Brachial a. and radial recurrent a.
mus|Brachialis muscle.accion: Main elbow flexor in any position of the forearm
mus|Brachialis muscle.clinica: It is the muscle most affected by myositis ossificans after elbow fractures or dislocations.
mus|Brachialis muscle.prueba: Sitting or supine, forearm pronated. Stabilize the arm. Elbow flexion. Resistance on the distal forearm toward extension (grades 4–5); grade 3 is full flexion against gravity.
mus|Brachialis muscle.biomecanica: Elbow flexion regardless of forearm position (sagittal plane, frontal axis).

mus|Brachioradialis muscle.origen: Proximal two thirds of the lateral supracondylar ridge of the humerus
mus|Brachioradialis muscle.insercion: Lateral surface of the distal end of the radius, proximal to the styloid process
mus|Brachioradialis muscle.clinica: The brachioradialis (styloradial) reflex tests the C6 root.
mus|Brachioradialis muscle.prueba: Sitting, forearm in neutral position (thumb up). Stabilize the arm. Elbow flexion maintaining neutral position. Resistance on the radial side of the distal forearm toward extension (grades 4–5); palpate the muscle belly.
mus|Brachioradialis muscle.biomecanica: Elbow flexion (sagittal plane, frontal axis); brings the forearm to the neutral position of pronation–supination (transverse plane, longitudinal axis).

mus|Bucinator.origen: Alveolar processes of the maxilla and mandible (at molar level) and pterygomandibular raphe
mus|Bucinator.insercion: Angle of the mouth (modiolus) and orbicularis oris m.
mus|Bucinator.irrigacion: Facial a. and buccal a. (from the maxillary a.)
mus|Bucinator.accion: Compresses the cheek against the teeth; keeps the bolus in the mouth; blowing
mus|Bucinator.clinica: In facial paralysis, food accumulates in the oral vestibule. The parotid duct pierces it.
mus|Bucinator.prueba: Clinical assessment: ask the patient to puff out and compress the cheeks or to whistle; the examiner presses the cheeks or palpates with an intraoral finger.

mus|Calcaneal tendon.origen: Junction of the tendons of the gastrocnemius and soleus mm.
mus|Calcaneal tendon.insercion: Middle part of the posterior surface of the calcaneus
mus|Calcaneal tendon.irrigacion: Posterior tibial a. and fibular a. (hypovascular zone 2–6 cm from the insertion)
mus|Calcaneal tendon.accion: Transmits plantar flexion from the triceps surae to the foot
mus|Calcaneal tendon.clinica: Achilles reflex (S1); its rupture is detected with the Thompson test.
mus|Calcaneal tendon.prueba: Tendon (not muscle): Thompson test (calf squeeze in prone; absence of plantar flexion indicates rupture) and palpation of the tendon.
mus|Calcaneal tendon.biomecanica: Transmits the force of the triceps surae: ankle plantar flexion (sagittal plane, frontal axis).

mus|Clavicular head of pectoralis major.origen: Anterior surface of the medial half of the clavicle
mus|Clavicular head of pectoralis major.insercion: Crest of the greater tubercle of the humerus (lateral lip of the intertubercular sulcus)
mus|Clavicular head of pectoralis major.accion: Flexion of the arm; adduction and medial rotation
mus|Clavicular head of pectoralis major.clinica: It is assessed in isolation with forward flexion of the arm against resistance.
mus|Clavicular head of pectoralis major.prueba: Supine, shoulder abducted 90°, elbow extended. Stabilize the contralateral shoulder. Horizontal adduction upward and medially. Resistance on the distal forearm toward horizontal abduction (grades 4–5).
mus|Clavicular head of pectoralis major.biomecanica: Shoulder flexion (sagittal plane, frontal axis); horizontal adduction (transverse plane, vertical axis); internal rotation.

mus|Clavicular part of deltoid muscle.origen: Anterior border of the lateral third of the clavicle
mus|Clavicular part of deltoid muscle.irrigacion: Thoracoacromial a. (deltoid branch) and anterior circumflex humeral a.
mus|Clavicular part of deltoid muscle.accion: Flexion and medial rotation of the arm; assists abduction
mus|Clavicular part of deltoid muscle.prueba: Sitting, shoulder flexed 90° with slight abduction and external rotation, elbow flexed. Stabilize the scapula. Shoulder flexion. Resistance on the anteromedial surface of the arm, proximal to the elbow, toward extension (grades 4–5).
mus|Clavicular part of deltoid muscle.biomecanica: Shoulder flexion (sagittal plane, frontal axis); horizontal adduction and internal rotation (transverse plane, vertical/longitudinal axis).

mus|Coccygeus muscle.insercion: Lateral borders of the lower part of the sacrum and of the coccyx
mus|Coccygeus muscle.irrigacion: Inferior gluteal a. and internal pudendal a.
mus|Coccygeus muscle.accion: Supports the pelvic viscera; flexes the coccyx
mus|Coccygeus muscle.clinica: It forms the posterior part of the pelvic diaphragm, over the sacrospinous ligament.
mus|Coccygeus muscle.prueba: Cannot be assessed manually in a standard way; posterolateral intrarectal/intravaginal palpation in pelvic floor assessment.
mus|Coccygeus muscle.biomecanica: Coccygeal flexion and support of the posterior pelvic floor.

mus|Common tendinous ring.origen: Around the optic canal and middle part of the superior orbital fissure
mus|Common tendinous ring.accion: Origin of the four rectus muscles of the eye
mus|Common tendinous ring.clinica: The optic n., ophthalmic a. and the oculomotor, nasociliary and abducens nn. pass through it.

mus|Coracobrachialis muscle.origen: Apex of the coracoid process (with the short head of the biceps)
mus|Coracobrachialis muscle.insercion: Middle third of the medial surface of the humerus
mus|Coracobrachialis muscle.accion: Flexion and adduction of the arm
mus|Coracobrachialis muscle.clinica: The musculocutaneous n. pierces it and can be compressed at that level.
mus|Coracobrachialis muscle.prueba: Sitting, shoulder externally rotated, elbow fully flexed and supinated. Stabilize the scapula. Shoulder flexion. Resistance on the distal anteromedial surface of the arm toward extension and slight abduction (grades 4–5).
mus|Coracobrachialis muscle.biomecanica: Shoulder flexion and adduction (sagittal plane, frontal axis; frontal plane, anteroposterior axis).

mus|Corrugator supercilii.origen: Medial end of the superciliary arch of the frontal bone
mus|Corrugator supercilii.insercion: Skin of the medial half of the eyebrow
mus|Corrugator supercilii.accion: Draws the eyebrow downward and medially (frowning)
mus|Corrugator supercilii.clinica: Usual target of botulinum toxin for glabellar wrinkles.
mus|Corrugator supercilii.prueba: Clinical assessment: ask the patient to frown, drawing the eyebrows together; observe the vertical wrinkles between the eyebrows.

mus|Deep head of flexor pollicis brevis.es: Flexor pollicis brevis m., deep head
mus|Deep head of flexor pollicis brevis.la: Caput profundum musculi flexoris pollicis brevis
mus|Deep head of flexor pollicis brevis.insercion: Lateral surface of the base of the proximal phalanx of the thumb (lateral sesamoid)
mus|Deep head of flexor pollicis brevis.accion: Flexion of the metacarpophalangeal joint of the thumb
mus|Deep head of flexor pollicis brevis.prueba: Sitting, forearm supinated. Stabilize the first metacarpal. Flexion of the thumb MCP without flexing the IP. Resistance on the palmar surface of the proximal phalanx toward extension; cannot be isolated from the superficial head.
mus|Deep head of flexor pollicis brevis.biomecanica: Flexion of the thumb MCP (frontal plane of the hand, anteroposterior axis); assists opposition and adduction.

mus|Deep head of pronator teres.origen: Medial border of the coronoid process of the ulna
mus|Deep head of pronator teres.insercion: Middle part of the lateral surface of the radius (pronator tuberosity)
mus|Deep head of pronator teres.accion: Pronation of the forearm; assists elbow flexion
mus|Deep head of pronator teres.clinica: The median n. passes between its two heads: site of pronator syndrome.
mus|Deep head of pronator teres.prueba: Cannot be isolated; tested with the pronator teres: sitting, elbow flexed 90°, forearm supinated. Stabilize the arm. Pronation. Resistance on the distal forearm toward supination (grades 4–5).
mus|Deep head of pronator teres.biomecanica: Forearm pronation (transverse plane, longitudinal axis); weak elbow flexion.

mus|Deep part of masseter.origen: Medial surface and inferior border of the zygomatic arch (posterior two thirds)
mus|Deep part of masseter.insercion: Lateral surface of the mandibular ramus, up to the coronoid process
mus|Deep part of masseter.inervacion: Masseteric n., from the mandibular n. (V3)
mus|Deep part of masseter.irrigacion: Masseteric a. (from the maxillary a.), facial a. and transverse facial a.
mus|Deep part of masseter.accion: Elevates the mandible; retracts the mandible
mus|Deep part of masseter.prueba: Clinical assessment: ask the patient to clench the teeth and palpate the mandibular angle; gentle resistance to mouth closing.
mus|Deep part of masseter.biomecanica: Mandibular elevation / mouth closing (sagittal plane, frontal axis); mandibular retrusion.

mus|Depressor anguli oris.accion: Depresses and draws the corner of the mouth laterally
mus|Depressor anguli oris.clinica: Its paralysis due to injury of the marginal mandibular branch causes asymmetry of the smile.
mus|Depressor anguli oris.prueba: Clinical assessment: ask the patient to lower the corners of the mouth (sad expression); observe symmetry.

mus|Depressor labii inferioris.origen: Oblique line of the mandible, between the symphysis and the mental foramen
mus|Depressor labii inferioris.insercion: Skin and mucosa of the lower lip
mus|Depressor labii inferioris.irrigacion: Inferior labial a. (from the facial a.)
mus|Depressor labii inferioris.accion: Depresses and everts the lower lip
mus|Depressor labii inferioris.prueba: Clinical assessment: ask the patient to lower and evert the lower lip, showing the lower teeth; observe symmetry.

mus|Depressor septi nasi.insercion: Mobile part of the nasal septum and ala of the nose
mus|Depressor septi nasi.irrigacion: Superior labial a. (from the facial a.)
mus|Depressor septi nasi.accion: Depresses the septum and the tip of the nose; widens the nostrils
mus|Depressor septi nasi.prueba: Clinical assessment: ask the patient to lower the tip of the nose / narrow the nostrils; observe.

mus|Descending part of trapezius muscle.origen: Medial third of the superior nuchal line, external occipital protuberance and nuchal ligament
mus|Descending part of trapezius muscle.insercion: Lateral third of the posterior border of the clavicle
mus|Descending part of trapezius muscle.inervacion: Accessory n. (XI); proprioceptive fibers from C3–C4
mus|Descending part of trapezius muscle.irrigacion: Transverse cervical a. and occipital a.
mus|Descending part of trapezius muscle.accion: Elevates the scapula; rotates the scapula upward; extends and tilts the neck
mus|Descending part of trapezius muscle.clinica: Tested by asking the patient to shrug the shoulders against resistance (accessory n.).
mus|Descending part of trapezius muscle.prueba: Sitting, arms at the sides. Stabilization unnecessary. Elevation of the shoulders toward the ears (shrugging). Resistance on the shoulders downward (grades 4–5); grade 3 is full elevation without resistance.
mus|Descending part of trapezius muscle.biomecanica: Scapular elevation (frontal plane); scapular upward rotation (frontal plane, anteroposterior axis); extension and ipsilateral tilt of the neck.

mus|Diaphragm.origen: Sternal part (xiphoid process), costal part (last 6 costal cartilages) and lumbar part (crura and arcuate ligaments)
mus|Diaphragm.irrigacion: Superior and inferior phrenic aa., pericardiacophrenic a. and musculophrenic a.
mus|Diaphragm.accion: Main muscle of inspiration; increases intra-abdominal pressure
mus|Diaphragm.clinica: Diaphragmatic irritation causes pain referred to the shoulder (C4). Hiatal and congenital hernias (Bochdalek, Morgagni).
mus|Diaphragm.prueba: Clinical assessment: supine, observe and palpate abdominal and lower costal excursion during deep inspiration; spirometry (vital capacity, maximal inspiratory pressure).
mus|Diaphragm.biomecanica: Inspiration: descent of the phrenic centre and elevation of the lower ribs, increasing the vertical and transverse diameters of the thorax.

mus|Dorsal interossei muscles of foot.insercion: Bases of the proximal phalanges: 2nd toe (both sides), 3rd and 4th (lateral side) and dorsal aponeurosis
mus|Dorsal interossei muscles of foot.inervacion: Lateral plantar n. (S2–S3); the 1st and 2nd also by the deep fibular n.
mus|Dorsal interossei muscles of foot.irrigacion: Arcuate a. (dorsal metatarsal aa.) and plantar arch
mus|Dorsal interossei muscles of foot.accion: Abduction of toes 2 to 4 relative to the axis of the 2nd toe; metatarsophalangeal flexion
mus|Dorsal interossei muscles of foot.prueba: Sitting or supine. Stabilize the metatarsals. Abduction of toes 2–4 relative to the axis of the 2nd toe. Resistance is not standardized; usually assessed by observing and palpating the abduction.
mus|Dorsal interossei muscles of foot.biomecanica: Abduction of toes 2–4 (transverse plane of the foot, vertical axis); flexion of the MTP joints.

mus|Dorsal interossei muscles of hand.insercion: Bases of the proximal phalanges and dorsal aponeurosis of fingers 2 to 4
mus|Dorsal interossei muscles of hand.accion: Abduction of fingers 2 to 4 relative to the middle finger; MCP flexion and interphalangeal extension
mus|Dorsal interossei muscles of hand.clinica: Its weakness (inability to spread the fingers) indicates ulnar n. injury; visible atrophy of the 1st web space.
mus|Dorsal interossei muscles of hand.prueba: Sitting, forearm pronated, hand resting. Stabilize the metacarpals. Abduction of the fingers away from the middle finger. Resistance on the lateral side of the proximal phalanx of each finger toward adduction (grades 4–5).
mus|Dorsal interossei muscles of hand.biomecanica: Abduction of fingers 2–4 relative to the middle finger at the MCP joint (frontal plane, anteroposterior axis); MCP flexion and IP extension.

mus|Dorsal parts of lateral intertransve.es: Lateral intertransversarii lumborum mm., dorsal parts
mus|Dorsal parts of lateral intertransve.la: Partes dorsales musculorum intertransversariorum lateralium lumborum
mus|Dorsal parts of lateral intertransve.origen: Accessory process of a lumbar vertebra
mus|Dorsal parts of lateral intertransve.insercion: Costal (transverse) process of the lumbar vertebra below
mus|Dorsal parts of lateral intertransve.inervacion: Posterior rami of the lumbar spinal nerves
mus|Dorsal parts of lateral intertransve.irrigacion: Dorsal branches of the lumbar aa.
mus|Dorsal parts of lateral intertransve.accion: Lateral flexion and stabilization of the lumbar spine
mus|Dorsal parts of lateral intertransve.prueba: Cannot be tested individually; assessed with lateral flexion of the trunk.
mus|Dorsal parts of lateral intertransve.biomecanica: Lateral flexion of the lumbar spine (frontal plane, anteroposterior axis); segmental stabilization.

mus|Extensor carpi radialis brevis.origen: Lateral epicondyle of the humerus (common extensor tendon)
mus|Extensor carpi radialis brevis.accion: Extension and radial abduction of the wrist
mus|Extensor carpi radialis brevis.clinica: Its origin is the main structure involved in lateral epicondylalgia (tennis elbow); Cozen test.
mus|Extensor carpi radialis brevis.prueba: Sitting, forearm pronated on the table. Stabilize the forearm. Extension of the wrist (without deviation). Resistance on the dorsum of the 2nd–3rd metacarpal toward flexion (grades 4–5).
mus|Extensor carpi radialis brevis.biomecanica: Wrist extension (sagittal plane, frontal axis); weak radial deviation (frontal plane, anteroposterior axis).

mus|Extensor carpi radialis longus.origen: Lateral supracondylar ridge of the humerus (distal third)
mus|Extensor carpi radialis longus.accion: Extension and radial abduction of the wrist
mus|Extensor carpi radialis longus.clinica: Paralyzed in high radial n. injury, causing wrist drop.
mus|Extensor carpi radialis longus.prueba: Sitting, forearm pronated. Stabilize the forearm. Extension of the wrist with radial deviation. Resistance on the dorsum of the 2nd metacarpal toward flexion and ulnar deviation (grades 4–5).
mus|Extensor carpi radialis longus.biomecanica: Wrist extension (sagittal plane, frontal axis) and radial deviation (frontal plane, anteroposterior axis); weak elbow flexion.

mus|Extensor digiti minimi.origen: Lateral epicondyle of the humerus (common extensor tendon)
mus|Extensor digiti minimi.inervacion: Posterior interosseous n., from the radial n. (C7–C8)
mus|Extensor digiti minimi.accion: Extension of the 5th finger; assists in extending the wrist
mus|Extensor digiti minimi.prueba: Sitting, forearm pronated, wrist neutral. Stabilize the 5th metacarpal. Extension of the little finger MCP with the IP joints relaxed. Resistance on the dorsum of the proximal phalanx toward flexion (grades 4–5).
mus|Extensor digiti minimi.biomecanica: Extension of the joints of the 5th finger, especially the MCP (sagittal plane, frontal axis).

mus|Extensor digitorum.origen: Lateral epicondyle of the humerus (common extensor tendon)
mus|Extensor digitorum.insercion: Dorsal aponeurosis (extensor expansion) of fingers 2 to 5
mus|Extensor digitorum.inervacion: Posterior interosseous n., from the radial n. (C7–C8)
mus|Extensor digitorum.accion: Extension of fingers 2 to 5 (mainly MCP) and of the wrist
mus|Extensor digitorum.clinica: Avulsion of its terminal band causes mallet finger; of the central slip, boutonnière deformity.
mus|Extensor digitorum.prueba: Sitting, forearm pronated, wrist neutral. Stabilize the metacarpals. Extension of the MCP joints of fingers 2–5 with the IP joints relaxed. Resistance on the dorsum of the proximal phalanges toward flexion (grades 4–5).
mus|Extensor digitorum.biomecanica: Extension of the MCP and IP joints of fingers 2–5 and wrist extension (sagittal plane, frontal axis).

mus|Extensor digitorum brevis.origen: Superolateral surface of the calcaneus and inferior extensor retinaculum
mus|Extensor digitorum brevis.insercion: Tendons of the extensor digitorum longus to toes 2 to 4
mus|Extensor digitorum brevis.irrigacion: Lateral tarsal a. (from the dorsalis pedis a.)
mus|Extensor digitorum brevis.clinica: Useful in electromyography to assess the deep fibular n. and the L5 root.
mus|Extensor digitorum brevis.prueba: Sitting or supine, ankle neutral. Stabilize the metatarsals. Extension of the MTP joints of toes 2–4. Resistance on the dorsum of the proximal phalanges toward flexion (grades 4–5); palpate the belly on the lateral dorsum of the foot.
mus|Extensor digitorum brevis.biomecanica: Extension of toes 2–4 at the MTP joints (sagittal plane, frontal axis).

mus|Extensor digitorum longus.origen: Lateral condyle of the tibia, proximal three quarters of the medial surface of the fibula and interosseous membrane
mus|Extensor digitorum longus.insercion: Middle and distal phalanges of toes 2 to 5 (extensor expansion)
mus|Extensor digitorum longus.accion: Extension of toes 2 to 5; dorsiflexion of the ankle
mus|Extensor digitorum longus.clinica: Affected in anterior compartment syndrome of the leg.
mus|Extensor digitorum longus.prueba: Sitting or supine, ankle neutral. Stabilize the metatarsals. Extension of the MTP joints of toes 2–5. Resistance on the dorsum of the proximal phalanges toward flexion (grades 4–5).
mus|Extensor digitorum longus.biomecanica: Extension of toes 2–5 and ankle dorsiflexion (sagittal plane, frontal axis); eversion of the foot.

mus|Extensor hallucis brevis.origen: Superolateral surface of the calcaneus (medial part of the extensor digitorum brevis)
mus|Extensor hallucis brevis.insercion: Base of the proximal phalanx of the great toe (dorsum)
mus|Extensor hallucis brevis.accion: Extension of the metatarsophalangeal joint of the great toe
mus|Extensor hallucis brevis.prueba: Sitting or supine, ankle neutral. Stabilize the first metatarsal. Extension of the MTP joint of the hallux. Resistance on the dorsum of the proximal phalanx toward flexion (grades 4–5).
mus|Extensor hallucis brevis.biomecanica: Extension of the 1st metatarsophalangeal joint (sagittal plane, frontal axis).

mus|Extensor hallucis longus.origen: Middle part of the medial surface of the fibula and interosseous membrane
mus|Extensor hallucis longus.insercion: Base of the distal phalanx of the great toe (dorsum)
mus|Extensor hallucis longus.accion: Extension of the great toe; dorsiflexion of the ankle
mus|Extensor hallucis longus.clinica: Its strength is the best motor test of the L5 root.
mus|Extensor hallucis longus.prueba: Sitting or supine, ankle neutral. Stabilize the first metatarsal and the proximal phalanx. Extension of the IP (and MTP) joint of the great toe. Resistance on the dorsum of the distal phalanx toward flexion (grades 4–5).
mus|Extensor hallucis longus.biomecanica: Extension of the great toe and ankle dorsiflexion (sagittal plane, frontal axis); weak inversion.

mus|Extensor indicis.origen: Posterior surface of the distal third of the ulna and interosseous membrane
mus|Extensor indicis.insercion: Dorsal aponeurosis of the index finger
mus|Extensor indicis.inervacion: Posterior interosseous n., from the radial n. (C7–C8)
mus|Extensor indicis.accion: Independent extension of the index finger; assists in extending the wrist
mus|Extensor indicis.clinica: Its tendon is used as a graft to repair a ruptured extensor pollicis longus.
mus|Extensor indicis.prueba: Sitting, forearm pronated, wrist neutral. Stabilize the 2nd metacarpal. Extension of the index finger MCP. Resistance on the dorsum of the proximal phalanx toward flexion (grades 4–5).
mus|Extensor indicis.biomecanica: Extension of the index finger, mainly at the MCP joint (sagittal plane, frontal axis).

mus|Extensor pollicis brevis.origen: Posterior surface of the distal third of the radius and interosseous membrane
mus|Extensor pollicis brevis.insercion: Base of the proximal phalanx of the thumb (dorsum)
mus|Extensor pollicis brevis.inervacion: Posterior interosseous n., from the radial n. (C7–C8)
mus|Extensor pollicis brevis.accion: Extension of the MCP and carpometacarpal joints of the thumb
mus|Extensor pollicis brevis.clinica: Affected in De Quervain tenosynovitis (Finkelstein test); lateral boundary of the anatomical snuffbox.
mus|Extensor pollicis brevis.prueba: Sitting, forearm in neutral position, wrist neutral. Stabilize the first metacarpal. Extension of the thumb MCP with the IP relaxed. Resistance on the dorsum of the proximal phalanx toward flexion (grades 4–5).
mus|Extensor pollicis brevis.biomecanica: Extension of the thumb MCP (frontal plane of the hand, anteroposterior axis); radial abduction.

mus|Extensor pollicis longus.origen: Posterior surface of the middle third of the ulna and interosseous membrane
mus|Extensor pollicis longus.insercion: Base of the distal phalanx of the thumb (dorsum)
mus|Extensor pollicis longus.inervacion: Posterior interosseous n., from the radial n. (C7–C8)
mus|Extensor pollicis longus.accion: Extension of all the joints of the thumb; retropulsion
mus|Extensor pollicis longus.clinica: May rupture after a distal radius fracture (Colles) as it winds around the dorsal (Lister) tubercle.
mus|Extensor pollicis longus.prueba: Sitting, forearm in neutral position. Stabilize the proximal phalanx of the thumb. Extension of the thumb IP joint. Resistance on the dorsum of the distal phalanx toward flexion (grades 4–5).
mus|Extensor pollicis longus.biomecanica: Extension of the IP and MCP joints of the thumb (frontal plane of the hand, anteroposterior axis); adduction/retroposition of the thumb; wrist extension.

mus|External abdominal oblique muscle.insercion: Linea alba, pubic tubercle and anterior half of the iliac crest
mus|External abdominal oblique muscle.irrigacion: Inferior posterior intercostal aa., subcostal a. and deep circumflex iliac a.
mus|External abdominal oblique muscle.accion: Flexion and contralateral rotation of the trunk; abdominal compression
mus|External abdominal oblique muscle.clinica: Its aponeurosis forms the inguinal ligament and the superficial inguinal ring.
mus|External abdominal oblique muscle.prueba: Supine, hands behind the head. Stabilize the legs. Trunk flexion with rotation toward the opposite side (elbow toward the contralateral knee). Grade 5: scapula lifted off with hands behind the head; 4: arms crossed; 3: arms extended.
mus|External abdominal oblique muscle.biomecanica: Trunk flexion (sagittal plane, frontal axis); rotation toward the opposite side (transverse plane, longitudinal axis); ipsilateral lateral flexion; forced expiration.

mus|External anal sphincter.origen: Deep, superficial and subcutaneous parts; the superficial part from the coccyx (anococcygeal ligament)
mus|External anal sphincter.inervacion: Inferior rectal n., from the pudendal n. (S2–S4)
mus|External anal sphincter.irrigacion: Inferior rectal a. (from the internal pudendal a.)
mus|External anal sphincter.accion: Voluntary closure of the anal canal (continence)
mus|External anal sphincter.clinica: Anal reflex (S2–S4); its injury in obstetric tears causes fecal incontinence.
mus|External anal sphincter.prueba: Clinical assessment: digital rectal examination asking for voluntary contraction (modified Oxford scale); anocutaneous reflex; anorectal manometry.

mus|External intercostal muscles.origen: Inferior border of the rib above
mus|External intercostal muscles.insercion: Superior border of the rib below (fibers directed obliquely downward and forward)
mus|External intercostal muscles.accion: Elevate the ribs during inspiration; reinforce the intercostal space
mus|External intercostal muscles.clinica: Anteriorly they are replaced by the external intercostal membrane.
mus|External intercostal muscles.prueba: Cannot be tested manually; assessed by observing rib expansion, cirtometry and maximal inspiratory pressure.
mus|External intercostal muscles.biomecanica: Elevation of the ribs during inspiration, increasing the anteroposterior and transverse diameters of the thorax.

mus|External part of thyro-arytenoid mus.origen: Posterior surface of the angle of the thyroid cartilage
mus|External part of thyro-arytenoid mus.insercion: Anterolateral surface of the arytenoid cartilage
mus|External part of thyro-arytenoid mus.inervacion: Recurrent (inferior) laryngeal n., from the vagus n. (X)
mus|External part of thyro-arytenoid mus.accion: Shortens and relaxes the vocal folds; assists in closing the glottis
mus|External part of thyro-arytenoid mus.prueba: Cannot be tested manually; assessed by laryngoscopy and voice analysis.

mus|Fibularis brevis muscle.origen: Distal two thirds of the lateral surface of the fibula
mus|Fibularis brevis muscle.insercion: Tuberosity of the base of the 5th metatarsal
mus|Fibularis brevis muscle.irrigacion: Fibular a. and anterior tibial a.
mus|Fibularis brevis muscle.accion: Eversion of the foot; weak plantar flexion
mus|Fibularis brevis muscle.clinica: Its traction can produce an avulsion fracture of the base of the 5th metatarsal in ankle sprains.
mus|Fibularis brevis muscle.prueba: Side-lying on the opposite side, ankle neutral. Stabilize the leg. Eversion of the foot with plantar flexion. Resistance on the lateral border of the foot toward inversion (grades 4–5); palpate the tendon posterior to the lateral malleolus.
mus|Fibularis brevis muscle.biomecanica: Eversion of the foot (frontal plane, anteroposterior axis); plantar flexion of the ankle (sagittal plane, frontal axis).

mus|Fibularis longus muscle.origen: Head and proximal two thirds of the lateral surface of the fibula
mus|Fibularis longus muscle.insercion: Base of the 1st metatarsal and medial cuneiform (plantar surface)
mus|Fibularis longus muscle.irrigacion: Fibular a. and anterior tibial a.
mus|Fibularis longus muscle.accion: Eversion and plantar flexion of the foot; supports the plantar arches
mus|Fibularis longus muscle.clinica: Weakened in injury of the common fibular n. at the neck of the fibula.
mus|Fibularis longus muscle.prueba: Side-lying on the opposite side, ankle neutral. Stabilize the leg. Eversion of the foot with plantar flexion and depression of the head of the 1st metatarsal. Resistance on the lateral border and plantar surface of the 1st metatarsal (grades 4–5).
mus|Fibularis longus muscle.biomecanica: Eversion of the foot (frontal plane, anteroposterior axis); plantar flexion of the ankle (sagittal plane, frontal axis); support of the transverse arch.

mus|Fibularis tertius muscle.origen: Distal third of the medial surface of the fibula and interosseous membrane
mus|Fibularis tertius muscle.accion: Dorsiflexion of the ankle and eversion of the foot
mus|Fibularis tertius muscle.clinica: Absent in part of the population.
mus|Fibularis tertius muscle.prueba: Sitting or supine. Stabilize the leg. Dorsiflexion with eversion of the foot. Resistance on the lateral dorsum of the foot (5th metatarsal) toward plantar flexion and inversion (grades 4–5).
mus|Fibularis tertius muscle.biomecanica: Ankle dorsiflexion (sagittal plane, frontal axis) and eversion of the foot (frontal plane, anteroposterior axis).

mus|Flexor carpi radialis.origen: Medial epicondyle of the humerus (common flexor tendon)
mus|Flexor carpi radialis.insercion: Base of the 2nd metacarpal (and of the 3rd)
mus|Flexor carpi radialis.accion: Flexion and radial abduction of the wrist
mus|Flexor carpi radialis.clinica: Its tendon is a landmark for locating the radial pulse, which lies lateral to it.
mus|Flexor carpi radialis.prueba: Sitting, forearm supinated on the table. Stabilize the forearm. Wrist flexion with radial deviation. Resistance in the palm over the base of the 2nd metacarpal toward extension and ulnar deviation (grades 4–5).
mus|Flexor carpi radialis.biomecanica: Wrist flexion (sagittal plane, frontal axis); radial deviation (frontal plane, anteroposterior axis).

mus|Flexor digiti minimi of foot.es: Flexor digiti minimi brevis m. of foot
mus|Flexor digiti minimi of foot.la: Musculus flexor digiti minimi brevis pedis
mus|Flexor digiti minimi of foot.origen: Base of the 5th metatarsal and sheath of the fibularis longus tendon
mus|Flexor digiti minimi of foot.insercion: Base of the proximal phalanx of the 5th toe
mus|Flexor digiti minimi of foot.accion: Flexion of the metatarsophalangeal joint of the 5th toe
mus|Flexor digiti minimi of foot.prueba: Sitting or supine. Stabilize the 5th metatarsal. Flexion of the MTP joint of the 5th toe. Resistance on the plantar surface of the proximal phalanx toward extension; usually assessed with toe flexion.
mus|Flexor digiti minimi of foot.biomecanica: Flexion of the MTP joint of the 5th toe (sagittal plane, frontal axis).

mus|Flexor digiti minimi of hand.es: Flexor digiti minimi brevis m. of hand
mus|Flexor digiti minimi of hand.la: Musculus flexor digiti minimi brevis manus
mus|Flexor digiti minimi of hand.origen: Hook of the hamate and flexor retinaculum
mus|Flexor digiti minimi of hand.insercion: Medial surface of the base of the proximal phalanx of the 5th finger
mus|Flexor digiti minimi of hand.accion: Flexion of the MCP joint of the 5th finger
mus|Flexor digiti minimi of hand.prueba: Sitting, forearm supinated. Stabilize the 5th metacarpal. Flexion of the little finger MCP with the IP joints extended. Resistance on the palmar surface of the proximal phalanx toward extension (grades 4–5).
mus|Flexor digiti minimi of hand.biomecanica: Flexion of the MCP of the 5th finger (sagittal plane, frontal axis).

mus|Flexor digitorum brevis.origen: Medial process of the calcaneal tuberosity and plantar aponeurosis
mus|Flexor digitorum brevis.insercion: Both sides of the middle phalanges of toes 2 to 5
mus|Flexor digitorum brevis.accion: Flexion of the proximal interphalangeal joints of toes 2 to 5
mus|Flexor digitorum brevis.prueba: Sitting or supine, ankle neutral. Stabilize the proximal phalanges. Flexion of the proximal IP joints of toes 2–5. Resistance on the plantar surface of the middle phalanges toward extension (grades 4–5).
mus|Flexor digitorum brevis.biomecanica: Flexion of the proximal IP and MTP joints of toes 2–5 (sagittal plane, frontal axis); support of the longitudinal arch.

mus|Flexor digitorum longus.origen: Posterior surface of the tibia, distal to the soleal line
mus|Flexor digitorum longus.insercion: Bases of the distal phalanges of toes 2 to 5
mus|Flexor digitorum longus.accion: Flexion of toes 2 to 5; plantar flexion and inversion; supports the arches
mus|Flexor digitorum longus.clinica: Its tendon passes through the tarsal tunnel, behind the medial malleolus.
mus|Flexor digitorum longus.prueba: Sitting or supine, ankle neutral. Stabilize the middle phalanges. Flexion of the distal IP joints of toes 2–5. Resistance on the plantar surface of the distal phalanges toward extension (grades 4–5).
mus|Flexor digitorum longus.biomecanica: Flexion of toes 2–5 and ankle plantar flexion (sagittal plane, frontal axis); inversion of the foot.

mus|Flexor digitorum profundus.origen: Proximal three quarters of the medial and anterior surfaces of the ulna and interosseous membrane
mus|Flexor digitorum profundus.insercion: Bases of the distal phalanges of fingers 2 to 5 (palmar surface)
mus|Flexor digitorum profundus.inervacion: Lateral part: anterior interosseous n. of the median n.; medial part: ulnar n. (C8–T1)
mus|Flexor digitorum profundus.irrigacion: Anterior interosseous a. and ulnar a.
mus|Flexor digitorum profundus.accion: Flexion of the distal interphalangeal joints and the other joints of the fingers; wrist flexion
mus|Flexor digitorum profundus.clinica: Tested by flexing the DIP with the PIP blocked; its distal avulsion is 'jersey finger'.
mus|Flexor digitorum profundus.prueba: Sitting, forearm supinated, wrist neutral. Stabilize the middle phalanx of each finger. Flexion of the distal IP joint. Resistance on the palmar surface of the distal phalanx toward extension (grades 4–5).
mus|Flexor digitorum profundus.biomecanica: Flexion of the distal IP, proximal IP and MCP joints of fingers 2–5; wrist flexion (sagittal plane, frontal axis).

mus|Flexor hallucis longus.origen: Distal two thirds of the posterior surface of the fibula and interosseous membrane
mus|Flexor hallucis longus.insercion: Base of the distal phalanx of the great toe (plantar surface)
mus|Flexor hallucis longus.accion: Flexion of the great toe; weak plantar flexion; supports the medial longitudinal arch; push-off in gait
mus|Flexor hallucis longus.clinica: Its tendinopathy is common in dancers ('hallux saltans'), in the posterior groove of the talus.
mus|Flexor hallucis longus.prueba: Sitting or supine, ankle neutral. Stabilize the proximal phalanx of the hallux. Flexion of the IP joint of the great toe. Resistance on the plantar surface of the distal phalanx toward extension (grades 4–5).
mus|Flexor hallucis longus.biomecanica: Flexion of the great toe and ankle plantar flexion (sagittal plane, frontal axis); inversion; support of the medial arch.

mus|Flexor pollicis longus.origen: Anterior surface of the radius and interosseous membrane; sometimes the coronoid process of the ulna or the medial epicondyle
mus|Flexor pollicis longus.insercion: Base of the distal phalanx of the thumb (palmar surface)
mus|Flexor pollicis longus.inervacion: Anterior interosseous n., branch of the median n. (C7–C8)
mus|Flexor pollicis longus.accion: Flexion of the distal phalanx of the thumb; contributes to flexion of the metacarpophalangeal and carpometacarpal joints
mus|Flexor pollicis longus.clinica: Its weakness, together with the flexor digitorum profundus of the index finger, prevents making the 'OK' sign in anterior interosseous n. injury.
mus|Flexor pollicis longus.prueba: Sitting or supine, forearm supinated and hand resting. Stabilize the proximal phalanx of the thumb in extension. Ask for flexion of the interphalangeal joint. Grade 3: full arc; grades 4–5: resistance on the palmar surface of the distal phalanx toward extension.
mus|Flexor pollicis longus.biomecanica: Flexion of the thumb interphalangeal joint (frontal plane of the hand, anteroposterior axis); assists metacarpophalangeal and wrist flexion.

mus|Frontalis muscle.insercion: Skin and subcutaneous tissue of the eyebrows and forehead, interwoven with the orbicularis oculi and procerus
mus|Frontalis muscle.inervacion: Temporal branches of the facial n. (VII)
mus|Frontalis muscle.irrigacion: Supraorbital a., supratrochlear a. and frontal branch of the superficial temporal a.
mus|Frontalis muscle.accion: Raises the eyebrows and wrinkles the forehead transversely
mus|Frontalis muscle.clinica: It is spared in central facial palsy (bilateral innervation) and lost in peripheral palsy (Bell's palsy).
mus|Frontalis muscle.prueba: Facial assessment: ask the patient to raise the eyebrows and wrinkle the forehead; observe symmetry of the horizontal folds (House-Brackmann scale).
mus|Frontalis muscle.biomecanica: Elevation of the eyebrows and horizontal wrinkling of the forehead (movement in the sagittal plane, cranial displacement of the skin).

mus|Genioglossus muscle.origen: Superior mental spine (superior genial tubercle) of the mandible
mus|Genioglossus muscle.insercion: Dorsum of the tongue along its entire length and body of the hyoid
mus|Genioglossus muscle.irrigacion: Lingual a. (sublingual a. and deep lingual a.)
mus|Genioglossus muscle.accion: Protrusion of the tongue; depresses its central part
mus|Genioglossus muscle.clinica: In hypoglossal n. injury the protruded tongue deviates toward the injured side.
mus|Genioglossus muscle.prueba: Ask the patient to protrude the tongue in the midline; deviation toward the weak side indicates hypoglossal n. injury. Resistance with a tongue depressor.
mus|Genioglossus muscle.biomecanica: Protrusion of the tongue (sagittal plane) and depression of its central part.

mus|Geniohyoid muscle.origen: Inferior mental spine (inferior genial tubercle) of the mandible
mus|Geniohyoid muscle.insercion: Anterior surface of the body of the hyoid
mus|Geniohyoid muscle.inervacion: C1 fibers carried by the hypoglossal n.
mus|Geniohyoid muscle.irrigacion: Sublingual a. (branch of the lingual a.)
mus|Geniohyoid muscle.accion: Elevates and advances the hyoid; depresses the mandible with the hyoid fixed
mus|Geniohyoid muscle.clinica: It participates in swallowing and in patency of the upper airway.
mus|Geniohyoid muscle.prueba: Cannot be tested in isolation; assessed with mandibular depression against resistance under the chin and hyoid elevation during swallowing.
mus|Geniohyoid muscle.biomecanica: Elevation and anterior displacement of the hyoid (sagittal plane); with the hyoid fixed, mandibular depression (sagittal plane, TMJ frontal axis).

mus|Gluteus maximus muscle.origen: Ilium behind the posterior gluteal line, posterior surface of the sacrum and coccyx, sacrotuberous ligament and thoracolumbar fascia
mus|Gluteus maximus muscle.insercion: Iliotibial tract and gluteal tuberosity of the femur
mus|Gluteus maximus muscle.irrigacion: Inferior gluteal a. and superior gluteal a.
mus|Gluteus maximus muscle.accion: Extension and lateral rotation of the hip; stabilizes the knee in extension via the iliotibial tract
mus|Gluteus maximus muscle.clinica: Its paralysis produces the gluteus maximus gait (trunk thrown backward) and difficulty climbing stairs or rising from a chair.
mus|Gluteus maximus muscle.prueba: Prone with the knee flexed to 90°. Stabilize the pelvis. Ask for hip extension, lifting the thigh. Grade 3: full arc; grades 4–5: resistance on the distal posterior surface of the thigh toward flexion.
mus|Gluteus maximus muscle.biomecanica: Hip extension (sagittal plane, frontal axis); external rotation (transverse plane, longitudinal axis); upper fibers abduct (frontal plane, anteroposterior axis).

mus|Gluteus medius muscle.origen: Gluteal surface of the ilium between the anterior and posterior gluteal lines
mus|Gluteus medius muscle.insercion: Lateral surface of the greater trochanter of the femur
mus|Gluteus medius muscle.accion: Abduction and medial rotation of the hip; stabilizes the pelvis in single-leg stance
mus|Gluteus medius muscle.clinica: Its weakness gives a positive Trendelenburg sign: drop of the pelvis on the side opposite the stance leg.
mus|Gluteus medius muscle.prueba: Side-lying on the side not being tested, hip slightly extended and knee extended. Stabilize the pelvis. Ask for hip abduction. Grade 3: full arc; grades 4–5: resistance on the distal lateral surface of the thigh or ankle toward adduction.
mus|Gluteus medius muscle.biomecanica: Hip abduction (frontal plane, anteroposterior axis); anterior fibers internal rotation and posterior fibers external rotation (transverse plane, longitudinal axis); stabilizes the pelvis in single-leg stance.

mus|Gluteus minimus muscle.origen: Gluteal surface of the ilium between the anterior and inferior gluteal lines
mus|Gluteus minimus muscle.insercion: Anterior surface of the greater trochanter of the femur
mus|Gluteus minimus muscle.accion: Abduction and medial rotation of the hip; stabilizes the pelvis
mus|Gluteus minimus muscle.clinica: Together with the gluteus medius, its deficit causes Trendelenburg gait; common in gluteal tendinopathy (greater trochanteric pain syndrome).
mus|Gluteus minimus muscle.prueba: Side-lying, hip in neutral or slight flexion. Stabilize the pelvis. Ask for abduction (and internal rotation). Grade 3: full arc; grades 4–5: resistance on the distal lateral surface of the thigh. Tested together with the gluteus medius.
mus|Gluteus minimus muscle.biomecanica: Hip abduction (frontal plane, anteroposterior axis); internal rotation (transverse plane, longitudinal axis).

mus|Gracilis muscle.origen: Body and inferior ramus of the pubis
mus|Gracilis muscle.insercion: Medial surface of the tibia, below the medial condyle (pes anserinus)
mus|Gracilis muscle.irrigacion: Deep femoral a., obturator a. and medial circumflex femoral a.
mus|Gracilis muscle.accion: Hip adduction; knee flexion and medial rotation
mus|Gracilis muscle.clinica: Its tendon is used as a graft in anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction; it takes part in pes anserine bursitis.
mus|Gracilis muscle.prueba: Side-lying on the side being tested, upper leg supported in abduction. Ask for adduction of the lower hip. Grade 3: full arc; grades 4–5: resistance on the distal medial surface of the thigh toward abduction.
mus|Gracilis muscle.biomecanica: Hip adduction (frontal plane, anteroposterior axis); knee flexion (sagittal plane, frontal axis) and internal rotation of the tibia (transverse plane, longitudinal axis).

mus|Humeral head of extensor carpi ulnar.es: Extensor carpi ulnaris m., humeral head
mus|Humeral head of extensor carpi ulnar.la: Caput humerale musculi extensoris carpi ulnaris
mus|Humeral head of extensor carpi ulnar.origen: Lateral epicondyle of the humerus (common extensor tendon)
mus|Humeral head of extensor carpi ulnar.insercion: Tubercle of the base of the fifth metacarpal
mus|Humeral head of extensor carpi ulnar.inervacion: Posterior interosseous n., deep branch of the radial n. (C7–C8)
mus|Humeral head of extensor carpi ulnar.irrigacion: Posterior interosseous a. and ulnar a.
mus|Humeral head of extensor carpi ulnar.accion: Extension and adduction (ulnar deviation) of the wrist
mus|Humeral head of extensor carpi ulnar.clinica: Tendinopathy or subluxation of the tendon in its ulnar groove causes pain on the ulnar border of the wrist.
mus|Humeral head of extensor carpi ulnar.prueba: Forearm pronated and resting. Stabilize the forearm. Ask for wrist extension with ulnar deviation. Grade 3: full arc; grades 4–5: resistance on the dorsum of the 5th metacarpal toward flexion and radial deviation.
mus|Humeral head of extensor carpi ulnar.biomecanica: Wrist extension (sagittal plane, frontal axis); ulnar deviation (frontal plane, anteroposterior axis).

mus|Humeral head of flexor carpi ulnaris.es: Flexor carpi ulnaris m., humeral head
mus|Humeral head of flexor carpi ulnaris.la: Caput humerale musculi flexoris carpi ulnaris
mus|Humeral head of flexor carpi ulnaris.origen: Medial epicondyle of the humerus (common flexor tendon)
mus|Humeral head of flexor carpi ulnaris.insercion: Pisiform, hook of the hamate and base of the fifth metacarpal
mus|Humeral head of flexor carpi ulnaris.irrigacion: Ulnar a. and posterior ulnar recurrent a.
mus|Humeral head of flexor carpi ulnaris.accion: Flexion and adduction (ulnar deviation) of the wrist
mus|Humeral head of flexor carpi ulnaris.clinica: The arch between its humeral and ulnar heads (Osborne's ligament) is a site of ulnar n. compression: cubital tunnel syndrome.
mus|Humeral head of flexor carpi ulnaris.prueba: Forearm supinated and resting. Stabilize the forearm. Ask for wrist flexion with ulnar deviation. Grade 3: full arc; grades 4–5: resistance in the palm over the 5th metacarpal toward extension and radial deviation.
mus|Humeral head of flexor carpi ulnaris.biomecanica: Wrist flexion (sagittal plane, frontal axis); ulnar deviation (frontal plane, anteroposterior axis); assists elbow flexion.

mus|Humero-ulnar head of flexor digitoru.es: Flexor digitorum superficialis m., humeroulnar head
mus|Humero-ulnar head of flexor digitoru.la: Caput humeroulnare musculi flexoris digitorum superficialis
mus|Humero-ulnar head of flexor digitoru.origen: Medial epicondyle of the humerus (common flexor tendon), ulnar collateral ligament and coronoid process of the ulna
mus|Humero-ulnar head of flexor digitoru.insercion: Lateral surfaces of the middle phalanges of fingers 2 to 5
mus|Humero-ulnar head of flexor digitoru.accion: Flexion of the proximal interphalangeal and metacarpophalangeal joints of fingers 2–5; assists wrist flexion
mus|Humero-ulnar head of flexor digitoru.clinica: Tested by flexing the proximal interphalangeal joint while the other fingers are held extended.
mus|Humero-ulnar head of flexor digitoru.prueba: Forearm supinated, wrist neutral. Hold the fingers not being tested in extension (blocking the profundus). Ask for flexion of the proximal interphalangeal joint. Grade 3: full arc; grades 4–5: resistance on the palmar surface of the middle phalanx.
mus|Humero-ulnar head of flexor digitoru.biomecanica: Flexion of the proximal interphalangeal joints of fingers 2–5 (sagittal plane, frontal axis); assists metacarpophalangeal and wrist flexion.

mus|Hyoglossus muscle.origen: Body and greater horn of the hyoid
mus|Hyoglossus muscle.insercion: Lateral and inferior part of the tongue
mus|Hyoglossus muscle.clinica: Surgical landmark: the hypoglossal n. and lingual n. pass on its lateral surface and the lingual a. on its medial surface.
mus|Hyoglossus muscle.prueba: Cannot be tested in isolation; tongue motility (retraction and depression) and integrity of the hypoglossal n. are assessed.
mus|Hyoglossus muscle.biomecanica: Depression and retraction of the tongue (sagittal plane).

mus|Iliacus muscle.origen: Iliac fossa, iliac crest, ala of the sacrum and anterior sacroiliac ligaments
mus|Iliacus muscle.insercion: Lesser trochanter of the femur (with the tendon of the psoas major)
mus|Iliacus muscle.irrigacion: Iliac branch of the iliolumbar a. and deep circumflex iliac a.
mus|Iliacus muscle.accion: Hip flexion; with the psoas, flexion of the trunk on the thigh
mus|Iliacus muscle.clinica: Iliacus hematoma (e.g. in anticoagulated patients) can compress the femoral n.
mus|Iliacus muscle.prueba: Sitting at the edge of the table, holding on with the hands. Stabilize the pelvis. Ask for hip flexion, lifting the thigh. Grade 3: full arc; grades 4–5: resistance on the distal anterior surface of the thigh toward extension (with psoas).
mus|Iliacus muscle.biomecanica: Hip flexion (sagittal plane, frontal axis); with the femur fixed, anterior pelvic tilt; slight external rotation.

mus|Iliococcygeus muscle.origen: Tendinous arch of the levator ani m. and ischial spine
mus|Iliococcygeus muscle.inervacion: Nerve to levator ani (S3–S4) and pudendal n. (inferior rectal branch)
mus|Iliococcygeus muscle.irrigacion: Inferior gluteal a., internal pudendal a. and inferior vesical a.
mus|Iliococcygeus muscle.accion: Support of the pelvic viscera; elevates the pelvic floor
mus|Iliococcygeus muscle.clinica: Its injury during childbirth contributes to pelvic organ prolapse.
mus|Iliococcygeus muscle.prueba: Pelvic floor: vaginal or rectal palpation with the modified Oxford scale (0–5), assessing strength, endurance and lift.
mus|Iliococcygeus muscle.biomecanica: Elevation and support of the pelvic floor and viscera (sagittal plane); pulls the coccyx anteriorly.

mus|Iliocostalis colli muscle.insercion: Posterior tubercles of the transverse processes of C4–C6
mus|Iliocostalis colli muscle.inervacion: Posterior rami of the cervical and thoracic spinal nn.
mus|Iliocostalis colli muscle.irrigacion: Deep cervical a., vertebral a. and posterior intercostal aa.
mus|Iliocostalis colli muscle.accion: Extension and ipsilateral lateral flexion of the cervical spine
mus|Iliocostalis colli muscle.prueba: Prone with the head off the table. Stabilize the upper thoracic region. Ask for cervical extension. Grade 3: full arc; grades 4–5: resistance on the occiput. Assessed together with the cervical extensors.
mus|Iliocostalis colli muscle.biomecanica: Cervical extension (sagittal plane, frontal axis) when acting bilaterally; unilaterally, ipsilateral lateral flexion (frontal plane, anteroposterior axis).

mus|Iliocostalis lumborum muscle.origen: Iliac crest, posterior surface of the sacrum and aponeurosis of the erector spinae
mus|Iliocostalis lumborum muscle.insercion: Angles of the last 6–9 ribs and lumbar transverse processes
mus|Iliocostalis lumborum muscle.inervacion: Posterior rami of the lumbar and lower thoracic spinal nn.
mus|Iliocostalis lumborum muscle.irrigacion: Lumbar aa. and inferior posterior intercostal aa.
mus|Iliocostalis lumborum muscle.accion: Extension and ipsilateral lateral flexion of the lumbar spine; depresses the ribs
mus|Iliocostalis lumborum muscle.clinica: Frequent source of mechanical low back pain from contracture or overload.
mus|Iliocostalis lumborum muscle.prueba: Prone with hands at the sides. Stabilize the pelvis and legs. Ask for trunk extension, lifting the chest. Grade 3: lift without resistance; grades 4–5: hold against resistance on the back or with hands behind the head.
mus|Iliocostalis lumborum muscle.biomecanica: Lumbar spine extension (sagittal plane, frontal axis); unilaterally, ipsilateral lateral flexion (frontal plane, anteroposterior axis).

mus|Iliocostalis thoracis muscle.insercion: Angles of the first 6 ribs and transverse process of C7
mus|Iliocostalis thoracis muscle.inervacion: Posterior rami of the thoracic spinal nn.
mus|Iliocostalis thoracis muscle.accion: Extension and ipsilateral lateral flexion of the thoracic spine
mus|Iliocostalis thoracis muscle.prueba: Prone with hands at the sides. Stabilize the pelvis. Ask for extension of the thoracic trunk. Grade 3: lift the whole chest; grades 4–5: hold against resistance or with hands behind the head.
mus|Iliocostalis thoracis muscle.biomecanica: Thoracic spine extension (sagittal plane, frontal axis); unilaterally, ipsilateral lateral flexion (frontal plane, anteroposterior axis).

mus|Iliopectineal arch.accion: Thickening of the iliac fascia that divides the retroinguinal space into the muscular lacuna and the vascular lacuna
mus|Iliopectineal arch.clinica: Separates the compartment of the iliopsoas and femoral n. from that of the femoral vessels; relevant in femoral hernias and nerve blocks.

mus|Inferior gemellus muscle.insercion: Tendon of the obturator internus and medial surface of the greater trochanter (trochanteric fossa)
mus|Inferior gemellus muscle.irrigacion: Medial circumflex femoral a. and inferior gluteal a.
mus|Inferior gemellus muscle.accion: Lateral rotation of the extended hip; abduction of the flexed hip; stabilizes the femoral head
mus|Inferior gemellus muscle.prueba: Sitting, knees flexed at the edge of the table. Stabilize the thigh. Ask for external rotation of the hip (foot moving medially). Grade 3: full arc; grades 4–5: resistance at the medial malleolus. Tested together with the external rotators.
mus|Inferior gemellus muscle.biomecanica: External rotation of the hip (transverse plane, longitudinal axis); abduction with the hip flexed.

mus|Inferior head of lateral pterygoid m.origen: Lateral surface of the lateral plate of the pterygoid process
mus|Inferior head of lateral pterygoid m.insercion: Pterygoid fovea of the neck of the mandibular condyle
mus|Inferior head of lateral pterygoid m.inervacion: Lateral pterygoid n., branch of the mandibular n. (V3)
mus|Inferior head of lateral pterygoid m.irrigacion: Pterygoid branches of the maxillary a.
mus|Inferior head of lateral pterygoid m.accion: Protrusion and depression of the mandible (mouth opening); bilaterally protrusion, unilaterally contralateral lateral movement
mus|Inferior head of lateral pterygoid m.clinica: Involved in temporomandibular disorders; its spasm limits opening and deviates the mandible.
mus|Inferior head of lateral pterygoid m.prueba: Ask the patient to open the mouth and protrude or move the mandible sideways against manual resistance at the chin; observe deviation.
mus|Inferior head of lateral pterygoid m.biomecanica: Mandibular protrusion (sagittal plane) and lateral movement toward the opposite side (horizontal plane, vertical axis); initiates mouth opening.

mus|Inferior oblique muscle.es: Inferior oblique m. of the eye
mus|Inferior oblique muscle.origen: Floor of the orbit, lateral to the lacrimal groove (maxilla)
mus|Inferior oblique muscle.insercion: Sclera, posterolateral quadrant of the eyeball, beneath the lateral rectus
mus|Inferior oblique muscle.irrigacion: Ophthalmic a. (muscular branches) and infraorbital a.
mus|Inferior oblique muscle.accion: Extorsion, elevation and abduction of the eyeball
mus|Inferior oblique muscle.clinica: Tested by asking the patient to look upward with the eye adducted.
mus|Inferior oblique muscle.prueba: Ocular motility: with the eye adducted, ask the patient to look upward; assess diplopia and tracking in the diagnostic positions of gaze.
mus|Inferior oblique muscle.biomecanica: Extorsion (anteroposterior axis), elevation (transverse axis) and abduction of the eyeball (vertical axis).

mus|Inferior pharyngeal constrictor.origen: Oblique line of the thyroid cartilage (thyropharyngeal part) and cricoid cartilage (cricopharyngeal part)
mus|Inferior pharyngeal constrictor.insercion: Posterior pharyngeal raphe; the cricopharyngeal part forms a continuous ring
mus|Inferior pharyngeal constrictor.inervacion: Pharyngeal plexus (vagus n., X); branches of the external laryngeal n. and recurrent n.
mus|Inferior pharyngeal constrictor.irrigacion: Ascending pharyngeal a. and superior and inferior thyroid aa.
mus|Inferior pharyngeal constrictor.accion: Constriction of the pharynx during swallowing; the cricopharyngeus acts as the upper esophageal sphincter
mus|Inferior pharyngeal constrictor.clinica: Zenker's diverticulum forms in Killian's triangle, between its thyropharyngeal and cricopharyngeal parts.
mus|Inferior pharyngeal constrictor.prueba: Swallowing assessment (clinical examination, videofluoroscopy or fiberoptic endoscopy); gag reflex.
mus|Inferior pharyngeal constrictor.biomecanica: Sequential constriction of the lower pharynx to propel the bolus during swallowing.

mus|Inferior rectus muscle.es: Inferior rectus muscle of the eye
mus|Inferior rectus muscle.insercion: Sclera, inferior surface of the eyeball, behind the limbus
mus|Inferior rectus muscle.irrigacion: Ophthalmic a. (muscular branches) and infraorbital a.
mus|Inferior rectus muscle.accion: Depression, adduction and extorsion of the eyeball
mus|Inferior rectus muscle.clinica: It may become entrapped in blowout fractures of the orbital floor, limiting upward gaze.
mus|Inferior rectus muscle.prueba: Ocular motility: with the eye in abduction, ask the patient to look down; assess diplopia in the diagnostic positions of gaze.
mus|Inferior rectus muscle.biomecanica: Depression (transverse axis), adduction (vertical axis) and extorsion of the eyeball (anteroposterior axis).

mus|Inferior tarsus.accion: Dense connective tissue plate that gives rigidity to the lower eyelid; contains tarsal (Meibomian) glands
mus|Inferior tarsus.clinica: Obstruction of its tarsal glands produces a chalazion.

mus|Infraspinatus muscle.insercion: Middle facet of the greater tubercle of the humerus
mus|Infraspinatus muscle.irrigacion: Suprascapular a. and circumflex scapular a.
mus|Infraspinatus muscle.accion: Lateral rotation of the shoulder; stabilizes the humeral head (rotator cuff)
mus|Infraspinatus muscle.clinica: Isolated atrophy suggests compression of the suprascapular n. in the spinoglenoid notch.
mus|Infraspinatus muscle.prueba: Prone, shoulder abducted 90°, elbow flexed 90° with the forearm hanging. Stabilize the distal humerus. Ask for external rotation. Grade 3: full range; grades 4-5: resistance on the dorsal aspect of the distal forearm toward internal rotation.
mus|Infraspinatus muscle.biomecanica: External rotation of the shoulder (transverse plane, longitudinal axis); stabilization and depression of the humeral head.

mus|Inguinal ligament.accion: Thickened inferior border of the external oblique aponeurosis; forms the floor of the inguinal canal
mus|Inguinal ligament.clinica: Inguinal hernias emerge above, and femoral hernias below and lateral to, the pubic tubercle.

mus|Innermost intercostal muscles.origen: Inferior border of the upper rib (inner surface)
mus|Innermost intercostal muscles.insercion: Superior border of the lower rib (inner surface)
mus|Innermost intercostal muscles.accion: They probably act with the internal intercostals in forced expiration
mus|Innermost intercostal muscles.clinica: The intercostal neurovascular bundle runs between them and the internal intercostals, beneath the costal groove.
mus|Innermost intercostal muscles.prueba: Cannot be tested in isolation; respiratory function is assessed (rib expansion, spirometry).
mus|Innermost intercostal muscles.biomecanica: Rib depression in forced expiration and stiffening of the intercostal spaces.

mus|Intermediate tendon of digastric mus.es: Intermediate tendon of the digastric muscle
mus|Intermediate tendon of digastric mus.insercion: Attached to the body and greater horn of the hyoid by a fibrous loop
mus|Intermediate tendon of digastric mus.accion: Joins the anterior and posterior bellies of the digastric; pierces the stylohyoid
mus|Intermediate tendon of digastric mus.clinica: Landmark of the submandibular triangle in cervical surgery.
mus|Intermediate tendon of digastric mus.prueba: Tendon: assessed together with the digastric, by mandibular depression against resistance beneath the chin.

mus|Internal abdominal oblique muscle.origen: Thoracolumbar fascia, iliac crest (anterior 2/3) and lateral half of the inguinal ligament
mus|Internal abdominal oblique muscle.insercion: Inferior borders of ribs 10–12, linea alba and, with the transversus, pubic crest (conjoint tendon)
mus|Internal abdominal oblique muscle.inervacion: Thoracoabdominal nn. (T7–T11), subcostal n. (T12), iliohypogastric and ilioinguinal nn. (L1)
mus|Internal abdominal oblique muscle.irrigacion: Superior and inferior epigastric aa., deep circumflex iliac a. and inferior intercostal aa.
mus|Internal abdominal oblique muscle.accion: Flexion and ipsilateral rotation of the trunk; compresses the abdomen
mus|Internal abdominal oblique muscle.clinica: Its inferior fibers give rise to the cremaster muscle; its arch forms the roof of the inguinal canal.
mus|Internal abdominal oblique muscle.prueba: Supine, hands behind the head. Stabilize the legs. Ask for trunk flexion with rotation, bringing the opposite shoulder toward the ipsilateral hip. Grade 5: hands behind the head; 4: arms crossed; 3: arms extended.
mus|Internal abdominal oblique muscle.biomecanica: Trunk flexion (sagittal plane, frontal axis); ipsilateral rotation (transverse plane, longitudinal axis); lateral flexion (frontal plane, anteroposterior axis); forced expiration.

mus|Internal intercostal muscles.origen: Inferior border and costal groove of the upper rib
mus|Internal intercostal muscles.insercion: Superior border of the lower rib
mus|Internal intercostal muscles.accion: They depress the ribs in forced expiration; the intercartilaginous part elevates the ribs
mus|Internal intercostal muscles.clinica: Thoracic punctures are made along the superior border of the lower rib to avoid the neurovascular bundle.
mus|Internal intercostal muscles.prueba: Cannot be tested in isolation; forced expiration and rib mobility are assessed (spirometry, cirtometry).
mus|Internal intercostal muscles.biomecanica: Rib depression in forced expiration (sagittal/frontal plane); the intercartilaginous part assists inspiration.

mus|Interspinales colli muscles.origen: Spinous processes of the cervical vertebrae (C2–T1)
mus|Interspinales colli muscles.insercion: Spinous process of the vertebra immediately above
mus|Interspinales colli muscles.inervacion: Posterior rami of the cervical spinal nerves
mus|Interspinales colli muscles.irrigacion: Deep cervical a. and occipital a.
mus|Interspinales colli muscles.accion: Extension of the cervical spine; segmental proprioception
mus|Interspinales colli muscles.prueba: Deep spinal muscle, cannot be tested in isolation; assessed with overall cervical extension.
mus|Interspinales colli muscles.biomecanica: Segmental extension of the cervical spine (sagittal plane, frontal axis).

mus|Interspinales lumborum muscles.origen: Spinous processes of the lumbar vertebrae
mus|Interspinales lumborum muscles.insercion: Spinous process of the vertebra immediately above
mus|Interspinales lumborum muscles.inervacion: Posterior rami of the lumbar spinal nerves
mus|Interspinales lumborum muscles.accion: Extension of the lumbar spine; segmental proprioception
mus|Interspinales lumborum muscles.prueba: Deep spinal muscle, cannot be tested in isolation; assessed with overall lumbar extension.
mus|Interspinales lumborum muscles.biomecanica: Segmental extension of the lumbar spine (sagittal plane, frontal axis); intervertebral stabilization.

mus|Interspinales thoracis muscles.origen: Spinous processes of the thoracic vertebrae (inconstant, mainly at T1–T2 and T11–T12)
mus|Interspinales thoracis muscles.insercion: Spinous process of the vertebra immediately above
mus|Interspinales thoracis muscles.inervacion: Posterior rami of the thoracic spinal nerves
mus|Interspinales thoracis muscles.accion: Extension of the thoracic spine; segmental proprioception
mus|Interspinales thoracis muscles.prueba: Deep spinal muscle, cannot be tested in isolation; assessed with overall thoracic extension.
mus|Interspinales thoracis muscles.biomecanica: Segmental extension of the thoracic spine (sagittal plane, frontal axis).

mus|Lateral crico-arytenoid muscle.origen: Superior border of the arch of the cricoid cartilage
mus|Lateral crico-arytenoid muscle.insercion: Muscular process of the arytenoid cartilage
mus|Lateral crico-arytenoid muscle.irrigacion: Inferior laryngeal a. and superior laryngeal a.
mus|Lateral crico-arytenoid muscle.accion: Medial rotation of the arytenoid: adduction of the vocal folds (closure of the glottis)
mus|Lateral crico-arytenoid muscle.prueba: Laryngeal assessment: laryngoscopy observing glottic closure during phonation; voice quality and maximum phonation time.
mus|Lateral crico-arytenoid muscle.biomecanica: Adduction of the vocal cords through internal rotation of the arytenoids (closure of the glottis).

mus|Lateral head of flexor hallucis brev.es: Flexor hallucis brevis muscle, lateral head
mus|Lateral head of flexor hallucis brev.la: Caput laterale musculi flexoris hallucis brevis
mus|Lateral head of flexor hallucis brev.insercion: Lateral side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the great toe, via the lateral sesamoid
mus|Lateral head of flexor hallucis brev.irrigacion: Medial plantar a. and first plantar metatarsal a.
mus|Lateral head of flexor hallucis brev.accion: Flexion of the metatarsophalangeal joint of the great toe
mus|Lateral head of flexor hallucis brev.clinica: Contains the lateral sesamoid, which may be affected in sesamoiditis.
mus|Lateral head of flexor hallucis brev.prueba: Supine, ankle neutral. Stabilize the first metatarsal. Ask for flexion of the metatarsophalangeal joint of the hallux. Grade 3: full range; grades 4-5: resistance beneath the proximal phalanx toward extension.
mus|Lateral head of flexor hallucis brev.biomecanica: Flexion of the metatarsophalangeal joint of the hallux (sagittal plane, frontal axis); support of the medial longitudinal arch.

mus|Lateral head of gastrocnemius.origen: Lateral surface of the lateral condyle of the femur
mus|Lateral head of gastrocnemius.insercion: Tuberosity of the calcaneus via the calcaneal (Achilles) tendon
mus|Lateral head of gastrocnemius.irrigacion: Sural a. (branch of the popliteal a.)
mus|Lateral head of gastrocnemius.accion: Plantar flexion of the ankle; flexion of the knee
mus|Lateral head of gastrocnemius.clinica: Achilles reflex (S1); may contain the fabella, an inconstant sesamoid.
mus|Lateral head of gastrocnemius.prueba: Single-leg standing with the knee extended, light support. Ask the patient to rise onto the toes. Grade 5: 25 full heel raises; 4: 2-24; 3: one heel raise. Grade 2 prone with manual resistance.
mus|Lateral head of gastrocnemius.biomecanica: Plantar flexion of the ankle (sagittal plane, frontal axis); knee flexion (sagittal plane, frontal axis).

mus|Lateral head of triceps brachii.origen: Posterior surface of the humerus, above the groove for the radial n.
mus|Lateral head of triceps brachii.irrigacion: Deep brachial a. and posterior circumflex humeral a.
mus|Lateral head of triceps brachii.clinica: Triceps reflex (C7); the radial n. passes between its lateral and medial heads in the radial groove.
