mus|Lateral head of triceps brachii.prueba: Prone, shoulder abducted 90° and elbow flexed, forearm hanging. Stabilize the humerus. Ask for elbow extension. Grade 3: full range; grades 4-5: resistance on the dorsal aspect of the distal forearm toward flexion.

mus|Lateral rectus muscle.es: Lateral rectus muscle of the eye
mus|Lateral rectus muscle.insercion: Sclera, lateral surface of the eyeball
mus|Lateral rectus muscle.irrigacion: Ophthalmic a. (muscular branches) and lacrimal a.
mus|Lateral rectus muscle.clinica: Palsy of cranial nerve VI produces convergent strabismus and horizontal diplopia; common in intracranial hypertension.
mus|Lateral rectus muscle.prueba: Ocular motility: ask the patient to look laterally; assess limitation of abduction and horizontal diplopia (cranial nerve VI).
mus|Lateral rectus muscle.biomecanica: Abduction of the eyeball (horizontal plane, vertical axis).

mus|Latissimus dorsi muscle.origen: Spinous processes T7–L5, thoracolumbar fascia, iliac crest, last 3–4 ribs and sometimes the inferior angle of the scapula
mus|Latissimus dorsi muscle.insercion: Floor of the intertubercular groove of the humerus
mus|Latissimus dorsi muscle.irrigacion: Thoracodorsal a. (branch of the subscapular a.) and posterior intercostal aa.
mus|Latissimus dorsi muscle.accion: Extension, adduction and medial rotation of the shoulder; raises the trunk toward the arms (climbing)
mus|Latissimus dorsi muscle.clinica: Widely used as a pedicled myocutaneous flap in breast reconstruction.
mus|Latissimus dorsi muscle.prueba: Prone, arm beside the body in internal rotation (palm up). Stabilize the pelvis. Ask for shoulder extension and adduction. Grade 3: full range; grades 4-5: resistance on the distal forearm toward flexion and abduction.
mus|Latissimus dorsi muscle.biomecanica: Extension (sagittal plane, frontal axis), adduction (frontal plane, anteroposterior axis) and internal rotation of the shoulder (transverse plane, longitudinal axis); scapular depression.

mus|Levator anguli oris.origen: Canine fossa of the maxilla, below the infraorbital foramen
mus|Levator anguli oris.inervacion: Buccal branches of the facial n. (VII)
mus|Levator anguli oris.accion: Elevates the angle of the mouth
mus|Levator anguli oris.prueba: Facial assessment: ask the patient to raise the corners of the mouth without raising the upper lip (smile); observe symmetry.
mus|Levator anguli oris.biomecanica: Elevation of the corner of the mouth and deepening of the nasolabial fold.

mus|Levator labii superioris.origen: Infraorbital margin of the maxilla, above the infraorbital foramen
mus|Levator labii superioris.insercion: Skin and muscle of the upper lip
mus|Levator labii superioris.inervacion: Zygomatic and buccal branches of the facial n. (VII)
mus|Levator labii superioris.accion: Elevates and everts the upper lip; deepens the nasolabial fold
mus|Levator labii superioris.prueba: Facial assessment: ask the patient to raise the upper lip showing the upper teeth; observe symmetry.
mus|Levator labii superioris.biomecanica: Elevation and eversion of the upper lip.

mus|Levator nasolabialis.es: Levator labii superioris alaeque nasi muscle
mus|Levator nasolabialis.la: Musculus levator labii superioris alaeque nasi
mus|Levator nasolabialis.insercion: Greater alar cartilage, skin of the nose and upper lip
mus|Levator nasolabialis.inervacion: Zygomatic and buccal branches of the facial n. (VII)
mus|Levator nasolabialis.accion: Elevates the upper lip and dilates the nostril
mus|Levator nasolabialis.prueba: Facial assessment: ask the patient to raise the upper lip and flare the nostrils (sneer); observe symmetry.
mus|Levator nasolabialis.biomecanica: Elevation of the upper lip and dilation of the nasal ala.

mus|Levator palpebrae superioris.origen: Lesser wing of the sphenoid, above and in front of the optic canal
mus|Levator palpebrae superioris.insercion: Skin of the upper eyelid and superior tarsus (smooth portion: superior tarsal muscle)
mus|Levator palpebrae superioris.inervacion: Oculomotor n. (III), superior division; smooth portion, sympathetic fibers
mus|Levator palpebrae superioris.clinica: Complete ptosis in cranial nerve III palsy; partial ptosis in Horner syndrome (tarsal muscle).
mus|Levator palpebrae superioris.prueba: Eyelid assessment: ask the patient to open the eyes and look up; measure levator function (eyelid excursion, normal 12-17 mm) while blocking the frontalis.
mus|Levator palpebrae superioris.biomecanica: Elevation of the upper eyelid (sagittal plane).

mus|Levator scapulae.origen: Posterior tubercles of the transverse processes of C1–C4
mus|Levator scapulae.insercion: Medial border of the scapula, from the superior angle to the root of the spine
mus|Levator scapulae.inervacion: Dorsal scapular n. (C5) and branches of C3–C4
mus|Levator scapulae.irrigacion: Dorsal scapular a. and transverse cervical a.
mus|Levator scapulae.accion: Elevates the scapula and rotates the glenoid cavity downward; tilts the neck ipsilaterally
mus|Levator scapulae.clinica: Frequent contracture in neck pain with pain at the superior angle of the scapula.
mus|Levator scapulae.prueba: Sitting or prone. Stabilize the head in ipsilateral tilt. Ask for scapular elevation. Grade 3: full range; grades 4-5: resistance over the shoulder toward depression. Evaluated together with the upper trapezius.
mus|Levator scapulae.biomecanica: Scapular elevation and downward rotation (frontal plane, anteroposterior axis); ipsilateral cervical tilt.

mus|Levatores breves costarum.insercion: Rib immediately below, between the tubercle and the angle
mus|Levatores breves costarum.inervacion: Posterior rami of the spinal nerves C8–T11
mus|Levatores breves costarum.accion: They elevate the ribs; lateral flexion and slight rotation of the spine
mus|Levatores breves costarum.prueba: Cannot be tested in isolation; respiratory function and rib expansion are assessed.
mus|Levatores breves costarum.biomecanica: Rib elevation in inspiration; segmental thoracic extension, ipsilateral lateral flexion and contralateral rotation.

mus|Levatores longi costarum.origen: Transverse processes of the lower thoracic vertebrae
mus|Levatores longi costarum.insercion: Second rib below its origin, between the tubercle and the angle
mus|Levatores longi costarum.inervacion: Posterior rami of the thoracic spinal nerves
mus|Levatores longi costarum.accion: They elevate the ribs; lateral flexion and slight rotation of the spine
mus|Levatores longi costarum.prueba: Cannot be tested in isolation; respiratory function and rib expansion are assessed.
mus|Levatores longi costarum.biomecanica: Rib elevation in inspiration; segmental thoracic extension, ipsilateral lateral flexion and contralateral rotation.

mus|Linea alba.irrigacion: Poor: branches of the superior and inferior epigastric arteries (hence its use for midline laparotomies with little bleeding)
mus|Linea alba.accion: Fibrous midline raphe formed by the interlacing aponeuroses of the external oblique, internal oblique and transversus abdominis. It separates the two rectus muscles, is 1–2 cm wide above the umbilicus and narrows below it; the umbilical ring opens in its middle. It transmits the tension of the flat muscles across the abdominal wall.
mus|Linea alba.clinica: Its widening and thinning with separation of the recti is diastasis recti (pregnancy, obesity): the inter-rectus distance is measured (more than 2 cm is usually considered abnormal). Epigastric and umbilical hernias arise through its defects. It is the access route for midline laparotomy.

mus|Long head of biceps brachii.origen: Supraglenoid tubercle of the scapula and glenoid labrum
mus|Long head of biceps brachii.insercion: Radial tuberosity and, via the bicipital aponeurosis, forearm fascia
mus|Long head of biceps brachii.irrigacion: Muscular branches of the brachial a.
mus|Long head of biceps brachii.accion: Supination of the forearm and flexion of the elbow; helps flex the shoulder and stabilizes the humeral head
mus|Long head of biceps brachii.clinica: Its rupture produces the 'Popeye' sign; SLAP lesion at its origin; Speed and Yergason tests.
mus|Long head of biceps brachii.prueba: Sitting, forearm supinated. Stabilize the humerus. Ask for elbow flexion. Grade 3: full range; grades 4-5: resistance on the anterior aspect of the distal forearm toward extension.
mus|Long head of biceps brachii.biomecanica: Elbow flexion (sagittal plane, frontal axis); supination (transverse plane, longitudinal axis); assists shoulder flexion and abduction.

mus|Long head of biceps femoris.origen: Ischial tuberosity (common tendon with the semitendinosus)
mus|Long head of biceps femoris.inervacion: Tibial n., part of the sciatic n. (L5–S2)
mus|Long head of biceps femoris.irrigacion: Perforating aa. of the deep femoral a. and inferior gluteal a.
mus|Long head of biceps femoris.accion: Hip extension; knee flexion and lateral rotation
mus|Long head of biceps femoris.clinica: It is the hamstring most frequently injured in athletic sprinting.
mus|Long head of biceps femoris.prueba: Prone, knee flexed 50-70° with external rotation of the leg. Stabilize the thigh. Ask for knee flexion. Grade 3: full range; grades 4-5: resistance on the posterior aspect of the ankle toward extension.
mus|Long head of biceps femoris.biomecanica: Knee flexion (sagittal plane, frontal axis); hip extension (sagittal plane, frontal axis); external rotation of the tibia (transverse plane, longitudinal axis).

mus|Long head of triceps brachii.irrigacion: Deep brachial a. and posterior circumflex humeral a.
mus|Long head of triceps brachii.accion: Elbow extension; shoulder extension and adduction
mus|Long head of triceps brachii.clinica: Bounds the quadrangular space (axillary n.) and the triangular space; triceps reflex (C7).
mus|Long head of triceps brachii.prueba: Prone, shoulder abducted 90° and elbow flexed, forearm hanging. Stabilize the humerus. Ask for elbow extension. Grade 3: full range; grades 4-5: resistance on the dorsal aspect of the distal forearm toward flexion.
mus|Long head of triceps brachii.biomecanica: Elbow extension (sagittal plane, frontal axis); shoulder extension and adduction.

mus|Longissimus capitis muscle.origen: Transverse processes of T1–T5 and articular processes of C4–C7
mus|Longissimus capitis muscle.insercion: Posterior border of the mastoid process
mus|Longissimus capitis muscle.inervacion: Posterior rami of the cervical spinal nerves
mus|Longissimus capitis muscle.irrigacion: Occipital a., deep cervical a. and vertebral a.
mus|Longissimus capitis muscle.accion: Extension of the head; ipsilateral tilt and rotation
mus|Longissimus capitis muscle.prueba: Prone with the head off the table. Stabilize the upper thoracic region. Ask for head and neck extension. Grade 3: full range; grades 4-5: resistance on the occiput. Evaluated together with the cervical extensors.
mus|Longissimus capitis muscle.biomecanica: Extension of the head (sagittal plane, frontal axis); unilaterally, ipsilateral tilt and rotation.

mus|Longissimus colli muscle.insercion: Posterior tubercles of the transverse processes of C2–C6
mus|Longissimus colli muscle.inervacion: Posterior rami of the cervical and thoracic spinal nerves
mus|Longissimus colli muscle.irrigacion: Deep cervical a., vertebral a. and posterior intercostal aa.
mus|Longissimus colli muscle.accion: Extension and ipsilateral flexion of the cervical spine
mus|Longissimus colli muscle.prueba: Prone with the head off the table. Stabilize the thoracic region. Ask for cervical extension. Grade 3: full range; grades 4-5: resistance on the occiput. Evaluated together with the cervical extensors.
mus|Longissimus colli muscle.biomecanica: Cervical extension (sagittal plane, frontal axis); unilaterally, ipsilateral tilt (frontal plane, anteroposterior axis).

mus|Longissimus thoracis muscle.origen: Aponeurosis of the erector spinae, lumbar transverse processes and thoracolumbar fascia
mus|Longissimus thoracis muscle.insercion: Thoracic transverse processes and ribs 2–12 between the tubercle and the angle
mus|Longissimus thoracis muscle.inervacion: Posterior rami of the thoracic and lumbar spinal nerves
mus|Longissimus thoracis muscle.irrigacion: Posterior intercostal aa. and lumbar aa.
mus|Longissimus thoracis muscle.accion: Extension and ipsilateral flexion of the thoracic and lumbar spine
mus|Longissimus thoracis muscle.clinica: Contributes to mechanical low back pain through paravertebral spasm.
mus|Longissimus thoracis muscle.prueba: Prone with hands at the sides. Stabilize the pelvis. Ask for trunk extension. Grade 3: lift the whole thorax; grades 4-5: hold against resistance or with hands behind the head.
mus|Longissimus thoracis muscle.biomecanica: Extension of the thoracolumbar spine (sagittal plane, frontal axis); unilaterally, ipsilateral lateral flexion (frontal plane, anteroposterior axis).

mus|Longus capitis muscle.origen: Anterior tubercles of the transverse processes of C3–C6
mus|Longus capitis muscle.insercion: Basilar part of the occipital bone
mus|Longus capitis muscle.irrigacion: Ascending pharyngeal a., ascending cervical a. and vertebral a.
mus|Longus capitis muscle.accion: Flexion of the head and neck
mus|Longus capitis muscle.clinica: May be affected in retropharyngeal calcific tendinitis of the longus colli/capitis.
mus|Longus capitis muscle.prueba: Supine. Stabilize the thorax. Ask for craniocervical flexion (nodding with the chin) without lifting the head; craniocervical flexion test with pressure biofeedback.
mus|Longus capitis muscle.biomecanica: Flexion of the head on the upper cervical spine (sagittal plane, frontal axis).

mus|Longus colli muscle.origen: Vertebral bodies C5–T3 and transverse processes of C3–C5
mus|Longus colli muscle.insercion: Anterior tubercle of the atlas, bodies of C2–C4 and transverse processes of C5–C6
mus|Longus colli muscle.irrigacion: Vertebral a., inferior thyroid a. and ascending cervical a.
mus|Longus colli muscle.accion: Flexion of the neck; slight rotation and lateral flexion
mus|Longus colli muscle.clinica: Its weakness (deep flexors) is associated with neck pain and whiplash injury; craniocervical flexion test.
mus|Longus colli muscle.prueba: Supine. Stabilize the thorax. Ask for cervical flexion with the chin tucked. Grade 3: full range; grades 4-5: resistance on the forehead. Craniocervical flexion test with biofeedback.
mus|Longus colli muscle.biomecanica: Cervical flexion (sagittal plane, frontal axis); stabilization of the cervical lordosis.

mus|Lumbrical muscles of foot.origen: Tendons of the flexor digitorum longus
mus|Lumbrical muscles of foot.insercion: Dorsal extensor expansion of toes 2–5 (medial side)
mus|Lumbrical muscles of foot.inervacion: 1st: medial plantar n.; 2nd–4th: lateral plantar n. (S2–S3)
mus|Lumbrical muscles of foot.irrigacion: Plantar arch and plantar metatarsal aa.
mus|Lumbrical muscles of foot.accion: Flexion of the metatarsophalangeal joints and extension of the interphalangeal joints of toes 2–5
mus|Lumbrical muscles of foot.clinica: Their weakness contributes to claw toes.
mus|Lumbrical muscles of foot.prueba: Supine or sitting. Stabilize the metatarsus. Ask for flexion of the metatarsophalangeal joints while keeping the interphalangeal joints extended. Grade 3: full range; grades 4-5: resistance beneath the proximal phalanges.
mus|Lumbrical muscles of foot.biomecanica: Flexion of the metatarsophalangeal joints (sagittal plane, frontal axis) and extension of the interphalangeal joints of toes 2–5.

mus|Lumbrical muscles of hand.origen: Tendons of the flexor digitorum profundus
mus|Lumbrical muscles of hand.insercion: Radial side of the dorsal extensor expansion of fingers 2–5
mus|Lumbrical muscles of hand.inervacion: 1st and 2nd: median n. (C8–T1); 3rd and 4th: ulnar n. (C8–T1)
mus|Lumbrical muscles of hand.accion: Flexion of the metacarpophalangeal joints and extension of the interphalangeal joints
mus|Lumbrical muscles of hand.clinica: In ulnar nerve injury, paralysis of the 3rd and 4th lumbricals produces the ulnar claw hand.
mus|Lumbrical muscles of hand.prueba: Forearm supinated, wrist neutral. Stabilize the metacarpals. Ask for metacarpophalangeal flexion with the interphalangeal joints extended. Grade 3: full range; grades 4-5: resistance on the palmar aspect of the proximal phalanges.
mus|Lumbrical muscles of hand.biomecanica: Flexion of the metacarpophalangeal joints (sagittal plane, frontal axis) and extension of the interphalangeal joints of fingers 2–5.

mus|Medial head of flexor hallucis brevi.es: Flexor hallucis brevis muscle, medial head
mus|Medial head of flexor hallucis brevi.la: Caput mediale musculi flexoris hallucis brevis
mus|Medial head of flexor hallucis brevi.origen: Cuboid, lateral cuneiform and tendon of the tibialis posterior
mus|Medial head of flexor hallucis brevi.insercion: Medial side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the great toe, via the medial sesamoid (with the abductor hallucis)
mus|Medial head of flexor hallucis brevi.irrigacion: Medial plantar a. and first plantar metatarsal a.
mus|Medial head of flexor hallucis brevi.accion: Flexion of the metatarsophalangeal joint of the great toe
mus|Medial head of flexor hallucis brevi.clinica: Contains the medial sesamoid, the one most often affected in stress fractures and sesamoiditis.
mus|Medial head of flexor hallucis brevi.prueba: Supine, ankle neutral. Stabilize the first metatarsal. Ask for flexion of the metatarsophalangeal joint of the hallux. Grade 3: full range; grades 4-5: resistance beneath the proximal phalanx toward extension.
mus|Medial head of flexor hallucis brevi.biomecanica: Flexion of the metatarsophalangeal joint of the hallux (sagittal plane, frontal axis); support of the medial longitudinal arch.

mus|Medial head of gastrocnemius.origen: Popliteal surface of the femur, above the medial condyle
mus|Medial head of gastrocnemius.insercion: Tuberosity of the calcaneus via the calcaneal (Achilles) tendon
mus|Medial head of gastrocnemius.irrigacion: Sural a. (branch of the popliteal a.)
mus|Medial head of gastrocnemius.accion: Plantar flexion of the ankle; flexion of the knee
mus|Medial head of gastrocnemius.clinica: Its tear at the musculotendinous junction is 'tennis leg'; Baker's cyst lies between it and the semimembranosus.
mus|Medial head of gastrocnemius.prueba: Single-leg standing with the knee extended, light support. Ask the patient to rise onto the toes. Grade 5: 25 full heel raises; 4: 2-24; 3: one heel raise. Grade 2 prone with manual resistance.
mus|Medial head of gastrocnemius.biomecanica: Plantar flexion of the ankle (sagittal plane, frontal axis); knee flexion (sagittal plane, frontal axis).

mus|Medial head of triceps brachii.origen: Posterior surface of the humerus, below the groove for the radial n., and intermuscular septa
mus|Medial head of triceps brachii.irrigacion: Deep brachial a. and ulnar collateral aa.
mus|Medial head of triceps brachii.accion: Elbow extension; it is the main head in light extension
mus|Medial head of triceps brachii.clinica: Triceps reflex (C7); in humeral shaft fractures the radial n. is injured in the radial groove.
mus|Medial head of triceps brachii.prueba: Prone, shoulder abducted 90° and elbow flexed, forearm hanging. Stabilize the humerus. Ask for elbow extension. Grade 3: full range; grades 4-5: resistance on the dorsal aspect of the distal forearm toward flexion.
mus|Medial head of triceps brachii.biomecanica: Elbow extension (sagittal plane, frontal axis); tenses the joint capsule.

mus|Medial pterygoid muscle.origen: Medial surface of the lateral plate of the pterygoid process, pterygoid fossa, pyramidal process of the palatine bone and maxillary tuberosity
mus|Medial pterygoid muscle.insercion: Medial surface of the angle and ramus of the mandible
mus|Medial pterygoid muscle.inervacion: Medial pterygoid n., branch of the mandibular n. (V3)
mus|Medial pterygoid muscle.irrigacion: Pterygoid branches of the maxillary a.
mus|Medial pterygoid muscle.accion: Elevates the mandible (closure); protrusion and contralateral lateral excursion
mus|Medial pterygoid muscle.clinica: Its irritation (e.g. after inferior alveolar nerve block) produces trismus.
mus|Medial pterygoid muscle.prueba: Ask the patient to close the mouth and move the mandible laterally against manual resistance at the chin; intraoral palpation.
mus|Medial pterygoid muscle.biomecanica: Mandibular elevation (sagittal plane, frontal axis of the TMJ); protrusion and contralateral lateral excursion (horizontal plane, vertical axis).

mus|Medial rectus muscle.insercion: Sclera, medial surface of the eyeball, in front of the equator
mus|Medial rectus muscle.clinica: Its palsy (CN III lesion) produces exotropia; affected in internuclear ophthalmoplegia (failure of adduction).
mus|Medial rectus muscle.prueba: Cannot be tested manually; assess ocular motility by following an object medially (adduction) and convergence; examine diplopia (cranial nerve III).
mus|Medial rectus muscle.biomecanica: Adduction of the eyeball (transverse plane, vertical axis).

mus|Mentalis muscle.inervacion: Facial n. (CN VII), marginal mandibular branch
mus|Mentalis muscle.irrigacion: Inferior labial a. and mental a.
mus|Mentalis muscle.accion: Elevates and wrinkles the skin of the chin; protrudes and everts the lower lip
mus|Mentalis muscle.clinica: Its hyperactivity produces an 'orange peel' chin; treated with botulinum toxin.
mus|Mentalis muscle.prueba: Facial assessment: ask the patient to raise and protrude the lower lip, wrinkling the chin skin (pouting); grade by symmetry and amplitude.
mus|Mentalis muscle.biomecanica: Elevation and protrusion of the lower lip; wrinkles the chin skin.

mus|Middle pharyngeal constrictor.origen: Stylohyoid ligament and greater and lesser horns of the hyoid bone
mus|Middle pharyngeal constrictor.inervacion: Vagus n. (CN X) via the pharyngeal plexus
mus|Middle pharyngeal constrictor.irrigacion: Ascending pharyngeal a. and ascending palatine a.; branches of the superior thyroid a.
mus|Middle pharyngeal constrictor.clinica: Its vagal injury contributes to oropharyngeal dysphagia.
mus|Middle pharyngeal constrictor.prueba: Cannot be tested manually; assess swallowing, gag reflex and elevation of the soft palate/pharyngeal wall (cranial nerves IX-X); videofluoroscopy if needed.
mus|Middle pharyngeal constrictor.biomecanica: Constriction of the pharynx during the pharyngeal phase of swallowing.

mus|Multifidus colli muscle.insercion: Spinous processes of vertebrae 2–4 levels above (up to C2)
mus|Multifidus colli muscle.inervacion: Posterior rami of the cervical spinal nerves
mus|Multifidus colli muscle.irrigacion: Vertebral a., deep cervical a. and occipital a.
mus|Multifidus colli muscle.accion: Stabilizes the cervical segments; extension, ipsilateral flexion and contralateral rotation
mus|Multifidus colli muscle.clinica: Its dysfunction is associated with chronic neck pain; target of deep stabilization exercises.
mus|Multifidus colli muscle.prueba: Cannot be tested in isolation; assessed with prone cervical extension (resistance on the occiput) and paravertebral palpation.
mus|Multifidus colli muscle.biomecanica: Cervical extension (sagittal plane, frontal axis); contralateral rotation (transverse plane, longitudinal axis); segmental stabilization.

mus|Multifidus lumborum muscle.origen: Posterior surface of the sacrum, posterior superior iliac spine, erector spinae aponeurosis and lumbar mammillary processes
mus|Multifidus lumborum muscle.insercion: Spinous processes of vertebrae 2–4 levels above
mus|Multifidus lumborum muscle.inervacion: Posterior rami of the lumbar and sacral spinal nerves
mus|Multifidus lumborum muscle.irrigacion: Lumbar aa. and lateral sacral a.
mus|Multifidus lumborum muscle.accion: Stabilizes the lumbar spine; extension, ipsilateral flexion and contralateral rotation
mus|Multifidus lumborum muscle.clinica: It atrophies in chronic low back pain; key in lumbar stabilization (core) programs.
mus|Multifidus lumborum muscle.prueba: Cannot be tested in isolation; assess with prone lumbar extension and palpation of paravertebral thickening (contraction with contralateral leg/arm lift); ultrasound.
mus|Multifidus lumborum muscle.biomecanica: Lumbar extension (sagittal plane, frontal axis); contralateral rotation (transverse plane, longitudinal axis); segmental stabilization.

mus|Multifidus thoracis muscle.origen: Transverse processes of the thoracic vertebrae
mus|Multifidus thoracis muscle.insercion: Spinous processes of vertebrae 2–4 levels above
mus|Multifidus thoracis muscle.inervacion: Posterior rami of the thoracic spinal nerves
mus|Multifidus thoracis muscle.accion: Stabilizes the thoracic segments; extension and contralateral rotation
mus|Multifidus thoracis muscle.prueba: Cannot be tested in isolation; assessed with prone trunk extension (stabilize the pelvis, lift the trunk) and paravertebral palpation.
mus|Multifidus thoracis muscle.biomecanica: Thoracic extension (sagittal plane, frontal axis); contralateral rotation (transverse plane, longitudinal axis); segmental stabilization.

mus|Muscular system.accion: Set of skeletal muscles that produce movement, maintain posture and generate heat

mus|Mylohyoid muscle.insercion: Mylohyoid raphe and body of the hyoid bone
mus|Mylohyoid muscle.inervacion: Mylohyoid n., branch of the inferior alveolar n. (CN V3)
mus|Mylohyoid muscle.irrigacion: Mylohyoid a. (inferior alveolar a.) and submental a.
mus|Mylohyoid muscle.accion: Elevates the hyoid and the floor of the mouth; helps depress the mandible
mus|Mylohyoid muscle.clinica: Forms the oral diaphragm; determines the sublingual or submandibular spread of dental infections (Ludwig angina).
mus|Mylohyoid muscle.prueba: Cannot be tested with standard grades; palpate beneath the chin while the patient swallows or presses the tongue against the palate; resist mouth opening.
mus|Mylohyoid muscle.biomecanica: Elevates the floor of the mouth and the hyoid in swallowing; mandibular depression with the hyoid fixed (sagittal plane, frontal axis).

mus|Nasalis muscle.origen: Maxilla, above the incisors and canine
mus|Nasalis muscle.insercion: Aponeurosis of the nasal dorsum (transverse part) and alar cartilage (alar part)
mus|Nasalis muscle.accion: Compresses (transverse part) and dilates (alar part) the nostrils
mus|Nasalis muscle.clinica: Nasal flaring from its alar part is a sign of respiratory distress.
mus|Nasalis muscle.prueba: Facial assessment: ask the patient to flare and compress the nasal alae; observe symmetry and amplitude.
mus|Nasalis muscle.biomecanica: The transverse part compresses the nostril; the alar part dilates the nostril.

mus|Oblique head of adductor hallucis.origen: Bases of metatarsals II–IV and sheath of the fibularis longus tendon
mus|Oblique head of adductor hallucis.insercion: Lateral sesamoid and lateral surface of the base of the proximal phalanx of the great toe
mus|Oblique head of adductor hallucis.accion: Adducts the great toe; supports the transverse arch
mus|Oblique head of adductor hallucis.clinica: Its traction contributes to hallux valgus.
mus|Oblique head of adductor hallucis.prueba: Patient supine, stabilize the metatarsals; ask the patient to adduct the great toe toward the second toe; resistance on the medial aspect of the proximal phalanx. Difficult to isolate.
mus|Oblique head of adductor hallucis.biomecanica: Adduction of the hallux (transverse plane of the foot, vertical axis); MTP flexion; support of the transverse arch.

mus|Oblique head of adductor pollicis.origen: Bases of metacarpals II–III, capitate and trapezoid
mus|Oblique head of adductor pollicis.insercion: Medial sesamoid and ulnar side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the thumb
mus|Oblique head of adductor pollicis.accion: Adducts the thumb; contributes strength to pinch
mus|Oblique head of adductor pollicis.clinica: Froment sign: in ulnar nerve injury the IP joint of the thumb flexes to compensate for its weakness.
mus|Oblique head of adductor pollicis.prueba: Sitting, forearm pronated, stabilize the metacarpals; ask the patient to adduct the thumb toward the palm; resistance on the medial aspect of the proximal phalanx (Froment sign).
mus|Oblique head of adductor pollicis.biomecanica: Adduction of the thumb at the trapeziometacarpal joint (sagittal plane of the hand, anteroposterior axis); MCP flexion.

mus|Oblique part of cricothyroid muscle.origen: Anterolateral surface of the arch of the cricoid cartilage
mus|Oblique part of cricothyroid muscle.insercion: Inferior horn of the thyroid cartilage
mus|Oblique part of cricothyroid muscle.inervacion: Superior laryngeal n., external branch (vagus n.)
mus|Oblique part of cricothyroid muscle.accion: Tilts the thyroid over the cricoid; tenses and lengthens the vocal folds
mus|Oblique part of cricothyroid muscle.clinica: Injury of the external branch during thyroidectomy causes a monotone voice and inability to produce high pitches.
mus|Oblique part of cricothyroid muscle.prueba: Cannot be tested manually; assess high-pitched voice (glissando) and laryngoscopy; laryngeal EMG (superior laryngeal nerve).
mus|Oblique part of cricothyroid muscle.biomecanica: Slides the thyroid forward over the cricoid, tensing and lengthening the vocal cords.

mus|Obliquus inferior capitis muscle.accion: Ipsilateral rotation of the head (atlantoaxial joint)
mus|Obliquus inferior capitis muscle.clinica: Inferolateral boundary of the suboccipital triangle, through which the vertebral a. runs.
mus|Obliquus inferior capitis muscle.prueba: Cannot be tested in isolation; assessed with resisted upper cervical rotation (C1-C2) in sitting and suboccipital palpation.
mus|Obliquus inferior capitis muscle.biomecanica: Ipsilateral rotation of the atlas on the axis (transverse plane, longitudinal axis).

mus|Obliquus superior capitis muscle.insercion: Occipital bone, between the superior and inferior nuchal lines
mus|Obliquus superior capitis muscle.accion: Extension and ipsilateral flexion of the head
mus|Obliquus superior capitis muscle.clinica: Superolateral boundary of the suboccipital triangle; implicated in cervicogenic headache.
mus|Obliquus superior capitis muscle.prueba: Cannot be tested in isolation; assessed with resisted craniocervical extension at the occiput and suboccipital palpation.
mus|Obliquus superior capitis muscle.biomecanica: Extension of the head (sagittal plane, frontal axis); ipsilateral tilt (frontal plane, anteroposterior axis).

mus|Obturator externus.origen: External surface of the obturator membrane and bony margins of the obturator foramen
mus|Obturator externus.irrigacion: Obturator a. and medial circumflex femoral a.
mus|Obturator externus.accion: Lateral rotation of the thigh; stabilizes the femoral head
mus|Obturator externus.prueba: Assessed with the external rotators: sitting, knee at 90°; stabilize the thigh; ask the patient to move the foot medially; resistance at the medial malleolus and lateral aspect of the knee.
mus|Obturator externus.biomecanica: External rotation of the hip (transverse plane, longitudinal axis); assists adduction (frontal plane, anteroposterior axis).

mus|Obturator internus.origen: Internal surface of the obturator membrane and bony margins of the obturator foramen
mus|Obturator internus.insercion: Medial surface of the greater trochanter, above the trochanteric fossa
mus|Obturator internus.irrigacion: Internal pudendal a. and obturator a.
mus|Obturator internus.accion: Lateral rotation of the extended thigh; abduction of the flexed thigh
mus|Obturator internus.clinica: Its fascia forms the pudendal (Alcock) canal, a site of pudendal n. entrapment.
mus|Obturator internus.prueba: Assessed with the external rotators: sitting, knee at 90°; stabilize the thigh; ask the patient to move the foot medially; resistance at the medial malleolus and lateral aspect of the knee.
mus|Obturator internus.biomecanica: External rotation of the hip (transverse plane, longitudinal axis); abduction with the hip flexed (transverse plane).

mus|Occipitalis muscle.origen: Lateral two thirds of the superior nuchal line and mastoid process
mus|Occipitalis muscle.inervacion: Facial n. (CN VII), posterior auricular branch
mus|Occipitalis muscle.irrigacion: Occipital a. and posterior auricular a.
mus|Occipitalis muscle.prueba: Facial assessment: ask the patient to raise the eyebrows and retract the scalp backward; palpate over the occipital bone.
mus|Occipitalis muscle.biomecanica: Posterior retraction of the scalp; fixes the epicranial aponeurosis for the frontalis.

mus|Omohyoid muscle.origen: Inferior belly: superior border of the scapula next to the scapular notch
mus|Omohyoid muscle.insercion: Superior belly: inferior border of the body of the hyoid (both joined by an intermediate tendon)
mus|Omohyoid muscle.irrigacion: Superior thyroid a. and transverse cervical a.
mus|Omohyoid muscle.clinica: Surgical landmark: divides the posterior cervical triangle into occipital and omoclavicular triangles; crosses the carotid sheath.
mus|Omohyoid muscle.prueba: Cannot be tested with standard grades; palpate in the posterior triangle during swallowing or deep inspiration.
mus|Omohyoid muscle.biomecanica: Depression and fixation of the hyoid after swallowing; tenses the cervical fascia.

mus|Opponens digiti minimi muscle of foo.es: Opponens digiti minimi muscle of the foot
mus|Opponens digiti minimi muscle of foo.origen: Long plantar ligament and sheath of the fibularis longus tendon
mus|Opponens digiti minimi muscle of foo.insercion: Lateral border of the fifth metatarsal
mus|Opponens digiti minimi muscle of foo.accion: Slightly displaces the fifth metatarsal plantarward and medially
mus|Opponens digiti minimi muscle of foo.clinica: Inconstant; often considered part of the flexor digiti minimi brevis.
mus|Opponens digiti minimi muscle of foo.biomecanica: Flexion and slight adduction of the fifth metatarsal (sagittal plane, frontal axis); support of the lateral arch.

mus|Opponens digiti minimi muscle of han.es: Opponens digiti minimi muscle of the hand
mus|Opponens digiti minimi muscle of han.origen: Hook of the hamate and flexor retinaculum
mus|Opponens digiti minimi muscle of han.insercion: Medial border of the fifth metacarpal
mus|Opponens digiti minimi muscle of han.accion: Brings the fifth metacarpal forward and rotates it to oppose the thumb
mus|Opponens digiti minimi muscle of han.clinica: Hypothenar atrophy in ulnar nerve lesions (Guyon canal).
mus|Opponens digiti minimi muscle of han.prueba: Sitting, hand supinated, stabilize the first metacarpal; ask the patient to oppose the little finger toward the thumb; resistance on the palmar aspect of the fifth metacarpal, rotating it outward.
mus|Opponens digiti minimi muscle of han.biomecanica: Opposition of the fifth finger: flexion and lateral rotation of the fifth metacarpal (sagittal and transverse planes).

mus|Opponens pollicis muscle.origen: Flexor retinaculum and tubercle of the trapezium
mus|Opponens pollicis muscle.insercion: Lateral border of the first metacarpal
mus|Opponens pollicis muscle.accion: Opposition of the thumb: flexion and medial rotation of the first metacarpal
mus|Opponens pollicis muscle.clinica: Thenar atrophy and loss of opposition in advanced carpal tunnel syndrome.
mus|Opponens pollicis muscle.prueba: Sitting, hand supinated, stabilize the fifth metacarpal; ask the patient to bring the thumb pad toward the little finger pad; resistance on the head of the first metacarpal, derotating it.
mus|Opponens pollicis muscle.biomecanica: Opposition of the thumb: abduction, flexion and medial rotation of the first metacarpal at the trapeziometacarpal joint (combined, multiplanar).

mus|Orbicularis oris muscle.origen: Maxilla, mandible, modiolus and fibers of other facial muscles; skin and mucosa of the lip
mus|Orbicularis oris muscle.insercion: Skin and mucosa of the lips
mus|Orbicularis oris muscle.inervacion: Facial n. (CN VII), buccal and marginal mandibular branches
mus|Orbicularis oris muscle.irrigacion: Facial a. (superior and inferior labial aa.)
mus|Orbicularis oris muscle.accion: Closes and protrudes the lips; oral sphincter
mus|Orbicularis oris muscle.clinica: In peripheral facial palsy the patient cannot whistle or hold air in the mouth.
mus|Orbicularis oris muscle.prueba: Facial assessment: ask the patient to close and purse the lips (whistle, kiss); resist with a tongue depressor or try to separate the lips; observe symmetry.
mus|Orbicularis oris muscle.biomecanica: Closure, compression and protrusion of the lips (oral sphincter).

mus|Orbital part of orbicularis oculi.origen: Nasal part of the frontal bone, frontal process of the maxilla and medial palpebral ligament
mus|Orbital part of orbicularis oculi.insercion: Encircles the orbital margin; fibers to the skin of the eyebrow and cheek
mus|Orbital part of orbicularis oculi.inervacion: Facial n. (CN VII), temporal and zygomatic branches
mus|Orbital part of orbicularis oculi.irrigacion: Facial a. (angular), superficial temporal a. and branches of the ophthalmic a.
mus|Orbital part of orbicularis oculi.clinica: Its weakness (facial palsy) prevents forced eye closure; risk of exposure keratitis.
mus|Orbital part of orbicularis oculi.prueba: Facial assessment: ask the patient to close the eyes tightly; try to open the eyelids with the fingers; observe the eyelash sign.
mus|Orbital part of orbicularis oculi.biomecanica: Forced closure of the eyelids; wrinkles the periorbital skin and lowers the eyebrow.

mus|Palatopharyngeus muscle.insercion: Lateral wall of the pharynx and posterior border of the thyroid cartilage
mus|Palatopharyngeus muscle.inervacion: Vagus n. (CN X) via the pharyngeal plexus
mus|Palatopharyngeus muscle.irrigacion: Ascending palatine a. and ascending pharyngeal a.
mus|Palatopharyngeus muscle.accion: Elevates the pharynx and larynx; approximates the palatopharyngeal arches in swallowing
mus|Palatopharyngeus muscle.clinica: Forms the palatopharyngeal arch, the posterior boundary of the tonsillar fossa.
mus|Palatopharyngeus muscle.prueba: Cannot be tested manually; assess velar elevation and gag reflex (phonation of 'ah'), swallowing (cranial nerves IX-X).
mus|Palatopharyngeus muscle.biomecanica: Elevates the pharynx and larynx; approximates the posterior pillars, closing the oropharyngeal isthmus in swallowing.

mus|Palmar interossei muscles.origen: Palmar surfaces of metacarpals II, IV and V (side facing the middle finger)
mus|Palmar interossei muscles.insercion: Extensor expansion and base of the proximal phalanx of fingers II, IV and V
mus|Palmar interossei muscles.irrigacion: Deep palmar arch and palmar metacarpal aa.
mus|Palmar interossei muscles.accion: Adduct the fingers toward the axis of the middle finger (PAD); flex the MCP joints and extend the IP joints
mus|Palmar interossei muscles.clinica: Card test: inability to hold a piece of paper between the fingers in ulnar nerve injury.
mus|Palmar interossei muscles.prueba: Sitting, hand pronated, fingers extended; ask the patient to adduct the fingers toward the middle finger; resistance by pulling each abducted finger at the proximal phalanx (paper test).
mus|Palmar interossei muscles.biomecanica: Adduction of fingers 2, 4 and 5 toward the axis of the middle finger (frontal plane of the hand, anteroposterior axis); MCP flexion and IP extension.

mus|Palmaris longus muscle.origen: Medial epicondyle of the humerus (common flexor tendon)
mus|Palmaris longus muscle.accion: Weak flexion of the wrist; tenses the palmar aponeurosis
mus|Palmaris longus muscle.clinica: Absent in ~14% of people (Schaeffer test); its tendon is a frequent graft.
mus|Palmaris longus muscle.prueba: Sitting, forearm supinated; ask the patient to flex the wrist while opposing thumb and little finger (prominent tendon); resistance on the palm toward extension. Absent in ~15%.
mus|Palmaris longus muscle.biomecanica: Wrist flexion (sagittal plane, frontal axis); tenses the palmar aponeurosis.

mus|Palpebral part of orbicularis oculi.inervacion: Facial n. (CN VII), temporal and zygomatic branches
mus|Palpebral part of orbicularis oculi.accion: Gentle closure of the eyelids and blinking
mus|Palpebral part of orbicularis oculi.clinica: Efferent limb of the corneal reflex (afferent CN V1, efferent CN VII).
mus|Palpebral part of orbicularis oculi.prueba: Facial assessment: observe blinking and gentle eyelid closure; corneal reflex (cranial nerves V-VII).
mus|Palpebral part of orbicularis oculi.biomecanica: Gentle closure of the eyelids (blinking); facilitates lacrimal drainage.

mus|Pectineus muscle.origen: Pectineal line of the pubis (superior ramus)
mus|Pectineus muscle.insercion: Pectineal line of the femur, below the lesser trochanter
mus|Pectineus muscle.inervacion: Femoral n. (L2–L3); sometimes a branch of the obturator n.
mus|Pectineus muscle.irrigacion: Medial circumflex femoral a. and obturator a.
mus|Pectineus muscle.accion: Adduction and flexion of the thigh
mus|Pectineus muscle.clinica: Forms part of the floor of the femoral triangle.
mus|Pectineus muscle.prueba: Assessed with the hip adductors: side-lying on the side to be tested, support the upper leg in abduction; ask the patient to adduct the lower leg; resistance on the medial aspect of the distal thigh.
mus|Pectineus muscle.biomecanica: Adduction (frontal plane, anteroposterior axis) and hip flexion (sagittal plane, frontal axis).

mus|Pectoralis minor muscle.origen: Ribs III–V, near their costal cartilages
mus|Pectoralis minor muscle.irrigacion: Thoracoacromial a. (pectoral branch) and lateral thoracic a.
mus|Pectoralis minor muscle.accion: Depresses and protracts the scapula; accessory inspiratory muscle when the scapula is fixed
mus|Pectoralis minor muscle.clinica: Divides the axillary a. into three parts; its shortening may compress the axillary neurovascular bundle.
mus|Pectoralis minor muscle.prueba: Supine, arm at the side; ask the patient to push the shoulder forward and down (without elbow flexion); resistance on the anterior aspect of the shoulder toward the table.
mus|Pectoralis minor muscle.biomecanica: Depression, abduction (protraction) and anterior tilt of the scapula; accessory inspiratory muscle with the scapula fixed.

mus|Piriformis muscle.origen: Anterior surface of the sacrum (S2–S4) and sacrotuberous ligament
mus|Piriformis muscle.insercion: Superior border of the greater trochanter
mus|Piriformis muscle.accion: Lateral rotation of the extended thigh; abduction of the flexed thigh
mus|Piriformis muscle.clinica: Piriformis syndrome: compression of the sciatic n.; landmark of the greater sciatic foramen.
mus|Piriformis muscle.prueba: Assessed with the external rotators: sitting, knee at 90°; stabilize the thigh; ask the patient to move the foot medially; resistance at the medial malleolus and lateral aspect of the knee.
mus|Piriformis muscle.biomecanica: External rotation of the extended hip (transverse plane, longitudinal axis); abduction with the hip flexed >60°.

mus|Plantar interossei muscles.insercion: Medial surface of the base of proximal phalanges III–V and extensor expansions
mus|Plantar interossei muscles.irrigacion: Deep plantar arch and plantar metatarsal aa.
mus|Plantar interossei muscles.accion: Adduct toes III–V toward the axis of the second toe; flex the MTP joints
mus|Plantar interossei muscles.prueba: Cannot be reliably tested; observe adduction of toes 3-5 toward the second and MTP flexion; paper grip test.
mus|Plantar interossei muscles.biomecanica: Adduction of toes 3, 4 and 5 toward the second (transverse plane of the foot, vertical axis); MTP flexion.

mus|Plantaris muscle.origen: Lower end of the lateral supracondylar line of the femur and oblique popliteal ligament
mus|Plantaris muscle.insercion: Calcaneal tendon or medial surface of the calcaneus
mus|Plantaris muscle.accion: Weak plantar flexion and knee flexion
mus|Plantaris muscle.clinica: Its tendon is used as a graft; inconstant (absent in ~10%).
mus|Plantaris muscle.prueba: Cannot be tested in isolation; assessed together with the triceps surae (plantar flexion in single-leg standing, heel raises).
mus|Plantaris muscle.biomecanica: Weak plantar flexion of the ankle and knee flexion (sagittal plane, frontal axis).

mus|Platysma.origen: Subcutaneous tissue of the infraclavicular and supraclavicular regions
mus|Platysma.insercion: Inferior border of the mandible, skin of the cheek and corner of the mouth
mus|Platysma.accion: Tenses the skin of the neck; depresses the mandible and the corner of the mouth
mus|Platysma.clinica: Sutured in layers in cervical surgery to improve the scar; platysmal bands in aging.
mus|Platysma.prueba: Facial assessment: ask the patient to depress the corners of the mouth and tense the neck skin (clench the teeth); observe the neck bands.
mus|Platysma.biomecanica: Tenses the skin of the neck; depresses the corner of the mouth and the mandible.

mus|Popliteus muscle.origen: Lateral surface of the lateral condyle of the femur and lateral meniscus
mus|Popliteus muscle.insercion: Posterior surface of the tibia, above the soleal line
mus|Popliteus muscle.accion: Unlocks the knee by rotating the femur laterally on the tibia; knee flexion
mus|Popliteus muscle.clinica: Its tendon is intra-articular; popliteal tendinitis causes posterolateral knee pain.
mus|Popliteus muscle.prueba: Sitting, knee at 90°, foot everted; ask the patient to rotate the tibia medially; resistance at the foot/distal tibia toward external rotation.
mus|Popliteus muscle.biomecanica: Internal rotation of the tibia (transverse plane, longitudinal axis); unlocking of the knee at the start of flexion (sagittal plane).

mus|Posterior belly of digastric muscle.origen: Mastoid notch of the temporal bone
mus|Posterior belly of digastric muscle.insercion: Intermediate tendon, fixed to the body and greater horn of the hyoid by a fibrous loop
mus|Posterior belly of digastric muscle.irrigacion: Occipital a. and posterior auricular a.
mus|Posterior belly of digastric muscle.accion: Elevates and retracts the hyoid; helps depress the mandible
mus|Posterior belly of digastric muscle.clinica: Surgical landmark in the neck: crosses superficial to the carotid aa., internal jugular v. and CN XII.
mus|Posterior belly of digastric muscle.prueba: Cannot be tested with standard grades; palpate beneath the mandibular angle during swallowing or resisted mouth opening.
mus|Posterior belly of digastric muscle.biomecanica: Elevation and retraction of the hyoid in swallowing; mandibular depression with the hyoid fixed.

mus|Posterior crico-arytenoid muscle.origen: Posterior surface of the lamina of the cricoid cartilage
mus|Posterior crico-arytenoid muscle.insercion: Muscular process of the arytenoid cartilage
mus|Posterior crico-arytenoid muscle.accion: Sole abductor of the vocal folds; opens the glottis
mus|Posterior crico-arytenoid muscle.clinica: Bilateral injury of the recurrent laryngeal n. causes airway obstruction and stridor.
mus|Posterior crico-arytenoid muscle.prueba: Cannot be tested manually; assess vocal cord abduction on inspiration by laryngoscopy; stridor/dyspnea if bilateral paralysis.
mus|Posterior crico-arytenoid muscle.biomecanica: External rotation of the arytenoids: abduction of the vocal cords (sole glottic abductor).

mus|Procerus muscle.origen: Fascia over the nasal bone and lateral nasal cartilage
mus|Procerus muscle.insercion: Skin of the glabella, between the eyebrows
mus|Procerus muscle.inervacion: Facial n. (CN VII), temporal and zygomatic branches
mus|Procerus muscle.accion: Lowers the medial end of the eyebrows; produces transverse wrinkles at the root of the nose
mus|Procerus muscle.clinica: Target of botulinum toxin for glabellar lines.
mus|Procerus muscle.prueba: Facial assessment: ask the patient to frown and wrinkle the nose; observe the transverse folds at the nasal root.
mus|Procerus muscle.biomecanica: Lowers the medial end of the eyebrows; transverse wrinkles at the nasal root.

mus|Pronator quadratus.origen: Distal quarter of the anterior surface of the ulna
mus|Pronator quadratus.insercion: Distal quarter of the anterior surface of the radius
mus|Pronator quadratus.inervacion: Anterior interosseous n., branch of the median n. (C8–T1)
mus|Pronator quadratus.accion: Main pronator of the forearm; holds the distal radius and ulna together
mus|Pronator quadratus.clinica: Examined by resisting pronation with the elbow flexed, to assess the anterior interosseous n.
mus|Pronator quadratus.prueba: Sitting, elbow fully flexed (minimizes pronator teres), forearm supinated; ask for pronation; resistance on the dorsal aspect of the distal radius toward supination.
mus|Pronator quadratus.biomecanica: Pronation of the forearm (transverse plane, longitudinal axis); distal radioulnar cohesion.

mus|Psoas major.origen: Lateral surfaces of the bodies and discs of T12–L4 and lumbar transverse processes
mus|Psoas major.insercion: Lesser trochanter of the femur (iliopsoas tendon)
mus|Psoas major.accion: Flexion of the thigh; flexion and lateral flexion of the trunk
mus|Psoas major.clinica: Psoas sign in retrocecal appendicitis; abscesses may descend along its sheath to the thigh.
mus|Psoas major.prueba: Assessed with the iliopsoas: sitting, stabilize the pelvis; ask for hip flexion beyond 90°; resistance on the anterior aspect of the distal thigh. Kendall: supine, flexion-abduction-external rotation.
mus|Psoas major.biomecanica: Hip flexion (sagittal plane, frontal axis); lumbar flexion and lateral flexion; slight external rotation.

mus|Pubo-analis muscle.origen: Posterior surface of the body of the pubis
mus|Pubo-analis muscle.inervacion: Nerve to levator ani (S3–S4) and pudendal n.
mus|Pubo-analis muscle.irrigacion: Internal pudendal a. and inferior rectal a.
mus|Pubo-analis muscle.accion: Elevates the anus; contributes to continence
mus|Pubo-analis muscle.prueba: Pelvic floor assessment: rectal/vaginal examination asking for contraction (modified Oxford scale 0-5); perineometry/EMG.
mus|Pubo-analis muscle.biomecanica: Elevates the anus and contributes to the anorectal angulation and continence.

mus|Pubococcygeus muscle.origen: Posterior surface of the body of the pubis and anterior part of the tendinous arch of the levator ani
mus|Pubococcygeus muscle.inervacion: Nerve to levator ani (S3–S4) and pudendal n.
mus|Pubococcygeus muscle.irrigacion: Internal pudendal a. and inferior gluteal a.
mus|Pubococcygeus muscle.accion: Supports the pelvic viscera; elevates the pelvic floor
mus|Pubococcygeus muscle.clinica: Injured in vaginal delivery; target of Kegel exercises.
mus|Pubococcygeus muscle.prueba: Pelvic floor assessment: vaginal/rectal palpation asking for contraction and lift (modified Oxford scale 0-5); perineometry/EMG.
mus|Pubococcygeus muscle.biomecanica: Support of the pelvic viscera; elevation of the pelvic floor and urinary and fecal continence.

mus|Quadratus femoris muscle.origen: Lateral border of the ischial tuberosity
mus|Quadratus femoris muscle.insercion: Quadrate tubercle of the intertrochanteric crest
mus|Quadratus femoris muscle.prueba: Assessed with the external rotators: sitting, knee at 90°; stabilize the thigh; ask the patient to move the foot medially; resistance at the medial malleolus and lateral aspect of the knee.
mus|Quadratus femoris muscle.biomecanica: External rotation of the hip (transverse plane, longitudinal axis); assists adduction.

mus|Quadratus lumborum muscle.origen: Inner lip of the iliac crest and iliolumbar ligament
mus|Quadratus lumborum muscle.insercion: Inferior border of rib XII and transverse processes of L1–L4
mus|Quadratus lumborum muscle.inervacion: Subcostal n. and anterior rami of L1–L4 (T12–L4)
mus|Quadratus lumborum muscle.irrigacion: Lumbar aa., subcostal a. and iliolumbar a.
mus|Quadratus lumborum muscle.accion: Lateral flexion of the trunk; fixes rib XII in inspiration
mus|Quadratus lumborum muscle.clinica: Frequent source of myofascial low back pain.
mus|Quadratus lumborum muscle.prueba: Prone or supine, hold the leg with the hip extended; ask the patient to raise the pelvis toward the rib cage (hip hiking); resistance by traction on the ankle.
mus|Quadratus lumborum muscle.biomecanica: Elevation of the hemipelvis and lateral flexion of the trunk (frontal plane, anteroposterior axis); fixation of the 12th rib in inspiration.

mus|Quadratus plantae muscle.origen: Medial surface and lateral border of the plantar surface of the calcaneus
mus|Quadratus plantae muscle.insercion: Posterolateral border of the flexor digitorum longus tendon
mus|Quadratus plantae muscle.accion: Corrects the oblique pull of the flexor digitorum longus; helps flex toes II–V
mus|Quadratus plantae muscle.prueba: Cannot be tested in isolation; assessed with toe flexion (flexor digitorum longus) in supine, resisting beneath the distal phalanges.
mus|Quadratus plantae muscle.biomecanica: Corrects the oblique pull of the flexor digitorum longus, assisting flexion of the IP joints of toes 2–5 (sagittal plane).

mus|Radial head of flexor digitorum supe.es: Flexor digitorum superficialis muscle, radial head
mus|Radial head of flexor digitorum supe.la: Caput radiale musculi flexoris digitorum superficialis
mus|Radial head of flexor digitorum supe.origen: Upper half of the anterior border of the radius (oblique line)
mus|Radial head of flexor digitorum supe.insercion: Lateral surfaces of the middle phalanges of fingers II–V
mus|Radial head of flexor digitorum supe.irrigacion: Radial a. and ulnar a. (muscular branches)
mus|Radial head of flexor digitorum supe.accion: Flexion of the PIP and MCP joints of fingers II–V; wrist flexion
mus|Radial head of flexor digitorum supe.clinica: Examined by flexing the PIP joint while the other fingers are held in extension.
mus|Radial head of flexor digitorum supe.prueba: Flexor superficialis test: sitting, hand supinated, keep the other fingers extended; ask for PIP flexion; resistance on the middle phalanx.
mus|Radial head of flexor digitorum supe.biomecanica: Flexion of the PIP and MCP joints of fingers 2–5 and of the wrist (sagittal plane, frontal axis).

mus|Rectus abdominis muscle.insercion: Xiphoid process and costal cartilages V–VII
mus|Rectus abdominis muscle.accion: Trunk flexion; compresses the abdominal viscera
mus|Rectus abdominis muscle.clinica: Diastasis recti in pregnancy; basis of the TRAM flap in breast reconstruction.
mus|Rectus abdominis muscle.prueba: Supine, legs extended; ask the patient to curl the trunk until the scapulae lift off: hands forward (3), crossed over the chest (4), behind the head (5).
mus|Rectus abdominis muscle.biomecanica: Trunk flexion (sagittal plane, frontal axis); posterior pelvic tilt; increase of intra-abdominal pressure.

mus|Rectus anterior capitis muscle.origen: Anterior surface of the lateral mass of the atlas
mus|Rectus anterior capitis muscle.insercion: Basilar part of the occipital bone, in front of the foramen magnum
mus|Rectus anterior capitis muscle.irrigacion: Vertebral a. and ascending pharyngeal a.
mus|Rectus anterior capitis muscle.accion: Flexion of the head at the atlanto-occipital joint
mus|Rectus anterior capitis muscle.prueba: Cannot be tested in isolation; assessed with craniocervical flexion (nodding) in supine, resistance on the forehead/chin; craniocervical flexion test with biofeedback.
mus|Rectus anterior capitis muscle.biomecanica: Flexion of the head on the atlas (sagittal plane, frontal axis); atlanto-occipital stabilization.

mus|Rectus femoris muscle.origen: Anterior inferior iliac spine (direct head) and supra-acetabular groove (reflected head)
mus|Rectus femoris muscle.insercion: Base of the patella and, via the patellar ligament, tibial tuberosity
mus|Rectus femoris muscle.clinica: Patellar reflex (L3–L4); its shortening is assessed with the Thomas/Ely test; AIIS avulsion in adolescents.
mus|Rectus femoris muscle.prueba: Sitting at the edge of the table, stabilize the thigh; ask for knee extension without locking; resistance on the anterior aspect of the distal tibia. Shortening: Ely/Thomas test.
mus|Rectus femoris muscle.biomecanica: Knee extension and hip flexion (sagittal plane, frontal axis).

mus|Rectus lateralis capitis muscle.origen: Superior surface of the transverse process of the atlas
mus|Rectus lateralis capitis muscle.insercion: Jugular process of the occipital bone
mus|Rectus lateralis capitis muscle.accion: Ipsilateral lateral flexion of the head
mus|Rectus lateralis capitis muscle.prueba: Cannot be tested in isolation; assessed with resisted upper cervical lateral flexion at the temporal region.
mus|Rectus lateralis capitis muscle.biomecanica: Lateral flexion of the head (frontal plane, anteroposterior axis); stabilizes the atlanto-occipital joint.

mus|Rectus posterior major capitis muscl.insercion: Lateral part of the inferior nuchal line of the occipital bone
mus|Rectus posterior major capitis muscl.accion: Extension and ipsilateral rotation of the head
mus|Rectus posterior major capitis muscl.clinica: Superomedial boundary of the suboccipital triangle; implicated in cervicogenic headache.
mus|Rectus posterior major capitis muscl.prueba: Cannot be tested in isolation; assessed with resisted craniocervical extension at the occiput (prone) and suboccipital palpation.
mus|Rectus posterior major capitis muscl.biomecanica: Extension of the head (sagittal plane, frontal axis); ipsilateral rotation (transverse plane, longitudinal axis).

mus|Rectus posterior minor capitis muscl.insercion: Medial part of the inferior nuchal line of the occipital bone
mus|Rectus posterior minor capitis muscl.clinica: Connected to the dura mater (myodural bridge); related to tension-type headache.
mus|Rectus posterior minor capitis muscl.prueba: Cannot be tested in isolation; assessed with resisted craniocervical extension at the occiput and suboccipital palpation.
mus|Rectus posterior minor capitis muscl.biomecanica: Extension of the head on the atlas (sagittal plane, frontal axis); suboccipital proprioception.

mus|Rhomboid major muscle.origen: Spinous processes of T2–T5 and supraspinous ligaments
mus|Rhomboid major muscle.insercion: Medial border of the scapula, from the root of the spine to the inferior angle
mus|Rhomboid major muscle.accion: Retraction and elevation of the scapula; downward rotation of the glenoid cavity
mus|Rhomboid major muscle.clinica: Its weakness (injury to the dorsal scapular n.) causes mild lateral winged scapula.
mus|Rhomboid major muscle.prueba: Prone, hand behind the back (shoulder in internal rotation and adduction); ask the patient to lift the hand off the back; resistance at the medial scapular border/arm toward scapular abduction.
mus|Rhomboid major muscle.biomecanica: Adduction (retraction), elevation and downward rotation (inward tilt) of the scapula (frontal plane).

mus|Rhomboid minor muscle.origen: Nuchal ligament and spinous processes of C7–T1
mus|Rhomboid minor muscle.insercion: Medial border of the scapula, at the level of the root of the spine
mus|Rhomboid minor muscle.accion: Retraction and elevation of the scapula; downward rotation of the glenoid cavity
mus|Rhomboid minor muscle.prueba: Prone, hand behind the back (shoulder in internal rotation and adduction); ask the patient to lift the hand off the back; resistance at the medial scapular border toward scapular abduction.
mus|Rhomboid minor muscle.biomecanica: Adduction (retraction), elevation and downward rotation of the scapula (frontal plane).

mus|Risorius muscle.insercion: Skin of the angle of the mouth (modiolus)
mus|Risorius muscle.accion: Retracts the angle of the mouth laterally
mus|Risorius muscle.clinica: Inconstant; its tetanic contraction contributes to the sardonic grin (risus sardonicus).
mus|Risorius muscle.prueba: Facial assessment: ask the patient to retract the corners of the mouth laterally (forced smile without elevation); observe symmetry.
mus|Risorius muscle.biomecanica: Lateral retraction of the angle of the lips.

mus|Rotatores.insercion: Lamina and base of the spinous process of the vertebra 1–2 levels above
mus|Rotatores.inervacion: Posterior rami of the spinal nerves
mus|Rotatores.irrigacion: Dorsal branches of the posterior intercostal, lumbar and vertebral aa.
mus|Rotatores.accion: Stabilize the vertebrae; contralateral rotation and proprioceptive function
mus|Rotatores.clinica: Most developed in the thoracic region.
mus|Rotatores.prueba: Cannot be tested in isolation; assessed with resisted trunk extension and rotation and deep paravertebral palpation.
mus|Rotatores.biomecanica: Contralateral rotation (transverse plane, longitudinal axis) and segmental extension; proprioception and stabilization.

mus|Sartorius muscle.insercion: Upper part of the medial surface of the tibia (pes anserinus)
mus|Sartorius muscle.accion: Flexion, abduction and lateral rotation of the hip; flexion of the knee
mus|Sartorius muscle.clinica: Lateral boundary of the femoral triangle and roof of the adductor canal; anserine bursitis.
mus|Sartorius muscle.prueba: Sitting; ask for hip flexion, abduction and external rotation with knee flexion (heel toward the opposite knee); resistance at the anterolateral thigh and posteromedial ankle.
mus|Sartorius muscle.biomecanica: Hip flexion, abduction and external rotation; knee flexion and internal rotation (multiplanar).

mus|Scalenus anterior muscle.origen: Anterior tubercles of the transverse processes of C3–C6
mus|Scalenus anterior muscle.insercion: Scalene tubercle of the first rib
mus|Scalenus anterior muscle.accion: Elevates the first rib; flexion and lateral flexion of the neck
mus|Scalenus anterior muscle.clinica: The phrenic n. descends over its anterior surface; implicated in thoracic outlet syndrome.
mus|Scalenus anterior muscle.prueba: Assessed with anterolateral neck flexion: supine, ask the patient to flex and laterally flex the neck rotated contralaterally; resistance at the temple.
mus|Scalenus anterior muscle.biomecanica: Cervical lateral flexion (frontal plane, anteroposterior axis); cervical flexion; elevation of the 1st rib during inspiration.

mus|Scalenus medius muscle.origen: Posterior tubercles of the transverse processes of C2–C7
mus|Scalenus medius muscle.insercion: Superior surface of the first rib, behind the groove for the subclavian a.
mus|Scalenus medius muscle.irrigacion: Ascending cervical a. and transverse cervical a.
mus|Scalenus medius muscle.accion: Elevates the first rib; lateral flexion of the neck
mus|Scalenus medius muscle.clinica: The brachial plexus and the subclavian a. pass between the scalenus anterior and medius mm. (interscalene triangle).
mus|Scalenus medius muscle.prueba: Assessed with resisted cervical lateral flexion at the temple (sitting or side-lying, stabilize the shoulder).
mus|Scalenus medius muscle.biomecanica: Cervical lateral flexion (frontal plane, anteroposterior axis); elevation of the 1st rib during inspiration.

mus|Scalenus posterior muscle.origen: Posterior tubercles of the transverse processes of C4–C6
mus|Scalenus posterior muscle.insercion: External surface of the second rib
mus|Scalenus posterior muscle.irrigacion: Ascending cervical a. and transverse cervical a.
mus|Scalenus posterior muscle.accion: Elevates the second rib; lateral flexion of the neck
mus|Scalenus posterior muscle.prueba: Assessed with resisted cervical lateral flexion at the temple (sitting or side-lying, stabilize the shoulder).
mus|Scalenus posterior muscle.biomecanica: Cervical lateral flexion (frontal plane, anteroposterior axis); elevation of the 2nd rib during inspiration.

mus|Scapular spinal part of deltoid musc.origen: Inferior border of the spine of the scapula
mus|Scapular spinal part of deltoid musc.accion: Extension and lateral rotation of the arm
mus|Scapular spinal part of deltoid musc.clinica: Atrophy and sensory loss in the 'regimental badge' area due to axillary n. injury (fracture of the surgical neck).
mus|Scapular spinal part of deltoid musc.prueba: Posterior deltoid: prone, shoulder at 90° of abduction in internal rotation, elbow flexed; ask for horizontal abduction; resistance at the posterior surface of the distal arm.
mus|Scapular spinal part of deltoid musc.biomecanica: Shoulder extension (sagittal plane, frontal axis); horizontal abduction (transverse plane, vertical axis); external rotation.

mus|Semimembranosus muscle.insercion: Posterior surface of the medial condyle of the tibia; expansions: oblique popliteal ligament and popliteal fascia
mus|Semimembranosus muscle.inervacion: Tibial n., part of the sciatic n. (L5–S2)
mus|Semimembranosus muscle.irrigacion: Perforating aa. of the deep femoral a.; branches of the popliteal a.
mus|Semimembranosus muscle.accion: Hip extension, knee flexion and medial rotation of the leg with the knee flexed
mus|Semimembranosus muscle.clinica: Its bursa, communicating with the joint, gives rise to the popliteal Baker's cyst.
mus|Semimembranosus muscle.prueba: Prone, knee at 50-70° of flexion, internal rotation of the leg and foot. Stabilize the thigh. Flex the knee while maintaining internal rotation. Grade 3: no resistance against gravity; 4-5: resistance at the posterior surface of the leg, proximal to the ankle, toward extension.
mus|Semimembranosus muscle.biomecanica: Knee flexion (sagittal plane, frontal axis); hip extension (sagittal plane, frontal axis); internal rotation of the tibia with the knee flexed (transverse plane, longitudinal axis).

mus|Semispinalis colli muscle.insercion: Spinous processes of C2–C5, especially the axis
mus|Semispinalis colli muscle.inervacion: Posterior rami of cervical and thoracic spinal nerves
mus|Semispinalis colli muscle.irrigacion: Deep cervical a., vertebral a. and posterior intercostal aa.
mus|Semispinalis colli muscle.accion: Extension of the cervical spine and contralateral rotation
mus|Semispinalis colli muscle.prueba: Cannot be tested in isolation; assessed with cervical extension in prone: stabilize the upper thorax, extend the neck, resistance at the occipital region.
mus|Semispinalis colli muscle.biomecanica: Extension of the cervical and upper thoracic spine (sagittal plane, frontal axis); contralateral rotation (transverse plane, longitudinal axis).

mus|Semispinalis thoracis muscle.inervacion: Posterior rami of thoracic spinal nerves
mus|Semispinalis thoracis muscle.irrigacion: Dorsal branches of the posterior intercostal aa.
mus|Semispinalis thoracis muscle.accion: Extension of the thoracic spine and contralateral rotation
mus|Semispinalis thoracis muscle.prueba: Cannot be tested in isolation; assessed with trunk extension in prone, hands behind the head, stabilizing the pelvis and legs.
mus|Semispinalis thoracis muscle.biomecanica: Extension of the thoracic spine (sagittal plane, frontal axis); contralateral rotation (transverse plane, longitudinal axis).

mus|Semitendinosus muscle.origen: Ischial tuberosity (common tendon with the long head of the biceps femoris)
mus|Semitendinosus muscle.insercion: Medial surface of the upper part of the tibia (pes anserinus)
mus|Semitendinosus muscle.inervacion: Tibial n., part of the sciatic n. (L5–S2)
mus|Semitendinosus muscle.irrigacion: Perforating aa. of the deep femoral a.
mus|Semitendinosus muscle.accion: Hip extension, knee flexion and medial rotation of the leg
mus|Semitendinosus muscle.clinica: Its tendon is frequently used as a graft in anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction.
mus|Semitendinosus muscle.prueba: Prone, knee at 50-70° of flexion, internal rotation of the leg. Stabilize the thigh. Flex the knee while maintaining internal rotation. Grade 3: against gravity without resistance; 4-5: resistance proximal to the ankle, on the posterior surface of the leg, toward extension.
mus|Semitendinosus muscle.biomecanica: Knee flexion (sagittal plane, frontal axis); hip extension (sagittal plane, frontal axis); internal rotation of the tibia (transverse plane, longitudinal axis).

mus|Serratus anterior muscle.insercion: Costal surface of the medial border of the scapula, from the superior to the inferior angle
mus|Serratus anterior muscle.irrigacion: Lateral thoracic a. and thoracodorsal a.
mus|Serratus anterior muscle.accion: Protraction and upward rotation of the scapula; holds it against the thorax
mus|Serratus anterior muscle.clinica: Injury to the long thoracic n. produces winged scapula, visible when pushing against a wall.
mus|Serratus anterior muscle.prueba: Supine, shoulder at 90° of flexion, elbow extended. Stabilize the thorax. Protract the scapula by raising the arm toward the ceiling. Grade 3: no resistance; 4-5: resistance on the fist/forearm pushing toward the table. Observe scapular lifting off.
mus|Serratus anterior muscle.biomecanica: Scapular abduction/protraction (transverse plane, vertical axis); upward rotation of the scapula (frontal plane, anteroposterior axis).

mus|Serratus posterior inferior muscle.origen: Spinous processes of T11–L2 and supraspinous ligaments
mus|Serratus posterior inferior muscle.irrigacion: Posterior intercostal aa. and subcostal a.
mus|Serratus posterior inferior muscle.accion: Depresses the lower ribs; respiratory function debated
mus|Serratus posterior inferior muscle.prueba: Cannot be tested in isolation; assessed clinically by palpation and observation during forced expiration.
mus|Serratus posterior inferior muscle.biomecanica: Depression of ribs IX-XII (sagittal plane, frontal axis); accessory respiratory muscle.

mus|Serratus posterior superior muscle.origen: Nuchal ligament and spinous processes of C7–T3
mus|Serratus posterior superior muscle.accion: Elevates the upper ribs; respiratory function debated
mus|Serratus posterior superior muscle.prueba: Cannot be tested in isolation; assessed by palpation during forced inspiration.
mus|Serratus posterior superior muscle.biomecanica: Elevation of ribs II-V (sagittal plane, frontal axis); accessory inspiratory muscle.

mus|Short head of biceps brachii.origen: Apex of the coracoid process (common tendon with the coracobrachialis)
mus|Short head of biceps brachii.irrigacion: Muscular branches of the brachial a.
mus|Short head of biceps brachii.accion: Supination of the forearm, elbow flexion; assists in shoulder flexion and adduction
mus|Short head of biceps brachii.prueba: Sitting, arm beside the trunk, forearm supinated. Stabilize the humerus. Flex the elbow. Grade 3: full range without resistance; 4-5: resistance at the anterior surface of the distal forearm, toward extension.
mus|Short head of biceps brachii.biomecanica: Elbow flexion (sagittal plane, frontal axis); supination (transverse plane, longitudinal axis); shoulder flexion and adduction (sagittal/frontal plane).

mus|Short head of biceps femoris.origen: Lateral lip of the linea aspera and lateral supracondylar line of the femur
mus|Short head of biceps femoris.insercion: Head of the fibula (common tendon with the long head)
mus|Short head of biceps femoris.inervacion: Common fibular n., part of the sciatic n. (L5–S2)
mus|Short head of biceps femoris.irrigacion: Perforating aa. of the deep femoral a.
mus|Short head of biceps femoris.accion: Knee flexion and lateral rotation of the leg with the knee flexed
mus|Short head of biceps femoris.clinica: The only hamstring portion innervated by the common fibular n.; it does not act on the hip.
mus|Short head of biceps femoris.prueba: Prone, knee at 50-70° of flexion, external rotation of the leg. Stabilize the thigh. Flex the knee while maintaining external rotation. Grade 3: no resistance; 4-5: resistance proximal to the ankle, posterior surface, toward extension.
mus|Short head of biceps femoris.biomecanica: Knee flexion (sagittal plane, frontal axis); external rotation of the tibia with the knee flexed (transverse plane, longitudinal axis).

mus|Soleus muscle.origen: Head and posterior upper quarter of the fibula, soleal line of the tibia and tendinous arch of the soleus
mus|Soleus muscle.insercion: Calcaneal tuberosity via the calcaneal (Achilles) tendon
mus|Soleus muscle.irrigacion: Popliteal a., posterior tibial a. and fibular a.
mus|Soleus muscle.accion: Plantar flexion of the ankle; stabilizes the leg in standing
mus|Soleus muscle.clinica: An important muscular venous pump; its veins are a frequent site of deep vein thrombosis.
mus|Soleus muscle.prueba: Prone, knee flexed to 90°. Stabilize the leg. Plantar flexion of the ankle. Grade 3: full range without resistance; 4-5: resistance on the calcaneus pushing toward dorsiflexion. Alternative in standing: heel raise with the knee flexed.
mus|Soleus muscle.biomecanica: Plantar flexion of the ankle (sagittal plane, frontal axis); stabilization of the tibia in standing.

mus|Spinalis capitis muscle.origen: Spinous processes of C7–T1 (often fused with the semispinalis capitis)
mus|Spinalis capitis muscle.insercion: Occipital bone, between the superior and inferior nuchal lines
mus|Spinalis capitis muscle.inervacion: Posterior rami of cervical spinal nerves
mus|Spinalis capitis muscle.irrigacion: Occipital a. and deep cervical a.
mus|Spinalis capitis muscle.prueba: Cannot be tested in isolation; assessed with head and neck extension in prone with resistance at the occiput.
mus|Spinalis capitis muscle.biomecanica: Extension of the head and cervical spine (sagittal plane, frontal axis).

mus|Spinalis colli muscle.origen: Nuchal ligament and spinous processes of C7–T2
mus|Spinalis colli muscle.inervacion: Posterior rami of cervical spinal nerves
mus|Spinalis colli muscle.irrigacion: Deep cervical a. and vertebral a.
mus|Spinalis colli muscle.prueba: Cannot be tested in isolation; assessed with cervical extension in prone with resistance at the occiput.
mus|Spinalis colli muscle.biomecanica: Extension of the cervical spine (sagittal plane, frontal axis).

mus|Spinalis thoracis muscle.inervacion: Posterior rami of thoracic and lumbar spinal nerves
mus|Spinalis thoracis muscle.irrigacion: Dorsal branches of the posterior intercostal and lumbar aa.
mus|Spinalis thoracis muscle.prueba: Cannot be tested in isolation; assessed with trunk extension in prone, stabilizing the pelvis and legs.
mus|Spinalis thoracis muscle.biomecanica: Extension of the thoracic spine (sagittal plane, frontal axis); ipsilateral lateral flexion (frontal plane, anteroposterior axis).

mus|Splenius capitis muscle.origen: Lower half of the nuchal ligament and spinous processes of C7–T3/T4
mus|Splenius capitis muscle.insercion: Mastoid process and lateral third of the superior nuchal line
mus|Splenius capitis muscle.inervacion: Posterior rami of the middle cervical nerves (C3–C5)
mus|Splenius capitis muscle.irrigacion: Occipital a. and transverse cervical a.
mus|Splenius capitis muscle.accion: Bilateral: extension of the head and neck; unilateral: ipsilateral lateral flexion and rotation
mus|Splenius capitis muscle.prueba: Prone, head off the table. Stabilize the upper thorax. Extend and rotate the head toward the tested side. Grade 3: no resistance; 4-5: resistance at the posterolateral occipitoparietal region toward flexion and opposite rotation.
mus|Splenius capitis muscle.biomecanica: Extension of the head and neck (sagittal plane, frontal axis); ipsilateral rotation (transverse plane, longitudinal axis); ipsilateral lateral flexion (frontal plane, anteroposterior axis).

mus|Splenius colli muscle.insercion: Posterior tubercles of the transverse processes of C1–C3/C4
mus|Splenius colli muscle.inervacion: Posterior rami of the lower cervical nerves
mus|Splenius colli muscle.irrigacion: Occipital a. and transverse cervical a.
mus|Splenius colli muscle.accion: Bilateral: extension of the neck; unilateral: ipsilateral lateral flexion and rotation
mus|Splenius colli muscle.prueba: Prone, head off the table. Stabilize the upper thorax. Extend the neck with ipsilateral rotation. Grade 3: no resistance; 4-5: resistance at the posterolateral occipital region.
mus|Splenius colli muscle.biomecanica: Extension of the cervical spine (sagittal plane, frontal axis); ipsilateral rotation (transverse plane, longitudinal axis).

mus|Sternocleidomastoid muscle.origen: Sternal head: anterior surface of the manubrium; clavicular head: medial third of the clavicle
mus|Sternocleidomastoid muscle.insercion: Mastoid process and lateral half of the superior nuchal line
mus|Sternocleidomastoid muscle.inervacion: Accessory n. (CN XI); proprioceptive fibers from C2–C3
mus|Sternocleidomastoid muscle.irrigacion: Occipital a., superior thyroid a. and suprascapular a.
mus|Sternocleidomastoid muscle.accion: Unilateral: ipsilateral lateral flexion and contralateral rotation of the head; bilateral: neck flexion
mus|Sternocleidomastoid muscle.clinica: Its fibrosis or shortening produces congenital torticollis.
mus|Sternocleidomastoid muscle.prueba: Supine, head rotated to the opposite side. Stabilize the thorax. Flex the neck by lifting the head off the table. Grade 3: no resistance; 4-5: resistance at the temporal region, toward the table.
mus|Sternocleidomastoid muscle.biomecanica: Bilateral cervical flexion (sagittal plane, frontal axis); ipsilateral lateral flexion (frontal plane, anteroposterior axis); contralateral rotation (transverse plane, longitudinal axis).

mus|Sternocostal head of pectoralis majo.origen: Anterior surface of the sternum and costal cartilages 1–6
mus|Sternocostal head of pectoralis majo.insercion: Lateral lip of the intertubercular groove of the humerus (common tendon)
mus|Sternocostal head of pectoralis majo.irrigacion: Pectoral branches of the thoracoacromial a. and internal thoracic a.
mus|Sternocostal head of pectoralis majo.accion: Adduction and medial rotation of the humerus; extends the arm from flexion
mus|Sternocostal head of pectoralis majo.prueba: Supine, shoulder at ~120° of flexion, elbow extended. Stabilize the opposite hemipelvis. Adduct diagonally toward the opposite hip. Grade 3: no resistance; 4-5: resistance at the distal forearm upward and outward.
mus|Sternocostal head of pectoralis majo.biomecanica: Horizontal adduction (transverse plane, vertical axis); extension from flexion (sagittal plane, frontal axis); internal rotation of the shoulder (transverse plane, longitudinal axis).

mus|Sternohyoid muscle.origen: Manubrium of the sternum and medial end of the clavicle
mus|Sternohyoid muscle.insercion: Inferior border of the body of the hyoid bone
mus|Sternohyoid muscle.accion: Depresses the hyoid bone after swallowing
mus|Sternohyoid muscle.prueba: Cannot be tested in isolation; assessed by palpation during swallowing or hyoid depression.
mus|Sternohyoid muscle.biomecanica: Depression of the hyoid bone (sagittal plane, frontal axis).

mus|Sternothyroid muscle.origen: Posterior surface of the manubrium of the sternum and first costal cartilage
mus|Sternothyroid muscle.insercion: Oblique line of the thyroid cartilage
mus|Sternothyroid muscle.clinica: Limits the upward growth of goiter, which tends to extend downward.
mus|Sternothyroid muscle.prueba: Cannot be tested in isolation; assessed by palpation during swallowing and phonation.
mus|Sternothyroid muscle.biomecanica: Depression of the thyroid cartilage and larynx (sagittal plane, frontal axis).

mus|Straight part of cricothyroid muscle.origen: Anterolateral surface of the arch of the cricoid cartilage
mus|Straight part of cricothyroid muscle.insercion: Inferior border of the lamina of the thyroid cartilage
mus|Straight part of cricothyroid muscle.inervacion: External branch of the superior laryngeal n. (vagus n.)
mus|Straight part of cricothyroid muscle.irrigacion: Cricothyroid a., branch of the superior thyroid a.
mus|Straight part of cricothyroid muscle.accion: Tenses and lengthens the vocal folds by tilting the thyroid
mus|Straight part of cricothyroid muscle.clinica: Injury to the external laryngeal n. during thyroidectomy causes a weak voice and loss of high pitches.
