mus|Straight part of cricothyroid muscle.prueba: Cannot be tested manually; assessed by laryngoscopy and production of high-pitched tones (laryngeal EMG).
mus|Straight part of cricothyroid muscle.biomecanica: Tilting of the thyroid cartilage on the cricoid (sagittal plane, frontal axis); tenses the vocal cords.

mus|Stylohyoid muscle.origen: Styloid process of the temporal bone
mus|Stylohyoid muscle.insercion: Body of the hyoid bone, junction with the greater horn (splits around the tendon of the digastric)
mus|Stylohyoid muscle.accion: Elevates and retracts the hyoid bone
mus|Stylohyoid muscle.prueba: Cannot be tested in isolation; assessed by palpation during swallowing.
mus|Stylohyoid muscle.biomecanica: Elevation and retraction of the hyoid bone (sagittal plane, frontal axis).

mus|Stylopharyngeus muscle.origen: Medial surface of the base of the styloid process
mus|Stylopharyngeus muscle.insercion: Pharyngeal wall and posterior border of the thyroid cartilage
mus|Stylopharyngeus muscle.accion: Elevates the pharynx and larynx and widens the pharynx during swallowing
mus|Stylopharyngeus muscle.clinica: The only muscle innervated by the glossopharyngeal n.
mus|Stylopharyngeus muscle.prueba: Cannot be tested manually; assessed with swallowing and the gag reflex (glossopharyngeal nerve).
mus|Stylopharyngeus muscle.biomecanica: Elevation and widening of the pharynx and larynx during swallowing.

mus|Subclavius muscle.origen: Junction of the 1st rib with its costal cartilage
mus|Subclavius muscle.insercion: Groove for the subclavius on the inferior surface of the middle third of the clavicle
mus|Subclavius muscle.irrigacion: Clavicular branch of the thoracoacromial a.
mus|Subclavius muscle.clinica: Cushions and protects the subclavian vessels in clavicle fractures.
mus|Subclavius muscle.prueba: Cannot be tested in isolation; assessed by infraclavicular palpation during shoulder depression.
mus|Subclavius muscle.biomecanica: Depression and stabilization of the clavicle at the sternoclavicular joint (frontal plane, anteroposterior axis).

mus|Subscapularis muscle.accion: Medial rotation and adduction of the humerus; stabilizes the humeral head (rotator cuff)
mus|Subscapularis muscle.clinica: Assessed with the Gerber test (lift-off) and the belly-press.
mus|Subscapularis muscle.prueba: Prone, shoulder abducted 90°, elbow flexed 90° with the forearm hanging. Stabilize the humerus. Internal rotation bringing the palm upward and backward. Grade 3: no resistance; 4-5: resistance at the palmar surface of the distal forearm toward external rotation.
mus|Subscapularis muscle.biomecanica: Internal rotation of the shoulder (transverse plane, longitudinal axis); anterior stabilization of the humeral head.

mus|Superficial head of flexor pollicis.es: Flexor pollicis brevis m., superficial head
mus|Superficial head of flexor pollicis.la: Caput superficiale musculi flexoris pollicis brevis
mus|Superficial head of flexor pollicis.origen: Flexor retinaculum and tubercle of the trapezium
mus|Superficial head of flexor pollicis.insercion: Radial side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the thumb (via the lateral sesamoid)
mus|Superficial head of flexor pollicis.inervacion: Recurrent branch of the median n. (C8–T1)
mus|Superficial head of flexor pollicis.irrigacion: Superficial palmar branch of the radial a.
mus|Superficial head of flexor pollicis.accion: Flexion of the metacarpophalangeal joint of the thumb
mus|Superficial head of flexor pollicis.clinica: Atrophy of the thenar eminence in advanced carpal tunnel syndrome.
mus|Superficial head of flexor pollicis.prueba: Sitting, forearm supinated. Stabilize the first metacarpal. Flex the MCP of the thumb while keeping the IP extended. Grade 3: full range; 4-5: resistance at the palmar surface of the proximal phalanx toward extension.
mus|Superficial head of flexor pollicis.biomecanica: Flexion of the MCP of the thumb (frontal plane of the hand, anteroposterior axis); assists in opposition.

mus|Superficial head of pronator teres.origen: Medial epicondyle of the humerus (common flexor tendon) and medial supracondylar ridge
mus|Superficial head of pronator teres.insercion: Lateral surface of the middle part of the radius
mus|Superficial head of pronator teres.irrigacion: Ulnar a. and anterior ulnar recurrent a.
mus|Superficial head of pronator teres.accion: Pronation of the forearm; weak elbow flexion
mus|Superficial head of pronator teres.clinica: The median n. passes between its two heads: pronator syndrome.
mus|Superficial head of pronator teres.prueba: Sitting, elbow flexed ~90°, forearm supinated. Stabilize the humerus. Pronate. Grade 3: full range; 4-5: resistance at the distal forearm, dorsal surface of the radius and palmar surface of the ulna, toward supination.
mus|Superficial head of pronator teres.biomecanica: Pronation of the forearm (transverse plane, longitudinal axis); weak elbow flexion (sagittal plane, frontal axis).

mus|Superficial part of masseter.origen: Maxillary process of the zygomatic bone and anterior two thirds of the inferior border of the zygomatic arch
mus|Superficial part of masseter.insercion: Angle and lower half of the lateral surface of the mandibular ramus
mus|Superficial part of masseter.inervacion: Masseteric n., from the mandibular n. (CN V3)
mus|Superficial part of masseter.irrigacion: Masseteric a., facial a. and transverse facial a.
mus|Superficial part of masseter.accion: Elevation and protrusion of the mandible
mus|Superficial part of masseter.prueba: Sitting; ask the patient to close the mouth clenching the teeth and palpate the muscle; resistance at the chin against mandibular elevation.
mus|Superficial part of masseter.biomecanica: Elevation of the mandible (sagittal plane, frontal axis); slight protrusion (sagittal plane).

mus|Superficial transverse metacarpal li.accion: Transverse bundles of the palmar aponeurosis at the level of the metacarpal heads; they reinforce the palmar skin

mus|Superficial transverse metatarsal li.accion: Superficial transverse bundles of the plantar aponeurosis beneath the metatarsal heads

mus|Superior gemellus muscle.origen: External surface of the ischial spine
mus|Superior gemellus muscle.insercion: Medial surface of the greater trochanter with the tendon of the obturator internus
mus|Superior gemellus muscle.accion: Lateral rotation of the extended thigh; abduction of the flexed thigh; stabilizes the hip
mus|Superior gemellus muscle.prueba: Cannot be tested in isolation; assessed with the hip external rotators: sitting, knee at 90°, resistance at the medial surface of the ankle toward internal rotation.
mus|Superior gemellus muscle.biomecanica: External rotation of the hip (transverse plane, longitudinal axis); abduction with the hip flexed (transverse plane).

mus|Superior head of lateral pterygoid m.origen: Infratemporal surface and infratemporal crest of the greater wing of the sphenoid
mus|Superior head of lateral pterygoid m.insercion: Capsule and articular disc of the TMJ and pterygoid fovea
mus|Superior head of lateral pterygoid m.inervacion: Nerve to lateral pterygoid, from the mandibular n. (CN V3)
mus|Superior head of lateral pterygoid m.irrigacion: Pterygoid branches of the maxillary a.
mus|Superior head of lateral pterygoid m.accion: Stabilizes the articular disc during mandibular closing
mus|Superior head of lateral pterygoid m.clinica: Implicated in disc displacement in TMJ disorders.
mus|Superior head of lateral pterygoid m.prueba: Cannot be tested in isolation; assessed through TMJ function and intraoral palpation.
mus|Superior head of lateral pterygoid m.biomecanica: Stabilization of the disc and condyle of the TMJ during mandibular closing.

mus|Superior oblique muscle.origen: Body of the sphenoid, above and medial to the optic canal
mus|Superior oblique muscle.insercion: Sclera, posterosuperolateral quadrant, after passing through the trochlea
mus|Superior oblique muscle.accion: Intorsion, depression (maximal in adduction) and abduction of the eyeball
mus|Superior oblique muscle.clinica: Its paralysis causes vertical diplopia when going down stairs; compensatory head tilt.
mus|Superior oblique muscle.prueba: Ocular motility examination: look downward with the eye adducted (trochlear nerve).
mus|Superior oblique muscle.biomecanica: Intorsion (frontal plane, anteroposterior axis); depression (sagittal plane, transverse axis) and abduction of the eyeball (horizontal plane, vertical axis).

mus|Superior pharyngeal constrictor.origen: Pterygoid hamulus, pterygomandibular raphe, posterior end of the mylohyoid line and side of the tongue
mus|Superior pharyngeal constrictor.insercion: Pharyngeal raphe and pharyngeal tubercle of the occipital bone
mus|Superior pharyngeal constrictor.irrigacion: Ascending pharyngeal a. and ascending palatine a.
mus|Superior pharyngeal constrictor.accion: Constricts the nasopharynx and oropharynx during swallowing
mus|Superior pharyngeal constrictor.prueba: Cannot be tested manually; assessed with swallowing, the gag reflex and videofluoroscopy.
mus|Superior pharyngeal constrictor.biomecanica: Constriction of the nasopharynx during swallowing; contributes to velopharyngeal closure.

mus|Superior rectus muscle.insercion: Superior sclera, about 7–8 mm behind the limbus
mus|Superior rectus muscle.inervacion: Superior branch of the oculomotor n. (CN III)
mus|Superior rectus muscle.accion: Elevation (maximal in abduction), adduction and intorsion of the eyeball
mus|Superior rectus muscle.clinica: Assessed by asking the patient to look up and out.
mus|Superior rectus muscle.prueba: Ocular motility examination: look upward with the eye abducted (oculomotor nerve).
mus|Superior rectus muscle.biomecanica: Elevation (sagittal plane, transverse axis); adduction (horizontal plane, vertical axis) and intorsion of the eyeball.

mus|Superior tarsus.irrigacion: Palpebral arcades of the ophthalmic a.
mus|Superior tarsus.accion: Dense connective tissue plate that gives shape and support to the upper eyelid; contains tarsal glands
mus|Superior tarsus.clinica: It is everted to look for subpalpebral foreign bodies; obstruction of its glands causes chalazion.

mus|Supinator.origen: Lateral epicondyle, radial collateral and annular ligaments, supinator crest and fossa of the ulna
mus|Supinator.insercion: Lateral, posterior and anterior surfaces of the proximal third of the radius
mus|Supinator.inervacion: Deep branch of the radial n. (C6–C7)
mus|Supinator.irrigacion: Radial recurrent a. and recurrent interosseous a.
mus|Supinator.clinica: Compression of the posterior interosseous n. at the arcade of Frohse.
mus|Supinator.prueba: Sitting, elbow extended or flexed to the maximum, forearm pronated. Stabilize the humerus. Supinate. Grade 3: full range; 4-5: resistance at the distal forearm toward pronation.
mus|Supinator.biomecanica: Supination of the forearm (transverse plane, longitudinal axis).

mus|Supraspinatus muscle.insercion: Superior facet of the greater tubercle of the humerus
mus|Supraspinatus muscle.accion: Initiates abduction of the arm; stabilizes the humeral head (rotator cuff)
mus|Supraspinatus muscle.clinica: Most frequently injured tendon of the cuff; Jobe test (empty can).
mus|Supraspinatus muscle.prueba: Sitting, arm beside the trunk. Stabilize the scapula. Abduct the shoulder to 90° in the scapular plane (neutral rotation). Grade 3: no resistance; 4-5: resistance on the distal arm, proximal to the elbow, toward adduction.
mus|Supraspinatus muscle.biomecanica: Shoulder abduction (frontal/scapular plane, anteroposterior axis); coaptation of the humeral head.

mus|Temporalis muscle.insercion: Coronoid process and anterior border of the mandibular ramus
mus|Temporalis muscle.inervacion: Deep temporal nn., from the mandibular n. (CN V3)
mus|Temporalis muscle.irrigacion: Deep temporal aa. (maxillary a.) and middle temporal a.
mus|Temporalis muscle.accion: Elevation of the mandible; posterior fibers retract it
mus|Temporalis muscle.clinica: Palpated when clenching the teeth to assess the motor part of CN V.
mus|Temporalis muscle.prueba: Sitting; close the mouth clenching the teeth while palpating the temporal fossa; resistance at the chin against mandibular elevation.
mus|Temporalis muscle.biomecanica: Elevation (sagittal plane, frontal axis) and retraction of the mandible (posterior fibers).

mus|Temporoparietalis muscle.insercion: Lateral border of the epicranial aponeurosis
mus|Temporoparietalis muscle.inervacion: Temporal branches of the facial n. (CN VII)
mus|Temporoparietalis muscle.prueba: Functional facial assessment: observe scalp tension and ear movement when raising the eyebrows.
mus|Temporoparietalis muscle.biomecanica: Scalp tension and elevation of the ear.

mus|Tendon of extensor digitorum longus.es: Tendon of extensor digitorum longus m.
mus|Tendon of extensor digitorum longus.insercion: Extensor expansions of toes 2–5, on the middle and distal phalanges
mus|Tendon of extensor digitorum longus.accion: Extension of toes 2–5 and dorsiflexion of the ankle
mus|Tendon of extensor digitorum longus.clinica: Palpable on the dorsum of the foot, lateral to the tendon of the extensor hallucis longus.
mus|Tendon of extensor digitorum longus.prueba: Assessed with extension of toes 2-5 against resistance on the dorsum of the proximal phalanges, observing and palpating the tendon.
mus|Tendon of extensor digitorum longus.biomecanica: Transmits extension of the MTP joints of toes 2-5 (sagittal plane, frontal axis) and dorsiflexion of the ankle.

mus|Teres major muscle.origen: Posterior surface of the inferior angle of the scapula
mus|Teres major muscle.insercion: Medial lip of the intertubercular groove of the humerus
mus|Teres major muscle.irrigacion: Circumflex scapular a. and thoracodorsal a.
mus|Teres major muscle.accion: Adduction, medial rotation and extension of the humerus
mus|Teres major muscle.clinica: Its inferior border marks the transition from the axillary a. to the brachial a.
mus|Teres major muscle.prueba: Prone, hand resting on the lumbar region (extension, adduction and internal rotation). Stabilize the scapula. Raise the elbow toward the ceiling. Grade 3: no resistance; 4-5: resistance proximal to the elbow toward abduction and flexion.
mus|Teres major muscle.biomecanica: Extension (sagittal plane, frontal axis), adduction (frontal plane, anteroposterior axis) and internal rotation of the shoulder (transverse plane, longitudinal axis).

mus|Teres minor muscle.origen: Upper two thirds of the lateral border of the scapula
mus|Teres minor muscle.insercion: Inferior facet of the greater tubercle of the humerus
mus|Teres minor muscle.accion: Lateral rotation of the humerus; stabilizes the humeral head (rotator cuff)
mus|Teres minor muscle.clinica: Assessed with the Hornblower sign and resisted external rotation.
mus|Teres minor muscle.prueba: Prone, shoulder abducted 90°, elbow flexed 90°, forearm hanging. Stabilize the humerus. External rotation bringing the back of the hand toward the ceiling. Grade 3: no resistance; 4-5: resistance at the distal forearm toward internal rotation.
mus|Teres minor muscle.biomecanica: External rotation of the shoulder (transverse plane, longitudinal axis); posterior stabilization of the humeral head.

mus|Thyro-epiglottic part of thyro-aryte.origen: Internal surface of the thyroid cartilage, near the angle
mus|Thyro-epiglottic part of thyro-aryte.insercion: Lateral border of the epiglottis and aryepiglottic fold
mus|Thyro-epiglottic part of thyro-aryte.prueba: Cannot be tested manually; assessed by laryngoscopy and swallowing evaluation.
mus|Thyro-epiglottic part of thyro-aryte.biomecanica: Widens the laryngeal inlet and modifies the position of the epiglottis.

mus|Thyrohyoid muscle.origen: Oblique line of the thyroid cartilage
mus|Thyrohyoid muscle.insercion: Inferior border of the body and greater horn of the hyoid bone
mus|Thyrohyoid muscle.inervacion: C1 fibers carried by the hypoglossal n.
mus|Thyrohyoid muscle.accion: Depresses the hyoid bone; with the hyoid fixed, elevates the larynx
mus|Thyrohyoid muscle.prueba: Cannot be tested in isolation; assessed by palpation during swallowing.
mus|Thyrohyoid muscle.biomecanica: Depression of the hyoid or elevation of the larynx (sagittal plane, frontal axis).

mus|Tibialis anterior muscle.origen: Lateral condyle and upper half of the lateral surface of the tibia, interosseous membrane
mus|Tibialis anterior muscle.insercion: Medial and inferior surface of the medial cuneiform and base of the 1st metatarsal
mus|Tibialis anterior muscle.accion: Dorsiflexion and inversion of the foot
mus|Tibialis anterior muscle.clinica: Its weakness causes foot drop and steppage gait; affected in anterior compartment syndrome.
mus|Tibialis anterior muscle.prueba: Sitting, knee flexed. Stabilize the leg. Dorsiflexion and inversion of the ankle with toes relaxed. Grade 3: full range; 4-5: resistance at the dorsomedial foot toward plantar flexion and eversion.
mus|Tibialis anterior muscle.biomecanica: Dorsiflexion of the ankle (sagittal plane, frontal axis); inversion of the foot (frontal plane, anteroposterior axis).

mus|Tibialis posterior muscle.origen: Interosseous membrane and adjacent posterior surfaces of the tibia and fibula
mus|Tibialis posterior muscle.insercion: Tuberosity of the navicular, cuneiforms, cuboid and bases of metatarsals 2–4
mus|Tibialis posterior muscle.irrigacion: Posterior tibial a. and fibular a.
mus|Tibialis posterior muscle.accion: Plantar flexion and inversion of the foot; supports the medial longitudinal arch
mus|Tibialis posterior muscle.clinica: Its dysfunction is the most frequent cause of acquired adult flatfoot.
mus|Tibialis posterior muscle.prueba: Ipsilateral side-lying, ankle in slight plantar flexion. Stabilize the leg. Invert the foot. Grade 3: full range; 4-5: resistance at the medial border of the forefoot toward eversion and dorsiflexion.
mus|Tibialis posterior muscle.biomecanica: Inversion of the foot (frontal plane, anteroposterior axis); plantar flexion of the ankle (sagittal plane, frontal axis); support of the medial longitudinal arch.

mus|Transverse arytenoid muscle.origen: Posterior surface and lateral border of one arytenoid cartilage
mus|Transverse arytenoid muscle.insercion: Posterior surface and lateral border of the contralateral arytenoid
mus|Transverse arytenoid muscle.accion: Approximates the arytenoids and closes the intercartilaginous part of the glottis
mus|Transverse arytenoid muscle.clinica: The only unpaired intrinsic muscle of the larynx.
mus|Transverse arytenoid muscle.prueba: Cannot be tested manually; assessed by laryngoscopy (posterior glottic closure during phonation).
mus|Transverse arytenoid muscle.biomecanica: Approximation of the arytenoid cartilages; closure of the posterior glottis.

mus|Transverse head of adductor hallucis.origen: Plantar ligaments of the 3rd–5th metatarsophalangeal joints
mus|Transverse head of adductor hallucis.insercion: Lateral side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the great toe (lateral sesamoid)
mus|Transverse head of adductor hallucis.inervacion: Deep branch of the lateral plantar n. (S2–S3)
mus|Transverse head of adductor hallucis.accion: Adduction of the great toe; supports the transverse arch
mus|Transverse head of adductor hallucis.prueba: Difficult to isolate; adduction of the first toe toward the second with resistance at the medial border of the proximal phalanx.
mus|Transverse head of adductor hallucis.biomecanica: Adduction of the hallux (transverse plane of the foot, vertical axis); support of the transverse arch.

mus|Transverse head of adductor pollicis.origen: Anterior surface of the shaft of the 3rd metacarpal
mus|Transverse head of adductor pollicis.insercion: Medial side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the thumb (medial sesamoid)
mus|Transverse head of adductor pollicis.inervacion: Deep branch of the ulnar n. (C8–T1)
mus|Transverse head of adductor pollicis.clinica: Froment's sign in ulnar n. injury.
mus|Transverse head of adductor pollicis.prueba: Sitting, forearm pronated. Stabilize metacarpals 2-5. Adduct the thumb toward the palm. Grade 3: full range; 4-5: resistance at the medial border of the proximal phalanx toward abduction. Froment's sign.
mus|Transverse head of adductor pollicis.biomecanica: Adduction of the thumb at the trapeziometacarpal joint (sagittal plane of the hand, frontal axis).

mus|Transverse part of trapezius muscle.origen: Spinous processes of C7–T3 and supraspinous ligaments
mus|Transverse part of trapezius muscle.insercion: Medial border of the acromion and superior lip of the spine of the scapula
mus|Transverse part of trapezius muscle.inervacion: Accessory n. (CN XI); proprioceptive fibers from C3–C4
mus|Transverse part of trapezius muscle.prueba: Prone, shoulder abducted 90° in external rotation, elbow extended. Stabilize the thorax. Adduct the scapula by raising the arm horizontally. Grade 3: no resistance; 4-5: resistance at the distal arm toward the table.

mus|Transversus abdominis muscle.origen: Internal surface of costal cartilages 7–12, thoracolumbar fascia, iliac crest and lateral third of the inguinal ligament
mus|Transversus abdominis muscle.insercion: Linea alba, pubic crest and pectineal line (via the conjoint tendon)
mus|Transversus abdominis muscle.inervacion: Thoracoabdominal nn. (T7–T11), subcostal n. (T12), iliohypogastric and ilioinguinal nn. (L1)
mus|Transversus abdominis muscle.irrigacion: Inferior posterior intercostal aa., subcostal a., epigastric aa. and deep circumflex iliac a.
mus|Transversus abdominis muscle.accion: Compresses the abdominal contents; stabilizes the trunk
mus|Transversus abdominis muscle.clinica: Fascial plane for the TAP block of the abdominal wall.
mus|Transversus abdominis muscle.prueba: Cannot be tested with the manual scale; assessed with the abdominal drawing-in maneuver (pulling in the navel) in the supine/lying position, palpating medial to the ASIS or with pressure biofeedback.
mus|Transversus abdominis muscle.biomecanica: Compression of the abdominal contents and increase of intra-abdominal pressure; lumbopelvic stabilization; forced expiration.

mus|Transversus thoracis muscle.origen: Posterior surface of the lower part of the sternum and xiphoid process
mus|Transversus thoracis muscle.prueba: Cannot be tested in isolation; assessed with forced expiration.
mus|Transversus thoracis muscle.biomecanica: Depression of costal cartilages II-VI (sagittal plane, frontal axis); expiratory accessory muscle.

mus|Trochlea of superior oblique muscle.es: Trochlea of the superior oblique m.
mus|Trochlea of superior oblique muscle.accion: Fibrocartilaginous pulley attached to the trochlear fovea of the frontal bone; redirects the tendon of the superior oblique
mus|Trochlea of superior oblique muscle.clinica: Its inflammation (trochleitis) produces superomedial orbital pain.
mus|Trochlea of superior oblique muscle.biomecanica: Fibrocartilaginous pulley that redirects the pull of the superior oblique backward and laterally.

mus|Ulnar head of extensor carpi ulnaris.es: Extensor carpi ulnaris m., ulnar head
mus|Ulnar head of extensor carpi ulnaris.la: Caput ulnare musculi extensoris carpi ulnaris
mus|Ulnar head of extensor carpi ulnaris.origen: Posterior border of the ulna (via aponeurosis)
mus|Ulnar head of extensor carpi ulnaris.inervacion: Posterior interosseous n., from the radial n. (C7–C8)
mus|Ulnar head of extensor carpi ulnaris.accion: Extension and adduction (ulnar deviation) of the wrist
mus|Ulnar head of extensor carpi ulnaris.prueba: Sitting, forearm pronated. Stabilize the forearm. Extend the wrist with ulnar deviation. Grade 3: full range; 4-5: resistance on the dorsum of the 5th metacarpal toward flexion and radial deviation.
mus|Ulnar head of extensor carpi ulnaris.biomecanica: Wrist extension (sagittal plane, frontal axis); ulnar deviation (frontal plane, anteroposterior axis).

mus|Ulnar head of flexor carpi ulnaris.es: Flexor carpi ulnaris m., ulnar head
mus|Ulnar head of flexor carpi ulnaris.la: Caput ulnare musculi flexoris carpi ulnaris
mus|Ulnar head of flexor carpi ulnaris.origen: Medial border of the olecranon and upper two thirds of the posterior border of the ulna
mus|Ulnar head of flexor carpi ulnaris.insercion: Pisiform, hook of the hamate and base of the 5th metacarpal
mus|Ulnar head of flexor carpi ulnaris.irrigacion: Posterior ulnar recurrent a. and ulnar a.
mus|Ulnar head of flexor carpi ulnaris.accion: Flexion and adduction of the wrist
mus|Ulnar head of flexor carpi ulnaris.clinica: The ulnar n. passes between its heads: site of cubital tunnel syndrome.
mus|Ulnar head of flexor carpi ulnaris.prueba: Sitting, forearm supinated. Stabilize the forearm. Flex the wrist with ulnar deviation. Grade 3: full range; 4-5: resistance at the hypothenar eminence toward extension and radial deviation.
mus|Ulnar head of flexor carpi ulnaris.biomecanica: Wrist flexion (sagittal plane, frontal axis); ulnar deviation (frontal plane, anteroposterior axis).

mus|Vastus intermedius muscle.origen: Anterior and lateral surfaces of the upper two thirds of the femoral shaft
mus|Vastus intermedius muscle.insercion: Base of the patella and, via the patellar ligament, the tibial tuberosity
mus|Vastus intermedius muscle.irrigacion: Lateral circumflex femoral a. and deep femoral a.
mus|Vastus intermedius muscle.prueba: Sitting at the edge of the table, knee flexed. Stabilize the thigh. Extend the knee without locking it. Grade 3: full range; 4-5: resistance at the anterior surface of the distal leg toward flexion.

mus|Vastus lateralis muscle.origen: Greater trochanter and lateral lip of the linea aspera of the femur
mus|Vastus lateralis muscle.insercion: Base and lateral border of the patella; tibial tuberosity via the patellar ligament
mus|Vastus lateralis muscle.clinica: Usual site of intramuscular injection in infants and of muscle biopsy.
mus|Vastus lateralis muscle.prueba: Sitting at the edge of the table, knee flexed. Stabilize the thigh. Extend the knee without locking it. Grade 3: full range; 4-5: resistance at the anterior surface of the distal leg toward flexion.
mus|Vastus lateralis muscle.biomecanica: Knee extension (sagittal plane, frontal axis); lateral pull on the patella.

mus|Vastus medialis muscle.origen: Intertrochanteric line and medial lip of the linea aspera of the femur
mus|Vastus medialis muscle.insercion: Base and medial border of the patella; tibial tuberosity via the patellar ligament
mus|Vastus medialis muscle.irrigacion: Femoral a. and deep femoral a.
mus|Vastus medialis muscle.accion: Knee extension; its oblique fibers stabilize the patella medially
mus|Vastus medialis muscle.clinica: Its weakness favors lateral patellar tracking and patellofemoral pain.
mus|Vastus medialis muscle.prueba: Sitting at the edge of the table, knee flexed. Stabilize the thigh. Extend the knee, emphasizing the last degrees. Grade 3: full range; 4-5: resistance at the anterior surface of the distal leg toward flexion.
mus|Vastus medialis muscle.biomecanica: Knee extension (sagittal plane, frontal axis); medial stabilization of the patella (oblique fibers).

mus|Ventral parts of lateral intertransv.es: Lateral lumbar intertransversarii mm., anterior parts
mus|Ventral parts of lateral intertransv.la: Partes anteriores musculorum intertransversariorum lateralium lumborum
mus|Ventral parts of lateral intertransv.origen: Transverse process of a lumbar vertebra
mus|Ventral parts of lateral intertransv.insercion: Transverse process of the adjacent superior lumbar vertebra
mus|Ventral parts of lateral intertransv.inervacion: Anterior rami of lumbar spinal nerves
mus|Ventral parts of lateral intertransv.accion: Lateral flexion of the lumbar spine; segmental stabilization
mus|Ventral parts of lateral intertransv.prueba: Cannot be tested in isolation; assessed with lateral flexion of the trunk.
mus|Ventral parts of lateral intertransv.biomecanica: Ipsilateral lateral flexion of the lumbar spine (frontal plane, anteroposterior axis); segmental stabilization.

mus|Zygomaticus major muscle.origen: Lateral surface of the zygomatic bone
mus|Zygomaticus major muscle.insercion: Modiolus and skin of the angle of the mouth
mus|Zygomaticus major muscle.inervacion: Zygomatic and buccal branches of the facial n. (CN VII)
mus|Zygomaticus major muscle.accion: Elevates and draws the corner of the lips laterally (smile)
mus|Zygomaticus major muscle.clinica: Assessed by asking the patient to smile in facial paralysis.
mus|Zygomaticus major muscle.prueba: Functional facial assessment: ask for a broad smile raising the corner of the lips upward and outward; observe symmetry.
mus|Zygomaticus major muscle.biomecanica: Elevation and lateral movement of the corner of the lips (smile).

mus|Zygomaticus minor muscle.origen: Anterior surface of the zygomatic bone
mus|Zygomaticus minor muscle.insercion: Skin and musculature of the upper lip, lateral to the levator labii superioris
mus|Zygomaticus minor muscle.inervacion: Zygomatic and buccal branches of the facial n. (CN VII)
mus|Zygomaticus minor muscle.accion: Elevates the upper lip and deepens the nasolabial fold
mus|Zygomaticus minor muscle.prueba: Functional facial assessment: ask the patient to raise the upper lip showing the upper teeth; observe symmetry.
mus|Zygomaticus minor muscle.biomecanica: Elevation of the upper lip; deepens the nasolabial fold.

lig|Acetabular labrum.une: Rim of the acetabulum, completed inferiorly by the transverse acetabular ligament
lig|Acetabular labrum.funcion: Deepens the acetabulum, seals the joint and increases the stability of the femoral head
lig|Acetabular labrum.clinica: Tears are associated with femoroacetabular impingement; positive FADIR test with groin pain.

lig|Acromioclavicular ligament.une: Acromial end of the clavicle → acromion
lig|Acromioclavicular ligament.funcion: Reinforces the superior capsule and limits anteroposterior horizontal displacement of the clavicle
lig|Acromioclavicular ligament.clinica: First ligament injured in acromioclavicular dislocation (Rockwood classification).

lig|Annular ligament of radius.une: Anterior border → posterior border of the radial notch of the ulna, encircling the head of the radius
lig|Annular ligament of radius.funcion: Holds the head of the radius against the ulna while allowing pronation-supination
lig|Annular ligament of radius.clinica: Painful pronation (nursemaid's elbow): subluxation of the radial head under the ligament due to traction in children.

lig|Anterior cruciate ligament.une: Anterior intercondylar area of the tibia → medial surface of the lateral condyle of the femur
lig|Anterior cruciate ligament.funcion: Prevents anterior displacement of the tibia relative to the femur and limits internal rotation
lig|Anterior cruciate ligament.clinica: Frequently ruptured in pivoting sports; Lachman, anterior drawer and pivot shift tests.

lig|Anterior ligament of fibular head.es: Anterior ligament of the head of the fibula
lig|Anterior ligament of fibular head.une: Anterior surface of the head of the fibula → lateral condyle of the tibia
lig|Anterior ligament of fibular head.funcion: Reinforces the capsule of the proximal tibiofibular joint anteriorly

lig|Anterior longitudinal ligament.une: Occipital bone and anterior tubercle of the atlas → anterior surface of the vertebral bodies down to the sacrum
lig|Anterior longitudinal ligament.funcion: Limits extension of the spine and reinforces the discs anteriorly
lig|Anterior longitudinal ligament.clinica: Its ossification appears in diffuse idiopathic skeletal hyperostosis (DISH); injured in whiplash.

lig|Anterior meniscotibial ligament (Lat.une: Anterior horn of the lateral meniscus → anterior intercondylar area of the tibia
lig|Anterior meniscotibial ligament (Lat.funcion: Anchors the anterior horn of the lateral meniscus to the tibia

lig|Anterior meniscotibial ligament (Med.une: Anterior horn of the medial meniscus → anterior intercondylar area of the tibia
lig|Anterior meniscotibial ligament (Med.funcion: Anchors the anterior horn of the medial meniscus to the tibia

lig|Anterior sacro-iliac ligament.une: Pelvic surface of the sacrum → ilium (preauricular surface)
lig|Anterior sacro-iliac ligament.funcion: Reinforces the sacroiliac capsule anteriorly; it is the weakest of the sacroiliac ligaments
lig|Anterior sacro-iliac ligament.clinica: Ruptured in open-book pelvic fractures (anteroposterior compression).

lig|Anterior sternoclavicular ligament.une: Sternal end of the clavicle → anterior surface of the manubrium of the sternum
lig|Anterior sternoclavicular ligament.funcion: Reinforces the anterior capsule and limits anterior displacement of the clavicle
lig|Anterior sternoclavicular ligament.clinica: Anterior sternoclavicular dislocation is more frequent and more benign than posterior dislocation.

lig|Anterior talocalcaneal ligament.une: Neck of the talus → superior surface of the calcaneus

lig|Anterior talofibular ligament.une: Lateral malleolus → neck of the talus
lig|Anterior talofibular ligament.funcion: Limits inversion and anterior displacement of the talus in plantar flexion
lig|Anterior talofibular ligament.clinica: Most frequently injured ligament in ankle sprain; anterior drawer test.

lig|Anterior tibiofibular ligament.une: Anterior border of the fibular notch of the tibia → lateral malleolus
lig|Anterior tibiofibular ligament.funcion: Maintains the syndesmosis and the integrity of the tibiofibular mortise
lig|Anterior tibiofibular ligament.clinica: Injured in high ankle sprain; squeeze test and external rotation test.

lig|Arcuate popliteal ligament.une: Head of the fibula → posterior capsule, arching over the tendon of the popliteus
lig|Arcuate popliteal ligament.funcion: Reinforces the posterolateral corner of the capsule and limits external rotation and varus
lig|Arcuate popliteal ligament.clinica: Part of the posterolateral complex; its injury causes posterolateral rotatory instability (dial test).

lig|Articular capsule of acromioclavicul.es: Articular capsule of the acromioclavicular joint
lig|Articular capsule of acromioclavicul.une: Acromial end of the clavicle → acromion
lig|Articular capsule of acromioclavicul.funcion: Encloses the joint and limits horizontal displacements of the clavicle
lig|Articular capsule of acromioclavicul.clinica: Injured in acromioclavicular separation; pain on cross-body adduction (cross-body test).

lig|Articular capsule of elbow joint.es: Articular capsule of the elbow joint
lig|Articular capsule of elbow joint.une: Distal humerus → proximal ulna and annular ligament of the radius
lig|Articular capsule of elbow joint.funcion: Encloses the humeroulnar, humeroradial and proximal radioulnar joints; lax anteriorly and posteriorly
lig|Articular capsule of elbow joint.clinica: Post-traumatic capsular stiffness is frequent; effusion elevates the fat pads on radiographs.

lig|Articular capsule of glenohumeral jo.es: Articular capsule of the glenohumeral joint
lig|Articular capsule of glenohumeral jo.une: Rim of the glenoid cavity and labrum → anatomical neck of the humerus
lig|Articular capsule of glenohumeral jo.funcion: Lax, allows great mobility; reinforced by glenohumeral ligaments and the rotator cuff
lig|Articular capsule of glenohumeral jo.clinica: Adhesive capsulitis (frozen shoulder) limits active and passive external rotation.

lig|Articular capsule of hip joint.es: Articular capsule of the hip joint
lig|Articular capsule of hip joint.une: Rim of the acetabulum → intertrochanteric line anteriorly and femoral neck posteriorly
lig|Articular capsule of hip joint.funcion: Strong and reinforced by the iliofemoral, pubofemoral and ischiofemoral ligaments
lig|Articular capsule of hip joint.clinica: Intracapsular fractures of the femoral neck can interrupt the retinacular arteries and cause avascular necrosis.

lig|Articular capsule of interphalangeal.es: Articular capsule of the interphalangeal joint of the great toe
lig|Articular capsule of interphalangeal.articulacion: Interphalangeal joint of the great toe
lig|Articular capsule of interphalangeal.une: Proximal phalanx → distal phalanx of the great toe
lig|Articular capsule of interphalangeal.funcion: Encloses the hinge joint; reinforced by collateral and plantar ligaments

lig|Articular capsule of knee joint.es: Articular capsule of the knee joint
lig|Articular capsule of knee joint.une: Distal femur → proximal tibia, incorporating the patella anteriorly
lig|Articular capsule of knee joint.funcion: Encloses the joint; reinforced by the patellar retinacula, popliteal and collateral ligaments
lig|Articular capsule of knee joint.clinica: Joint effusion is detected by the patellar tap (ballottement) or the sweep (bulge) sign.

lig|Articular capsule of radiocarpal joi.es: Articular capsule of the radiocarpal joint
lig|Articular capsule of radiocarpal joi.une: Distal radius and articular disc → proximal row of the carpus
lig|Articular capsule of radiocarpal joi.funcion: Encloses the joint; reinforced by radiocarpal and ulnocarpal ligaments
lig|Articular capsule of radiocarpal joi.clinica: Dorsal wrist ganglia usually originate from the capsule near the scapholunate ligament.

lig|Articular capsule of sternoclavicula.es: Articular capsule of the sternoclavicular joint
lig|Articular capsule of sternoclavicula.une: Sternal end of the clavicle → manubrium of the sternum and first costal cartilage
lig|Articular capsule of sternoclavicula.funcion: Encloses the joint; reinforced by the anterior and posterior sternoclavicular ligaments
lig|Articular capsule of sternoclavicula.clinica: Posterior dislocation can compress the trachea, esophagus or great vessels; it is an emergency.

lig|Articular capsule of superior tibiof.es: Articular capsule of the proximal tibiofibular joint
lig|Articular capsule of superior tibiof.une: Head of the fibula → lateral condyle of the tibia
lig|Articular capsule of superior tibiof.funcion: Encloses the plane joint; reinforced by the anterior and posterior ligaments of the head of the fibula

lig|Articular capsule of temporomandibul.es: Articular capsule of the temporomandibular joint
lig|Articular capsule of temporomandibul.une: Articular tubercle and mandibular fossa of the temporal bone → neck of the mandible
lig|Articular capsule of temporomandibul.funcion: Lax, attaches to the articular disc; reinforced laterally by the lateral ligament
lig|Articular capsule of temporomandibul.clinica: In anterior dislocation the condyle lies in front of the articular eminence and the mouth cannot close.

lig|Articular capsules of distal interph.es: Articular capsules of the distal interphalangeal joints of the hand
lig|Articular capsules of distal interph.la: Capsulae articulares articulationum interphalangearum distalium manus
lig|Articular capsules of distal interph.articulacion: Distal interphalangeal joints of the hand
lig|Articular capsules of distal interph.funcion: Enclose the joints; reinforced by collateral ligaments and the palmar plate
lig|Articular capsules of distal interph.clinica: Heberden's nodes of osteoarthritis appear at these joints.

lig|Articular capsules of distal interph.es: Articular capsules of the distal interphalangeal joints of the foot
lig|Articular capsules of distal interph.la: Capsulae articulares articulationum interphalangearum distalium pedis
lig|Articular capsules of distal interph.articulacion: Distal interphalangeal joints of the foot
lig|Articular capsules of distal interph.une: Middle phalanx → distal phalanx of toes 2–5
lig|Articular capsules of distal interph.funcion: Enclose the joints; reinforced by collateral and plantar ligaments
lig|Articular capsules of distal interph.clinica: Flexion contracture of this joint participates in mallet toe or hammer toe.

lig|Articular capsules of metacarpophala.es: Articular capsules of the metacarpophalangeal joints
lig|Articular capsules of metacarpophala.une: Head of the metacarpal → base of the proximal phalanx
lig|Articular capsules of metacarpophala.funcion: Enclose the joints; reinforced by collateral ligaments and the palmar plate
lig|Articular capsules of metacarpophala.clinica: Immobilizing in flexion prevents shortening of the collateral ligaments (intrinsic-plus position).

lig|Articular capsules of metatarsophala.es: Articular capsules of the metatarsophalangeal joints
lig|Articular capsules of metatarsophala.une: Head of the metatarsal → base of the proximal phalanx
lig|Articular capsules of metatarsophala.funcion: Enclose the joints; reinforced by collateral ligaments and the plantar plate
lig|Articular capsules of metatarsophala.clinica: Injury to the plantar capsule of the first joint produces turf toe.

lig|Articular capsules of proximal inter.es: Articular capsules of the proximal interphalangeal joints of the hand
lig|Articular capsules of proximal inter.la: Capsulae articulares articulationum interphalangearum proximalium manus
lig|Articular capsules of proximal inter.articulacion: Proximal interphalangeal joints of the hand
lig|Articular capsules of proximal inter.funcion: Enclose the joints; reinforced by collateral ligaments and the palmar plate
lig|Articular capsules of proximal inter.clinica: Bouchard's nodes of osteoarthritis appear at these joints.

lig|Articular capsules of proximal inter.es: Articular capsules of the proximal interphalangeal joints of the foot
lig|Articular capsules of proximal inter.la: Capsulae articulares articulationum interphalangearum proximalium pedis
lig|Articular capsules of proximal inter.articulacion: Proximal interphalangeal joints of the foot
lig|Articular capsules of proximal inter.une: Proximal phalanx → middle phalanx of toes 2–5
lig|Articular capsules of proximal inter.funcion: Enclose the joints; reinforced by collateral and plantar ligaments
lig|Articular capsules of proximal inter.clinica: Flexion contracture of this joint characterizes hammer toe.

lig|Articular disc of acromioclavicular.es: Articular disc of the acromioclavicular joint
lig|Articular disc of acromioclavicular.une: Between the acromial end of the clavicle and the acromion
lig|Articular disc of acromioclavicular.funcion: Improves joint congruence; inconstant and incomplete
lig|Articular disc of acromioclavicular.clinica: Degenerates early, contributing to acromioclavicular osteoarthritis.

lig|Articular disc of distal radio-ulnar.es: Articular disc of the distal radioulnar joint
lig|Articular disc of distal radio-ulnar.une: Ulnar border of the distal radius → base of the styloid process of the ulna
lig|Articular disc of distal radio-ulnar.funcion: Main stabilizer of the distal radioulnar joint; separates this joint from the radiocarpal joint
lig|Articular disc of distal radio-ulnar.clinica: Central component of the triangular fibrocartilage complex (TFCC); its injury causes ulnar-sided wrist pain.

lig|Articular disc of sternoclavicular j.es: Articular disc of the sternoclavicular joint
lig|Articular disc of sternoclavicular j.une: Superior border of the clavicle → first costal cartilage
lig|Articular disc of sternoclavicular j.funcion: Divides the joint into two cavities and prevents medial displacement of the clavicle

lig|Articular disc of temporomandibular.es: Articular disc of the temporomandibular joint
lig|Articular disc of temporomandibular.une: Between the mandibular condyle and the mandibular fossa; attached to the lateral pterygoid
lig|Articular disc of temporomandibular.funcion: Divides the joint into superior (gliding) and inferior (rotation) compartments
lig|Articular disc of temporomandibular.clinica: Anterior displacement of the disc produces joint clicking and may cause locking of mouth opening.

lig|Calcaneocuboid ligament.une: Calcaneus → dorsal surface of the cuboid; lateral fascicle of the bifurcate ligament
lig|Calcaneocuboid ligament.clinica: May be injured in inversion sprains together with the bifurcate ligament.

lig|Calcaneofibular ligament.une: Apex of the lateral malleolus → lateral surface of the calcaneus
lig|Calcaneofibular ligament.funcion: Limits inversion, especially with the ankle in dorsiflexion
lig|Calcaneofibular ligament.clinica: Second ligament injured in lateral ankle sprain; talar tilt test.

lig|Calcaneonavicular ligament.une: Calcaneus → dorsolateral surface of the navicular; medial fascicle of the bifurcate ligament
lig|Calcaneonavicular ligament.funcion: Joins the calcaneus and navicular, stabilizing the midfoot dorsally

lig|Capitohamate interosseous ligament.funcion: Stabilizes the distal carpal row as a rigid unit

lig|Collateral interphalangeal ligaments.es: Collateral interphalangeal ligaments of the foot
lig|Collateral interphalangeal ligaments.une: Head of the proximal or middle phalanx → base of the next phalanx
lig|Collateral interphalangeal ligaments.funcion: Limit lateral deviations (varus-valgus) of the interphalangeal joints

lig|Collateral interphalangeal ligaments.es: Collateral interphalangeal ligaments of the hand
lig|Collateral interphalangeal ligaments.une: Head of the proximal or middle phalanx → base of the next phalanx
lig|Collateral interphalangeal ligaments.funcion: Limit radial and ulnar deviations; taut in extension
lig|Collateral interphalangeal ligaments.clinica: Frequent sprains in ball sports; assessed with varus and valgus stress.

lig|Collateral metacarpophalangeal ligam.une: Head of the metacarpal → base of the proximal phalanx
lig|Collateral metacarpophalangeal ligam.funcion: Limit abduction-adduction; taut in flexion because of the shape of the metacarpal head
lig|Collateral metacarpophalangeal ligam.clinica: Rupture of the ulnar collateral ligament of the thumb: skier's or gamekeeper's thumb (Stener lesion).

lig|Collateral metatarsophalangeal ligam.une: Head of the metatarsal → base of the proximal phalanx
lig|Collateral metatarsophalangeal ligam.funcion: Limit lateral deviations of the toes
lig|Collateral metatarsophalangeal ligam.clinica: Their insufficiency contributes to deformities such as hallux valgus and crossover toe.

lig|Conoid ligament.une: Base of the coracoid process → conoid tubercle of the clavicle
lig|Conoid ligament.funcion: Medial part of the coracoclavicular ligament; prevents superior displacement of the clavicle
lig|Conoid ligament.clinica: Its rupture in grade III or higher acromioclavicular dislocations produces the piano key sign.

lig|Coraco-acromial ligament.funcion: Forms the coracoacromial arch with the acromion and coracoid, which prevents superior displacement of the humeral head
lig|Coraco-acromial ligament.clinica: Implicated in subacromial syndrome; it is divided or released in acromioplasty.

lig|Coracohumeral ligament.une: Base of the coracoid process → greater and lesser tubercles of the humerus
lig|Coracohumeral ligament.funcion: Reinforces the superior capsule and limits external rotation and inferior translation
lig|Coracohumeral ligament.clinica: Thickened and contracted in adhesive capsulitis, in the rotator interval.

lig|Costoclavicular ligament.une: First rib and its cartilage → costoclavicular ligament impression of the clavicle
lig|Costoclavicular ligament.funcion: Main sternoclavicular stabilizer; limits elevation of the clavicle
lig|Costoclavicular ligament.clinica: Serves as a fulcrum in clavicular movements; key to stability after sternoclavicular dislocations.

lig|Costotransverse ligament.une: Neck of the rib → transverse process of the corresponding vertebra
lig|Costotransverse ligament.funcion: Stabilizes the costotransverse joint during respiratory movements

lig|Cricopharyngeal ligament.une: Corniculate cartilage → lamina of the cricoid cartilage and pharyngeal mucosa
lig|Cricopharyngeal ligament.funcion: Inferior continuation of the intercorniculate ligament; fixes the laryngeal cartilages posteriorly

lig|Cuneocuboid interosseous ligament.funcion: Main connection between the lateral cuneiform and the cuboid; stabilizes the transverse arch

lig|Cuneometatarsal interosseous ligamen.une: Cuneiforms → bases of the metatarsals; the medial one includes the Lisfranc ligament
lig|Cuneometatarsal interosseous ligamen.funcion: Stabilize the Lisfranc joint; the medial one connects the medial cuneiform and the base of the 2nd metatarsal
lig|Cuneometatarsal interosseous ligamen.clinica: Rupture of the Lisfranc ligament produces tarsometatarsal instability, often underdiagnosed.

lig|Deep part of tibial collateral ligam.es: Deep part of the tibial collateral ligament
lig|Deep part of tibial collateral ligam.une: Medial epicondyle of the femur → proximal tibia, attached to the medial meniscus (meniscofemoral and meniscotibial ligaments)
lig|Deep part of tibial collateral ligam.funcion: Secondary valgus stabilizer; anchors the medial meniscus to the capsule
lig|Deep part of tibial collateral ligam.clinica: Its attachment to the medial meniscus explains the unhappy triad (ACL, medial collateral ligament and medial meniscus).

lig|Deep transverse metacarpal ligament.une: Palmar plates of the 2nd to 5th metacarpophalangeal joints to one another
lig|Deep transverse metacarpal ligament.funcion: Holds the metacarpal heads together and limits their separation
lig|Deep transverse metacarpal ligament.clinica: The lumbricals pass palmar and the interossei dorsal to it; a landmark in hand surgery.

lig|Deep transverse metatarsal ligament.une: Plantar plates of the five metatarsophalangeal joints to one another
lig|Deep transverse metatarsal ligament.funcion: Holds the metatarsal heads and the anterior transverse arch together
lig|Deep transverse metatarsal ligament.clinica: Morton's neuroma forms on the plantar digital nerve beneath this ligament; it is released surgically.

lig|Descending part of iliofemoral ligam.es: Descending part of the iliofemoral ligament
lig|Descending part of iliofemoral ligam.une: Anterior inferior iliac spine → inferior part of the intertrochanteric line
lig|Descending part of iliofemoral ligam.funcion: Medial limb of the Y-shaped ligament; limits hyperextension of the hip

lig|Dorsal calcaneocuboid ligament.une: Dorsal surface of the calcaneus → dorsal surface of the cuboid

lig|Dorsal carpometacarpal ligaments.une: Bones of the distal carpal row → bases of metacarpals 2–5

lig|Dorsal cuboideonavicular ligament.une: Dorsal surface of the cuboid → dorsal surface of the navicular
lig|Dorsal cuboideonavicular ligament.funcion: Reinforces the connection between the cuboid and navicular dorsally

lig|Dorsal cuneocuboid ligament.une: Dorsal surface of the lateral cuneiform → dorsal surface of the cuboid

lig|Dorsal cuneonavicular ligaments.une: Dorsal surface of the navicular → dorsal surface of the three cuneiforms

lig|Dorsal intercarpal ligaments.une: Dorsal surfaces of adjacent carpal bones; mainly triquetrum → scaphoid and trapezium
lig|Dorsal intercarpal ligaments.funcion: Stabilize the carpus and the proximal row dorsally
lig|Dorsal intercarpal ligaments.clinica: Contribute to secondary scapholunate stability; implicated in carpal instabilities.

lig|Dorsal intercuneiform ligaments.une: Dorsal surfaces of adjacent cuneiforms to one another
lig|Dorsal intercuneiform ligaments.funcion: Reinforce the intercuneiform joints and the transverse arch dorsally

lig|Dorsal metacarpal ligaments.une: Dorsal surfaces of the bases of adjacent metacarpals 2–5
lig|Dorsal metacarpal ligaments.funcion: Connect the bases of the metacarpals dorsally

lig|Dorsal metatarsal ligaments.une: Dorsal surfaces of the bases of adjacent metatarsals 2–5
lig|Dorsal metatarsal ligaments.funcion: Connect the bases of the metatarsals dorsally

lig|Dorsal radio-ulnar ligament.une: Dorsal margin of the ulnar notch of the radius → head and styloid process of the ulna
lig|Dorsal radio-ulnar ligament.funcion: Stabilizes the distal radioulnar joint; part of the triangular fibrocartilage complex
lig|Dorsal radio-ulnar ligament.clinica: Its injury causes distal radioulnar instability; ulnar piano key test.

lig|Dorsal radiocarpal ligament.une: Dorsal margin of the distal radius → lunate and triquetrum
lig|Dorsal radiocarpal ligament.funcion: Limits palmar flexion and ulnar slide of the carpus
lig|Dorsal radiocarpal ligament.clinica: Secondary stabilizer in scapholunate and lunotriquetral instability.

lig|Dorsal scaphotriquetral ligament.une: Triquetrum → scaphoid (dorsally), part of the dorsal intercarpal ligament
lig|Dorsal scaphotriquetral ligament.funcion: Stabilizes the proximal carpal row dorsally

lig|Dorsal tarsometatarsal ligaments.une: Cuneiforms and cuboid → bases of the metatarsals
lig|Dorsal tarsometatarsal ligaments.clinica: They are weaker than the plantar ones, so Lisfranc dislocation is usually dorsal.

lig|Dorsal ulnocarpal ligament.une: Distal ulna and articular disc → triquetrum and lunate
lig|Dorsal ulnocarpal ligament.funcion: Reinforces the ulnar side of the carpus dorsally

lig|External intercostal membrane.une: Adjacent ribs, from the costochondral junctions to the sternum
lig|External intercostal membrane.funcion: Replaces the external intercostal muscle anteriorly, closing the intercostal space

lig|Fibular collateral ligament.une: Lateral epicondyle of the femur → head of the fibula
lig|Fibular collateral ligament.funcion: Limits varus of the knee; extracapsular, separate from the lateral meniscus
lig|Fibular collateral ligament.clinica: Examined with varus stress at 30° of flexion; its injury may be associated with injury to the common fibular nerve.

lig|Frenula capsulae.une: Synovial folds of the capsule reflected onto the neck of the femur
lig|Frenula capsulae.funcion: Capsular folds (retinacula) along which vessels run to the femoral head

lig|Glenoid labrum.une: Rim of the glenoid cavity; superiorly it blends with the tendon of the long head of the biceps
lig|Glenoid labrum.funcion: Deepens the glenoid cavity and increases stability of the humeral head
lig|Glenoid labrum.clinica: Bankart lesion (anteroinferior) in anterior dislocation; SLAP lesion in the superior labrum.

lig|Iliolumbar ligament.une: Transverse process of L5 → posterior iliac crest and ala of the sacrum
lig|Iliolumbar ligament.funcion: Stabilizes L5 on the sacrum and limits its anterior displacement and rotation
lig|Iliolumbar ligament.clinica: Its avulsion together with the transverse process of L5 indicates an unstable pelvic fracture.

lig|Inferior glenohumeral ligament.une: Anteroinferior glenoid labrum → anatomical neck of the humerus
lig|Inferior glenohumeral ligament.funcion: Main anterior stabilizer in abduction and external rotation
lig|Inferior glenohumeral ligament.clinica: Injured in anterior shoulder dislocation; apprehension and relocation test.

lig|Inferior pubic ligament.une: Inferior rami of both pubic bones, arching beneath the symphysis
lig|Inferior pubic ligament.funcion: Reinforces the symphysis inferiorly and rounds off the pubic arch

lig|Inferior transverse scapular ligamen.une: Lateral border of the spine of the scapula → posterior border of the glenoid cavity
lig|Inferior transverse scapular ligamen.funcion: Forms an opening for the suprascapular nerve and vessels in the spinoglenoid notch
lig|Inferior transverse scapular ligamen.clinica: May compress the suprascapular nerve, with isolated atrophy of infraspinatus.

lig|Infrapatellar fat pad.une: Between the patellar ligament, capsule and synovial membrane, beneath the patella
lig|Infrapatellar fat pad.funcion: Cushions and fills the anterior joint space during flexion-extension
lig|Infrapatellar fat pad.clinica: Its inflammation (Hoffa's disease) causes anterior knee pain.

lig|Interclavicular ligament.une: Sternal end of one clavicle → the contralateral one, over the jugular notch
lig|Interclavicular ligament.funcion: Reinforces the sternoclavicular capsules superiorly and limits depression of the clavicle

lig|Intercornual ligament.une: Cornua of the sacrum → cornua of the coccyx

lig|Intercuneiform interosseous ligament.funcion: Firmly bind the cuneiforms together and maintain the transverse arch

lig|Internal intercostal membrane.une: Adjacent ribs, from the costal angles to the vertebral column
lig|Internal intercostal membrane.funcion: Replaces the internal intercostal muscle posteriorly, closing the intercostal space

lig|Interosseous membrane of forearm.une: Interosseous border of the radius → interosseous border of the ulna
lig|Interosseous membrane of forearm.funcion: Transmits loads from the radius to the ulna and gives origin to forearm muscles
lig|Interosseous membrane of forearm.clinica: Its rupture is part of the Essex-Lopresti injury with proximal migration of the radius.

lig|Interosseous membrane of leg.une: Interosseous border of the tibia → interosseous border of the fibula
lig|Interosseous membrane of leg.funcion: Binds tibia and fibula, separates compartments and gives origin to muscles
lig|Interosseous membrane of leg.clinica: Its high rupture is associated with the Maisonneuve fracture.

lig|Interosseous metacarpal ligaments.une: Opposing surfaces of the bases of metacarpals 2–5
lig|Interosseous metacarpal ligaments.funcion: Firmly bind the metacarpal bases to one another

lig|Interosseous sacro-iliac ligament.funcion: Strongest ligament of the sacroiliac joint; transmits trunk weight to the pelvis
lig|Interosseous sacro-iliac ligament.clinica: Its rupture indicates complete posterior pelvic instability.

lig|Interpubic disc.une: Symphyseal surfaces of both pubic bones
lig|Interpubic disc.funcion: Joins the pubic bones and cushions loads; relaxes during pregnancy
lig|Interpubic disc.clinica: Symphyseal diastasis may occur in childbirth; osteitis pubis in athletes.

lig|Intersesamoid ligament.une: Medial sesamoid → lateral sesamoid of the great toe
lig|Intersesamoid ligament.funcion: Holds the sesamoids together and forms the groove for the flexor hallucis longus

lig|Interspinous ligaments.clinica: Traversed in lumbar puncture with a midline approach; injured in flexion-distraction fractures.

lig|Intervertebral disc C2-C3.une: Body of C2 → body of C3
lig|Intervertebral disc C2-C3.funcion: Cushions axial loads and allows intervertebral mobility; first cervical disc
lig|Intervertebral disc C2-C3.clinica: Herniations at this level are rare; they would affect the C3 root.

lig|Intervertebral disc C3-C4.une: Body of C3 → body of C4
lig|Intervertebral disc C3-C4.funcion: Cushions axial loads and allows intervertebral mobility
lig|Intervertebral disc C3-C4.clinica: A herniation compresses the C4 root.

lig|Intervertebral disc C4-C5.une: Body of C4 → body of C5
lig|Intervertebral disc C4-C5.funcion: Cushions axial loads and allows intervertebral mobility
lig|Intervertebral disc C4-C5.clinica: A herniation compresses the C5 root: deltoid weakness and diminished biceps reflex.

lig|Intervertebral disc C5-C6.une: Body of C5 → body of C6
lig|Intervertebral disc C5-C6.funcion: Cushions axial loads and allows intervertebral mobility
lig|Intervertebral disc C5-C6.clinica: Common cervical herniation level; compresses the C6 root (brachioradialis reflex, thumb).

lig|Intervertebral disc C6-C7.une: Body of C6 → body of C7
lig|Intervertebral disc C6-C7.funcion: Cushions axial loads and allows intervertebral mobility
lig|Intervertebral disc C6-C7.clinica: Most common cervical herniation level; compresses the C7 root (triceps, middle finger).

lig|Intervertebral disc C7-T1.une: Body of C7 → body of T1
lig|Intervertebral disc C7-T1.funcion: Cushions axial loads at the cervicothoracic junction
lig|Intervertebral disc C7-T1.clinica: A herniation compresses the C8 root: weakness of the intrinsic muscles of the hand.

lig|Intervertebral disc L1-L2.une: Body of L1 → body of L2
lig|Intervertebral disc L1-L2.funcion: Cushions axial loads and allows lumbar mobility
lig|Intervertebral disc L1-L2.clinica: Located at the level of the conus medullaris in adults; herniations are uncommon.

lig|Intervertebral disc L2-L3.une: Body of L2 → body of L3
lig|Intervertebral disc L2-L3.funcion: Cushions axial loads and allows lumbar mobility
lig|Intervertebral disc L2-L3.clinica: A posterolateral herniation usually compresses the L3 root.

lig|Intervertebral disc L3-L4.une: Body of L3 → body of L4
lig|Intervertebral disc L3-L4.funcion: Cushions axial loads and allows lumbar mobility
lig|Intervertebral disc L3-L4.clinica: A posterolateral herniation compresses the L4 root: diminished patellar reflex.

lig|Intervertebral disc L4-L5.une: Body of L4 → body of L5
lig|Intervertebral disc L4-L5.funcion: Cushions axial loads and allows lumbar mobility
lig|Intervertebral disc L4-L5.clinica: Common herniation level; a posterolateral herniation compresses the L5 root (great toe extension).

lig|Intervertebral disc L5-S1.une: Body of L5 → base of the sacrum
lig|Intervertebral disc L5-S1.funcion: Cushions loads at the lumbosacral junction; it is wedge-shaped, taller anteriorly
lig|Intervertebral disc L5-S1.clinica: Common herniation level; compresses the S1 root: diminished Achilles reflex, positive Lasègue test.

lig|Intervertebral disc T1-T2.une: Body of T1 → body of T2
lig|Intervertebral disc T1-T2.funcion: Cushions axial loads; mobility limited by the rib cage

lig|Intervertebral disc T10-T11.une: Body of T10 → body of T11
lig|Intervertebral disc T10-T11.funcion: Cushions axial loads and allows low thoracic mobility
lig|Intervertebral disc T10-T11.clinica: Thoracic herniations predominate at the lower levels, although they are rare.

lig|Intervertebral disc T11-T12.une: Body of T11 → body of T12
lig|Intervertebral disc T11-T12.funcion: Cushions axial loads; level of greatest thoracic mobility
lig|Intervertebral disc T11-T12.clinica: Thoracic level with the most disc herniations, which can cause myelopathy.

lig|Intervertebral disc T12-L1.une: Body of T12 → body of L1
lig|Intervertebral disc T12-L1.funcion: Cushions loads at the thoracolumbar junction
lig|Intervertebral disc T12-L1.clinica: The thoracolumbar junction is the most frequent site of vertebral fractures.

lig|Intervertebral disc T2-T3.une: Body of T2 → body of T3
lig|Intervertebral disc T2-T3.funcion: Cushions axial loads; mobility limited by the rib cage

lig|Intervertebral disc T3-T4.une: Body of T3 → body of T4
lig|Intervertebral disc T3-T4.funcion: Cushions axial loads; mobility limited by the rib cage

lig|Intervertebral disc T4-T5.une: Body of T4 → body of T5
lig|Intervertebral disc T4-T5.funcion: Cushions axial loads; mobility limited by the rib cage

lig|Intervertebral disc T5-T6.une: Body of T5 → body of T6
lig|Intervertebral disc T5-T6.funcion: Cushions axial loads; mobility limited by the rib cage

lig|Intervertebral disc T6-T7.une: Body of T6 → body of T7
lig|Intervertebral disc T6-T7.funcion: Cushions axial loads; mobility limited by the rib cage

lig|Intervertebral disc T7-T8.une: Body of T7 → body of T8
lig|Intervertebral disc T7-T8.funcion: Cushions axial loads; mobility limited by the rib cage
lig|Intervertebral disc T7-T8.clinica: Thoracic herniations are rare; they predominate below T8.

lig|Intervertebral disc T8-T9.une: Body of T8 → body of T9
lig|Intervertebral disc T8-T9.funcion: Cushions axial loads and allows thoracic mobility
lig|Intervertebral disc T8-T9.clinica: Thoracic herniations are rare; they predominate below T8.

lig|Intervertebral disc T9-T10.une: Body of T9 → body of T10
lig|Intervertebral disc T9-T10.funcion: Cushions axial loads and allows thoracic mobility
lig|Intervertebral disc T9-T10.clinica: Thoracic herniations are rare; they predominate below T8.

lig|Intra-articular ligament of head of.es: Intra-articular ligament of the head of the rib
lig|Intra-articular ligament of head of.articulacion: Joint of the head of the rib
lig|Intra-articular ligament of head of.une: Crest of the rib head → intervertebral disc
lig|Intra-articular ligament of head of.funcion: Divides the joint into two cavities; absent in ribs 1, 10, 11 and 12

lig|Ischiofemoral ligament.une: Body of the ischium posterior to the acetabulum → femoral neck, near the greater trochanter
lig|Ischiofemoral ligament.funcion: Reinforces the posterior capsule and limits internal rotation and extension
lig|Ischiofemoral ligament.clinica: Injured in posterior hip dislocation, typical of traffic accidents.

lig|Joints.funcion: Set of connections between bones or cartilages: fibrous, cartilaginous and synovial

lig|Lateral meniscus.une: Intercondylar area of the tibia (anterior and posterior horns), over the lateral tibial condyle
lig|Lateral meniscus.funcion: Increases congruence, distributes loads and absorbs shock; nearly circular and more mobile than the medial one
lig|Lateral meniscus.clinica: Tears less often than the medial meniscus because of its mobility; associated with acute ACL tears. McMurray test.

lig|Lateral talocalcaneal ligament.une: Lateral process of the talus → lateral surface of the calcaneus

lig|Lateral temporomandibular ligament.es: Lateral ligament of the temporomandibular joint
lig|Lateral temporomandibular ligament.une: Articular tubercle and zygomatic arch → posterolateral surface of the mandibular neck
lig|Lateral temporomandibular ligament.funcion: Reinforces the capsule laterally and limits posterior and inferior displacement of the condyle
lig|Lateral temporomandibular ligament.clinica: Prevents posterior dislocation of the condyle into the external acoustic meatus.

lig|Lateral thyrohyoid ligament.une: Superior horn of the thyroid cartilage → tip of the greater horn of the hyoid
lig|Lateral thyrohyoid ligament.funcion: Thickened posterior border of the thyrohyoid membrane; suspends the larynx from the hyoid
lig|Lateral thyrohyoid ligament.clinica: It often contains the triticeal cartilage, which can be mistaken for a calcified foreign body on radiographs.

lig|Ligament of head of femur.es: Ligament of the head of the femur
lig|Ligament of head of femur.une: Fovea of the femoral head → acetabular notch and transverse acetabular ligament
lig|Ligament of head of femur.funcion: Little stabilizing function; carries the artery of the ligamentum teres to the femoral head.
lig|Ligament of head of femur.clinica: Its artery is relevant in children; its injury may contribute to avascular necrosis of the femoral head.

lig|Ligamenta flava.une: Laminae of adjacent vertebrae, from C2 to S1
lig|Ligamenta flava.funcion: Limit flexion, help restore extension and form the posterior wall of the vertebral canal.
lig|Ligamenta flava.clinica: Traversed in lumbar puncture (loss of resistance); their hypertrophy causes canal stenosis.

lig|Long plantar ligament.une: Plantar surface of the calcaneus → ridge of the cuboid and bases of metatarsals II–V
lig|Long plantar ligament.funcion: Supports the lateral longitudinal arch of the foot; forms a tunnel for the tendon of fibularis longus.

lig|Lunotriquetral interosseous ligament.funcion: Stabilizes the lunate with the triquetrum and coordinates the proximal carpal row.
lig|Lunotriquetral interosseous ligament.clinica: Its rupture causes lunotriquetral instability and ulnar-sided wrist pain; Reagan's ballottement test.

lig|Medial meniscus.une: Anterior and posterior intercondylar areas of the tibia; attached to the capsule and the tibial collateral ligament
lig|Medial meniscus.funcion: Increases femorotibial congruence, absorbs loads and stabilizes the knee.
lig|Medial meniscus.clinica: Injured more often than the lateral one because of its fixation; unhappy triad with ACL and MCL; McMurray test.

lig|Medial talocalcaneal ligament.une: Medial tubercle of the talus → sustentaculum tali of the calcaneus

lig|Median cricothyroid ligament.une: Superior border of the arch of the cricoid → inferior border of the thyroid cartilage
lig|Median cricothyroid ligament.funcion: Anterior thickening of the conus elasticus; joins the thyroid and cricoid cartilages.
lig|Median cricothyroid ligament.clinica: Site of emergency cricothyrotomy for airway access.

lig|Median thyrohyoid ligament.une: Superior thyroid notch → body of the hyoid bone
lig|Median thyrohyoid ligament.funcion: Median thickening of the thyrohyoid membrane; suspends the larynx from the hyoid.

lig|Meniscopatellar ligament.une: Border of the patella → medial or lateral meniscus
lig|Meniscopatellar ligament.funcion: Draws the menisci anteriorly during knee extension.

lig|Metatarsal interosseous ligaments.funcion: Hold the metatarsal bases together and stabilize the forefoot.

lig|Middle glenohumeral ligament.une: Anterosuperior glenoid labrum → anterior surface of the anatomical neck of the humerus
lig|Middle glenohumeral ligament.funcion: Limits lateral rotation and anterior translation with the arm in mid-abduction.
lig|Middle glenohumeral ligament.clinica: May be absent or cord-like (Buford complex), a variant that mimics a labral lesion.

lig|Nuchal ligament.une: External occipital protuberance and crest → cervical spinous processes down to C7
lig|Nuchal ligament.funcion: Limits cervical flexion and serves as an attachment for posterior neck muscles.

lig|Nucleus pulposus C2-C3.funcion: Gelatinous center of the intervertebral disc; distributes compressive loads and allows movement between vertebrae.
lig|Nucleus pulposus C2-C3.clinica: First intervertebral disc; herniation at this level is uncommon.

lig|Nucleus pulposus C3-C4.funcion: Gelatinous center of the intervertebral disc; distributes compressive loads and allows movement between vertebrae.
lig|Nucleus pulposus C3-C4.clinica: Its posterolateral herniation compresses the C4 root.

lig|Nucleus pulposus C4-C5.funcion: Gelatinous center of the intervertebral disc; distributes compressive loads and allows movement between vertebrae.
lig|Nucleus pulposus C4-C5.clinica: Its posterolateral herniation compresses the C5 root: deltoid weakness.

lig|Nucleus pulposus C5-C6.funcion: Gelatinous center of the intervertebral disc; distributes compressive loads and allows movement between vertebrae.
lig|Nucleus pulposus C5-C6.clinica: Common cervical herniation level; compresses the C6 root: pain toward the thumb, diminished biceps/brachioradialis reflex.

lig|Nucleus pulposus C6-C7.funcion: Gelatinous center of the intervertebral disc; distributes compressive loads and allows movement between vertebrae.
lig|Nucleus pulposus C6-C7.clinica: Most common cervical herniation level; compresses the C7 root: diminished triceps reflex.

lig|Nucleus pulposus C7-T1.funcion: Gelatinous center of the intervertebral disc; distributes compressive loads and allows movement between vertebrae.
lig|Nucleus pulposus C7-T1.clinica: Its herniation compresses the C8 root: weakness of the intrinsic muscles of the hand.

lig|Nucleus pulposus L1-L2.funcion: Gelatinous center of the intervertebral disc; distributes compressive loads and allows movement between vertebrae.
lig|Nucleus pulposus L1-L2.clinica: Uncommon herniation; at this level it may affect the conus medullaris.

lig|Nucleus pulposus L2-L3.funcion: Gelatinous center of the intervertebral disc; distributes compressive loads and allows movement between vertebrae.
lig|Nucleus pulposus L2-L3.clinica: Uncommon herniation; its root compression (L3) causes pain in the anterior thigh.

lig|Nucleus pulposus L3-L4.funcion: Gelatinous center of the intervertebral disc; distributes compressive loads and allows movement between vertebrae.
lig|Nucleus pulposus L3-L4.clinica: Its posterolateral herniation compresses the L4 root: diminished patellar reflex.

lig|Nucleus pulposus L4-L5.funcion: Gelatinous center of the intervertebral disc; distributes compressive loads and allows movement between vertebrae.
lig|Nucleus pulposus L4-L5.clinica: Very common herniation level; compresses the L5 root: weakness of great toe dorsiflexion.

lig|Nucleus pulposus L5-S1.funcion: Gelatinous center of the intervertebral disc; distributes compressive loads and allows movement between vertebrae.
lig|Nucleus pulposus L5-S1.clinica: Very common herniation level; compresses the S1 root: diminished Achilles reflex, sciatica.

lig|Nucleus pulposus T1-T2.funcion: Gelatinous center of the intervertebral disc; distributes compressive loads and allows movement between vertebrae.
lig|Nucleus pulposus T1-T2.clinica: Thoracic herniations are rare because of the stability provided by the rib cage.

lig|Nucleus pulposus T10-T11.funcion: Gelatinous center of the intervertebral disc; distributes compressive loads and allows movement between vertebrae.
lig|Nucleus pulposus T10-T11.clinica: Thoracic herniations are rare; they predominate at the lower thoracic levels.

lig|Nucleus pulposus T11-T12.funcion: Gelatinous center of the intervertebral disc; distributes compressive loads and allows movement between vertebrae.
lig|Nucleus pulposus T11-T12.clinica: Thoracic level where herniations are most common, owing to the greater mobility of the thoracolumbar junction.

lig|Nucleus pulposus T12-L1.funcion: Gelatinous center of the intervertebral disc; distributes compressive loads and allows movement between vertebrae.
lig|Nucleus pulposus T12-L1.clinica: Heavily loaded thoracolumbar junction; frequent site of fractures and disc injuries.

lig|Nucleus pulposus T2-T3.funcion: Gelatinous center of the intervertebral disc; distributes compressive loads and allows movement between vertebrae.
lig|Nucleus pulposus T2-T3.clinica: Thoracic herniations are rare because of the stability provided by the rib cage.

lig|Nucleus pulposus T3-T4.funcion: Gelatinous center of the intervertebral disc; distributes compressive loads and allows movement between vertebrae.
lig|Nucleus pulposus T3-T4.clinica: Thoracic herniations are rare because of the stability provided by the rib cage.

lig|Nucleus pulposus T4-T5.funcion: Gelatinous center of the intervertebral disc; distributes compressive loads and allows movement between vertebrae.
lig|Nucleus pulposus T4-T5.clinica: Thoracic herniations are rare because of the stability provided by the rib cage.

lig|Nucleus pulposus T5-T6.funcion: Gelatinous center of the intervertebral disc; distributes compressive loads and allows movement between vertebrae.
lig|Nucleus pulposus T5-T6.clinica: Thoracic herniations are rare because of the stability provided by the rib cage.

lig|Nucleus pulposus T6-T7.funcion: Gelatinous center of the intervertebral disc; distributes compressive loads and allows movement between vertebrae.
lig|Nucleus pulposus T6-T7.clinica: Thoracic herniations are rare because of the stability provided by the rib cage.

lig|Nucleus pulposus T7-T8.funcion: Gelatinous center of the intervertebral disc; distributes compressive loads and allows movement between vertebrae.
lig|Nucleus pulposus T7-T8.clinica: Thoracic herniations are rare because of the stability provided by the rib cage.

lig|Nucleus pulposus T8-T9.funcion: Gelatinous center of the intervertebral disc; distributes compressive loads and allows movement between vertebrae.
lig|Nucleus pulposus T8-T9.clinica: Thoracic herniations are rare; they predominate at the lower thoracic levels.

lig|Nucleus pulposus T9-T10.funcion: Gelatinous center of the intervertebral disc; distributes compressive loads and allows movement between vertebrae.
lig|Nucleus pulposus T9-T10.clinica: Thoracic herniations are rare; they predominate at the lower thoracic levels.

lig|Oblique cord.une: Tuberosity of the ulna → radius, below its tuberosity
lig|Oblique cord.funcion: Reinforces the proximal radioulnar connection; its fibers run opposite to those of the interosseous membrane.

lig|Oblique popliteal ligament.une: Expansion of the semimembranosus tendon → lateral condyle of the femur
lig|Oblique popliteal ligament.funcion: Reinforces the posterior capsule and limits hyperextension and lateral rotation of the knee.
lig|Oblique popliteal ligament.clinica: Close relationship with the popliteal artery; Baker's cysts usually arise between the medial gastrocnemius and semimembranosus.

lig|Obturator membrane.une: Margins of the obturator foramen, closing it except for the obturator canal
lig|Obturator membrane.funcion: Closes the obturator foramen and gives origin to the obturator internus and externus muscles.
lig|Obturator membrane.clinica: The obturator canal that it leaves free is a site of obturator hernia, typical in thin elderly women.

lig|Palmar capitohamate ligament.une: Capitate → hamate, on its palmar surface

lig|Palmar carpometacarpal ligaments.une: Bones of the distal carpal row → bases of metacarpals II–V

lig|Palmar interphalangeal ligaments.es: Palmar ligaments of the interphalangeal joints of the hand
lig|Palmar interphalangeal ligaments.une: Proximal phalanx → base of the adjacent distal phalanx, on the palmar surface
lig|Palmar interphalangeal ligaments.funcion: Volar plates that prevent hyperextension of the interphalangeal joints.
lig|Palmar interphalangeal ligaments.clinica: Volar plate injury of the PIP joint from hyperextension is common in ball sports.

lig|Palmar lunotriquetral ligament.une: Lunate → triquetrum, on its palmar surface
lig|Palmar lunotriquetral ligament.funcion: Strongest portion of the lunotriquetral complex; stabilizes both bones.
lig|Palmar lunotriquetral ligament.clinica: Its injury contributes to lunotriquetral instability (VISI).

lig|Palmar metacarpal ligaments.une: Bases of adjacent metacarpals (II–V), on their palmar surface
lig|Palmar metacarpal ligaments.funcion: Connect the metacarpal bases and stabilize the palm.

lig|Palmar radio-ulnar ligament.une: Ulnar notch of the radius → head and fovea of the ulna
lig|Palmar radio-ulnar ligament.funcion: Component of the triangular fibrocartilage complex; stabilizes the distal radioulnar joint in pronation-supination.
lig|Palmar radio-ulnar ligament.clinica: Its injury (TFCC) produces distal radioulnar instability and ulnar-sided wrist pain.

lig|Palmar scaphotriquetral ligament.une: Triquetrum → scaphoid, crossing the palmar surface of the head of the capitate
lig|Palmar scaphotriquetral ligament.funcion: Supports the head of the capitate and stabilizes the midcarpal joint.

lig|Palmar trapezoideocapitate ligament.une: Trapezoid → capitate, on its palmar surface

lig|Pisohamate ligament.funcion: Extends the pull of flexor carpi ulnaris; forms the floor of Guyon's canal.
lig|Pisohamate ligament.clinica: Bounds Guyon's canal, a site of ulnar nerve compression at the wrist.

lig|Pisometacarpal ligament.une: Pisiform → base of the fifth metacarpal
lig|Pisometacarpal ligament.funcion: Extends the insertion of flexor carpi ulnaris to the metacarpus.

lig|Pisotriquetral ligament.funcion: Stabilizes the pisiform on the triquetrum.
lig|Pisotriquetral ligament.clinica: Pisotriquetral osteoarthritis causes hypothenar wrist pain.

lig|Plantar calcaneocuboid ligament.une: Anterior plantar surface of the calcaneus → plantar surface of the cuboid
lig|Plantar calcaneocuboid ligament.funcion: Short plantar ligament; supports the lateral longitudinal arch of the foot.

lig|Plantar calcaneonavicular ligament.une: Sustentaculum tali of the calcaneus → plantar surface of the navicular
lig|Plantar calcaneonavicular ligament.funcion: Spring ligament: supports the head of the talus and the medial longitudinal arch.
lig|Plantar calcaneonavicular ligament.clinica: Its insufficiency, together with posterior tibial dysfunction, causes adult acquired flatfoot.

lig|Plantar cuboideonavicular ligament.une: Cuboid → navicular, on its plantar surface
lig|Plantar cuboideonavicular ligament.funcion: Stabilizes the midtarsus and the transverse arch.

lig|Plantar cuneocuboid ligament.une: Lateral cuneiform → cuboid, on its plantar surface
lig|Plantar cuneocuboid ligament.funcion: Reinforces the transverse arch of the foot.

lig|Plantar cuneonavicular ligaments.une: Navicular → the three cuneiforms, on their plantar surface

lig|Plantar intercuneiform ligaments.une: Adjacent cuneiforms, on their plantar surface
lig|Plantar intercuneiform ligaments.funcion: Maintain the transverse arch of the foot.
