lig|Plantar interphalangeal ligaments.es: Plantar ligaments of the interphalangeal joints of the foot
lig|Plantar interphalangeal ligaments.une: Proximal phalanx → adjacent distal phalanx, on the plantar surface
lig|Plantar interphalangeal ligaments.funcion: Plantar plates that limit hyperextension of the toes.

lig|Plantar metatarsal ligaments.une: Bases of adjacent metatarsals, on their plantar surface
lig|Plantar metatarsal ligaments.funcion: Stabilize the metatarsal bases and the transverse arch.

lig|Plantar metatarsophalangeal ligament.es: Plantar ligaments of the metatarsophalangeal joints
lig|Plantar metatarsophalangeal ligament.une: Neck of the metatarsal → base of the proximal phalanx, on the plantar surface
lig|Plantar metatarsophalangeal ligament.funcion: Plantar plates that prevent hyperextension of the toes.
lig|Plantar metatarsophalangeal ligament.clinica: Plantar plate injury of the first toe is 'turf toe'; in the second toe, it causes MTP instability.

lig|Plantar tarsometatarsal ligaments.une: Cuneiforms and cuboid → bases of the metatarsals, on the plantar surface
lig|Plantar tarsometatarsal ligaments.clinica: Its injury is part of Lisfranc injuries; plantar ecchymosis in the midfoot is suggestive.

lig|Popliteofibular ligament.une: Popliteus tendon → styloid process of the head of the fibula
lig|Popliteofibular ligament.funcion: Component of the posterolateral corner; limits tibial lateral rotation and varus.
lig|Popliteofibular ligament.clinica: Its injury is part of posterolateral corner injuries; dial test.

lig|Posterior cruciate ligament.une: Posterior intercondylar area of the tibia → lateral surface of the medial condyle of the femur
lig|Posterior cruciate ligament.funcion: Prevents posterior displacement of the tibia on the femur, especially in flexion.
lig|Posterior cruciate ligament.clinica: Injured by a blow to the tibia with the knee flexed (dashboard injury); posterior drawer test.

lig|Posterior ligament of fibular head.es: Posterior ligament of the fibular head
lig|Posterior ligament of fibular head.une: Head of the fibula → posterior surface of the lateral condyle of the tibia
lig|Posterior ligament of fibular head.funcion: Reinforces the proximal tibiofibular joint posteriorly.

lig|Posterior longitudinal ligament.une: Posterior surface of the vertebral bodies and discs, from C2 (tectorial membrane) to the sacrum
lig|Posterior longitudinal ligament.funcion: Limits flexion of the spine and restrains posteromedial herniation of the disc.
lig|Posterior longitudinal ligament.clinica: It is narrower in the lumbar region, which is why herniations are usually posterolateral; its ossification causes myelopathy.

lig|Posterior meniscotibial ligament (La.es: Posterior meniscotibial ligament of the lateral meniscus
lig|Posterior meniscotibial ligament (La.une: Posterior horn of the lateral meniscus → posterior intercondylar area of the tibia
lig|Posterior meniscotibial ligament (La.funcion: Anchors the posterior root of the lateral meniscus to the tibia.
lig|Posterior meniscotibial ligament (La.clinica: Posterior root tears of the lateral meniscus are associated with ACL tears.

lig|Posterior meniscotibial ligament (Me.es: Posterior meniscotibial ligament of the medial meniscus
lig|Posterior meniscotibial ligament (Me.une: Posterior horn of the medial meniscus → posterior intercondylar area of the tibia
lig|Posterior meniscotibial ligament (Me.funcion: Anchors the posterior root of the medial meniscus to the tibia.
lig|Posterior meniscotibial ligament (Me.clinica: A medial posterior root tear is functionally equivalent to a total meniscectomy and accelerates osteoarthritis.

lig|Posterior sacro-iliac ligament.une: Posterior superior iliac spine and iliac crest → intermediate and lateral sacral crests
lig|Posterior sacro-iliac ligament.funcion: Limits nutation and stabilizes the sacroiliac joint posteriorly.
lig|Posterior sacro-iliac ligament.clinica: Possible source of low back pain and sacroiliac tenderness on palpation.

lig|Posterior sternoclavicular ligament.une: Sternal end of the clavicle → posterior surface of the manubrium of the sternum
lig|Posterior sternoclavicular ligament.funcion: Main restraint to anterior and posterior translation of the medial clavicle.
lig|Posterior sternoclavicular ligament.clinica: Posterior sternoclavicular dislocation can compress the trachea, esophagus and great vessels: an emergency.

lig|Posterior talocalcaneal ligament.une: Posterior process of the talus → superior surface of the calcaneus

lig|Posterior talofibular ligament.une: Malleolar fossa of the fibula → posterior process of the talus
lig|Posterior talofibular ligament.funcion: Limits posterior displacement of the talus and lateral rotation.
lig|Posterior talofibular ligament.clinica: The strongest of the lateral complex; it tears only in severe sprains or dislocations.

lig|Posterior tibiofibular ligament.une: Lateral malleolus → posterior margin of the distal tibia
lig|Posterior tibiofibular ligament.funcion: Stabilizes the syndesmosis and maintains the ankle mortise.
lig|Posterior tibiofibular ligament.clinica: Its bony avulsion produces the posterior malleolus fragment in ankle fractures.

lig|Posterior tibiotalar ligament.es: Posterior tibiotalar part of the medial ligament
lig|Posterior tibiotalar ligament.la: Pars tibiotalaris posterior ligamenti collateralis medialis
lig|Posterior tibiotalar ligament.une: Medial malleolus → medial surface and medial tubercle of the talus
lig|Posterior tibiotalar ligament.funcion: Deep part of the deltoid ligament; limits eversion and lateral rotation of the talus.
lig|Posterior tibiotalar ligament.clinica: May be injured in bimalleolar fractures and eversion sprains.

lig|Pterygospinous ligament.une: Lateral plate of the pterygoid process → spine of the sphenoid
lig|Pterygospinous ligament.funcion: Fibrous band that forms an opening (pterygospinous foramen) for branches of the mandibular nerve.
lig|Pterygospinous ligament.clinica: Its ossification may compress the lingual nerve or hinder mandibular nerve block.

lig|Pubic symphysis.une: Body of the right pubis → body of the left pubis, via the interpubic disc
lig|Pubic symphysis.funcion: Joins the hip bones anteriorly and cushions forces in the pelvic ring.
lig|Pubic symphysis.clinica: Widens in pregnancy; diastasis in pelvic trauma (open book); osteitis pubis in athletes.

lig|Pubofemoral ligament.une: Superior pubic ramus and iliopubic eminence → inferior capsule and intertrochanteric line
lig|Pubofemoral ligament.funcion: Limits excessive abduction and extension of the hip.

lig|Quadrangular membrane.une: Lateral border of the epiglottis → arytenoid cartilage
lig|Quadrangular membrane.funcion: Forms the wall of the laryngeal vestibule; its inferior border forms the vestibular ligament.

lig|Quadrate ligament.une: Inferior border of the radial notch of the ulna → neck of the radius
lig|Quadrate ligament.funcion: Limits extreme pronation and supination and reinforces the inferior part of the capsule.

lig|Radial collateral ligament.une: Lateral epicondyle of the humerus → annular ligament of the radius
lig|Radial collateral ligament.funcion: Limits varus of the elbow and is part of the lateral ligament complex.
lig|Radial collateral ligament.clinica: Its injury (together with the lateral ulnar collateral ligament) causes posterolateral rotatory instability of the elbow.

lig|Radial collateral ligament of wrist.es: Radial collateral ligament of the wrist
lig|Radial collateral ligament of wrist.une: Styloid process of the radius → scaphoid
lig|Radial collateral ligament of wrist.funcion: Limits ulnar deviation of the wrist.

lig|Radiate carpal ligament.une: Head of the capitate → neighboring carpal bones (scaphoid, lunate, triquetrum, hamate)
lig|Radiate carpal ligament.funcion: Stabilizes the capitate and the midcarpal joint palmarly.

lig|Radiate ligament of head of rib.es: Radiate ligament of the head of the rib
lig|Radiate ligament of head of rib.articulacion: Joint of the head of the rib
lig|Radiate ligament of head of rib.une: Head of the rib → bodies of the two adjacent vertebrae and the disc

lig|Radiocapitate ligament.une: Styloid process of the radius → capitate
lig|Radiocapitate ligament.funcion: Stabilizes the scaphoid and limits ulnar translation of the carpus.

lig|Radioscaphocapitate ligament.une: Styloid process of the radius → waist of the scaphoid → capitate
lig|Radioscaphocapitate ligament.funcion: Acts as a fulcrum for the scaphoid and limits ulnar translation of the carpus.
lig|Radioscaphocapitate ligament.clinica: Preserving it is key in radial styloidectomy to avoid ulnar translation of the carpus.

lig|Sacrococcygeal symphysis.une: Apex of the sacrum → base of the coccyx, via a fibrocartilaginous disc
lig|Sacrococcygeal symphysis.funcion: Allows slight flexion and extension of the coccyx, especially during childbirth.
lig|Sacrococcygeal symphysis.clinica: Its dislocation or hypermobility causes coccydynia after falls onto the buttocks or childbirth.

lig|Sacrospinous ligament.une: Lateral border of the sacrum and coccyx → ischial spine
lig|Sacrospinous ligament.funcion: Limits nutation of the sacrum; separates the greater and lesser sciatic foramina.
lig|Sacrospinous ligament.clinica: Landmark for pudendal nerve block and for sacrospinous colpopexy.

lig|Sacrotuberous ligament.une: Posterior iliac spines, sacrum and coccyx → ischial tuberosity
lig|Sacrotuberous ligament.funcion: Limits nutation of the sacrum and bounds the lesser sciatic foramen.
lig|Sacrotuberous ligament.clinica: It may entrap the pudendal nerve between itself and the sacrospinous ligament (pudendal neuralgia).

lig|Scaphocapitate ligament.une: Distal pole of the scaphoid → capitate
lig|Scaphocapitate ligament.funcion: Stabilizes the scaphoid within the midcarpal joint.

lig|Scapholunate interosseous ligament.une: Scaphoid → lunate; its dorsal portion is the strongest
lig|Scapholunate interosseous ligament.funcion: Main scapholunate stabilizer; prevents dissociation between the two bones.
lig|Scapholunate interosseous ligament.clinica: Its rupture causes scapholunate dissociation (Terry Thomas sign, DISI); Watson test.

lig|Scaphotrapeziotrapezoidal ligament.une: Distal pole of the scaphoid → trapezium and trapezoid
lig|Scaphotrapeziotrapezoidal ligament.funcion: Stabilizes the distal pole of the scaphoid and limits its flexion.
lig|Scaphotrapeziotrapezoidal ligament.clinica: STT osteoarthritis is a frequent cause of radial-sided wrist pain, often together with thumb carpometacarpal osteoarthritis.

lig|Sphenomandibular ligament.une: Spine of the sphenoid → lingula of the mandible
lig|Sphenomandibular ligament.funcion: Acts as the suspension axis of the mandible during mouth opening.
lig|Sphenomandibular ligament.clinica: Landmark in inferior alveolar nerve block; the nerve passes lateral to it.

lig|Stylohyoid ligament.une: Styloid process of the temporal bone → lesser horn of the hyoid
lig|Stylohyoid ligament.clinica: Its calcification with an elongated styloid process causes Eagle syndrome.

lig|Stylomandibular ligament.une: Styloid process → angle and posterior border of the mandibular ramus
lig|Stylomandibular ligament.funcion: Limits excessive protrusion of the mandible.

lig|Superficial part of tibial collatera.es: Superficial part of the tibial collateral ligament
lig|Superficial part of tibial collatera.une: Medial epicondyle of the femur → medial surface of the tibia, beneath the pes anserinus
lig|Superficial part of tibial collatera.funcion: Main restraint to valgus of the knee; also limits tibial lateral rotation.
lig|Superficial part of tibial collatera.clinica: Injured by forced valgus; valgus stress test at 30° of flexion.

lig|Superior glenohumeral ligament.une: Supraglenoid tubercle and superior labrum → near the lesser tubercle of the humerus
lig|Superior glenohumeral ligament.funcion: Limits inferior translation and lateral rotation with the arm adducted.
lig|Superior glenohumeral ligament.clinica: Part of the biceps pulley; its injury destabilizes the tendon of the long head.

lig|Superior pubic ligament.une: Pubic crests and tubercles of both sides

lig|Superior transverse scapular ligamen.une: Margins of the scapular notch, next to the base of the coracoid
lig|Superior transverse scapular ligamen.funcion: Converts the scapular notch into a foramen for the suprascapular nerve.
lig|Superior transverse scapular ligamen.clinica: Site of suprascapular nerve entrapment: weakness of supraspinatus and infraspinatus.

lig|Supraspinous ligament.une: Tips of the spinous processes from C7 to the sacrum
lig|Supraspinous ligament.clinica: First ligament traversed in midline lumbar puncture.

lig|Talocalcaneal interosseous ligament.une: Sulcus of the talus → sulcus of the calcaneus, in the tarsal sinus
lig|Talocalcaneal interosseous ligament.funcion: Main connection between talus and calcaneus; limits eversion.
lig|Talocalcaneal interosseous ligament.clinica: Its injury is associated with sinus tarsi syndrome after ankle sprains.

lig|Talonavicular ligament.une: Neck of the talus → dorsal surface of the navicular

lig|Tibiocalcaneal ligament.es: Tibiocalcaneal part of the medial ligament
lig|Tibiocalcaneal ligament.une: Medial malleolus → sustentaculum tali of the calcaneus
lig|Tibiocalcaneal ligament.funcion: Superficial part of the deltoid ligament; limits eversion of the hindfoot.

lig|Tibionavicular ligament.es: Tibionavicular part of the medial ligament
lig|Tibionavicular ligament.une: Medial malleolus → tuberosity of the navicular and plantar calcaneonavicular ligament
lig|Tibionavicular ligament.funcion: Superficial part of the deltoid ligament; limits abduction and eversion of the foot.

lig|Transverse acetabular ligament.une: Margins of the acetabular notch, completing the labrum
lig|Transverse acetabular ligament.funcion: Closes the acetabular notch, forming a foramen for vessels and nerves of the femoral head.
lig|Transverse acetabular ligament.clinica: Landmark for orienting the acetabular component in hip arthroplasty.

lig|Transverse humeral ligament.une: Greater tubercle → lesser tubercle of the humerus, over the intertubercular groove
lig|Transverse humeral ligament.funcion: Keeps the tendon of the long head of the biceps within the intertubercular groove.
lig|Transverse humeral ligament.clinica: Its rupture allows medial subluxation of the biceps tendon.

lig|Transverse ligament of knee.une: Anterior border of the lateral meniscus → anterior border of the medial meniscus
lig|Transverse ligament of knee.funcion: Joins the anterior horns of both menisci; inconstant.
lig|Transverse ligament of knee.clinica: May mimic a tear of the anterior horn of the lateral meniscus on MRI.

lig|Transverse part of iliofemoral ligam.es: Transverse part of the iliofemoral ligament
lig|Transverse part of iliofemoral ligam.une: Anterior inferior iliac spine → superior part of the intertrochanteric line
lig|Transverse part of iliofemoral ligam.funcion: Superior band of the Y-shaped ligament of Bigelow; limits extension and lateral rotation.

lig|Transverse tibiofibular ligament.une: Malleolar fossa of the fibula → posterior margin of the distal tibia
lig|Transverse tibiofibular ligament.funcion: Deep portion of the posterior tibiofibular ligament; deepens the mortise and prevents posterior translation of the talus.

lig|Trapezoid ligament.une: Superior surface of the coracoid process → trapezoid line of the clavicle
lig|Trapezoid ligament.funcion: Lateral part of the coracoclavicular ligament; limits medial displacement of the scapula beneath the clavicle.
lig|Trapezoid ligament.clinica: Tears in grade III or higher acromioclavicular dislocations.

lig|Triquetrocapitate ligament.une: Triquetrum → capitate, on its palmar surface
lig|Triquetrocapitate ligament.funcion: Ulnar limb of the arcuate ligament; stabilizes the midcarpal joint.
lig|Triquetrocapitate ligament.clinica: Its insufficiency contributes to midcarpal instability (painful clunk).

lig|Triquetrohamate ligament.funcion: Stabilizes the midcarpal joint on its ulnar side.
lig|Triquetrohamate ligament.clinica: Its laxity contributes to palmar midcarpal instability.

lig|Triradiate cartilage.une: Ilium, ischium and pubis at the acetabulum
lig|Triradiate cartilage.funcion: Growth cartilage of the acetabulum; ossifies at around 14-16 years.
lig|Triradiate cartilage.clinica: Its injury in children can cause acetabular dysplasia; marker of skeletal maturity.

lig|Ulnar collateral ligament.une: Medial epicondyle of the humerus → coronoid process and olecranon of the ulna
lig|Ulnar collateral ligament.funcion: Main restraint to elbow valgus, especially its anterior bundle.
lig|Ulnar collateral ligament.clinica: Typical injury of throwers; valgus stress test and 'moving valgus' test.

lig|Ulnar collateral ligament of wrist j.une: Styloid process of the ulna → triquetrum and pisiform
lig|Ulnar collateral ligament of wrist j.funcion: Limits radial deviation of the wrist.

lig|Ulnocapitate ligament.funcion: Provides palmar stabilization of the ulnar side of the carpus.

lig|Ulnolunate ligament.funcion: Part of the triangular fibrocartilage complex; stabilizes the ulnar side of the carpus.

lig|Ulnopisiform ligament.une: Styloid process of the ulna → pisiform
lig|Ulnopisiform ligament.funcion: Reinforces the palmar ulnar side of the wrist.

lig|Ulnotriquetral ligament.funcion: Part of the triangular fibrocartilage complex; stabilizes the ulnar side of the carpus.
lig|Ulnotriquetral ligament.clinica: Its longitudinal tear causes ulnar-sided wrist pain; positive fovea sign.

bone|Anterior cells of ethmoid bone.descripcion: Pneumatic cavities of the anterior part of the ethmoidal labyrinth, between the orbit and the nasal cavity; they drain into the middle nasal meatus.
bone|Anterior cells of ethmoid bone.referencias: Ethmoidal bulla, ethmoidal infundibulum and semilunar hiatus on coronal CT; agger nasi cell.
bone|Anterior cells of ethmoid bone.clinica: Anterior ethmoiditis can spread to the orbit through the lamina papyracea, causing orbital cellulitis.

bone|Arytenoid cartilage.descripcion: Paired pyramidal cartilage of the larynx, on the superior border of the cricoid lamina; gives attachment to the vocal ligaments and intrinsic muscles.
bone|Arytenoid cartilage.articula: Cricoid cartilage (cricoarytenoid joint) and corniculate cartilage at its apex.
bone|Arytenoid cartilage.referencias: Vocal process and muscular process; visible on laryngoscopy as the posterior arytenoid prominences.
bone|Arytenoid cartilage.clinica: Traumatic intubation can dislocate the arytenoid, causing persistent dysphonia after extubation.

bone|Atlas (C1).descripcion: First cervical vertebra, ring-shaped and without a body; supports the skull and permits flexion-extension of the head.
bone|Atlas (C1).articula: Occipital condyles (atlanto-occipital) and axis (median and lateral atlantoaxial).
bone|Atlas (C1).referencias: Transverse process palpable between the mastoid and the angle of the mandible; anterior arch and lateral masses on transoral radiograph.
bone|Atlas (C1).clinica: Jefferson fracture is a burst of the ring from axial loading; assessed on the transoral view.

bone|Axis (C2).descripcion: Second cervical vertebra, characterized by the dens (odontoid process), the axis of rotation of the atlas.
bone|Axis (C2).articula: Atlas (atlantoaxial joints) and third cervical vertebra.
bone|Axis (C2).referencias: Bifid spinous process, the first palpable below the occiput; dens of the axis on transoral radiograph.
bone|Axis (C2).clinica: Odontoid fractures (Anderson-D'Alonzo types I–III) and the hangman's fracture involve the axis.

bone|Body of sternum.descripcion: Middle and longest portion of the sternum, between the manubrium and xiphoid process, in the anterior thoracic wall.
bone|Body of sternum.articula: Manubrium, xiphoid process and costal cartilages 2nd to 7th.
bone|Body of sternum.referencias: Sternal angle (junction with the manubrium, 2nd rib); subcutaneous anterior surface; xiphisternal junction.
bone|Body of sternum.clinica: Site of compressions in cardiopulmonary resuscitation (lower half) and of median sternotomy in cardiac surgery.

bone|Calcaneus.descripcion: Largest bone of the tarsus, forms the heel; receives the calcaneal tendon and supports the talus.
bone|Calcaneus.referencias: Calcaneal tuberosity, sustentaculum tali, fibular trochlea; Böhler angle on lateral radiograph.
bone|Calcaneus.clinica: Typical fracture from a fall from height (decreased Böhler angle); also look for lumbar vertebral fracture.

bone|Capitate bone.descripcion: Largest carpal bone, in the center of the distal row; axis of the wrist.
bone|Capitate bone.articula: Scaphoid, lunate, trapezoid, hamate and metacarpals 2nd to 4th (mainly the 3rd).
bone|Capitate bone.referencias: Palpable dorsal depression proximal to the base of the 3rd metacarpal; center of the carpus on PA radiograph.
bone|Capitate bone.clinica: It may suffer avascular necrosis after fracture of its neck, although this is uncommon.

bone|Clavicle.descripcion: Italic S-shaped bone that joins the sternum with the scapula, at the base of the neck.
bone|Clavicle.articula: Manubrium of the sternum (sternoclavicular), acromion (acromioclavicular) and first costal cartilage.
bone|Clavicle.referencias: Entirely subcutaneous; sternal end, medial convex curvature, acromial end; conoid tubercle.
bone|Clavicle.clinica: Most frequently fractured bone, typically in the middle third from a fall onto the shoulder.

bone|Coccyx.descripcion: Terminal bone of the vertebral column, formed by 3–5 fused coccygeal vertebrae, below the sacrum.
bone|Coccyx.referencias: Apex palpable in the intergluteal cleft and on rectal examination; coccygeal cornua.
bone|Coccyx.clinica: Coccydynia usually follows falls onto the buttocks or childbirth.

bone|Corniculate cartilage.descripcion: Small paired nodule of elastic cartilage located on the apex of each arytenoid, in the aryepiglottic fold.
bone|Corniculate cartilage.referencias: Corniculate tubercle visible on laryngoscopy in the posterior aryepiglottic fold.

bone|Costal cartilage of rib.descripcion: Bars of hyaline cartilage that extend the ribs anteriorly and give elasticity to the thoracic wall.
bone|Costal cartilage of rib.articula: Anterior end of the rib; sternum (1st–7th) or superior cartilage (8th–10th).
bone|Costal cartilage of rib.referencias: Costal margin formed by the 7th–10th cartilages; palpable chondrocostal junctions.
bone|Costal cartilage of rib.clinica: Its inflammation produces costochondritis (Tietze syndrome when there is swelling), a frequent cause of chest pain.

bone|Cricoid cartilage.descripcion: Only complete cartilaginous ring of the airway, signet-ring shaped, base of the larynx at the level of C6.
bone|Cricoid cartilage.articula: Thyroid cartilage (cricothyroid) and arytenoid (cricoarytenoid); continues with the trachea.
bone|Cricoid cartilage.referencias: Anterior arch palpable below the cricothyroid membrane; vertebral level C6.
bone|Cricoid cartilage.clinica: The cricothyroid membrane, above it, is the site of emergency cricothyrotomy; cricoid pressure (Sellick maneuver).

bone|Cuboid bone.descripcion: Tarsal bone on the lateral border of the foot, between the calcaneus and the 4th and 5th metatarsals.
bone|Cuboid bone.articula: Calcaneus, navicular (occasional), lateral cuneiform and 4th and 5th metatarsals.
bone|Cuboid bone.referencias: Groove for the fibularis longus tendon on its plantar surface; palpable proximal to the base of the 5th metatarsal.
bone|Cuboid bone.clinica: Nutcracker fracture from forced abduction of the forefoot; cuboid syndrome in dancers.

bone|Distal phalanx of finger of foot.descripcion: Last bone of each toe, under the nail; the great toe has only two phalanges.
bone|Distal phalanx of finger of foot.articula: Middle phalanx (or proximal in the great toe) via the distal interphalangeal joint.
bone|Distal phalanx of finger of foot.referencias: Tuberosity of the distal phalanx under the nail; articular base.
bone|Distal phalanx of finger of foot.clinica: Crush fractures with subungual hematoma may be open and require prophylaxis.

bone|Distal phalanx of finger of hand.descripcion: Terminal bone of each finger of the hand, under the nail bed and the finger pulp.
bone|Distal phalanx of finger of hand.articula: Middle phalanx (or proximal in the thumb) via the distal interphalangeal joint.
bone|Distal phalanx of finger of hand.referencias: Ungual tuberosity, base with attachment of the extensor tendon and the flexor digitorum profundus.
bone|Distal phalanx of finger of hand.clinica: Mallet finger is avulsion of the extensor at its dorsal base.

bone|Ethmoid bone.descripcion: Unpaired, pneumatized bone of the anterior cranial base, between the orbits; forms the roof and walls of the nasal cavity.
bone|Ethmoid bone.articula: Frontal, sphenoid, nasals, maxillae, lacrimals, palatines, inferior nasal conchae and vomer.
bone|Ethmoid bone.referencias: Cribriform plate, crista galli, perpendicular plate, orbital plate; labyrinth on CT.
bone|Ethmoid bone.clinica: Fracture of the cribriform plate can produce CSF rhinorrhea (CSF fistula) and anosmia.

bone|Femur.descripcion: Bone of the thigh, the longest and strongest of the body, between the hip and the knee.
bone|Femur.articula: Hip bone (hip joint), tibia (tibiofemoral) and patella (patellofemoral).
bone|Femur.referencias: Greater trochanter palpable laterally; femoral epicondyles and condyles; neck-shaft angle on radiograph.
bone|Femur.clinica: Femoral neck fracture in the elderly can cause avascular necrosis of the head.

bone|Fibula.descripcion: Slender lateral bone of the leg, without relevant weight-bearing function; forms the lateral malleolus.
bone|Fibula.articula: Tibia (proximal and distal tibiofibular) and talus.
bone|Fibula.referencias: Head of the fibula palpable posterolateral to the knee; subcutaneous lateral malleolus.
bone|Fibula.clinica: The common fibular nerve wraps around its neck and is injured in fractures or compression (foot drop).

bone|Frontal bone.descripcion: Unpaired bone that forms the forehead, the roof of the orbits and part of the anterior cranial fossa.
bone|Frontal bone.articula: Parietals, sphenoid, ethmoid, nasals, maxillae, lacrimals and zygomatics.
bone|Frontal bone.referencias: Superciliary arches, glabella, supraorbital notch, nasion; frontal sinuses on radiograph.
bone|Frontal bone.clinica: Fractures of the posterior wall of the frontal sinus can cause CSF fistula.

bone|Hamate bone.descripcion: Wedge-shaped bone of the distal carpal row, on the ulnar side, with a palmar hook-shaped process.
bone|Hamate bone.articula: Lunate, triquetrum, capitate and 4th and 5th metacarpals.
bone|Hamate bone.referencias: Hook of the hamate palpable distal and radial to the pisiform; boundary of Guyon's canal.
bone|Hamate bone.clinica: Hook fracture occurs in golfers and tennis players and may irritate the ulnar nerve.

bone|Hip bone.descripcion: Paired bone of the pelvis formed by the ilium, ischium and pubis fused at the acetabulum.
bone|Hip bone.articula: Sacrum (sacroiliac), contralateral hip bone (pubic symphysis) and femur (hip joint).
bone|Hip bone.referencias: Iliac crest, anterior superior iliac spine, ischial tuberosity, pubic tubercle.
bone|Hip bone.clinica: The posterior iliac crest is the usual site for bone marrow biopsy and aspiration.

bone|Humerus.descripcion: Bone of the arm, between the scapula and the bones of the forearm.
bone|Humerus.referencias: Greater and lesser tubercles, medial and lateral epicondyles, radial nerve groove.
bone|Humerus.clinica: Shaft fracture can injure the radial nerve (wrist drop); supracondylar fracture, the brachial artery.

bone|Hyoid bone.descripcion: U-shaped bone of the anterior neck at the level of C3, suspended by muscles and ligaments without direct bony articulation.
bone|Hyoid bone.referencias: Body palpable above the thyroid cartilage; greater and lesser horns; level C3.
bone|Hyoid bone.clinica: Its fracture suggests manual strangulation in forensic medicine.

bone|Incus.descripcion: Intermediate ossicle of the middle ear that transmits vibrations from the malleus to the stapes.
bone|Incus.referencias: Body and short process in the epitympanic recess; long process visible through the tympanic membrane.
bone|Incus.clinica: Its long process is the point most vulnerable to erosion in chronic otitis media and cholesteatoma.

bone|Inferior nasal concha bone.descripcion: Independent curved bony lamina on the lateral wall of the nasal cavity, above the inferior meatus.
bone|Inferior nasal concha bone.referencias: Visible on anterior rhinoscopy; inferior meatus with the opening of the nasolacrimal duct.
bone|Inferior nasal concha bone.clinica: Its mucosal hypertrophy is a common cause of nasal obstruction and is treated with turbinoplasty.

bone|Intermediate cuneiform bone.descripcion: The smallest of the three cuneiforms, in the distal tarsus, between the medial and lateral cuneiforms.
bone|Intermediate cuneiform bone.articula: Navicular, medial and lateral cuneiforms and base of the 2nd metatarsal.
bone|Intermediate cuneiform bone.referencias: Being shorter, it creates a mortise that receives the base of the 2nd metatarsal.
bone|Intermediate cuneiform bone.clinica: Part of the Lisfranc complex, whose injuries are frequently missed.

bone|Lacrimal bone.descripcion: Smallest and most fragile bone of the face, in the medial wall of the orbit, housing the lacrimal sac.
bone|Lacrimal bone.articula: Frontal, ethmoid, maxilla and inferior nasal concha.
bone|Lacrimal bone.referencias: Posterior lacrimal crest and fossa for the lacrimal sac in the medial orbital wall.
bone|Lacrimal bone.clinica: It is perforated in dacryocystorhinostomy to treat obstruction of the nasolacrimal duct.

bone|Lateral cuneiform bone.descripcion: Cuneiform bone of the distal tarsus located between the intermediate cuneiform and the cuboid.
bone|Lateral cuneiform bone.articula: Navicular, intermediate cuneiform, cuboid and 2nd, 3rd and 4th metatarsals.
bone|Lateral cuneiform bone.referencias: Base of the 3rd metatarsal; central position on the dorsoplantar radiograph.

bone|Lateral process of nasal septal car.es: Lateral process of septal nasal cartilage
bone|Lateral process of nasal septal car.descripcion: Triangular expansion on each side of the septal cartilage (upper lateral cartilage) that forms the lateral wall of the middle nasal dorsum.
bone|Lateral process of nasal septal car.articula: Inferior border of the nasal bone and frontal process of the maxilla; continuous with the septal cartilage.
bone|Lateral process of nasal septal car.referencias: Middle third of the nasal dorsum; internal nasal valve with the septum.
bone|Lateral process of nasal septal car.clinica: Its collapse narrows the internal nasal valve, a frequent cause of obstruction after rhinoplasty.

bone|Lower canine.descripcion: Single-rooted tooth with a pointed cusp in the mandibular arch, distal to the lateral incisor.
bone|Lower canine.referencias: Canine eminence; FDI 33 and 43; erupts at around 9–10 years.

bone|Lower first molar tooth.descripcion: Permanent mandibular tooth with five cusps and two roots (mesial and distal), the first to erupt (6 years).
bone|Lower first molar tooth.referencias: FDI 36 and 46; roots close to the mandibular canal on panoramic radiograph.
bone|Lower first molar tooth.clinica: It is the permanent tooth most affected by caries and often the first to be lost.

bone|Lower first premolar.descripcion: Single-rooted mandibular tooth with a dominant buccal cusp, distal to the canine.
bone|Lower first premolar.referencias: FDI 34 and 44; mental foramen located near its apex or between the premolars.
bone|Lower first premolar.clinica: Its proximity to the mental foramen requires care in surgery to avoid injuring the mental nerve.

bone|Lower lateral incisor.descripcion: Single-rooted cutting mandibular tooth, distal to the central incisor.
bone|Lower lateral incisor.referencias: FDI 32 and 42; erupts at around 7–8 years.

bone|Lower medial incisor.descripcion: Smallest tooth of the permanent dentition, cutting, on each side of the mandibular midline.
bone|Lower medial incisor.referencias: FDI 31 and 41; first permanent anterior tooth to erupt (6–7 years).
bone|Lower medial incisor.clinica: Frequent site of calculus accumulation because of the opening of the submandibular ducts.

bone|Lower second molar tooth.descripcion: Permanent mandibular molar with four cusps and two roots, distal to the first molar; erupts at around 12 years.
bone|Lower second molar tooth.referencias: FDI 37 and 47; relationship with the third molar on panoramic radiograph.
bone|Lower second molar tooth.clinica: An impacted third molar can cause caries or resorption on its distal surface.

bone|Lower second premolar.descripcion: Single-rooted bicuspid or tricuspid mandibular tooth, mesial to the first molar.
bone|Lower second premolar.referencias: FDI 35 and 45; mental foramen often under its apex.
bone|Lower second premolar.clinica: It is one of the teeth with the most congenital agenesis after the third molars.

bone|Lunate bone.descripcion: Crescent-shaped bone of the proximal carpal row, between the scaphoid and the triquetrum.
bone|Lunate bone.articula: Radius, scaphoid, triquetrum, capitate and sometimes hamate.
bone|Lunate bone.referencias: Palpable dorsally distal to Lister's tubercle in flexion; radio-lunate-capitate alignment on lateral radiograph.
bone|Lunate bone.clinica: It is the carpal bone that dislocates most frequently; its avascular necrosis is Kienböck disease.

bone|Major alar cartilage.descripcion: Paired U-shaped cartilage that surrounds each nostril and shapes the tip and alae of the nose.
bone|Major alar cartilage.articula: Joined by fibrous tissue to the septal cartilage, lateral process and contralateral cartilage.
bone|Major alar cartilage.referencias: Medial crus in the columella, lateral crus in the ala; dome at the nasal tip.
bone|Major alar cartilage.clinica: Its modification is the basis of tip surgery in rhinoplasty.

bone|Malleus.descripcion: Most lateral ossicle of the middle ear, with its handle attached to the tympanic membrane.
bone|Malleus.referencias: Handle and lateral process (umbo) visible on otoscopy through the tympanic membrane.
bone|Malleus.clinica: The umbo is a key otoscopic landmark; its position changes in a retracted or bulging tympanic membrane.

bone|Mandible.descripcion: The only mobile bone of the skull, horseshoe-shaped, which forms the skeleton of the lower jaw and houses the lower teeth.
bone|Mandible.referencias: Mandibular angle, mental protuberance, condyle palpable in front of the tragus; mental foramen.
bone|Mandible.clinica: Being a ring with the skull base, it usually fractures at two sites (e.g., angle and contralateral condyle).

bone|Manubrium of sternum.descripcion: Superior and widest portion of the sternum, at the level of T3–T4.
bone|Manubrium of sternum.articula: Clavicles, first costal cartilages, part of the 2nd cartilage and body of the sternum.
bone|Manubrium of sternum.referencias: Jugular notch; sternal angle (of Louis) at the level of the 2nd costal cartilage and the T4–T5 disc.
bone|Manubrium of sternum.clinica: The sternal angle is a landmark for counting ribs and marks the tracheal bifurcation and the aortic arch.

bone|Maxilla.descripcion: Central paired bone of the facial massif; forms the upper jaw, the anterior hard palate and the orbital floor, and houses the maxillary sinus.
bone|Maxilla.articula: Frontal, ethmoid, nasals, zygomatic, lacrimal, inferior concha, palatine, vomer and contralateral maxilla.
bone|Maxilla.referencias: Infraorbital foramen, anterior nasal spine, alveolar process, maxillary sinus on Waters view radiograph.
bone|Maxilla.clinica: Midfacial fractures are classified according to Le Fort I, II and III.

bone|Medial cuneiform bone.descripcion: The largest of the cuneiforms, on the medial border of the tarsus, between the navicular and the first metatarsal.
bone|Medial cuneiform bone.articula: Navicular, intermediate cuneiform and 1st and 2nd metatarsals.
bone|Medial cuneiform bone.referencias: Palpable on the medial border of the foot; attachment of tibialis anterior; Lisfranc ligament toward the 2nd metatarsal.
bone|Medial cuneiform bone.clinica: The Lisfranc ligament joins its lateral surface with the base of the 2nd metatarsal; its rupture destabilizes the midfoot.

bone|Middle cells of ethmoid bone.descripcion: Intermediate group of air cells of the ethmoidal labyrinth, which form the ethmoidal bulla and drain into the middle meatus.
bone|Middle cells of ethmoid bone.referencias: Ethmoidal bulla on coronal CT and nasal endoscopy; lateral lamina papyracea.

bone|Middle phalanx of finger of foot.descripcion: Intermediate phalanx of the 2nd to 5th toes; absent in the great toe.
bone|Middle phalanx of finger of foot.articula: Proximal phalanx and distal phalanx (proximal and distal interphalangeal joints).
bone|Middle phalanx of finger of foot.referencias: Frequently fused with the distal phalanx in the 5th toe.

bone|Middle phalanx of finger of hand.descripcion: Intermediate phalanx of the 2nd to 5th fingers of the hand; absent in the thumb.
bone|Middle phalanx of finger of hand.articula: Proximal phalanx and distal phalanx (proximal and distal interphalangeal joints).
bone|Middle phalanx of finger of hand.referencias: Attachment of flexor digitorum superficialis on its surfaces; dorsal base with attachment of the central extensor band.
bone|Middle phalanx of finger of hand.clinica: Rupture of the central slip over its base produces boutonnière deformity.

bone|Nasal bone.descripcion: Small, elongated paired bone that forms the bridge or bony dorsum of the nose.
bone|Nasal bone.articula: Frontal, ethmoid, maxilla and contralateral nasal.
bone|Nasal bone.referencias: Upper nasal dorsum palpable; nasion; junction with lateral cartilages (rhinion).
bone|Nasal bone.clinica: It is the facial bone most frequently fractured; rule out septal hematoma.

bone|Nasal septal cartilage.descripcion: Quadrangular lamina of hyaline cartilage that forms the anterior part of the nasal septum.
bone|Nasal septal cartilage.articula: Perpendicular plate of the ethmoid, vomer, anterior nasal spine and nasal bones.
bone|Nasal septal cartilage.referencias: Visible on anterior rhinoscopy; Kiesselbach area on its anteroinferior mucosa.
bone|Nasal septal cartilage.clinica: Undrained septal hematoma can necrose the cartilage and cause a saddle nose.

bone|Navicular bone.descripcion: Bone of the medial tarsus, boat-shaped, between the head of the talus and the cuneiforms.
bone|Navicular bone.articula: Talus, three cuneiforms and occasionally the cuboid.
bone|Navicular bone.referencias: Navicular tuberosity palpable on the medial border of the foot, attachment of tibialis posterior.
bone|Navicular bone.clinica: Navicular stress fractures in athletes often go unnoticed on plain radiograph.

bone|Occipital bone.descripcion: Unpaired posteroinferior bone of the skull that surrounds the foramen magnum and forms the posterior cranial fossa.
bone|Occipital bone.referencias: External occipital protuberance (inion), nuchal lines, occipital condyles, foramen magnum.
bone|Occipital bone.clinica: Tonsillar herniation through the foramen magnum compresses the brainstem.

bone|Palatine bone.descripcion: Paired L-shaped bone that forms the posterior part of the hard palate and part of the lateral nasal wall and orbital floor.
bone|Palatine bone.articula: Maxilla, sphenoid, ethmoid, inferior concha, vomer and contralateral palatine.
bone|Palatine bone.referencias: Greater palatine foramen medial to the 3rd molar; posterior nasal spine.
bone|Palatine bone.clinica: The greater palatine foramen is the site of anesthetic block of the greater palatine nerve.

bone|Parietal bone.descripcion: Paired bone that forms most of the roof and lateral walls of the cranial vault.
bone|Parietal bone.articula: Contralateral parietal, frontal, occipital, temporal and sphenoid.
bone|Parietal bone.referencias: Parietal eminence, sagittal, coronal and lambdoid sutures; grooves for the middle meningeal artery.
bone|Parietal bone.clinica: Fractures at the pterion, where it contacts the sphenoid, can cause epidural hematoma.

bone|Patella.descripcion: Largest sesamoid bone of the body, within the quadriceps tendon, anterior to the knee.
bone|Patella.referencias: Base, apex and borders palpable; tibial tuberosity at its ligament; axial (skyline) view.
bone|Patella.clinica: Lateral dislocation is common in young people; do not confuse bipartite patella with fracture.

bone|Pisiform bone.descripcion: Small sesamoid bone in the tendon of flexor carpi ulnaris, on the palmar surface of the triquetrum.
bone|Pisiform bone.referencias: Palpable at the proximal hypothenar eminence, at the distal wrist crease; boundary of Guyon's canal.
bone|Pisiform bone.clinica: Landmark for locating the ulnar nerve and artery in Guyon's canal.

bone|Posterior cells of ethmoid bone.descripcion: Posterior air cells of the ethmoidal labyrinth, which drain into the superior nasal meatus.
bone|Posterior cells of ethmoid bone.referencias: Basal lamella of the middle concha as anterior limit; Onodi cell on CT.
bone|Posterior cells of ethmoid bone.clinica: An Onodi cell may contain the optic nerve, at risk during endoscopic sinus surgery.

bone|Proximal phalanx of finger of foot.descripcion: Longest phalanx of each toe, joined to the corresponding metatarsal.
bone|Proximal phalanx of finger of foot.articula: Head of the metatarsal (metatarsophalangeal) and middle or distal phalanx.
bone|Proximal phalanx of finger of foot.referencias: Articular base with the metatarsal; deviation of the great toe on dorsoplantar radiograph.
bone|Proximal phalanx of finger of foot.clinica: In hallux valgus the proximal phalanx of the great toe deviates laterally.

bone|Proximal phalanx of finger of hand.descripcion: Longest phalanx of each finger of the hand, joined to the metacarpal.
bone|Proximal phalanx of finger of hand.articula: Head of the metacarpal (metacarpophalangeal) and middle phalanx (or distal in the thumb).
bone|Proximal phalanx of finger of hand.referencias: Palpable on the dorsal surface of the finger; base with collateral ligaments.
bone|Proximal phalanx of finger of hand.clinica: Injury of the ulnar collateral ligament of the thumb MCP joint is skier's thumb.

bone|Radius.descripcion: Lateral bone of the forearm, which rotates around the ulna in pronation-supination.
bone|Radius.articula: Humerus, ulna (proximal and distal radioulnar), scaphoid and lunate.
bone|Radius.referencias: Head of the radius palpable in supination; radial styloid process; Lister's tubercle.
bone|Radius.clinica: Colles fracture (distal radius with dorsal displacement) is typical after a fall onto the outstretched hand.

bone|Sacrum.descripcion: Triangular bone formed by five fused sacral vertebrae, posterior base of the pelvis.
bone|Sacrum.referencias: Promontory, sacral foramina, sacral hiatus, posterior superior iliac spines (dimples of Venus) at the S2 level.
bone|Sacrum.clinica: The sacral hiatus is the access route for caudal epidural anesthesia.

bone|Scaphoid bone.descripcion: Largest bone of the proximal carpal row, on the radial side, which links both rows.
bone|Scaphoid bone.articula: Radius, lunate, capitate, trapezium and trapezoid.
bone|Scaphoid bone.referencias: Palpable in the anatomical snuffbox; scaphoid tubercle in the palm.
bone|Scaphoid bone.clinica: Its retrograde blood supply predisposes to avascular necrosis of the proximal pole after fracture.

bone|Scapula.descripcion: Triangular flat bone of the posterior thorax that forms the posterior part of the shoulder girdle.
bone|Scapula.referencias: Scapular spine at the level of T3, inferior angle at the level of T7, acromion and coracoid process.
bone|Scapula.clinica: Winged scapula is due to injury of the long thoracic nerve (serratus anterior palsy).

bone|Sesamoid bones of foot.descripcion: Small bones embedded in tendons of the foot, constantly two beneath the head of the 1st metatarsal in flexor hallucis brevis.
bone|Sesamoid bones of foot.referencias: Medial (tibial) and lateral (fibular) sesamoids on the sesamoid axial view.
bone|Sesamoid bones of foot.clinica: Sesamoiditis and stress fractures cause plantar pain in runners and dancers; do not confuse with bipartite sesamoid.

bone|Sinus of frontal bone.descripcion: Paired paranasal cavity, often asymmetric, within the frontal bone above the orbits; drains into the middle meatus.
bone|Sinus of frontal bone.referencias: Caldwell view; frontal recess on CT; posterior wall adjacent to the anterior cranial fossa.
bone|Sinus of frontal bone.clinica: Frontal sinusitis can be complicated by osteomyelitis (Pott puffy tumor) or intracranial abscess.

bone|Sinus of sphenoid bone.descripcion: Paranasal cavity in the body of the sphenoid, below the sella turcica; drains into the sphenoethmoidal recess.
bone|Sinus of sphenoid bone.referencias: Superior sella turcica; internal carotid and optic nerve prominences in its lateral walls (CT).
bone|Sinus of sphenoid bone.clinica: Transsphenoidal access route to the pituitary; its infection can cause cavernous sinus thrombosis.

bone|Skeletal system.descripcion: Set of bones, cartilages and joints that supports the body, protects organs, allows movement and houses the bone marrow.
bone|Skeletal system.referencias: The adult has about 206 bones: axial and appendicular skeleton.
bone|Skeletal system.clinica: Osteoporosis is the most frequent bone disease and causes fragility fractures.

bone|Sphenoid bone.descripcion: Unpaired butterfly-shaped bone, in the center of the cranial base, between the anterior and middle cranial fossae.
bone|Sphenoid bone.articula: Frontal, parietals, temporals, occipital, ethmoid, vomer, palatines, zygomatics and processes of the maxilla.
bone|Sphenoid bone.referencias: Sella turcica, greater and lesser wings, pterygoid processes, foramina rotundum, ovale and spinosum.
bone|Sphenoid bone.clinica: The pterion, junction of the greater wing with the frontal, parietal and temporal, overlies the middle meningeal artery.

bone|Stapes.descripcion: Smallest ossicle of the body, in the middle ear; its footplate is fixed to the oval window.
bone|Stapes.referencias: Head, anterior and posterior crura and footplate at the oval window; visible on temporal bone CT.
bone|Stapes.clinica: In otosclerosis its footplate becomes fixed to the oval window, causing conductive hearing loss; treated with stapedectomy.

bone|Talus.descripcion: Tarsal bone that transmits weight from the tibia to the foot; no muscle attachments.
bone|Talus.referencias: Head palpable anterior to the medial malleolus in eversion; trochlea in the tibiofibular mortise.
bone|Talus.clinica: Fractures of the talar neck carry a high risk of avascular necrosis of the body.

bone|Temporal bone.descripcion: Paired bone of the lateral wall and base of the skull that houses the middle and inner ears.
bone|Temporal bone.articula: Parietal, occipital, sphenoid, zygomatic and mandible.
bone|Temporal bone.referencias: Mastoid process, zygomatic process, external acoustic meatus, styloid process.
bone|Temporal bone.clinica: Petrous bone fractures can cause facial palsy, hearing loss and otorrhagia (CSF otorrhea); Battle sign.

bone|Thyroid cartilage.descripcion: Largest cartilage of the larynx, formed by two laminae joined anteriorly; protects the vocal folds at the level of C4–C5.
bone|Thyroid cartilage.articula: Cricoid cartilage (cricothyroid joints); attached to the hyoid by the thyrohyoid membrane.
bone|Thyroid cartilage.referencias: Laryngeal prominence (Adam's apple), superior thyroid notch; superior and inferior horns.
bone|Thyroid cartilage.clinica: The cricothyroid membrane is located below its inferior border for emergency cricothyrotomy.

bone|Tibia.descripcion: Medial and main weight-bearing bone of the leg, between the knee and the ankle.
bone|Tibia.referencias: Tibial tuberosity, subcutaneous anterior border and medial surface, medial malleolus, tibial condyles.
bone|Tibia.clinica: Its subcutaneous medial surface favors open fractures; risk of compartment syndrome.

bone|Trapezium bone.descripcion: Bone of the distal carpal row on the radial side, base of the thumb.
bone|Trapezium bone.referencias: Trapezium tubercle palpable in the thenar eminence; saddle joint with the 1st metacarpal.
bone|Trapezium bone.clinica: Trapeziometacarpal osteoarthritis (rhizarthrosis) is very frequent in older women.

bone|Trapezoid bone.descripcion: Small wedge-shaped bone of the distal carpal row, between the trapezium and the capitate.
bone|Trapezoid bone.referencias: Proximal to the base of the 2nd metacarpal on PA radiograph.
bone|Trapezoid bone.clinica: It is the carpal bone that fractures least frequently.

bone|Triquetrum bone.descripcion: Pyramidal bone of the proximal carpal row on the ulnar side, under the pisiform.
bone|Triquetrum bone.articula: Lunate, pisiform, hamate and articular disc of the radioulnar joint.
bone|Triquetrum bone.referencias: Palpable dorsally distal to the ulnar styloid process in radial deviation.
bone|Triquetrum bone.clinica: Dorsal avulsion fracture is the second most frequent carpal fracture, visible on lateral radiograph.

bone|Ulna.descripcion: Medial bone of the forearm, the principal one at the elbow joint.
bone|Ulna.articula: Humerus (humeroulnar), radius (proximal and distal radioulnar) and articular disc of the carpus.
bone|Ulna.referencias: Olecranon, subcutaneous posterior border, ulnar styloid process, head of the ulna.
bone|Ulna.clinica: Monteggia fracture combines a proximal ulnar fracture with dislocation of the radial head.

bone|Upper canine.descripcion: Tooth with the longest root of the dentition, in the maxillary arch, distal to the lateral incisor.
bone|Upper canine.referencias: Canine eminence of the maxilla; FDI 13 and 23; erupts at around 11–12 years.
bone|Upper canine.clinica: It is the tooth most often retained (impacted) after the third molars, usually in the palate.

bone|Upper first molar tooth.descripcion: Permanent maxillary molar with four cusps and three roots (two buccal and one palatal); erupts at around 6 years.
bone|Upper first molar tooth.referencias: FDI 16 and 26; roots close to the floor of the maxillary sinus; cusp of Carabelli.
bone|Upper first molar tooth.clinica: Its extraction can create an oroantral communication because of the proximity to the maxillary sinus.

bone|Upper first premolar.descripcion: Bicuspid maxillary tooth, usually with two roots (buccal and palatal), distal to the canine.
bone|Upper first premolar.clinica: It is the tooth most often extracted in orthodontic treatment.

bone|Upper lateral incisor.descripcion: Single-rooted cutting tooth of the maxilla, distal to the central incisor and smaller than it.
bone|Upper lateral incisor.referencias: FDI 12 and 22; erupts at around 8–9 years.
bone|Upper lateral incisor.clinica: Frequent agenesis or conical shape; cleft site in cleft lip and palate.

bone|Upper medial incisor.descripcion: Largest cutting tooth of the anterior arch, on each side of the maxillary midline.
bone|Upper medial incisor.referencias: FDI 11 and 21; palatine incisive foramen between them; erupts at around 7–8 years.
bone|Upper medial incisor.clinica: It is the tooth most exposed to dental trauma, especially with increased overjet.

bone|Upper second molar tooth.descripcion: Permanent maxillary molar, generally with three roots, distal to the first molar; erupts at around 12 years.
bone|Upper second molar tooth.referencias: FDI 17 and 27; opening of the parotid duct opposite it on the buccal mucosa.
bone|Upper second molar tooth.clinica: The papilla of Stensen's duct opposite this tooth is a landmark for parotid sialography.

bone|Upper second premolar.descripcion: Bicuspid maxillary tooth, usually single-rooted, mesial to the first molar.
bone|Upper second premolar.referencias: FDI 15 and 25; apex close to the floor of the maxillary sinus.
bone|Upper second premolar.clinica: Periapical infections can spread to the maxillary sinus (odontogenic sinusitis).

bone|Vertebra.descripcion: Bone of the vertebral column formed by a body and a vertebral arch surrounding the vertebral canal; 33 in total.
bone|Vertebra.articula: Adjacent vertebrae (intervertebral discs and zygapophyseal joints); ribs in the thoracic ones.
bone|Vertebra.referencias: Palpable spinous processes (C7 prominent, L4 at the level of the iliac crests); pedicles on AP radiograph.
bone|Vertebra.clinica: Osteoporotic vertebral compression fractures are the most frequent fragility fractures.

bone|Vomer.descripcion: Unpaired, thin, trapezoidal bone that forms the posteroinferior part of the nasal septum.
bone|Vomer.articula: Sphenoid, ethmoid, maxillae, palatines and septal nasal cartilage.
bone|Vomer.referencias: Free posterior border separating the choanae; alae of the vomer on the body of the sphenoid.
bone|Vomer.clinica: It takes part in bony septal deviations, which may require septoplasty.

bone|Xiphoid process.descripcion: Small, variable inferior portion of the sternum, cartilaginous in the young and ossified with age, at the T10 level.
bone|Xiphoid process.referencias: Palpable in the epigastrium at the apex of the infrasternal angle; level T10.
bone|Xiphoid process.clinica: CPR compressions over it can fracture it and injure the liver.

bone|Zygomatic bone.descripcion: Paired bone of the cheek that forms the malar prominence and part of the lateral wall and floor of the orbit.
bone|Zygomatic bone.referencias: Malar prominence, zygomatic arch, frontozygomatic suture palpable at the lateral orbital rim.
bone|Zygomatic bone.clinica: Tripod fracture (zygomaticomaxillary complex) causes malar flattening and infraorbital paresthesia.

bone|metacarpal bone.descripcion: Each of the five long bones of the palm of the hand, numbered from the thumb (I) to the little finger (V).
bone|metacarpal bone.articula: Bones of the distal carpal row, adjacent metacarpals and proximal phalanges.
bone|metacarpal bone.referencias: Heads palpable as knuckles; base of the 1st in the snuffbox; subcutaneous dorsal shafts.
bone|metacarpal bone.clinica: Fracture of the neck of the 5th metacarpal (boxer's fracture) is the most frequent.

bone|metatarsal bone.descripcion: Each of the five long bones of the forefoot, numbered from medial (I) to lateral (V).
bone|metatarsal bone.articula: Cuneiforms or cuboid, adjacent metatarsals and proximal phalanges.
bone|metatarsal bone.referencias: Tuberosity of the 5th metatarsal palpable on the lateral border; heads on the sole; sesamoids of the 1st.
bone|metatarsal bone.clinica: Jones fracture (metaphyseal-diaphyseal junction of the 5th) with risk of nonunion; stress fractures of the 2nd.

bone|rib.descripcion: Each of the twelve pairs of curved bones that form the thoracic wall; true (1–7), false (8–10) and floating (11–12).
bone|rib.articula: Thoracic vertebrae (costovertebral and costotransverse) and costal cartilages anteriorly.
bone|rib.referencias: Costal angle, costal groove with neurovascular bundle; 2nd rib at the sternal angle for counting them.
bone|rib.clinica: Flail chest occurs with fractures of three or more consecutive ribs at two points.

rest|????????.descripcion: Name not recognizable in the source atlas; does not correspond to an identifiable anatomical structure.

rest|?x.descripcion: Name not recognizable in the source atlas; does not correspond to an identifiable anatomical structure.

rest|Abdominal aorta.descripcion: Segment of the descending aorta from the aortic hiatus of the diaphragm (T12) to its bifurcation at the level of L4, retroperitoneal and to the left of the midline.
rest|Abdominal aorta.origen: Continuation of the thoracic aorta at the aortic hiatus (T12)
rest|Abdominal aorta.destino: Bifurcates into the right and left common iliac arteries (L4); continues as the median sacral artery
rest|Abdominal aorta.ramas: Celiac trunk, superior and inferior mesenteric, renal, middle suprarenal, gonadal, inferior phrenic, lumbar, median sacral
rest|Abdominal aorta.territorio: Abdominal viscera, posterior abdominal wall, diaphragm, pelvis and lower limbs
rest|Abdominal aorta.clinica: Most frequent site of aortic aneurysm (infrarenal); its rupture is a life-threatening emergency.

rest|Accessory branch of middle meningea.es: Accessory branch of middle meningeal artery
rest|Accessory branch of middle meningea.descripcion: Small branch that enters the skull through the foramen ovale; also called the accessory meningeal artery.
rest|Accessory branch of middle meningea.origen: Middle meningeal artery or maxillary artery
rest|Accessory branch of middle meningea.territorio: Pterygoid muscles, tensor veli palatini, trigeminal ganglion and neighboring dura mater

rest|Angular artery.descripcion: Terminal branch of the facial artery that ascends alongside the nose to the medial angle of the eye.
rest|Angular artery.destino: Anastomoses with the dorsal nasal artery (branch of the ophthalmic)
rest|Angular artery.territorio: Side of the nose, lacrimal sac, orbicularis oculi muscle and cheek
rest|Angular artery.clinica: Anastomosis between external and internal carotid; clinically relevant communication route in carotid occlusion.

rest|Anterior basal segmental artery of.es: Anterior basal segmental artery of left lung
rest|Anterior basal segmental artery of.la: Arteria segmentalis basalis anterior pulmonis sinistri
rest|Anterior basal segmental artery of.descripcion: Branch of the left pulmonary artery (basal part) that accompanies the anterior basal segmental bronchus of the left lower lobe.
rest|Anterior basal segmental artery of.origen: Inferior lobar artery (basal part) of the left pulmonary artery
rest|Anterior basal segmental artery of.territorio: Anterior basal segment (S8) of the left lower lobe
rest|Anterior basal segmental artery of.funcion: Carries deoxygenated blood for gas exchange

rest|Anterior basal segmental artery of.es: Anterior basal segmental artery of right lung
rest|Anterior basal segmental artery of.la: Arteria segmentalis basalis anterior pulmonis dextri
rest|Anterior basal segmental artery of.descripcion: Branch of the basal part of the right inferior lobar artery that accompanies the anterior basal segmental bronchus.
rest|Anterior basal segmental artery of.origen: Inferior lobar artery of the right pulmonary artery
rest|Anterior basal segmental artery of.territorio: Anterior basal segment (S8) of the right lower lobe
rest|Anterior basal segmental artery of.funcion: Carries deoxygenated blood for gas exchange

rest|Anterior branch of renal artery.descripcion: Prepelvic division of the renal artery at the hilum, which gives rise to the superior, anterosuperior, anteroinferior and inferior segmental arteries.
rest|Anterior branch of renal artery.destino: Anterior segmental arteries of the kidney
rest|Anterior branch of renal artery.ramas: Superior, anterior superior, anterior inferior and inferior segmental arteries
rest|Anterior branch of renal artery.territorio: Most of the anterior part of the renal parenchyma
rest|Anterior branch of renal artery.clinica: Segmental arteries are end arteries: their occlusion produces infarction of the corresponding renal segment.

rest|Anterior cerebral artery.descripcion: Medial terminal branch of the internal carotid; runs in the longitudinal fissure over the corpus callosum.
rest|Anterior cerebral artery.destino: Pericallosal artery and medial cortical branches to the parieto-occipital sulcus
rest|Anterior cerebral artery.ramas: Anterior communicating (junction), distal medial striate artery (of Heubner), orbitofrontal, frontopolar, callosomarginal, pericallosal
rest|Anterior cerebral artery.territorio: Medial surface of the frontal and parietal lobes, corpus callosum, part of the caudate nucleus and internal capsule
rest|Anterior cerebral artery.clinica: Its occlusion produces paresis and sensory loss of the contralateral lower limb.

rest|Anterior circumflex humeral artery.descripcion: Small artery that winds around the front of the surgical neck of the humerus, deep to coracobrachialis and biceps.
rest|Anterior circumflex humeral artery.origen: Third part of the axillary artery
rest|Anterior circumflex humeral artery.destino: Anastomoses with the posterior circumflex humeral
rest|Anterior circumflex humeral artery.ramas: Ascending branch to the intertubercular groove
rest|Anterior circumflex humeral artery.territorio: Humeral head, shoulder joint, tendon of the long head of biceps
rest|Anterior circumflex humeral artery.clinica: Its ascending branch is the main blood supply of the humeral head; relevant in necrosis after proximal fractures.

rest|Anterior communicating artery.descripcion: Short artery that joins both anterior cerebral arteries in the longitudinal fissure; anterior part of the cerebral arterial circle (of Willis).
rest|Anterior communicating artery.origen: Joins the right and left anterior cerebral arteries
rest|Anterior communicating artery.territorio: Lamina terminalis, optic chiasm, anterior hypothalamus
rest|Anterior communicating artery.funcion: Anastomosis that allows collateral flow between both hemispheres
rest|Anterior communicating artery.clinica: Most frequent location of intracranial saccular aneurysms.

rest|Anterior deep temporal artery.descripcion: Branch of the pterygoid part of the maxillary that ascends between the temporal bone and the temporalis muscle.
rest|Anterior deep temporal artery.territorio: Temporalis muscle; anastomosis with the lacrimal

rest|Anterior division of internal iliac.es: Anterior division of internal iliac artery
rest|Anterior division of internal iliac.descripcion: Anterior division of the internal iliac in the pelvis, origin of most visceral branches and of the inferior gluteal and obturator branches.
rest|Anterior division of internal iliac.destino: Ends as the internal pudendal and inferior gluteal arteries
rest|Anterior division of internal iliac.ramas: Umbilical (superior vesical), obturator, inferior vesical/vaginal, uterine, middle rectal, internal pudendal, inferior gluteal
rest|Anterior division of internal iliac.territorio: Pelvic viscera, perineum, gluteal region and medial compartment of the thigh
rest|Anterior division of internal iliac.clinica: Ligation or embolization of its branches is used to control pelvic or postpartum hemorrhage.

rest|Anterior ethmoidal artery.descripcion: Branch of the ophthalmic that passes through the anterior ethmoidal canal, crosses the anterior cranial fossa and descends into the nasal cavity.
rest|Anterior ethmoidal artery.destino: Ends as the external nasal branch on the nasal dorsum
rest|Anterior ethmoidal artery.ramas: Anterior meningeal branch, septal and anterior lateral nasal branches, external nasal branch
rest|Anterior ethmoidal artery.territorio: Anterior ethmoidal cells, frontal sinus, anterior dura mater, anterosuperior part of the nasal cavity
rest|Anterior ethmoidal artery.clinica: Its injury in endoscopic sinus surgery causes orbital hemorrhage; source of posterior-superior epistaxis.

rest|Anterior inferior cerebellar artery.descripcion: Branch of the inferior part of the basilar that runs laterally toward the cerebellopontine angle.
rest|Anterior inferior cerebellar artery.territorio: Anteroinferior surface of the cerebellum, flocculus, inferolateral part of the pons, inner ear
rest|Anterior inferior cerebellar artery.clinica: Its occlusion produces lateral inferior pontine syndrome with ipsilateral hearing loss and vertigo.

rest|Anterior inferior pancreaticoduoden.descripcion: Branch of the inferior pancreaticoduodenal that ascends in front of the head of the pancreas.
rest|Anterior inferior pancreaticoduoden.origen: Inferior pancreaticoduodenal artery (from the superior mesenteric)
rest|Anterior inferior pancreaticoduoden.destino: Anastomoses with the anterior superior pancreaticoduodenal
rest|Anterior inferior pancreaticoduoden.territorio: Head of the pancreas and duodenum
rest|Anterior inferior pancreaticoduoden.clinica: Part of the celiac-mesenteric anastomosis, a collateral pathway in celiac trunk stenosis.

rest|Anterior interventricular artery.la: Ramus interventricularis anterior arteriae coronariae sinistrae
rest|Anterior interventricular artery.descripcion: Branch of the left coronary that descends in the anterior interventricular groove to the cardiac apex (left anterior descending artery).
rest|Anterior interventricular artery.destino: Wraps around the apex and anastomoses with the posterior interventricular
rest|Anterior interventricular artery.ramas: Diagonal (lateral) branches, interventricular septal branches, conus arteriosus branch
rest|Anterior interventricular artery.territorio: Anterior wall of both ventricles, anterior two thirds of the interventricular septum, apex
rest|Anterior interventricular artery.clinica: Its proximal occlusion produces extensive anterior infarction (the 'widowmaker' artery).

rest|Anterior papillary muscle of right.es: Anterior papillary muscle of right ventricle
rest|Anterior papillary muscle of right.descripcion: Largest papillary muscle of the right ventricle, on the anterior wall; receives the septomarginal trabecula.
rest|Anterior papillary muscle of right.funcion: Through the chordae tendineae it prevents eversion of the anterior and posterior leaflets of the tricuspid valve in systole
rest|Anterior papillary muscle of right.clinica: The septomarginal trabecula carries the right bundle branch of the bundle of His to its base.

rest|Anterior segmental artery of left l.es: Anterior segmental artery of left lung
rest|Anterior segmental artery of left l.descripcion: Branch of the left pulmonary artery for the anterior segment of the left upper lobe.
rest|Anterior segmental artery of left l.territorio: Anterior segment (S3) of the left upper lobe
rest|Anterior segmental artery of left l.funcion: Carries deoxygenated blood for gas exchange

rest|Anterior segmental artery of right.es: Anterior segmental artery of right lung
rest|Anterior segmental artery of right.descripcion: Branch of the right superior lobar artery (anterior trunk) for the anterior segment of the right upper lobe.
rest|Anterior segmental artery of right.origen: Superior lobar artery of the right pulmonary artery
rest|Anterior segmental artery of right.territorio: Anterior segment (S3) of the right upper lobe
rest|Anterior segmental artery of right.funcion: Carries deoxygenated blood for gas exchange

rest|Anterior semilunar leaflet of pulmo.es: Anterior semilunar cusp of pulmonary valve
rest|Anterior semilunar leaflet of pulmo.la: Valvula semilunaris anterior valvae trunci pulmonalis
rest|Anterior semilunar leaflet of pulmo.descripcion: One of the three semilunar cusps of the pulmonary trunk valve, located anteriorly, with nodule and lunules.
rest|Anterior semilunar leaflet of pulmo.funcion: Prevents backflow of blood from the pulmonary trunk into the right ventricle in diastole
rest|Anterior semilunar leaflet of pulmo.clinica: The pulmonary valve is auscultated in the left parasternal second intercostal space.

rest|Anterior septal branches of anterio.es: Anterior septal branches of anterior ethmoidal artery
rest|Anterior septal branches of anterio.la: Rami septales anteriores arteriae ethmoidalis anterioris
rest|Anterior septal branches of anterio.descripcion: Branches of the anterior ethmoidal that supply the anterosuperior portion of the nasal septum.
rest|Anterior septal branches of anterio.territorio: Anterosuperior part of the nasal septum
rest|Anterior septal branches of anterio.clinica: They take part in Little's area, the most frequent site of anterior epistaxis.

rest|Anterior spinal artery.descripcion: Single artery in the anterior median fissure of the cord, formed by branches of both vertebrals and reinforced by segmental medullary arteries.
rest|Anterior spinal artery.origen: Union of branches of both vertebral arteries
rest|Anterior spinal artery.destino: Descends to the conus medullaris and filum terminale
rest|Anterior spinal artery.territorio: Anterior two thirds of the spinal cord and medial part of the medulla oblongata
rest|Anterior spinal artery.clinica: Its occlusion causes anterior cord syndrome: paraplegia and loss of pain and temperature sensation with preserved proprioception.

rest|Anterior temporal branch.descripcion: Cortical branch that supplies the anterior part of the temporal lobe; may arise from the middle cerebral or from the posterior cerebral.
rest|Anterior temporal branch.origen: Middle cerebral artery (insular/cortical part) or posterior cerebral artery
rest|Anterior temporal branch.territorio: Pole and anterior part of the temporal lobe

rest|Anterior tibial artery.descripcion: Terminal branch of the popliteal that passes through the interosseous membrane and descends in the anterior compartment of the leg.
rest|Anterior tibial artery.destino: Continues as the dorsalis pedis artery at the ankle
rest|Anterior tibial artery.ramas: Anterior and posterior tibial recurrent, anterior medial and lateral malleolar, muscular branches
rest|Anterior tibial artery.territorio: Anterior compartment of the leg, knee and ankle
rest|Anterior tibial artery.clinica: Affected in anterior compartment syndrome of the leg.

rest|Aortic arch.descripcion: Curved segment of the aorta in the superior mediastinum, from the right 2nd sternocostal joint to T4, passing over the left main bronchus.
rest|Aortic arch.destino: Continues as the descending thoracic aorta at the level of T4
rest|Aortic arch.ramas: Brachiocephalic trunk, left common carotid, left subclavian
rest|Aortic arch.clinica: Aortic coarctation is usually located distal to the left subclavian, near the ligamentum arteriosum.

rest|Apical segmental artery of left lun.es: Apical segmental artery of left lung
rest|Apical segmental artery of left lun.descripcion: Branch of the left pulmonary artery for the apical portion of the apicoposterior segment of the left upper lobe.
rest|Apical segmental artery of left lun.territorio: Apical segment (S1) of the left upper lobe
rest|Apical segmental artery of left lun.funcion: Carries deoxygenated blood for gas exchange

rest|Apical segmental artery of right lu.es: Apical segmental artery of right lung
rest|Apical segmental artery of right lu.descripcion: Branch of the anterior trunk (superior lobar artery) of the right pulmonary for the apical segment.
rest|Apical segmental artery of right lu.origen: Superior lobar artery of the right pulmonary artery
rest|Apical segmental artery of right lu.territorio: Apical segment (S1) of the right upper lobe
rest|Apical segmental artery of right lu.funcion: Carries deoxygenated blood for gas exchange

rest|Appendicular artery.descripcion: Artery that descends behind the terminal ileum and runs in the free border of the mesoappendix.
rest|Appendicular artery.origen: Ileocolic artery (ileal or posterior cecal branch)
rest|Appendicular artery.destino: Ends at the tip of the appendix
rest|Appendicular artery.clinica: It is an end artery: its thrombosis in appendicitis favors gangrene and perforation; it is ligated in appendectomy.

rest|Arcuate artery.descripcion: Artery that crosses laterally the dorsum of the foot over the bases of the metatarsals.
rest|Arcuate artery.destino: Anastomoses with the lateral tarsal and lateral plantar
rest|Arcuate artery.territorio: Dorsum of the foot and toes

rest|Artery of central sulcus.descripcion: Cortical branch of the middle cerebral that runs in the central (rolandic) sulcus.
rest|Artery of central sulcus.territorio: Motor and somatosensory cortex adjacent to the central sulcus (lateral)
rest|Artery of central sulcus.clinica: Its involvement produces contralateral motor and sensory deficit predominantly in the face and upper limb.

rest|Artery of precentral sulcus.descripcion: Cortical branch of the middle cerebral that ascends in the precentral sulcus.
rest|Artery of precentral sulcus.territorio: Posterior precentral gyrus and neighboring parts of the middle and inferior frontal gyri

rest|Artery of pterygoid canal.descripcion: Small artery that runs through the pterygoid (vidian) canal accompanying the nerve of the same name.
rest|Artery of pterygoid canal.origen: Maxillary artery (pterygopalatine part); sometimes internal carotid
rest|Artery of pterygoid canal.territorio: Upper part of the pharynx, auditory tube and tympanic cavity

rest|Ascending aorta.descripcion: First segment of the aorta, from the aortic orifice of the left ventricle to the right 2nd sternocostal joint, within the pericardium.
rest|Ascending aorta.ramas: Right and left coronary arteries (from the aortic sinuses)
rest|Ascending aorta.clinica: Site of Stanford type A aortic dissection, a surgical emergency.

rest|Ascending branch of left colic arte.es: Ascending branch of left colic artery
rest|Ascending branch of left colic arte.descripcion: Branch of the left colic that ascends toward the left colic flexure and anastomoses with the middle colic.
rest|Ascending branch of left colic arte.destino: Anastomoses with the middle colic artery forming the marginal artery
rest|Ascending branch of left colic arte.territorio: Distal part of the transverse colon and left colic flexure
rest|Ascending branch of left colic arte.clinica: Griffiths watershed zone, vulnerable to ischemic colitis.

rest|Ascending pharyngeal artery.descripcion: Slender branch of the external carotid that ascends between the internal carotid and the pharynx to the skull base.
rest|Ascending pharyngeal artery.origen: External carotid artery (medial surface, near its origin)
rest|Ascending pharyngeal artery.ramas: Pharyngeal branches, inferior tympanic, posterior meningeal, prevertebral branches
rest|Ascending pharyngeal artery.territorio: Pharynx, prevertebral muscles, middle ear, palatine tonsil and dura mater of the posterior fossa

rest|Axillary artery.descripcion: Continuation of the subclavian from the lateral border of the 1st rib to the inferior border of teres major; divided into three parts by pectoralis minor.
rest|Axillary artery.origen: Subclavian artery (lateral border of the first rib)
rest|Axillary artery.destino: Continues as the brachial artery at the inferior border of teres major
rest|Axillary artery.ramas: Superior thoracic, thoracoacromial, lateral thoracic, subscapular, anterior and posterior circumflex humeral
rest|Axillary artery.territorio: Thoracic wall, scapular region, shoulder and upper limb
rest|Axillary artery.clinica: It may be compressed or injured in shoulder dislocations and fractures of the humeral neck.

rest|Basilar artery.descripcion: Unpaired artery formed by the union of both vertebrals at the inferior border of the pons, ascending in the basilar groove.
rest|Basilar artery.origen: Union of the right and left vertebral arteries
rest|Basilar artery.destino: Bifurcates into the posterior cerebral arteries at the superior border of the pons
rest|Basilar artery.ramas: Anterior inferior cerebellar, labyrinthine, pontine branches, mesencephalic, superior cerebellar, posterior cerebral
rest|Basilar artery.territorio: Brainstem, cerebellum, inner ear, occipital lobes and part of the temporal lobes
rest|Basilar artery.clinica: Its thrombosis can produce locked-in syndrome or coma.

rest|Bifurcation of pulmonary trunk.descripcion: Point of division of the pulmonary trunk into the right and left pulmonary arteries, under the aortic arch at the level of T4-T5.
rest|Bifurcation of pulmonary trunk.clinica: Joined to the aortic arch by the ligamentum arteriosum; site of saddle embolus (massive pulmonary embolism).

rest|Brachial artery.descripcion: Continuation of the axillary in the arm, medial to the humerus alongside the median nerve, to the cubital fossa.
rest|Brachial artery.origen: Axillary artery (inferior border of teres major)
rest|Brachial artery.destino: Divides into the radial and ulnar arteries in the cubital fossa (neck of the radius)
rest|Brachial artery.ramas: Deep brachial, superior and inferior ulnar collaterals, nutrient humeral, muscular
rest|Brachial artery.territorio: Arm, elbow and, through its terminal branches, forearm and hand
rest|Brachial artery.clinica: Used to measure blood pressure; in supracondylar fractures its injury can cause Volkmann ischemic contracture.

rest|Brachiocephalic trunk.descripcion: First and largest branch of the aortic arch; ascends to the right of the trachea to the right sternoclavicular joint.
rest|Brachiocephalic trunk.destino: Divides into the right subclavian and right common carotid behind the right sternoclavicular joint
rest|Brachiocephalic trunk.ramas: Right subclavian, right common carotid (inconstant: thyroid ima artery)
rest|Brachiocephalic trunk.territorio: Right half of the head and neck and right upper limb
rest|Brachiocephalic trunk.clinica: Risk of injury in low tracheostomy; can cause tracheo-innominate fistula.

rest|Branch to angular gyrus.descripcion: Terminal cortical branch of the middle cerebral that emerges from the posterior end of the lateral sulcus toward the angular gyrus.
rest|Branch to angular gyrus.origen: Middle cerebral artery (cortical part, terminal branch)
rest|Branch to angular gyrus.territorio: Angular gyrus and posterior inferior parietal lobule
rest|Branch to angular gyrus.clinica: Its occlusion in the dominant hemisphere can cause Gerstmann syndrome or alexia.

rest|Buccal artery.descripcion: Branch of the second part of the maxillary that runs with the buccal nerve over the buccinator.
rest|Buccal artery.destino: Anastomoses with branches of the facial and infraorbital
rest|Buccal artery.territorio: Buccinator muscle, skin and mucosa of the cheek

rest|Calcaneal branches of fibular arter.descripcion: Terminal branches of the fibular artery to the lateral surface of the calcaneus.
rest|Calcaneal branches of fibular arter.territorio: Lateral and posterior surface of the heel

rest|Calcaneal branches of posterior tib.es: Calcaneal branches of posterior tibial artery
rest|Calcaneal branches of posterior tib.descripcion: Branches that pierce the flexor retinaculum toward the medial surface of the heel.
rest|Calcaneal branches of posterior tib.territorio: Skin and tissues of the medial and plantar surface of the heel

rest|Callosomarginal artery.descripcion: Branch of the anterior cerebral artery that runs in the cingulate sulcus, parallel to the pericallosal artery.
rest|Callosomarginal artery.ramas: Anteromedial, intermediomedial and posteromedial frontal branches, cingular branch, paracentral branch
rest|Callosomarginal artery.territorio: Medial surface of the frontal and parietal lobes, cingulate gyrus, paracentral lobule
rest|Callosomarginal artery.clinica: Involvement of the paracentral lobule produces contralateral lower limb deficit.

rest|Central retinal artery.descripcion: First branch of the ophthalmic artery; it penetrates the optic nerve and emerges at the optic disc, dividing into retinal branches.
rest|Central retinal artery.destino: Superior and inferior temporal and nasal branches of the retina
rest|Central retinal artery.ramas: Superior and inferior temporal and nasal arterioles
rest|Central retinal artery.clinica: It is an end artery: its occlusion causes sudden monocular blindness with a macular cherry-red spot.

rest|Circumflex artery of heart.es: Circumflex branch of the left coronary artery
rest|Circumflex artery of heart.descripcion: Branch of the left coronary artery that runs in the left coronary sulcus toward the posterior surface of the heart.
