rest|Circumflex artery of heart.destino: Ends on the posterior surface of the left ventricle; in left dominance it gives off the posterior interventricular artery
rest|Circumflex artery of heart.ramas: Left marginal, atrial and posterior left ventricular branches, sometimes the sinoatrial nodal artery
rest|Circumflex artery of heart.territorio: Left atrium and lateral and posterior walls of the left ventricle
rest|Circumflex artery of heart.clinica: Its occlusion produces lateral infarction, often poorly visible on the ECG.

rest|Circumflex scapular artery.descripcion: Branch of the subscapular artery that passes through the triangular space toward the infraspinous fossa.
rest|Circumflex scapular artery.destino: Anastomoses with the suprascapular artery and the deep branch of the transverse cervical artery
rest|Circumflex scapular artery.territorio: Infraspinatus, teres major and teres minor muscles, skin of the scapular region
rest|Circumflex scapular artery.clinica: Takes part in the scapular anastomosis, a collateral route in axillary artery occlusion; basis of the scapular flap.

rest|Coeliac trunk.descripcion: Short trunk arising from the anterior surface of the abdominal aorta at T12, just below the aortic hiatus.
rest|Coeliac trunk.destino: Trifurcates into the left gastric, splenic and common hepatic arteries
rest|Coeliac trunk.ramas: Left gastric artery, splenic artery, common hepatic artery
rest|Coeliac trunk.territorio: Foregut derivatives: abdominal esophagus, stomach, proximal duodenum, liver, gallbladder, pancreas and spleen
rest|Coeliac trunk.clinica: May be compressed by the median arcuate ligament (Dunbar syndrome).

rest|Colic branch of ileocolic artery.es: Colic branch of the ileocolic artery
rest|Colic branch of ileocolic artery.descripcion: Ascending branch of the ileocolic artery that runs up alongside the ascending colon.
rest|Colic branch of ileocolic artery.destino: Anastomoses with the right colic artery
rest|Colic branch of ileocolic artery.territorio: Lower part of the ascending colon

rest|Common hepatic artery.descripcion: Branch of the coeliac trunk that runs to the right along the upper border of the pancreas.
rest|Common hepatic artery.destino: Continues as the proper hepatic artery after giving off the gastroduodenal artery
rest|Common hepatic artery.ramas: Gastroduodenal artery, proper hepatic artery (and right gastric artery)
rest|Common hepatic artery.territorio: Liver, gallbladder, stomach, duodenum and pancreas
rest|Common hepatic artery.clinica: Landmark in gastric and pancreatic lymphadenectomies (common hepatic nodes).

rest|Common iliac artery.descripcion: Terminal branch of the abdominal aorta that descends laterally to the sacroiliac joint.
rest|Common iliac artery.destino: Divides into the external and internal iliac arteries in front of the sacroiliac joint
rest|Common iliac artery.territorio: Pelvis, perineum, gluteal region and lower limb
rest|Common iliac artery.clinica: The right common iliac artery crosses the left common iliac vein (May-Thurner syndrome).

rest|Common interosseous artery.descripcion: Short branch of the ulnar artery, near its origin, that divides at the upper border of the interosseous membrane.
rest|Common interosseous artery.destino: Divides into the anterior and posterior interosseous arteries
rest|Common interosseous artery.ramas: Anterior interosseous, posterior interosseous (with the interosseous recurrent)
rest|Common interosseous artery.territorio: Deep muscles of the forearm, radius and ulna

rest|Common palmar digital arteries.descripcion: Three arteries that arise from the convexity of the superficial palmar arch and descend over the lumbricals.
rest|Common palmar digital arteries.destino: Each divides into two proper palmar digital arteries

rest|Common plantar digital arteries.descripcion: Distal continuation of the plantar metatarsal arteries in the interdigital spaces.
rest|Common plantar digital arteries.destino: Divide into the proper plantar digital arteries

rest|Costocervical trunk.descripcion: Short trunk from the posterior surface of the subclavian artery that arches backward over the pleural dome.
rest|Costocervical trunk.origen: Subclavian artery (second part on the right side; first part on the left)
rest|Costocervical trunk.destino: Divides into the supreme intercostal artery and the deep cervical artery
rest|Costocervical trunk.ramas: Supreme intercostal artery, deep cervical artery
rest|Costocervical trunk.territorio: First two intercostal spaces and deep posterior muscles of the neck

rest|Deep artery of penis.descripcion: Terminal branch of the internal pudendal artery that penetrates the corpus cavernosum and runs through its center.
rest|Deep artery of penis.territorio: Erectile tissue of the corpus cavernosum
rest|Deep artery of penis.funcion: Its dilation fills the cavernous spaces and produces erection
rest|Deep artery of penis.clinica: Target of vasodilators in erectile dysfunction; affected in atherosclerosis.

rest|Deep brachial artery.descripcion: Branch of the brachial artery that accompanies the radial nerve in the radial groove of the humerus.
rest|Deep brachial artery.destino: Ends as the middle and radial collateral arteries (elbow anastomosis)
rest|Deep brachial artery.ramas: Deltoid branch, humeral nutrient artery, middle collateral, radial collateral
rest|Deep brachial artery.territorio: Triceps brachii, humerus and posterior part of the arm
rest|Deep brachial artery.clinica: May be injured together with the radial nerve in fractures of the humeral shaft.

rest|Deep branch of transverse cervical.es: Deep branch of the transverse cervical artery
rest|Deep branch of transverse cervical.descripcion: Branch that descends along the medial border of the scapula, deep to the rhomboids (dorsal scapular artery when it arises from the subclavian artery).
rest|Deep branch of transverse cervical.destino: Anastomoses with the circumflex scapular and suprascapular arteries
rest|Deep branch of transverse cervical.territorio: Rhomboid muscles, levator scapulae and serratus anterior
rest|Deep branch of transverse cervical.clinica: Takes part in the scapular anastomosis, a collateral route in subclavian-axillary occlusion.

rest|Deep cervical artery.descripcion: Branch of the costocervical trunk that ascends between the semispinalis capitis and semispinalis cervicis.
rest|Deep cervical artery.destino: Anastomoses with the descending branch of the occipital artery and branches of the vertebral artery
rest|Deep cervical artery.territorio: Deep posterior muscles of the neck

rest|Deep external pudendal artery.descripcion: Branch of the femoral artery that crosses medially over the pectineus and adductor longus, deep to the fascia lata.
rest|Deep external pudendal artery.territorio: Skin of the scrotum or labia majora and anterior perineum

rest|Deep femoral artery.descripcion: Large branch of the femoral artery, 3-4 cm below the inguinal ligament, that descends posterior to the adductor longus.
rest|Deep femoral artery.destino: Ends as the fourth perforating artery
rest|Deep femoral artery.ramas: Medial and lateral circumflex femoral arteries, perforating arteries (three or four)
rest|Deep femoral artery.territorio: Thigh muscles (medial and posterior compartments), hip and femur
rest|Deep femoral artery.clinica: Main collateral route in occlusion of the superficial femoral artery.

rest|Deep palmar arch.descripcion: Arterial arch over the metacarpal bases, deep to the flexor tendons, proximal to the superficial arch.
rest|Deep palmar arch.origen: Mainly the radial artery, completed by the deep palmar branch of the ulnar artery
rest|Deep palmar arch.ramas: Palmar metacarpal arteries, perforating branches, recurrent branches
rest|Deep palmar arch.territorio: Interosseous muscles and deep structures of the hand
rest|Deep palmar arch.clinica: Lies about 1-2 cm proximal to the superficial arch; important in deep palmar wounds.

rest|Deep plantar artery.descripcion: Branch of the dorsalis pedis artery that passes to the plantar plane through the first interosseous space.
rest|Deep plantar artery.destino: Joins the lateral plantar artery to complete the deep plantar arch
rest|Deep plantar artery.territorio: Sole of the foot (via the plantar arch)

rest|Descending branch of lateral circum.es: Descending branch of the lateral circumflex femoral artery
rest|Descending branch of lateral circum.la: Ramus descendens arteriae circumflexae femoris lateralis
rest|Descending branch of lateral circum.descripcion: Branch that descends under the rectus femoris alongside the nerve to the vastus lateralis.
rest|Descending branch of lateral circum.territorio: Vastus lateralis and anterolateral thigh muscles
rest|Descending branch of lateral circum.clinica: Pedicle of the anterolateral thigh flap, widely used in reconstructive surgery.

rest|Descending branch of left colic art.es: Descending branch of the left colic artery
rest|Descending branch of left colic art.descripcion: Branch of the left colic artery that descends toward the descending colon.

rest|Descending palatine artery.descripcion: Branch of the pterygopalatine part of the maxillary artery that descends through the greater palatine canal.
rest|Descending palatine artery.destino: Divides into the greater and lesser palatine arteries
rest|Descending palatine artery.ramas: Greater palatine artery, lesser palatine arteries
rest|Descending palatine artery.territorio: Hard and soft palate, palatal gingiva, palatine tonsil

rest|Distal lateral striate branches.descripcion: Lateral lenticulostriate arteries that arise from the insular or distal part of the middle cerebral artery and penetrate the anterior perforated substance.
rest|Distal lateral striate branches.territorio: Putamen, lateral globus pallidus, internal capsule and caudate nucleus
rest|Distal lateral striate branches.clinica: The lenticulostriate arteries are a typical site of hypertensive hemorrhage and lacunar infarcts.

rest|Dorsal artery of penis.descripcion: Terminal branch of the internal pudendal artery that runs on the dorsum of the penis, between the deep dorsal vein and the dorsal nerve.
rest|Dorsal artery of penis.territorio: Glans, foreskin, skin and fasciae of the penis

rest|Dorsal carpal anastomosis.descripcion: Arterial network on the dorsum of the carpus, deep to the extensor tendons.
rest|Dorsal carpal anastomosis.origen: Dorsal carpal branches of the radial and ulnar arteries, and the anterior and posterior interosseous arteries
rest|Dorsal carpal anastomosis.territorio: Bones and joints of the carpus and dorsum of the hand

rest|Dorsal carpal branch of ulnar arter.es: Dorsal carpal branch of the ulnar artery
rest|Dorsal carpal branch of ulnar arter.descripcion: Branch that winds around the ulnar border of the wrist under the tendon of the flexor carpi ulnaris.
rest|Dorsal carpal branch of ulnar arter.territorio: Dorsum of the carpus; may give rise to the dorsal metacarpal artery of the 5th digit

rest|Dorsal digital arteries of foot.es: Dorsal digital arteries of the foot
rest|Dorsal digital arteries of foot.descripcion: Small arteries that run along the dorsum of the toes.
rest|Dorsal digital arteries of foot.territorio: Skin and tissues of the dorsum of the toes

rest|Dorsal digital arteries of hand.es: Dorsal digital arteries of the hand
rest|Dorsal digital arteries of hand.descripcion: Small arteries on the dorsum of the fingers, reaching approximately the middle phalanx.
rest|Dorsal digital arteries of hand.territorio: Dorsum of the proximal and middle phalanges

rest|Dorsal metacarpal arteries.descripcion: Arteries over the dorsal interossei in the intermetacarpal spaces.
rest|Dorsal metacarpal arteries.origen: Dorsal carpal arch (and radial artery for the first)
rest|Dorsal metacarpal arteries.territorio: Dorsum of the hand and fingers
rest|Dorsal metacarpal arteries.clinica: The first is the pedicle of the Foucher flap (kite flap).

rest|Dorsal metatarsal arteries.descripcion: Arteries that run in the intermetatarsal spaces over the dorsal interossei.
rest|Dorsal metatarsal arteries.origen: Arcuate artery (2nd-4th) and dorsalis pedis artery (1st)
rest|Dorsal metatarsal arteries.territorio: Dorsum of the foot and toes

rest|Dorsalis pedis artery.descripcion: Continuation of the anterior tibial artery on the dorsum of the foot, lateral to the tendon of the extensor hallucis longus.
rest|Dorsalis pedis artery.origen: Anterior tibial artery (at the level of the ankle)
rest|Dorsalis pedis artery.destino: Ends as the deep plantar artery and the first dorsal metatarsal artery
rest|Dorsalis pedis artery.ramas: Lateral and medial tarsal, arcuate, first dorsal metatarsal, deep plantar
rest|Dorsalis pedis artery.territorio: Dorsum of the foot and toes
rest|Dorsalis pedis artery.clinica: Its pulse is palpated between the tendons of the extensor hallucis longus and extensor digitorum longus.

rest|External carotid artery.descripcion: Branch of the common carotid artery at the level of the upper border of the thyroid cartilage, which ascends to the parotid region.
rest|External carotid artery.destino: Divides into the maxillary and superficial temporal arteries within the parotid gland
rest|External carotid artery.ramas: Superior thyroid, ascending pharyngeal, lingual, facial, occipital, posterior auricular, maxillary, superficial temporal
rest|External carotid artery.territorio: Neck, face, scalp, oral and nasal cavities, dura mater
rest|External carotid artery.clinica: Distinguished from the internal carotid by having branches in the neck; it can be ligated safely thanks to anastomoses.

rest|External iliac artery.descripcion: Branch of the common iliac artery that descends along the medial border of the psoas major to the inguinal ligament.
rest|External iliac artery.destino: Continues as the femoral artery below the inguinal ligament
rest|External iliac artery.territorio: Lower anterior abdominal wall and lower limb
rest|External iliac artery.clinica: Used for anastomosis of the renal artery in kidney transplantation.

rest|Facial artery.descripcion: Anterior branch of the external carotid artery that crosses the lower border of the mandible in front of the masseter and ascends tortuously over the face.
rest|Facial artery.ramas: Ascending palatine, tonsillar, submental, glandular, inferior and superior labial, lateral nasal, angular
rest|Facial artery.territorio: Face, lips, nose, palatine tonsil, submandibular gland
rest|Facial artery.clinica: Its pulse is palpated at the lower border of the mandible, in front of the masseter.

rest|Femoral artery.descripcion: Continuation of the external iliac artery; it passes through the femoral triangle and the adductor canal.
rest|Femoral artery.origen: External iliac artery (below the inguinal ligament)
rest|Femoral artery.destino: Continues as the popliteal artery at the adductor hiatus
rest|Femoral artery.ramas: Superficial epigastric, superficial circumflex iliac, external pudendal, deep femoral, descending genicular
rest|Femoral artery.territorio: Lower abdominal wall, external genitalia and lower limb
rest|Femoral artery.clinica: Usual access route for catheterization; pulse palpable at the mid-inguinal point.

rest|Fibular artery.descripcion: Largest branch of the posterior tibial artery; it descends alongside the fibula in the deep posterior compartment.
rest|Fibular artery.ramas: Muscular branches, nutrient artery of the fibula, perforating, communicating, lateral malleolar, calcaneal
rest|Fibular artery.territorio: Posterior and lateral compartments of the leg, fibula
rest|Fibular artery.clinica: Pedicle of the free fibula flap for mandibular reconstruction.

rest|First posterior intercostal artery.descripcion: Artery of the first intercostal space, arising from the supreme intercostal artery.
rest|First posterior intercostal artery.destino: Anastomoses with anterior intercostal branches of the internal thoracic artery
rest|First posterior intercostal artery.territorio: First intercostal space: muscles, ribs, pleura and skin

rest|Frontal branch of superficial tempo.es: Frontal branch of the superficial temporal artery
rest|Frontal branch of superficial tempo.descripcion: Anterior terminal branch of the superficial temporal artery that runs tortuously toward the forehead.
rest|Frontal branch of superficial tempo.destino: Anastomoses with the supraorbital and supratrochlear arteries
rest|Frontal branch of superficial tempo.clinica: Visible and thickened in giant cell arteritis; site of temporal biopsy.

rest|Frontal branches of callosomarginal.es: Frontal branches of the callosomarginal artery
rest|Frontal branches of callosomarginal.descripcion: Anteromedial, intermediomedial and posteromedial branches that supply the medial surface of the frontal lobe.
rest|Frontal branches of callosomarginal.ramas: Anteromedial, intermediomedial and posteromedial frontal branches
rest|Frontal branches of callosomarginal.territorio: Superior frontal gyrus on its medial surface and superior border of the hemisphere

rest|Gastroduodenal artery.descripcion: Branch of the common hepatic artery that descends behind the first part of the duodenum.
rest|Gastroduodenal artery.destino: Divides into the right gastro-omental and the anterior superior pancreaticoduodenal arteries
rest|Gastroduodenal artery.ramas: Supraduodenal, posterior superior pancreaticoduodenal, right gastro-omental, anterior superior pancreaticoduodenal
rest|Gastroduodenal artery.territorio: Proximal duodenum, head of the pancreas, greater curvature of the stomach
rest|Gastroduodenal artery.clinica: A posterior duodenal ulcer may erode it and cause severe gastrointestinal hemorrhage.

rest|Greater palatine artery.descripcion: Branch of the descending palatine artery that emerges through the greater palatine foramen and runs forward along the hard palate.
rest|Greater palatine artery.destino: Ascends through the incisive canal and anastomoses with the sphenopalatine artery
rest|Greater palatine artery.territorio: Hard palate, palatal mucosa and gingiva
rest|Greater palatine artery.clinica: It must be protected when harvesting palatal mucosal grafts.

rest|Ileal branch of ileocolic artery.es: Ileal branch of the ileocolic artery
rest|Ileal branch of ileocolic artery.descripcion: Branch of the ileocolic artery that runs to the terminal ileum.
rest|Ileal branch of ileocolic artery.destino: Anastomoses with the end of the superior mesenteric artery (ileal branches)

rest|Ileocolic artery.descripcion: Last branch from the concavity of the superior mesenteric artery, descending toward the right iliac fossa.
rest|Ileocolic artery.ramas: Colic branch, anterior and posterior cecal, appendicular artery, ileal branch
rest|Ileocolic artery.territorio: Terminal ileum, cecum, appendix and initial ascending colon

rest|Iliacus branch of iliolumbar artery.es: Iliacus branch of the iliolumbar artery
rest|Iliacus branch of iliolumbar artery.descripcion: Branch that runs laterally in the iliac fossa, deep to the iliacus muscle.
rest|Iliacus branch of iliolumbar artery.destino: Anastomoses with the deep circumflex iliac and obturator arteries

rest|Iliolumbar artery.descripcion: Branch of the posterior trunk of the internal iliac artery that ascends in front of the sacroiliac joint and behind the psoas.
rest|Iliolumbar artery.ramas: Lumbar branch, spinal branch, iliac branch
rest|Iliolumbar artery.territorio: Psoas major, quadratus lumborum, iliacus, cauda equina

rest|Inferior alveolar artery.descripcion: Branch of the first part of the maxillary artery that enters the mandibular canal with the nerve of the same name.
rest|Inferior alveolar artery.destino: Ends as the mental and incisive arteries
rest|Inferior alveolar artery.ramas: Mylohyoid branch, dental branches, peridental branches, mental branch
rest|Inferior alveolar artery.territorio: Mandible, lower teeth, gingiva and chin
rest|Inferior alveolar artery.clinica: May be injured during nerve block anesthesia or third molar surgery.

rest|Inferior epigastric artery.descripcion: Branch of the external iliac artery that ascends medial to the deep inguinal ring and penetrates the rectus sheath.
rest|Inferior epigastric artery.origen: External iliac artery (above the inguinal ligament)
rest|Inferior epigastric artery.destino: Anastomoses with the superior epigastric artery in the rectus sheath
rest|Inferior epigastric artery.ramas: Cremasteric artery (or artery of the round ligament), pubic branch (may give rise to an accessory obturator artery)
rest|Inferior epigastric artery.territorio: Rectus abdominis muscle and lower anterior abdominal wall
rest|Inferior epigastric artery.clinica: Separates direct (medial) from indirect (lateral) inguinal hernias; pedicle of the DIEP flap.

rest|Inferior gluteal artery.descripcion: Branch of the anterior trunk of the internal iliac artery that leaves the pelvis through the greater sciatic foramen below the piriformis.
rest|Inferior gluteal artery.ramas: Artery accompanying the sciatic nerve, muscular branches, cruciate anastomosis
rest|Inferior gluteal artery.territorio: Gluteus maximus, lateral rotators of the hip, sciatic nerve and posterior part of the thigh

rest|Inferior labial artery.descripcion: Branch of the facial artery near the angle of the mouth that runs through the lower lip.
rest|Inferior labial artery.destino: Anastomoses with the contralateral artery and the mental artery
rest|Inferior labial artery.territorio: Lower lip: glands, mucosa and muscles

rest|Inferior lateral genicular artery.descripcion: Branch of the popliteal artery that winds around the lateral condyle of the tibia, deep to the fibular collateral ligament.
rest|Inferior lateral genicular artery.clinica: May be injured in lateral meniscus surgery or arthroscopy.

rest|Inferior leaflet of right atriovent.es: Posterior (inferior) leaflet of the tricuspid valve
rest|Inferior leaflet of right atriovent.descripcion: Leaflet of the right atrioventricular valve attached to the fibrous annulus in its inferior/posterior part; its tendinous cords reach the posterior and anterior papillary muscles.
rest|Inferior leaflet of right atriovent.funcion: Closes the right atrioventricular orifice in systole, preventing backflow into the right atrium
rest|Inferior leaflet of right atriovent.clinica: Affected in tricuspid regurgitation and in endocarditis of intravenous drug users.

rest|Inferior lingular artery of left lu.es: Inferior lingular artery of the left lung
rest|Inferior lingular artery of left lu.descripcion: Branch of the lingular artery (of the left pulmonary artery) for the inferior lingular segment.
rest|Inferior lingular artery of left lu.origen: Lingular artery of the left pulmonary artery
rest|Inferior lingular artery of left lu.territorio: Inferior lingular segment (S5) of the left upper lobe
rest|Inferior lingular artery of left lu.funcion: Carries deoxygenated blood for gas exchange

rest|Inferior lobar artery of right lung.es: Inferior lobar artery of the right lung
rest|Inferior lobar artery of right lung.descripcion: Continuation of the right pulmonary artery (interlobar part) toward the lower lobe.
rest|Inferior lobar artery of right lung.destino: Segmental arteries of the lower lobe
rest|Inferior lobar artery of right lung.ramas: Superior segmental, medial, anterior, lateral and posterior basal
rest|Inferior lobar artery of right lung.territorio: Lower lobe of the right lung
rest|Inferior lobar artery of right lung.funcion: Carries deoxygenated blood for gas exchange

rest|Inferior medial genicular artery.descripcion: Branch of the popliteal artery that winds around the medial condyle of the tibia, deep to the tibial collateral ligament.
rest|Inferior medial genicular artery.territorio: Knee joint, proximal end of the tibia and popliteus muscle

rest|Inferior mesenteric artery.descripcion: Unpaired anterior branch of the abdominal aorta at L3, which descends retroperitoneally toward the left.
rest|Inferior mesenteric artery.destino: Continues as the superior rectal artery as it crosses the left common iliac vessels
rest|Inferior mesenteric artery.ramas: Left colic, sigmoid arteries, superior rectal
rest|Inferior mesenteric artery.territorio: Hindgut derivatives: distal third of the transverse colon, descending colon, sigmoid and upper rectum
rest|Inferior mesenteric artery.clinica: Ligated in left colectomy; in aortic aneurysm repair its sacrifice may cause sigmoid ischemia.

rest|Inferior pancreaticoduodenal artery.descripcion: First branch of the superior mesenteric artery (or of the first jejunal artery), which runs to the right toward the pancreatic head.
rest|Inferior pancreaticoduodenal artery.destino: Divides into anterior and posterior branches
rest|Inferior pancreaticoduodenal artery.ramas: Anterior and posterior inferior pancreaticoduodenal branches
rest|Inferior pancreaticoduodenal artery.territorio: Head of the pancreas and third and fourth parts of the duodenum
rest|Inferior pancreaticoduodenal artery.clinica: The pancreaticoduodenal arcades are a collateral route in coeliac trunk stenosis.

rest|Inferior papillary muscle of left v.es: Posterior (inferior) papillary muscle of the left ventricle
rest|Inferior papillary muscle of left v.descripcion: Papillary muscle of the inferior (posteromedial) wall of the left ventricle, connected to both mitral leaflets.
rest|Inferior papillary muscle of left v.funcion: Through the tendinous cords it prevents prolapse of the mitral leaflets in systole
rest|Inferior papillary muscle of left v.clinica: Single blood supply (usually right coronary): its rupture after inferior infarction causes acute mitral regurgitation.

rest|Inferior papillary muscle of right.es: Posterior (inferior) papillary muscle of the right ventricle
rest|Inferior papillary muscle of right.descripcion: Papillary muscle of the inferior wall of the right ventricle, often multiple.
rest|Inferior papillary muscle of right.funcion: Through the tendinous cords it tenses the posterior and septal leaflets of the tricuspid valve in systole

rest|Inferior phrenic artery.descripcion: Paired artery arising from the abdominal aorta (or the coeliac trunk) that ascends along the inferior surface of the diaphragm.
rest|Inferior phrenic artery.territorio: Inferior surface of the diaphragm, suprarenal gland, abdominal esophagus
rest|Inferior phrenic artery.clinica: Source of parasitic blood supply in hepatocellular carcinoma; considered in chemoembolization.

rest|Inferior suprarenal artery.descripcion: Branch of the renal artery that ascends to the lower part of the suprarenal gland.

rest|Inferior thyroid artery.descripcion: Branch of the thyrocervical trunk that ascends and then descends medially, behind the carotid sheath, toward the inferior pole of the thyroid.
rest|Inferior thyroid artery.destino: Glandular branches on the posterior surface of the thyroid
rest|Inferior thyroid artery.ramas: Ascending cervical, inferior laryngeal, pharyngeal, esophageal, tracheal, glandular
rest|Inferior thyroid artery.territorio: Thyroid, parathyroids, lower larynx, trachea and cervical esophagus
rest|Inferior thyroid artery.clinica: Intimate relationship with the recurrent laryngeal nerve; risk of injury when ligating it in thyroidectomy.

rest|Inferior ulnar collateral artery.descripcion: Branch of the brachial artery about 5 cm above the elbow that passes medially over the brachialis.
rest|Inferior ulnar collateral artery.destino: Anastomoses with the anterior ulnar recurrent artery (elbow articular network)
rest|Inferior ulnar collateral artery.territorio: Brachialis and pronator teres muscles, elbow joint

rest|Infra-orbital artery.descripcion: Branch of the pterygopalatine part of the maxillary artery that runs through the infraorbital groove and canal and exits through the infraorbital foramen.
rest|Infra-orbital artery.destino: Anastomoses with branches of the facial and ophthalmic arteries
rest|Infra-orbital artery.ramas: Anterior superior alveolar arteries, orbital branches
rest|Infra-orbital artery.territorio: Lower eyelid, cheek, upper lip, lateral nose, upper anterior teeth, maxillary sinus

rest|Insular branches of middle cerebral.es: Insular branches of the middle cerebral artery (M2)
rest|Insular branches of middle cerebral.descripcion: Branches of the insular segment (M2) of the middle cerebral artery that run over the insula in the lateral sulcus.
rest|Insular branches of middle cerebral.destino: Continue as opercular (M3) and cortical (M4) branches
rest|Insular branches of middle cerebral.clinica: M2 occlusions are a frequent target of mechanical thrombectomy in stroke.

rest|Insular branches of middle cerebral.es: Insular branches of the middle cerebral artery (M2 segment)
rest|Insular branches of middle cerebral.descripcion: Branches of the insular segment (M2) of the middle cerebral artery, superior and inferior, that run over the insula.
rest|Insular branches of middle cerebral.destino: Continue as opercular (M3) and cortical (M4) branches
rest|Insular branches of middle cerebral.clinica: M2 occlusions are a frequent target of mechanical thrombectomy in stroke.

rest|Internal carotid artery.descripcion: Branch of the common carotid artery that ascends without cervical branches, enters the skull through the carotid canal and crosses the cavernous sinus.
rest|Internal carotid artery.origen: Common carotid artery (upper border of the thyroid cartilage)
rest|Internal carotid artery.destino: Divides into the anterior and middle cerebral arteries
rest|Internal carotid artery.ramas: Ophthalmic, hypophyseal, posterior communicating, anterior choroidal, anterior cerebral, middle cerebral
rest|Internal carotid artery.territorio: Brain (anterior circulation), eye and orbit, forehead and nose
rest|Internal carotid artery.clinica: Stenosis at its origin (carotid bulb) causes ischemic attacks and amaurosis fugax.

rest|Internal iliac artery.descripcion: Branch of the common iliac artery that descends into the pelvis in front of the sacroiliac joint.
rest|Internal iliac artery.destino: Divides into anterior and posterior trunks next to the greater sciatic foramen
rest|Internal iliac artery.ramas: Posterior trunk (iliolumbar, lateral sacral, superior gluteal) and anterior trunk (umbilical, obturator, vesical, uterine, middle rectal, internal pudendal, inferior gluteal)
rest|Internal iliac artery.territorio: Pelvic viscera, perineum, gluteal region and medial thigh
rest|Internal iliac artery.clinica: Its ligation or embolization controls pelvic hemorrhage thanks to the extensive collateral circulation.

rest|Internal pudendal artery.descripcion: Branch of the anterior trunk of the internal iliac artery that exits through the greater sciatic foramen and enters the perineum through the lesser one, in the pudendal canal.
rest|Internal pudendal artery.destino: Ends as the dorsal and deep arteries of the penis/clitoris
rest|Internal pudendal artery.ramas: Inferior rectal, perineal, of the bulb, urethral, deep and dorsal artery of the penis or clitoris
rest|Internal pudendal artery.territorio: Perineum, anal canal, external genitalia and erectile tissue
rest|Internal pudendal artery.clinica: Its atherosclerotic involvement contributes to vasculogenic erectile dysfunction.

rest|Internal thoracic artery.descripcion: Branch of the subclavian artery that descends 1 cm lateral to the sternum, behind the costal cartilages.
rest|Internal thoracic artery.destino: Divides into the superior epigastric and musculophrenic arteries in the 6th intercostal space
rest|Internal thoracic artery.ramas: Pericardiacophrenic, mediastinal, thymic, anterior intercostal, perforating, musculophrenic, superior epigastric
rest|Internal thoracic artery.territorio: Anterior thoracic wall, breast, pericardium, diaphragm and upper abdominal wall
rest|Internal thoracic artery.clinica: Graft of choice (internal mammary artery) for coronary revascularization.

rest|Intrarenal arteries of left kidney.es: Intrarenal arteries of the left kidney
rest|Intrarenal arteries of left kidney.descripcion: Set of segmental, interlobar, arcuate and radiate cortical arteries of the left kidney.
rest|Intrarenal arteries of left kidney.ramas: Segmental, interlobar, arcuate, radiate cortical, afferent arterioles
rest|Intrarenal arteries of left kidney.funcion: They distribute renal flow for glomerular filtration
rest|Intrarenal arteries of left kidney.clinica: The segmental arteries are end arteries: basis of segmental partial nephrectomy.

rest|Intrarenal arteries of right kidney.es: Intrarenal arteries of the right kidney
rest|Intrarenal arteries of right kidney.descripcion: Set of segmental, interlobar, arcuate and radiate cortical arteries of the right kidney.
rest|Intrarenal arteries of right kidney.ramas: Segmental, interlobar, arcuate, radiate cortical, afferent arterioles
rest|Intrarenal arteries of right kidney.funcion: They distribute renal flow for glomerular filtration
rest|Intrarenal arteries of right kidney.clinica: The segmental arteries are end arteries: basis of segmental partial nephrectomy.

rest|Lacrimal artery.descripcion: Branch of the ophthalmic artery that runs along the upper border of the lateral rectus toward the lacrimal gland.
rest|Lacrimal artery.destino: Ends in the lateral palpebral arteries
rest|Lacrimal artery.ramas: Anastomotic branch with the middle meningeal artery, zygomatic, lateral palpebral
rest|Lacrimal artery.territorio: Lacrimal gland, conjunctiva, lateral upper eyelid, lateral rectus
rest|Lacrimal artery.clinica: Its anastomotic branch with the middle meningeal artery may give origin to the ophthalmic artery (a relevant variant in embolizations).

rest|Lateral basal segmental artery of l.es: Lateral basal segmental artery of the left lung
rest|Lateral basal segmental artery of l.la: Arteria segmentalis basalis lateralis pulmonis sinistri
rest|Lateral basal segmental artery of l.descripcion: Branch of the basal part of the left pulmonary artery for the lateral basal segment.
rest|Lateral basal segmental artery of l.origen: Inferior lobar artery (basal part) of the left pulmonary artery
rest|Lateral basal segmental artery of l.territorio: Lateral basal segment (S9) of the left lower lobe
rest|Lateral basal segmental artery of l.funcion: Carries deoxygenated blood for gas exchange

rest|Lateral basal segmental artery of r.es: Lateral basal segmental artery of the right lung
rest|Lateral basal segmental artery of r.la: Arteria segmentalis basalis lateralis pulmonis dextri
rest|Lateral basal segmental artery of r.descripcion: Branch of the basal part of the right inferior lobar artery for the lateral basal segment.
rest|Lateral basal segmental artery of r.origen: Inferior lobar artery of the right pulmonary artery
rest|Lateral basal segmental artery of r.territorio: Lateral basal segment (S9) of the right lower lobe
rest|Lateral basal segmental artery of r.funcion: Carries deoxygenated blood for gas exchange

rest|Lateral circumflex femoral artery.descripcion: Branch of the deep femoral artery (sometimes of the femoral artery) that passes laterally between the divisions of the femoral nerve, behind the sartorius and rectus femoris.
rest|Lateral circumflex femoral artery.territorio: Quadriceps, tensor fasciae latae, femoral neck and greater trochanter
rest|Lateral circumflex femoral artery.clinica: Its descending branch is the pedicle of the anterolateral thigh flap.

rest|Lateral frontobasal artery.descripcion: Cortical branch of the middle cerebral artery (lateral orbitofrontal artery) that runs to the orbital surface of the frontal lobe.
rest|Lateral frontobasal artery.territorio: Lateral part of the orbital surface of the frontal lobe and inferior frontal gyrus

rest|Lateral occipital artery.descripcion: Terminal branch of the posterior cerebral artery that runs along the inferior surface of the temporal and occipital lobes.
rest|Lateral occipital artery.ramas: Anterior, intermediate and posterior temporal branches
rest|Lateral occipital artery.territorio: Inferior surface of the temporal and occipital lobes (fusiform and parahippocampal gyri)

rest|Lateral plantar artery.descripcion: Larger terminal branch of the posterior tibial artery that crosses the sole laterally between the flexor digitorum brevis and the quadratus plantae.
rest|Lateral plantar artery.origen: Posterior tibial artery (below the flexor retinaculum)
rest|Lateral plantar artery.destino: Forms the deep plantar arch by joining the deep plantar artery
rest|Lateral plantar artery.ramas: Calcaneal, muscular branches, deep plantar arch (plantar metatarsal, perforating)
rest|Lateral plantar artery.territorio: Lateral sole of the foot and deep structures of the sole

rest|Lateral pontine branches of basilar.es: Lateral pontine branches of the basilar artery
rest|Lateral pontine branches of basilar.descripcion: Short circumferential branches of the basilar artery that wrap around the lateral aspect of the pons.
rest|Lateral pontine branches of basilar.clinica: Their occlusion produces lateral pontine syndromes with cranial nerve deficits and ataxia.

rest|Lateral segmental artery of right l.es: Lateral segmental artery of the right lung
rest|Lateral segmental artery of right l.descripcion: Branch of the right middle lobar artery for the lateral segment of the middle lobe.
rest|Lateral segmental artery of right l.origen: Middle lobar artery of the right pulmonary artery
rest|Lateral segmental artery of right l.territorio: Lateral segment (S4) of the right middle lobe
rest|Lateral segmental artery of right l.funcion: Carries deoxygenated blood for gas exchange

rest|Lateral tarsal artery.descripcion: Branch of the dorsalis pedis artery that runs laterally under the extensor digitorum brevis.
rest|Lateral tarsal artery.destino: Anastomoses with the arcuate artery and branches of the fibular and lateral plantar arteries
rest|Lateral tarsal artery.territorio: Extensor digitorum brevis and tarsal joints

rest|Lateral thoracic artery.descripcion: Branch of the second part of the axillary artery that descends along the lateral border of the pectoralis minor over the serratus anterior.
rest|Lateral thoracic artery.territorio: Serratus anterior, pectoral muscles, axillary lymph nodes and lateral part of the breast
rest|Lateral thoracic artery.clinica: Makes an important contribution to the blood supply of the breast in women.

rest|Left atrium.descripcion: Posterior cardiac chamber that forms most of the base of the heart; it receives the four pulmonary veins and has a left auricle.
rest|Left atrium.destino: Left ventricle, through the mitral valve
rest|Left atrium.funcion: Reservoir and priming pump that receives oxygenated pulmonary blood and propels it into the left ventricle
rest|Left atrium.clinica: In atrial fibrillation thrombi form in the left auricle; its dilation may compress the esophagus.

rest|Left colic artery.descripcion: First branch of the inferior mesenteric artery, retroperitoneal, which runs to the left toward the descending colon.
rest|Left colic artery.destino: Divides into ascending and descending branches
rest|Left colic artery.territorio: Distal transverse colon, left colic flexure and descending colon
rest|Left colic artery.clinica: Contributes to the marginal artery; relevant in ischemic colitis of the splenic flexure.

rest|Left common carotid artery.descripcion: Second branch of the aortic arch; it has a thoracic and a cervical part within the carotid sheath.
rest|Left common carotid artery.destino: Divides into the internal and external carotid arteries at the level of the upper border of the thyroid cartilage (C3-C4)
rest|Left common carotid artery.territorio: Left side of the head, neck and brain
rest|Left common carotid artery.clinica: The carotid sinus and carotid body are at its bifurcation; site of atherosclerotic plaques.

rest|Left coronary artery.descripcion: Arises from the left aortic sinus and passes between the pulmonary trunk and the left auricle (left main trunk) before dividing.
rest|Left coronary artery.destino: Divides into the anterior interventricular and circumflex arteries
rest|Left coronary artery.ramas: Anterior interventricular branch, circumflex branch (sometimes an intermediate branch)
rest|Left coronary artery.territorio: Left atrium, most of the left ventricle, anterior part of the septum and of the right ventricle
rest|Left coronary artery.clinica: Left main stenosis compromises a large part of the myocardium: an indication for revascularization.

rest|Left coronary leaflet.es: Left semilunar cusp of the aortic valve
rest|Left coronary leaflet.descripcion: Cusp of the aortic valve above the left aortic sinus, from which the left coronary artery arises.
rest|Left coronary leaflet.funcion: Prevents diastolic backflow from the aorta into the left ventricle
rest|Left coronary leaflet.clinica: Fusion of cusps (bicuspid valve) predisposes to early aortic stenosis.

rest|Left gastric artery.descripcion: Smallest branch of the coeliac trunk that ascends to the cardia and descends along the lesser curvature in the lesser omentum.
rest|Left gastric artery.destino: Anastomoses with the right gastric artery on the lesser curvature
rest|Left gastric artery.territorio: Lesser curvature of the stomach and abdominal esophagus
rest|Left gastric artery.clinica: Frequent source of bleeding in ulcers of the lesser curvature; its esophageal branches in varices.

rest|Left pulmonary artery.descripcion: Shorter branch of the pulmonary trunk that passes in front of the descending aorta and arches over the left main bronchus.
rest|Left pulmonary artery.destino: Lobar and segmental arteries of the left lung
rest|Left pulmonary artery.ramas: Arteries of the upper lobe (apical, posterior, anterior, lingular) and lower lobe
rest|Left pulmonary artery.funcion: Carries deoxygenated blood for gas exchange
rest|Left pulmonary artery.clinica: Joined to the aortic arch by the ligamentum arteriosum; site of pulmonary embolism.

rest|Left renal artery.descripcion: Lateral branch of the abdominal aorta at L1-L2, shorter than the right, posterior to the left renal vein.
rest|Left renal artery.destino: Divides into anterior and posterior branches at the renal hilum
rest|Left renal artery.ramas: Inferior suprarenal, ureteric, anterior and posterior branches (segmental arteries)
rest|Left renal artery.territorio: Left kidney, suprarenal gland and proximal ureter
rest|Left renal artery.clinica: Renal artery stenosis causes renovascular hypertension.

rest|Left semilunar leaflet of pulmonary.es: Left semilunar cusp of the pulmonary valve
rest|Left semilunar leaflet of pulmonary.la: Valvula semilunaris sinistra valvae trunci pulmonalis
rest|Left semilunar leaflet of pulmonary.descripcion: One of the three semilunar cusps of the pulmonary valve, located on the left at the orifice of the pulmonary trunk.
rest|Left semilunar leaflet of pulmonary.funcion: Prevents backflow of blood from the pulmonary trunk into the right ventricle during diastole.
rest|Left semilunar leaflet of pulmonary.clinica: Congenital pulmonary stenosis usually involves fusion of the cusps; it produces a systolic murmur in the left 2nd intercostal space.

rest|Left subclavian artery.descripcion: Artery that arises directly from the aortic arch, ascends through the superior mediastinum and arches over the first rib behind the scalene muscles.
rest|Left subclavian artery.destino: Continues as the axillary artery at the lateral border of the first rib.
rest|Left subclavian artery.ramas: Vertebral artery, internal thoracic artery, thyrocervical trunk, costocervical trunk, dorsal scapular artery.
rest|Left subclavian artery.territorio: Left upper limb, part of the brain, neck and thoracic wall.
rest|Left subclavian artery.clinica: Its proximal stenosis causes subclavian steal syndrome: retrograde vertebral flow with vertebrobasilar symptoms on exercising the arm.

rest|Left testicular artery.descripcion: Long, thin artery that descends retroperitoneally over the psoas, crosses the inguinal canal in the spermatic cord and reaches the testis.
rest|Left testicular artery.origen: Anterior surface of the abdominal aorta, below the renal arteries (L2).
rest|Left testicular artery.clinica: Its ligation in orchiopexy or varicocelectomy is usually tolerated thanks to the collateral circulation from the artery to the ductus deferens and the cremasteric artery.

rest|Left ventricle.descripcion: Left posteroinferior cardiac chamber that forms the apex of the heart; thick muscular wall with trabeculae carneae and two papillary muscles.
rest|Left ventricle.origen: Receives blood from the left atrium through the mitral valve.
rest|Left ventricle.destino: Pumps blood into the aorta through the aortic valve.
rest|Left ventricle.funcion: Propels oxygenated blood into the systemic circulation at high pressure.
rest|Left ventricle.clinica: Left ventricular hypertrophy is a typical consequence of arterial hypertension and aortic stenosis.

rest|Long posterior ciliary arteries.descripcion: Two arteries that pierce the sclera near the optic nerve and advance between the sclera and choroid to the ciliary body.
rest|Long posterior ciliary arteries.destino: Greater arterial circle of the iris.

rest|Lumbar arteries.descripcion: Four pairs of segmental arteries that wrap around the lumbar vertebral bodies and run behind the psoas and quadratus lumborum.
rest|Lumbar arteries.origen: Posterior surface of the abdominal aorta (L1-L4).
rest|Lumbar arteries.destino: Posterolateral abdominal wall, anastomosing with the epigastric, subcostal and iliolumbar arteries.
rest|Lumbar arteries.ramas: Dorsal rami, spinal rami, muscular rami.
rest|Lumbar arteries.territorio: Muscles of the posterior abdominal wall, muscles of the back, vertebrae, spinal cord and meninges.
rest|Lumbar arteries.clinica: They may be injured in lateral surgical approaches to the lumbar spine, causing retroperitoneal hematoma.

rest|Lumbar branch of iliolumbar artery.es: Lumbar branch of the iliolumbar artery
rest|Lumbar branch of iliolumbar artery.descripcion: Ascending branch of the iliolumbar artery that ascends behind the psoas major, equivalent to a fifth lumbar artery.

rest|Marginal artery.descripcion: Continuous arterial arcade parallel to the mesenteric border of the colon, from the ileocolic flexure to the upper rectum.
rest|Marginal artery.origen: Anastomosis of branches of the ileocolic, right, middle and left colic, and sigmoid arteries.
rest|Marginal artery.ramas: Vasa recta to the colic wall.
rest|Marginal artery.clinica: Ensures collateral circulation between the mesenteric arteries; it is weak at Griffiths' point (splenic flexure), an area vulnerable to ischemia.

rest|Maxillary artery.descripcion: Larger terminal branch of the external carotid artery; it arises behind the mandibular neck and runs through the infratemporal fossa to the pterygopalatine fossa. Three parts: mandibular, pterygoid and pterygopalatine.
rest|Maxillary artery.destino: Sphenopalatine artery in the nasal cavity.
rest|Maxillary artery.ramas: Middle meningeal, inferior alveolar, deep temporal, masseteric, buccal, posterior superior alveolar, infraorbital, descending palatine, sphenopalatine.
rest|Maxillary artery.territorio: Maxillae, teeth, muscles of mastication, dura mater, nasal cavity, palate.
rest|Maxillary artery.clinica: Embolized or ligated in refractory posterior epistaxis.

rest|Medial basal segmental artery of le.es: Medial basal segmental artery of the left lung
rest|Medial basal segmental artery of le.la: Arteria segmentalis basalis medialis pulmonis sinistri
rest|Medial basal segmental artery of le.descripcion: Branch of the basal part of the left pulmonary artery that supplies the medial basal segment (S7) of the left lower lobe.
rest|Medial basal segmental artery of le.territorio: Medial basal (anteromedial) segment of the left lower lobe.
rest|Medial basal segmental artery of le.clinica: In the left lung it usually shares a trunk with the anterior basal artery (anteromedial segment).

rest|Medial basal segmental artery of ri.es: Medial basal segmental artery of the right lung
rest|Medial basal segmental artery of ri.la: Arteria segmentalis basalis medialis pulmonis dextri
rest|Medial basal segmental artery of ri.descripcion: Branch of the basal part of the right pulmonary artery destined for the medial basal segment (S7) of the right lower lobe.
rest|Medial basal segmental artery of ri.territorio: Medial basal (cardiac) segment of the right lower lobe.

rest|Medial circumflex femoral artery.descripcion: Artery that winds around the medial and posterior aspects of the femoral neck, passing between the pectineus and iliopsoas.
rest|Medial circumflex femoral artery.origen: Deep femoral artery (sometimes the femoral artery).
rest|Medial circumflex femoral artery.destino: Cruciate anastomosis and lateral circumflex artery around the femoral neck.
rest|Medial circumflex femoral artery.ramas: Superficial branch, deep branch, acetabular branch, ascending and transverse branches.
rest|Medial circumflex femoral artery.territorio: Adductors, head and neck of the femur, hip joint.
rest|Medial circumflex femoral artery.clinica: Main blood supply of the femoral head; its injury in subcapital fractures causes avascular necrosis.

rest|Medial occipital artery.descripcion: Terminal branch of the posterior cerebral artery (P4 segment) that runs to the medial surface of the occipital lobe.
rest|Medial occipital artery.ramas: Calcarine, parieto-occipital, dorsal callosal branch, cuneal and precuneal branches.
rest|Medial occipital artery.territorio: Visual cortex (cuneus, lingual gyrus), precuneus and splenium of the corpus callosum.
rest|Medial occipital artery.clinica: Its occlusion produces contralateral homonymous hemianopsia with macular sparing.

rest|Medial plantar artery.descripcion: Smaller terminal branch of the posterior tibial artery; it runs along the medial border of the sole between the abductor hallucis and the flexor digitorum brevis.
rest|Medial plantar artery.origen: Posterior tibial artery (below the flexor retinaculum).
rest|Medial plantar artery.destino: Digital artery to the medial border of the great toe.
rest|Medial plantar artery.territorio: Muscles and skin of the medial plantar region and great toe.

rest|Medial pontine branches of basilar.es: Medial pontine branches of the basilar artery
rest|Medial pontine branches of basilar.descripcion: Short paramedian branches that penetrate the pons next to the midline.
rest|Medial pontine branches of basilar.territorio: Paramedian region of the pons: corticospinal tract, abducens nucleus and medial lemniscus.
rest|Medial pontine branches of basilar.clinica: Their occlusion causes pontine lacunar infarcts (pure motor hemiparesis, dysarthria-clumsy hand).

rest|Medial segmental artery of right lu.es: Medial segmental artery of the right lung
rest|Medial segmental artery of right lu.descripcion: Branch of the middle lobar artery that supplies the medial segment (S5) of the right middle lobe.
rest|Medial segmental artery of right lu.origen: Middle lobar artery of the right lung.
rest|Medial segmental artery of right lu.territorio: Medial segment of the right middle lobe.

rest|Median sacral artery.descripcion: Thin unpaired artery that descends in the midline over L4-L5, the sacrum and the coccyx; a vestige of the caudal aorta.
rest|Median sacral artery.origen: Posterior surface of the abdominal aorta, just above its bifurcation.
rest|Median sacral artery.ramas: Lumbar ima artery, lateral sacral branches.
rest|Median sacral artery.clinica: Source of hemorrhage in surgery of the anterior surface of the sacrum and in anterior L5-S1 approaches.

rest|Mental branch of inferior alveolar.es: Mental branch of the inferior alveolar artery
rest|Mental branch of inferior alveolar.descripcion: Terminal branch of the inferior alveolar artery that exits through the mental foramen alongside the mental nerve.
rest|Mental branch of inferior alveolar.destino: Anastomoses with the submental and inferior labial arteries.
rest|Mental branch of inferior alveolar.clinica: Risk of bleeding in surgery and implants in the mandibular premolar region.

rest|Middle cerebral artery (M1-segment).es: Middle cerebral artery, M1 segment (sphenoidal part)
rest|Middle cerebral artery (M1-segment).descripcion: Horizontal segment of the middle cerebral artery from the carotid bifurcation to the limen insulae, parallel to the lesser wing of the sphenoid.
rest|Middle cerebral artery (M1-segment).destino: Bifurcates or trifurcates into the M2 (insular) segment.
rest|Middle cerebral artery (M1-segment).ramas: Lenticulostriate arteries (lateral striate), anterior temporal artery.
rest|Middle cerebral artery (M1-segment).territorio: Basal ganglia, internal capsule and, distally, the lateral hemispheric convexity.
rest|Middle cerebral artery (M1-segment).clinica: Its occlusion causes contralateral hemiplegia and hemianesthesia predominantly of the arm and face, and aphasia if in the dominant hemisphere.

rest|Middle cerebral artery (M3 segment).descripcion: Branches of the middle cerebral artery that run over the opercula from the circular sulcus of the insula to the surface of the lateral sulcus.
rest|Middle cerebral artery (M3 segment).origen: M2 (insular) segment of the middle cerebral artery.
rest|Middle cerebral artery (M3 segment).destino: Continues as M4 cortical branches on the convexity.
rest|Middle cerebral artery (M3 segment).clinica: Distal M3 occlusions produce partial cortical deficits; they are accessible to thrombectomy in selected cases.

rest|Middle cerebral artery (M3-segment).descripcion: Opercular part of the middle cerebral artery: branches that leave the insula over the opercula toward the lateral surface of the hemisphere.
rest|Middle cerebral artery (M3-segment).origen: M2 (insular) segment of the middle cerebral artery.
rest|Middle cerebral artery (M3-segment).destino: Terminal cortical branches (M4) of the convexity.

rest|Middle colic artery.descripcion: Artery that arises below the pancreas and enters the transverse mesocolon, dividing into right and left branches.
rest|Middle colic artery.clinica: It must be preserved or carefully ligated in pancreatic and gastric surgery, because of the risk of ischemia of the transverse colon.

rest|Middle collateral artery.descripcion: Posterior branch of the deep brachial artery that descends through the medial head of the triceps to the posterior aspect of the elbow.
rest|Middle collateral artery.destino: Articular network of the elbow, anastomosing with the interosseous recurrent artery.

rest|Middle genicular artery.descripcion: Unpaired branch of the popliteal artery that pierces the posterior capsule of the knee (oblique popliteal ligament).
rest|Middle genicular artery.territorio: Cruciate ligaments, synovium and posterior capsule of the knee.
rest|Middle genicular artery.clinica: Main blood supply of the cruciate ligaments; may bleed in ACL reconstructions.

rest|Middle lobar artery of right lung.es: Middle lobar artery of the right lung
rest|Middle lobar artery of right lung.descripcion: Branch of the interlobar part of the right pulmonary artery destined for the middle lobe.
rest|Middle lobar artery of right lung.territorio: Middle lobe of the right lung.

rest|Middle meningeal artery.descripcion: Artery that enters the skull through the foramen spinosum and runs between the dura mater and bone, dividing into frontal and parietal branches.
rest|Middle meningeal artery.ramas: Frontal branch, parietal branch, petrosal branch, orbital branch, superior temporal branches.
rest|Middle meningeal artery.clinica: Its rupture from a fracture of the pterion causes epidural hematoma with a lucid interval.

rest|Musculophrenic artery.descripcion: Lateral terminal branch of the internal thoracic artery that follows the costal margin behind the 7th-9th cartilages.
rest|Musculophrenic artery.ramas: Anterior intercostal branches (7th-9th spaces), phrenic branches.
rest|Musculophrenic artery.territorio: Diaphragm, lower intercostal spaces and abdominal muscles.

rest|Mylohyoid branch of inferior alveol.es: Mylohyoid branch of the inferior alveolar artery
rest|Mylohyoid branch of inferior alveol.descripcion: Branch that arises before the mandibular foramen and descends with the mylohyoid nerve in the mylohyoid groove.

rest|Non-coronary leaflet.es: Posterior (non-coronary) semilunar cusp of the aortic valve
rest|Non-coronary leaflet.descripcion: Posterior semilunar cusp of the aortic valve, whose sinus does not give rise to a coronary artery; it contacts the interatrial septum.
rest|Non-coronary leaflet.funcion: Contributes to closure of the aortic valve, preventing backflow into the left ventricle in diastole.
rest|Non-coronary leaflet.clinica: Its sinus is related to both atria; aneurysms of the non-coronary sinus may fistulize into the right atrium.

rest|Obturator artery.descripcion: Artery that runs along the lateral wall of the lesser pelvis and exits through the obturator canal into the thigh.
rest|Obturator artery.ramas: Anterior and posterior branches, acetabular branch, pubic branch.
rest|Obturator artery.territorio: Adductor muscles, obturator externus, femoral head (artery of the ligament of the head).
rest|Obturator artery.clinica: An aberrant obturator artery arising from the inferior epigastric artery (“corona mortis”) may be injured in femoral herniorrhaphy.

rest|Occipital artery.descripcion: Artery that arises opposite the origin of the facial artery, runs under the posterior belly of the digastric in the occipital groove and ascends to the scalp.
rest|Occipital artery.ramas: Sternocleidomastoid branches, mastoid, auricular, meningeal, descending, occipital branches.
rest|Occipital artery.territorio: Occipital scalp, posterior neck muscles, meninges.
rest|Occipital artery.clinica: Its descending branch is a key collateral with the vertebral artery in carotid occlusions.

rest|Ophthalmic artery.descripcion: Artery that enters the orbit through the optic canal below the optic nerve and then crosses it medially.
rest|Ophthalmic artery.origen: Internal carotid artery (cerebral part, after the cavernous sinus).
rest|Ophthalmic artery.ramas: Central retinal, posterior ciliary, lacrimal, supraorbital, anterior and posterior ethmoidal, muscular, palpebral.
rest|Ophthalmic artery.territorio: Eyeball, orbit, forehead, nasal dorsum and part of the nasal cavity.
rest|Ophthalmic artery.clinica: Occlusion of its central retinal branch causes sudden monocular blindness with a “cherry-red” macula.

rest|Orbitofrontal branches of anterior.descripcion: Branch of the A2 segment of the anterior cerebral artery that runs to the orbital surface of the frontal lobe.
rest|Orbitofrontal branches of anterior.territorio: Medial orbital surface of the frontal lobe, gyrus rectus and olfactory bulb.

rest|Palmar carpal branch of radial arte.es: Palmar carpal branch of the radial artery
rest|Palmar carpal branch of radial arte.descripcion: Small branch that crosses the anterior surface of the distal radius under the flexor tendons.
rest|Palmar carpal branch of radial arte.origen: Radial artery (lower border of the pronator quadratus).
rest|Palmar carpal branch of radial arte.destino: Palmar carpal arch, joining the corresponding branch of the ulnar artery.
rest|Palmar carpal branch of radial arte.territorio: Bones and joints of the carpus.

rest|Palmar metacarpal arteries.descripcion: Three arteries that descend through the 2nd-4th interosseous spaces over the palmar interossei.
rest|Palmar metacarpal arteries.destino: Join the common palmar digital arteries.

rest|Parietal branches of middle cerebra.es: Parietal branches of the middle cerebral artery
rest|Parietal branches of middle cerebra.descripcion: Cortical branches of the terminal part (M4) of the middle cerebral artery destined for the lateral parietal lobe.
rest|Parietal branches of middle cerebra.ramas: Anterior and posterior parietal arteries, artery of the angular gyrus.
rest|Parietal branches of middle cerebra.territorio: Lateral parietal cortex: postcentral gyrus, superior and inferior parietal lobules.
rest|Parietal branches of middle cerebra.clinica: Its infarction in the non-dominant hemisphere produces contralateral hemineglect.

rest|Parieto-occipital artery.es: Parieto-occipital branch of the posterior cerebral artery
rest|Parieto-occipital artery.descripcion: Branch of the medial occipital artery that runs along the parieto-occipital sulcus.

rest|Patellar anastomosis.descripcion: Superficial arterial plexus around the patella formed by the genicular and recurrent arteries.
rest|Patellar anastomosis.origen: Superior and inferior genicular arteries, descending genicular artery, anterior tibial recurrent artery, descending branch of the lateral circumflex femoral artery.
rest|Patellar anastomosis.territorio: Patella, patellar tendon and prepatellar skin.
rest|Patellar anastomosis.clinica: Ensures collateral circulation in popliteal occlusion; its interruption in arthroplasty approaches may compromise the vascularization of the patella.

rest|Pectoral branches of thoraco-acromi.es: Pectoral branches of the thoracoacromial artery
rest|Pectoral branches of thoraco-acromi.descripcion: Branches that descend between pectoralis major and minor.
rest|Pectoral branches of thoraco-acromi.territorio: Pectoralis major and minor muscles and breast.
rest|Pectoral branches of thoraco-acromi.clinica: They support the pectoralis major myocutaneous flap used in head and neck reconstruction.

rest|Perforating branches of plantar met.es: Perforating branches of the plantar metatarsal arteries
rest|Perforating branches of plantar met.descripcion: Branches that pass through the intermetatarsal spaces from the sole to the dorsum of the foot.
rest|Perforating branches of plantar met.origen: Plantar metatarsal arteries / deep plantar arch.
rest|Perforating branches of plantar met.territorio: Interossei and connection between the plantar and dorsal circulation.

rest|Perforating femoral arteries.descripcion: Usually three or four arteries that pierce adductor magnus near the linea aspera into the posterior compartment of the thigh.
rest|Perforating femoral arteries.destino: Anastomoses with each other and with the gluteal and popliteal arteries.
rest|Perforating femoral arteries.ramas: Nutrient artery of the femur, muscular branches.
rest|Perforating femoral arteries.territorio: Hamstrings, adductors, vastus lateralis and femoral shaft.
rest|Perforating femoral arteries.clinica: They may be injured in femoral osteosynthesis with screws or cerclage.

rest|Pericallosal artery.descripcion: Continuation of the anterior cerebral artery (A3) that wraps around the corpus callosum in the callosal sulcus.
rest|Pericallosal artery.origen: Anterior cerebral artery (after giving off the callosomarginal artery).
rest|Pericallosal artery.ramas: Precuneal and paracentral arteries (sometimes), callosal branches.
rest|Pericallosal artery.territorio: Corpus callosum, precuneus and medial parietal surface.
rest|Pericallosal artery.clinica: Frequent site of distal anterior cerebral aneurysms.

rest|Plantar arch.descripcion: Deep arterial arch in the sole, over the metatarsal bases, between the third and fourth muscular layers.
rest|Plantar arch.origen: Continuation of the lateral plantar artery; it closes with the deep plantar branch of the dorsalis pedis artery.
rest|Plantar arch.territorio: Toes, muscles and bones of the sole.
rest|Plantar arch.clinica: Deep plantar puncture wounds can injure it with hemorrhage that is difficult to control.

rest|Plantar metatarsal arteries.descripcion: Four arteries that run through the plantar intermetatarsal spaces.
rest|Plantar metatarsal arteries.ramas: Perforating branches, common plantar digital arteries.
rest|Plantar metatarsal arteries.territorio: Toes and interossei of the foot.

rest|Popliteal artery.descripcion: Continuation of the femoral artery from the adductor hiatus; it crosses the popliteal fossa deep to the tibial vein and nerve.
rest|Popliteal artery.origen: Femoral artery (at the adductor magnus hiatus).
rest|Popliteal artery.destino: Divides into the anterior tibial and posterior tibial arteries at the inferior border of popliteus.
rest|Popliteal artery.ramas: Superior, middle and inferior genicular arteries, sural arteries.
rest|Popliteal artery.clinica: Vulnerable in knee dislocations; it is the most frequent location of peripheral aneurysms.

rest|Postcentral arterial branch.descripcion: Cortical branch of the middle cerebral artery that runs along the postcentral sulcus on the lateral surface of the hemisphere.
rest|Postcentral arterial branch.territorio: Postcentral gyrus (primary somatosensory cortex) and anterior parietal lobe.
rest|Postcentral arterial branch.clinica: Its infarction causes a contralateral cortical sensory deficit.

rest|Posterior basal segmental artery of.es: Posterior basal segmental artery of the left lung
rest|Posterior basal segmental artery of.la: Arteria segmentalis basalis posterior pulmonis sinistri
rest|Posterior basal segmental artery of.descripcion: Branch of the basal part of the left pulmonary artery destined for the posterior basal segment (S10).
rest|Posterior basal segmental artery of.territorio: Posterior basal segment of the left lower lobe.
rest|Posterior basal segmental artery of.clinica: Dependent segment frequently affected in aspiration pneumonia in the recumbent position.

rest|Posterior basal segmental artery of.es: Posterior basal segmental artery of the right lung
rest|Posterior basal segmental artery of.la: Arteria segmentalis basalis posterior pulmonis dextri
rest|Posterior basal segmental artery of.descripcion: Branch of the basal part of the right pulmonary artery destined for the posterior basal segment (S10).
rest|Posterior basal segmental artery of.territorio: Posterior basal segment of the right lower lobe.

rest|Posterior branch of renal artery.es: Posterior branch of the renal artery
rest|Posterior branch of renal artery.descripcion: Division of the renal artery that passes behind the renal pelvis.
rest|Posterior branch of renal artery.clinica: Brödel's avascular line between the anterior and posterior territories, useful in nephrolithotomy.

rest|Posterior cerebral artery.descripcion: Terminal branch of the basilar artery that wraps around the midbrain and runs to the medial and inferior surfaces of the occipital and temporal lobes.
rest|Posterior cerebral artery.origen: Bifurcation of the basilar artery (sometimes fetal origin from the internal carotid).
rest|Posterior cerebral artery.ramas: Posteromedial and posterolateral central arteries, posterior choroidal arteries, temporal and lateral and medial occipital arteries.
rest|Posterior cerebral artery.territorio: Midbrain, thalamus, occipital lobe and inferior surface of the temporal lobe.
rest|Posterior cerebral artery.clinica: Its occlusion produces contralateral homonymous hemianopia with macular sparing.

rest|Posterior circumflex humeral artery.descripcion: Artery that passes through the quadrangular space with the axillary nerve and winds around the surgical neck of the humerus.
rest|Posterior circumflex humeral artery.destino: Anastomosis with the anterior circumflex humeral artery.
rest|Posterior circumflex humeral artery.territorio: Deltoid, teres minor, triceps and shoulder joint.
rest|Posterior circumflex humeral artery.clinica: Can be injured along with the axillary nerve in fractures of the surgical neck; main blood supply of the humeral head.

rest|Posterior communicating artery.descripcion: Artery of the circle of Willis that joins the internal carotid and posterior cerebral arteries; it runs alongside the oculomotor nerve.
rest|Posterior communicating artery.ramas: Thalamic and hypothalamic branches (anteromedial central arteries).
rest|Posterior communicating artery.territorio: Thalamus, hypothalamus, optic chiasm, internal capsule.
rest|Posterior communicating artery.clinica: An aneurysm at its origin compresses cranial nerve III: mydriasis and ptosis.

rest|Posterior deep temporal artery.descripcion: Branch that ascends between the temporalis and the skull through the temporal fossa.

rest|Posterior division of internal ilia.es: Posterior division of the internal iliac artery
rest|Posterior division of internal ilia.descripcion: Posterior division of the internal iliac artery that runs backward to the posterior pelvic wall and the gluteal region.
rest|Posterior division of internal ilia.ramas: Iliolumbar, lateral sacral and superior gluteal arteries.
rest|Posterior division of internal ilia.territorio: Posterior pelvic wall, gluteal muscles and lower back.
rest|Posterior division of internal ilia.clinica: In pelvic embolization for trauma, an attempt is made to preserve it to avoid gluteal necrosis.

rest|Posterior ethmoidal artery.descripcion: Artery that passes through the posterior ethmoidal foramen into the nasal cavity and anterior cranial fossa.
rest|Posterior ethmoidal artery.ramas: Meningeal branches, septal and posterior lateral nasal branches.
rest|Posterior ethmoidal artery.territorio: Posterior ethmoidal cells, posterosuperior part of the nasal cavity, dura mater.
rest|Posterior ethmoidal artery.clinica: Surgical landmark: it lies a few millimeters from the optic nerve.

rest|Posterior inferior cerebellar arter.descripcion: Largest branch of the vertebral artery that wraps around the medulla oblongata and runs to the inferior surface of the cerebellum.
rest|Posterior inferior cerebellar arter.ramas: Lateral bulbar branches, choroidal branch to the fourth ventricle, vermian and hemispheric branches.
rest|Posterior inferior cerebellar arter.territorio: Lateral medulla, inferior surface of the cerebellum, choroid plexus of the fourth ventricle.
rest|Posterior inferior cerebellar arter.clinica: Its occlusion causes Wallenberg's lateral medullary syndrome.

rest|Posterior intercostal arteries.descripcion: Arteries that run through the intercostal spaces in the costal groove, between the internal and innermost intercostals, with the vein and nerve.
rest|Posterior intercostal arteries.origen: The first two from the supreme intercostal artery; the 3rd-11th from the thoracic aorta.
rest|Posterior intercostal arteries.destino: Anastomosis with the anterior intercostal arteries.
rest|Posterior intercostal arteries.ramas: Dorsal branch, spinal branches, collateral, lateral cutaneous and mammary branches.
rest|Posterior intercostal arteries.territorio: Thoracic wall, back muscles, spinal cord, breast.
rest|Posterior intercostal arteries.clinica: Thoracentesis is performed at the upper border of the rib to avoid the intercostal neurovascular bundle.

rest|Posterior interosseous artery.descripcion: Artery that passes above the interosseous membrane and descends through the posterior compartment of the forearm.
rest|Posterior interosseous artery.clinica: Pedicle of the posterior interosseous flap for hand reconstruction.

rest|Posterior lateral nasal branches of.descripcion: Branches of the sphenopalatine artery that are distributed to the lateral wall of the nasal cavity.
rest|Posterior lateral nasal branches of.territorio: Conchae, meatuses and paranasal sinuses (maxillary, ethmoidal, sphenoidal).
rest|Posterior lateral nasal branches of.clinica: Source of posterior epistaxis; controlled by endoscopic ligation of the sphenopalatine artery.

rest|Posterior leaflet of left atriovent.es: Posterior leaflet of the mitral valve
rest|Posterior leaflet of left atriovent.descripcion: Posterior (mural) leaflet of the mitral valve, wider at its attachment and divided into scallops P1-P3.
rest|Posterior leaflet of left atriovent.funcion: Closes the left atrioventricular orifice in systole together with the anterior leaflet.
rest|Posterior leaflet of left atriovent.clinica: P2 prolapse is the most frequent cause of repairable degenerative mitral regurgitation.

rest|Posterior parietal artery.descripcion: Cortical branch of the middle cerebral artery that runs along the intraparietal sulcus.

rest|Posterior segmental artery of left.es: Posterior segmental artery of the left lung
rest|Posterior segmental artery of left.descripcion: Branch of the left pulmonary artery destined for the posterior (apicoposterior) segment of the left upper lobe.
rest|Posterior segmental artery of left.territorio: Apicoposterior segment of the left upper lobe.

rest|Posterior segmental artery of right.es: Posterior segmental artery of the right lung
rest|Posterior segmental artery of right.descripcion: Artery destined for the posterior segment (S2) of the right upper lobe; ascending and descending branches.
rest|Posterior segmental artery of right.origen: Superior lobar artery / interlobar part of the right pulmonary artery.
rest|Posterior segmental artery of right.territorio: Posterior segment of the right upper lobe.
rest|Posterior segmental artery of right.clinica: Frequent segment of reactivation tuberculosis and aspiration pneumonia.

rest|Posterior septal branches of spheno.es: Posterior septal branches of the sphenopalatine artery
rest|Posterior septal branches of spheno.descripcion: Branches that cross the nasal roof and descend along the nasal septum toward the incisive canal.
rest|Posterior septal branches of spheno.destino: Anastomosis with the greater palatine and superior labial arteries in Kiesselbach's plexus.
rest|Posterior septal branches of spheno.clinica: They contribute to Kiesselbach's plexus, the origin of most anterior epistaxis.

rest|Posterior superior alveolar artery.descripcion: Artery that descends along the maxillary tuberosity and enters the alveolar foramina.
rest|Posterior superior alveolar artery.territorio: Upper molars and premolars, gingiva, maxillary sinus.
rest|Posterior superior alveolar artery.clinica: It may be injured during posterior superior alveolar nerve block anesthesia, causing a hematoma.

rest|Posterior temporal branch.es: Posterior temporal branch of the middle cerebral artery
rest|Posterior temporal branch.la: Ramus temporalis posterior arteriae cerebri mediae
rest|Posterior temporal branch.descripcion: Cortical branch of the middle cerebral artery that runs along the posterior part of the temporal lobe.
rest|Posterior temporal branch.territorio: Posterior superior, middle and inferior temporal gyri.
rest|Posterior temporal branch.clinica: Its infarction in the dominant hemisphere produces Wernicke's aphasia.

rest|Posterior tibial artery.descripcion: Larger terminal branch of the popliteal artery that descends through the deep posterior compartment of the leg and passes behind the medial malleolus.
rest|Posterior tibial artery.destino: Divides into the medial and lateral plantar arteries beneath the flexor retinaculum.
rest|Posterior tibial artery.ramas: Fibular artery, circumflex fibular artery, nutrient artery of the tibia, medial malleolar and calcaneal branches.
rest|Posterior tibial artery.territorio: Posterior compartment of the leg and sole of the foot.
rest|Posterior tibial artery.clinica: Its pulse is palpated between the medial malleolus and the Achilles tendon.

rest|Prefrontal artery.descripcion: Cortical branch of the middle cerebral artery that ascends along the lateral surface of the anterior frontal lobe.

rest|Proper hepatic artery.descripcion: Artery that ascends in the hepatoduodenal ligament, to the left of the common bile duct and in front of the portal vein.
rest|Proper hepatic artery.origen: Common hepatic artery (after giving off the gastroduodenal artery).
rest|Proper hepatic artery.destino: Divides into the right and left hepatic arteries at the hilum.
rest|Proper hepatic artery.ramas: Right gastric artery (often), right and left hepatic arteries, cystic artery (from the right).
rest|Proper hepatic artery.clinica: Can be compressed in the Pringle maneuver to control hepatic bleeding.

rest|Proper palmar digital arteries.descripcion: Arteries that run along the palmar lateral borders of each finger alongside the digital nerves.
rest|Proper palmar digital arteries.origen: Common palmar digital arteries; those of the thumb and radial side of the index finger from the princeps pollicis artery.
rest|Proper palmar digital arteries.territorio: Fingers, including the nail bed and finger pulps.
rest|Proper palmar digital arteries.clinica: Its transection in digital wounds, along with the accompanying nerve, requires microsurgical repair to preserve the viability of the finger.

rest|Proper plantar digital arteries.descripcion: Arteries that run along the plantar borders of the toes.

rest|Proximal lateral striate branches.descripcion: Proximal lenticulostriate arteries that enter through the anterior perforated substance.
rest|Proximal lateral striate branches.territorio: Putamen, globus pallidus and internal capsule.
rest|Proximal lateral striate branches.clinica: They are end arteries; their rupture causes putaminal hypertensive hemorrhages.

rest|Pulmonary trunk.descripcion: Large arterial trunk that leaves the conus arteriosus of the right ventricle and ascends to the left of the aorta.
rest|Pulmonary trunk.destino: Bifurcates into the right and left pulmonary arteries beneath the aortic arch.
rest|Pulmonary trunk.territorio: Carries deoxygenated blood to the lungs.
rest|Pulmonary trunk.clinica: Its bifurcation is the site of the "saddle" pulmonary thromboembolism.

rest|Radial artery.descripcion: Lateral terminal branch of the brachial artery that descends under brachioradialis, passes through the anatomical snuffbox and forms the deep palmar arch.
rest|Radial artery.ramas: Radial recurrent, palmar and dorsal carpal, superficial palmar, princeps pollicis and radialis indicis arteries.
rest|Radial artery.territorio: Lateral compartment of the forearm, wrist and hand.
rest|Radial artery.clinica: Usual site for pulse, blood gas sampling and catheterization; before cannulating it, collateral flow is assessed with the Allen test.

rest|Radial collateral artery.descripcion: Terminal anterior branch of the deep brachial artery that accompanies the radial nerve to the lateral intermuscular septum.
rest|Radial collateral artery.destino: Anastomosis with the radial recurrent artery in the elbow articular network.
rest|Radial collateral artery.clinica: Pedicle of the lateral arm flap.

rest|Recurrent interosseous artery.descripcion: Branch that ascends behind the elbow between supinator and anconeus.
rest|Recurrent interosseous artery.destino: Elbow articular network, anastomosing with the middle collateral artery.

rest|Right atrium.descripcion: Right cardiac chamber that receives systemic venous blood; it consists of the smooth sinus venarum and the trabeculated portion with the auricle.
rest|Right atrium.origen: Receives the superior and inferior venae cavae and the coronary sinus.
rest|Right atrium.destino: Right ventricle through the tricuspid valve.
rest|Right atrium.funcion: Receives systemic venous blood and houses the sinoatrial and atrioventricular nodes.
rest|Right atrium.clinica: Site of pacemaker lead placement; the fossa ovalis may persist as a patent foramen ovale.

rest|Right colic artery.descripcion: Retroperitoneal artery that runs to the right toward the ascending colon; inconstant.
rest|Right colic artery.origen: Superior mesenteric artery (sometimes from the ileocolic artery).

rest|Right common carotid artery.descripcion: Artery that ascends in the neck within the carotid sheath, medial to the internal jugular vein.
rest|Right common carotid artery.origen: Brachiocephalic trunk (behind the right sternoclavicular joint).
rest|Right common carotid artery.destino: Bifurcates into the internal and external carotid arteries at the level of C4 (upper border of the thyroid cartilage).
