rest|Right common carotid artery.clinica: Its pulse is palpated at the anterior border of sternocleidomastoid; the bifurcation houses the carotid sinus and body.

rest|Right coronary artery.descripcion: Artery arising from the right aortic sinus and running in the right coronary groove to the diaphragmatic surface.
rest|Right coronary artery.destino: Usually continues as the posterior interventricular artery.
rest|Right coronary artery.ramas: Conus branch, sinoatrial nodal branch, right marginal branch, AV nodal branch, posterior interventricular branch.
rest|Right coronary artery.territorio: Right atrium and ventricle, inferior part of the LV, posterior septum, SA and AV nodes.
rest|Right coronary artery.clinica: Its occlusion produces inferior infarction and bradyarrhythmias due to nodal ischemia.

rest|Right coronary leaflet.es: Right semilunar cusp of the aortic valve
rest|Right coronary leaflet.descripcion: Anterior semilunar cusp of the aortic valve whose sinus gives rise to the right coronary artery.
rest|Right coronary leaflet.funcion: Closes the aortic valve in diastole, preventing regurgitation into the left ventricle.
rest|Right coronary leaflet.clinica: In the bicuspid valve, the most frequent finding is fusion of the right and left coronary cusps.

rest|Right inferolateral branch of right.es: Right posterolateral branch of the right coronary artery
rest|Right inferolateral branch of right.la: Ramus posterolateralis dexter arteriae coronariae dextrae
rest|Right inferolateral branch of right.descripcion: Branch of the distal right coronary artery that runs to the inferolateral surface of the left ventricle in right dominance.
rest|Right inferolateral branch of right.territorio: Inferolateral wall of the left ventricle.

rest|Right pulmonary artery.descripcion: Artery that passes beneath the aortic arch and behind the ascending aorta and superior vena cava toward the right pulmonary hilum.
rest|Right pulmonary artery.destino: Lobar and segmental arteries of the right lung.
rest|Right pulmonary artery.ramas: Superior lobar artery, interlobar part, middle lobar, inferior lobar.

rest|Right renal artery.descripcion: Artery longer than the left, passing behind the inferior vena cava toward the right renal hilum.
rest|Right renal artery.ramas: Inferior suprarenal artery, ureteric branches, anterior and posterior branches.
rest|Right renal artery.territorio: Right kidney, suprarenal gland and proximal ureter.

rest|Right semilunar leaflet of pulmonar.es: Right semilunar cusp of the pulmonary valve
rest|Right semilunar leaflet of pulmonar.la: Valvula semilunaris dextra valvae trunci pulmonalis
rest|Right semilunar leaflet of pulmonar.descripcion: One of the three semilunar cusps of the pulmonary valve, to the right of the pulmonary orifice.
rest|Right semilunar leaflet of pulmonar.funcion: Prevents backflow of blood from the pulmonary trunk to the right ventricle.

rest|Right subclavian artery.descripcion: Artery arising behind the right sternoclavicular joint and arching over the first rib behind scalenus anterior.
rest|Right subclavian artery.destino: Continues as the axillary artery at the lateral border of the first rib.
rest|Right subclavian artery.ramas: Vertebral, internal thoracic, thyrocervical trunk, costocervical trunk, dorsal scapular.
rest|Right subclavian artery.territorio: Right upper limb, posterior brain, neck and thoracic wall.
rest|Right subclavian artery.clinica: An aberrant right subclavian artery (arteria lusoria) may compress the esophagus (dysphagia lusoria).

rest|Right testicular artery.descripcion: Slender artery that descends retroperitoneally, crosses in front of the inferior vena cava and ureter, and reaches the testis through the inguinal canal.

rest|Right ventricle.descripcion: Cardiac chamber that forms most of the anterior surface of the heart; it has a septomarginal trabecula and three papillary muscles.
rest|Right ventricle.origen: Receives blood from the right atrium through the tricuspid valve.
rest|Right ventricle.destino: Pumps blood to the pulmonary trunk through the conus arteriosus.
rest|Right ventricle.funcion: Propels deoxygenated blood into the low-pressure pulmonary circulation.
rest|Right ventricle.clinica: It dilates and fails in pulmonary hypertension and massive thromboembolism (cor pulmonale).

rest|Second posterior intercostal artery.descripcion: Artery of the second intercostal space.
rest|Second posterior intercostal artery.destino: Anastomosis with the anterior intercostal artery of the 2nd space.
rest|Second posterior intercostal artery.ramas: Dorsal branch, collateral branch, cutaneous branches.
rest|Second posterior intercostal artery.territorio: Second intercostal space, back muscles and spinal cord.

rest|Septal branches of anterior interve.es: Septal interventricular branches of the anterior interventricular artery
rest|Septal branches of anterior interve.la: Rami interventriculares septales arteriae interventricularis anterioris
rest|Septal branches of anterior interve.descripcion: Perforating branches that penetrate the interventricular septum perpendicularly.
rest|Septal branches of anterior interve.territorio: Anterior two thirds of the interventricular septum and right bundle branch of the bundle of His.
rest|Septal branches of anterior interve.clinica: The first septal branch is the target of alcohol septal ablation in hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy.

rest|Septal branches of posterior ethmoi.es: Septal branches of the posterior ethmoidal artery
rest|Septal branches of posterior ethmoi.descripcion: Small branches that supply the posterosuperior part of the nasal septum.
rest|Septal branches of posterior ethmoi.territorio: Posterosuperior part of the nasal septum.

rest|Septal leaflet of right atrioventri.es: Septal leaflet of the tricuspid valve
rest|Septal leaflet of right atrioventri.descripcion: Medial leaflet of the tricuspid valve, attached to the interventricular septum, near the membranous part.
rest|Septal leaflet of right atrioventri.funcion: Closes the right atrioventricular orifice in systole together with the anterior and posterior leaflets.
rest|Septal leaflet of right atrioventri.clinica: In Ebstein's anomaly it is displaced apically; its attachment is a landmark for the AV node (triangle of Koch).

rest|Septal papillary muscle of right ve.es: Septal papillary muscle of the right ventricle
rest|Septal papillary muscle of right ve.descripcion: Small papillary muscle (sometimes multiple) arising from the interventricular septum of the right ventricle.
rest|Septal papillary muscle of right ve.funcion: Its chordae tendineae tense the septal and anterior leaflets of the tricuspid valve, preventing their eversion in systole.

rest|Short posterior ciliary arteries.descripcion: Numerous arteries (about 10-20) that pierce the sclera around the optic nerve.
rest|Short posterior ciliary arteries.territorio: Choroid, outer layers of the retina and optic nerve head (circle of Zinn-Haller).
rest|Short posterior ciliary arteries.clinica: Their ischemia causes anterior ischemic optic neuropathy, typical of giant cell arteritis.

rest|Sigmoid arteries.descripcion: Two to four arteries that run obliquely in the sigmoid mesocolon.
rest|Sigmoid arteries.territorio: Sigmoid colon and lower descending colon.
rest|Sigmoid arteries.clinica: Ligated in sigmoidectomy; Sudeck's point is an area of weak collateral supply.

rest|Spinal branch of iliolumbar artery.es: Spinal branch of the iliolumbar artery
rest|Spinal branch of iliolumbar artery.descripcion: Small branch that enters the vertebral canal through the L5-S1 intervertebral foramen.
rest|Spinal branch of iliolumbar artery.origen: Lumbar branch of the iliolumbar artery.
rest|Spinal branch of iliolumbar artery.territorio: Cauda equina, meninges and L5-S1 vertebrae.

rest|Splenic artery.descripcion: Thickest and most tortuous branch of the celiac trunk; it runs along the upper border of the pancreas and reaches the spleen through the splenorenal ligament.
rest|Splenic artery.destino: Terminal branches at the splenic hilum.
rest|Splenic artery.ramas: Pancreatic branches (dorsal pancreatic, pancreatica magna), short gastric, left gastro-omental, posterior gastric.
rest|Splenic artery.territorio: Spleen, pancreas (body and tail), gastric fundus and greater curvature.
rest|Splenic artery.clinica: Its aneurysms are the most frequent visceral aneurysms and carry a risk of rupture in pregnancy.

rest|Subcostal artery.descripcion: Last segmental parietal thoracic artery; it runs beneath the 12th rib in front of quadratus lumborum.
rest|Subcostal artery.territorio: Abdominal wall, back muscles and spinal cord.

rest|Submental artery.descripcion: Branch that runs forward over mylohyoid, beneath the mandibular border.
rest|Submental artery.territorio: Submandibular gland, mylohyoid, anterior digastric, skin of the chin.
rest|Submental artery.clinica: Pedicle of the submental flap in facial reconstruction.

rest|Subscapular artery.descripcion: Largest branch of the axillary artery; it descends along the lateral border of the scapula over subscapularis.
rest|Subscapular artery.territorio: Subscapularis, latissimus dorsi, teres major and serratus anterior.
rest|Subscapular artery.clinica: Takes part in the scapular anastomosis, a collateral route in occlusions of the subclavian or axillary artery.

rest|Superficial branch of medial planta.es: Superficial branch of the medial plantar artery
rest|Superficial branch of medial planta.descripcion: Branch that runs along the medial border of the sole to the great toe.
rest|Superficial branch of medial planta.destino: Plantar digital artery of the medial border of the great toe.

rest|Superficial branch of transverse ce.es: Superficial branch of the transverse cervical artery
rest|Superficial branch of transverse ce.descripcion: Branch (superficial cervical artery) that ascends beneath trapezius.
rest|Superficial branch of transverse ce.territorio: Trapezius, levator scapulae, cervical lymph nodes.

rest|Superficial epigastric artery.descripcion: Artery that passes through the cribriform fascia and ascends in the subcutaneous tissue of the lower abdominal wall toward the umbilicus.
rest|Superficial epigastric artery.territorio: Skin and subcutaneous tissue of the infraumbilical abdominal wall.
rest|Superficial epigastric artery.clinica: Pedicle of the SIEA flap for breast reconstruction.

rest|Superficial external pudendal arter.descripcion: Artery that crosses medially over the spermatic cord or round ligament.
rest|Superficial external pudendal arter.territorio: Skin of the pubis, scrotum or labia majora.

rest|Superficial palmar arch.descripcion: Arterial arch beneath the palmar aponeurosis, at the level of the distal border of the extended thumb.
rest|Superficial palmar arch.origen: Continuation of the ulnar artery; completed by the superficial palmar branch of the radial artery.
rest|Superficial palmar arch.territorio: Fingers (except in part the thumb and index finger) and palm.
rest|Superficial palmar arch.clinica: Can be injured in palmar wounds and in carpal tunnel release.

rest|Superficial temporal artery.descripcion: Smaller terminal branch of the external carotid artery that ascends in front of the tragus over the root of the zygomatic process.
rest|Superficial temporal artery.destino: Divides into frontal and parietal branches.
rest|Superficial temporal artery.ramas: Transverse facial, anterior auricular, middle temporal, zygomatico-orbital, frontal, parietal.
rest|Superficial temporal artery.territorio: Temporal and frontoparietal scalp, parotid, temporalis muscle.
rest|Superficial temporal artery.clinica: Biopsied to diagnose giant cell arteritis; its pulse is palpable in front of the tragus.

rest|Superior anorectal artery.descripcion: Continuation of the inferior mesenteric artery that descends in the sigmoid mesocolon and divides over the rectum.
rest|Superior anorectal artery.origen: Inferior mesenteric artery (after crossing the common iliac vessels).
rest|Superior anorectal artery.territorio: Upper rectum and anal canal down to the pectinate line.
rest|Superior anorectal artery.clinica: Its anastomosis with the middle and inferior rectal arteries is a relevant portosystemic connection.

rest|Superior cerebellar artery.descripcion: Artery arising near the end of the basilar artery and wrapping around the cerebral peduncle, beneath the oculomotor nerve.
rest|Superior cerebellar artery.territorio: Superior surface of the cerebellum, cerebellar nuclei, midbrain and upper pons.
rest|Superior cerebellar artery.clinica: Its contact with the trigeminal nerve is the most frequent cause of trigeminal neuralgia.

rest|Superior epigastric artery.descripcion: Artery that descends in the rectus sheath behind rectus abdominis.
rest|Superior epigastric artery.destino: Anastomosis with the inferior epigastric artery within rectus abdominis.
rest|Superior epigastric artery.territorio: Rectus abdominis, supraumbilical abdominal wall, diaphragm.
rest|Superior epigastric artery.clinica: Pedicle of the pedicled TRAM flap; collateral in aortic coarctation.

rest|Superior gluteal artery.descripcion: Artery that leaves the pelvis through the greater sciatic foramen above piriformis.
rest|Superior gluteal artery.origen: Posterior division of the internal iliac artery.
rest|Superior gluteal artery.ramas: Superficial branch, deep branch (superior and inferior).
rest|Superior gluteal artery.territorio: Gluteus maximus, medius and minimus, tensor fasciae latae.
rest|Superior gluteal artery.clinica: Can be injured in pelvic fractures or fractures of the sciatic notch, with severe hemorrhage.

rest|Superior labial artery.descripcion: Tortuous branch that runs in the upper lip between orbicularis oris and the mucosa, anastomosing with its contralateral counterpart.
rest|Superior labial artery.territorio: Upper lip, anterior nasal septum and nasal ala.
rest|Superior labial artery.clinica: Contributes to Kiesselbach's plexus; at risk in lip fillers with vascular occlusion.

rest|Superior lateral genicular artery.descripcion: Branch that winds around the femur above the lateral condyle, beneath the biceps femoris tendon.
rest|Superior lateral genicular artery.clinica: Can be injured in arthroplasty (lateral retinacular release).

rest|Superior lingular artery of left lu.es: Superior lingular artery of the left lung
rest|Superior lingular artery of left lu.descripcion: Branch of the lingular artery that supplies the superior lingular segment (S4).
rest|Superior lingular artery of left lu.territorio: Superior lingular segment of the left upper lobe.

rest|Superior lobar artery of right lung.es: Superior lobar artery of the right lung
rest|Superior lobar artery of right lung.descripcion: First branch of the right pulmonary artery (anterior trunk), arising before the hilum.
rest|Superior lobar artery of right lung.ramas: Apical, anterior and posterior segmental arteries.
rest|Superior lobar artery of right lung.clinica: First arterial structure to be controlled in right upper lobectomy.

rest|Superior medial genicular artery.descripcion: Branch that winds around the femur above the medial condyle, beneath the tendons of semimembranosus and adductor magnus.

rest|Superior mesenteric artery.descripcion: Unpaired artery arising at the level of L1, passing behind the pancreas and in front of the duodenum toward the root of the mesentery.
rest|Superior mesenteric artery.origen: Anterior surface of the abdominal aorta (L1).
rest|Superior mesenteric artery.ramas: Inferior pancreaticoduodenal, jejunal, ileal, middle colic, right colic, ileocolic.
rest|Superior mesenteric artery.territorio: Midgut: distal duodenum to two thirds of the transverse colon, head of the pancreas.
rest|Superior mesenteric artery.clinica: Its embolism causes acute mesenteric ischemia; it may compress the duodenum (Wilkie's syndrome).

rest|Superior phrenic arteries.descripcion: Small paired arteries arising from the distal thoracic aorta.
rest|Superior phrenic arteries.origen: Thoracic aorta (just above the aortic hiatus).
rest|Superior phrenic arteries.territorio: Superior posterior surface of the diaphragm.

rest|Superior segmental artery of left l.es: Superior segmental artery of the left lung
rest|Superior segmental artery of left l.descripcion: Branch of the left pulmonary artery destined for the superior (apical, S6) segment of the lower lobe.
rest|Superior segmental artery of left l.territorio: Superior segment of the left lower lobe.
rest|Superior segmental artery of left l.clinica: The superior segment is a frequent site of aspiration pneumonia in the supine position.

rest|Superior segmental artery of right.es: Superior segmental artery of the right lung
rest|Superior segmental artery of right.descripcion: Branch of the interlobar part of the right pulmonary artery destined for the superior segment (S6) of the lower lobe.
rest|Superior segmental artery of right.territorio: Superior segment of the right lower lobe.
rest|Superior segmental artery of right.clinica: Frequent segment of aspiration pneumonia in the supine position.

rest|Superior ulnar collateral artery.descripcion: Artery that accompanies the ulnar nerve and passes behind the medial epicondyle.
rest|Superior ulnar collateral artery.destino: Anastomosis with the posterior ulnar recurrent artery.
rest|Superior ulnar collateral artery.territorio: Medial triceps, ulnar nerve and elbow.

rest|Supra-orbital artery.descripcion: Artery that leaves the orbit through the supra-orbital notch or foramen with the supra-orbital nerve.
rest|Supra-orbital artery.territorio: Forehead, scalp, upper eyelid, frontal sinus.
rest|Supra-orbital artery.clinica: Anastomosis with the superficial temporal artery: internal-external carotid communication.

rest|Suprascapular artery.descripcion: Artery that crosses scalenus anterior and the brachial plexus and passes over the superior transverse ligament of the scapula.
rest|Suprascapular artery.origen: Thyrocervical trunk (sometimes directly from the subclavian).
rest|Suprascapular artery.destino: Scapular anastomosis with the circumflex scapular and dorsal scapular arteries.
rest|Suprascapular artery.territorio: Supraspinatus, infraspinatus, acromioclavicular and glenohumeral joints.
rest|Suprascapular artery.clinica: Takes part in the scapular collateral network in subclavian occlusions.

rest|Supratrochlear artery.descripcion: Terminal branch of the ophthalmic artery that exits at the superomedial angle of the orbit with the supratrochlear nerve.
rest|Supratrochlear artery.clinica: Pedicle of the paramedian forehead flap in nasal reconstruction.

rest|Supreme intercostal artery.descripcion: Artery that descends in front of the necks of the 1st and 2nd ribs.

rest|Temporal branches of middle cerebra.es: Temporal branches of the middle cerebral artery
rest|Temporal branches of middle cerebra.descripcion: Cortical branches of the middle cerebral artery destined for the lateral surface of the temporal lobe.
rest|Temporal branches of middle cerebra.ramas: Anterior, middle and posterior temporal branches; temporopolar.
rest|Temporal branches of middle cerebra.territorio: Superior, middle and inferior temporal gyri.
rest|Temporal branches of middle cerebra.clinica: Their infarction in the dominant hemisphere causes comprehension aphasia.

rest|Temporo-occipital branch.es: Temporo-occipital branch of the middle cerebral artery
rest|Temporo-occipital branch.descripcion: Posterior cortical branch of the middle cerebral artery that runs to the temporo-occipital junction.

rest|Thoracic aorta.descripcion: Portion of the descending aorta in the posterior mediastinum, from T4 to T12, to the left of the vertebral column.
rest|Thoracic aorta.destino: Continues as the abdominal aorta on passing through the aortic hiatus (T12).
rest|Thoracic aorta.ramas: Bronchial, esophageal, pericardial, mediastinal, 3rd-11th posterior intercostal, subcostal, superior phrenic.
rest|Thoracic aorta.territorio: Thoracic wall, esophagus, bronchi, pericardium, diaphragm, spinal cord.
rest|Thoracic aorta.clinica: Site of type B aortic dissection and thoracoabdominal aneurysms.

rest|Thoraco-acromial artery.descripcion: Short trunk that pierces the clavipectoral fascia above pectoralis minor.
rest|Thoraco-acromial artery.ramas: Acromial, clavicular, deltoid and pectoral branches.
rest|Thoraco-acromial artery.territorio: Pectoral muscles, deltoid, acromioclavicular joint, clavicle.
rest|Thoraco-acromial artery.clinica: Pedicle of the pectoralis major flap.

rest|Thoracodorsal artery.descripcion: Continuation of the subscapular artery that accompanies the thoracodorsal nerve to latissimus dorsi.
rest|Thoracodorsal artery.clinica: Pedicle of the latissimus dorsi flap for breast reconstruction.

rest|Thyrocervical trunk.descripcion: Short trunk arising from the first part of the subclavian artery, next to the medial border of scalenus anterior.
rest|Thyrocervical trunk.ramas: Inferior thyroid, transverse cervical, suprascapular (ascending cervical via the inferior thyroid).

rest|Transverse cervical artery.descripcion: Artery that crosses the posterior triangle of the neck laterally, in front of the brachial plexus.
rest|Transverse cervical artery.clinica: Useful as a recipient vessel in head and neck microsurgery.

rest|Transverse facial artery.descripcion: Artery that crosses the face horizontally between the zygomatic arch and the parotid duct.
rest|Transverse facial artery.territorio: Parotid, parotid duct, masseter, skin of the cheek.

rest|Ulnar artery.descripcion: Larger terminal branch of the brachial artery that descends through the anterior compartment beneath pronator teres and the flexors, alongside the ulnar nerve.
rest|Ulnar artery.ramas: Ulnar recurrent arteries, common interosseous, palmar and dorsal carpal, deep palmar.
rest|Ulnar artery.clinica: The Allen test assesses its sufficiency before cannulating the radial artery.

rest|Ulnar recurrent artery.descripcion: Artery that ascends with anterior and posterior branches around the medial epicondyle.
rest|Ulnar recurrent artery.destino: Anastomosis with the superior and inferior ulnar collateral arteries.
rest|Ulnar recurrent artery.territorio: Medial elbow, flexor muscles and ulnar nerve.

rest|Vertebral artery.descripcion: Artery that ascends through the transverse foramina C6-C1, winds around the atlas and enters the skull through the foramen magnum; four segments V1-V4.
rest|Vertebral artery.destino: Joins its contralateral counterpart to form the basilar artery at the lower border of the pons.
rest|Vertebral artery.ramas: Spinal branches, meningeal, anterior spinal, posterior spinal, posterior inferior cerebellar.
rest|Vertebral artery.territorio: Cervical spinal cord, medulla, cerebellum and, via the basilar artery, brainstem and occipital lobes.
rest|Vertebral artery.clinica: Its dissection from cervical manipulation or trauma can cause vertebrobasilar stroke.

rest|Accessory hemi-azygos vein.descripcion: Longitudinal vein on the left side of the posterior mediastinum, paravertebral, between T4 and T8.
rest|Accessory hemi-azygos vein.origen: Confluence of the left 4th to 8th posterior intercostal veins.
rest|Accessory hemi-azygos vein.destino: Azygos vein (crossing behind the aorta at the level of T7-T8) or hemiazygos vein.
rest|Accessory hemi-azygos vein.ramas: Left 4th-8th posterior intercostal veins, bronchial and esophageal veins.
rest|Accessory hemi-azygos vein.clinica: Cavo-caval collateral pathway in obstruction of the superior or inferior vena cava.

rest|Angular vein.descripcion: Short vein at the medial angle of the eye, next to the root of the nose; beginning of the facial vein.
rest|Angular vein.origen: Junction of the supratrochlear and supra-orbital veins.
rest|Angular vein.territorio: Forehead, eyelids and root of the nose.
rest|Angular vein.clinica: Communicates with the superior ophthalmic vein: route of spread of infections from the "danger triangle" to the cavernous sinus.

rest|Anterior circumflex humeral vein.descripcion: Satellite vein of the artery of the same name that winds around the front of the surgical neck of the humerus.
rest|Anterior circumflex humeral vein.origen: Venous network of the shoulder joint and neighboring muscles.
rest|Anterior circumflex humeral vein.territorio: Glenohumeral joint, head of the humerus, deltoid and biceps.

rest|Anterior division of retromandibula.es: Anterior division of the retromandibular vein
rest|Anterior division of retromandibula.descripcion: Anterior branch of the retromandibular vein that emerges below the parotid gland.
rest|Anterior division of retromandibula.origen: Retromandibular vein, at the inferior pole of the parotid.
rest|Anterior division of retromandibula.destino: Joins the facial vein to form the common facial vein.

rest|Anterior intercavernous sinus.descripcion: Transverse dural sinus located in front of the pituitary gland, in the diaphragma sellae.
rest|Anterior intercavernous sinus.clinica: Together with the posterior one it forms the circular sinus; it may bleed in transsphenoidal approaches.

rest|Anterior jugular vein.descripcion: Superficial vein of the neck that descends near the midline, in front of the infrahyoid muscles.
rest|Anterior jugular vein.origen: Superficial submental veins, near the hyoid bone.
rest|Anterior jugular vein.destino: External jugular vein or subclavian vein.
rest|Anterior jugular vein.ramas: Jugular venous arch (joins both anterior jugular veins in the suprasternal space).
rest|Anterior jugular vein.clinica: The jugular venous arch may bleed during tracheostomy.

rest|Anterior tibial veins.descripcion: Paired deep veins that accompany the anterior tibial artery in the anterior compartment of the leg.
rest|Anterior tibial veins.origen: Continuation of the dorsal veins of the foot (dorsal vein of the foot).
rest|Anterior tibial veins.destino: They join the posterior tibial veins to form the popliteal vein.
rest|Anterior tibial veins.territorio: Anterior compartment of the leg and dorsum of the foot.
rest|Anterior tibial veins.clinica: They may be affected in distal deep vein thrombosis.

rest|Anterior vein of left lung.es: Anterior vein of the left lung
rest|Anterior vein of left lung.descripcion: Segmental pulmonary vein of the left upper lobe that drains the anterior segment.
rest|Anterior vein of left lung.origen: Intrasegmental and intersegmental tributaries of the anterior segment (S3).
rest|Anterior vein of left lung.territorio: Anterior segment of the left upper lobe (oxygenated blood).
rest|Anterior vein of left lung.clinica: Intersegmental veins serve as landmarks in segmentectomies.

rest|Anterior vein of right lung.es: Anterior vein of the right lung
rest|Anterior vein of right lung.descripcion: Segmental pulmonary vein of the right upper lobe that drains the anterior segment.
rest|Anterior vein of right lung.territorio: Anterior segment of the right upper lobe.
rest|Anterior vein of right lung.clinica: Surgical landmark in segmentectomies and upper lobectomies.

rest|Apical vein of right lung.es: Apical vein of the right lung
rest|Apical vein of right lung.descripcion: Segmental pulmonary vein of the right upper lobe that drains the apical segment.
rest|Apical vein of right lung.territorio: Apical segment of the right upper lobe.

rest|Apicoposterior vein of left lung.es: Apicoposterior vein of the left lung
rest|Apicoposterior vein of left lung.descripcion: Segmental pulmonary vein of the left upper lobe that drains the apicoposterior segment.
rest|Apicoposterior vein of left lung.territorio: Apicoposterior segment of the left upper lobe.

rest|Axillary vein.descripcion: Large vein of the axilla, medial to the axillary artery, from the lower border of teres major to the lateral border of the 1st rib.
rest|Axillary vein.origen: Junction of the brachial veins with the basilic vein.
rest|Axillary vein.destino: Continues as the subclavian vein at the lateral border of the 1st rib.
rest|Axillary vein.ramas: Cephalic vein, circumflex humeral veins, subscapular, lateral thoracic, thoraco-epigastric.
rest|Axillary vein.territorio: Upper limb, lateral thoracic wall and breast.
rest|Axillary vein.clinica: Effort thrombosis (Paget-Schroetter syndrome); risk of injury in axillary dissection.

rest|Azygos vein.descripcion: Unpaired vein of the posterior mediastinum, to the right of the vertebral bodies, which arches over the right main bronchus.
rest|Azygos vein.origen: Junction of the right ascending lumbar vein and the right subcostal vein (sometimes from the inferior vena cava).
rest|Azygos vein.destino: Superior vena cava, at the level of T4.
rest|Azygos vein.ramas: Right posterior intercostal veins, right superior intercostal vein, hemiazygos, accessory hemiazygos, esophageal, bronchial, pericardial.
rest|Azygos vein.territorio: Posterior thoracic wall, part of the abdominal wall, esophagus and bronchi.
rest|Azygos vein.clinica: Main cavo-caval collateral; in inferior vena cava obstruction it may become greatly dilated (azygos continuation).

rest|Basilar venous plexus.descripcion: Network of dural venous channels over the clivus, between both inferior petrosal sinuses.
rest|Basilar venous plexus.origen: Interconnection of the cavernous and inferior petrosal sinuses.
rest|Basilar venous plexus.destino: Petrosal sinuses and anterior internal vertebral venous plexus.
rest|Basilar venous plexus.territorio: Clivus and dorsal region of the sella turcica.
rest|Basilar venous plexus.clinica: Route of communication of infections and metastases with the vertebral plexus.

rest|Basilic vein.descripcion: Superficial vein of the medial border of the forearm and arm that pierces the brachial fascia at mid-arm.
rest|Basilic vein.origen: Ulnar part of the dorsal venous network of the hand.
rest|Basilic vein.destino: Joins the brachial veins to form the axillary vein.
rest|Basilic vein.territorio: Ulnar (medial) side of the hand, forearm and arm.
rest|Basilic vein.clinica: Used for peripherally inserted central catheters (PICC) and arteriovenous fistulas for hemodialysis.

rest|Brachial veins.descripcion: Paired deep (comitant) veins that accompany the brachial artery in the arm.
rest|Brachial veins.origen: Junction of the radial and ulnar veins in the cubital fossa.
rest|Brachial veins.destino: They join the basilic vein to form the axillary vein.
rest|Brachial veins.ramas: Muscular veins of the arm, deep brachial vein.
rest|Brachial veins.territorio: Deep structures of the arm and forearm.

rest|Cavernous sinus.descripcion: Paired dural sinus on each side of the sella turcica and the body of the sphenoid; it contains the internal carotid artery and the abducens nerve.
rest|Cavernous sinus.origen: Receives the superior and inferior ophthalmic veins, sphenoparietal sinus and superficial middle cerebral veins.
rest|Cavernous sinus.destino: Superior and inferior petrosal sinuses; pterygoid plexus via emissary veins.
rest|Cavernous sinus.ramas: Ophthalmic veins, sphenoparietal sinus, superficial middle cerebral vein, intercavernous sinuses.
rest|Cavernous sinus.territorio: Orbit, part of the cerebral cortex, pituitary gland.
rest|Cavernous sinus.clinica: Septic thrombosis of the cavernous sinus: ophthalmoplegia, proptosis and chemosis; carotid-cavernous fistula.

rest|Cephalic vein.descripcion: Superficial vein of the lateral border of the forearm and arm that ascends in the deltopectoral groove.
rest|Cephalic vein.origen: Radial part of the dorsal venous network of the hand (anatomical snuffbox).
rest|Cephalic vein.destino: Axillary vein, after piercing the clavipectoral fascia.
rest|Cephalic vein.ramas: Median cubital vein, accessory cephalic vein, antebrachial veins.
rest|Cephalic vein.territorio: Radial (lateral) side of the hand, forearm and arm.
rest|Cephalic vein.clinica: Frequent venous access; used for arteriovenous fistulas and pacemaker implantation.

rest|Circumflex scapular vein.descripcion: Vein that accompanies the artery of the same name through the triangular space on the posterior surface of the scapula.
rest|Circumflex scapular vein.territorio: Muscles of the posterior surface of the scapula.
rest|Circumflex scapular vein.clinica: Pedicle of the scapular flap in reconstructive surgery.

rest|Common facial vein.descripcion: Short venous trunk below the angle of the mandible.
rest|Common facial vein.origen: Junction of the facial vein with the anterior division of the retromandibular vein.
rest|Common facial vein.destino: Internal jugular vein, at the level of the hyoid bone.
rest|Common facial vein.ramas: Facial vein, anterior division of the retromandibular vein; sometimes lingual and superior thyroid.
rest|Common facial vein.clinica: Landmark in neck dissection for locating the carotid bifurcation.

rest|Common iliac vein.descripcion: Paired pelvic venous trunk, posterior and medial to the common iliac artery.
rest|Common iliac vein.origen: Junction of the external and internal iliac veins in front of the sacroiliac joint.
rest|Common iliac vein.destino: Joins its contralateral counterpart to form the inferior vena cava at the level of L5.
rest|Common iliac vein.ramas: Iliolumbar vein, sometimes lateral sacral; the left receives the median sacral vein.
rest|Common iliac vein.clinica: Compression of the left common iliac vein by the right common iliac artery (May-Thurner syndrome).

rest|Coronary sinus.descripcion: Large venous channel in the posterior part of the coronary groove, between the left atrium and ventricle.
rest|Coronary sinus.origen: Continuation of the great cardiac vein (at the level of the oblique vein of the left atrium).
rest|Coronary sinus.destino: Right atrium, orifice with the valve of the coronary sinus.
rest|Coronary sinus.ramas: Great, middle and small cardiac veins, posterior vein of the left ventricle, oblique vein of the left atrium.
rest|Coronary sinus.clinica: Access for cardiac resynchronization leads (left ventricle).

rest|Deep dorsal vein of penis.es: Deep dorsal vein of the penis
rest|Deep dorsal vein of penis.descripcion: Unpaired subfascial vein in the midline of the dorsum of the penis, between the dorsal arteries.
rest|Deep dorsal vein of penis.origen: Veins of the glans and corpora cavernosa (circumflex veins).
rest|Deep dorsal vein of penis.destino: Prostatic venous plexus, passing beneath the pubic symphysis.
rest|Deep dorsal vein of penis.ramas: Circumflex veins, veins of the glans.
rest|Deep dorsal vein of penis.clinica: Its compression contributes to erection; ligated in some treatments of venous leak.

rest|Deep femoral vein.descripcion: Deep vein of the thigh, anterior to the deep femoral artery.
rest|Deep femoral vein.origen: Perforating veins of the thigh and circumflex femoral veins.
rest|Deep femoral vein.destino: Femoral vein, about 8 cm below the inguinal ligament.
rest|Deep femoral vein.ramas: Perforating veins, medial and lateral circumflex femoral veins.
rest|Deep femoral vein.clinica: May be the site of deep vein thrombosis.

rest|Deep venous palmar arch.descripcion: Deep venous arch of the palm that accompanies the deep palmar arterial arch.

rest|Dorsal digital veins of foot.es: Dorsal digital veins of the foot
rest|Dorsal digital veins of foot.descripcion: Superficial veins that run along the dorsal borders of the toes.
rest|Dorsal digital veins of foot.origen: Dorsal venous plexuses of the toes.

rest|Dorsal digital veins of hand.es: Dorsal digital veins of the hand
rest|Dorsal digital veins of hand.descripcion: Superficial veins that run along the dorsal borders of the fingers.

rest|Dorsal metatarsal veins.descripcion: Superficial veins of the dorsum of the foot located over the intermetatarsal spaces.
rest|Dorsal metatarsal veins.origen: Junction of adjacent dorsal digital veins.
rest|Dorsal metatarsal veins.destino: Dorsal venous arch of the foot.
rest|Dorsal metatarsal veins.territorio: Dorsum of the forefoot and toes.

rest|Dorsal venous arch of foot.es: Dorsal venous arch of the foot
rest|Dorsal venous arch of foot.descripcion: Transverse subcutaneous venous arch on the dorsum of the foot, over the proximal part of the metatarsals.
rest|Dorsal venous arch of foot.destino: Medially the great saphenous vein; laterally the small saphenous vein.
rest|Dorsal venous arch of foot.territorio: Dorsum of the foot and toes.
rest|Dorsal venous arch of foot.clinica: Visible and palpable; useful for venous cannulation in pediatrics.

rest|Dorsal venous network of hand.es: Dorsal venous network of the hand
rest|Dorsal venous network of hand.descripcion: Subcutaneous venous plexus on the dorsum of the hand.
rest|Dorsal venous network of hand.destino: Cephalic vein (radial side) and basilic vein (ulnar side).
rest|Dorsal venous network of hand.territorio: Dorsum of the hand and fingers.
rest|Dorsal venous network of hand.clinica: Usual site of peripheral venous cannulation.

rest|External iliac vein.descripcion: Vein of the lateral pelvic wall, medial to the external iliac artery.
rest|External iliac vein.origen: Continuation of the femoral vein after the inguinal ligament.
rest|External iliac vein.destino: Joins the internal iliac vein to form the common iliac vein.
rest|External iliac vein.ramas: Inferior epigastric vein, deep circumflex iliac vein, pubic vein.
rest|External iliac vein.territorio: Lower limb and lower anterior abdominal wall.
rest|External iliac vein.clinica: Risk of injury in laparoscopic hernia repair ("triangle of doom").

rest|External jugular vein.descripcion: Superficial vein of the neck that obliquely crosses sternocleidomastoid beneath platysma.
rest|External jugular vein.origen: Junction of the posterior division of the retromandibular vein and the posterior auricular vein, near the mandibular angle.
rest|External jugular vein.ramas: Posterior external jugular, transverse cervical, suprascapular, anterior jugular.
rest|External jugular vein.territorio: Scalp, lateral face and superficial neck.
rest|External jugular vein.clinica: Its engorgement indicates raised central venous pressure; useful for emergency venous access.

rest|External pudendal veins.descripcion: Superficial veins of the inguinal and external genital region.
rest|External pudendal veins.origen: Veins of the scrotum or labia majora and of the penis or clitoris (superficial dorsal veins).
rest|External pudendal veins.destino: Great saphenous vein or femoral vein.
rest|External pudendal veins.ramas: Anterior scrotal/labial veins, superficial dorsal veins of the penis/clitoris.
rest|External pudendal veins.territorio: External genitalia and skin of the pubis.
rest|External pudendal veins.clinica: They must be ligated in saphenofemoral crossectomy for varicose veins.

rest|Facial vein.descripcion: Main vein of the face, descending obliquely behind the facial artery and crossing the mandible in front of masseter.
rest|Facial vein.destino: Common facial vein or directly the internal jugular vein.
rest|Facial vein.ramas: Palpebral, external nasal, superior and inferior labial, deep facial, submental, external palatine veins.
rest|Facial vein.clinica: Without effective valves; communicates with the cavernous sinus via the ophthalmic and deep facial veins.

rest|Femoral vein.descripcion: Deep vein of the thigh that accompanies the femoral artery, medial to it in the femoral triangle.
rest|Femoral vein.origen: Continuation of the popliteal vein at the adductor hiatus.
rest|Femoral vein.destino: Continues as the external iliac vein beneath the inguinal ligament.
rest|Femoral vein.ramas: Deep femoral vein, great saphenous vein, external pudendal veins, circumflex femoral veins.
rest|Femoral vein.clinica: Central venous access in the groin; frequent location of deep vein thrombosis.

rest|Fibular veins.descripcion: Paired deep veins accompanying the fibular artery in the posterior compartment of the leg.
rest|Fibular veins.origen: Veins of the lateral and deep posterior compartments of the leg.
rest|Fibular veins.territorio: Posterior and lateral compartments of the leg.
rest|Fibular veins.clinica: Frequent site of distal deep vein thrombosis.

rest|Genicular veins.descripcion: Veins accompanying the genicular arteries around the knee.
rest|Genicular veins.origen: Periarticular venous network of the knee.

rest|Great cardiac vein.descripcion: Vein of the heart that ascends in the anterior interventricular groove and turns into the left coronary (atrioventricular) groove.
rest|Great cardiac vein.origen: Near the cardiac apex, in the anterior interventricular groove.
rest|Great cardiac vein.ramas: Left ventricular veins, left marginal vein, interventricular veins.
rest|Great cardiac vein.territorio: Territory of the left coronary artery (anterior surface of both ventricles).
rest|Great cardiac vein.clinica: Route for leads and epicardial ablation techniques.

rest|Great saphenous vein.descripcion: Longest superficial vein of the body; ascends in front of the medial malleolus and along the medial aspect of the leg and thigh.
rest|Great saphenous vein.origen: Medial end of the dorsal venous arch of the foot.
rest|Great saphenous vein.destino: Femoral vein, through the saphenous hiatus (saphenofemoral junction).
rest|Great saphenous vein.ramas: External pudendal veins, superficial epigastric, superficial circumflex iliac, accessory saphenous veins, perforators.
rest|Great saphenous vein.territorio: Skin and subcutaneous tissue of the medial aspect of the lower limb.
rest|Great saphenous vein.clinica: Used as a graft in coronary bypass; frequent site of varicose veins.

rest|Hemi-azygos vein.descripcion: Vein on the left side of the lower thoracic spine, in the posterior mediastinum.
rest|Hemi-azygos vein.origen: Union of the left ascending lumbar vein and the left subcostal vein (often from the left renal vein).
rest|Hemi-azygos vein.destino: Azygos vein, crossing behind the aorta at the level of T8-T9.
rest|Hemi-azygos vein.ramas: Left lower posterior intercostal veins (9th-11th), esophageal, mediastinal.

rest|Hepatic portal vein.descripcion: Large vein carrying blood from the digestive tract and spleen to the liver; ascends in the hepatoduodenal ligament behind the common bile duct and the hepatic artery.
rest|Hepatic portal vein.origen: Union of the superior mesenteric and splenic veins behind the neck of the pancreas.
rest|Hepatic portal vein.destino: Hepatic hilum: divides into right and left branches.
rest|Hepatic portal vein.ramas: Left gastric vein, right gastric, prepyloric, cystic, posterosuperior pancreaticoduodenal, paraumbilical veins.
rest|Hepatic portal vein.territorio: Abdominal digestive tract, spleen, pancreas and gallbladder.
rest|Hepatic portal vein.clinica: Portal hypertension: esophageal varices, ascites and caput medusae.

rest|Hepatic veins.descripcion: Valveless intrahepatic veins (right, middle and left) that separate the hepatic sectors.
rest|Hepatic veins.origen: Confluence of the centrilobular and sublobular veins.
rest|Hepatic veins.destino: Inferior vena cava, immediately below the diaphragm.
rest|Hepatic veins.ramas: Right, middle and left hepatic veins; accessory hepatic veins of the caudate lobe.

rest|Iliolumbar vein.descripcion: Vein accompanying the iliolumbar artery in the iliac fossa, behind the psoas.
rest|Iliolumbar vein.origen: Veins of the iliac fossa and of the psoas, iliacus and quadratus lumborum muscles.
rest|Iliolumbar vein.destino: Common iliac vein (or internal iliac vein).
rest|Iliolumbar vein.territorio: Psoas, iliacus and quadratus lumborum muscles; lower lumbar spine.
rest|Iliolumbar vein.clinica: May be injured when mobilizing the common iliac vein in anterior lumbar surgery.

rest|Inferior basal vein of left lung.es: Inferior basal vein of the left lung
rest|Inferior basal vein of left lung.descripcion: Vein of the left lower lobe draining the posterior basal segments.
rest|Inferior basal vein of left lung.origen: Tributaries from the basal segments (mainly posterior basal).
rest|Inferior basal vein of left lung.territorio: Basal segments of the left lower lobe.

rest|Inferior basal vein of right lung.es: Inferior basal vein of the right lung
rest|Inferior basal vein of right lung.descripcion: Vein of the right lower lobe draining the posterior basal segments.
rest|Inferior basal vein of right lung.origen: Tributaries from the basal segments (mainly posterior basal).
rest|Inferior basal vein of right lung.territorio: Basal segments of the right lower lobe.

rest|Inferior epigastric vein.descripcion: Vein(s) accompanying the inferior epigastric artery behind the rectus abdominis muscle.
rest|Inferior epigastric vein.origen: Anastomosis with the superior epigastric veins in the rectus sheath.
rest|Inferior epigastric vein.clinica: Cavo-caval collateral pathway; pedicle of the DIEP flap in breast reconstruction.

rest|Inferior gluteal veins.descripcion: Veins accompanying the inferior gluteal artery and leaving the pelvis below the piriformis.
rest|Inferior gluteal veins.origen: Veins of the gluteus maximus and posterior thigh.
rest|Inferior gluteal veins.territorio: Gluteus maximus and upper posterior thigh.
rest|Inferior gluteal veins.clinica: They communicate with the medial circumflex femoral vein: collateral pathway.

rest|Inferior labial veins.origen: Venous plexus of the lower lip.

rest|Inferior lingular vein of left lung.es: Inferior lingular vein of the left lung
rest|Inferior lingular vein of left lung.descripcion: Tributary of the lingular vein draining the inferior lingular segment of the left upper lobe.
rest|Inferior lingular vein of left lung.origen: Tributaries from the inferior lingular segment (S5).
rest|Inferior lingular vein of left lung.destino: Lingular vein, tributary of the left superior pulmonary vein.

rest|Inferior mesenteric vein.descripcion: Retroperitoneal vein to the left of the inferior mesenteric artery, ascending lateral to the duodenojejunal flexure.
rest|Inferior mesenteric vein.origen: Continuation of the superior rectal vein.
rest|Inferior mesenteric vein.destino: Splenic vein (sometimes the superior mesenteric vein or the confluence).
rest|Inferior mesenteric vein.ramas: Sigmoid veins, left colic, superior rectal.
rest|Inferior mesenteric vein.territorio: Descending colon, sigmoid and upper rectum.
rest|Inferior mesenteric vein.clinica: Rectal anastomoses with caval veins form a portosystemic shunt (internal hemorrhoids).

rest|Inferior ophthalmic vein.descripcion: Vein of the floor of the orbit, above the inferior rectus.
rest|Inferior ophthalmic vein.origen: Venous plexus in the anterior part of the orbital floor.
rest|Inferior ophthalmic vein.destino: Cavernous sinus (directly or via the superior ophthalmic vein); communicates with the pterygoid plexus through the inferior orbital fissure.
rest|Inferior ophthalmic vein.ramas: Muscular veins, inferior vorticose veins, lacrimal veins.
rest|Inferior ophthalmic vein.territorio: Inferior orbital muscles, lower eyelid, lacrimal sac.
rest|Inferior ophthalmic vein.clinica: Route of spread of facial infections to the cavernous sinus.

rest|Inferior petrosal sinus.descripcion: Dural sinus in the groove between the petrous part of the temporal bone and the occipital bone.
rest|Inferior petrosal sinus.origen: Posteroinferior part of the cavernous sinus.
rest|Inferior petrosal sinus.destino: Superior bulb of the internal jugular vein, through the jugular foramen.
rest|Inferior petrosal sinus.ramas: Labyrinthine veins, veins of the medulla oblongata and pons, basilar plexus.
rest|Inferior petrosal sinus.clinica: Bilateral inferior petrosal sinus venous sampling diagnoses the pituitary origin of Cushing syndrome.

rest|Inferior sagittal sinus.descripcion: Small dural sinus in the inferior free border of the falx cerebri.
rest|Inferior sagittal sinus.origen: Veins of the falx and of the medial surface of the hemispheres.
rest|Inferior sagittal sinus.destino: Joins the great cerebral vein to form the straight sinus.
rest|Inferior sagittal sinus.ramas: Veins of the falx cerebri and medial surfaces of the hemispheres.
rest|Inferior sagittal sinus.territorio: Falx cerebri and medial surfaces of the hemispheres.

rest|Inferior vein of left ventricle.es: Posterior vein of the left ventricle
rest|Inferior vein of left ventricle.descripcion: Cardiac vein on the diaphragmatic surface of the left ventricle.
rest|Inferior vein of left ventricle.origen: Inferior (diaphragmatic) surface of the left ventricle.
rest|Inferior vein of left ventricle.territorio: Inferior surface of the left ventricle.
rest|Inferior vein of left ventricle.clinica: Usual target for the left ventricular lead in resynchronization therapy.

rest|Inferior vein of left ventricle (//.es: Posterior vein of the left ventricle
rest|Inferior vein of left ventricle (//.descripcion: Cardiac vein on the diaphragmatic (posteroinferior) surface of the left ventricle.
rest|Inferior vein of left ventricle (//.origen: Inferior (diaphragmatic) surface of the left ventricle.
rest|Inferior vein of left ventricle (//.territorio: Inferior surface of the left ventricle.
rest|Inferior vein of left ventricle (//.clinica: Usual target for the left ventricular lead in resynchronization therapy.

rest|Inferior vena cava (abdominal part).descripcion: Large retroperitoneal vein to the right of the aorta, from L5 to the caval opening in the diaphragm (T8).
rest|Inferior vena cava (abdominal part).origen: Union of the common iliac veins at the level of L5.
rest|Inferior vena cava (abdominal part).destino: Passes through the diaphragm and continues as the thoracic part to the right atrium.
rest|Inferior vena cava (abdominal part).ramas: Lumbar veins, right gonadal, renal, right suprarenal, inferior phrenic, hepatic veins.
rest|Inferior vena cava (abdominal part).territorio: Lower limbs, pelvis, abdomen and abdominal viscera (via hepatic veins).
rest|Inferior vena cava (abdominal part).clinica: Its compression by the gravid uterus in the supine position causes hypotension (aortocaval compression syndrome).

rest|Inferior vena cava (thoracic part).descripcion: Short segment of the inferior vena cava between the diaphragm and the right atrium, partly intrapericardial.
rest|Inferior vena cava (thoracic part).origen: Continuation of the abdominal part after the caval opening (T8).
rest|Inferior vena cava (thoracic part).destino: Right atrium, in its lower part (valve of the inferior vena cava).
rest|Inferior vena cava (thoracic part).clinica: Access route for catheters and vena cava filters.

rest|Intercapitular veins of foot.descripcion: Communicating veins between the heads of the metatarsals.
rest|Intercapitular veins of foot.destino: Dorsal metatarsal veins and dorsal venous arch.
rest|Intercapitular veins of foot.clinica: They allow plantar blood to pass to the dorsum during gait (plantar pump).

rest|Internal iliac vein.descripcion: Short venous trunk of the posterolateral wall of the pelvis, posteromedial to the internal iliac artery.
rest|Internal iliac vein.origen: Confluence of pelvic veins near the greater sciatic foramen.
rest|Internal iliac vein.destino: Joins the external iliac vein to form the common iliac vein.
rest|Internal iliac vein.ramas: Gluteal veins, obturator, lateral sacral, internal pudendal, middle rectal, vesical, uterine veins; visceral plexuses.
rest|Internal iliac vein.clinica: Severe hemorrhage in pelvic fractures due to injury of the internal iliac venous plexus.

rest|Internal jugular vein.descripcion: Large vein of the neck in the carotid sheath, lateral to the carotid, from the jugular foramen to behind the clavicle.
rest|Internal jugular vein.origen: Continuation of the sigmoid sinus at the jugular foramen (superior bulb).
rest|Internal jugular vein.destino: Joins the subclavian vein to form the brachiocephalic vein.
rest|Internal jugular vein.ramas: Inferior petrosal sinus, facial vein (common), lingual, pharyngeal, superior and middle thyroid veins.
rest|Internal jugular vein.clinica: Common route for central venous access; reflects jugular venous pressure.

rest|Internal pudendal vein.descripcion: Vein accompanying the internal pudendal artery through the pudendal (Alcock's) canal.
rest|Internal pudendal vein.origen: Veins of the perineum, including the deep veins of the penis/clitoris and the inferior rectal veins.
rest|Internal pudendal vein.ramas: Inferior rectal veins, posterior scrotal/labial, deep veins of the penis/clitoris, of the bulb.

rest|Internal thoracic veins.descripcion: Paired veins accompanying the internal thoracic artery behind the costal cartilages.
rest|Internal thoracic veins.origen: Union of the superior epigastric and musculophrenic veins.
rest|Internal thoracic veins.destino: Brachiocephalic vein of the same side.
rest|Internal thoracic veins.ramas: Anterior intercostal veins, perforating, superior epigastric, musculophrenic veins.
rest|Internal thoracic veins.territorio: Anterior chest wall, breast and diaphragm.
rest|Internal thoracic veins.clinica: Recipient vessels in free flaps for breast reconstruction.

rest|Intrarenal veins of left kidney.es: Intrarenal veins of the left kidney
rest|Intrarenal veins of left kidney.descripcion: Venous system within the left kidney: interlobular, arcuate and interlobar veins.
rest|Intrarenal veins of left kidney.origen: Peritubular capillaries and cortical stellate veins.
rest|Intrarenal veins of left kidney.destino: Left renal vein, in the renal sinus.
rest|Intrarenal veins of left kidney.ramas: Interlobular, arcuate, interlobar and straight veins.
rest|Intrarenal veins of left kidney.clinica: Unlike the arteries, they anastomose widely (they are not end vessels).

rest|Intrarenal veins of right kidney.es: Intrarenal veins of the right kidney
rest|Intrarenal veins of right kidney.descripcion: Venous system within the right kidney: interlobular, arcuate and interlobar veins.
rest|Intrarenal veins of right kidney.origen: Peritubular capillaries and cortical stellate veins.
rest|Intrarenal veins of right kidney.destino: Right renal vein, in the renal sinus.
rest|Intrarenal veins of right kidney.ramas: Interlobular, arcuate, interlobar and straight veins.
rest|Intrarenal veins of right kidney.clinica: Unlike the arteries, they anastomose widely (they are not end vessels).

rest|Lateral circumflex femoral veins.descripcion: Veins accompanying the lateral circumflex femoral artery in the proximal thigh.
rest|Lateral circumflex femoral veins.origen: Anterolateral muscles of the thigh and hip.
rest|Lateral circumflex femoral veins.destino: Deep femoral vein or femoral vein.
rest|Lateral circumflex femoral veins.territorio: Quadriceps, tensor fasciae latae and hip.
rest|Lateral circumflex femoral veins.clinica: Pedicle of the anterolateral thigh (ALT) flap.

rest|Lateral plantar veins.descripcion: Deep veins accompanying the lateral plantar artery in the sole of the foot.
rest|Lateral plantar veins.destino: They join the medial plantar veins to form the posterior tibial veins.
rest|Lateral plantar veins.territorio: Sole of the foot, lateral region.

rest|Lateral sacral veins.descripcion: Veins on the pelvic surface of the sacrum, next to the anterior sacral foramina.
rest|Lateral sacral veins.clinica: Their injury in presacral surgery causes bleeding that is difficult to control.

rest|Lateral thoracic vein.descripcion: Vein descending along the lateral wall of the thorax next to the lateral thoracic artery.
rest|Lateral thoracic vein.origen: Lateral thoracic wall; anastomoses with the thoracoepigastric vein.
rest|Lateral thoracic vein.territorio: Serratus anterior, lateral thoracic wall and breast.
rest|Lateral thoracic vein.clinica: Cavo-caval collateral pathway in inferior vena cava obstruction.

rest|Lateral vein of right lung.es: Lateral vein of the right lung
rest|Lateral vein of right lung.descripcion: Tributary of the middle lobe vein draining the lateral segment.
rest|Lateral vein of right lung.destino: Middle lobe vein, tributary of the right superior pulmonary vein.
rest|Lateral vein of right lung.territorio: Lateral segment of the right middle lobe.

rest|Left ascending lumbar vein.descripcion: Left longitudinal vein in front of the lumbar transverse processes, behind the psoas.
rest|Left ascending lumbar vein.destino: Joins the left subcostal vein to form the hemiazygos vein.
rest|Left ascending lumbar vein.territorio: Left posterior abdominal wall and lumbar spine.

rest|Left brachiocephalic vein.descripcion: Long vein crossing obliquely behind the manubrium, in front of the branches of the aortic arch.
rest|Left brachiocephalic vein.origen: Union of the left internal jugular and subclavian veins behind the sternoclavicular joint.
rest|Left brachiocephalic vein.destino: Joins the right brachiocephalic vein to form the superior vena cava.
rest|Left brachiocephalic vein.ramas: Vertebral, internal thoracic, inferior thyroid, left superior intercostal, thymic, pericardiacophrenic veins.
rest|Left brachiocephalic vein.territorio: Left head, neck and upper limb.
rest|Left brachiocephalic vein.clinica: May be injured in sternotomy or tracheostomy in children, in whom it projects above the manubrium.

rest|Left gastro-omental vein.descripcion: Vein running along the greater curvature of the stomach from right to left beside the artery of the same name.
rest|Left gastro-omental vein.origen: Greater curvature of the stomach and greater omentum.
rest|Left gastro-omental vein.territorio: Greater gastric curvature and greater omentum.

rest|Left inferior pulmonary vein.descripcion: Pulmonary vein of the left hilum, the lowest, carrying oxygenated blood to the left atrium.
rest|Left inferior pulmonary vein.origen: Veins of the left lower lobe (superior and common basal).
rest|Left inferior pulmonary vein.ramas: Superior vein, common basal vein (superior and inferior basal).
rest|Left inferior pulmonary vein.territorio: Lower lobe of the left lung.
rest|Left inferior pulmonary vein.clinica: Target of pulmonary vein isolation in atrial fibrillation ablation.

rest|Left renal vein.descripcion: Long vein crossing in front of the aorta, below the origin of the superior mesenteric artery.
rest|Left renal vein.origen: Hilum of the left kidney (intrarenal veins).
rest|Left renal vein.ramas: Left suprarenal vein, left gonadal vein, left inferior phrenic vein, lumbar veins.
rest|Left renal vein.territorio: Left kidney and suprarenal gland, left gonad.
rest|Left renal vein.clinica: Its aortomesenteric compression produces nutcracker syndrome; preferred for kidney donation because of its length.

rest|Left subclavian vein.descripcion: Vein passing over the 1st rib in front of the scalenus anterior.
rest|Left subclavian vein.origen: Continuation of the axillary vein at the lateral border of the 1st rib.
rest|Left subclavian vein.destino: Joins the internal jugular vein to form the left brachiocephalic vein (venous angle, receives the thoracic duct).
rest|Left subclavian vein.ramas: External jugular vein, sometimes dorsal scapular; thoracic duct at the venous angle.
rest|Left subclavian vein.clinica: Central venous access; risk of pneumothorax on puncture.

rest|Left subcostal vein.descripcion: Vein running below the left 12th rib beside the subcostal artery.
rest|Left subcostal vein.destino: Joins the left ascending lumbar vein to form the hemiazygos vein.
rest|Left subcostal vein.territorio: Abdominal wall below the left 12th rib.

rest|Left superior intercostal vein.descripcion: Vein crossing the aortic arch on its left lateral surface, between the phrenic and vagus nerves.
rest|Left superior intercostal vein.ramas: 2nd-3rd posterior intercostal veins, left bronchial veins.
rest|Left superior intercostal vein.clinica: Visible on radiographs as the 'aortic nipple'.

rest|Left superior pulmonary vein.descripcion: Pulmonary vein of the left hilum, anterior and inferior to the pulmonary artery, carrying oxygenated blood.
rest|Left superior pulmonary vein.origen: Veins of the left upper lobe.
rest|Left superior pulmonary vein.territorio: Upper lobe of the left lung, including the lingula.
rest|Left superior pulmonary vein.clinica: Target of pulmonary vein isolation in atrial fibrillation ablation.

rest|Left testicular vein.descripcion: Vein of the spermatic cord ascending through the retroperitoneum to the left kidney.
rest|Left testicular vein.origen: Pampiniform plexus, at the deep inguinal ring.
rest|Left testicular vein.destino: Left renal vein, at a right angle.
rest|Left testicular vein.clinica: Varicocele is much more frequent on the left side because of its right-angle drainage.

rest|Lingual vein.descripcion: Vein draining the tongue; accompanies the lingual artery and the hypoglossal nerve.
rest|Lingual vein.origen: Dorsal lingual veins, deep lingual vein and sublingual vein.
rest|Lingual vein.destino: Internal jugular vein or common facial vein.
rest|Lingual vein.ramas: Dorsal veins of the tongue, deep vein, sublingual vein, vena comitans of the hypoglossal nerve.
rest|Lingual vein.territorio: Tongue and floor of the mouth.
rest|Lingual vein.clinica: The sublingual veins allow rapid absorption of sublingual drugs.

rest|Lingular vein of left lung.es: Lingular vein of the left lung
rest|Lingular vein of left lung.descripcion: Vein of the left upper lobe draining the lingula.
rest|Lingular vein of left lung.origen: Union of the superior and inferior lingular parts.

rest|Lumbar veins.descripcion: Paired segmental veins accompanying the lumbar arteries in the posterior abdominal wall.
rest|Lumbar veins.origen: Posterior abdominal wall and vertebral venous plexuses.
rest|Lumbar veins.destino: Inferior vena cava (3rd and 4th); the upper ones to the ascending lumbar veins.
rest|Lumbar veins.territorio: Lumbar muscles and skin, lumbar spine.
rest|Lumbar veins.clinica: Their injury is a source of bleeding in aortic or anterior lumbar surgery.

rest|Maxillary veins.descripcion: Short veins in the infratemporal fossa accompanying the first part of the maxillary artery.
rest|Maxillary veins.destino: They join the superficial temporal vein to form the retromandibular vein.
rest|Maxillary veins.territorio: Infratemporal fossa, muscles of mastication, maxillae and nasal cavity.

rest|Medial circumflex femoral veins.descripcion: Veins accompanying the medial circumflex femoral artery around the femoral neck.
rest|Medial circumflex femoral veins.origen: Adductor muscles, hip and femoral neck.
rest|Medial circumflex femoral veins.destino: Deep femoral vein or femoral vein.
rest|Medial circumflex femoral veins.clinica: They communicate with the inferior gluteal veins: collateral pathway.

rest|Medial plantar veins.descripcion: Deep veins accompanying the medial plantar artery in the sole of the foot.
rest|Medial plantar veins.origen: Plantar digital veins and medial region of the sole.
rest|Medial plantar veins.destino: They join the lateral plantar veins to form the posterior tibial veins.
rest|Medial plantar veins.territorio: Sole of the foot, medial region.

rest|Medial vein of right lung.es: Medial vein of the right lung
rest|Medial vein of right lung.descripcion: Tributary of the middle lobe vein draining the medial segment.
rest|Medial vein of right lung.destino: Middle lobe vein, tributary of the right superior pulmonary vein.
rest|Medial vein of right lung.territorio: Medial segment of the right middle lobe.

rest|Median antebrachial vein.descripcion: Inconstant superficial vein ascending along the anterior surface of the forearm.
rest|Median antebrachial vein.destino: Basilic vein, cephalic vein or median cubital vein.
rest|Median antebrachial vein.territorio: Palmar surface of the hand and anterior forearm.

rest|Median cubital vein.descripcion: Oblique superficial vein in the cubital fossa, separated from the brachial artery by the bicipital aponeurosis.
rest|Median cubital vein.territorio: Connects the cephalic and basilic systems; receives deep perforators.
rest|Median cubital vein.clinica: Site of choice for venipuncture and blood sampling.

rest|Middle cardiac vein.descripcion: Vein of the posterior interventricular groove accompanying the posterior interventricular artery.
rest|Middle cardiac vein.origen: Near the cardiac apex, on the diaphragmatic surface.
rest|Middle cardiac vein.territorio: Diaphragmatic surface of both ventricles and posterior interventricular septum.
rest|Middle cardiac vein.clinica: Used for resynchronization leads and ablation of accessory pathways.

rest|Middle colic vein.descripcion: Vein of the transverse mesocolon accompanying the middle colic artery.
rest|Middle colic vein.destino: Superior mesenteric vein (sometimes the gastrocolic trunk).

rest|Musculophrenic veins.descripcion: Veins accompanying the musculophrenic artery along the costal margins.
rest|Musculophrenic veins.territorio: Anterior diaphragm and lower chest wall.

rest|Occipital sinus.descripcion: Small dural sinus at the attached border of the falx cerebelli.
rest|Occipital sinus.origen: Venous plexus around the foramen magnum (internal vertebral plexuses).
rest|Occipital sinus.clinica: May be prominent in children; risk of bleeding in suboccipital approaches.

rest|Occipital vein.descripcion: Vein of the occipital scalp accompanying the occipital artery.
rest|Occipital vein.origen: Venous plexus of the occipital scalp.
rest|Occipital vein.destino: Suboccipital venous plexus, internal jugular vein or posterior auricular vein.
rest|Occipital vein.ramas: Mastoid emissary vein (communication with the sigmoid sinus).
rest|Occipital vein.clinica: Route of infection to the dural sinuses via emissary veins.

rest|Palmar digital veins.descripcion: Small veins on the palmar surface of the fingers.
rest|Palmar digital veins.origen: Palmar venous plexuses of the fingers.
rest|Palmar digital veins.destino: Palmar metacarpal veins and intercapitular veins toward the dorsum.

rest|Perforating veins.descripcion: Veins that pierce the deep fascia connecting the superficial venous system with the deep one, with valves that direct flow toward the depth.
rest|Perforating veins.origen: Superficial venous system (saphenous veins and tributaries).
rest|Perforating veins.clinica: Their insufficiency contributes to varicose veins and venous ulcers.

rest|Plantar digital veins.descripcion: Small veins on the plantar surface of the toes.
rest|Plantar digital veins.destino: Plantar metatarsal veins; they communicate with the dorsum through intercapitular veins.

rest|Plantar metatarsal veins.descripcion: Deep veins of the sole accompanying the plantar metatarsal arteries.

rest|Plantar venous arch.descripcion: Deep venous arch of the sole accompanying the plantar arterial arch.
rest|Plantar venous arch.clinica: Its compression on weight-bearing propels blood upward (plantar venous pump).

rest|Popliteal vein.descripcion: Vein of the popliteal fossa located between the popliteal artery (deep) and the tibial nerve (superficial).
rest|Popliteal vein.origen: Union of the anterior and posterior tibial veins at the lower border of the popliteus.
rest|Popliteal vein.destino: Continues as the femoral vein at the adductor hiatus.
rest|Popliteal vein.ramas: Small saphenous vein, genicular veins, sural veins (gastrocnemius, soleal).
rest|Popliteal vein.clinica: Frequent site of deep vein thrombosis; a Baker cyst may compress it.

rest|Posterior auricular vein.descripcion: Vein of the scalp behind the ear.
rest|Posterior auricular vein.origen: Venous plexus of the retroauricular scalp.
rest|Posterior auricular vein.destino: Joins the posterior division of the retromandibular vein to form the external jugular vein.

rest|Posterior circumflex humeral vein.descripcion: Vein accompanying the posterior circumflex humeral artery and the axillary nerve through the quadrangular space.
rest|Posterior circumflex humeral vein.clinica: May be injured in fractures of the surgical neck of the humerus.

rest|Posterior division of retromandibul.es: Posterior division of the retromandibular vein
rest|Posterior division of retromandibul.descripcion: Posterior branch of the retromandibular vein emerging below the parotid.
rest|Posterior division of retromandibul.destino: Joins the posterior auricular vein to form the external jugular vein.

rest|Posterior intercavernous sinus.descripcion: Transverse dural sinus located behind the pituitary gland.
rest|Posterior intercavernous sinus.clinica: Together with the anterior one it forms the circular sinus; relevant in pituitary surgery.

rest|Posterior tibial veins.descripcion: Paired deep veins accompanying the posterior tibial artery behind the medial malleolus.
rest|Posterior tibial veins.origen: Union of the medial and lateral plantar veins.
rest|Posterior tibial veins.destino: They join the anterior tibial veins to form the popliteal vein.
rest|Posterior tibial veins.ramas: Fibular veins, perforating veins of the leg, soleal veins.
rest|Posterior tibial veins.territorio: Posterior compartment of the leg and sole of the foot.
rest|Posterior tibial veins.clinica: Frequent site of distal deep vein thrombosis.

rest|Posterior vein of right lung.es: Posterior vein of the right lung
rest|Posterior vein of right lung.descripcion: Vein of the right upper lobe draining the posterior segment.
rest|Posterior vein of right lung.territorio: Posterior segment of the right upper lobe.

rest|Radial veins.descripcion: Paired deep veins accompanying the radial artery in the forearm.
rest|Radial veins.origen: Deep palmar venous arch and dorsal metacarpal veins.
rest|Radial veins.destino: They join the ulnar veins to form the brachial veins at the elbow.
rest|Radial veins.territorio: Deep lateral region of the forearm and hand.

rest|Retromandibular vein.descripcion: Vein descending within the parotid, deep to the facial nerve, behind the mandibular ramus.
rest|Retromandibular vein.origen: Union of the superficial temporal vein and the maxillary veins in front of the ear.
rest|Retromandibular vein.destino: Divides into an anterior division (to the facial vein) and a posterior division (to the external jugular).
rest|Retromandibular vein.ramas: Superficial temporal, maxillary, transverse facial, parotid veins.
rest|Retromandibular vein.territorio: Temporal region, infratemporal fossa and parotid.
rest|Retromandibular vein.clinica: Landmark in parotidectomy: the facial nerve is superficial to it.

rest|Right ascending lumbar vein.descripcion: Right longitudinal vein in front of the lumbar transverse processes, behind the psoas.
rest|Right ascending lumbar vein.destino: Joins the right subcostal vein to form the azygos vein.
rest|Right ascending lumbar vein.territorio: Right posterior abdominal wall and lumbar spine.

rest|Right brachiocephalic vein.descripcion: Short, almost vertical vein behind the right border of the manubrium.
rest|Right brachiocephalic vein.origen: Union of the right internal jugular and subclavian veins behind the sternoclavicular joint.
rest|Right brachiocephalic vein.destino: Joins the left brachiocephalic vein to form the superior vena cava.
rest|Right brachiocephalic vein.ramas: Vertebral, internal thoracic, inferior thyroid, first right posterior intercostal veins.
rest|Right brachiocephalic vein.territorio: Right head, neck and upper limb.
rest|Right brachiocephalic vein.clinica: Straight course preferred for central venous catheters.

rest|Right colic vein.descripcion: Vein draining the ascending colon behind the peritoneum.
rest|Right colic vein.destino: Superior mesenteric vein (often via the gastrocolic trunk).

rest|Right gastro-omental vein.descripcion: Vein running along the greater gastric curvature from left to right beside the artery of the same name.
rest|Right gastro-omental vein.origen: Greater curvature of the stomach and greater omentum.
rest|Right gastro-omental vein.destino: Superior mesenteric vein (often via the gastrocolic trunk).

rest|Right inferior pulmonary vein.descripcion: Lowest pulmonary vein of the right hilum, in the pulmonary ligament.
rest|Right inferior pulmonary vein.origen: Veins of the right lower lobe (superior and common basal).
rest|Right inferior pulmonary vein.ramas: Superior vein, common basal vein (superior and inferior basal).
rest|Right inferior pulmonary vein.territorio: Lower lobe of the right lung.
rest|Right inferior pulmonary vein.clinica: Target of pulmonary vein isolation in atrial fibrillation ablation.

rest|Right renal vein.descripcion: Short vein running from the right kidney to the inferior vena cava.
rest|Right renal vein.origen: Hilum of the right kidney (intrarenal veins).
rest|Right renal vein.clinica: Its shortness makes living-donor right kidney transplantation difficult.

rest|Right subclavian vein.descripcion: Vein passing over the 1st rib in front of the scalenus anterior.
rest|Right subclavian vein.origen: Continuation of the axillary vein at the lateral border of the 1st rib.
rest|Right subclavian vein.destino: Joins the internal jugular vein to form the right brachiocephalic vein (venous angle, receives the right lymphatic duct).
rest|Right subclavian vein.ramas: External jugular vein, sometimes dorsal scapular.
rest|Right subclavian vein.clinica: Central venous access; risk of pneumothorax on puncture.

rest|Right subcostal vein.descripcion: Vein running below the right 12th rib beside the subcostal artery.
rest|Right subcostal vein.destino: Joins the right ascending lumbar vein to form the azygos vein.
rest|Right subcostal vein.territorio: Abdominal wall below the right 12th rib.

rest|Right superior intercostal vein.descripcion: Venous trunk collecting the right upper intercostal spaces.

rest|Right superior phrenic vein.descripcion: Small vein of the thoracic surface of the right diaphragm.
rest|Right superior phrenic vein.territorio: Posterior portion of the superior surface of the diaphragm.

rest|Right superior pulmonary vein.descripcion: Anterior pulmonary vein of the right hilum, passing behind the superior vena cava.
rest|Right superior pulmonary vein.origen: Veins of the right upper and middle lobes.
rest|Right superior pulmonary vein.ramas: Apical, anterior, posterior and middle lobe veins.
rest|Right superior pulmonary vein.territorio: Upper and middle lobes of the right lung.
rest|Right superior pulmonary vein.clinica: Target of pulmonary vein isolation in atrial fibrillation ablation.

rest|Right testicular vein.descripcion: Vein of the spermatic cord ascending in the retroperitoneum on the right.
rest|Right testicular vein.origen: Pampiniform plexus, at the deep inguinal ring.
rest|Right testicular vein.destino: Inferior vena cava, at an acute angle.
rest|Right testicular vein.clinica: An isolated right varicocele suggests retroperitoneal compression (e.g., tumor).

rest|Sigmoid sinus.descripcion: S-shaped dural sinus in the groove of the mastoid part of the temporal bone.
rest|Sigmoid sinus.destino: Internal jugular vein, at the jugular foramen.
rest|Sigmoid sinus.ramas: Superior petrosal sinus (at its junction), mastoid and condylar emissary veins.
rest|Sigmoid sinus.clinica: Thrombosis from otogenic mastoiditis; landmark in retrosigmoid surgery.

rest|Sigmoid veins.descripcion: Veins of the sigmoid mesocolon accompanying the sigmoid arteries.

rest|Small saphenous vein.descripcion: Superficial vein passing behind the lateral malleolus and ascending along the posterior midline of the leg beside the sural nerve.
rest|Small saphenous vein.origen: Lateral end of the dorsal venous arch of the foot.
rest|Small saphenous vein.destino: Popliteal vein in the popliteal fossa (saphenopopliteal junction).
rest|Small saphenous vein.ramas: Veins of the posterior surface of the leg, intersaphenous vein (of Giacomini).
rest|Small saphenous vein.territorio: Lateral border of the foot and posterior surface of the leg.
rest|Small saphenous vein.clinica: Site of varicose veins; risk of sural nerve injury when treating it.

rest|Splenic vein.descripcion: Vein running behind the pancreas from the splenic hilum.
rest|Splenic vein.origen: Union of several veins at the hilum of the spleen.
rest|Splenic vein.destino: Joins the superior mesenteric vein behind the neck of the pancreas to form the portal vein.
rest|Splenic vein.ramas: Short gastric veins, left gastro-omental, pancreatic, inferior mesenteric veins.
rest|Splenic vein.territorio: Spleen, pancreas and part of the stomach.
rest|Splenic vein.clinica: Its thrombosis (e.g., from pancreatitis) causes segmental portal hypertension with gastric varices.

rest|Straight sinus.descripcion: Dural sinus at the junction of the falx cerebri with the tentorium cerebelli.
rest|Straight sinus.origen: Union of the inferior sagittal sinus and the great cerebral vein (of Galen).
rest|Straight sinus.destino: Confluence of sinuses (usually toward the left transverse sinus).
rest|Straight sinus.ramas: Great cerebral vein, inferior sagittal sinus, superior cerebellar veins.
rest|Straight sinus.territorio: Deep venous system of the brain.
rest|Straight sinus.clinica: Its thrombosis compromises deep drainage (thalami, basal ganglia).

rest|Submental vein.descripcion: Vein accompanying the submental artery under the floor of the mouth.
rest|Submental vein.origen: Chin, lower lip and submandibular gland.

rest|Subscapular vein.descripcion: Vein accompanying the subscapular artery in the posterior wall of the axilla.
rest|Subscapular vein.origen: Union of the circumflex scapular and thoracodorsal veins.
rest|Subscapular vein.territorio: Subscapularis, latissimus dorsi, teres major and scapular muscles.

rest|Superficial dorsal veins of penis.es: Superficial dorsal veins of the penis
rest|Superficial dorsal veins of penis.descripcion: Subcutaneous veins of the dorsum of the penis, superficial to the deep (Buck's) fascia.
rest|Superficial dorsal veins of penis.origen: Foreskin and skin of the penis.
rest|Superficial dorsal veins of penis.destino: Superficial external pudendal veins (toward the great saphenous vein).
rest|Superficial dorsal veins of penis.territorio: Skin and foreskin of the penis.

rest|Superficial epigastric vein.descripcion: Subcutaneous vein of the lower abdominal wall.
rest|Superficial epigastric vein.origen: Infraumbilical subcutaneous tissue; anastomoses with thoracoepigastric and paraumbilical veins.
rest|Superficial epigastric vein.territorio: Skin and subcutaneous tissue of the lower abdominal wall.
rest|Superficial epigastric vein.clinica: It dilates in portal hypertension (caput medusae) and caval obstruction.

rest|Superficial temporal veins.descripcion: Veins of the temporal scalp descending in front of the ear.
rest|Superficial temporal veins.origen: Venous plexus of the temporoparietal scalp.
rest|Superficial temporal veins.destino: They join the maxillary veins to form the retromandibular vein.
rest|Superficial temporal veins.ramas: Parietal, frontal, middle temporal, transverse facial veins.

rest|Superficial venous palmar arch.descripcion: Venous arch accompanying the superficial palmar arterial arch.
rest|Superficial venous palmar arch.destino: Superficial ulnar and radial veins; median antebrachial vein.

rest|Superior basal vein of left lung.es: Superior basal vein of the left lung
rest|Superior basal vein of left lung.descripcion: Vein of the left lower lobe draining the anteromedial and lateral basal segments.
rest|Superior basal vein of left lung.origen: Tributaries from the anterior basal segments.
rest|Superior basal vein of left lung.destino: Common basal vein, tributary of the left inferior pulmonary vein.
rest|Superior basal vein of left lung.territorio: Anterior basal segments of the left lower lobe.

rest|Superior basal vein of right lung.es: Superior basal vein of the right lung
rest|Superior basal vein of right lung.descripcion: Vein of the right lower lobe draining the anterior basal segments.
rest|Superior basal vein of right lung.origen: Tributaries from the anterior basal segments.
