rest|Superior basal vein of right lung.destino: Common basal vein, tributary of the right inferior pulmonary vein.
rest|Superior basal vein of right lung.territorio: Anterior basal segments of the right lower lobe.

rest|Superior epigastric veins.descripcion: Veins accompanying the superior epigastric artery within the rectus sheath.
rest|Superior epigastric veins.origen: Rectus abdominis muscle; anastomosis with the inferior epigastric veins.
rest|Superior epigastric veins.clinica: Cavo-caval collateral pathway in venous obstruction.

rest|Superior gluteal veins.descripcion: Veins accompanying the superior gluteal artery and entering the pelvis above the piriformis.
rest|Superior gluteal veins.territorio: Gluteus medius, minimus and tensor fasciae latae.
rest|Superior gluteal veins.clinica: Risk of bleeding in pelvic fractures and acetabular approaches.

rest|Superior labial vein.origen: Venous plexus of the upper lip.
rest|Superior labial vein.clinica: Part of the facial 'danger triangle' with communication to the cavernous sinus.

rest|Superior lingular vein of left lung.es: Superior lingular vein of the left lung
rest|Superior lingular vein of left lung.descripcion: Tributary of the lingular vein draining the superior lingular segment.
rest|Superior lingular vein of left lung.origen: Tributaries from the superior lingular segment (S4).
rest|Superior lingular vein of left lung.destino: Lingular vein, tributary of the left superior pulmonary vein.

rest|Superior mesenteric vein.descripcion: Vein of the mesentery, to the right of the superior mesenteric artery, crossing in front of the duodenum.
rest|Superior mesenteric vein.origen: Veins of the terminal ileum, cecum and appendix in the right iliac fossa.
rest|Superior mesenteric vein.destino: Joins the splenic vein behind the neck of the pancreas to form the portal vein.
rest|Superior mesenteric vein.ramas: Jejunal, ileal, ileocolic, right colic, middle colic, right gastro-omental, pancreaticoduodenal veins.
rest|Superior mesenteric vein.territorio: Small intestine, right and transverse colon, pancreas.
rest|Superior mesenteric vein.clinica: Its thrombosis causes venous mesenteric ischemia.

rest|Superior ophthalmic vein.descripcion: Main vein of the orbit passing through the superior orbital fissure.
rest|Superior ophthalmic vein.origen: Anastomosis with the angular vein at the medial angle of the eye (supraorbital and supratrochlear veins).
rest|Superior ophthalmic vein.ramas: Ethmoidal, lacrimal, superior vorticose, central retinal, palpebral veins.
rest|Superior ophthalmic vein.territorio: Contents of the orbit and part of the face.
rest|Superior ophthalmic vein.clinica: Its dilation is a sign of carotid-cavernous fistula.

rest|Superior petrosal sinus.descripcion: Dural sinus on the superior border of the petrous part of the temporal bone, at the attachment of the tentorium cerebelli.
rest|Superior petrosal sinus.origen: Posterior part of the cavernous sinus.
rest|Superior petrosal sinus.destino: Junction of the transverse sinus with the sigmoid sinus.
rest|Superior petrosal sinus.ramas: Cerebellar, inferior cerebral, tympanic veins, petrosal vein (of Dandy).

rest|Superior sagittal sinus.descripcion: Unpaired dural sinus on the attached superior border of the falx cerebri, from the foramen cecum to the internal occipital protuberance.
rest|Superior sagittal sinus.origen: Near the foramen cecum (nasal emissary veins).
rest|Superior sagittal sinus.destino: Confluence of sinuses (usually toward the right transverse sinus).
rest|Superior sagittal sinus.ramas: Superior cerebral veins, lateral venous lacunae, parietal emissary veins, diploic veins.
rest|Superior sagittal sinus.territorio: Superolateral and medial surfaces of the brain; reabsorbs CSF through the arachnoid granulations.
rest|Superior sagittal sinus.clinica: Its thrombosis causes intracranial hypertension, seizures and hemorrhagic infarcts.

rest|Superior thyroid vein.descripcion: Vein accompanying the superior thyroid artery from the upper pole of the thyroid.
rest|Superior thyroid vein.origen: Upper pole of the thyroid gland.
rest|Superior thyroid vein.destino: Internal jugular vein (or common facial vein).
rest|Superior thyroid vein.territorio: Upper pole of the thyroid and larynx.
rest|Superior thyroid vein.clinica: Ligated in thyroidectomy together with the superior pedicle.

rest|Superior vein of left lung.es: Superior vein of the left lung
rest|Superior vein of left lung.descripcion: Vein of the left lower lobe draining the superior segment (apical segment of the lower lobe).
rest|Superior vein of left lung.territorio: Superior segment of the left lower lobe.

rest|Superior vein of right lung.es: Superior vein of the right lung
rest|Superior vein of right lung.descripcion: Vein of the right lower lobe draining the superior segment (apical segment of the lower lobe).
rest|Superior vein of right lung.territorio: Superior segment of the right lower lobe.

rest|Superior vena cava.descripcion: Large valveless vein of the superior and middle mediastinum, to the right of the ascending aorta.
rest|Superior vena cava.origen: Union of the right and left brachiocephalic veins behind the right 1st costal cartilage.
rest|Superior vena cava.destino: Right atrium, at the level of the right 3rd costal cartilage.
rest|Superior vena cava.ramas: Brachiocephalic veins, azygos vein, small pericardial and mediastinal veins.
rest|Superior vena cava.territorio: Head, neck, upper limbs and thorax (upper half of the body).
rest|Superior vena cava.clinica: Superior vena cava syndrome due to tumor compression (e.g., lung cancer): facial edema and collateral circulation.

rest|Suprascapular vein.descripcion: Vein accompanying the suprascapular artery over the superior transverse ligament of the scapula.

rest|Thoracodorsal vein.descripcion: Vein accompanying the thoracodorsal artery and nerve over the latissimus dorsi.
rest|Thoracodorsal vein.clinica: Pedicle of the latissimus dorsi flap; landmark in axillary dissection.

rest|Transverse sinus.descripcion: Paired dural sinus on the attached border of the tentorium cerebelli, in the transverse groove of the occipital bone.
rest|Transverse sinus.ramas: Superior petrosal sinus, inferior cerebral veins, cerebellar veins, inferior anastomotic vein (of Labbé).
rest|Transverse sinus.clinica: Its thrombosis or stenosis is associated with idiopathic intracranial hypertension; usual asymmetry (right dominant).

rest|Ulnar veins.descripcion: Paired deep veins accompanying the ulnar artery in the forearm.
rest|Ulnar veins.origen: Deep and superficial palmar venous arches.
rest|Ulnar veins.destino: They join the radial veins to form the brachial veins.
rest|Ulnar veins.territorio: Deep medial region of the forearm and hand.

rest|Vertebral vein.descripcion: Vein descending through the transverse foramina of C1-C6, forming a plexus around the vertebral artery.
rest|Vertebral vein.origen: Suboccipital and internal vertebral venous plexus at the level of the atlas.
rest|Vertebral vein.destino: Brachiocephalic vein, behind the internal jugular.
rest|Vertebral vein.ramas: Internal and external vertebral plexuses, anterior vertebral vein, deep cervical vein.
rest|Vertebral vein.territorio: Cervical spinal cord, deep muscles of the neck.
rest|Vertebral vein.clinica: Communicates with the vertebral plexuses (of Batson), a route of metastasis.

rest|Anterior axillary nodes.la: Nodi lymphoidei axillares anteriores; nodi pectorales
rest|Anterior axillary nodes.descripcion: Axillary group located along the lower border of the pectoralis minor, next to the lateral thoracic vessels.
rest|Anterior axillary nodes.territorio: Most of the breast (lateral quadrants), anterolateral chest wall and supraumbilical abdomen.
rest|Anterior axillary nodes.funcion: Filter the lymph from its territory and generate an immune response.
rest|Anterior axillary nodes.clinica: Frequent first station of breast cancer metastasis; included in Berg level I.

rest|Anterior inferior jugular nodes.descripcion: Small nodes along the anterior jugular vein, in the infrahyoid region of the neck.
rest|Anterior inferior jugular nodes.territorio: Skin and superficial tissues of the infrahyoid anterior cervical region.
rest|Anterior inferior jugular nodes.funcion: Filter the lymph from its territory and generate an immune response.

rest|Anterior tibial node.descripcion: Inconstant node located on the interosseous membrane, next to the proximal part of the anterior tibial vessels.
rest|Anterior tibial node.territorio: Deep structures of the anterior compartment of the leg and dorsum of the foot.
rest|Anterior tibial node.funcion: Filter the lymph from its territory and generate an immune response.

rest|Apical axillary nodes.descripcion: Group at the apex of the axilla, medial to the axillary vein and above the pectoralis minor.
rest|Apical axillary nodes.destino: Subclavian lymphatic trunk (directly or via supraclavicular nodes).
rest|Apical axillary nodes.territorio: Receives lymph from all the other axillary groups, from the upper part of the breast and from the upper limb.
rest|Apical axillary nodes.funcion: Filter the lymph from its territory and generate an immune response.
rest|Apical axillary nodes.clinica: Berg level III; their involvement in breast cancer indicates a worse prognosis.

rest|Appendicular nodes.descripcion: Nodes located in the mesoappendix, next to the appendicular artery.
rest|Appendicular nodes.funcion: Filter the lymph from its territory and generate an immune response.
rest|Appendicular nodes.clinica: They may enlarge in appendicitis and in mesenteric adenitis, which mimics it.

rest|Brachial nodes.la: Nodi lymphoidei axillares laterales; nodi humerales
rest|Brachial nodes.descripcion: Nodes of the lateral wall of the axilla, posteromedial to the axillary vein.
rest|Brachial nodes.destino: Central, apical and supraclavicular axillary nodes.
rest|Brachial nodes.territorio: Almost the entire upper limb, except the territory of the cephalic vein.
rest|Brachial nodes.funcion: Filter the lymph from its territory and generate an immune response.
rest|Brachial nodes.clinica: Their removal in axillary lymphadenectomy predisposes to lymphedema of the upper limb.

rest|Brachiocephalic nodes.descripcion: Anterior mediastinal nodes located along the brachiocephalic veins.
rest|Brachiocephalic nodes.territorio: Thymus, thyroid, anterior pericardium and part of the diaphragm and anterior mediastinum.
rest|Brachiocephalic nodes.funcion: Filter the lymph from its territory and generate an immune response.

rest|Bucinator node.descripcion: Inconstant facial node located on the buccinator muscle, along the facial vein.
rest|Bucinator node.territorio: Cheek, eyelids and lateral nasal region.
rest|Bucinator node.funcion: Filter the lymph from its territory and generate an immune response.

rest|Central axillary nodes.descripcion: Deep group in the central fat of the axillary base, behind the pectoralis minor.
rest|Central axillary nodes.territorio: Lymph from the anterior, posterior and lateral axillary groups.
rest|Central axillary nodes.funcion: Filter the lymph from its territory and generate an immune response.
rest|Central axillary nodes.clinica: They are the most easily palpable on axillary examination.

rest|Central superior mesenteric nodes.descripcion: Nodes located at the root of the mesentery, next to the trunk of the superior mesenteric artery.
rest|Central superior mesenteric nodes.destino: Superior mesenteric nodes at the root and intestinal trunk, toward the cisterna chyli.
rest|Central superior mesenteric nodes.territorio: Jejunum, ileum, cecum, ascending and transverse colon through peripheral nodes.
rest|Central superior mesenteric nodes.funcion: Filter the lymph from its territory and generate an immune response.

rest|Coeliac nodes.descripcion: Preaortic nodes around the origin of the celiac trunk.
rest|Coeliac nodes.territorio: Stomach, proximal duodenum, liver, biliary tract, pancreas and spleen via gastric, hepatic and pancreaticosplenic nodes.
rest|Coeliac nodes.funcion: Filter the lymph from its territory and generate an immune response.
rest|Coeliac nodes.clinica: Their involvement in gastric and pancreatic cancers determines resectability.

rest|Cubital nodes.descripcion: Nodes of the elbow region; includes the superficial supratrochlear and some deep ones next to the brachial artery.
rest|Cubital nodes.territorio: Medial fingers, ulnar side of the hand and forearm.
rest|Cubital nodes.funcion: Filter the lymph from its territory and generate an immune response.

rest|Cystic node.descripcion: Node in the cystohepatic triangle (of Calot), next to the neck of the gallbladder and the cystic artery.
rest|Cystic node.funcion: Filter the lymph from its territory and generate an immune response.
rest|Cystic node.clinica: Surgical landmark in cholecystectomy for identifying the cystic artery.

rest|Deep popliteal nodes.descripcion: Nodes in the popliteal fossa, next to the popliteal vessels and the knee joint.
rest|Deep popliteal nodes.destino: Deep inguinal nodes, through vessels that follow the femoral vein.
rest|Deep popliteal nodes.territorio: Knee, deep structures of the leg and vessels of the small saphenous vein.
rest|Deep popliteal nodes.funcion: Filter the lymph from its territory and generate an immune response.

rest|Fibular node.descripcion: Inconstant node in the proximal part of the leg, next to the fibular vessels.
rest|Fibular node.territorio: Deep structures of the lateral and posterior region of the leg.
rest|Fibular node.funcion: Filter the lymph from its territory and generate an immune response.

rest|Ileocolic nodes.descripcion: Chain along the ileocolic artery; includes prececal, retrocecal and appendicular groups.
rest|Ileocolic nodes.territorio: Terminal ileum, cecum, appendix and proximal ascending colon.
rest|Ileocolic nodes.funcion: Filter the lymph from its territory and generate an immune response.

rest|Inferior deep lateral cervical node.es: Inferior deep lateral cervical lymph nodes
rest|Inferior deep lateral cervical node.la: Nodi lymphoidei cervicales laterales profundi inferiores
rest|Inferior deep lateral cervical node.descripcion: Nodes of the internal jugular chain below the omohyoid; includes the jugulo-omohyoid node.
rest|Inferior deep lateral cervical node.destino: Jugular trunk, thoracic duct or right lymphatic duct.
rest|Inferior deep lateral cervical node.territorio: Lymph from the superior nodes and from the tongue, thyroid, larynx, trachea and lower neck.
rest|Inferior deep lateral cervical node.funcion: Filter the lymph from its territory and generate an immune response.
rest|Inferior deep lateral cervical node.clinica: They correspond to cervical levels III–IV in the oncologic classification.

rest|Inferior diaphragmatic nodes.descripcion: Nodes on the abdominal surface of the diaphragm, next to the inferior phrenic arteries.
rest|Inferior diaphragmatic nodes.territorio: Inferior surface of the diaphragm and posterior part of the right lobe of the liver.
rest|Inferior diaphragmatic nodes.funcion: Filter the lymph from its territory and generate an immune response.

rest|Inferior epigastric nodes.descripcion: Small parietal nodes along the inferior epigastric vessels.
rest|Inferior epigastric nodes.funcion: Filter the lymph from its territory and generate an immune response.

rest|Inferior gluteal nodes.descripcion: Parietal internal iliac nodes next to the inferior gluteal vessels, in the infrapiriform foramen.
rest|Inferior gluteal nodes.territorio: Deep gluteal region, posterior surface of the thigh and part of the prostate and rectum.
rest|Inferior gluteal nodes.funcion: Filter the lymph from its territory and generate an immune response.

rest|Inferior pancreatic nodes.descripcion: Nodes along the inferior border of the body and head of the pancreas.
rest|Inferior pancreatic nodes.destino: Superior mesenteric and lateral aortic nodes.
rest|Inferior pancreatic nodes.funcion: Filter the lymph from its territory and generate an immune response.

rest|Inferior superficial inguinal nodes.descripcion: Vertical group along the termination of the great saphenous vein, in the femoral triangle.
rest|Inferior superficial inguinal nodes.destino: Deep inguinal and external iliac nodes.
rest|Inferior superficial inguinal nodes.territorio: Most of the superficial lower limb, following the great saphenous vein.
rest|Inferior superficial inguinal nodes.funcion: Filter the lymph from its territory and generate an immune response.
rest|Inferior superficial inguinal nodes.clinica: They enlarge with infections or wounds of the foot and leg.

rest|Inferior tracheobronchial nodes.descripcion: Nodes located below the tracheal bifurcation (carina), between the main bronchi.
rest|Inferior tracheobronchial nodes.destino: Superior tracheobronchial and paratracheal nodes, toward the bronchomediastinal trunks.
rest|Inferior tracheobronchial nodes.territorio: Both lungs (lower lobes), bronchi, heart and esophagus.
rest|Inferior tracheobronchial nodes.funcion: Filter the lymph from its territory and generate an immune response.
rest|Inferior tracheobronchial nodes.clinica: Station 7 in lung cancer staging; their enlargement widens the carinal angle.

rest|Infra-auricular nodes.descripcion: Parotid nodes located below the auricle, at the inferior pole of the parotid gland.
rest|Infra-auricular nodes.territorio: Auricle, external acoustic meatus and parotid region.
rest|Infra-auricular nodes.funcion: Filter the lymph of its territory and generate an immune response.

rest|Supratrochlear nodes.clinica: Their enlargement suggests hand infection, secondary syphilis or lymphoma.

rest|Thyroid nodes.descripcion: Deep anterior cervical nodes located next to the thyroid gland.
rest|Thyroid nodes.destino: Pretracheal, paratracheal and deep cervical nodes.
rest|Thyroid nodes.funcion: Filter the lymph of its territory and generate an immune response.

rest|Ampulla of lacrimal canaliculus.descripcion: Dilation of the lacrimal canaliculus at the angle where its vertical portion, beginning at the lacrimal punctum, continues with the horizontal portion.
rest|Ampulla of lacrimal canaliculus.funcion: Part of the drainage of tears from the lacrimal punctum toward the lacrimal sac.
rest|Ampulla of lacrimal canaliculus.clinica: It may be affected in canaliculitis or stenosis of the lacrimal pathway, causing epiphora.

rest|Amygdaloid body.descripcion: Nuclear complex of the medial temporal lobe, anterior to the hippocampus and to the temporal horn of the lateral ventricle, beneath the uncus.
rest|Amygdaloid body.territorio: Anterior choroidal artery and branches of the middle cerebral artery
rest|Amygdaloid body.funcion: Emotional processing, especially fear and aggression; emotional memory and associated autonomic and endocrine responses.
rest|Amygdaloid body.clinica: Bilateral lesion produces Klüver-Bucy syndrome (hyperorality, hypersexuality, loss of fear).

rest|Angular gyrus.descripcion: Gyrus of the inferior parietal lobule that curves around the posterior end of the superior temporal sulcus; Brodmann area 39.
rest|Angular gyrus.funcion: Multimodal integration of language: reading, writing, calculation and right-left orientation.
rest|Angular gyrus.clinica: Its lesion in the dominant hemisphere produces Gerstmann syndrome and alexia with agraphia.

rest|Anterior chamber of eyeball.descripcion: Space between the posterior surface of the cornea and the anterior surface of the iris, filled with aqueous humor; it communicates with the posterior chamber through the pupil.
rest|Anterior chamber of eyeball.funcion: Contains aqueous humor, which nourishes the cornea and lens; the iridocorneal angle drains the aqueous humor.
rest|Anterior chamber of eyeball.clinica: A narrow angle predisposes to acute angle-closure glaucoma; hyphema is blood in this chamber.

rest|Anterior cochlear nucleus.descripcion: Sensory nucleus of the medulla oblongata located ventrolaterally on the inferior cerebellar peduncle, at the bulbopontine junction.
rest|Anterior cochlear nucleus.funcion: Receives fibers from the cochlear nerve and projects bilaterally to the superior olivary complex for sound localization.
rest|Anterior cochlear nucleus.clinica: Its lesion causes ipsilateral sensorineural hearing loss.

rest|Anterior commissure.descripcion: Bundle of transverse fibers in the lamina terminalis, in front of the columns of the fornix, crossing the midline.
rest|Anterior commissure.origen: Olfactory bulb and tract, anterior temporal lobe and amygdala of one hemisphere
rest|Anterior commissure.destino: Homologous structures of the contralateral hemisphere
rest|Anterior commissure.territorio: Branches of the anterior cerebral artery and anterior choroidal artery
rest|Anterior commissure.funcion: Interconnects olfactory and temporal regions of both hemispheres.
rest|Anterior commissure.clinica: Radiological landmark: the anterior commissure-posterior commissure (AC-PC) line is used in stereotaxy.

rest|Anterior corticospinal tract.descripcion: Uncrossed descending fasciculus in the anterior funiculus of the spinal cord, next to the anterior median fissure; it reaches the thoracic spinal cord.
rest|Anterior corticospinal tract.destino: Interneurons and motor neurons of the anterior horn, after crossing in the white commissure
rest|Anterior corticospinal tract.funcion: Voluntary motor control of axial and proximal musculature.
rest|Anterior corticospinal tract.clinica: Its isolated lesion gives little weakness; it is affected together with the lateral tract in anterior spinal artery syndrome.

rest|Anterior fasciculus proprius.descripcion: Intersegmental fibers surrounding the gray matter in the anterior funiculus of the spinal cord.
rest|Anterior fasciculus proprius.origen: Neurons of the spinal gray matter
rest|Anterior fasciculus proprius.destino: Other spinal segments, ascending and descending
rest|Anterior fasciculus proprius.funcion: Intersegmental connections for spinal reflexes and coordination between segments.

rest|Anterior horn of spinal cord.es: Anterior horn of the spinal cord
rest|Anterior horn of spinal cord.descripcion: Ventral projection of the spinal gray matter (Rexed laminae VIII-IX), containing alpha and gamma motor neurons.
rest|Anterior horn of spinal cord.funcion: Origin of the somatic motor fibers of the anterior roots that innervate skeletal muscle.
rest|Anterior horn of spinal cord.clinica: Its lesion (poliomyelitis, ALS) causes flaccid paralysis, atrophy, fasciculations and hyporeflexia.

rest|Anterior occipital sulcus.descripcion: Inconstant vertical sulcus on the lateral surface, at the boundary between the occipital and temporal lobes.
rest|Anterior occipital sulcus.territorio: Middle cerebral artery and posterior cerebral artery
rest|Anterior occipital sulcus.funcion: Landmark of the temporo-occipital boundary; close to the visual motion area (V5/MT).

rest|Anterior quadrangular lobule.descripcion: Hemispheric part of the anterior lobe of the cerebellum, lateral to the culmen, between the ala of the central lobule and the primary fissure.
rest|Anterior quadrangular lobule.funcion: Belongs to the spinocerebellum; regulates tone and coordination of the ipsilateral limbs.
rest|Anterior quadrangular lobule.clinica: Its atrophy (e.g. alcoholic) produces gait ataxia and ataxia of the lower limbs.

rest|Anterior segment of eyeball.descripcion: Portion of the eye anterior to the lens: cornea, iris, ciliary body, anterior and posterior chambers and aqueous humor.
rest|Anterior segment of eyeball.territorio: Anterior ciliary arteries and long posterior ciliary arteries
rest|Anterior segment of eyeball.funcion: Refraction of light, regulation of the entry of light and production and drainage of aqueous humor.
rest|Anterior segment of eyeball.clinica: Site of glaucoma, anterior uveitis and cataracts; examined with a slit lamp.

rest|Anterior spinocerebellar tract.descripcion: Ascending fasciculus at the periphery of the lateral funiculus of the spinal cord, anterior to the posterior spinocerebellar tract.
rest|Anterior spinocerebellar tract.origen: Neurons of the border of the posterior and intermediate horn of the lumbosacral spinal cord (spinal border cells)
rest|Anterior spinocerebellar tract.destino: Cortex of the vermis and paravermis of the anterior lobe, via the superior cerebellar peduncle, after a double crossing
rest|Anterior spinocerebellar tract.territorio: Anterior spinal artery and vasocorona arteries
rest|Anterior spinocerebellar tract.funcion: Informs the cerebellum of the activity of the spinal circuits of the lower limb.
rest|Anterior spinocerebellar tract.clinica: Affected in Friedreich ataxia, with gait ataxia.

rest|Anterior spinothalamic tract.descripcion: Ascending fasciculus of the anterior funiculus of the spinal cord, part of the anterolateral system.
rest|Anterior spinothalamic tract.origen: Neurons of the contralateral posterior horn; they cross in the anterior white commissure
rest|Anterior spinothalamic tract.destino: Ventral posterolateral nucleus of the thalamus
rest|Anterior spinothalamic tract.clinica: Its lesion barely reduces touch because of redundancy with the posterior funiculus.

rest|Aqueduct of midbrain.descripcion: Narrow channel of the midbrain, between the tectum and the tegmentum, joining the third and fourth ventricles; surrounded by periaqueductal gray matter.
rest|Aqueduct of midbrain.funcion: Conveys cerebrospinal fluid from the third to the fourth ventricle.
rest|Aqueduct of midbrain.clinica: Its stenosis causes obstructive hydrocephalus with dilation of the lateral and third ventricles.

rest|Auditory tube.descripcion: Osteocartilaginous duct that connects the anterior wall of the tympanic cavity with the nasopharynx.
rest|Auditory tube.territorio: Ascending pharyngeal artery and middle meningeal artery
rest|Auditory tube.funcion: Equalizes middle ear pressure with atmospheric pressure and drains secretions; it opens on swallowing (tensor veli palatini).
rest|Auditory tube.clinica: Its dysfunction or obstruction favors serous otitis media, more frequent in children because the tube is more horizontal.

rest|Base of peduncle.descripcion: Ventral portion of the cerebral peduncle of the midbrain, anterior to the substantia nigra; it contains corticofugal fibers.
rest|Base of peduncle.destino: Brainstem (pontine nuclei, cranial motor nuclei) and spinal cord
rest|Base of peduncle.territorio: Posterior cerebral and anterior choroidal arteries (paramedian branches)
rest|Base of peduncle.funcion: Contains the corticospinal, corticonuclear and corticopontine tracts.
rest|Base of peduncle.clinica: Its lesion with cranial nerve III produces Weber syndrome: ipsilateral ophthalmoplegia and contralateral hemiplegia.

rest|Biventral lobule.descripcion: Lobule of the inferior surface of the cerebellar hemisphere, lateral to the pyramis of the vermis and anterior to the inferior semilunar lobule.
rest|Biventral lobule.funcion: Participates in the motor coordination of the ipsilateral limbs (posterior spinocerebellum).

rest|Calcarine sulcus.descripcion: Deep sulcus on the medial surface of the occipital lobe, from the occipital pole to its junction with the parieto-occipital sulcus; it separates the cuneus and the lingual gyrus.
rest|Calcarine sulcus.funcion: Its banks house the primary visual cortex (area 17).
rest|Calcarine sulcus.clinica: Its lesion produces contralateral homonymous hemianopia, often with macular sparing.

rest|Cauda equina.descripcion: Bundle of lumbar, sacral and coccygeal nerve roots descending in the dural sac below the conus medullaris (L1-L2).
rest|Cauda equina.origen: Lumbar, sacral and coccygeal spinal cord segments
rest|Cauda equina.funcion: Motor and sensory innervation of the lower limbs, perineum, bladder and rectum.
rest|Cauda equina.clinica: Cauda equina syndrome gives saddle anesthesia, urinary retention and flaccid paraparesis: a surgical emergency.

rest|Caudate nucleus.descripcion: C-shaped basal nucleus with head, body and tail, bordering the lateral ventricle; together with the putamen it forms the striatum.
rest|Caudate nucleus.territorio: Recurrent artery of Heubner, lenticulostriate arteries and anterior choroidal artery
rest|Caudate nucleus.funcion: Motor control, habit learning and cognitive and motivational functions of the basal ganglia circuit.
rest|Caudate nucleus.clinica: It atrophies in Huntington disease, with dilation of the frontal horns and chorea.

rest|Central canal.es: Central canal of the spinal cord
rest|Central canal.descripcion: Narrow duct lined by ependyma in the center of the spinal gray matter, continuation of the fourth ventricle.
rest|Central canal.funcion: Contains cerebrospinal fluid; it is often obliterated in the adult.
rest|Central canal.clinica: Its dilation (syringomyelia) produces suspended, cape-like thermoalgesic anesthesia.

rest|Central canal'.descripcion: Variant/segment of the central canal, in the lower half of the medulla oblongata, which opens into the fourth ventricle at the level of the obex.
rest|Central canal'.funcion: Communicates the ventricular system with the spinal central canal; contains cerebrospinal fluid.
rest|Central canal'.clinica: Its cavitary extension into the medulla is called syringobulbia.

rest|Central lobule.descripcion: Segment of the vermis of the anterior lobe of the cerebellum, between the lingula and the culmen; it continues laterally with its alae.
rest|Central lobule.funcion: Belongs to the spinocerebellum; regulates tone, posture and gait.
rest|Central lobule.clinica: Its (alcoholic) degeneration produces gait and truncal ataxia.

rest|Central sulcus.descripcion: Sulcus of the lateral surface that separates the frontal lobe from the parietal lobe, between the precentral and postcentral gyri.
rest|Central sulcus.territorio: Middle cerebral artery (rolandic branch) and anterior cerebral artery at its medial end
rest|Central sulcus.funcion: Separates the primary motor cortex from the primary somatosensory cortex.
rest|Central sulcus.clinica: Key neurosurgical landmark; identified on MRI by the 'hand' (omega) sign.

rest|Cingulate gyrus (Posteroventral par.descripcion: Posterior and inferior part of the cingulate gyrus, retrosplenial, which continues through the isthmus with the parahippocampal gyrus.
rest|Cingulate gyrus (Posteroventral par.territorio: Posterior cerebral artery (parieto-occipital and splenial branch)
rest|Cingulate gyrus (Posteroventral par.funcion: Part of the limbic system; episodic memory, spatial orientation and self-reference.
rest|Cingulate gyrus (Posteroventral par.clinica: Its retrosplenial lesion causes amnesia and topographic disorientation.

rest|Cingulate gyrus and sulcus (Middle.es: Cingulate gyrus and sulcus (middle anterior part)
rest|Cingulate gyrus and sulcus (Middle.la: Gyrus et sulcus cinguli, pars media anterior
rest|Cingulate gyrus and sulcus (Middle.descripcion: Middle-anterior segment of the cingulate gyrus and its sulcus, on the medial surface of the hemisphere above the corpus callosum.
rest|Cingulate gyrus and sulcus (Middle.funcion: Middle cingulate cortex: motor control, response selection, conflict detection and pain.
rest|Cingulate gyrus and sulcus (Middle.clinica: Its bilateral lesion may cause akinetic mutism or abulia.

rest|Cingulate gyrus and sulcus (Middle.es: Cingulate gyrus and sulcus (middle posterior part)
rest|Cingulate gyrus and sulcus (Middle.la: Gyrus et sulcus cinguli, pars media posterior
rest|Cingulate gyrus and sulcus (Middle.descripcion: Middle-posterior segment of the cingulate gyrus and its sulcus, above the body of the corpus callosum.
rest|Cingulate gyrus and sulcus (Middle.funcion: Sensorimotor integration, body orientation and pain processing.

rest|Cingulate gyrus and sulcus (Posteri.es: Cingulate gyrus and sulcus (posterior dorsal part)
rest|Cingulate gyrus and sulcus (Posteri.la: Gyrus et sulcus cinguli, pars posterior dorsalis
rest|Cingulate gyrus and sulcus (Posteri.descripcion: Dorsal portion of the posterior cingulate, above the splenium of the corpus callosum, below the precuneus.
rest|Cingulate gyrus and sulcus (Posteri.territorio: Anterior cerebral artery and branches of the posterior cerebral artery
rest|Cingulate gyrus and sulcus (Posteri.funcion: Node of the default mode network: autobiographical memory and spatial evaluation.

rest|Cingulate sulcus (Marginal part).descripcion: Ascending branch of the posterior end of the cingulate sulcus that reaches the superior border of the hemisphere behind the paracentral lobule.
rest|Cingulate sulcus (Marginal part).funcion: Limits the paracentral lobule from the precuneus; helps to locate the central sulcus on axial slices.
rest|Cingulate sulcus (Marginal part).clinica: MRI landmark ('pars marginalis' sign) to identify the central sulcus.

rest|Circular sulcus of insula.descripcion: Sulcus that surrounds the insula, separating it from the frontal, parietal and temporal opercula.
rest|Circular sulcus of insula.clinica: Landmark in insular glioma surgery and in the identification of M2 branches.

rest|Cochlea.descripcion: Anterior portion of the bony labyrinth of the inner ear, a spiral of about 2.5 turns around the modiolus; it contains the cochlear duct and the organ of Corti.
rest|Cochlea.territorio: Labyrinthine artery (branch of the anterior inferior cerebellar artery)
rest|Cochlea.funcion: Transduction of sound vibrations into nerve impulses with tonotopic organization.
rest|Cochlea.clinica: Its lesion produces sensorineural hearing loss; ototoxic drugs and noise damage the outer hair cells.

rest|Collateral sulcus.descripcion: Longitudinal sulcus of the inferior surface of the hemisphere, between the lateral occipitotemporal gyrus and the parahippocampal and lingual gyri.
rest|Collateral sulcus.funcion: Separates the parahippocampal limbic cortex from the temporal association cortex; it bulges into the ventricle (collateral eminence).
rest|Collateral sulcus.clinica: Its banks house the entorhinal and perirhinal cortex, affected early in Alzheimer disease.

rest|Cornea.descripcion: Transparent, avascular anterior portion of the fibrous tunic of the eye, continuous with the sclera at the limbus.
rest|Cornea.territorio: Avascular; nourished by aqueous humor, tears and limbal loops (anterior ciliary)
rest|Cornea.funcion: Main refractive medium of the eye (about 43 diopters) and protection; very sensitive (ophthalmic nerve).
rest|Cornea.clinica: The corneal reflex tests V1 (afferent) and VII (efferent).

rest|Corpus callosum.descripcion: Large interhemispheric commissure at the bottom of the longitudinal fissure: rostrum, genu, trunk and isthmus, and splenium.
rest|Corpus callosum.destino: Homologous cortex of the contralateral hemisphere
rest|Corpus callosum.territorio: Anterior cerebral artery (pericallosal); splenium by the posterior cerebral artery
rest|Corpus callosum.funcion: Integrates and exchanges information between both hemispheres.
rest|Corpus callosum.clinica: Its section produces a disconnection syndrome (e.g. tactile anomia of the left hand).

rest|Culmen.descripcion: Highest segment of the vermis of the anterior lobe of the cerebellum, between the central lobule and the primary fissure.
rest|Culmen.funcion: Spinocerebellum: control of tone, posture and gait.
rest|Culmen.clinica: Its atrophy in alcoholism produces gait ataxia.

rest|Cuneate fasciculus.descripcion: Lateral part of the posterior funiculus of the spinal cord, present above T6, lateral to the gracile fasciculus.
rest|Cuneate fasciculus.origen: Dorsal root ganglion neurons of the upper limb and upper trunk (ipsilateral)
rest|Cuneate fasciculus.destino: Cuneate nucleus of the medulla oblongata
rest|Cuneate fasciculus.funcion: Conveys fine touch, vibration and conscious proprioception of the upper limb and upper trunk.
rest|Cuneate fasciculus.clinica: Its lesion gives ipsilateral loss of proprioception and vibration of the upper limb.

rest|Cuneus.descripcion: Triangular area of the medial surface of the occipital lobe, between the calcarine and parieto-occipital sulci.
rest|Cuneus.funcion: Contains primary visual cortex (upper lip) and association cortex; processes the contralateral inferior visual field.
rest|Cuneus.clinica: Its lesion causes contralateral inferior homonymous quadrantanopia.

rest|Declive.descripcion: Segment of the vermis of the posterior lobe of the cerebellum, immediately behind the primary fissure.
rest|Declive.funcion: Together with the folium, control of saccadic eye movements and pursuit.

rest|Falx cerebri.descripcion: Sickle-shaped fold of dura mater in the longitudinal fissure, from the crista galli to the tentorium cerebelli; it contains the superior and inferior sagittal sinuses.
rest|Falx cerebri.funcion: Separates and stabilizes the cerebral hemispheres.
rest|Falx cerebri.clinica: Beneath its free edge subfalcine herniation occurs, which may compress the anterior cerebral artery.

rest|Flocculus.descripcion: Small lobule of the anteroinferior surface of the cerebellar hemisphere, next to the middle cerebellar peduncle; with the nodulus it forms the flocculonodular lobe.
rest|Flocculus.funcion: Vestibulocerebellum: balance, vestibulo-ocular reflex and smooth ocular pursuit.
rest|Flocculus.clinica: Its lesion causes nystagmus (gaze-evoked, downbeat) and impaired pursuit.

rest|Folium of vermis.descripcion: Small lamina of the posterior vermis between the declive and the tuber, in the horizontal fissure.
rest|Folium of vermis.funcion: Control of saccadic eye movements (oculomotor vermis).

rest|Fornix.descripcion: Arched bundle beneath the corpus callosum with crura, body and columns; main efferent pathway of the hippocampus.
rest|Fornix.destino: Mammillary bodies, septal nuclei and anterior thalamus
rest|Fornix.territorio: Pericallosal, choroidal and anterior communicating arteries (subcallosal)
rest|Fornix.funcion: Component of the Papez circuit; essential for episodic memory.
rest|Fornix.clinica: Its bilateral lesion (e.g. colloid cyst resection) causes anterograde amnesia.

rest|Fourth ventricle.descripcion: Rhomboid cavity between the pons and medulla (floor) and the cerebellum (roof); it communicates with the aqueduct, the central canal and the subarachnoid space.
rest|Fourth ventricle.territorio: Choroid plexus supplied by the posterior inferior cerebellar artery
rest|Fourth ventricle.funcion: Contains CSF, which exits to the subarachnoid space through the median (Magendie) and lateral (Luschka) apertures.
rest|Fourth ventricle.clinica: Posterior fossa tumors (medulloblastoma, ependymoma) obstruct it, causing hydrocephalus.

rest|Globus pallidus.descripcion: Basal nucleus medial to the putamen, with external and internal segments separated by a medullary lamina; with the putamen it forms the lentiform nucleus.
rest|Globus pallidus.territorio: Anterior choroidal artery and lenticulostriate arteries
rest|Globus pallidus.funcion: Main output of the basal ganglia (internal segment) to the thalamus; modulates movement.
rest|Globus pallidus.clinica: Target of deep brain stimulation in dystonia and Parkinson disease; injured in carbon monoxide poisoning.

rest|Gracile fasciculus.descripcion: Medial part of the posterior funiculus of the spinal cord, present along its entire length, next to the posterior median sulcus.
rest|Gracile fasciculus.origen: Dorsal root ganglion neurons of the lower limb and lower trunk (below T6, ipsilateral)
rest|Gracile fasciculus.destino: Gracile nucleus of the medulla oblongata
rest|Gracile fasciculus.funcion: Conveys fine touch, vibration and conscious proprioception of the lower limb and lower trunk.
rest|Gracile fasciculus.clinica: Its lesion (tabes dorsalis, B12 deficiency) gives sensory ataxia with a positive Romberg sign.

rest|Gracile lobule.descripcion: Narrow lobule of the inferior surface of the cerebellar hemisphere, between the inferior semilunar lobule and the biventral lobule; lateral part of the tuber.
rest|Gracile lobule.funcion: Belongs to the cerebrocerebellum; coordination and planning of movements.

rest|Habenula.descripcion: Small eminence of the epithalamus in the posterior part of the roof of the third ventricle, next to the pineal gland; it contains the habenular nuclei.
rest|Habenula.funcion: Relates the limbic system and midbrain (via the fasciculus retroflexus); regulates reward, aversion and behavior.
rest|Habenula.clinica: Its calcification is a frequent radiological finding; implicated in depression.

rest|Hippocampal commissure.descripcion: Lamina of transverse fibers between the crura of the fornix, beneath the splenium of the corpus callosum.
rest|Hippocampal commissure.territorio: Pericallosal artery and posterior choroidal arteries
rest|Hippocampal commissure.clinica: Route of bilateral spread of temporal epileptic seizures.

rest|Hippocampus.descripcion: Curved eminence of archicortex in the floor of the temporal horn of the lateral ventricle, in the medial temporal lobe.
rest|Hippocampus.territorio: Posterior cerebral artery (hippocampal branches) and anterior choroidal artery
rest|Hippocampus.funcion: Consolidation of declarative memory and spatial navigation.
rest|Hippocampus.clinica: Its bilateral lesion causes anterograde amnesia; mesial temporal sclerosis is a cause of epilepsy; it atrophies early in Alzheimer disease.

rest|Hypothalamus.descripcion: Ventral part of the diencephalon below the hypothalamic sulcus, forming the floor and inferior walls of the third ventricle; includes the optic chiasm, tuber cinereum and mammillary bodies.
rest|Hypothalamus.territorio: Branches of the circle of Willis (communicating, anterior and posterior cerebral)
rest|Hypothalamus.funcion: Control of homeostasis: autonomic system, pituitary gland, temperature, thirst, hunger, circadian rhythms and behavior.
rest|Hypothalamus.clinica: Its injury causes diabetes insipidus, thermal disturbances, obesity or sleep disorders.

rest|Inferior colliculus.descripcion: Caudal eminence of the midbrain tectum, below the superior colliculus; joined to the medial geniculate body by its brachium.
rest|Inferior colliculus.funcion: Obligatory auditory relay: receives the lateral lemniscus and projects to the medial geniculate; integrates sound localization.
rest|Inferior colliculus.clinica: Its unilateral lesion produces little hearing loss because of the bilaterality of the auditory pathway.

rest|Inferior frontal sulcus.descripcion: Longitudinal sulcus on the lateral surface of the frontal lobe, between the middle and inferior frontal gyri.
rest|Inferior frontal sulcus.funcion: Superiorly bounds the inferior frontal gyrus (Broca's area in the dominant hemisphere).

rest|Inferior occipital gyrus and sulcus.descripcion: Gyrus of the inferolateral part of the occipital lobe and its sulcus, next to the inferior border of the hemisphere.
rest|Inferior occipital gyrus and sulcus.territorio: Posterior cerebral and middle cerebral artery
rest|Inferior occipital gyrus and sulcus.funcion: Visual association cortex; early processing of shapes and faces.
rest|Inferior occipital gyrus and sulcus.clinica: Its lesion may contribute to prosopagnosia.

rest|Inferior salivatory nucleus.descripcion: Preganglionic parasympathetic nucleus of the rostral medulla oblongata, associated with the glossopharyngeal nerve.
rest|Inferior salivatory nucleus.destino: Otic ganglion (via tympanic nerve and lesser petrosal nerve)
rest|Inferior salivatory nucleus.territorio: Vertebral and posterior inferior cerebellar artery
rest|Inferior salivatory nucleus.funcion: Secretomotor innervation of the parotid gland.
rest|Inferior salivatory nucleus.clinica: Its pathway explains Frey syndrome (gustatory sweating) after parotidectomy.

rest|Inferior semilunar lobule.la: Lobulus semilunaris inferior (H VII A, crus II)
rest|Inferior semilunar lobule.descripcion: Lobule of the inferior surface of the cerebellar hemisphere, below the horizontal fissure; lateral to the tuber of the vermis.
rest|Inferior semilunar lobule.funcion: Cerebrocerebellum: planning and coordination of fine movements and cognitive functions.
rest|Inferior semilunar lobule.clinica: Its lesion produces ipsilateral dysmetria and dysdiadochokinesia.

rest|Inferior temporal gyrus.descripcion: Gyrus of the inferolateral border of the temporal lobe, below the inferior temporal sulcus.
rest|Inferior temporal gyrus.territorio: Middle cerebral and posterior cerebral artery (temporal branches)
rest|Inferior temporal gyrus.funcion: Associative visual cortex of the ventral pathway: recognition of objects and shapes.
rest|Inferior temporal gyrus.clinica: Its lesion causes visual object agnosia.

rest|Inferior temporal sulcus.descripcion: Discontinuous longitudinal sulcus on the lateral surface of the temporal lobe, between the middle and inferior temporal gyri.
rest|Inferior temporal sulcus.funcion: Delimits the middle and inferior temporal gyri.

rest|Insula (Subcentral gyrus and ant. a.es: Subcentral gyrus and anterior and posterior subcentral sulci
rest|Insula (Subcentral gyrus and ant. a.la: Gyrus subcentralis; sulci subcentrales anterior et posterior
rest|Insula (Subcentral gyrus and ant. a.descripcion: Opercular gyrus joining the inferior ends of the precentral and postcentral gyri over the insula, bounded by subcentral sulci.
rest|Insula (Subcentral gyrus and ant. a.funcion: Sensorimotor representation of the face, tongue and larynx; participates in speech articulation and taste.
rest|Insula (Subcentral gyrus and ant. a.clinica: Its lesion may cause dysarthria and contralateral oral sensory disturbance.

rest|Intermediolateral nucleus.descripcion: Cell column of the lateral horn of the spinal cord from T1 to L2 (and S2-S4 for the sacral parasympathetic nucleus).
rest|Intermediolateral nucleus.destino: Paravertebral and prevertebral sympathetic ganglia and adrenal medulla (via anterior root and white rami communicantes)
rest|Intermediolateral nucleus.funcion: Origin of the preganglionic sympathetic outflow.
rest|Intermediolateral nucleus.clinica: Its disconnection in high spinal cord injuries produces autonomic dysreflexia; T1 involvement causes Horner syndrome.

rest|Intermediomedial nucleus.descripcion: Neuronal group of the medial intermediate zone of the spinal gray matter (lamina VII), present throughout the spinal cord.
rest|Intermediomedial nucleus.funcion: Receives visceral afferents and participates in autonomic reflexes.

rest|Interpeduncular fossa.descripcion: Depression on the ventral surface of the midbrain between the cerebral peduncles; its floor is the posterior perforated substance; the III cranial nerve emerges here.
rest|Interpeduncular fossa.territorio: Perforating arteries of the posterior cerebral and basilar arteries
rest|Interpeduncular fossa.funcion: Passage of perforating vessels to the midbrain and diencephalon; contains the interpeduncular cistern.
rest|Interpeduncular fossa.clinica: Site of basilar tip aneurysms and of oculomotor nerve compression.

rest|Intraparietal sulcus.descripcion: Horizontal sulcus of the parietal lobe separating the superior and inferior parietal lobules.
rest|Intraparietal sulcus.funcion: Its walls integrate vision and movement: spatial attention, saccades and manual reaching.
rest|Intraparietal sulcus.clinica: Its lesion contributes to spatial neglect and optic ataxia.

rest|Iris.descripcion: Pigmented diaphragm of the vascular tunic, between the cornea and lens, with a central opening (pupil).
rest|Iris.territorio: Long posterior ciliary and anterior ciliary arteries (major arterial circle of the iris)
rest|Iris.funcion: Regulates the amount of light entering the eye by means of the sphincter (parasympathetic) and dilator (sympathetic) muscles of the pupil.
rest|Iris.clinica: Non-reactive mydriasis suggests compression of the III cranial nerve; miosis in Horner syndrome.

rest|Lacrimal canaliculus.descripcion: Fine duct (superior and inferior) running from the lacrimal punctum of each eyelid to the lacrimal sac.
rest|Lacrimal canaliculus.funcion: Drains tears from the lacrimal lake to the lacrimal sac.
rest|Lacrimal canaliculus.clinica: Its transection in medial eyelid lacerations requires repair with intubation to avoid epiphora.

rest|Lacrimal gland.descripcion: Serous gland in the lacrimal fossa of the superolateral angle of the orbit, divided by the aponeurosis of the levator into orbital and palpebral portions.
rest|Lacrimal gland.funcion: Secretes tears; parasympathetic secretory innervation from the superior salivatory nucleus via the pterygopalatine ganglion.
rest|Lacrimal gland.clinica: Lesions of the VII cranial nerve proximal to the geniculate ganglion produce dry eye.

rest|Lacrimal sac.descripcion: Dilated upper end of the nasolacrimal duct, in the fossa of the lacrimal sac on the medial wall of the orbit.
rest|Lacrimal sac.funcion: Receives tears from the canaliculi and conducts them to the inferior nasal meatus.
rest|Lacrimal sac.clinica: Its distal obstruction produces dacryocystitis with swelling at the medial angle of the eye.

rest|Lat_Fis-ant-Horizont.es: Anterior horizontal ramus of the lateral sulcus
rest|Lat_Fis-ant-Horizont.descripcion: Short ramus directed forward from the lateral sulcus, separating the orbital part from the triangular part of the inferior frontal gyrus.

rest|Lat_Fis-ant-Vertical.es: Ascending ramus of the lateral sulcus
rest|Lat_Fis-ant-Vertical.descripcion: Ramus ascending from the lateral sulcus, separating the triangular part from the opercular part of the inferior frontal gyrus.
rest|Lat_Fis-ant-Vertical.funcion: Landmark for delimiting Broca's area (triangular and opercular parts).

rest|Lat_Fis-post.es: Posterior ramus of the lateral sulcus
rest|Lat_Fis-post.descripcion: Long ramus of the lateral sulcus (Sylvian fissure) that separates the temporal lobe from the frontal and parietal lobes and ends by ascending into the supramarginal gyrus.
rest|Lat_Fis-post.funcion: Its lower lip contains the auditory cortex (transverse temporal gyri) and its end, Wernicke's area.
rest|Lat_Fis-post.clinica: Perisylvian lesions of the dominant hemisphere produce aphasia.

rest|Lateral corticospinal tract.descripcion: Main descending motor pathway, located in the lateral funiculus of the spinal cord after crossing in the pyramidal decussation.
rest|Lateral corticospinal tract.origen: Primary motor, premotor and somatosensory cortex
rest|Lateral corticospinal tract.destino: Interneurons and motor neurons of the anterior horn contralateral to the origin
rest|Lateral corticospinal tract.territorio: Anterior spinal artery and vasocorona arteries
rest|Lateral corticospinal tract.funcion: Control of fine voluntary movements, especially distal ones.
rest|Lateral corticospinal tract.clinica: Its spinal lesion causes ipsilateral spastic paralysis with hyperreflexia and Babinski sign below the lesion.

rest|Lateral fasciculus proprius.descripcion: Intersegmental fibers surrounding the gray matter in the lateral funiculus of the spinal cord.
rest|Lateral fasciculus proprius.origen: Neurons of the spinal gray matter

rest|Lateral geniculate body.descripcion: Thalamic nucleus (metathalamus) on the inferoposterior surface of the thalamus, with six layers, where the optic tract terminates.
rest|Lateral geniculate body.territorio: Anterior choroidal and posterolateral choroidal arteries
rest|Lateral geniculate body.funcion: Relay of the visual pathway; projects to the primary visual cortex via the optic radiation.
rest|Lateral geniculate body.clinica: Its lesion produces contralateral homonymous hemianopia, sometimes sectoral.

rest|Lateral intermediate substance.descripcion: Lateral part of the intermediate zone of the spinal gray matter (lamina VII), between the anterior and posterior horns.
rest|Lateral intermediate substance.funcion: Contains interneurons and, in thoracic and upper lumbar segments, autonomic neurons of the lateral horn.

rest|Lateral occipital gyrus (Middle occ.descripcion: Gyrus of the lateral surface of the occipital lobe, between the superior and inferior occipital sulci.
rest|Lateral occipital gyrus (Middle occ.territorio: Posterior cerebral and middle cerebral artery
rest|Lateral occipital gyrus (Middle occ.funcion: Visual association cortex; perception of objects and motion.

rest|Lateral occipitotemporal gyrus.descripcion: Gyrus of the inferior surface of the temporal and occipital lobes, between the occipitotemporal and collateral sulci.
rest|Lateral occipitotemporal gyrus.funcion: Recognition of faces (fusiform face area), written words and colors.
rest|Lateral occipitotemporal gyrus.clinica: Its bilateral lesion causes prosopagnosia; on the left it may produce pure alexia.

rest|Lateral reticulospinal tract.descripcion: Descending pathway of the lateral funiculus of the spinal cord, mainly ipsilateral.
rest|Lateral reticulospinal tract.destino: Interneurons of the spinal gray matter (laminae VII-IX)
rest|Lateral reticulospinal tract.funcion: Inhibits extensor tone and modulates reflexes, locomotion and autonomic functions.
rest|Lateral reticulospinal tract.clinica: Its disinhibition contributes to spasticity after cortical lesions.

rest|Lateral spinothalamic tract.descripcion: Ascending pathway of the lateral funiculus of the spinal cord (anterolateral system), with somatotopic organization.
rest|Lateral spinothalamic tract.origen: Contralateral posterior horn neurons (laminae I and V); they cross in the anterior white commissure
rest|Lateral spinothalamic tract.destino: Ventral posterolateral nucleus of the thalamus
rest|Lateral spinothalamic tract.funcion: Conveys pain and temperature from the contralateral half of the body.
rest|Lateral spinothalamic tract.clinica: In spinal hemisection (Brown-Séquard) there is contralateral loss of pain and temperature sensation 1-2 segments below; basis of cordotomy.

rest|Lateral ventricle.descripcion: C-shaped cavity in each hemisphere with frontal horn, body, atrium, occipital horn and temporal horn; communicates with the third ventricle through the interventricular foramen.
rest|Lateral ventricle.territorio: Choroid plexus: anterior and posterior choroidal arteries
rest|Lateral ventricle.funcion: Contains CSF produced mainly by its choroid plexus.
rest|Lateral ventricle.clinica: Its dilation indicates hydrocephalus or atrophy; displacement due to mass effect.

rest|Lateral vestibulospinal tract.descripcion: Ipsilateral descending pathway of the anterior/anterolateral funiculus that runs the entire length of the spinal cord.
rest|Lateral vestibulospinal tract.destino: Motor neurons and interneurons of the ipsilateral anterior horn
rest|Lateral vestibulospinal tract.funcion: Facilitates the antigravity extensor muscles to maintain posture and balance.
rest|Lateral vestibulospinal tract.clinica: Its unopposed action generates decerebrate rigidity.

rest|Lens.descripcion: Transparent, avascular biconvex lens behind the iris, suspended from the ciliary body by the zonule.
rest|Lens.funcion: Variable focusing (accommodation) of the image onto the retina by means of the ciliary muscle.
rest|Lens.clinica: Its opacification is cataract; the loss of accommodation with age is presbyopia.

rest|Lentiform nucleus.descripcion: Lens-shaped nuclear mass lateral to the internal capsule and medial to the external capsule; formed by the putamen and globus pallidus.
rest|Lentiform nucleus.territorio: Lenticulostriate arteries (middle cerebral) and anterior choroidal
rest|Lentiform nucleus.funcion: Part of the basal ganglia; regulates the initiation and scaling of movement.
rest|Lentiform nucleus.clinica: Typical site of hypertensive hemorrhage (putamen) from rupture of lenticulostriate arteries; affected in Wilson's disease.

rest|Lingual gyrus.descripcion: Gyrus of the medial and inferior surface of the occipital lobe, below the calcarine sulcus and medial to the collateral sulcus.
rest|Lingual gyrus.territorio: Posterior cerebral artery (calcarine and medial occipital)
rest|Lingual gyrus.funcion: Contains visual cortex (lower lip) for the contralateral superior visual field; color processing.
rest|Lingual gyrus.clinica: Its lesion produces contralateral superior homonymous quadrantanopia and achromatopsia.

rest|Lingula of cerebellum.descripcion: Most anterior segment of the vermis of the anterior lobe, resting on the superior medullary velum.
rest|Lingula of cerebellum.funcion: Belongs to the spinocerebellum of the vermis; postural control.

rest|Lunate sulcus.descripcion: Inconstant sulcus on the lateral surface of the occipital pole, curved and concave backward.
rest|Lunate sulcus.funcion: Approximately marks the anterior limit of the primary visual cortex on the lateral surface.

rest|Mamillary body.descripcion: Pair of rounded eminences of the posterior hypothalamus, in the interpeduncular fossa, in front of the posterior perforated substance.
rest|Mamillary body.territorio: Posterior communicating and posterior cerebral arteries (perforating branches)
rest|Mamillary body.funcion: Part of the Papez circuit: receives the fornix and projects to the anterior thalamus (mammillothalamic tract); memory.
rest|Mamillary body.clinica: It atrophies in Wernicke-Korsakoff encephalopathy due to thiamine deficiency.

rest|Medial geniculate body.descripcion: Thalamic nucleus (metathalamus) below the pulvinar, joined to the inferior colliculus by its brachium.
rest|Medial geniculate body.territorio: Posterolateral choroidal artery and thalamogeniculate arteries (posterior cerebral)
rest|Medial geniculate body.funcion: Relay of the auditory pathway to the primary auditory cortex (Heschl's gyri) via the acoustic radiation.
rest|Medial geniculate body.clinica: Its unilateral lesion causes little hearing loss; the bilateral one may cause cortical deafness or auditory agnosia.

rest|Medial occipitotemporal gyrus (Para.descripcion: Gyrus of the inferomedial surface of the temporal lobe, medial to the collateral sulcus; its anterior end forms the uncus.
rest|Medial occipitotemporal gyrus (Para.territorio: Posterior cerebral and anterior choroidal artery
rest|Medial occipitotemporal gyrus (Para.funcion: Includes the entorhinal cortex; gateway to the hippocampus; memory and scene recognition.
rest|Medial occipitotemporal gyrus (Para.clinica: The uncus herniates through the tentorium compressing the III cranial nerve (ipsilateral mydriasis).

rest|Medial reticulospinal tract.descripcion: Ipsilateral descending pathway of the anterior funiculus of the spinal cord.
rest|Medial reticulospinal tract.origen: Pontine reticular formation (oral and caudal pontine reticular nuclei)
rest|Medial reticulospinal tract.destino: Interneurons and motor neurons of the spinal gray matter (laminae VII-VIII)
rest|Medial reticulospinal tract.funcion: Facilitates extensor tone and postural and axial movements.

rest|Medial vestibulospinal tract.descripcion: Bilateral descending pathway that travels in the medial longitudinal fasciculus and reaches the cervical spinal cord.
rest|Medial vestibulospinal tract.destino: Cervical motor neurons of the neck muscles
rest|Medial vestibulospinal tract.funcion: Stabilizes the head and coordinates its movements with eye movements (vestibulocollic reflex).

rest|Medulla oblongata.descripcion: Inferior part of the brainstem, between the pons and the spinal cord at the level of the foramen magnum.
rest|Medulla oblongata.territorio: Vertebral, spinal and posterior inferior cerebellar arteries
rest|Medulla oblongata.funcion: Contains cardiorespiratory and vasomotor centers, nuclei of cranial nerves IX-XII, and ascending and descending pathways.
rest|Medulla oblongata.clinica: Its lesion (lateral medullary syndrome of Wallenberg, due to PICA occlusion) produces crossed sensory disturbances, dysphagia and Horner syndrome.

rest|Midbrain.descripcion: Superior part of the brainstem, between the diencephalon and pons; comprises the tectum, tegmentum and cerebral peduncles, traversed by the aqueduct.
rest|Midbrain.territorio: Posterior cerebral, superior cerebellar arteries and branches of the basilar
rest|Midbrain.funcion: Contains nuclei of cranial nerves III and IV, substantia nigra, red nucleus and centers for visual and auditory reflexes.
rest|Midbrain.clinica: Weber syndrome (peduncle lesion) causes ipsilateral III cranial nerve palsy and contralateral hemiplegia.

rest|Middle frontal gyrus.descripcion: Gyrus of the lateral frontal lobe, between the superior and inferior frontal sulci.
rest|Middle frontal gyrus.funcion: Contains the frontal eye field (area 8) for voluntary saccadic movements and participates in executive functions and working memory.
rest|Middle frontal gyrus.clinica: Its acute lesion deviates conjugate gaze toward the injured side.

rest|Middle temporal gyrus.descripcion: Gyrus of the lateral surface of the temporal lobe, between the superior and inferior temporal sulci.
rest|Middle temporal gyrus.funcion: Semantic language processing, object recognition and perception of visual motion (MT/V5 region in its posterior part).

rest|Nasolacrimal duct.descripcion: Duct that descends from the lacrimal sac through the bony nasolacrimal canal and opens into the inferior nasal meatus.
rest|Nasolacrimal duct.territorio: Branches of the facial and ophthalmic arteries
rest|Nasolacrimal duct.funcion: Drains tears from the lacrimal sac to the nasal cavity.
rest|Nasolacrimal duct.clinica: Its obstruction (congenital or acquired) produces epiphora and dacryocystitis.

rest|Nodule of vermis.descripcion: Most inferior lobule of the cerebellar vermis, which together with the flocculi forms the flocculonodular lobe.
rest|Nodule of vermis.funcion: Part of the vestibulocerebellum: control of balance and eye movements.
rest|Nodule of vermis.clinica: Its lesion (e.g. childhood medulloblastoma) produces truncal ataxia and impaired balance.

rest|Nucleus ambiguus.descripcion: Column of branchial motor neurons in the reticular formation of the medulla oblongata.
rest|Nucleus ambiguus.funcion: Innervates the musculature of the pharynx, larynx and soft palate via cranial nerves IX and X (and the cranial root of XI); vagal cardioinhibitory component.
rest|Nucleus ambiguus.clinica: Its lesion (Wallenberg syndrome) causes dysphagia, dysphonia and deviation of the uvula toward the healthy side.

rest|Nucleus proprius.es: Nucleus proprius of the posterior horn
rest|Nucleus proprius.descripcion: Neuronal group of Rexed laminae III-IV in the head of the posterior horn of the spinal cord.
rest|Nucleus proprius.funcion: Integrates tactile, proprioceptive and nociceptive sensory information; gives rise to fibers of ascending pathways.

rest|Occipital pole.descripcion: Posterior end of the cerebral hemisphere, in the occipital lobe.
rest|Occipital pole.territorio: Posterior cerebral artery (with supply from the middle cerebral)
rest|Occipital pole.funcion: Contains the primary visual cortex representing central macular vision.
rest|Occipital pole.clinica: Macular sparing in posterior cerebral artery infarcts is due to the dual arterial supply of the occipital pole.

rest|Occipitotemporal sulcus (Lateral pa.descripcion: Sulcus of the inferior surface of the temporal and occipital lobes, between the inferior temporal gyrus and the lateral occipitotemporal (fusiform) gyrus.
rest|Occipitotemporal sulcus (Lateral pa.funcion: Topographic landmark of the ventral visual cortex related to shape recognition.

rest|Olfactory sulcus.descripcion: Anteroposterior sulcus on the orbital surface of the frontal lobe, lateral to the gyrus rectus, where the olfactory bulb and tract lie.
rest|Olfactory sulcus.funcion: Topographic landmark housing the olfactory pathway.
rest|Olfactory sulcus.clinica: Olfactory groove meningiomas can cause anosmia and personality changes (Foster Kennedy syndrome).

rest|Olive.descripcion: Oval relief on the anterolateral surface of the medulla, lateral to the pyramid, produced by the inferior olivary nucleus.
rest|Olive.territorio: Vertebral and posterior inferior cerebellar artery
rest|Olive.funcion: The inferior olivary nucleus gives rise to the climbing fibers to the cerebellum, important for motor learning.
rest|Olive.clinica: Hypertrophic olivary degeneration after lesions of the Guillain-Mollaret triangle causes palatal myoclonus.

rest|Opercular part of inferior frontal.es: Opercular part of inferior frontal gyrus
rest|Opercular part of inferior frontal.descripcion: Posterior part of the inferior frontal gyrus, between the ascending ramus of the lateral sulcus and the precentral sulcus (area 44).
rest|Opercular part of inferior frontal.funcion: Part of Broca's area in the dominant hemisphere: motor planning of speech.
rest|Opercular part of inferior frontal.clinica: Its lesion in the dominant hemisphere produces Broca's aphasia (non-fluent expression).

rest|Optic chiasm.descripcion: X-shaped structure over the sella turcica, where the optic nerves join and the fibers from the nasal hemiretinae cross.
rest|Optic chiasm.territorio: Superior hypophyseal, anterior communicating and internal carotid arteries
rest|Optic chiasm.funcion: Allows partial decussation of visual fibers for binocular vision.
rest|Optic chiasm.clinica: Its compression by a pituitary adenoma causes bitemporal hemianopia.

rest|Optic tract.descripcion: Bundle that wraps around the cerebral peduncle from the chiasm to the lateral geniculate body.
rest|Optic tract.origen: Ganglion cells of the ipsilateral temporal and contralateral nasal hemiretina
rest|Optic tract.destino: Lateral geniculate body (and superior colliculus, pretectal area, hypothalamus)
rest|Optic tract.funcion: Transmits information from the contralateral visual hemifield.
rest|Optic tract.clinica: Its lesion produces incongruent contralateral homonymous hemianopia.

rest|Orbital gyri.descripcion: Gyri of the orbital surface of the frontal lobe, lateral to the gyrus rectus, delimited by the orbital sulci.
rest|Orbital gyri.territorio: Anterior cerebral and middle cerebral arteries (orbitofrontal)
rest|Orbital gyri.funcion: Orbitofrontal cortex: decision making, emotional regulation, social behavior and reward processing.
rest|Orbital gyri.clinica: Its lesion produces disinhibition, impulsivity and impaired social behavior.

rest|Orbital gyri (Frontomarginal gyrus.descripcion: Gyrus and sulcus of the anterior inferior border of the frontal lobe, at the transition between the orbital and lateral surfaces of the frontal pole.
rest|Orbital gyri (Frontomarginal gyrus.funcion: Part of the anterior prefrontal cortex; higher executive and cognitive functions.

rest|Orbital part of inferior frontal g.es: Orbital part of inferior frontal gyrus
rest|Orbital part of inferior frontal g.descripcion: Anteroinferior part of the inferior frontal gyrus, below the horizontal ramus of the lateral sulcus (area 47).
rest|Orbital part of inferior frontal g.funcion: Semantic language processing and prefrontal functions.

rest|Orbital sulci (H-shaped orbital sul.descripcion: Sulci of the orbital surface of the frontal lobe, characteristically arranged in an H shape, which delimit the orbital gyri.
rest|Orbital sulci (H-shaped orbital sul.funcion: Topographic landmarks of the orbitofrontal cortex.

rest|Orbital sulci (Lateral Orbital sulc.descripcion: Longitudinal lateral limb of the H-shaped orbital sulcal system on the orbital surface of the frontal lobe.
rest|Orbital sulci (Lateral Orbital sulc.funcion: Topographic landmark separating the lateral and posterior/anterior orbital gyri.

rest|Paracentral gyrus and sulcus.descripcion: Region of the medial surface of the hemisphere surrounding the upper end of the central sulcus, bounded by the paracentral and marginal sulci.
rest|Paracentral gyrus and sulcus.funcion: Contains the primary motor and somatosensory areas of the lower limb; voluntary bladder control.
rest|Paracentral gyrus and sulcus.clinica: Its lesion (anterior cerebral artery infarct, parasagittal meningioma) produces contralateral lower limb paresis and urinary incontinence.

rest|Paracentral sulcus.descripcion: Sulcus of the medial surface of the hemisphere, ascending branch of the cingulate sulcus that bounds the paracentral lobule anteriorly.
rest|Paracentral sulcus.funcion: Topographic landmark separating the medial superior frontal gyrus from the paracentral lobule.

rest|Parieto-occipital sulcus.descripcion: Deep sulcus of the medial surface of the hemisphere that separates the parietal lobe (precuneus) from the occipital lobe (cuneus).
rest|Parieto-occipital sulcus.funcion: Anatomical boundary between the parietal and occipital lobes.

rest|Peduncle of flocculus.descripcion: Band of white matter joining the flocculus with the nodule of the vermis through the inferior medullary velum.
rest|Peduncle of flocculus.funcion: Connects the components of the flocculonodular lobe (vestibulocerebellum).

rest|Pons.descripcion: Middle part of the brainstem, between the midbrain and medulla, ventral to the cerebellum and fourth ventricle.
rest|Pons.funcion: Contains nuclei of cranial nerves V-VIII, pontine nuclei that relay cortex-cerebellum, and long ascending and descending pathways.
rest|Pons.clinica: An extensive pontine infarct can produce locked-in syndrome.

rest|Postcentral gyrus.descripcion: Gyrus of the parietal lobe located between the central and postcentral sulci (areas 3, 1 and 2).
rest|Postcentral gyrus.territorio: Middle cerebral artery (lateral surface) and anterior cerebral artery (medial surface)
rest|Postcentral gyrus.funcion: Primary somatosensory cortex with somatotopic representation (homunculus) of the contralateral half of the body.
rest|Postcentral gyrus.clinica: Its lesion causes contralateral cortical hypoesthesia, astereognosis and loss of two-point discrimination.

rest|Postcentral sulcus.descripcion: Sulcus parallel and posterior to the central sulcus, which bounds the postcentral gyrus posteriorly.
rest|Postcentral sulcus.funcion: Topographic landmark between the primary somatosensory cortex and the parietal lobules.

rest|Posterior cochlear nucleus.descripcion: Nucleus on the dorsolateral surface of the inferior cerebellar peduncle, at the pontomedullary junction (acoustic tubercle).
rest|Posterior cochlear nucleus.origen: Fibers of the cochlear part of the vestibulocochlear nerve
rest|Posterior cochlear nucleus.funcion: First central relay of the auditory pathway; analysis of spectral features of sound.
rest|Posterior cochlear nucleus.clinica: Its lesion produces ipsilateral sensorineural hearing loss.

rest|Posterior commissure.descripcion: Bundle of fibers crossing the midline at the midbrain-diencephalon junction, below the base of the pineal gland, above the aqueduct.
rest|Posterior commissure.origen: Pretectal nuclei and other midbrain nuclei
rest|Posterior commissure.funcion: Mediates the consensual pupillary light reflex and vertical gaze.
rest|Posterior commissure.clinica: Its lesion (pinealoma) produces Parinaud syndrome: paralysis of upward vertical gaze.

rest|Posterior fasciculus proprius.descripcion: White matter fibers adjacent to the gray matter in the posterior funiculus of the spinal cord.
rest|Posterior fasciculus proprius.origen: Interneurons of the spinal gray matter
rest|Posterior fasciculus proprius.funcion: Ascending and descending intersegmental connections for spinal reflexes.

rest|Posterior horn of spinal cord.descripcion: Dorsal extension of the spinal gray matter (Rexed laminae I-VI), which receives the posterior roots.
rest|Posterior horn of spinal cord.funcion: Reception and processing of somatic and visceral sensory information (pain, temperature, touch, proprioception).
rest|Posterior horn of spinal cord.clinica: Its lesion produces ipsilateral segmental sensory loss (e.g. syringomyelia affects the commissure and horns).

rest|Posterior quadrangular lobule.descripcion: Hemispheric lobule of the cerebellum located immediately behind the primary fissure (simple lobule, HVI).
rest|Posterior quadrangular lobule.funcion: Part of the spinocerebellum/cerebrocerebellum; coordination of limb movements.
rest|Posterior quadrangular lobule.clinica: Its lesion produces ipsilateral ataxia and dysmetria.

rest|Posterior segment of eyeball.descripcion: Portion of the eyeball behind the lens: vitreous body, retina, choroid and optic nerve.
rest|Posterior segment of eyeball.territorio: Ophthalmic artery (central retinal and posterior ciliary)
rest|Posterior segment of eyeball.funcion: Contains the photoreceptive and nutritive structures responsible for the formation of the visual image.
rest|Posterior segment of eyeball.clinica: Site of pathologies such as retinal detachment, diabetic retinopathy and macular degeneration.

rest|Posterior spinocerebellar tract.descripcion: Ascending bundle in the posterolateral periphery of the lateral funiculus of the spinal cord.
rest|Posterior spinocerebellar tract.destino: Ipsilateral spinocerebellum cortex (via inferior cerebellar peduncle)
rest|Posterior spinocerebellar tract.funcion: Transmits unconscious proprioception from the trunk and ipsilateral lower limb to the cerebellum.
rest|Posterior spinocerebellar tract.clinica: Affected in Friedreich ataxia, with sensory ataxia.

rest|Posterior transverse collateral sul.descripcion: Small transverse sulcus of the inferior surface of the occipitotemporal lobe, related to the posterior end of the collateral sulcus.
rest|Posterior transverse collateral sul.funcion: Topographic landmark of the basal surface of the hemisphere.

rest|Posterolateral tract.descripcion: Bundle of fine fibers between the apex of the posterior horn and the surface of the spinal cord, at the entry of the posterior roots.
rest|Posterolateral tract.origen: Fine fibers of the posterior roots (pain and temperature)
rest|Posterolateral tract.destino: Gray matter of the posterior horn 1-2 segments above and below
rest|Posterolateral tract.funcion: Distributes nociceptive and thermal afferents to neighboring spinal segments.

rest|Precentral gyrus.descripcion: Gyrus of the frontal lobe between the precentral and central sulci (area 4).
rest|Precentral gyrus.territorio: Middle cerebral artery (lateral surface) and anterior cerebral artery (medial surface)
rest|Precentral gyrus.funcion: Primary motor cortex with somatotopic organization; main origin of the corticospinal tract.
rest|Precentral gyrus.clinica: Its lesion produces contralateral upper motor neuron paresis, predominantly faciobrachial in middle cerebral artery infarcts.

rest|Precentral sulcus (Superior part).descripcion: Superior segment of the precentral sulcus, in front of the precentral gyrus, where it usually joins the superior frontal sulcus.
rest|Precentral sulcus (Superior part).funcion: Anterior boundary of the primary motor cortex; landmark for the premotor cortex and frontal eye field.

rest|Precentral sulcus (inferior part).descripcion: Inferior segment of the precentral sulcus, in front of the precentral gyrus, related to the inferior frontal sulcus.
rest|Precentral sulcus (inferior part).funcion: Anterior boundary of the primary motor cortex in its faciolingual portion.

rest|Precuneus.descripcion: Region of the medial surface of the parietal lobe, between the paracentral lobule, the parieto-occipital sulcus and the subparietal sulcus.
rest|Precuneus.territorio: Anterior cerebral artery (pericallosal) and posterior cerebral
rest|Precuneus.funcion: Visuospatial integration, mental imagery, episodic memory and self-awareness; node of the default mode network.

rest|Putamen.descripcion: Lateral basal nucleus of the corpus striatum, lateral to the globus pallidus and separated from the caudate by the internal capsule.
rest|Putamen.funcion: Component of the striatum; regulates movement through the basal ganglia circuits.
rest|Putamen.clinica: Most frequent location of hypertensive intracerebral hemorrhage.

rest|Pyramid of medulla oblongata.descripcion: Longitudinal relief on the anterior surface of the medulla, on each side of the anterior median fissure, formed by corticospinal fibers.
rest|Pyramid of medulla oblongata.origen: Motor cortex (precentral gyrus and premotor areas)
rest|Pyramid of medulla oblongata.funcion: Carries the corticospinal tract; at its lower end most fibers decussate.
rest|Pyramid of medulla oblongata.clinica: Medial medullary syndrome (Dejerine) produces contralateral hemiplegia sparing the face and ipsilateral tongue paralysis.

rest|Pyramis of vermis.descripcion: Lobule of the inferior cerebellar vermis, between the tuber and the uvula.
rest|Pyramis of vermis.funcion: Part of the spinocerebellum; postural and tone control.

rest|Red nucleus.descripcion: Ovoid nucleus of the midbrain tegmentum at the level of the superior colliculus, traversed by fibers of the III cranial nerve.
rest|Red nucleus.territorio: Posterior cerebral artery (paramedian branches) and basilar
rest|Red nucleus.funcion: Relay in cerebellar and motor circuits; gives rise to the rubrospinal tract and projects to the inferior olive.
rest|Red nucleus.clinica: Its lesion (Benedikt/Claude syndrome) produces tremor, contralateral ataxia and ipsilateral III cranial nerve palsy.

rest|Retina.descripcion: Inner tunic of the eyeball, of neuroectodermal origin, with photoreceptors, bipolar cells and ganglion cells.
rest|Retina.territorio: Central retinal artery (inner layers) and choriocapillaris (outer layers)
rest|Retina.funcion: Transforms light into nerve signals and performs initial visual processing.
rest|Retina.clinica: Occlusion of the central retinal artery causes sudden monocular blindness with a cherry-red spot.

rest|Rubrospinal tract.descripcion: Descending bundle that decussates in the midbrain tegmentum and descends in the lateral funiculus, ventral to the lateral corticospinal tract.
rest|Rubrospinal tract.destino: Interneurons of the anterior horn of the contralateral cervical spinal cord
rest|Rubrospinal tract.funcion: Facilitates the activity of upper limb flexor muscles.
rest|Rubrospinal tract.clinica: Implicated in decorticate posturing (flexion of the upper limbs).

rest|Sclera.descripcion: Opaque posterior portion of the fibrous tunic of the eyeball, continuous with the cornea at the limbus.
rest|Sclera.funcion: Protects the ocular contents, maintains its shape and serves as insertion for the extraocular muscles.
rest|Sclera.clinica: Yellowish coloration in jaundice; bluish in osteogenesis imperfecta.

rest|Septal nuclei.descripcion: Group of nuclei of the septal region, below the rostrum of the corpus callosum and in front of the lamina terminalis.
rest|Septal nuclei.funcion: Component of the limbic system: connection with the hippocampus and hypothalamus; reinforcement, pleasure and emotional modulation.

rest|Septum pellucidum.descripcion: Thin vertical double lamina between the corpus callosum and the fornix, separating the frontal horns of the lateral ventricles.
rest|Septum pellucidum.funcion: Separates the lateral ventricles and houses septohippocampal connecting fibers.
rest|Septum pellucidum.clinica: Its absence is associated with septo-optic dysplasia; the cavum septi pellucidi is a frequent variant.

rest|Spinal dura.descripcion: Fibrous outer meninx of the spinal cord, separated from the bone by the epidural space; ends at S2.
rest|Spinal dura.funcion: Protects the spinal cord and forms the dural sac containing the cerebrospinal fluid.
rest|Spinal dura.clinica: The epidural space is used for anesthesia; dural puncture may cause post-puncture headache.

rest|Spinal reticular process.descripcion: Zone of intermingled gray and white matter in the angle between the posterior and lateral horns, mainly in the cervical spinal cord.
rest|Spinal reticular process.funcion: Intersegmental connections and with the reticular formation of the brainstem.
