rest|Spinotectal tract.descripcion: Ascending bundle of the anterolateral funiculus of the spinal cord, accompanying the spinothalamic tract.
rest|Spinotectal tract.origen: Posterior horn of the spinal cord (contralateral)
rest|Spinotectal tract.destino: Superior colliculus and periaqueductal gray matter
rest|Spinotectal tract.funcion: Mediates spinovisual orienting reflexes of the head and eyes toward somatic stimuli.

rest|Straight gyrus (Gyrus rectus).descripcion: Medial gyrus of the orbital surface of the frontal lobe, between the longitudinal fissure and the olfactory sulcus.
rest|Straight gyrus (Gyrus rectus).funcion: Part of the medial orbitofrontal cortex; emotional and behavioral functions.
rest|Straight gyrus (Gyrus rectus).clinica: Frequently affected by rupture of anterior communicating artery aneurysms.

rest|Stria medullaris thalami.descripcion: Bundle of fibers along the dorsomedial border of the thalamus, at the junction of its medial and dorsal surfaces.
rest|Stria medullaris thalami.origen: Septal nuclei, lateral preoptic area and hypothalamus
rest|Stria medullaris thalami.funcion: Epithalamic pathway connecting the limbic system with the habenula.

rest|Stria terminalis.descripcion: Arched bundle in the groove between the caudate nucleus and thalamus, on the floor of the lateral ventricle.
rest|Stria terminalis.destino: Hypothalamus, septal nuclei and bed nucleus of the stria terminalis
rest|Stria terminalis.funcion: Main efferent pathway of the amygdala; regulates autonomic, endocrine and emotional responses.

rest|Subparietal sulcus.descripcion: Sulcus of the medial surface of the hemisphere, posterior continuation of the cingulate sulcus, below the precuneus.
rest|Subparietal sulcus.funcion: Separates the precuneus from the posterior cingulate gyrus.

rest|Sulcus interm_prim-Jensen.descripcion: Inconstant sulcus of the inferior parietal lobule that separates the supramarginal gyrus from the angular gyrus, descending branch of the intraparietal sulcus.
rest|Sulcus interm_prim-Jensen.funcion: Topographic landmark of the inferior parietal lobule.

rest|Superior cerebellar peduncle.descripcion: Bundle joining the cerebellum with the midbrain, in the dorsolateral wall of the upper part of the fourth ventricle.
rest|Superior cerebellar peduncle.destino: Contralateral red nucleus and thalamus (ventral lateral)
rest|Superior cerebellar peduncle.funcion: Main cerebellar efferent pathway; also contains the anterior spinocerebellar tract.
rest|Superior cerebellar peduncle.clinica: Its lesion produces ipsilateral ataxia and intention tremor.

rest|Superior colliculus.descripcion: Paired eminence of the midbrain tectum, above the inferior colliculus.
rest|Superior colliculus.territorio: Posterior cerebral and superior cerebellar arteries (quadrigeminal)
rest|Superior colliculus.funcion: Coordinates orienting movements of the eyes and head toward visual, auditory and somatic stimuli.
rest|Superior colliculus.clinica: Compression of the tectum (pinealoma) produces Parinaud syndrome.

rest|Superior frontal gyrus.descripcion: Superior longitudinal gyrus of the frontal lobe, above the superior frontal sulcus, extending onto the medial surface.
rest|Superior frontal gyrus.funcion: Contains the supplementary motor area and prefrontal cortex; motor planning and executive functions.
rest|Superior frontal gyrus.clinica: Lesions of the supplementary motor area produce akinesia and transient mutism.

rest|Superior frontal sulcus.descripcion: Longitudinal sulcus on the lateral surface of the frontal lobe, between the superior and middle frontal gyri.
rest|Superior frontal sulcus.funcion: Topographic landmark; its posterior end is related to the frontal eye field.

rest|Superior occipital gyri.descripcion: Gyrus of the lateral surface of the occipital lobe, above the transverse/lateral occipital sulcus.
rest|Superior occipital gyri.funcion: Visual association cortex of the dorsal pathway (spatial processing).

rest|Superior parietal lobule.descripcion: Region of the parietal lobe above the intraparietal sulcus and behind the postcentral gyrus (areas 5 and 7).
rest|Superior parietal lobule.territorio: Middle cerebral and anterior cerebral artery
rest|Superior parietal lobule.funcion: Somatosensory and visuospatial integration for body orientation and goal-directed movement.
rest|Superior parietal lobule.clinica: Its lesion produces optic ataxia, astereognosis and neglect of the contralateral half of the body.

rest|Superior salivatory nucleus.descripcion: Preganglionic parasympathetic nucleus in the caudal pontine tegmentum.
rest|Superior salivatory nucleus.destino: Pterygopalatine and submandibular ganglia (via nervus intermedius)
rest|Superior salivatory nucleus.funcion: Controls secretion of the lacrimal, submandibular, sublingual and nasal glands.
rest|Superior salivatory nucleus.clinica: Lesions of the facial nerve proximal to the geniculate ganglion reduce tear secretion.

rest|Superior semilunar lobule.descripcion: Hemispheric lobule of the cerebellum (Crus I, HVIIA) between the posterosuperior and horizontal fissures.
rest|Superior semilunar lobule.funcion: Part of the cerebrocerebellum; planning and coordination of movements and cognitive functions.
rest|Superior semilunar lobule.clinica: Its lesion produces ipsilateral dysmetria and decomposition of movement.

rest|Superior temporal gyrus (Lateral pa.descripcion: Gyrus of the lateral surface of the temporal lobe, between the lateral sulcus and the superior temporal sulcus.
rest|Superior temporal gyrus (Lateral pa.funcion: Contains the auditory association cortex and, in its posterior dominant part, Wernicke's area (language comprehension).
rest|Superior temporal gyrus (Lateral pa.clinica: Its posterior lesion in the dominant hemisphere produces Wernicke's aphasia (fluent, with poor comprehension).

rest|Superior temporal sulcus.descripcion: Sulcus parallel to the lateral sulcus on the lateral surface of the temporal lobe, between the superior and middle temporal gyri.
rest|Superior temporal sulcus.funcion: Its cortex processes social perception, biological motion, voices and language.

rest|Supramarginal gyrus.descripcion: Gyrus of the inferior parietal lobule that surrounds the posterior end of the lateral sulcus (area 40).
rest|Supramarginal gyrus.funcion: Phonological processing, praxis and integrated somatosensory perception.
rest|Supramarginal gyrus.clinica: Its dominant lesion produces conduction aphasia and ideomotor apraxia.

rest|Suspensory ligament of eyeball.descripcion: Hammock-like fascial band beneath the eyeball, formed by the bulbar sheath and the fascia of the inferior rectus and inferior oblique muscles, attached to the orbital walls.
rest|Suspensory ligament of eyeball.funcion: Supports the eyeball in the orbit.
rest|Suspensory ligament of eyeball.clinica: Maintains the position of the eye after resections of the orbital floor if it is preserved.

rest|Tectospinal tract.descripcion: Descending bundle that decussates in the midbrain (dorsal tegmental decussation) and descends in the anterior funiculus of the cervical spinal cord.
rest|Tectospinal tract.destino: Interneurons of the contralateral cervical anterior horn
rest|Tectospinal tract.funcion: Mediates reflex orienting movements of the head in response to visual and auditory stimuli.

rest|Temporal plane.descripcion: Superior surface of the superior temporal gyrus, behind the transverse temporal gyri, on the floor of the lateral sulcus.
rest|Temporal plane.funcion: Auditory association cortex; in the left hemisphere, part of Wernicke's area and language processing.
rest|Temporal plane.clinica: It is usually larger in the left hemisphere; asymmetry related to language dominance.

rest|Temporal pole.descripcion: Anterior end of the temporal lobe, lodged in the middle cranial fossa.
rest|Temporal pole.funcion: Semantic, emotional and social integration; recognition of people.
rest|Temporal pole.clinica: Its atrophy characterizes semantic dementia; it is a frequent site of traumatic contusions.

rest|Tentorium cerebelli.descripcion: Fold of dura mater between the occipital lobes and the cerebellum, separating the supratentorial and infratentorial compartments.
rest|Tentorium cerebelli.territorio: Meningeal branches (tentorial artery of the internal carotid)
rest|Tentorium cerebelli.funcion: Supports the occipital lobes and contains the straight, transverse and superior petrosal sinuses.
rest|Tentorium cerebelli.clinica: Transtentorial (uncal) herniation occurs through its incisura, with mydriasis due to compression of the III cranial nerve.

rest|Thalamus.descripcion: Paired ovoid mass of gray matter of the diencephalon, on either side of the third ventricle, medial to the internal capsule.
rest|Thalamus.territorio: Posterior cerebral arteries (thalamoperforating, thalamogeniculate) and posterior communicating
rest|Thalamus.funcion: Main relay station of sensory, motor (cerebellum, basal ganglia) and limbic pathways to the cortex; wakefulness.
rest|Thalamus.clinica: Thalamic infarction can produce Dejerine-Roussy syndrome (contralateral central pain).

rest|Third ventricle.descripcion: Narrow median cavity of the diencephalon, between both thalami and hypothalami, communicating with the lateral ventricles and the aqueduct.
rest|Third ventricle.funcion: Contains and conducts the cerebrospinal fluid.
rest|Third ventricle.clinica: Colloid cysts in its roof can obstruct the interventricular foramina and cause acute hydrocephalus.

rest|Tonsil of cerebellum.descripcion: Rounded lobule of the inferior surface of the cerebellar hemisphere, on either side of the uvula, next to the foramen magnum.
rest|Tonsil of cerebellum.funcion: Part of the posterior cerebellum (HIX); motor coordination.
rest|Tonsil of cerebellum.clinica: Its herniation through the foramen magnum compresses the medulla (cardiorespiratory arrest); descended in Chiari I malformation.

rest|Transverse frontopolar gyrus and su.descripcion: Small gyri and sulci with transverse orientation at the frontal pole.
rest|Transverse frontopolar gyrus and su.funcion: Anterior prefrontal cortex; complex executive functions and metacognition.

rest|Transverse occipital sulcus.descripcion: Sulcus of the lateral surface of the occipital lobe, posterior continuation of the intraparietal sulcus.
rest|Transverse occipital sulcus.funcion: Topographic landmark of the dorsal visual association cortex.

rest|Transverse temporal gyri.descripcion: Gyri of the superior surface of the superior temporal gyrus, on the floor of the lateral sulcus, obliquely oriented (areas 41 and 42).
rest|Transverse temporal gyri.funcion: Primary auditory cortex, with tonotopic organization.
rest|Transverse temporal gyri.clinica: Its unilateral lesion barely reduces hearing; the bilateral one produces cortical deafness.

rest|Triangular part of inferior frontal.es: Triangular part of inferior frontal gyrus
rest|Triangular part of inferior frontal.descripcion: Middle part of the inferior frontal gyrus between the horizontal and ascending rami of the lateral sulcus (area 45).
rest|Triangular part of inferior frontal.funcion: Part of Broca's area in the dominant hemisphere; language production and semantic processing.
rest|Triangular part of inferior frontal.clinica: Its dominant lesion contributes to Broca's aphasia.

rest|Tuber of vermis.descripcion: Lobule of the posterior cerebellar vermis (VIIB), between the folium and the pyramis.
rest|Tuber of vermis.territorio: Superior and posterior inferior cerebellar artery
rest|Tuber of vermis.funcion: Part of the posterior vermis; eye movements and postural control.

rest|Tympanic membrane.descripcion: Thin, oval, conical membrane between the external acoustic meatus and the tympanic cavity, with the handle of the malleus attached.
rest|Tympanic membrane.territorio: Deep auricular and anterior tympanic arteries (maxillary)
rest|Tympanic membrane.funcion: Transmits sound vibrations to the ossicular chain.
rest|Tympanic membrane.clinica: Its perforation produces conductive hearing loss; in otitis media it appears bulging.

rest|Uvula of vermis.descripcion: Lobule of the inferior cerebellar vermis (IX), between the pyramis and the nodule, flanked by the tonsils.
rest|Uvula of vermis.funcion: Participates in vestibular, postural and oculomotor control.

rest|Vestibular nuclei.descripcion: Four nuclei (superior, lateral, medial and inferior) in the floor of the fourth ventricle, at the pontomedullary junction.
rest|Vestibular nuclei.destino: Spinal cord (vestibulospinal tracts), oculomotor nuclei (medial longitudinal fasciculus), cerebellum and thalamus
rest|Vestibular nuclei.territorio: Anterior inferior and posterior inferior cerebellar arteries
rest|Vestibular nuclei.funcion: Maintain balance, posture and gaze stability (vestibulo-ocular reflex).
rest|Vestibular nuclei.clinica: Their lesion produces vertigo, nystagmus, nausea and ataxia.

rest|Vestibule.descripcion: Central cavity of the bony labyrinth of the inner ear, between the cochlea and the semicircular canals; houses the utricle and saccule.
rest|Vestibule.funcion: Its otolithic organs detect linear accelerations and the position of the head relative to gravity.
rest|Vestibule.clinica: Displaced otoliths cause benign paroxysmal positional vertigo.

rest|Vitreous body.descripcion: Transparent gel occupying the vitreous chamber, between the lens and the retina.
rest|Vitreous body.funcion: Maintains the shape of the eyeball, supports the retina and transmits light.
rest|Vitreous body.clinica: Posterior vitreous detachment produces floaters and may cause retinal tears.

rest|White matter of spinal cord.descripcion: Peripheral mantle of myelinated fibers of the spinal cord, organized into posterior, lateral and anterior funiculi.
rest|White matter of spinal cord.territorio: Anterior spinal artery (anterior two thirds) and posterior spinal arteries
rest|White matter of spinal cord.funcion: Conducts the ascending and descending pathways between the spinal cord and the brain and the intersegmental connections.
rest|White matter of spinal cord.clinica: Spinal hemisection (Brown-Séquard) produces ipsilateral motor and proprioceptive deficit and contralateral loss of pain and temperature sensation.

rest|White matter of telencephalon.descripcion: Mass of myelinated fibers beneath the cerebral cortex (centrum semiovale), formed by association, commissural and projection fibers.
rest|White matter of telencephalon.territorio: Cerebral arteries (long medullary branches) and lenticulostriate
rest|White matter of telencephalon.funcion: Connects cortical areas with each other, both hemispheres, and the cortex with subcortical structures.
rest|White matter of telencephalon.clinica: Affected in multiple sclerosis and in leukoaraiosis due to small vessel disease.

rest|Wing of central lobule.descripcion: Lateral extension of the central lobule of the vermis into the anterior cerebellar hemisphere (HII-HIII).
rest|Wing of central lobule.funcion: Part of the spinocerebellum of the anterior lobe; coordination of gait and lower limbs.
rest|Wing of central lobule.clinica: Alcoholic degeneration of the anterior lobe produces gait ataxia.

rest|Zonular fibres.descripcion: Fine fibers extending from the ciliary body to the equator of the lens capsule (ciliary zonule).
rest|Zonular fibres.funcion: Support the lens and transmit the tension of the ciliary muscle for accommodation.
rest|Zonular fibres.clinica: Their weakness (Marfan syndrome) produces subluxation of the lens (ectopia lentis).

rest|Abducens nerve (VI).descripcion: Motor nerve that emerges from the pontomedullary sulcus, has a long subarachnoid course, passes through the cavernous sinus and enters the orbit through the superior orbital fissure.
rest|Abducens nerve (VI).territorio: Motor: lateral rectus muscle of the eye (abduction).
rest|Abducens nerve (VI).clinica: Its lesion produces convergent strabismus and horizontal diplopia; it is frequently affected in intracranial hypertension because of its long course.

rest|Accessory nerve (XI).descripcion: Motor nerve with spinal roots (C1–C5) that ascends through the foramen magnum and exits through the jugular foramen; crosses the posterior cervical triangle to the trapezius.
rest|Accessory nerve (XI).origen: Nucleus of the accessory nerve (upper cervical spinal cord); cranial root from the nucleus ambiguus
rest|Accessory nerve (XI).ramas: Cranial root (joins the vagus), external/spinal ramus
rest|Accessory nerve (XI).clinica: Can be injured in biopsies of the posterior cervical triangle: lateral winged scapula and difficulty elevating the shoulder.

rest|Accessory nucleus of oculomotor ner.descripcion: Preganglionic parasympathetic nucleus of the midbrain, dorsal to the motor nucleus of the oculomotor nerve, at the level of the superior colliculus.
rest|Accessory nucleus of oculomotor ner.territorio: Sphincter pupillae and ciliary muscle (via postganglionic fibers of the ciliary ganglion).
rest|Accessory nucleus of oculomotor ner.clinica: Its involvement produces non-reactive mydriasis, as in compression of the III cranial nerve by uncal herniation.

rest|Anterior branch of medial antebrach.es: Anterior branch of medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve
rest|Anterior branch of medial antebrach.la: Ramus anterior nervi cutanei antebrachii medialis
rest|Anterior branch of medial antebrach.descripcion: Terminal branch that descends along the anteromedial surface of the forearm, near the basilic vein, to the wrist.
rest|Anterior branch of medial antebrach.destino: Anteromedial skin of the forearm to the wrist
rest|Anterior branch of medial antebrach.territorio: Sensory: skin of the anterior and medial surface of the forearm.
rest|Anterior branch of medial antebrach.clinica: It can be injured in venipuncture of the basilic or median cubital vein.

rest|Anterior branch of obturator nerve.descripcion: Descends in front of the adductor brevis, behind the pectineus and adductor longus, in the medial thigh.
rest|Anterior branch of obturator nerve.destino: Subsartorial plexus and medial skin of the thigh
rest|Anterior branch of obturator nerve.ramas: Muscular branches, articular branch to the hip, cutaneous branch
rest|Anterior branch of obturator nerve.territorio: Motor: adductor longus, adductor brevis, gracilis (sometimes pectineus). Sensory: skin of the medial surface of the thigh.

rest|Anterior cutaneous branches of femo.es: Anterior cutaneous branches of the femoral nerve
rest|Anterior cutaneous branches of femo.descripcion: Branches that pierce the fascia lata along the anterior thigh (intermediate and medial femoral cutaneous nerves).
rest|Anterior cutaneous branches of femo.destino: Skin of the anterior and medial thigh down to the knee
rest|Anterior cutaneous branches of femo.territorio: Sensory: skin of the anterior and anteromedial surfaces of the thigh; they contribute to the patellar plexus.

rest|Anterior division of inferior trunk.es: Anterior division of the inferior trunk of the brachial plexus
rest|Anterior division of inferior trunk.la: Divisio anterior trunci inferioris plexus brachialis
rest|Anterior division of inferior trunk.descripcion: Division of the inferior trunk (C8–T1) behind the clavicle; it continues directly as the medial cord.
rest|Anterior division of inferior trunk.origen: Inferior trunk of the brachial plexus
rest|Anterior division of inferior trunk.territorio: Fibers for the flexor muscles (anterior compartment) of the upper limb and hand.

rest|Anterior division of mandibular ner.es: Anterior trunk of the mandibular nerve
rest|Anterior division of mandibular ner.descripcion: Smaller division of the mandibular nerve in the infratemporal fossa, predominantly motor.
rest|Anterior division of mandibular ner.ramas: Masseteric nerve, deep temporal nerves, lateral pterygoid nerve, buccal nerve
rest|Anterior division of mandibular ner.territorio: Motor: masseter, temporalis, lateral pterygoid. Sensory (buccal): skin and mucosa of the cheek.

rest|Anterior division of middle trunk o.es: Anterior division of the middle trunk of the brachial plexus
rest|Anterior division of middle trunk o.la: Divisio anterior trunci medii plexus brachialis
rest|Anterior division of middle trunk o.descripcion: Division of the middle trunk (C7) behind the clavicle; it joins that of the superior trunk to form the lateral cord.
rest|Anterior division of middle trunk o.origen: Middle trunk of the brachial plexus
rest|Anterior division of middle trunk o.territorio: Fibers for the flexor compartment of the upper limb.

rest|Anterior division of superior trunk.es: Anterior division of the superior trunk of the brachial plexus
rest|Anterior division of superior trunk.la: Divisio anterior trunci superioris plexus brachialis
rest|Anterior division of superior trunk.descripcion: Division of the superior trunk (C5–C6) behind the clavicle; together with that of the middle trunk it forms the lateral cord.
rest|Anterior division of superior trunk.origen: Superior trunk of the brachial plexus
rest|Anterior division of superior trunk.territorio: Fibers for the flexor compartment of the upper limb.

rest|Anterior interosseous nerve of fore.es: Anterior interosseous nerve of the forearm
rest|Anterior interosseous nerve of fore.descripcion: Deep branch of the median nerve that descends on the interosseous membrane between the flexor digitorum profundus and flexor pollicis longus down to the pronator quadratus.
rest|Anterior interosseous nerve of fore.territorio: Motor: flexor pollicis longus, lateral half of the flexor digitorum profundus (digits II–III), pronator quadratus. No cutaneous territory.
rest|Anterior interosseous nerve of fore.clinica: Its injury prevents forming the 'OK' sign (tip-to-tip pinch between thumb and index), without sensory deficit.

rest|Anterior root of posterior femoral.es: Anterior root of the posterior femoral cutaneous nerve
rest|Anterior root of posterior femoral.la: Radix anterior nervi cutanei femoris posterioris
rest|Anterior root of posterior femoral.descripcion: Contribution of the anterior divisions of the ventral rami S2–S3 to the posterior femoral cutaneous nerve, within the pelvis.
rest|Anterior root of posterior femoral.territorio: Contributes fibers to the perineal branches and inferior clunial nerves.

rest|Anterior root of spinal nerve.es: Anterior root of the spinal nerve
rest|Anterior root of spinal nerve.descripcion: Motor (efferent) root that emerges from the anterolateral sulcus of the spinal cord and joins the posterior root in the intervertebral foramen.
rest|Anterior root of spinal nerve.origen: Neurons of the anterior horn (and lateral horn at T1–L2) of the spinal cord
rest|Anterior root of spinal nerve.territorio: Somatic motor to the corresponding myotome; preganglionic sympathetic fibers at T1–L2 and parasympathetic at S2–S4.
rest|Anterior root of spinal nerve.clinica: Its compression (disc herniation) causes weakness and loss of reflexes of the corresponding myotome.

rest|Axillary nerve.descripcion: Terminal branch of the posterior cord; it passes through the quadrangular space with the posterior circumflex humeral artery and winds around the surgical neck of the humerus.
rest|Axillary nerve.origen: Posterior cord of the brachial plexus (C5–C6)
rest|Axillary nerve.destino: Deltoid muscle and skin of the shoulder
rest|Axillary nerve.ramas: Anterior branch, posterior branch, superior lateral brachial cutaneous nerve
rest|Axillary nerve.territorio: Motor: deltoid and teres minor. Sensory: skin over the lower portion of the deltoid ('regimental badge' patch).
rest|Axillary nerve.clinica: It is injured in fractures of the surgical neck and shoulder dislocations: loss of abduction and anesthesia of the deltoid patch.

rest|Buccal nerve.descripcion: Sensory branch of the anterior trunk of the mandibular nerve that passes between the heads of the lateral pterygoid and runs over the buccinator.
rest|Buccal nerve.destino: Skin and mucosa of the cheek
rest|Buccal nerve.territorio: Sensory: skin of the cheek, buccal mucosa and vestibular gingiva of the lower molars. It does not innervate the buccinator.
rest|Buccal nerve.clinica: It requires a separate block from the inferior alveolar to anesthetize the vestibular gingiva of the lower molars.

rest|Chorda tympani.descripcion: Branch of the facial nerve that crosses the tympanic cavity next to the malleus, exits through the petrotympanic fissure and joins the lingual nerve.
rest|Chorda tympani.origen: Facial nerve (mastoid portion of the facial canal)
rest|Chorda tympani.territorio: Taste of the anterior two thirds of the tongue; preganglionic parasympathetic to the submandibular and sublingual glands.
rest|Chorda tympani.clinica: It may be injured in middle ear surgery: taste disturbance (dysgeusia) in the anterior half of the tongue.

rest|Choroid plexus.descripcion: Vascular structure with specialized ependymal epithelium in the lateral, third and fourth ventricles; it is not a nerve plexus.
rest|Choroid plexus.funcion: Produces cerebrospinal fluid and forms the blood–CSF barrier.
rest|Choroid plexus.clinica: Its calcification is visible on neuroimaging; choroid plexus papillomas can cause hydrocephalus.

rest|Cochlear nerve.descripcion: Auditory portion of cranial nerve VIII; formed by the axons of the spiral ganglion of the cochlea, it runs through the internal acoustic meatus to the cerebellopontine angle.
rest|Cochlear nerve.destino: Cochlear nuclei of the medulla oblongata
rest|Cochlear nerve.territorio: Special sensory: hearing (spiral organ of Corti).
rest|Cochlear nerve.clinica: Vestibular schwannoma compresses the cochlear nerve: unilateral sensorineural hearing loss and tinnitus.

rest|Common fibular nerve.descripcion: Lateral division of the sciatic nerve; it follows the medial border of the biceps femoris and winds around the neck of the fibula, where it divides.
rest|Common fibular nerve.ramas: Lateral sural cutaneous nerve, fibular communicating branch, articular branches of the knee
rest|Common fibular nerve.territorio: Motor (via its branches): anterior and lateral compartments of the leg and dorsum of the foot. Sensory: lateral aspect of the leg and dorsum of the foot.
rest|Common fibular nerve.clinica: Its compression at the neck of the fibula (casts, crossed legs) causes foot drop and steppage gait.

rest|Common palmar digital branches of m.es: Common palmar digital nerves of the median nerve
rest|Common palmar digital branches of m.la: Nervi digitales palmares communes nervi mediani
rest|Common palmar digital branches of m.descripcion: Branches that arise from the median nerve distal to the carpal tunnel and run beneath the palmar aponeurosis toward interdigital spaces I–III.
rest|Common palmar digital branches of m.ramas: Proper palmar digital nerves; branches to lumbricals I–II
rest|Common palmar digital branches of m.territorio: Motor: 1st and 2nd lumbricals. Sensory: palmar skin of the thumb, index, middle and lateral half of the ring finger.

rest|Common palmar digital branches of u.es: Common palmar digital nerve of the ulnar nerve
rest|Common palmar digital branches of u.la: Nervus digitalis palmaris communis nervi ulnaris
rest|Common palmar digital branches of u.descripcion: Branch of the superficial branch of the ulnar nerve to the fourth interdigital space; it often communicates with the median nerve.
rest|Common palmar digital branches of u.origen: Superficial branch of the ulnar nerve
rest|Common palmar digital branches of u.destino: Proper palmar digital nerves of the ring and little fingers
rest|Common palmar digital branches of u.territorio: Sensory: palmar skin of the medial half of the ring finger and the little finger.

rest|Common plantar digital branches of.es: Common plantar digital nerves of the lateral plantar nerve
rest|Common plantar digital branches of.la: Nervi digitales plantares communes nervi plantaris lateralis
rest|Common plantar digital branches of.descripcion: Branches of the superficial branch of the lateral plantar nerve to the fourth interdigital space and the fifth toe.
rest|Common plantar digital branches of.origen: Superficial branch of the lateral plantar nerve
rest|Common plantar digital branches of.territorio: Sensory: plantar skin of the fifth toe and lateral half of the fourth.

rest|Common plantar digital branches of.es: Common plantar digital nerves of the medial plantar nerve
rest|Common plantar digital branches of.la: Nervi digitales plantares communes nervi plantaris medialis
rest|Common plantar digital branches of.descripcion: Branches of the medial plantar nerve that run toward interdigital spaces I–III on the sole.
rest|Common plantar digital branches of.ramas: Proper plantar digital nerves; branch to the first lumbrical
rest|Common plantar digital branches of.territorio: Motor: first lumbrical. Sensory: plantar skin of toes 1 to 3 and the medial half of the 4th.
rest|Common plantar digital branches of.clinica: Its compression between the metatarsal heads causes Morton's neuroma (typically in the third space).

rest|Communicating branch of median nerv.es: Communicating branch of the median nerve with the ulnar nerve
rest|Communicating branch of median nerv.la: Ramus communicans nervi mediani cum nervo ulnari
rest|Communicating branch of median nerv.descripcion: Variable nerve connection between the median and ulnar nerves, in the palm (Riche-Cannieu anastomosis) or the forearm (Martin-Gruber).
rest|Communicating branch of median nerv.clinica: It explains atypical patterns of motor deficit in median or ulnar nerve injuries and anomalous electromyographic findings.

rest|Deep branch of radial nerve.es: Deep branch of the radial nerve
rest|Deep branch of radial nerve.descripcion: Motor branch of the radial nerve that arises at the level of the lateral epicondyle and passes through the supinator (arcade of Frohse) to continue as the posterior interosseous nerve.
rest|Deep branch of radial nerve.destino: Posterior interosseous nerve of the forearm
rest|Deep branch of radial nerve.ramas: Branches to the extensor carpi radialis brevis and supinator
rest|Deep branch of radial nerve.territorio: Motor: extensor carpi radialis brevis, supinator and the extensor muscles of the posterior compartment of the forearm.
rest|Deep branch of radial nerve.clinica: Its entrapment at the arcade of Frohse causes finger drop without wrist drop or sensory deficit.

rest|Deep branch of ulnar nerve.es: Deep branch of the ulnar nerve
rest|Deep branch of ulnar nerve.descripcion: Motor branch that passes between the abductor and flexor digiti minimi brevis, winds around the hook of the hamate and crosses the palm with the deep palmar arch.
rest|Deep branch of ulnar nerve.destino: Adductor pollicis and first dorsal interosseous
rest|Deep branch of ulnar nerve.territorio: Motor: hypothenar muscles, interossei, 3rd–4th lumbricals, adductor pollicis and deep head of the flexor pollicis brevis.
rest|Deep branch of ulnar nerve.clinica: Injury: Froment's sign (thumb flexion when pinching a sheet of paper) and atrophy of the first dorsal interosseous.

rest|Deep fibular nerve.descripcion: Branch of the common fibular nerve that enters the anterior compartment of the leg, descends with the anterior tibial artery and reaches the dorsum of the foot.
rest|Deep fibular nerve.destino: First interdigital space of the dorsum of the foot
rest|Deep fibular nerve.ramas: Muscular branches, lateral branch (extensor brevis), dorsal digital nerves
rest|Deep fibular nerve.territorio: Motor: tibialis anterior, extensors digitorum longus and hallucis longus, fibularis tertius, short extensors. Sensory: skin of the first interdigital space.
rest|Deep fibular nerve.clinica: Its injury causes foot drop; anterior compartment syndrome affects it early.

rest|Dorsal branch of ulnar nerve.es: Dorsal branch of the ulnar nerve
rest|Dorsal branch of ulnar nerve.descripcion: Arises about 5 cm proximal to the wrist, passes beneath the flexor carpi ulnaris and winds around the ulna to the dorsum of the hand.
rest|Dorsal branch of ulnar nerve.territorio: Sensory: dorsomedial skin of the hand, little finger and medial half of the ring finger.
rest|Dorsal branch of ulnar nerve.clinica: Spared in compression in Guyon's canal (it arises earlier): it helps localize the ulnar lesion.

rest|Dorsal digital branches of deep fib.es: Dorsal digital nerves of the deep fibular nerve
rest|Dorsal digital branches of deep fib.la: Nervi digitales dorsales nervi fibularis profundi
rest|Dorsal digital branches of deep fib.descripcion: Two terminal branches of the deep fibular nerve in the first dorsal interosseous space of the foot.
rest|Dorsal digital branches of deep fib.destino: Adjacent sides of the 1st and 2nd toes
rest|Dorsal digital branches of deep fib.territorio: Sensory: skin of the adjacent sides of the great toe and second toe (first space).
rest|Dorsal digital branches of deep fib.clinica: Anesthesia of the first interdigital space indicates a deep fibular nerve injury.

rest|Dorsal digital branches of radial n.es: Dorsal digital nerves of the radial nerve
rest|Dorsal digital branches of radial n.descripcion: Terminal branches of the superficial branch of the radial nerve on the dorsum of the hand and lateral digits.
rest|Dorsal digital branches of radial n.origen: Superficial branch of the radial nerve
rest|Dorsal digital branches of radial n.destino: Dorsum of the thumb, index, middle and half of the ring finger up to the middle phalanx
rest|Dorsal digital branches of radial n.territorio: Sensory: dorsum of the lateral 3½ digits, except the nail beds.

rest|Dorsal digital branches of superfic.es: Dorsal digital nerves of the foot (superficial fibular nerve)
rest|Dorsal digital branches of superfic.descripcion: Terminal branches of the medial and intermediate dorsal cutaneous nerves on the dorsum of the toes.
rest|Dorsal digital branches of superfic.origen: Medial and intermediate dorsal cutaneous nerves of the foot
rest|Dorsal digital branches of superfic.territorio: Sensory: dorsum of the toes except the first space and the lateral border of the fifth.

rest|Dorsal digital branches of ulnar ne.es: Dorsal digital nerves of the ulnar nerve
rest|Dorsal digital branches of ulnar ne.descripcion: Terminal branches of the dorsal branch of the ulnar nerve on the medial dorsum of the hand.
rest|Dorsal digital branches of ulnar ne.origen: Dorsal branch of the ulnar nerve
rest|Dorsal digital branches of ulnar ne.destino: Dorsum of the little finger and medial half of the ring finger
rest|Dorsal digital branches of ulnar ne.territorio: Sensory: dorsal skin of the little finger and the medial half of the ring finger (and sometimes the middle finger).

rest|Dorsal scapular nerve.descripcion: Arises from the C5 root, pierces the middle scalene and descends deep to the levator scapulae and rhomboids along the medial border of the scapula.
rest|Dorsal scapular nerve.origen: C5 root of the brachial plexus
rest|Dorsal scapular nerve.territorio: Motor: rhomboid major and minor, levator scapulae.
rest|Dorsal scapular nerve.clinica: Its injury causes slight winging of the medial border of the scapula; useful for distinguishing a root lesion from a trunk lesion.

rest|Facial nerve (VII).descripcion: Emerges from the pontomedullary sulcus, runs through the internal acoustic meatus and the facial canal of the temporal bone, exits through the stylomastoid foramen and crosses the parotid gland.
rest|Facial nerve (VII).origen: Motor nucleus of the facial nerve, superior salivatory nucleus and nucleus of the solitary tract
rest|Facial nerve (VII).destino: Muscles of facial expression (intraparotid terminal branches)
rest|Facial nerve (VII).ramas: Greater petrosal nerve, nerve to the stapedius, chorda tympani, posterior auricular, temporal, zygomatic, buccal, marginal mandibular and cervical branches
rest|Facial nerve (VII).territorio: Motor: facial expression, stapedius, stylohyoid, posterior belly of the digastric. Taste of the anterior 2/3 of the tongue; sensation of part of the auricle.
rest|Facial nerve (VII).funcion: Secretomotor to the lacrimal, nasal, submandibular and sublingual glands.
rest|Facial nerve (VII).clinica: Bell's palsy: peripheral facial paralysis of the entire hemiface; central paralysis spares the forehead.

rest|Femoral branch of genitofemoral ner.es: Femoral branch of the genitofemoral nerve
rest|Femoral branch of genitofemoral ner.descripcion: Passes beneath the inguinal ligament in the femoral sheath, lateral to the femoral artery, and pierces the fascia at the saphenous opening.
rest|Femoral branch of genitofemoral ner.territorio: Sensory: skin of the upper anterior thigh over the femoral triangle.
rest|Femoral branch of genitofemoral ner.clinica: Afferent limb of the cremasteric reflex.

rest|Femoral nerve.descripcion: Largest branch of the lumbar plexus; it descends between the psoas and iliacus, passes beneath the inguinal ligament lateral to the femoral artery and branches in the femoral triangle.
rest|Femoral nerve.ramas: Muscular branches, anterior cutaneous branches, saphenous nerve, articular branches
rest|Femoral nerve.territorio: Motor: iliacus, pectineus, sartorius and quadriceps femoris. Sensory: anterior aspect of the thigh and medial aspect of the leg and foot (saphenous).
rest|Femoral nerve.clinica: Its injury abolishes the patellar reflex and knee extension; it may be affected by a psoas hematoma.

rest|Ganglia of sympathetic trunk.descripcion: Chain of paravertebral ganglia on both sides of the vertebral column, from the base of the skull to the coccyx (cervical, thoracic, lumbar, sacral and ganglion impar).
rest|Ganglia of sympathetic trunk.origen: Preganglionic fibers from T1–L2 via white rami communicantes
rest|Ganglia of sympathetic trunk.destino: Gray rami communicantes, splanchnic and visceral nerves
rest|Ganglia of sympathetic trunk.ramas: Gray rami communicantes, cardiac nerves, thoracic and lumbar splanchnic nerves
rest|Ganglia of sympathetic trunk.territorio: Sympathetic innervation of vessels, sweat glands and arrector pili muscles throughout the body and of the viscera.
rest|Ganglia of sympathetic trunk.funcion: They contain postganglionic sympathetic neurons (fight-or-flight response).
rest|Ganglia of sympathetic trunk.clinica: Injury to the cervicothoracic (stellate) ganglion produces Horner syndrome.

rest|Genital branch of genitofemoral ner.es: Genital branch of the genitofemoral nerve
rest|Genital branch of genitofemoral ner.descripcion: Enters through the deep inguinal ring and runs through the inguinal canal with the spermatic cord or the round ligament.
rest|Genital branch of genitofemoral ner.territorio: Motor: cremaster muscle. Sensory: anterior skin of the scrotum or of the mons pubis and labium majus.
rest|Genital branch of genitofemoral ner.clinica: Efferent limb of the cremasteric reflex; it may be injured in inguinal hernia repairs.

rest|Genitofemoral nerve.descripcion: Branch of the lumbar plexus that pierces the psoas major and descends on its anterior surface, dividing into genital and femoral branches.
rest|Genitofemoral nerve.territorio: Motor: cremaster. Sensory: scrotum/labium majus and skin of the femoral triangle.
rest|Genitofemoral nerve.clinica: Genitofemoral neuralgia after inguinal surgery or appendectomy.

rest|Glossopharyngeal nerve (IX).descripcion: Emerges from the retro-olivary sulcus of the medulla, exits through the jugular foramen and descends between the internal and external carotid arteries toward the pharynx and tongue.
rest|Glossopharyngeal nerve (IX).origen: Nucleus ambiguus, inferior salivatory nucleus, nucleus of the solitary tract and spinal nucleus of the trigeminal
rest|Glossopharyngeal nerve (IX).destino: Posterior third of the tongue and pharynx
rest|Glossopharyngeal nerve (IX).ramas: Tympanic nerve, carotid sinus branch, pharyngeal branches, branch to the stylopharyngeus, tonsillar and lingual branches
rest|Glossopharyngeal nerve (IX).territorio: Motor: stylopharyngeus. General sensation and taste of the posterior third of the tongue; pharynx, tonsil, middle ear; carotid sinus and body.
rest|Glossopharyngeal nerve (IX).funcion: Secretomotor to the parotid (via the otic ganglion); baroreceptor and chemoreceptor afferents.
rest|Glossopharyngeal nerve (IX).clinica: Afferent limb of the gag reflex; its injury abolishes it together with loss of taste in the posterior third.

rest|Hypoglossal nerve (XII).descripcion: Emerges from the preolivary sulcus of the medulla, exits through the hypoglossal canal, crosses lateral to the carotids and enters the tongue over the hyoglossus.
rest|Hypoglossal nerve (XII).ramas: Lingual branches (carries C1 fibers for the superior root of the ansa cervicalis and thyrohyoid)
rest|Hypoglossal nerve (XII).territorio: Motor: all intrinsic and extrinsic muscles of the tongue except the palatoglossus.
rest|Hypoglossal nerve (XII).clinica: In peripheral injury the protruded tongue deviates toward the injured side, with atrophy and fasciculations.

rest|Ilio-inguinal nerve.descripcion: Branch of L1 that crosses the quadratus lumborum, pierces the transversus abdominis and internal oblique and runs through the inguinal canal to the superficial ring.
rest|Ilio-inguinal nerve.destino: Skin of the inguinal and genital region
rest|Ilio-inguinal nerve.territorio: Motor: internal oblique and transversus (lower fibers). Sensory: upper medial thigh, root of the penis and anterior scrotum or mons pubis and labium majus.
rest|Ilio-inguinal nerve.clinica: Injured in inguinal hernia repairs and Pfannenstiel incisions: inguinal pain or anesthesia.

rest|Iliohypogastric nerve.descripcion: Branch of L1 that crosses the quadratus lumborum, pierces the transversus abdominis and runs between it and the internal oblique over the iliac crest.
rest|Iliohypogastric nerve.ramas: Lateral cutaneous branch, anterior cutaneous branch
rest|Iliohypogastric nerve.territorio: Motor: internal oblique and transversus abdominis. Sensory: skin of the superolateral gluteal and suprapubic regions.
rest|Iliohypogastric nerve.clinica: Vulnerable in low abdominal incisions; its injury weakens the wall and predisposes to direct inguinal hernias.

rest|Inferior alveolar nerve.descripcion: Branch of the posterior trunk of the mandibular nerve that enters through the mandibular foramen and runs through the mandibular canal, exiting as the mental nerve.
rest|Inferior alveolar nerve.ramas: Nerve to mylohyoid, inferior dental branches, mental nerve, incisive branch
rest|Inferior alveolar nerve.territorio: Motor (via the mylohyoid nerve): mylohyoid and anterior belly of the digastric. Sensory: lower teeth, skin of the chin and lower lip.
rest|Inferior alveolar nerve.clinica: Blocked at the lingula for dental anesthesia; injured in third molar extractions (lip paresthesia).

rest|Inferior lateral brachial cutaneous.descripcion: Branch of the radial nerve in the arm that pierces the lateral head of the triceps below the deltoid.
rest|Inferior lateral brachial cutaneous.territorio: Sensory: skin of the lateral aspect of the lower half of the arm.

rest|Inferior subscapular nerve.descripcion: Branch of the posterior cord that descends over the subscapularis to the teres major.
rest|Inferior subscapular nerve.origen: Posterior cord of the brachial plexus (C5–C6)
rest|Inferior subscapular nerve.territorio: Motor: lower portion of the subscapularis and teres major.

rest|Inferior trunk of brachial plexus.es: Inferior trunk of the brachial plexus
rest|Inferior trunk of brachial plexus.descripcion: Formed by the union of the C8 and T1 roots behind the anterior scalene, resting on the first rib.
rest|Inferior trunk of brachial plexus.territorio: Contributes to the ulnar, median (medial portion), radial and medial cutaneous nerves of the arm and forearm.
rest|Inferior trunk of brachial plexus.clinica: Klumpke's palsy (traction of the arm in abduction): claw hand and possible Horner syndrome; affected in thoracic outlet syndrome.

rest|Infrapatellar branch of saphenous n.es: Infrapatellar branch of the saphenous nerve
rest|Infrapatellar branch of saphenous n.descripcion: Branch of the saphenous nerve that pierces the sartorius and fascia lata and runs laterally below the patella.
rest|Infrapatellar branch of saphenous n.territorio: Sensory: anterior skin of the knee and infrapatellar region.
rest|Infrapatellar branch of saphenous n.clinica: Frequently injured in arthroscopies and medial approaches to the knee: anterolateral hypoesthesia of the knee.

rest|Intercostal nerves.descripcion: Ventral rami of T1–T11 that run through the intercostal space in the costal groove, between the internal and innermost intercostals, below the vein and artery.
rest|Intercostal nerves.origen: Ventral rami of spinal nerves T1–T11
rest|Intercostal nerves.destino: Skin of the anterior wall of the thorax and abdomen (T7–T11)
rest|Intercostal nerves.ramas: Collateral branches, lateral and anterior cutaneous branches, muscular branches
rest|Intercostal nerves.territorio: Motor: intercostals, subcostals, transversus thoracis, serratus posterior and muscles of the abdominal wall (T7–T11). Sensory: thoracic dermatomes and parietal pleura.
rest|Intercostal nerves.clinica: The intercostal block is performed below the lower border of the rib; thoracentesis is performed along the upper border.

rest|Intermediate dorsal cutaneous nerve.es: Intermediate dorsal cutaneous nerve of the foot
rest|Intermediate dorsal cutaneous nerve.descripcion: Lateral terminal branch of the superficial fibular nerve that crosses the ankle to the lateral dorsum of the foot.
rest|Intermediate dorsal cutaneous nerve.ramas: Dorsal digital nerves of the foot
rest|Intermediate dorsal cutaneous nerve.territorio: Sensory: lateral dorsum of the foot and adjacent sides of toes 3 to 5.

rest|Lateral antebrachial cutaneous nerv.descripcion: Continuation of the musculocutaneous nerve that emerges lateral to the biceps tendon at the elbow and descends alongside the cephalic vein.
rest|Lateral antebrachial cutaneous nerv.destino: Lateral skin of the forearm down to the thenar eminence
rest|Lateral antebrachial cutaneous nerv.territorio: Sensory: skin of the lateral (radial) aspect of the forearm.
rest|Lateral antebrachial cutaneous nerv.clinica: May be injured in venipuncture of the cephalic vein at the elbow.

rest|Lateral femoral cutaneous nerve.descripcion: Branch of the lumbar plexus that crosses the iliacus and passes beneath or through the inguinal ligament, medial to the anterior superior iliac spine.
rest|Lateral femoral cutaneous nerve.territorio: Sensory: skin of the anterolateral aspect of the thigh down to the knee.
rest|Lateral femoral cutaneous nerve.clinica: Its entrapment beneath the inguinal ligament produces meralgia paresthetica (obesity, tight belts, pregnancy).

rest|Lateral pectoral nerve.descripcion: Branch of the lateral cord that pierces the clavipectoral fascia alongside the thoracoacromial artery.
rest|Lateral pectoral nerve.origen: Lateral cord of the brachial plexus (C5–C7)
rest|Lateral pectoral nerve.ramas: Pectoral loop (with the medial pectoral nerve)
rest|Lateral pectoral nerve.territorio: Motor: pectoralis major, especially its clavicular portion; contributes to the pectoralis minor via the pectoral loop.

rest|Lateral plantar nerve.descripcion: Terminal branch of the tibial nerve that crosses the sole obliquely between the flexor digitorum brevis and quadratus plantae, dividing into superficial and deep branches.
rest|Lateral plantar nerve.ramas: Superficial branch, deep branch, branches to quadratus plantae and abductor digiti minimi
rest|Lateral plantar nerve.territorio: Motor: almost all intrinsic plantar muscles except abductor hallucis, flexor digitorum brevis, flexor hallucis brevis and 1st lumbrical. Sensory: lateral sole and lateral 1½ toes.
rest|Lateral plantar nerve.clinica: Its first branch (Baxter's nerve) may be entrapped and cause plantar heel pain.

rest|Lingual nerve.descripcion: Branch of the posterior trunk of the mandibular nerve that descends between the pterygoids, receives the chorda tympani, contacts the third molar and crosses the submandibular duct.
rest|Lingual nerve.destino: Mucosa of the anterior two thirds of the tongue
rest|Lingual nerve.ramas: Lingual branches, branches to the submandibular ganglion, sublingual branch
rest|Lingual nerve.territorio: General sensory: anterior two thirds of the tongue, floor of the mouth and lingual gingiva of the lower teeth. Carries taste and parasympathetic fibers from the chorda tympani.
rest|Lingual nerve.clinica: Injured in lower third molar extractions: anesthesia and loss of taste in the anterior half of the tongue.

rest|Long thoracic nerve.descripcion: Arises from roots C5–C7, descends behind the plexus and runs along the lateral surface of the serratus anterior in the midaxillary line.
rest|Long thoracic nerve.origen: Roots C5–C7 of the brachial plexus
rest|Long thoracic nerve.clinica: Its injury (mastectomy, trauma, carrying loads on the shoulder) produces medial winging of the scapula when pushing against a wall.

rest|Maxillary nerve.descripcion: Second division of the trigeminal nerve; it runs along the lateral wall of the cavernous sinus, exits through the foramen rotundum into the pterygopalatine fossa and continues as the infraorbital nerve.
rest|Maxillary nerve.ramas: Meningeal branch, zygomatic nerve, ganglionic branches, posterior superior alveolar nerves, infraorbital nerve
rest|Maxillary nerve.territorio: Sensory: skin of the cheek, lower eyelid, upper lip and side of the nose; upper teeth, maxillary sinus, palate and nasal cavity.
rest|Maxillary nerve.clinica: Trigeminal neuralgia frequently affects V2; fractures of the orbital floor damage the infraorbital nerve.

rest|Medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve.descripcion: Branch of the medial cord that descends medial to the brachial artery, pierces the fascia alongside the basilic vein and divides into anterior and posterior branches.
rest|Medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve.origen: Medial cord of the brachial plexus (C8–T1)
rest|Medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve.territorio: Sensory: skin of the medial aspect of the forearm down to the wrist and skin over the biceps.
rest|Medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve.clinica: May be affected in cubital tunnel surgery and in venipuncture of the basilic vein.

rest|Medial brachial cutaneous nerve.descripcion: Smallest branch of the brachial plexus; it descends through the axilla medial to the axillary vein and communicates with the intercostobrachial nerve.
rest|Medial brachial cutaneous nerve.origen: Medial cord of the brachial plexus (C8–T1)
rest|Medial brachial cutaneous nerve.territorio: Sensory: skin of the medial aspect of the distal third of the arm.

rest|Medial crural cutaneous branches of.es: Medial crural cutaneous branches of the saphenous nerve
rest|Medial crural cutaneous branches of.la: Rami cutanei cruris mediales nervi sapheni
rest|Medial crural cutaneous branches of.descripcion: Branches of the saphenous nerve distributed on the medial aspect of the leg, accompanying the great saphenous vein.
rest|Medial crural cutaneous branches of.territorio: Sensory: skin of the medial and anteromedial aspects of the leg.
rest|Medial crural cutaneous branches of.clinica: They may be injured in great saphenous vein stripping (saphenectomy).

rest|Medial dorsal cutaneous nerve of fo.es: Medial dorsal cutaneous nerve of the foot
rest|Medial dorsal cutaneous nerve of fo.descripcion: Medial terminal branch of the superficial fibular nerve that crosses the front of the ankle to the medial dorsum of the foot.
rest|Medial dorsal cutaneous nerve of fo.ramas: Dorsal digital nerves of the foot
rest|Medial dorsal cutaneous nerve of fo.territorio: Sensory: medial dorsum of the foot and great toe, and adjacent sides of toes 2 and 3.

rest|Medial pectoral nerve.descripcion: Branch of the medial cord that passes between the axillary artery and vein and pierces the pectoralis minor to reach the pectoralis major.
rest|Medial pectoral nerve.origen: Medial cord of the brachial plexus (C8–T1)
rest|Medial pectoral nerve.territorio: Motor: pectoralis minor and sternocostal portion of the pectoralis major.

rest|Medial plantar nerve.descripcion: Larger terminal branch of the tibial nerve; it runs beneath the abductor hallucis and between it and the flexor digitorum brevis.
rest|Medial plantar nerve.ramas: Muscular branches, proper plantar digital nerve of the great toe, common plantar digital nerves
rest|Medial plantar nerve.territorio: Motor: abductor hallucis, flexor digitorum brevis, flexor hallucis brevis, 1st lumbrical. Sensory: medial sole and medial 3½ toes.
rest|Medial plantar nerve.clinica: Affected in tarsal tunnel syndrome (medial plantar paresthesias).

rest|Medial sural cutaneous nerve.descripcion: Branch of the tibial nerve in the popliteal fossa that descends between the heads of the gastrocnemius and joins the fibular communicating branch to form the sural nerve.
rest|Medial sural cutaneous nerve.territorio: Sensory: posterior skin of the leg (via the sural nerve).

rest|Median nerve.descripcion: Formed by roots from the lateral and medial cords; it descends with the brachial artery, crosses the cubital fossa, passes between the heads of the pronator teres and enters the hand through the carpal tunnel.
rest|Median nerve.origen: Lateral and medial cords of the brachial plexus (C6–T1)
rest|Median nerve.destino: Recurrent thenar branch and palmar digital nerves
rest|Median nerve.ramas: Muscular branches, anterior interosseous nerve, palmar branch, recurrent branch, common palmar digital nerves
rest|Median nerve.territorio: Motor: almost all forearm flexors, pronators, thenar muscles (abductor pollicis brevis, opponens, flexor brevis) and lumbricals 1–2. Sensory: lateral palm and lateral 3½ digits.
rest|Median nerve.clinica: Carpal tunnel syndrome: nocturnal paresthesias, positive Tinel and Phalen signs; high lesion: benediction hand.

rest|Meningeal branch of maxillary nerve.es: Meningeal branch of the maxillary nerve
rest|Meningeal branch of maxillary nerve.descripcion: Branch that arises from the maxillary nerve in the middle cranial fossa before the foramen rotundum, accompanying the middle meningeal artery.
rest|Meningeal branch of maxillary nerve.destino: Dura mater of the middle cranial fossa
rest|Meningeal branch of maxillary nerve.territorio: Sensory: dura mater of the middle cranial fossa.

rest|Mental nerve.descripcion: Terminal branch of the inferior alveolar nerve that emerges through the mental foramen, at the level of the lower second premolar.
rest|Mental nerve.destino: Skin of the chin and lower lip
rest|Mental nerve.ramas: Mental, inferior labial and gingival branches
rest|Mental nerve.territorio: Sensory: skin of the chin, skin and mucosa of the lower lip and anterior vestibular gingiva.
rest|Mental nerve.clinica: Numb chin sign (Roger): mental hypoesthesia that may indicate mandibular metastasis.

rest|Middle trunk of brachial plexus.es: Middle trunk of the brachial plexus
rest|Middle trunk of brachial plexus.descripcion: Continuation of the ventral ramus of C7 between the anterior and middle scalenes.
rest|Middle trunk of brachial plexus.territorio: Contributes to the radial, median and musculocutaneous nerves (via cords).

rest|Motor nucleus of facial nerve.es: Motor nucleus of the facial nerve
rest|Motor nucleus of facial nerve.descripcion: Nucleus in the reticular formation of the caudal pons; its axons loop around the abducens nucleus (internal genu, facial colliculus).
rest|Motor nucleus of facial nerve.territorio: Motor: muscles of facial expression, stapedius, stylohyoid and posterior belly of the digastric.
rest|Motor nucleus of facial nerve.clinica: The portion that innervates the forehead receives bilateral corticobulbar projection: central lesions spare the forehead.

rest|Motor root of trigeminal nerve.es: Motor root of the trigeminal nerve
rest|Motor root of trigeminal nerve.descripcion: Smaller root that emerges from the pons, passes beneath the trigeminal ganglion and joins the mandibular nerve at the foramen ovale.
rest|Motor root of trigeminal nerve.territorio: Motor: muscles of mastication (masseter, temporalis, pterygoids), mylohyoid, anterior belly of the digastric, tensor tympani and tensor veli palatini.
rest|Motor root of trigeminal nerve.clinica: Its injury produces deviation of the mandible toward the injured side on opening the mouth.

rest|Muscular branches of axillary nerve.es: Muscular branches of the axillary nerve
rest|Muscular branches of axillary nerve.descripcion: Motor branches of the axillary nerve after passing through the quadrangular space.

rest|Muscular branches of deep fibular n.es: Muscular branches of the deep fibular nerve
rest|Muscular branches of deep fibular n.descripcion: Motor branches of the deep fibular nerve in the anterior compartment of the leg and dorsum of the foot.
rest|Muscular branches of deep fibular n.destino: Muscles of the anterior compartment and short extensors
rest|Muscular branches of deep fibular n.territorio: Motor: tibialis anterior, extensor digitorum longus, extensor hallucis longus, fibularis tertius, extensor digitorum brevis and extensor hallucis brevis.
rest|Muscular branches of deep fibular n.clinica: Its deficit produces foot drop (loss of dorsiflexion).

rest|Muscular branches of median nerve.es: Muscular branches of the median nerve
rest|Muscular branches of median nerve.descripcion: Motor branches of the median nerve in the cubital fossa and proximal forearm.
rest|Muscular branches of median nerve.destino: Superficial flexor muscles of the forearm
rest|Muscular branches of median nerve.territorio: Motor: pronator teres, flexor carpi radialis, palmaris longus, flexor digitorum superficialis.
rest|Muscular branches of median nerve.clinica: Pronator syndrome: compression of the median nerve between the heads of the pronator teres.

rest|Muscular branches of radial nerve.es: Muscular branches of the radial nerve
rest|Muscular branches of radial nerve.descripcion: Motor branches of the radial nerve in the axilla, radial groove and lateral region of the elbow.
rest|Muscular branches of radial nerve.destino: Triceps, anconeus, brachioradialis and extensor carpi radialis longus
rest|Muscular branches of radial nerve.territorio: Motor: triceps brachii, anconeus, brachioradialis, extensor carpi radialis longus (and lateral part of the brachialis).
rest|Muscular branches of radial nerve.clinica: In humeral shaft fractures the triceps branches are usually preserved (they arise proximally).

rest|Muscular branches of ulnar nerve.es: Muscular branches of the ulnar nerve
rest|Muscular branches of ulnar nerve.descripcion: Motor branches of the ulnar nerve in the proximal forearm after passing between the heads of the flexor carpi ulnaris.
rest|Muscular branches of ulnar nerve.destino: Flexor carpi ulnaris and flexor digitorum profundus
rest|Muscular branches of ulnar nerve.territorio: Motor: flexor carpi ulnaris and medial half of the flexor digitorum profundus (IV–V).

rest|Musculocutaneous nerve.descripcion: Terminal branch of the lateral cord that pierces the coracobrachialis and descends between the biceps and brachialis.
rest|Musculocutaneous nerve.origen: Lateral cord of the brachial plexus (C5–C7)
rest|Musculocutaneous nerve.ramas: Muscular branches, lateral antebrachial cutaneous nerve
rest|Musculocutaneous nerve.territorio: Motor: coracobrachialis, biceps brachii and brachialis. Sensory: lateral skin of the forearm.
rest|Musculocutaneous nerve.clinica: Its injury weakens elbow flexion and supination, with loss of the biceps reflex.

rest|Nerve to mylohyoid muscle.descripcion: Branch of the inferior alveolar nerve before the mandibular foramen; it descends along the mylohyoid groove of the mandible.
rest|Nerve to mylohyoid muscle.destino: Mylohyoid and anterior belly of the digastric
rest|Nerve to mylohyoid muscle.territorio: Motor: mylohyoid and anterior belly of the digastric.

rest|Nerve to piriformis muscle.descripcion: Short branch of the sacral plexus that enters the anterior surface of the piriformis directly within the pelvis.

rest|Nerve to quadratus femoris muscle.es: Nerve to the quadratus femoris muscle
rest|Nerve to quadratus femoris muscle.descripcion: Exits through the greater sciatic foramen beneath the piriformis, deep to the sciatic nerve, and descends behind the hip joint.
rest|Nerve to quadratus femoris muscle.territorio: Motor: quadratus femoris and inferior gemellus.

rest|Nucleus of abducens nerve.descripcion: Motor nucleus of the caudal pons beneath the facial colliculus, surrounded by the fibers of the facial nerve.
rest|Nucleus of abducens nerve.territorio: Motor: lateral rectus; its interneurons project to the contralateral oculomotor nucleus via the medial longitudinal fasciculus.
rest|Nucleus of abducens nerve.clinica: Its injury produces paralysis of horizontal gaze toward the same side, often with facial paralysis.

rest|Nucleus of accessory nerve.descripcion: Column of motor neurons in the anterior horn of spinal cord segments C1–C5.

rest|Nucleus of hypoglossal nerve.descripcion: Motor nucleus of the medulla oblongata, next to the midline beneath the hypoglossal trigone of the floor of the fourth ventricle.
rest|Nucleus of hypoglossal nerve.territorio: Motor: muscles of the tongue (except palatoglossus).
rest|Nucleus of hypoglossal nerve.clinica: Affected in medial medullary syndrome (Dejerine): tongue deviation toward the lesion and contralateral hemiplegia.

rest|Nucleus of oculomotor nerve.descripcion: Nuclear complex in the midbrain at the level of the superior colliculus, ventral to the aqueduct.
rest|Nucleus of oculomotor nerve.territorio: Motor: levator palpebrae, superior, medial and inferior recti and inferior oblique.
rest|Nucleus of oculomotor nerve.clinica: The levator subnucleus is single and central: nuclear lesions cause bilateral ptosis.

rest|Nucleus of trochlear nerve.descripcion: Nucleus of the midbrain at the level of the inferior colliculus, ventral to the aqueduct; its fibers decussate in the superior medullary velum.
rest|Nucleus of trochlear nerve.clinica: A nuclear lesion affects the superior oblique of the opposite side.

rest|Obturator nerve.descripcion: Branch of the lumbar plexus that emerges medial to the psoas, runs along the lateral wall of the pelvis and passes through the obturator canal into the medial thigh.
rest|Obturator nerve.ramas: Anterior branch, posterior branch, articular branches
rest|Obturator nerve.territorio: Motor: adductors longus, brevis and magnus (adductor portion), gracilis, obturator externus (± pectineus). Sensory: medial skin of the thigh.
rest|Obturator nerve.clinica: May be injured in pelvic surgery or childbirth: weakness of adduction and circumduction gait.

rest|Oculomotor nerve (III).descripcion: Emerges from the interpeduncular fossa, passes between the posterior cerebral and superior cerebellar arteries, runs along the lateral wall of the cavernous sinus and enters the orbit through the superior orbital fissure.
rest|Oculomotor nerve (III).ramas: Superior branch, inferior branch (with the parasympathetic root of the ciliary ganglion)
rest|Oculomotor nerve (III).territorio: Motor: levator palpebrae superioris, superior, medial and inferior recti, inferior oblique. Parasympathetic: pupillary sphincter and ciliary muscle.
rest|Oculomotor nerve (III).funcion: Miosis and accommodation (via the ciliary ganglion).
rest|Oculomotor nerve (III).clinica: Injury: ptosis, 'down and out' eye and mydriasis; a posterior communicating artery aneurysm affects the pupil first.

rest|Olfactory nerve (I).descripcion: Set of olfactory filaments that arise in the olfactory mucosa of the nasal roof and cross the cribriform plate of the ethmoid to the olfactory bulb.
rest|Olfactory nerve (I).origen: Olfactory receptor neurons of the nasal mucosa
rest|Olfactory nerve (I).clinica: Fractures of the cribriform plate cause anosmia and CSF rhinorrhea.

rest|Ophthalmic nerve.descripcion: First division of the trigeminal nerve, purely sensory; it runs along the lateral wall of the cavernous sinus and enters the orbit through the superior orbital fissure.
rest|Ophthalmic nerve.ramas: Lacrimal, frontal and nasociliary nerves; tentorial branch
rest|Ophthalmic nerve.territorio: Sensory: eyeball, cornea, conjunctiva, upper eyelid, nasal dorsum, forehead and scalp up to the vertex.
rest|Ophthalmic nerve.clinica: Afferent limb of the corneal reflex; herpes zoster ophthalmicus with a lesion on the tip of the nose (Hutchinson's sign) suggests ocular involvement.

rest|Optic nerve (II).descripcion: CNS tract formed by axons of the retinal ganglion cells; it crosses the orbit and the optic canal to the optic chiasm. Surrounded by meninges.
rest|Optic nerve (II).clinica: Afferent limb of the pupillary light reflex; papilledema reflects intracranial hypertension and optic neuritis is typical of multiple sclerosis.

rest|Palmar branch of median nerve.es: Palmar branch of the median nerve
rest|Palmar branch of median nerve.descripcion: Arises from the median nerve proximal to the wrist and passes superficial to the flexor retinaculum, outside the carpal tunnel.
rest|Palmar branch of median nerve.destino: Skin of the central palm and thenar eminence
rest|Palmar branch of median nerve.territorio: Sensory: skin of the central part of the palm and the thenar eminence.
rest|Palmar branch of median nerve.clinica: Spared in carpal tunnel syndrome: sensation of the central palm is preserved.

rest|Palmar branch of ulnar nerve.es: Palmar branch of the ulnar nerve
rest|Palmar branch of ulnar nerve.descripcion: Arises in the distal forearm and descends anterior to the ulnar artery, superficial to the flexor retinaculum.
rest|Palmar branch of ulnar nerve.territorio: Sensory: skin of the medial part of the palm (hypothenar eminence).

rest|Posterior antebrachial cutaneous ne.descripcion: Branch of the radial nerve in the radial groove that pierces the lateral head of the triceps and descends along the back of the forearm.
rest|Posterior antebrachial cutaneous ne.destino: Posterior skin of the forearm down to the wrist
rest|Posterior antebrachial cutaneous ne.territorio: Sensory: skin of the posterior aspect of the forearm (and inferolateral part of the arm).

rest|Posterior branch of medial antebrac.es: Ulnar (posterior) branch of the medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve
rest|Posterior branch of medial antebrac.la: Ramus ulnaris nervi cutanei antebrachii medialis
rest|Posterior branch of medial antebrac.descripcion: Branch that descends along the posteromedial aspect of the forearm, anterior to the medial epicondyle, down to the wrist.
rest|Posterior branch of medial antebrac.territorio: Sensory: skin of the posteromedial aspect of the forearm.
rest|Posterior branch of medial antebrac.clinica: May be injured in cubital tunnel surgery (painful neuroma).

rest|Posterior branch of obturator nerve.es: Posterior branch of the obturator nerve
rest|Posterior branch of obturator nerve.descripcion: Passes through the obturator externus and descends between the adductor brevis and adductor magnus.
rest|Posterior branch of obturator nerve.ramas: Muscular branches, articular branch of the knee
rest|Posterior branch of obturator nerve.territorio: Motor: obturator externus, adductor magnus (adductor portion) and sometimes adductor brevis.
rest|Posterior branch of obturator nerve.clinica: Its articular branch explains hip pain referred to the knee.

rest|Posterior cord of brachial plexus.es: Posterior cord of the brachial plexus
rest|Posterior cord of brachial plexus.descripcion: Formed by the three posterior divisions; it lies behind the second part of the axillary artery.
rest|Posterior cord of brachial plexus.origen: Posterior divisions of the superior, middle and inferior trunks (C5–T1)
rest|Posterior cord of brachial plexus.ramas: Superior and inferior subscapular nerves, thoracodorsal, axillary, radial
rest|Posterior cord of brachial plexus.territorio: Motor: extensor muscles of the upper limb, deltoid, subscapularis, teres major, latissimus dorsi. Sensory: posterior aspect of the upper limb.
rest|Posterior cord of brachial plexus.clinica: May be compressed by poorly fitted axillary crutches (crutch palsy).

rest|Posterior division of inferior trun.es: Posterior division of the inferior trunk of the brachial plexus
rest|Posterior division of inferior trun.la: Divisio posterior trunci inferioris plexus brachialis
rest|Posterior division of inferior trun.descripcion: Division of the inferior trunk (C8–T1) behind the clavicle; it is the smallest and joins the posterior cord.
rest|Posterior division of inferior trun.origen: Inferior trunk of the brachial plexus
rest|Posterior division of inferior trun.territorio: Fibers for the extensor compartment of the upper limb.

rest|Posterior division of mandibular ne.es: Posterior trunk of the mandibular nerve
rest|Posterior division of mandibular ne.descripcion: Larger, predominantly sensory division of the mandibular nerve in the infratemporal fossa.
rest|Posterior division of mandibular ne.ramas: Auriculotemporal, lingual and inferior alveolar nerves (with the mylohyoid nerve)
rest|Posterior division of mandibular ne.territorio: Sensory: temporal region, tongue (anterior 2/3), lower teeth, chin. Motor (mylohyoid): mylohyoid and anterior belly of the digastric.

rest|Posterior division of middle trunk.es: Posterior division of the middle trunk of the brachial plexus
rest|Posterior division of middle trunk.la: Divisio posterior trunci medii plexus brachialis
rest|Posterior division of middle trunk.descripcion: Division of the middle trunk (C7) behind the clavicle that joins the posterior cord.
rest|Posterior division of middle trunk.origen: Middle trunk of the brachial plexus
rest|Posterior division of middle trunk.territorio: Fibers for the extensor compartment of the upper limb.

rest|Posterior division of superior trun.es: Posterior division of the superior trunk of the brachial plexus
rest|Posterior division of superior trun.la: Divisio posterior trunci superioris plexus brachialis
rest|Posterior division of superior trun.descripcion: Division of the superior trunk (C5–C6) behind the clavicle that forms part of the posterior cord.
rest|Posterior division of superior trun.origen: Superior trunk of the brachial plexus
rest|Posterior division of superior trun.territorio: Fibers for the deltoid, teres minor, subscapularis and extensors.

rest|Posterior femoral cutaneous nerve.descripcion: Leaves the pelvis through the greater sciatic foramen beneath the piriformis and descends beneath the fascia lata on the posterior thigh to the popliteal fossa.
rest|Posterior femoral cutaneous nerve.destino: Skin of the popliteal fossa and proximal calf
rest|Posterior femoral cutaneous nerve.territorio: Sensory: skin of the gluteal fold, lateral perineum, posterior thigh and upper calf.

rest|Posterior interosseous nerve of for.es: Posterior interosseous nerve of the forearm
rest|Posterior interosseous nerve of for.descripcion: Continuation of the deep branch of the radial nerve after passing through the supinator; it descends between the superficial and deep extensors and over the interosseous membrane.
rest|Posterior interosseous nerve of for.origen: Deep branch of the radial nerve
rest|Posterior interosseous nerve of for.ramas: Muscular branches, articular branch of the wrist
rest|Posterior interosseous nerve of for.territorio: Motor: extensor digitorum, extensor digiti minimi, extensor carpi ulnaris, abductor pollicis longus and thumb extensors, extensor indicis. Sensory: wrist joints.
rest|Posterior interosseous nerve of for.clinica: Posterior interosseous syndrome: inability to extend the fingers, with wrist extension in radial deviation.

rest|Posterior nucleus of vagus nerve.es: Posterior nucleus of the vagus nerve
rest|Posterior nucleus of vagus nerve.descripcion: Preganglionic parasympathetic nucleus of the medulla beneath the vagal trigone in the floor of the fourth ventricle, lateral to the hypoglossal nucleus.
rest|Posterior nucleus of vagus nerve.territorio: Thoracic and abdominal viscera up to the left colic flexure (via intramural ganglia).
rest|Posterior nucleus of vagus nerve.funcion: Gastrointestinal motility and secretion, bronchoconstriction and parasympathetic cardiac effects.

rest|Posterior root of posterior femoral.es: Posterior root of the posterior femoral cutaneous nerve
rest|Posterior root of posterior femoral.la: Radix posterior nervi cutanei femoris posterioris
rest|Posterior root of posterior femoral.descripcion: Contribution of the posterior divisions of the ventral rami S1–S2 to the posterior femoral cutaneous nerve, within the pelvis.
rest|Posterior root of posterior femoral.territorio: Contributes fibers to the skin of the posterior thigh.

rest|Posterior root of spinal nerve.es: Posterior root of the spinal nerve
rest|Posterior root of spinal nerve.descripcion: Sensory root that enters the posterolateral sulcus of the spinal cord; it bears the spinal ganglion in the intervertebral foramen.
rest|Posterior root of spinal nerve.destino: Posterior horn and posterior columns of the spinal cord
rest|Posterior root of spinal nerve.territorio: Sensory: dermatome, proprioception and visceral afferents of the corresponding segment.
rest|Posterior root of spinal nerve.clinica: Its compression causes radicular pain and sensory disturbance in the dermatome (radiculopathy).

rest|Proper palmar digital branches of m.es: Proper palmar digital nerves of the median nerve
rest|Proper palmar digital branches of m.la: Nervi digitales palmares proprii nervi mediani
rest|Proper palmar digital branches of m.descripcion: Terminal branches that run along the palmar borders of the fingers and extend dorsally to the distal phalanges.
rest|Proper palmar digital branches of m.origen: Common palmar digital nerves of the median nerve
rest|Proper palmar digital branches of m.territorio: Sensory: palmar aspect of the thumb, index, middle and lateral half of the ring finger, plus the distal dorsum and nail beds.
rest|Proper palmar digital branches of m.clinica: Blocked in digital anesthesia (Oberst block) at the base of the finger.

rest|Proper palmar digital branches of u.es: Proper palmar digital nerves of the ulnar nerve
rest|Proper palmar digital branches of u.la: Nervi digitales palmares proprii nervi ulnaris
rest|Proper palmar digital branches of u.descripcion: Terminal branches of the superficial branch of the ulnar nerve along the borders of the little finger and medial half of the ring finger.
rest|Proper palmar digital branches of u.origen: Superficial branch of the ulnar nerve
rest|Proper palmar digital branches of u.destino: Finger pads of the little finger and medial ring finger
rest|Proper palmar digital branches of u.territorio: Sensory: palmar aspect and distal dorsum of the little finger and medial half of the ring finger.

rest|Proper plantar digital branches of.es: Proper plantar digital nerves of the lateral plantar nerve
rest|Proper plantar digital branches of.la: Nervi digitales plantares proprii nervi plantaris lateralis
rest|Proper plantar digital branches of.descripcion: Terminal branches for the borders of the fifth toe and the lateral side of the fourth.
rest|Proper plantar digital branches of.origen: Common plantar digital nerves of the lateral plantar nerve
rest|Proper plantar digital branches of.destino: Plantar skin of the 5th toe and lateral side of the 4th
rest|Proper plantar digital branches of.territorio: Sensory: plantar skin and nail beds of the fifth toe and lateral half of the fourth.

rest|Proper plantar digital branches of.es: Proper plantar digital nerves of the medial plantar nerve
rest|Proper plantar digital branches of.la: Nervi digitales plantares proprii nervi plantaris medialis
rest|Proper plantar digital branches of.descripcion: Terminal branches that run along the plantar borders of the medial toes.
rest|Proper plantar digital branches of.origen: Common plantar digital nerves of the medial plantar nerve
rest|Proper plantar digital branches of.destino: Plantar skin of toes 1–3 and medial side of the 4th
rest|Proper plantar digital branches of.territorio: Sensory: plantar skin and nail beds of the medial 3½ toes.

rest|Pudendal nerve.descripcion: Exits through the greater sciatic foramen, winds around the ischial spine and enters the perineum through the lesser sciatic foramen, running through the pudendal canal (Alcock).
rest|Pudendal nerve.destino: Dorsal nerve of the penis or clitoris
rest|Pudendal nerve.ramas: Inferior rectal nerves, perineal nerves, dorsal nerve of the penis/clitoris
rest|Pudendal nerve.territorio: Motor: external anal sphincter, external urethral sphincter and perineal muscles. Sensory: perineum, external genitalia and lower anal canal.
rest|Pudendal nerve.funcion: Voluntary urinary and fecal continence; sexual function.
rest|Pudendal nerve.clinica: Pudendal block at the ischial spine for childbirth; pudendal neuralgia in cyclists.

rest|Radial nerve.descripcion: Larger terminal branch of the posterior cord; it winds around the humerus in the radial groove with the deep brachial artery and divides in front of the lateral epicondyle.
rest|Radial nerve.origen: Posterior cord of the brachial plexus (C5–T1)
rest|Radial nerve.ramas: Muscular branches, posterior cutaneous nerve of the arm, inferior lateral cutaneous nerve of the arm and posterior cutaneous nerve of the forearm, superficial branch, deep branch
rest|Radial nerve.territorio: Motor: triceps, anconeus, brachioradialis and all extensors of the forearm. Sensory: posterior aspect of the arm and forearm and lateral dorsum of the hand.
rest|Radial nerve.clinica: Humeral shaft fracture or 'Saturday night palsy': wrist drop (dropped wrist).

rest|Roots of brachial plexus.descripcion: Ventral rami of C5–T1 that emerge between the anterior and middle scalenes and unite to form the trunks.
rest|Roots of brachial plexus.origen: Ventral rami of spinal nerves C5–T1
rest|Roots of brachial plexus.ramas: Dorsal scapular nerve (C5), long thoracic nerve (C5–C7), branch to the phrenic nerve
rest|Roots of brachial plexus.territorio: Motor and sensory innervation of the entire upper limb.
rest|Roots of brachial plexus.clinica: Preganglionic root avulsion is suggested by winged scapula, rhomboid paralysis or Horner syndrome.

rest|Saphenous nerve.descripcion: Longest sensory branch of the femoral nerve; it runs through the adductor canal, pierces the fascia between the sartorius and gracilis and descends with the great saphenous vein to the foot.
rest|Saphenous nerve.ramas: Infrapatellar branch, medial crural cutaneous branches
rest|Saphenous nerve.territorio: Sensory: medial skin of the knee, leg, ankle and medial border of the foot.
rest|Saphenous nerve.clinica: May be injured in saphenectomies or in the adductor canal (adductor canal block in knee surgery).

rest|Sciatic nerve.descripcion: Thickest nerve of the body; it exits through the greater sciatic foramen beneath the piriformis, descends the posterior thigh beneath the biceps femoris and divides above the popliteal fossa.
rest|Sciatic nerve.ramas: Branches to the hamstrings and adductor magnus, tibial nerve, common fibular nerve
rest|Sciatic nerve.territorio: Motor: hamstrings, ischial portion of the adductor magnus and all muscles of the leg and foot. Sensory: leg (except medial) and foot.
rest|Sciatic nerve.clinica: Intramuscular injections should be given in the superolateral quadrant of the buttock to avoid it; piriformis syndrome.

rest|Sensory root of trigeminal nerve.es: Sensory root of the trigeminal nerve
