rest|Sensory root of trigeminal nerve.descripcion: Larger root that connects the trigeminal ganglion to the pons, crossing the superior border of the petrous part of the temporal bone.
rest|Sensory root of trigeminal nerve.territorio: Sensory: face, oral and nasal mucosae, teeth, cornea and supratentorial dura mater.
rest|Sensory root of trigeminal nerve.clinica: Vascular compression of the root (superior cerebellar artery) causes trigeminal neuralgia; target of microvascular decompression.

rest|Spinal ganglion.es: Sensory ganglion of a spinal nerve
rest|Spinal ganglion.descripcion: Swelling of the posterior root in the intervertebral foramen that contains the cell bodies of the pseudounipolar sensory neurons.
rest|Spinal ganglion.origen: Posterior root of the spinal nerve
rest|Spinal ganglion.territorio: Somatic and visceral sensation of the segment (dermatome).
rest|Spinal ganglion.clinica: Site of latency of the varicella-zoster virus; its reactivation produces dermatomal herpes zoster.

rest|Subclavian nerve.descripcion: Small branch of the superior trunk that descends in front of the plexus and the subclavian artery.
rest|Subclavian nerve.origen: Superior trunk of the brachial plexus (C5–C6)
rest|Subclavian nerve.ramas: Accessory branch to the phrenic nerve (inconstant)
rest|Subclavian nerve.clinica: It may provide an accessory phrenic nerve, relevant in cervical surgery.

rest|Superficial branch of radial nerve.es: Superficial branch of the radial nerve
rest|Superficial branch of radial nerve.descripcion: Sensory branch that descends beneath the brachioradialis alongside the radial artery and emerges onto the dorsum of the wrist in the distal third of the forearm.
rest|Superficial branch of radial nerve.territorio: Sensory: lateral dorsum of the hand, anatomical snuffbox and dorsum of the lateral 3½ digits up to the middle phalanx.
rest|Superficial branch of radial nerve.clinica: Cheiralgia paresthetica (Wartenberg syndrome) from compression by watches or handcuffs.

rest|Superficial branch of ulnar nerve.es: Superficial branch of the ulnar nerve
rest|Superficial branch of ulnar nerve.descripcion: Branch of the ulnar nerve in Guyon's canal that runs beneath the palmaris brevis toward the medial palm.
rest|Superficial branch of ulnar nerve.ramas: Branch to the palmaris brevis, common and proper palmar digital nerves
rest|Superficial branch of ulnar nerve.territorio: Motor: palmaris brevis. Sensory: palmar skin of the little finger and medial half of the ring finger.

rest|Superficial fibular nerve.descripcion: Branch of the common fibular nerve that descends in the lateral compartment of the leg and pierces the crural fascia in the distal third.
rest|Superficial fibular nerve.destino: Medial and intermediate dorsal cutaneous nerves of the foot
rest|Superficial fibular nerve.ramas: Muscular branches, medial dorsal cutaneous nerve, intermediate dorsal cutaneous nerve
rest|Superficial fibular nerve.territorio: Motor: fibularis longus and brevis. Sensory: distal anterolateral skin of the leg and most of the dorsum of the foot.
rest|Superficial fibular nerve.clinica: Its injury weakens eversion; it may be entrapped where it pierces the crural fascia.

rest|Superior gluteal nerve.descripcion: Exits through the greater sciatic foramen above the piriformis with the superior gluteal vessels and runs between the gluteus medius and minimus.
rest|Superior gluteal nerve.territorio: Motor: gluteus medius, gluteus minimus and tensor fasciae latae.
rest|Superior gluteal nerve.clinica: Its injury produces a positive Trendelenburg sign (drop of the contralateral pelvis in single-leg stance).

rest|Superior lateral brachial cutaneous.descripcion: Cutaneous continuation of the posterior branch of the axillary nerve that winds around the posterior border of the deltoid.
rest|Superior lateral brachial cutaneous.destino: Skin over the lower portion of the deltoid
rest|Superior lateral brachial cutaneous.territorio: Sensory: skin of the lower deltoid region ('regimental badge' patch).
rest|Superior lateral brachial cutaneous.clinica: Its anesthesia is a useful sign of axillary nerve injury after shoulder dislocation.

rest|Superior subscapular nerve.descripcion: Short branch of the posterior cord that enters the upper portion of the subscapularis.
rest|Superior subscapular nerve.origen: Posterior cord of the brachial plexus (C5–C6)
rest|Superior subscapular nerve.territorio: Motor: upper portion of the subscapularis.

rest|Superior trunk of brachial plexus.es: Superior trunk of the brachial plexus
rest|Superior trunk of brachial plexus.descripcion: Formed by the union of the C5 and C6 roots at the lateral border of the middle scalene (Erb's point).
rest|Superior trunk of brachial plexus.ramas: Suprascapular nerve, subclavian nerve, anterior and posterior divisions
rest|Superior trunk of brachial plexus.territorio: Contributes to the suprascapular, musculocutaneous, axillary, radial and median (lateral portion) nerves.
rest|Superior trunk of brachial plexus.clinica: Erb-Duchenne palsy: arm in internal rotation and adduction with extended elbow ('waiter's tip').

rest|Suprascapular nerve.descripcion: Branch of the superior trunk that crosses the posterior cervical triangle and passes through the scapular notch beneath the superior transverse ligament.
rest|Suprascapular nerve.origen: Superior trunk of the brachial plexus (C5–C6)
rest|Suprascapular nerve.ramas: Branches to the supraspinatus, infraspinatus, and articular branches to the shoulder and acromioclavicular joints
rest|Suprascapular nerve.territorio: Motor: supraspinatus and infraspinatus. Sensory: glenohumeral and acromioclavicular joints.
rest|Suprascapular nerve.clinica: Its entrapment at the scapular or spinoglenoid notch causes atrophy of the supraspinatus and/or infraspinatus.

rest|Sural communicating branch of commo.es: Communicating branch of common fibular nerve
rest|Sural communicating branch of commo.la: Ramus communicans fibularis nervi fibularis communis
rest|Sural communicating branch of commo.descripcion: Branch of the common fibular nerve in the popliteal fossa that descends over the lateral head of the gastrocnemius to join the medial sural cutaneous nerve.
rest|Sural communicating branch of commo.territorio: Sensory: contributes to the territory of the sural nerve.

rest|Sural nerve.descripcion: Formed by the medial sural cutaneous nerve and the fibular communicating branch; descends with the small saphenous vein behind the lateral malleolus.
rest|Sural nerve.origen: Medial sural cutaneous nerve (tibial) and fibular communicating branch
rest|Sural nerve.destino: Lateral border of the foot and of the fifth toe (lateral dorsal cutaneous nerve)
rest|Sural nerve.ramas: Lateral calcaneal branches, lateral dorsal cutaneous nerve of the foot
rest|Sural nerve.territorio: Sensory: posterolateral skin of the distal leg, lateral heel and lateral border of the foot.
rest|Sural nerve.clinica: Usual site for nerve biopsy and a source of nerve grafts.

rest|Sympathetic nerves.descripcion: Sympathetic postganglionic fibres that pass from the trunk or prevertebral ganglia to viscera, vessels and skin, often alongside arteries or spinal nerves.
rest|Sympathetic nerves.territorio: Vascular and visceral smooth muscle, sweat glands, arrector pili muscles, heart.
rest|Sympathetic nerves.funcion: Fight-or-flight response: vasoconstriction, tachycardia, bronchodilation, mydriasis, sweating.

rest|Sympathetic trunk.descripcion: Bilateral paravertebral ganglionic chain extending from the base of the skull to the coccyx, where both trunks converge at the ganglion impar.
rest|Sympathetic trunk.origen: Preganglionic fibres from the intermediolateral column T1–L2
rest|Sympathetic trunk.ramas: Grey rami communicantes, cervical and thoracic cardiac nerves, splanchnic nerves
rest|Sympathetic trunk.territorio: Sympathetic innervation of the entire body: head, limbs, body wall and viscera.
rest|Sympathetic trunk.funcion: Distributes sympathetic efferent output to all segmental levels.
rest|Sympathetic trunk.clinica: Thoracic sympathectomy is used for hyperhidrosis; cervical injury causes Horner syndrome (ptosis, miosis, anhidrosis).

rest|Thoracodorsal nerve.descripcion: Branch of the posterior cord that descends along the posterior wall of the axilla with the thoracodorsal artery to the latissimus dorsi.
rest|Thoracodorsal nerve.origen: Posterior cord of the brachial plexus (C6–C8)
rest|Thoracodorsal nerve.clinica: Vulnerable in axillary dissection; relevant in latissimus dorsi flaps.

rest|Tibial nerve.descripcion: Medial division of the sciatic nerve; crosses the popliteal fossa, descends deep to soleus with the posterior tibial vessels and passes behind the medial malleolus in the tarsal tunnel.
rest|Tibial nerve.ramas: Muscular branches, medial sural cutaneous nerve, medial calcaneal branches, medial and lateral plantar nerves
rest|Tibial nerve.territorio: Motor: posterior muscles of the leg (gastrocnemius, soleus, popliteus, tibialis posterior, long flexors) and of the sole. Sensory: heel and sole.
rest|Tibial nerve.clinica: Tarsal tunnel syndrome; its injury prevents plantar flexion and abolishes the Achilles reflex.

rest|Trigeminal nerve (V).descripcion: Largest cranial nerve; emerges from the lateral surface of the pons with sensory and motor roots, forms the trigeminal ganglion in the trigeminal cave and divides into three branches.
rest|Trigeminal nerve (V).origen: Sensory and motor nuclei of the trigeminal nerve (brainstem)
rest|Trigeminal nerve (V).territorio: Sensory: face, anterior scalp, eye, nasal and oral cavities, teeth, dura mater. Motor: muscles of mastication, mylohyoid, anterior belly of digastric, tensor tympani and tensor veli palatini.
rest|Trigeminal nerve (V).clinica: Trigeminal neuralgia: paroxysmal lancinating pain in the V2 or V3 territory; the corneal reflex tests V1.

rest|Trochlear nerve (IV).descripcion: Only cranial nerve that emerges dorsally from the brainstem (after decussating); wraps around the cerebral peduncle, runs through the cavernous sinus and enters the orbit through the superior orbital fissure.
rest|Trochlear nerve (IV).territorio: Motor: superior oblique muscle (depression of the eye in adduction and intorsion).
rest|Trochlear nerve (IV).clinica: Lesion: vertical diplopia when going down stairs or reading; the patient tilts the head toward the healthy side.

rest|Ulnar nerve.descripcion: Terminal branch of the medial cord; descends medial to the brachial artery, passes behind the medial epicondyle, between the heads of flexor carpi ulnaris, and enters the hand through Guyon's canal.
rest|Ulnar nerve.origen: Medial cord of the brachial plexus (C8–T1, sometimes C7)
rest|Ulnar nerve.ramas: Muscular branches, palmar branch, dorsal branch, superficial branch, deep branch
rest|Ulnar nerve.territorio: Motor: flexor carpi ulnaris, medial half of flexor digitorum profundus and most intrinsic muscles of the hand. Sensory: medial border of the hand, little finger and half of the ring finger.
rest|Ulnar nerve.clinica: Entrapment in the cubital tunnel or Guyon's canal: ulnar claw hand, Froment and Wartenberg signs.

rest|Vagus nerve (X).descripcion: Emerges from the retro-olivary sulcus of the medulla, exits through the jugular foramen, descends in the carotid sheath and crosses the thorax and abdomen forming visceral plexuses.
rest|Vagus nerve (X).origen: Nucleus ambiguus, dorsal nucleus of the vagus, nucleus of the solitary tract and spinal nucleus of the trigeminal
rest|Vagus nerve (X).destino: Abdominal visceral plexuses up to the left colic flexure
rest|Vagus nerve (X).ramas: Auricular branch, pharyngeal, superior laryngeal, recurrent laryngeal, cardiac, pulmonary and oesophageal branches, anterior and posterior vagal trunks
rest|Vagus nerve (X).territorio: Motor: muscles of the pharynx, larynx and palate (except tensor veli palatini). Sensory: external acoustic meatus, larynx, thoracoabdominal viscera; taste from the epiglottis.
rest|Vagus nerve (X).funcion: Parasympathetic supply of the heart, lungs and digestive tract up to the left colic flexure.
rest|Vagus nerve (X).clinica: Its injury deviates the uvula toward the healthy side; the recurrent laryngeal nerve is injured in thyroidectomies (dysphonia).

rest|Vestibular nerve.descripcion: Balance portion of cranial nerve VIII formed by the axons of the vestibular ganglion at the fundus of the internal acoustic meatus.
rest|Vestibular nerve.destino: Vestibular nuclei of the brainstem and cerebellum
rest|Vestibular nerve.territorio: Special sensory: balance (maculae of the utricle and saccule, ampullary crests of the semicircular ducts).
rest|Vestibular nerve.clinica: Vestibular neuritis causes acute vertigo with nystagmus and an abnormal head impulse test.

rest|Vestibulocochlear nerve (VIII).descripcion: Sensory nerve that emerges from the cerebellopontine angle and enters the internal acoustic meatus alongside the facial nerve, dividing into cochlear and vestibular parts.
rest|Vestibulocochlear nerve (VIII).destino: Cochlear and vestibular nuclei of the brainstem
rest|Vestibulocochlear nerve (VIII).clinica: Vestibular schwannoma at the cerebellopontine angle causes unilateral hearing loss, tinnitus and unsteadiness.

rest|Accessory pancreatic duct.descripcion: Duct of Santorini; drains part of the head of the pancreas and runs above the main pancreatic duct.
rest|Accessory pancreatic duct.origen: Upper part of the head of the pancreas, often communicating with the main pancreatic duct.
rest|Accessory pancreatic duct.destino: Minor duodenal papilla, in the descending part of the duodenum.
rest|Accessory pancreatic duct.funcion: Conveys exocrine pancreatic juice to the duodenum.
rest|Accessory pancreatic duct.clinica: In pancreas divisum it is the main drainage pathway and is associated with recurrent pancreatitis.

rest|Accessory parotid gland.descripcion: Small glandular lobule separate from the parotid, lying over the masseter muscle beside the parotid duct.
rest|Accessory parotid gland.clinica: May give rise to tumours that are mistaken for cheek masses.

rest|Anterior lateral segment of liver (.la: Segmentum anterius laterale dextrum hepatis (segmentum VI)
rest|Anterior lateral segment of liver (.descripcion: Inferior segment of the right lateral (posterior) sector of the right lobe of the liver, below segment VII.
rest|Anterior lateral segment of liver (.territorio: Posterior branch of the right hepatic artery and of the right portal vein.
rest|Anterior lateral segment of liver (.funcion: Hepatic parenchyma with its own blood supply and biliary drainage, basis of segmental resection.
rest|Anterior lateral segment of liver (.clinica: Surgical unit that can be resected independently (segmentectomy VI).

rest|Anterior medial segment of liver (V.la: Segmentum anterius mediale dextrum hepatis (segmentum V)
rest|Anterior medial segment of liver (V.descripcion: Inferior segment of the right paramedian (anterior) sector, next to the gallbladder fossa.
rest|Anterior medial segment of liver (V.territorio: Anterior branch of the right hepatic artery and of the right portal vein.
rest|Anterior medial segment of liver (V.funcion: Hepatic parenchyma with its own Glissonian pedicle.
rest|Anterior medial segment of liver (V.clinica: Resected together with IVb in radical cholecystectomy for gallbladder cancer.

rest|Ascending colon.descripcion: Part of the large intestine that ascends along the right flank from the caecum to the right colic flexure; secondarily retroperitoneal.
rest|Ascending colon.origen: Caecum, at the level of the ileocaecal valve.
rest|Ascending colon.territorio: Ileocolic and right colic arteries (superior mesenteric artery).
rest|Ascending colon.funcion: Absorption of water and electrolytes and propulsion of faecal content.
rest|Ascending colon.clinica: Right-sided colon tumours usually present with iron-deficiency anaemia rather than obstruction.

rest|Bile duct.descripcion: Biliary duct formed by the union of the common hepatic and cystic ducts; descends in the hepatoduodenal ligament, behind the duodenum and through the head of the pancreas.
rest|Bile duct.origen: Union of the common hepatic duct and the cystic duct.
rest|Bile duct.destino: Major duodenal papilla (hepatopancreatic ampulla), in the descending part of the duodenum.
rest|Bile duct.funcion: Conveys bile from the liver and gallbladder to the duodenum.
rest|Bile duct.clinica: Choledocholithiasis causes obstructive jaundice and may lead to cholangitis or pancreatitis.

rest|Descending colon.descripcion: Part of the large intestine that descends along the left flank from the left colic flexure to the sigmoid colon; retroperitoneal.
rest|Descending colon.destino: Sigmoid colon, at the level of the iliac crest.
rest|Descending colon.funcion: Storage and propulsion of faeces; water absorption.
rest|Descending colon.clinica: The splenic flexure is a vascular watershed zone, vulnerable to ischaemic colitis.

rest|Duodenum.descripcion: First part of the small intestine, C-shaped around the head of the pancreas; mostly retroperitoneal, with four parts.
rest|Duodenum.territorio: Superior and inferior pancreaticoduodenal arteries (coeliac trunk and superior mesenteric artery).
rest|Duodenum.funcion: Receives bile and pancreatic juice; neutralises chyme and begins chemical digestion and absorption.
rest|Duodenum.clinica: A posterior duodenal ulcer can erode the gastroduodenal artery and cause severe haemorrhage.

rest|Epiglottis.descripcion: Leaf-shaped lamina of elastic cartilage, situated behind the root of the tongue, above the laryngeal inlet.
rest|Epiglottis.funcion: Protects the laryngeal inlet during swallowing, diverting the bolus toward the pharynx.
rest|Epiglottis.clinica: Acute epiglottitis can obstruct the airway and is an emergency.

rest|Free taenia.descripcion: One of the three taeniae of the colon; longitudinal band of smooth muscle on the anterior surface of the ascending, descending and sigmoid colon, and the inferior surface of the transverse colon.
rest|Free taenia.destino: Rectosigmoid junction, where it continues with the longitudinal layer of the rectum.
rest|Free taenia.funcion: Longitudinal contraction of the colon; forms the haustra.
rest|Free taenia.clinica: The taeniae converge at the base of the appendix, a guide to locating it in surgery.

rest|Gallbladder.descripcion: Pear-shaped sac lying in the fossa on the visceral surface of the liver; has a fundus, body and neck.
rest|Gallbladder.destino: Drains via the cystic duct into the bile duct.
rest|Gallbladder.territorio: Cystic artery (normally from the right hepatic artery).
rest|Gallbladder.funcion: Stores and concentrates bile and expels it into the duodenum after a fatty meal.
rest|Gallbladder.clinica: Cholecystitis: right hypochondrial pain with positive Murphy sign.

rest|Gingiva.descripcion: Fibrous mucosa attached to the alveolar processes of the maxilla and mandible, surrounding the neck of the teeth.
rest|Gingiva.territorio: Branches of the maxillary arteries (alveolar, palatine, infraorbital) and lingual/facial.
rest|Gingiva.funcion: Protects the alveolar bone and seals the neck of the tooth.
rest|Gingiva.clinica: Gingivitis due to bacterial plaque is the most frequent form of periodontal disease.

rest|Greater omentum.descripcion: Four-layered peritoneal fold hanging from the greater curvature of the stomach like an apron over the intestinal loops.
rest|Greater omentum.destino: Folds back and attaches to the transverse colon.
rest|Greater omentum.funcion: Fat store, immune defence and isolation of abdominal inflammatory foci.
rest|Greater omentum.clinica: Called the 'policeman of the abdomen': it tends to wrap around foci such as appendicitis; frequent site of peritoneal metastases.

rest|Jejunum.descripcion: Second part of the small intestine, intraperitoneal and suspended by the mesentery, located mainly in the left upper quadrant.
rest|Jejunum.funcion: Main site of digestion and nutrient absorption; tall, numerous circular folds.

rest|Left anterior lateral segment of li.la: Segmentum anterius laterale sinistrum hepatis (segmentum III)
rest|Left anterior lateral segment of li.descripcion: Inferior segment of the anatomical left lobe, to the left of the falciform ligament and in front of segment II.
rest|Left anterior lateral segment of li.territorio: Left hepatic artery and left branch of the portal vein.
rest|Left anterior lateral segment of li.funcion: Hepatic parenchyma with its own Glissonian pedicle.
rest|Left anterior lateral segment of li.clinica: Segments II and III form the left lateral graft used in paediatric living-donor liver transplantation.

rest|Left medial segment of liver (IV).descripcion: Segment between the umbilical fissure and Cantlie's line; corresponds largely to the quadrate lobe; divided into IVa and IVb.
rest|Left medial segment of liver (IV).territorio: Left (or middle) hepatic artery and left branch of the portal vein.
rest|Left medial segment of liver (IV).funcion: Hepatic parenchyma of the functional left hemiliver.
rest|Left medial segment of liver (IV).clinica: IVb is resected together with V in gallbladder cancer.

rest|Left posterior lateral segment of l.la: Segmentum posterius laterale sinistrum hepatis (segmentum II)
rest|Left posterior lateral segment of l.descripcion: Superior and posterior segment of the anatomical left lobe, to the left of the falciform ligament.
rest|Left posterior lateral segment of l.territorio: Left hepatic artery and left branch of the portal vein.
rest|Left posterior lateral segment of l.funcion: Hepatic parenchyma with its own Glissonian pedicle.
rest|Left posterior lateral segment of l.clinica: Together with III it forms the left lateral sectorectomy.

rest|Lesser omentum.descripcion: Double peritoneal layer between the lesser curvature of the stomach, the proximal duodenum and the liver; hepatogastric and hepatoduodenal ligaments.
rest|Lesser omentum.origen: Fissure for the ligamentum venosum and porta hepatis.
rest|Lesser omentum.destino: Lesser curvature of the stomach and first part of the duodenum.
rest|Lesser omentum.funcion: Contains the portal triad in its free border; forms the anterior wall of the omental bursa.
rest|Lesser omentum.clinica: The Pringle manoeuvre compresses its free border to control hepatic haemorrhage.

rest|Liver.descripcion: Largest gland of the body, in the right hypochondrium and epigastrium, beneath the diaphragm; functionally divided into eight Couinaud segments.
rest|Liver.destino: Bile leaves via the hepatic ducts.
rest|Liver.territorio: Proper hepatic artery (25%) and portal vein (75% of the flow).
rest|Liver.funcion: Nutrient metabolism, synthesis of plasma proteins, bile production, detoxification and glycogen storage.
rest|Liver.clinica: Cirrhosis causes portal hypertension with oesophageal varices and ascites.

rest|Meso-appendix.descripcion: Triangular peritoneal fold that connects the vermiform appendix to the mesentery of the terminal ileum.
rest|Meso-appendix.origen: Posterior surface of the mesentery of the terminal ileum.
rest|Meso-appendix.territorio: Contains the appendicular artery (branch of the ileocolic).
rest|Meso-appendix.funcion: Suspends the appendix and carries its vessels.
rest|Meso-appendix.clinica: The appendicular artery, an end artery, is ligated in the meso-appendix during appendicectomy.

rest|Mesocolic taenia.descripcion: Taenia of the colon on the posteromedial surface of the ascending and descending colon and at the attachment of the transverse mesocolon.
rest|Mesocolic taenia.funcion: Longitudinal contraction of the colon and formation of the haustra.

rest|Mesocolon.descripcion: Peritoneal mesentery that connects the colon to the posterior abdominal wall; the transverse and sigmoid mesocolon persist.
rest|Mesocolon.territorio: Contains the middle colic and sigmoid arteries.
rest|Mesocolon.funcion: Fixes the colon and carries vessels, lymphatics and nerves.
rest|Mesocolon.clinica: Complete mesocolic excision improves lymph node clearance in colon cancer.

rest|Nasopharynx.descripcion: Superior part of the pharynx, behind the choanae and above the soft palate; contains the opening of the auditory tube and the pharyngeal tonsil.
rest|Nasopharynx.territorio: Ascending pharyngeal artery and branches of the maxillary.
rest|Nasopharynx.funcion: Respiratory pathway; communicates with the middle ear through the auditory tube.
rest|Nasopharynx.clinica: Adenoid hypertrophy obstructs nasal breathing and the auditory tube, causing otitis media.

rest|Oesophagus.descripcion: Muscular tube about 25 cm long from the pharynx to the stomach; cervical, thoracic and abdominal parts, passes through the diaphragm at T10.
rest|Oesophagus.origen: Pharynx, at the level of the cricoid cartilage (C6).
rest|Oesophagus.territorio: Inferior thyroid, oesophageal aortic and left gastric arteries.
rest|Oesophagus.funcion: Transport of the food bolus to the stomach by peristalsis.
rest|Oesophagus.clinica: Its portocaval anastomoses give rise to oesophageal varices in portal hypertension.

rest|Omental taenia.descripcion: Taenia of the colon on the posterolateral surface of the ascending and descending colon; in the transverse colon it is where the greater omentum attaches.
rest|Omental taenia.funcion: Longitudinal contraction of the colon and formation of the haustra.

rest|Oropharynx.descripcion: Middle part of the pharynx, behind the oral cavity, between the soft palate and the upper border of the epiglottis; contains the palatine tonsils.
rest|Oropharynx.territorio: Facial (ascending palatine, tonsillar), ascending pharyngeal and lingual arteries.
rest|Oropharynx.funcion: Common pathway for air and food; takes part in swallowing.
rest|Oropharynx.clinica: Oropharyngeal cancer is increasingly associated with human papillomavirus.

rest|Pancreas.descripcion: Mixed retroperitoneal gland lying transversely behind the stomach; head within the duodenal loop, neck, body and tail toward the spleen.
rest|Pancreas.destino: Drains through the pancreatic ducts into the duodenum.
rest|Pancreas.territorio: Pancreaticoduodenal arteries and pancreatic branches of the splenic artery.
rest|Pancreas.funcion: Exocrine: digestive enzymes and bicarbonate. Endocrine: insulin, glucagon and somatostatin from the islets.
rest|Pancreas.clinica: Cancer of the head of the pancreas causes painless jaundice by compression of the bile duct.

rest|Pancreatic duct.descripcion: Duct of Wirsung; runs through the pancreas from the tail to the head, collecting the interlobular ducts.
rest|Pancreatic duct.destino: Joins the bile duct at the hepatopancreatic ampulla and opens at the major duodenal papilla.
rest|Pancreatic duct.funcion: Conveys pancreatic juice to the duodenum.
rest|Pancreatic duct.clinica: A stone in the common ampulla can obstruct it and trigger biliary pancreatitis.

rest|Parotid duct.descripcion: Stensen's duct; crosses the masseter muscle one finger's breadth below the zygomatic arch and pierces the buccinator.
rest|Parotid duct.origen: Anterior border of the parotid gland.
rest|Parotid duct.destino: Oral vestibule, opposite the upper second molar.
rest|Parotid duct.funcion: Conveys serous saliva from the parotid to the mouth.
rest|Parotid duct.clinica: May be severed in cheek wounds; sialolithiasis is less frequent than in the submandibular duct.

rest|Parotid gland.descripcion: Largest salivary gland, in front of the ear and over the ramus of the mandible; traversed by the facial nerve, the retromandibular vein and the external carotid artery.
rest|Parotid gland.destino: Drains through the parotid duct into the oral vestibule.
rest|Parotid gland.territorio: External carotid artery and its branches (superficial temporal, transverse facial).
rest|Parotid gland.funcion: Secretion of amylase-rich serous saliva; secretory innervation by the glossopharyngeal nerve via the otic ganglion.
rest|Parotid gland.clinica: Parotidectomy puts the facial nerve at risk; viral parotitis is mumps.

rest|Pharynx.descripcion: Fibromuscular tube from the base of the skull to C6, behind the nasal and oral cavities and the larynx; nasal, oral and laryngeal parts.
rest|Pharynx.destino: Continues as the oesophagus at C6.
rest|Pharynx.territorio: Ascending pharyngeal artery and branches of the facial, maxillary and superior thyroid arteries.
rest|Pharynx.funcion: Common air and digestive pathway; takes part in swallowing and phonation.
rest|Pharynx.clinica: Zenker's diverticulum forms in Killian's triangle, in its lower posterior wall.

rest|Posterior lateral segment of liver.la: Segmentum posterius laterale dextrum hepatis (segmentum VII)
rest|Posterior lateral segment of liver.descripcion: Superior segment of the right lateral (posterior) sector, in the posterior dome of the right lobe, beneath the diaphragm.
rest|Posterior lateral segment of liver.territorio: Posterior branch of the right hepatic artery and of the right portal vein.
rest|Posterior lateral segment of liver.funcion: Hepatic parenchyma with its own Glissonian pedicle.
rest|Posterior lateral segment of liver.clinica: Its posterosuperior position makes laparoscopic access difficult.

rest|Posterior medial segment of liver (.la: Segmentum posterius mediale dextrum hepatis (segmentum VIII)
rest|Posterior medial segment of liver (.descripcion: Superior segment of the right paramedian (anterior) sector, between the middle and right hepatic veins, above segment V.
rest|Posterior medial segment of liver (.territorio: Anterior branch of the right hepatic artery and of the right portal vein.
rest|Posterior medial segment of liver (.funcion: Hepatic parenchyma with its own Glissonian pedicle.
rest|Posterior medial segment of liver (.clinica: Its proximity to the confluence of the hepatic veins complicates resection.

rest|Posterior segment of liver (I).descripcion: Posterior segment of the liver, between the inferior vena cava and the fissure for the ligamentum venosum.
rest|Posterior segment of liver (I).territorio: Branches of the hepatic arteries and of the right and left portal veins.
rest|Posterior segment of liver (I).funcion: Hepatic parenchyma that drains directly into the inferior vena cava through its own veins.
rest|Posterior segment of liver (I).clinica: In Budd-Chiari syndrome it hypertrophies because its venous drainage is independent.

rest|Sigmoid colon.descripcion: S-shaped part of the large intestine, intraperitoneal and mobile thanks to the sigmoid mesocolon, in the left iliac fossa and pelvis.
rest|Sigmoid colon.origen: Descending colon, at the level of the pelvic inlet.
rest|Sigmoid colon.destino: Rectum, at the level of S3 (in the model it is separated as its own structure).
rest|Sigmoid colon.funcion: Temporary storage of faeces before defecation.
rest|Sigmoid colon.clinica: Most frequent site of diverticulosis and colonic volvulus.

rest|Soft palate.descripcion: Mobile musculomembranous fold that continues the hard palate posteriorly, separating the nasopharynx and oropharynx; ends in the uvula.
rest|Soft palate.origen: Posterior border of the hard palate.
rest|Soft palate.territorio: Lesser palatine, ascending palatine and ascending pharyngeal arteries.
rest|Soft palate.funcion: Closes off the nasopharynx during swallowing and phonation.
rest|Soft palate.clinica: Cleft palate causes nasal regurgitation and hypernasal voice.

rest|Stomach.descripcion: Most dilated part of the digestive tube, in the epigastrium and left hypochondrium; cardia, fundus, body and pyloric part.
rest|Stomach.territorio: Gastric, gastro-omental and short gastric arteries (coeliac trunk).
rest|Stomach.funcion: Stores food, mixes it with acid and pepsin to form chyme and secretes intrinsic factor.
rest|Stomach.clinica: Helicobacter pylori is the main cause of gastric ulcer and a risk factor for gastric cancer.

rest|Sublingual gland.descripcion: Smallest of the major salivary glands, in the floor of the mouth beneath the mucosa of the sublingual fold, over the mylohyoid muscle.
rest|Sublingual gland.destino: Numerous minor sublingual ducts in the sublingual fold and one major duct to the submandibular duct or caruncle.
rest|Sublingual gland.territorio: Sublingual (from the lingual) and submental arteries.
rest|Sublingual gland.clinica: Obstruction of its ducts gives rise to a ranula.

rest|Submandibular duct.descripcion: Wharton's duct; runs in the floor of the mouth between mylohyoid and hyoglossus, crossed by the lingual nerve.
rest|Submandibular duct.origen: Deep part of the submandibular gland.
rest|Submandibular duct.destino: Sublingual caruncle, on each side of the lingual frenulum.
rest|Submandibular duct.funcion: Conveys submandibular saliva to the oral cavity.
rest|Submandibular duct.clinica: Most frequent site of sialolithiasis, with painful swelling on eating.

rest|Submandibular gland.descripcion: Major salivary gland in the submandibular triangle, with a superficial part and a deep part wrapping around the posterior border of the mylohyoid.
rest|Submandibular gland.destino: Drains through the submandibular duct to the sublingual caruncle.
rest|Submandibular gland.funcion: Secretion of mixed (seromucous) saliva; produces most of the saliva at rest.
rest|Submandibular gland.clinica: The marginal mandibular branch of the facial nerve may be injured during its excision.

rest|Tongue.descripcion: Mobile muscular organ of the floor of the mouth, with a body and root separated by the terminal sulcus; intrinsic and extrinsic muscles.
rest|Tongue.funcion: Taste, mastication, swallowing and articulation of speech.
rest|Tongue.clinica: Injury to the hypoglossal nerve deviates the tip of the tongue toward the injured side on protrusion.

rest|Transverse colon.descripcion: Longest and most mobile part of the colon, intraperitoneal, suspended by the transverse mesocolon between the right and left colic flexures.
rest|Transverse colon.territorio: Middle colic artery (superior mesenteric) and left colic artery in its distal third.
rest|Transverse colon.funcion: Absorption of water and electrolytes and propulsion of faecal content.
rest|Transverse colon.clinica: Its mesocolon serves as a landmark to divide the cavity into supra- and inframesocolic compartments.

rest|Uvula of palate.descripcion: Median conical projection of the posterior border of the soft palate that hangs toward the oropharynx.
rest|Uvula of palate.origen: Posterior border of the soft palate.
rest|Uvula of palate.territorio: Lesser palatine and ascending palatine arteries.
rest|Uvula of palate.funcion: Contributes to velopharyngeal closure during swallowing and speech.
rest|Uvula of palate.clinica: In vagus nerve injury it deviates toward the healthy side.

rest|Vermiform appendix.descripcion: Blind tubular diverticulum arising from the posteromedial surface of the caecum, at the convergence of the taeniae; variable position, frequently retrocaecal.
rest|Vermiform appendix.origen: Caecum, about 2 cm below the ileocaecal valve.
rest|Vermiform appendix.funcion: Gut-associated lymphoid tissue; possible reservoir of intestinal flora.
rest|Vermiform appendix.clinica: Appendicitis: periumbilical pain that migrates to McBurney's point.

rest|Anterior basal segmental bronchus o.es: Anterior basal segmental bronchus of left lung (B VIII)
rest|Anterior basal segmental bronchus o.la: Bronchus segmentalis basalis anterior pulmonis sinistri [B VIII]
rest|Anterior basal segmental bronchus o.descripcion: Branch of the basal part of the left inferior lobar bronchus directed forward and downward; often arises from a common trunk with B VII.
rest|Anterior basal segmental bronchus o.origen: Left inferior lobar bronchus (anteromedial basal trunk).
rest|Anterior basal segmental bronchus o.destino: Anterior basal segment (S VIII) of the left inferior lobe.
rest|Anterior basal segmental bronchus o.funcion: Conducts air to the anterior basal segment.

rest|Anterior basal segmental bronchus o.es: Anterior basal segmental bronchus of right lung (B VIII)
rest|Anterior basal segmental bronchus o.la: Bronchus segmentalis basalis anterior pulmonis dextri [B VIII]
rest|Anterior basal segmental bronchus o.descripcion: Branch of the basal part of the right inferior lobar bronchus directed forward and downward.
rest|Anterior basal segmental bronchus o.destino: Anterior basal segment (S VIII) of the right inferior lobe.
rest|Anterior basal segmental bronchus o.funcion: Conducts air to the anterior basal segment.

rest|Anterior segmental bronchus of left.es: Anterior segmental bronchus of left lung (B III)
rest|Anterior segmental bronchus of left.la: Bronchus segmentalis anterior pulmonis sinistri [B III]
rest|Anterior segmental bronchus of left.descripcion: Branch of the superior (culminal) division of the left superior lobar bronchus directed forward.
rest|Anterior segmental bronchus of left.destino: Anterior segment (S III) of the left superior lobe.
rest|Anterior segmental bronchus of left.funcion: Conducts air to the anterior segment.

rest|Anterior segmental bronchus of righ.es: Anterior segmental bronchus of right lung (B III)
rest|Anterior segmental bronchus of righ.la: Bronchus segmentalis anterior pulmonis dextri [B III]
rest|Anterior segmental bronchus of righ.descripcion: Branch of the right superior lobar bronchus directed forward and downward.
rest|Anterior segmental bronchus of righ.destino: Anterior segment (S III) of the right superior lobe.
rest|Anterior segmental bronchus of righ.funcion: Conducts air to the anterior segment.

rest|Anteromedial basal segmental bronch.es: Anteromedial basal segmental bronchus of left lung (B VII+VIII)
rest|Anteromedial basal segmental bronch.la: Bronchus segmentalis basalis anteromedialis pulmonis sinistri [B VII+VIII]
rest|Anteromedial basal segmental bronch.descripcion: Usual common trunk of the medial basal and anterior basal bronchi in the left inferior lobe.
rest|Anteromedial basal segmental bronch.destino: Medial basal and anterior basal segments of the left inferior lobe.
rest|Anteromedial basal segmental bronch.ramas: Medial basal (B VII) and anterior basal (B VIII) bronchi.
rest|Anteromedial basal segmental bronch.funcion: Conducts air to the anteromedial basal region of the left lung.

rest|Apical segmental bronchus of right.es: Apical segmental bronchus of right lung (B I)
rest|Apical segmental bronchus of right.la: Bronchus segmentalis apicalis pulmonis dextri [B I]
rest|Apical segmental bronchus of right.descripcion: Branch of the right superior lobar bronchus that ascends toward the apex of the lung.
rest|Apical segmental bronchus of right.destino: Apical segment (S I) of the right superior lobe.
rest|Apical segmental bronchus of right.funcion: Conducts air to the apex of the lung.
rest|Apical segmental bronchus of right.clinica: The apical and posterior segments are the typical location of reactivation tuberculosis.

rest|Apicoposterior segmental bronchus o.es: Apicoposterior segmental bronchus of left lung (B I+II)
rest|Apicoposterior segmental bronchus o.la: Bronchus segmentalis apicoposterior pulmonis sinistri [B I+II]
rest|Apicoposterior segmental bronchus o.descripcion: Branch of the superior division of the left superior lobar bronchus that ascends toward the apex and posterior part.
rest|Apicoposterior segmental bronchus o.destino: Apicoposterior segment (S I+II) of the left superior lobe.
rest|Apicoposterior segmental bronchus o.funcion: Conducts air to the apex of the left lung.

rest|Inferior lingular segmental bronchu.descripcion: Inferior branch of the lingular bronchus, the inferior division of the left superior lobar bronchus.
rest|Inferior lingular segmental bronchu.destino: Inferior lingular segment (S V) of the left superior lobe.
rest|Inferior lingular segmental bronchu.funcion: Conducts air to the inferior lingular segment.

rest|Inferior lobe of left lung.descripcion: Posteroinferior lobe of the left lung, below and behind the oblique fissure; forms most of the base.
rest|Inferior lobe of left lung.ramas: Superior, anteromedial basal, lateral basal and posterior basal segments.

rest|Inferior lobe of right lung.descripcion: Posteroinferior lobe of the right lung, below and behind the oblique fissure; rests on the diaphragm.
rest|Inferior lobe of right lung.ramas: Superior, medial basal, anterior basal, lateral basal and posterior basal segments.
rest|Inferior lobe of right lung.clinica: Most frequent site of aspiration pneumonia in the upright position.

rest|Intermediate bronchus.descripcion: Segment of the right main bronchus between the origin of the superior lobar bronchus and the origin of the middle lobar bronchus.
rest|Intermediate bronchus.origen: Right main bronchus, after the superior lobar bronchus.
rest|Intermediate bronchus.destino: Divides into the right middle and inferior lobar bronchi.
rest|Intermediate bronchus.ramas: Middle lobar bronchus and right inferior lobar bronchus.
rest|Intermediate bronchus.funcion: Conducts air to the right middle and inferior lobes.
rest|Intermediate bronchus.clinica: Frequent site of impaction of aspirated foreign bodies.

rest|Laryngopharynx.descripcion: Inferior part of the pharynx, behind the larynx, from the epiglottis to the cricoid cartilage; contains the piriform recesses.
rest|Laryngopharynx.destino: Continues as the oesophagus at C6.
rest|Laryngopharynx.territorio: Superior and inferior thyroid and ascending pharyngeal arteries.
rest|Laryngopharynx.funcion: Conveys the food bolus to the oesophagus.
rest|Laryngopharynx.clinica: Fish bones frequently lodge in the piriform recess.

rest|Lateral basal segmental bronchus of.es: Lateral basal segmental bronchus of left lung (B IX)
rest|Lateral basal segmental bronchus of.la: Bronchus segmentalis basalis lateralis pulmonis sinistri [B IX]
rest|Lateral basal segmental bronchus of.descripcion: Branch of the basal part of the left inferior lobar bronchus directed laterally downward.
rest|Lateral basal segmental bronchus of.destino: Lateral basal segment (S IX) of the left inferior lobe.
rest|Lateral basal segmental bronchus of.funcion: Conducts air to the lateral basal segment.

rest|Lateral basal segmental bronchus of.es: Lateral basal segmental bronchus of right lung (B IX)
rest|Lateral basal segmental bronchus of.la: Bronchus segmentalis basalis lateralis pulmonis dextri [B IX]
rest|Lateral basal segmental bronchus of.descripcion: Branch of the basal part of the right inferior lobar bronchus directed laterally downward.
rest|Lateral basal segmental bronchus of.destino: Lateral basal segment (S IX) of the right inferior lobe.
rest|Lateral basal segmental bronchus of.funcion: Conducts air to the lateral basal segment.

rest|Lateral segmental bronchus of right.es: Lateral segmental bronchus of right lung (B IV)
rest|Lateral segmental bronchus of right.la: Bronchus segmentalis lateralis pulmonis dextri [B IV]
rest|Lateral segmental bronchus of right.descripcion: Lateral branch of the right middle lobar bronchus.
rest|Lateral segmental bronchus of right.destino: Lateral segment (S IV) of the middle lobe.
rest|Lateral segmental bronchus of right.funcion: Conducts air to the lateral segment of the middle lobe.

rest|Left inferior lobar bronchus.descripcion: Continuation of the left main bronchus after the origin of the superior lobar bronchus; descends to the inferior lobe.
rest|Left inferior lobar bronchus.destino: Inferior lobe of the left lung.
rest|Left inferior lobar bronchus.ramas: Superior (B VI), anteromedial basal (B VII+VIII), lateral basal (B IX) and posterior basal (B X) segmental bronchi.
rest|Left inferior lobar bronchus.funcion: Conducts air to the left inferior lobe.

rest|Left main bronchus.descripcion: Left branch of the tracheal bifurcation; longer (about 5 cm), narrower and more horizontal than the right; passes beneath the aortic arch and in front of the oesophagus.
rest|Left main bronchus.origen: Tracheal bifurcation (carina), at the level of T4-T5.
rest|Left main bronchus.ramas: Left superior and inferior lobar bronchi.
rest|Left main bronchus.territorio: Left bronchial arteries (from the thoracic aorta).
rest|Left main bronchus.funcion: Conducts air to the left lung.
rest|Left main bronchus.clinica: Because of its more horizontal course it receives fewer aspirated foreign bodies than the right.

rest|Left superior lobar bronchus.descripcion: Branch of the left main bronchus that divides into a superior (culminal) and an inferior (lingular) part.
rest|Left superior lobar bronchus.destino: Superior lobe of the left lung.
rest|Left superior lobar bronchus.ramas: Apicoposterior (B I+II), anterior (B III), superior lingular (B IV) and inferior lingular (B V) bronchi.
rest|Left superior lobar bronchus.funcion: Conducts air to the left superior lobe, including the lingula.

rest|Medial basal segmental bronchus of.es: Medial basal segmental bronchus of left lung (B VII)
rest|Medial basal segmental bronchus of.la: Bronchus segmentalis basalis medialis pulmonis sinistri [B VII]
rest|Medial basal segmental bronchus of.descripcion: Medial basal branch of the left inferior lobe, usually in a common trunk with the anterior basal.
rest|Medial basal segmental bronchus of.origen: Left inferior lobar bronchus (anteromedial basal trunk).
rest|Medial basal segmental bronchus of.destino: Medial basal segment (S VII) of the left inferior lobe.
rest|Medial basal segmental bronchus of.funcion: Conducts air to the medial basal segment.

rest|Medial basal segmental bronchus of.es: Medial basal segmental bronchus of right lung (B VII)
rest|Medial basal segmental bronchus of.la: Bronchus segmentalis basalis medialis (cardiacus) pulmonis dextri [B VII]
rest|Medial basal segmental bronchus of.descripcion: Branch of the right inferior lobar bronchus directed medially downward, next to the heart (cardiac bronchus).
rest|Medial basal segmental bronchus of.destino: Medial basal segment (S VII) of the right inferior lobe.
rest|Medial basal segmental bronchus of.funcion: Conducts air to the medial basal segment.

rest|Medial segmental bronchus of right.es: Medial segmental bronchus of right lung (B V)
rest|Medial segmental bronchus of right.la: Bronchus segmentalis medialis pulmonis dextri [B V]
rest|Medial segmental bronchus of right.descripcion: Medial branch of the right middle lobar bronchus.
rest|Medial segmental bronchus of right.destino: Medial segment (S V) of the middle lobe.
rest|Medial segmental bronchus of right.funcion: Conducts air to the medial segment of the middle lobe.

rest|Middle lobar bronchus.descripcion: Anterior branch of the right intermediate bronchus, long and narrow, directed forward and downward.
rest|Middle lobar bronchus.destino: Middle lobe of the right lung.
rest|Middle lobar bronchus.ramas: Lateral (B IV) and medial (B V) segmental bronchi.
rest|Middle lobar bronchus.funcion: Conducts air to the middle lobe.
rest|Middle lobar bronchus.clinica: Its narrow calibre and neighbouring lymph nodes predispose to middle lobe syndrome.

rest|Middle lobe of right lung.descripcion: Anterior lobe of the right lung, between the horizontal and oblique fissures.
rest|Middle lobe of right lung.ramas: Lateral (S IV) and medial (S V) segments.
rest|Middle lobe of right lung.clinica: Pneumonia of this lobe obliterates the right heart border on radiography (silhouette sign).

rest|Mucosa of nasal cavity.descripcion: Mucous membrane lining the nasal cavity; respiratory region with ciliated pseudostratified epithelium and olfactory region in the roof.
rest|Mucosa of nasal cavity.territorio: Sphenopalatine, anterior and posterior ethmoidal, greater palatine and superior labial arteries.
rest|Mucosa of nasal cavity.funcion: Warms, humidifies and filters inspired air; houses olfactory receptors.
rest|Mucosa of nasal cavity.clinica: Anterior epistaxis usually originates in Kiesselbach's area of the septum.

rest|Pleura.descripcion: Serous membrane surrounding each lung; visceral layer on the lung and parietal layer on the chest wall, diaphragm and mediastinum, with the pleural cavity between them.
rest|Pleura.territorio: Parietal: intercostal and internal thoracic arteries; visceral: bronchial arteries.
rest|Pleura.funcion: Allows the lung to glide and couples the lung to the chest wall through negative pressure.
rest|Pleura.clinica: The parietal pleura is pain-sensitive (pleuritic pain); the visceral is not.

rest|Posterior basal segmental bronchus.es: Posterior basal segmental bronchus of left lung (B X)
rest|Posterior basal segmental bronchus.la: Bronchus segmentalis basalis posterior pulmonis sinistri [B X]
rest|Posterior basal segmental bronchus.descripcion: Posterior terminal branch of the basal part of the left inferior lobar bronchus.
rest|Posterior basal segmental bronchus.destino: Posterior basal segment (S X) of the left inferior lobe.
rest|Posterior basal segmental bronchus.funcion: Conducts air to the posterior basal segment.
rest|Posterior basal segmental bronchus.clinica: Dependent segment in the upright position; frequent in aspiration pneumonia.

rest|Posterior basal segmental bronchus.es: Posterior basal segmental bronchus of right lung (B X)
rest|Posterior basal segmental bronchus.la: Bronchus segmentalis basalis posterior pulmonis dextri [B X]
rest|Posterior basal segmental bronchus.descripcion: Posterior terminal branch of the basal part of the right inferior lobar bronchus.
rest|Posterior basal segmental bronchus.destino: Posterior basal segment (S X) of the right inferior lobe.
rest|Posterior basal segmental bronchus.funcion: Conducts air to the posterior basal segment.
rest|Posterior basal segmental bronchus.clinica: Dependent segment in the upright position; frequent in aspiration pneumonia.

rest|Posterior segmental bronchus of rig.es: Posterior segmental bronchus of right lung (B II)
rest|Posterior segmental bronchus of rig.la: Bronchus segmentalis posterior pulmonis dextri [B II]
rest|Posterior segmental bronchus of rig.descripcion: Branch of the right superior lobar bronchus directed backward and upward.
rest|Posterior segmental bronchus of rig.destino: Posterior segment (S II) of the right superior lobe.
rest|Posterior segmental bronchus of rig.funcion: Conducts air to the posterior segment.
rest|Posterior segmental bronchus of rig.clinica: Classic site of aspiration pneumonia or abscess in the supine position.

rest|Right inferior lobar bronchus.descripcion: Continuation of the intermediate bronchus after the origin of the middle lobar bronchus; descends to the right inferior lobe.
rest|Right inferior lobar bronchus.destino: Inferior lobe of the right lung.
rest|Right inferior lobar bronchus.ramas: Superior (B VI), medial basal (B VII), anterior basal (B VIII), lateral basal (B IX) and posterior basal (B X) segmental bronchi.
rest|Right inferior lobar bronchus.funcion: Conducts air to the right inferior lobe.

rest|Right main bronchus.descripcion: Right branch of the tracheal bifurcation; shorter (about 2.5 cm), wider and more vertical than the left; the azygos vein arches over it.
rest|Right main bronchus.origen: Tracheal bifurcation (carina), at the level of T4-T5.
rest|Right main bronchus.ramas: Right superior lobar bronchus and intermediate bronchus.
rest|Right main bronchus.funcion: Conducts air to the right lung.
rest|Right main bronchus.clinica: Most frequent destination of aspirated foreign bodies and of overly deep intubation.

rest|Right superior lobar bronchus.descripcion: First branch of the right main bronchus, arising above the pulmonary artery (eparterial bronchus).
rest|Right superior lobar bronchus.destino: Superior lobe of the right lung.
rest|Right superior lobar bronchus.ramas: Apical (B I), posterior (B II) and anterior (B III) segmental bronchi.
rest|Right superior lobar bronchus.funcion: Conducts air to the right superior lobe.
rest|Right superior lobar bronchus.clinica: Occasionally arises directly from the trachea (tracheal bronchus).

rest|Superior lingular segmental bronchu.descripcion: Superior branch of the lingular bronchus, the inferior division of the left superior lobar bronchus.
rest|Superior lingular segmental bronchu.destino: Superior lingular segment (S IV) of the left superior lobe.
rest|Superior lingular segmental bronchu.funcion: Conducts air to the superior lingular segment.

rest|Superior lobe of left lung.descripcion: Anterosuperior lobe of the left lung, above and in front of the oblique fissure; includes the lingula and the cardiac notch.
rest|Superior lobe of left lung.ramas: Apicoposterior, anterior, superior lingular and inferior lingular segments.
rest|Superior lobe of left lung.clinica: Lingular pneumonia obliterates the left heart border on radiography.

rest|Superior lobe of right lung.descripcion: Superior lobe of the right lung, above the horizontal fissure; includes the apex.
rest|Superior lobe of right lung.clinica: A Pancoast tumour of the apex can involve the brachial plexus and the sympathetic trunk (Horner syndrome).

rest|Superior segmental bronchus of left.es: Superior segmental bronchus of left lung (B VI)
rest|Superior segmental bronchus of left.la: Bronchus segmentalis superior pulmonis sinistri [B VI]
rest|Superior segmental bronchus of left.descripcion: First branch of the left inferior lobar bronchus, directed backward.
rest|Superior segmental bronchus of left.destino: Superior segment (S VI) of the left inferior lobe.
rest|Superior segmental bronchus of left.funcion: Conducts air to the superior segment of the inferior lobe.
rest|Superior segmental bronchus of left.clinica: Dependent segment in the supine position; frequent in aspiration pneumonia.

rest|Superior segmental bronchus of righ.es: Superior segmental bronchus of right lung (B VI)
rest|Superior segmental bronchus of righ.la: Bronchus segmentalis superior pulmonis dextri [B VI]
rest|Superior segmental bronchus of righ.descripcion: First branch of the right inferior lobar bronchus, directed backward, almost opposite the middle lobar bronchus.
rest|Superior segmental bronchus of righ.destino: Superior segment (S VI) of the right inferior lobe.
rest|Superior segmental bronchus of righ.funcion: Conducts air to the superior segment of the inferior lobe.
rest|Superior segmental bronchus of righ.clinica: Dependent segment in the supine position; frequent in aspiration pneumonia.

rest|Trachea.descripcion: Cartilaginous tube about 10-12 cm long from the cricoid cartilage (C6) to its bifurcation at T4-T5; C-shaped rings open posteriorly.
rest|Trachea.origen: Larynx, at the lower border of the cricoid cartilage (C6).
rest|Trachea.destino: Bifurcates into the main bronchi at the carina (T4-T5).
rest|Trachea.funcion: Conducts air between the larynx and bronchi; its ciliated epithelium clears mucus and particles.
rest|Trachea.clinica: Tracheostomy is usually performed between the second and fourth tracheal rings.

rest|Kidney.descripcion: Paired retroperitoneal bean-shaped organ on either side of the spine between T12 and L3; the right is slightly lower because of the liver.
rest|Kidney.destino: Urine leaves through the renal pelvis to the ureter.
rest|Kidney.funcion: Filters the blood and produces urine; regulates water, electrolytes, acid-base balance and blood pressure; secretes erythropoietin and renin.
rest|Kidney.clinica: Renal colic pain radiates from the lumbar fossa to the groin.

rest|Renal pelvis.descripcion: Funnel-shaped dilation of the upper end of the ureter, located in the renal sinus, formed by the confluence of the major calyces.
rest|Renal pelvis.funcion: Collects urine from the calyces and conveys it to the ureter.
rest|Renal pelvis.clinica: Stenosis of the pelviureteric junction is a frequent cause of congenital hydronephrosis.

rest|Ureter.descripcion: Retroperitoneal muscular tube 25-30 cm long that descends over the psoas, crosses the iliac vessels and enters the bladder obliquely.
rest|Ureter.destino: Urinary bladder, at the ureteric orifices of the trigone.
rest|Ureter.territorio: Branches of the renal, gonadal, aorta, common and internal iliac, and vesical arteries.
rest|Ureter.funcion: Transports urine from the kidney to the bladder by peristalsis.
rest|Ureter.clinica: Stones lodge at the pelviureteric junction, the iliac crossing and the vesicoureteric junction; risk of injury when ligating the uterine artery.

rest|Urethra.descripcion: Duct that carries urine from the bladder to the exterior; in males about 20 cm (prostatic, membranous and spongy parts), in females about 4 cm.
rest|Urethra.origen: Internal urethral orifice of the bladder.
rest|Urethra.destino: External urethral orifice (glans in males, vaginal vestibule in females).
rest|Urethra.territorio: Inferior vesical, middle rectal and internal pudendal arteries.
rest|Urethra.funcion: Voiding of urine; in males also the pathway of semen.
rest|Urethra.clinica: The short female urethra explains the higher frequency of cystitis in women.

rest|Urinary bladder.descripcion: Hollow muscular subperitoneal organ in the lesser pelvis, behind the pubic symphysis; apex, body, fundus and neck with the trigone.
rest|Urinary bladder.territorio: Superior and inferior vesical arteries (internal iliac).
rest|Urinary bladder.funcion: Stores urine and expels it by means of the detrusor muscle during micturition.
rest|Urinary bladder.clinica: When distended it rises above the pubis, allowing extraperitoneal suprapubic puncture.

rest|Corpus cavernosum of penis.descripcion: Pair of cylinders of erectile tissue on the dorsum of the penis, surrounded by the tunica albuginea; their crura attach to the ischiopubic rami.
rest|Corpus cavernosum of penis.origen: Crura of the penis on the ischiopubic rami.
rest|Corpus cavernosum of penis.territorio: Deep artery of the penis (internal pudendal).
rest|Corpus cavernosum of penis.funcion: Their blood filling produces the rigidity of erection.
rest|Corpus cavernosum of penis.clinica: Penile fracture is rupture of its tunica albuginea during erection.

rest|Corpus spongiosum of penis.descripcion: Single cylinder of erectile tissue on the ventral surface of the penis surrounding the spongy urethra; begins at the bulb and ends at the glans.
rest|Corpus spongiosum of penis.origen: Bulb of the penis, in the perineum.
rest|Corpus spongiosum of penis.territorio: Artery of the bulb of the penis and urethral artery (internal pudendal).
rest|Corpus spongiosum of penis.funcion: Protects the urethra and remains compressible during erection to allow ejaculation.

rest|Ductus deferens.descripcion: Muscular duct about 45 cm long that ascends in the spermatic cord, passes through the inguinal canal and descends through the pelvis behind the bladder.
rest|Ductus deferens.destino: Joins the duct of the seminal vesicle to form the ejaculatory duct.
rest|Ductus deferens.territorio: Artery to the ductus deferens (superior or inferior vesical).
rest|Ductus deferens.clinica: Divided in vasectomy; palpable as a firm cord in the scrotum.

rest|Ejaculatory duct.descripcion: Short paired duct that passes through the prostate.
rest|Ejaculatory duct.origen: Union of the ampulla of the ductus deferens with the excretory duct of the seminal vesicle.
rest|Ejaculatory duct.destino: Prostatic urethra, at the seminal colliculus on either side of the prostatic utricle.
rest|Ejaculatory duct.territorio: Artery to the ductus deferens and prostatic branches.
rest|Ejaculatory duct.funcion: Conveys sperm and seminal secretion to the urethra.
rest|Ejaculatory duct.clinica: Its obstruction causes azoospermia with low ejaculate volume.

rest|Epididymis.descripcion: Comma-shaped structure attached to the posterior border of the testis, with a head, body and tail; contains a highly coiled duct.
rest|Epididymis.destino: Continues as the ductus deferens from the tail.
rest|Epididymis.territorio: Testicular artery and artery to the ductus deferens.
rest|Epididymis.funcion: Stores sperm and allows their maturation and acquisition of motility.
rest|Epididymis.clinica: Epididymitis causes scrotal pain that is relieved by elevating the testis (Prehn sign).

rest|Glans penis.descripcion: Distal expansion of the corpus spongiosum that covers the ends of the corpora cavernosa; contains the external urethral orifice and is covered by the prepuce.
rest|Glans penis.territorio: Dorsal artery of the penis and arteries of the corpus spongiosum.
rest|Glans penis.funcion: Area of high sexual sensitivity (dorsal nerve of the penis).
rest|Glans penis.clinica: Paraphimosis is entrapment of the retracted foreskin behind the glans, with circulatory compromise.

rest|Prostate.descripcion: Single fibromuscular gland beneath the bladder surrounding the prostatic urethra; base, apex and peripheral, central and transition zones.
rest|Prostate.destino: Its ductules open into the prostatic urethra.
rest|Prostate.territorio: Inferior vesical, middle rectal and internal pudendal arteries.
rest|Prostate.funcion: Secretes a slightly acidic fluid rich in PSA and citrate that forms part of the semen.
rest|Prostate.clinica: Benign hyperplasia affects the transition zone; cancer affects the peripheral zone, palpable on digital rectal examination.

rest|Seminal gland.descripcion: Paired coiled tubular gland on the posterior surface of the bladder, lateral to the ampulla of the ductus deferens.
rest|Seminal gland.destino: Its excretory duct joins the ductus deferens to form the ejaculatory duct.
rest|Seminal gland.territorio: Inferior vesical and middle rectal arteries.
rest|Seminal gland.funcion: Produces most of the seminal volume, rich in fructose and prostaglandins.

rest|Testis.descripcion: Ovoid male gonad in the scrotum, covered by the tunica vaginalis and tunica albuginea; divided into lobules with seminiferous tubules.
rest|Testis.destino: Sperm leave through the rete testis and efferent ductules to the epididymis.
rest|Testis.territorio: Testicular artery (from the abdominal aorta, L2).
rest|Testis.clinica: Testicular torsion is a surgical emergency; its lymphatic drainage goes to lumbar nodes, not inguinal.

rest|Adenohypophysis.descripcion: Anterior lobe of the pituitary, derived from Rathke's pouch; pars distalis, intermedia and tuberalis, in the sella turcica.
rest|Adenohypophysis.territorio: Hypophyseal portal system (from the superior hypophyseal arteries).
rest|Adenohypophysis.funcion: Secretes GH, prolactin, ACTH, TSH, FSH and LH under the control of hypothalamic hormones.
rest|Adenohypophysis.clinica: Macroadenomas compress the optic chiasm and produce bitemporal hemianopia.

rest|Inferior parathyroid gland.descripcion: Small endocrine gland on the posterior surface of the lower pole of the thyroid; derived from the third pharyngeal pouch and of variable position.
rest|Inferior parathyroid gland.funcion: Secretes parathyroid hormone, which raises serum calcium.
rest|Inferior parathyroid gland.clinica: Because it descends with the thymus it may be ectopic in the mediastinum; accidental removal during thyroidectomy causes hypocalcaemia.

rest|Neurohypophysis.descripcion: Posterior lobe of the pituitary, an extension of the diencephalon; formed by the neural lobe and the infundibulum.
rest|Neurohypophysis.funcion: Stores and releases oxytocin and vasopressin (ADH) produced in the supraoptic and paraventricular nuclei.
rest|Neurohypophysis.clinica: Its injury, or that of the stalk, produces central diabetes insipidus.

rest|Pineal gland.descripcion: Small single gland of the epithalamus, above the superior colliculi, in the posterior wall of the third ventricle.
rest|Pineal gland.territorio: Posterior choroidal branches of the posterior cerebral artery.
rest|Pineal gland.funcion: Secretes melatonin according to the light-dark cycle, regulating the circadian rhythm.
rest|Pineal gland.clinica: Pineal tumours compress the tectum (Parinaud syndrome) and the aqueduct, causing hydrocephalus.

rest|Superior parathyroid gland.descripcion: Small endocrine gland on the posterior surface of the middle-upper third of the thyroid; derived from the fourth pharyngeal pouch, of more constant position.
rest|Superior parathyroid gland.funcion: Secretes parathyroid hormone, which raises serum calcium.
rest|Superior parathyroid gland.clinica: Its removal or devascularisation during thyroidectomy causes hypoparathyroidism.

rest|Suprarenal gland.descripcion: Paired retroperitoneal endocrine gland on the upper pole of each kidney; the right is pyramidal and the left semilunar; cortex and medulla.
rest|Suprarenal gland.territorio: Superior (inferior phrenic), middle (aorta) and inferior (renal) suprarenal arteries.
rest|Suprarenal gland.funcion: Cortex: aldosterone, cortisol and androgens. Medulla: adrenaline and noradrenaline.
rest|Suprarenal gland.clinica: Phaeochromocytoma of the medulla causes hypertensive crises.

rest|Thyroid gland.descripcion: Endocrine gland in the anterior part of the neck, with two lobes joined by an isthmus over the 2nd-4th tracheal rings.
rest|Thyroid gland.territorio: Superior (external carotid) and inferior (thyrocervical trunk) thyroid arteries.
rest|Thyroid gland.funcion: Secretes thyroxine and triiodothyronine, which regulate metabolism, and calcitonin (C cells).
rest|Thyroid gland.clinica: In thyroidectomy there is a risk of injuring the recurrent laryngeal nerve, with dysphonia.

rest|Anal region.descripcion: Posterior, triangular part of the perineum, around the anus; between the coccyx and the line joining the two ischial tuberosities.
rest|Anal region.territorio: Inferior anal (inferior rectal) nerves from the pudendal nerve; dermatomes S4-S5 and Co
rest|Anal region.clinica: Contains the ischioanal fossa, site of ischioanal abscesses; examination includes digital rectal examination.

rest|Angle of mouth.descripcion: Lateral point where the upper and lower lips meet, at the labial commissure; site of convergence of the modiolus.
rest|Angle of mouth.territorio: Maxillary nerve (upper lip) and mental nerve (lower lip), branches of the trigeminal
rest|Angle of mouth.clinica: Its unilateral drooping is an early sign of facial paralysis; angular cheilitis is located here.

rest|Anterior notch of auricle.descripcion: Cleft between the tragus and the root (crus) of the helix, in the anterior part of the auricle.
rest|Anterior notch of auricle.clinica: Site of the endaural incision in surgical approaches to the middle ear; site of preauricular fistulas.

rest|Anterior region of ankle.descripcion: Anterior surface of the talocrural joint, between both malleoli; contains the extensor tendons under the retinacula.
rest|Anterior region of ankle.territorio: Superficial fibular nerve; deep fibular nerve in the first interdigital space; dermatomes L4-L5
rest|Anterior region of ankle.clinica: The pulse of the dorsalis pedis artery is sought just distally, lateral to the tendon of extensor hallucis longus.

rest|Anterior region of arm.descripcion: Anterior surface of the arm, between the deltoid region and the anterior region of the elbow; contains the flexor compartment (biceps, brachialis, coracobrachialis).
rest|Anterior region of arm.territorio: Medial cutaneous nerve of the arm, intercostobrachial, and superior and inferior lateral cutaneous nerves of the arm; dermatomes C5-T2
rest|Anterior region of arm.clinica: The brachial artery is palpated in the medial bicipital groove to take blood pressure.

rest|Anterior region of elbow.descripcion: Anterior surface of the elbow; includes the cubital fossa, bounded by pronator teres, brachioradialis and the interepicondylar line.
rest|Anterior region of elbow.territorio: Lateral and medial cutaneous nerves of the forearm; dermatomes C6, T1
rest|Anterior region of elbow.clinica: Usual site of venepuncture in the median cubital vein; the brachial artery is auscultated when measuring blood pressure.

rest|Anterior region of forearm.descripcion: Anterior (palmar) surface of the forearm, between the anterior region of the elbow and that of the carpus; contains the flexor-pronator muscles.
rest|Anterior region of forearm.territorio: Lateral (musculocutaneous) and medial cutaneous nerves of the forearm; dermatomes C6, C8, T1
rest|Anterior region of forearm.clinica: Site of compartment syndrome after fractures or ischaemia (Volkmann contracture).

rest|Anterior region of knee.descripcion: Anterior surface of the knee, centered on the patella and the patellar ligament, between the thigh and the leg.
rest|Anterior region of knee.territorio: Saphenous nerve (infrapatellar branch), anterior femoral cutaneous nerves and lateral femoral cutaneous nerve; dermatomes L3-L4
rest|Anterior region of knee.clinica: The patellar ligament is tapped to elicit the patellar reflex (L3-L4); prepatellar bursitis.

rest|Anterior region of leg.descripcion: Anterior surface of the leg, between the knee and the ankle; includes the subcutaneous medial surface of the tibia and the anterior compartment.
rest|Anterior region of leg.territorio: Saphenous nerve (medial) and superficial fibular nerve (lateral); dermatomes L4-L5
rest|Anterior region of leg.clinica: Anterior compartment syndrome; the anterior border of the tibia is subcutaneous and palpable.

rest|Anterior region of thigh.descripcion: Anterior surface of the thigh, from the inguinal ligament to the knee; contains the femoral triangle and the quadriceps.
rest|Anterior region of thigh.territorio: Anterior cutaneous branches of the femoral nerve, lateral femoral cutaneous, femorogenital and obturator nerves; dermatomes L1-L3
rest|Anterior region of thigh.clinica: The anterolateral area (vastus lateralis) is used for intramuscular injections, especially in infants.

rest|Anterior region of wrist.descripcion: Palmar surface of the wrist, between the forearm and the palm; crossed by the carpal flexion creases.
rest|Anterior region of wrist.territorio: Lateral cutaneous nerve of the forearm, palmar branch of the median and ulnar nerves; dermatomes C6-C8
rest|Anterior region of wrist.clinica: The radial pulse is palpated lateral to the tendon of flexor carpi radialis; the median nerve passes beneath palmaris longus.

rest|Antihelix.descripcion: Curved ridge parallel and anterior to the helix; it separates the scaphoid fossa from the concha and divides superiorly into two crura.
rest|Antihelix.territorio: Great auricular nerve (posterior) and auricular branch of the vagus (concha area)
rest|Antihelix.clinica: Absent or hypoplastic folding causes the prominent (protruding) ear, corrected by otoplasty.

rest|Antitragus.descripcion: Small eminence located opposite the tragus, above the lobule, separated from it by the intertragic incisure.

rest|Apex of auricle.descripcion: Highest point of the helix, at the superior border of the auricle.
rest|Apex of auricle.territorio: Lesser occipital nerve and auriculotemporal nerve
rest|Apex of auricle.clinica: A prominent or pointed tip is the variant called 'satyr ear' or superior Darwin's tubercle.

rest|Auricular region.descripcion: Lateral region of the head corresponding to the auricle and the external acoustic meatus.
rest|Auricular region.territorio: Auriculotemporal nerve, great auricular, lesser occipital and auricular branch of the vagus
rest|Auricular region.clinica: Stimulation of the canal (auricular branch of the vagus) can provoke reflex cough (Arnold's reflex).

rest|Auricular tubercle.descripcion: Small, inconstant prominence on the border of the helix in its posterosuperior portion (Darwin's tubercle).
rest|Auricular tubercle.territorio: Great auricular and lesser occipital nerves
rest|Auricular tubercle.clinica: Anatomical variant with no pathological significance.

rest|Buccal region.descripcion: Region of the cheek, between the infraorbital, zygomatic, parotideomasseteric, oral and mental regions; contains the buccinator and the buccal fat pad.
rest|Buccal region.clinica: The papilla of the parotid duct opens opposite the second upper molar on the inner surface.

rest|Carotid triangle.descripcion: Subdivision of the anterior cervical triangle bounded by the sternocleidomastoid, the superior belly of the omohyoid and the posterior belly of the digastric.
rest|Carotid triangle.clinica: The carotid pulse is palpated and carotid sinus massage is performed; access for endarterectomy.

rest|Cavity of concha.descripcion: Inferior and deepest portion of the concha, below the crus of the helix, leading to the external acoustic meatus.
rest|Cavity of concha.territorio: Auricular branch of the vagus nerve
rest|Cavity of concha.clinica: Common site of vesicles in Ramsay Hunt syndrome (herpes zoster oticus).

rest|Concha of auricle.descripcion: Deep depression bounded by the antihelix, tragus and antitragus; divided by the crus of the helix into the cymba and the cavity.
rest|Concha of auricle.territorio: Auricular branch of the vagus nerve and great auricular nerve
rest|Concha of auricle.clinica: Usual source of cartilage for grafts in rhinoplasty and ear surgery.

rest|Crura of antihelix.descripcion: Two limbs, superior and inferior, into which the antihelix divides upward; they bound the triangular fossa.

rest|Cubital fossa.descripcion: Triangular depression anterior to the elbow, bounded by the interepicondylar line, pronator teres and brachioradialis; contains the biceps tendon, brachial artery and median nerve.
rest|Cubital fossa.territorio: Lateral and medial cutaneous nerves of the forearm
rest|Cubital fossa.clinica: Usual site of venipuncture; the brachial artery is auscultated medial to the biceps tendon.

rest|Cymba conchae.descripcion: Superior and smaller portion of the concha, located above the crus of the helix and below the inferior crus of the antihelix.
rest|Cymba conchae.territorio: Auricular branch of the vagus nerve
rest|Cymba conchae.clinica: Target of transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation.

rest|Deltoid region.descripcion: Region corresponding to the deltoid muscle, forming the rounded contour of the shoulder.
rest|Deltoid region.territorio: Superior lateral cutaneous nerve of the arm (axillary) and supraclavicular nerves; dermatome C5
rest|Deltoid region.clinica: Intramuscular injection site about 2-3 cm below the acromion; 'patch' anesthesia suggests axillary nerve injury.

rest|Deltopectoral triangle.descripcion: Depression between the deltoid, pectoralis major and clavicle (infraclavicular fossa); contains the cephalic vein.
rest|Deltopectoral triangle.clinica: The coracoid process is palpated; landmark for subclavian vein puncture and the deltopectoral approach.

rest|Distal transverse arch of foot.descripcion: Transverse arch at the level of the metatarsal heads, flatter than the proximal one.
rest|Distal transverse arch of foot.clinica: Its collapse is associated with metatarsalgia and calluses under the metatarsal heads.

rest|Dorsal surfaces of digits of foot.es: Dorsal surfaces of digits of foot
rest|Dorsal surfaces of digits of foot.descripcion: Upper surfaces of the toes, from the metatarsophalangeal joints to the nails.
rest|Dorsal surfaces of digits of foot.territorio: Superficial fibular nerve (dorsal digital nerves) and deep fibular nerve in the first space; dermatomes L4-S1

rest|Dorsal surfaces of digits of hand.es: Dorsal surfaces of digits of hand
rest|Dorsal surfaces of digits of hand.descripcion: Posterior surfaces of the fingers, over the phalanges and interphalangeal joints.
rest|Dorsal surfaces of digits of hand.territorio: Superficial branch of the radial nerve and dorsal branch of the ulnar nerve (proximal); palmar digital nerves of the median and ulnar nerves (distal); dermatomes C6-C8

rest|Dorsum of foot.descripcion: Upper surface of the foot, from the ankle to the base of the toes.
rest|Dorsum of foot.territorio: Superficial fibular nerve, deep fibular nerve (first space), sural nerve (lateral) and saphenous nerve (medial); dermatomes L4-S1
rest|Dorsum of foot.clinica: Pulse of the dorsalis pedis artery, lateral to the tendon of extensor hallucis longus.

rest|Dorsum of hand.descripcion: Posterior surface of the hand, between the wrist and the base of the fingers; contains the dorsal venous network and extensor tendons.
rest|Dorsum of hand.territorio: Superficial branch of the radial nerve (lateral) and dorsal branch of the ulnar nerve (medial); dermatomes C6-C8
rest|Dorsum of hand.clinica: The dorsal venous network is a usual site for peripheral venous cannulation.

rest|Eminentia conchae.descripcion: Elevation of the medial (cranial) surface of the auricle corresponding to the concha.
rest|Eminentia conchae.territorio: Great auricular and lesser occipital nerves

rest|Eminentia fossae triangularis.descripcion: Elevation of the medial (cranial) surface of the auricle corresponding to the triangular fossa.
rest|Eminentia fossae triangularis.territorio: Great auricular and lesser occipital nerves

rest|Eminentia scaphae.descripcion: Elevation of the medial (cranial) surface of the auricle corresponding to the scapha.
rest|Eminentia scaphae.territorio: Great auricular and lesser occipital nerves

rest|Epigastric region.descripcion: Central upper abdominal region, below the infrasternal angle, between both hypochondriac regions and above the umbilical region.
rest|Epigastric region.clinica: Visceral pain from the stomach, duodenum, pancreas and the onset of appendicitis is projected here.

rest|Eyebrow.descripcion: Arched cutaneous ridge bearing hairs over the supraorbital margin, between the forehead and the upper eyelid.
rest|Eyebrow.funcion: Diverts sweat and light away from the eyes; participates in facial expression.
rest|Eyebrow.clinica: When suturing wounds the eyebrow is not shaved and its border is aligned; loss of the lateral third is associated with hypothyroidism.

rest|Eyelashes.descripcion: Hairs arranged in two or three rows on the free margin of the eyelids.
rest|Eyelashes.funcion: Protect the eye from particles and trigger the blink reflex.
rest|Eyelashes.clinica: Infection of their glands (Zeis, Moll) produces the external stye; trichiasis irritates the cornea.

rest|Femoral triangle.descripcion: Space in the upper thigh bounded by the inguinal ligament, the medial border of sartorius and the medial border of adductor longus.
rest|Femoral triangle.territorio: Femoral branch of the genitofemoral nerve and anterior femoral cutaneous nerves; dermatome L1-L2
rest|Femoral triangle.clinica: Femoral pulse at the mid-inguinal point; access for arterial catheterization and femoral nerve block.

rest|Fossa antihelica.descripcion: Depression of the medial (cranial) surface of the auricle corresponding to the ridge of the antihelix.

rest|Frontal region.descripcion: Region of the forehead, over the frontal bone, between the eyebrows and the hairline.
rest|Frontal region.clinica: Wounds bleed profusely because of the rich vascularization; the forehead flap is used in nasal reconstruction.

rest|Gluteal fold.descripcion: Transverse skin fold that separates the gluteal region from the posterior surface of the thigh.
rest|Gluteal fold.territorio: Posterior femoral cutaneous nerve (inferior gluteal branches); dermatomes S2-S3
rest|Gluteal fold.clinica: Asymmetry of the gluteal folds in the infant suggests developmental dysplasia of the hip.

rest|Gluteal region.descripcion: Region of the buttock, between the iliac crest superiorly and the gluteal fold inferiorly; contains the gluteal muscles.
rest|Gluteal region.territorio: Superior (L1-L3), middle (S1-S3) and inferior (posterior femoral cutaneous) clunial nerves
rest|Gluteal region.clinica: Intramuscular injections are given in the superolateral quadrant to avoid the sciatic nerve.

rest|Greater supraclavicular fossa.descripcion: Depression over the middle third of the clavicle, lateral to the sternocleidomastoid; corresponds to the omoclavicular triangle.
rest|Greater supraclavicular fossa.clinica: Site for supraclavicular brachial plexus block and for palpation of lymph nodes (Virchow's node).
