rest|Hairs of eyebrow.descripcion: Short, thick hairs implanted in the eyebrow, directed laterally.
rest|Hairs of eyebrow.clinica: Madarosis of the lateral third is seen in hypothyroidism and leprosy.

rest|Hairs of head.descripcion: Hairs of the scalp covering the frontal, parietal, temporal and occipital regions.
rest|Hairs of head.clinica: Alopecia patterns point to androgenetic, autoimmune (areata) or fungal (tinea) causes.

rest|Hallucial eminence.descripcion: Medial elevation of the sole of the foot formed by the intrinsic muscles of the great toe, below the first metatarsal.

rest|Heel region.descripcion: Posterior and inferior region of the foot corresponding to the calcaneus and the calcaneal tendon.
rest|Heel region.territorio: Calcaneal branches of the tibial nerve and sural nerve; dermatome S1
rest|Heel region.clinica: Site of plantar fasciitis, retrocalcaneal bursitis and pressure ulcers in bedridden patients.

rest|Helix.descripcion: Rolled free border of the auricle; it arises in the concha (crus of the helix) and surrounds its contour as far as the lobule.
rest|Helix.territorio: Auriculotemporal (anterior), lesser occipital and great auricular nerves
rest|Helix.clinica: Frequent site of skin carcinomas and of chondrodermatitis nodularis due to sun exposure.

rest|Hip region.descripcion: Lateral region of the hip joint, centered on the greater trochanter, between the gluteal region and the thigh.
rest|Hip region.territorio: Lateral femoral cutaneous nerve, iliohypogastric (lateral branch) and superior clunial nerves
rest|Hip region.clinica: The greater trochanter is palpable; trochanteric bursitis in lateral hip pain.

rest|Hypochondriac region.descripcion: Lateral upper abdominal region, below the costal margin, lateral to the midclavicular line; right (liver, gallbladder) and left (spleen).
rest|Hypochondriac region.clinica: Murphy's sign on the right (cholecystitis); palpable splenomegaly on the left.

rest|Hypogastric region.descripcion: Central lower abdominal region (hypogastrium), between both inguinal regions, below the umbilical region and above the pubic symphysis.
rest|Hypogastric region.clinica: Pain from the bladder, uterus and sigmoid colon; route for suprapubic bladder puncture.

rest|Infra-orbital region.descripcion: Region of the face below the infraorbital margin, between the nasal, buccal and zygomatic regions.
rest|Infra-orbital region.clinica: Infraorbital nerve block at its foramen; hypoesthesia indicates a fracture of the orbital floor.

rest|Infraclavicular fossa.descripcion: Depression below the lateral third of the clavicle, between the deltoid and pectoralis major (deltopectoral triangle).
rest|Infraclavicular fossa.clinica: Landmark for the coracoid process, the cephalic vein and the infraclavicular brachial plexus block.

rest|Inframammary region.descripcion: Anterior thoracic region below the mammary region, as far as the costal margin.
rest|Inframammary region.territorio: Intercostal nerves T5-T7 (anterior and lateral cutaneous branches)
rest|Inframammary region.clinica: The inframammary fold is the usual approach route in breast augmentation.

rest|Infrascapular region.descripcion: Region of the back below the inferior angle of the scapula, lateral to the vertebral region and extending to the lumbar region.
rest|Infrascapular region.territorio: Posterior branches and lateral cutaneous branches of thoracic nerves T7-T12
rest|Infrascapular region.clinica: Auscultation of the lung bases; dullness on percussion in pleural effusion.

rest|Inguinal region.descripcion: Inferolateral abdominal region, on both sides of the pubic region, next to the inguinal ligament; contains the inguinal canal.
rest|Inguinal region.territorio: Ilioinguinal and iliohypogastric nerves; dermatome L1
rest|Inguinal region.clinica: Site of direct and indirect inguinal hernias.

rest|Interscapular region.descripcion: Region of the back between the medial borders of both scapulae.
rest|Interscapular region.territorio: Posterior branches of thoracic nerves T2-T7
rest|Interscapular region.clinica: Sudden interscapular pain suggests aortic dissection; pain referred from the gallbladder and esophagus.

rest|Intertragic incisure.descripcion: Notch between the tragus and the antitragus, in the lower part of the concha.

rest|Labial commissure.descripcion: Lateral junction of the upper and lower lips at the angle of the mouth.
rest|Labial commissure.territorio: Infraorbital nerve and mental nerve (V2, V3)
rest|Labial commissure.clinica: Site of angular cheilitis (vitamin deficiency, candidiasis).

rest|Lateral bicipital groove.descripcion: Longitudinal groove of the arm between the lateral border of the biceps and the brachialis; traversed superiorly by the cephalic vein.
rest|Lateral bicipital groove.territorio: Inferior lateral cutaneous nerve of the arm; dermatome C5
rest|Lateral bicipital groove.clinica: Landmark for locating the cephalic vein.

rest|Lateral border of foot.descripcion: Outer border of the foot, from the heel to the fifth toe; it rests on the ground.
rest|Lateral border of foot.territorio: Sural nerve (lateral dorsal cutaneous); dermatome S1
rest|Lateral border of foot.clinica: The tuberosity of the fifth metatarsal is palpable; criterion of the Ottawa rules.

rest|Lateral border of forearm.descripcion: Radial border of the forearm, traversed by the brachioradialis, from the lateral epicondyle to the styloid process of the radius.
rest|Lateral border of forearm.territorio: Lateral cutaneous nerve of the forearm (musculocutaneous); dermatome C6
rest|Lateral border of forearm.clinica: The cephalic vein runs along this border, useful for venous access.

rest|Lateral malleolus.descripcion: Distal prominence of the fibula on the lateral surface of the ankle, lower and more posterior than the medial malleolus.
rest|Lateral malleolus.clinica: Tenderness on palpation (posterior border and tip) indicates radiography according to the Ottawa rules.

rest|Lateral part of longitudinal arch o.es: Lateral part of longitudinal arch of foot
rest|Lateral part of longitudinal arch o.descripcion: Low arch formed by the calcaneus, cuboid and fourth and fifth metatarsals, in almost complete contact with the ground.
rest|Lateral part of longitudinal arch o.clinica: Transmits weight during gait; rigid and slightly elevated.

rest|Lateral region of abdomen.descripcion: Middle lateral abdominal region (flank), between the hypochondriac and inguinal regions, lateral to the midclavicular line.
rest|Lateral region of abdomen.territorio: Intercostal nerves T9-T11 and subcostal nerve
rest|Lateral region of abdomen.clinica: Flank ecchymosis (Grey Turner's sign) in hemorrhagic pancreatitis or retroperitoneal hemorrhage.

rest|Lateral region of neck.descripcion: Posterior cervical triangle: between the sternocleidomastoid, the trapezius and the clavicle.
rest|Lateral region of neck.territorio: Lesser occipital, great auricular, transverse cervical and supraclavicular nerves (C2-C4)
rest|Lateral region of neck.clinica: The accessory nerve is superficial here and is injured in lymph node biopsies.

rest|Lateral region of thorax.descripcion: Lateral costal region between the anterior and posterior axillary lines, below the axilla.
rest|Lateral region of thorax.territorio: Lateral cutaneous branches of intercostal nerves; dermatomes T3-T8
rest|Lateral region of thorax.clinica: Safety triangle for placing chest drainage tubes (5th intercostal space, midaxillary line).

rest|Lateral retromalleolar region.descripcion: Region between the lateral malleolus and the calcaneal tendon; contains the fibular tendons and the sural nerve.
rest|Lateral retromalleolar region.clinica: Dislocation of the fibular tendons; sural nerve block.

rest|Lesser supraclavicular fossa.descripcion: Small depression over the sternoclavicular joint, between the sternal and clavicular heads of the sternocleidomastoid.
rest|Lesser supraclavicular fossa.clinica: Landmark for central puncture of the internal jugular vein.

rest|Lobule of auricle.descripcion: Soft inferior portion of the auricle, without cartilage, formed by fibroadipose tissue.
rest|Lobule of auricle.clinica: Site of cosmetic piercing and of capillary blood sampling; keloids after piercing.

rest|Lumbar region.descripcion: Dorsal region between the twelfth rib and the iliac crest, lateral to the vertebral region.
rest|Lumbar region.territorio: Posterior branches of lumbar nerves and T12; superior clunial nerves
rest|Lumbar region.clinica: Renal punch percussion (Giordano's sign) over the costovertebral angle.

rest|Mammary region.descripcion: Anterior thoracic region corresponding to the breast, approximately from the 2nd to the 6th rib.
rest|Mammary region.territorio: Intercostal nerves T2-T6; nipple in dermatome T4
rest|Mammary region.clinica: Breast examination by quadrants; the superolateral quadrant harbors most carcinomas.

rest|Mastoid region.descripcion: Retroauricular region corresponding to the mastoid process of the temporal bone.
rest|Mastoid region.territorio: Great auricular and lesser occipital nerves (C2-C3)
rest|Mastoid region.clinica: Retroauricular ecchymosis (Battle's sign) in skull base fracture; mastoiditis.

rest|Medial bicipital groove.descripcion: Longitudinal groove of the arm between the biceps and the triceps; traversed by the brachial artery, median nerve and basilic vein.
rest|Medial bicipital groove.territorio: Medial cutaneous nerve of the arm and intercostobrachial nerve; dermatome T1-T2
rest|Medial bicipital groove.clinica: Site for compression of the brachial artery to control hemorrhage and for blood pressure measurement.

rest|Medial border of foot.descripcion: Inner border of the foot, from the heel to the great toe; arched by the medial longitudinal arch.
rest|Medial border of foot.territorio: Saphenous nerve (proximal) and medial plantar nerve; dermatome L4-L5
rest|Medial border of foot.clinica: The tuberosity of the navicular and the base of the first metatarsal are palpated.

rest|Medial border of forearm.descripcion: Ulnar border of the forearm, from the medial epicondyle to the styloid process of the ulna; the posterior border of the ulna is subcutaneous.
rest|Medial border of forearm.territorio: Medial cutaneous nerve of the forearm; dermatome C8
rest|Medial border of forearm.clinica: The subcutaneous border of the ulna is palpable along its entire length (parry fractures).

rest|Medial malleolus.descripcion: Distal prominence of the tibia on the medial surface of the ankle.
rest|Medial malleolus.clinica: Ottawa rules; the great saphenous vein passes anterior to it, a site for venous cutdown.

rest|Medial part of longitudinal arch of.es: Medial part of longitudinal arch of foot
rest|Medial part of longitudinal arch of.descripcion: High arch formed by the calcaneus, talus, navicular, three cuneiforms and the first three metatarsals; supported by tibialis posterior and the plantar aponeurosis.
rest|Medial part of longitudinal arch of.clinica: Its descent causes flatfoot; posterior tibial dysfunction is a frequent cause in adults.

rest|Medial retromalleolar region.descripcion: Region between the medial malleolus and the calcaneal tendon; contains the tarsal tunnel with flexor tendons, posterior tibial vessels and the tibial nerve.
rest|Medial retromalleolar region.territorio: Medial calcaneal branches of the tibial nerve and saphenous nerve
rest|Medial retromalleolar region.clinica: Posterior tibial pulse; entrapment of the tibial nerve in tarsal tunnel syndrome.

rest|Mental region.descripcion: Region of the chin, below the mentolabial sulcus, over the symphysis and mental protuberance.
rest|Mental region.clinica: Mental nerve block at the mental foramen, below the second premolar.

rest|Mentolabial sulcus.descripcion: Transverse groove that separates the lower lip from the mental region.

rest|Metatarsal region.descripcion: Region of the foot corresponding to the metatarsals, between the tarsus and the toes.
rest|Metatarsal region.territorio: Dorsal: superficial and deep fibular nerves; plantar: medial and lateral plantar nerves
rest|Metatarsal region.clinica: Stress fractures (march fractures) and Morton's neuroma between the 3rd and 4th metatarsals.

rest|Muscular triangle.descripcion: Subdivision of the anterior cervical triangle bounded by the midline of the neck, the superior belly of the omohyoid and the sternocleidomastoid; contains the infrahyoid muscles and the thyroid.
rest|Muscular triangle.clinica: Corresponds to the field of thyroidectomy and tracheostomy.

rest|Nail plate.descripcion: Hard, translucent keratin plate over the nail bed on the dorsum of the distal phalanx of the finger.
rest|Nail plate.territorio: Proper palmar digital nerves (median and ulnar)
rest|Nail plate.clinica: Clubbing, koilonychia and Beau's lines point to systemic diseases.

rest|Nail plate (foot).descripcion: Keratin plate over the nail bed on the dorsum of the distal phalanx of the toes.
rest|Nail plate (foot).territorio: Dorsal digital nerves (fibular) and plantar nerves
rest|Nail plate (foot).clinica: Ingrown nail (onychocryptosis) common on the great toe; onychomycosis.

rest|Nasal region.descripcion: Region of the external nose, from the root between the orbits to the nasolabial sulcus.
rest|Nasal region.territorio: Infratrochlear and external nasal nerves (V1) and infraorbital nerve (V2)
rest|Nasal region.clinica: Vesicles on the tip of the nose (Hutchinson's sign) predict ocular involvement in herpes zoster.

rest|Nasolabial sulcus.descripcion: Oblique groove from the ala of the nose to the angle of the mouth, between the cheek and the upper lip.
rest|Nasolabial sulcus.clinica: Its unilateral flattening is a sign of facial paralysis.

rest|Occipital region.descripcion: Posterior region of the head over the occipital bone, from the superior nuchal line to the lambdoid sutures.
rest|Occipital region.territorio: Greater occipital nerve (C2) and lesser occipital nerve
rest|Occipital region.clinica: Greater occipital nerve block in occipital neuralgia and headaches.

rest|Oral region.descripcion: Region of the mouth and lips, bounded by the nasolabial sulci and the mentolabial sulcus.
rest|Oral region.territorio: Infraorbital nerve (upper lip) and mental nerve (lower lip)

rest|Orbital region.descripcion: Region of the face corresponding to the orbit, the eyeball and the eyelids.
rest|Orbital region.territorio: Supraorbital, supratrochlear, infratrochlear, lacrimal (V1) and infraorbital (V2) nerves
rest|Orbital region.clinica: Bilateral periorbital hematoma (raccoon eyes) suggests an anterior skull base fracture.

rest|Palm.descripcion: Anterior surface of the hand, between the wrist and the fingers; with thenar and hypothenar eminences and a central concavity.
rest|Palm.territorio: Palmar branch of the median nerve (lateral) and of the ulnar nerve (medial); dermatomes C6-C8
rest|Palm.clinica: Infections of the palmar spaces; an atrophic thenar eminence suggests carpal tunnel syndrome.

rest|Palmar surfaces of digits of hand.es: Palmar surfaces of digits of hand
rest|Palmar surfaces of digits of hand.descripcion: Anterior surfaces of the fingers, with flexion creases and finger pads.
rest|Palmar surfaces of digits of hand.territorio: Palmar digital nerves of the median (lateral 3 and a half digits) and ulnar nerves; dermatomes C6-C8
rest|Palmar surfaces of digits of hand.clinica: Two-point discrimination is tested in wounds; felon in the finger pad.

rest|Parietal region.descripcion: Region of the cranial vault over the parietal bones, between the frontal, occipital and temporal regions.
rest|Parietal region.territorio: Supraorbital, auriculotemporal and greater occipital nerves

rest|Parotideomasseteric region.descripcion: Lateral region of the face over the parotid gland and the masseter muscle, in front of the ear.
rest|Parotideomasseteric region.territorio: Great auricular nerve (C2-C3) and auriculotemporal nerve (V3)
rest|Parotideomasseteric region.clinica: The facial nerve passes through the parotid; risk of injury in parotidectomy.

rest|Pectoral region.descripcion: Anterior thoracic region corresponding to the pectoralis major muscle, below the clavicle.
rest|Pectoral region.territorio: Supraclavicular nerves and anterior cutaneous branches of intercostal nerves T2-T6
rest|Pectoral region.clinica: Usual site for pacemaker implantation (infraclavicular subcutaneous pocket).

rest|Perionyx.descripcion: Band of epidermis that covers the proximal border of the nail plate (cuticle/eponychium) on the fingers.
rest|Perionyx.clinica: Its injury favors acute or chronic paronychia.

rest|Perionyx (foot).descripcion: Band of epidermis that covers the proximal border of the nail plate on the toes.
rest|Perionyx (foot).territorio: Dorsal digital nerves of the foot
rest|Perionyx (foot).clinica: Paronychia, often associated with an ingrown nail.

rest|Philtrum.descripcion: Midline vertical groove of the upper lip, between the nasal septum and the tubercle of the upper lip, bounded by two ridges.
rest|Philtrum.clinica: Its flattening is a feature of fetal alcohol syndrome; affected in cleft lip.

rest|Plantar surfaces of digits of foot.es: Plantar surfaces of digits of foot
rest|Plantar surfaces of digits of foot.descripcion: Inferior surfaces of the toes, weight-bearing during gait.
rest|Plantar surfaces of digits of foot.territorio: Plantar digital nerves from the medial and lateral plantar nerves; dermatomes L5-S1

rest|Popliteal fossa.descripcion: Rhomboid space posterior to the knee bounded by biceps femoris, semimembranosus and semitendinosus above and both heads of the gastrocnemius below.
rest|Popliteal fossa.territorio: Posterior femoral cutaneous nerve; dermatomes S1-S2
rest|Popliteal fossa.clinica: Popliteal pulse (deep, with the knee flexed); Baker's cyst.

rest|Posterior auricular groove.descripcion: Shallow groove that separates the antihelix from the antitragus.

rest|Posterior region of arm.descripcion: Posterior surface of the arm, corresponding to the triceps brachii.
rest|Posterior region of arm.territorio: Posterior cutaneous nerve of the arm (radial) and superior lateral cutaneous nerve (axillary); dermatomes C5-C8
rest|Posterior region of arm.clinica: The radial nerve crosses the radial groove of the humerus; at risk in shaft fractures.

rest|Posterior region of elbow.descripcion: Posterior surface of the elbow, centered on the olecranon and both epicondyles.
rest|Posterior region of elbow.territorio: Posterior cutaneous nerve of the forearm (radial); dermatome C7
rest|Posterior region of elbow.clinica: Hueter's triangle (olecranon and epicondyles) to assess dislocations; olecranon bursitis; ulnar nerve behind the medial epicondyle.

rest|Posterior region of forearm.descripcion: Dorsal surface of the forearm; contains the extensor-supinator muscles.
rest|Posterior region of forearm.territorio: Posterior cutaneous nerve of the forearm (radial); dermatomes C6-C8
rest|Posterior region of forearm.clinica: Thompson approach to the radius; lateral epicondyle tendinopathy.

rest|Posterior region of knee.descripcion: Posterior surface of the knee; includes the popliteal fossa.
rest|Posterior region of knee.territorio: Posterior femoral cutaneous nerve; dermatomes S1-S2

rest|Posterior region of leg.descripcion: Posterior surface of the leg (calf), formed by the triceps surae.
rest|Posterior region of leg.territorio: Sural, saphenous and posterior femoral cutaneous nerves; dermatomes L5-S2
rest|Posterior region of leg.clinica: Thompson test for rupture of the calcaneal tendon; deep vein thrombosis.

rest|Posterior region of neck.descripcion: Nape: posterior region of the neck between the anterior borders of the trapezius, from the occiput to C7.
rest|Posterior region of neck.territorio: Posterior branches of C2-C5 (greater occipital and third occipital)
rest|Posterior region of neck.clinica: The spinous process of C7 (vertebra prominens) is the palpable landmark.

rest|Posterior region of thigh.descripcion: Posterior surface of the thigh, from the gluteal fold to the popliteal fossa; contains the hamstrings and the sciatic nerve.
rest|Posterior region of thigh.territorio: Posterior femoral cutaneous nerve; dermatomes S1-S2
rest|Posterior region of thigh.clinica: Frequent hamstring muscle injuries in athletes.

rest|Posterior region of wrist.descripcion: Dorsal surface of the wrist beneath the extensor retinaculum; includes the anatomical snuffbox laterally.
rest|Posterior region of wrist.territorio: Superficial branch of the radial nerve and dorsal branch of the ulnar nerve; dermatomes C6-C8
rest|Posterior region of wrist.clinica: Pain in the anatomical snuffbox suggests scaphoid fracture; De Quervain's tenosynovitis.

rest|Presternal region.descripcion: Middle anterior thoracic region corresponding to the sternum.
rest|Presternal region.territorio: Anterior cutaneous branches of intercostal nerves T2-T6
rest|Presternal region.clinica: Chest compression point in CPR (lower half of the sternum); sternal angle as the landmark of the 2nd rib.

rest|Proximal transverse arch of foot.descripcion: Transverse arch at the level of the cuneiforms, the cuboid and the metatarsal bases; supported by fibularis longus and tibialis posterior.

rest|Pubic hairs.descripcion: Terminal hairs of the pubic and external genital region, which appear at puberty.
rest|Pubic hairs.clinica: Its development is assessed with the Tanner stages.

rest|Radial foveola.descripcion: Dorsolateral depression of the carpus between the tendons of extensor pollicis longus and those of abductor pollicis longus and extensor pollicis brevis.
rest|Radial foveola.territorio: Superficial branch of the radial nerve; dermatome C6
rest|Radial foveola.clinica: Tenderness on palpation suggests scaphoid fracture; the radial artery is palpated at its floor.

rest|Sacral region.descripcion: Middle dorsal region corresponding to the sacrum, between both gluteal regions.
rest|Sacral region.clinica: Frequent site of pressure ulcers; access for caudal block through the sacral hiatus.

rest|Scapha.descripcion: Elongated groove between the helix and the antihelix.
rest|Scapha.territorio: Great auricular and lesser occipital nerves

rest|Scapular region.descripcion: Region of the back corresponding to the scapula and its muscles.
rest|Scapular region.territorio: Posterior branches of upper thoracic nerves and supraclavicular nerves; dermatomes C4-T2
rest|Scapular region.clinica: The inferior angle of the scapula marks approximately the level of T7; winged scapula in long thoracic nerve injury.

rest|Sole.descripcion: Inferior surface of the foot, from the heel to the toes.
rest|Sole.territorio: Medial and lateral plantar nerves, calcaneal branches of the tibial nerve; dermatomes L4-S1
rest|Sole.clinica: Plantar response (Babinski reflex) elicited by stimulating its lateral border.

rest|Sternocleidomastoid region.descripcion: Region of the neck corresponding to the sternocleidomastoid muscle, between the anterior and lateral cervical regions.
rest|Sternocleidomastoid region.territorio: Transverse cervical, great auricular and supraclavicular nerves (C2-C4)
rest|Sternocleidomastoid region.clinica: Landmark for puncture of the internal jugular vein; congenital muscular torticollis.

rest|Submandibular triangle.descripcion: Triangle bounded by the inferior border of the mandible and both bellies of the digastric; contains the submandibular gland.
rest|Submandibular triangle.clinica: Bimanual palpation of the submandibular gland and its stones; lymphadenopathy.

rest|Submental triangle.descripcion: Unpaired triangle beneath the chin, between both anterior bellies of the digastric and the hyoid bone.
rest|Submental triangle.clinica: Contains submental lymph nodes that drain the lower lip, chin and tip of the tongue.

rest|Temporal region.descripcion: Lateral region of the head over the temporal fossa and the temporalis muscle, above the zygomatic arch.
rest|Temporal region.clinica: Pulse of the superficial temporal artery in front of the tragus; biopsy in giant cell arteritis; pterion.

rest|Tragus.descripcion: Small cartilaginous tongue in front of the concha that partially covers the opening of the external acoustic meatus.
rest|Tragus.clinica: Pain on pressure of the tragus suggests otitis externa; the superficial temporal artery is palpated in front of it.

rest|Triangle of auscultation.descripcion: Area of the back between the lateral border of the trapezius, the superior border of the latissimus dorsi and the medial border of the scapula.
rest|Triangle of auscultation.territorio: Posterior branches of thoracic nerves T6-T7
rest|Triangle of auscultation.clinica: Sparse musculature: best lung auscultation with the scapula abducted; route for blocks and thoracotomy.

rest|Triangular fossa.descripcion: Depression between the superior and inferior crura of the antihelix.

rest|Tubercle of upper lip.descripcion: Small median prominence of the red border of the upper lip, at the end of the philtrum.
rest|Tubercle of upper lip.clinica: Alignment landmark in cleft lip repair.

rest|Umbilical region.descripcion: Central middle abdominal region around the umbilicus, between both lateral regions, the epigastric and the pubic regions.
rest|Umbilical region.territorio: Intercostal nerve T10 (dermatome of the umbilicus)
rest|Umbilical region.clinica: Initial periumbilical pain of appendicitis and of small intestine disease.

rest|Umbilicus.descripcion: Depressed scar of the anterior abdominal wall in the linea alba, remnant of the umbilical cord; usually at the L3-L4 level.
rest|Umbilicus.clinica: Umbilical hernias; periumbilical ecchymosis (Cullen's sign); access route in laparoscopy.

rest|Urogenital region.descripcion: Anterior, triangular part of the perineum, between the pubic symphysis and the line joining the ischial tuberosities.
rest|Urogenital region.territorio: Pudendal nerve (perineal nerve), ilioinguinal nerve and genital branch of the genitofemoral nerve; dermatomes S2-S4
rest|Urogenital region.clinica: Episiotomy and pudendal nerve block in obstetrics.

rest|Vertebral region.descripcion: Middle dorsal region corresponding to the vertebral column and the adjacent erector musculature.
rest|Vertebral region.territorio: Posterior branches of segmental spinal nerves
rest|Vertebral region.clinica: The spinous processes are palpable; Tuffier's line (iliac crests, L4) guides lumbar puncture.

rest|Zygomatic region.descripcion: Region of the cheekbone over the zygomatic bone and its arch, between the orbital, temporal and infraorbital regions.
rest|Zygomatic region.clinica: Fractures of the zygomatic complex with malar flattening and infraorbital hypoesthesia.

rest|Anserine bursa.descripcion: Bursa located on the medial surface of the proximal tibia, between the pes anserinus and the tibial collateral ligament.
rest|Anserine bursa.territorio: Separates the tendons of sartorius, gracilis and semitendinosus from the tibial collateral ligament and the tibia.
rest|Anserine bursa.funcion: Reduces friction of the pes anserinus tendons over the tibia and the medial collateral ligament.
rest|Anserine bursa.clinica: Anserine bursitis causes medial knee pain below the joint line, frequent in runners, obesity and knee osteoarthritis.

rest|Antebrachial fascia.descripcion: Deep fascia that encloses the forearm musculature, continuation of the brachial fascia.
rest|Antebrachial fascia.origen: Humeral epicondyles, olecranon and continuity with the brachial fascia.
rest|Antebrachial fascia.destino: Posterior border of the ulna; it thickens distally forming the retinacula of the wrist.
rest|Antebrachial fascia.territorio: Anterior (flexor) and posterior (extensor) compartments of the forearm.
rest|Antebrachial fascia.funcion: Contains the forearm muscles, gives origin to muscle fibers and forms the flexor and extensor retinacula.
rest|Antebrachial fascia.clinica: Its limited distensibility favors forearm compartment syndrome after fractures or ischemia (Volkmann's contracture).

rest|Anterior intermuscular septum of le.descripcion: Fibrous sheet running from the crural fascia to the anterior border of the fibula.
rest|Anterior intermuscular septum of le.origen: Deep surface of the crural fascia.
rest|Anterior intermuscular septum of le.territorio: Separates the anterior (extensor) compartment from the lateral (fibular) compartment of the leg.
rest|Anterior intermuscular septum of le.funcion: Delimits compartments and gives origin to fibers of the extensor and fibular muscles.
rest|Anterior intermuscular septum of le.clinica: It must be taken into account in fasciotomy of the anterior and lateral compartments in compartment syndrome.

rest|Anterior layer of thoracolumbar fas.descripcion: Thin layer covering the anterior surface of the quadratus lumborum.
rest|Anterior layer of thoracolumbar fas.origen: Anterior surface of the lumbar transverse processes.
rest|Anterior layer of thoracolumbar fas.destino: Joins laterally with the other layers and with the origin of the transversus abdominis; inferiorly to the iliac crest.
rest|Anterior layer of thoracolumbar fas.territorio: Covers the anterior surface of the quadratus lumborum muscle.
rest|Anterior layer of thoracolumbar fas.funcion: Encloses the quadratus lumborum and participates in the aponeurosis of origin of the transversus abdominis.

rest|Bicipitoradial bursa.descripcion: Bursa located between the distal tendon of the biceps brachii and the anterior part of the radial tuberosity.
rest|Bicipitoradial bursa.territorio: Separates the biceps brachii tendon from the radial tuberosity.
rest|Bicipitoradial bursa.funcion: Reduces friction of the biceps tendon over the radius during pronation and supination.
rest|Bicipitoradial bursa.clinica: Its bursitis produces pain and swelling in the cubital fold and may compress the posterior interosseous nerve.

rest|Brachial fascia.descripcion: Deep fascia that encloses the arm muscles, continuous with the deltoid, pectoral, axillary and antebrachial fasciae.
rest|Brachial fascia.origen: Continuity with the deltoid, pectoral and axillary fasciae.
rest|Brachial fascia.destino: Humeral epicondyles and olecranon; it continues with the antebrachial fascia.
rest|Brachial fascia.territorio: Sends out the medial and lateral intermuscular septa that separate the anterior and posterior compartments of the arm.
rest|Brachial fascia.funcion: Contains and compartmentalizes the arm musculature.
rest|Brachial fascia.clinica: It may participate in compartment syndrome of the arm, uncommon, after severe trauma.

rest|Bursa of piriformis muscle.descripcion: Bursa located between the piriformis tendon and the superior border of the greater trochanter or the hip capsule.
rest|Bursa of piriformis muscle.territorio: Tendon of the piriformis muscle at its trochanteric insertion.
rest|Bursa of piriformis muscle.funcion: Reduces friction of the piriformis tendon over the femur.

rest|Clavipectoral fascia.descripcion: Fascial sheet located beneath pectoralis major, enclosing the subclavius and pectoralis minor.
rest|Clavipectoral fascia.destino: Coracoid process and axillary fascia (suspensory ligament of the axilla).
rest|Clavipectoral fascia.territorio: Encloses subclavius and pectoralis minor; the cephalic vein, thoracoacromial artery and lateral pectoral nerve pierce it.
rest|Clavipectoral fascia.funcion: Forms the anterior wall of the axilla and suspends the axillary fascia.
rest|Clavipectoral fascia.clinica: Its costocoracoid portion is a surgical landmark for locating the cephalic vein and the thoracoacromial vessels.

rest|Common flexor tendon sheath.descripcion: Synovial sheath (ulnar bursa) that encloses the superficial and deep flexor tendons in the carpal tunnel.
rest|Common flexor tendon sheath.territorio: Tendons of flexor digitorum superficialis and profundus; it usually continues with the sheath of the little finger.
rest|Common flexor tendon sheath.funcion: Allows the flexor tendons to glide beneath the flexor retinaculum.
rest|Common flexor tendon sheath.clinica: Infections of the little finger may spread to this bursa (horseshoe abscess if it communicates with the thumb sheath).

rest|Common tendon sheath of fibularis m.es: Common tendon sheath of fibularis muscles
rest|Common tendon sheath of fibularis m.descripcion: Synovial sheath that encloses the tendons of fibularis longus and brevis behind the lateral malleolus.
rest|Common tendon sheath of fibularis m.territorio: Tendons of the fibularis longus and fibularis brevis muscles.
rest|Common tendon sheath of fibularis m.funcion: Facilitates gliding of the fibular tendons in the lateral retromalleolar groove.
rest|Common tendon sheath of fibularis m.clinica: Site of fibular tenosynovitis and of longitudinal tears of fibularis brevis after ankle sprains.

rest|Coracobrachial bursa.descripcion: Bursa located between the common tendon of the coracobrachialis and short head of the biceps and the subscapularis.
rest|Coracobrachial bursa.territorio: Separates the coracoid conjoined tendon from the subscapularis muscle.
rest|Coracobrachial bursa.funcion: Reduces friction between the conjoined tendon and the subscapularis during shoulder movements.

rest|Cruciform part of fibrous sheath of.es: Cruciform part of fibrous sheath of digit of hand
rest|Cruciform part of fibrous sheath of.la: Pars cruciformis vaginae fibrosae digitorum manus
rest|Cruciform part of fibrous sheath of.descripcion: Thin crossed fibers (C pulleys) of the digital fibrous sheath, located over the interphalangeal joints.
rest|Cruciform part of fibrous sheath of.origen: Borders of the phalanges and palmar plates.
rest|Cruciform part of fibrous sheath of.destino: Opposite side of the phalanx or palmar plate, crossing over the tendons.
rest|Cruciform part of fibrous sheath of.territorio: Tendons of flexor digitorum superficialis and profundus.
rest|Cruciform part of fibrous sheath of.funcion: They keep the flexor tendons applied to the bone while allowing flexion of the joints.

rest|Crural fascia.descripcion: Deep fascia that encloses the leg musculature, continuation of the fascia lata.
rest|Crural fascia.origen: Continuity with the fascia lata and popliteal fascia; tibial condyles, head of the fibula.
rest|Crural fascia.destino: Medial surface of the tibia; distally it forms the retinacula of the ankle.
rest|Crural fascia.territorio: By means of intermuscular septa it forms the anterior, lateral, superficial posterior and deep posterior compartments.
rest|Crural fascia.funcion: Contains the leg musculature, promotes venous return and forms the retinacula of the ankle.
rest|Crural fascia.clinica: Its inextensibility is the basis of acute and chronic compartment syndrome of the leg, treated with fasciotomy.

rest|Deep infrapatellar bursa.descripcion: Bursa located between the patellar ligament and the anterior surface of the tibia, over the tuberosity.
rest|Deep infrapatellar bursa.territorio: Separates the patellar ligament from the tibia and from the infrapatellar fat pad.
rest|Deep infrapatellar bursa.funcion: Reduces friction of the patellar ligament over the tibia.
rest|Deep infrapatellar bursa.clinica: Its inflammation often accompanies patellar tendinopathy and Osgood-Schlatter disease.

rest|Deltoid fascia.descripcion: Fascia that covers the deltoid muscle and sends septa between its fascicles.
rest|Deltoid fascia.origen: Clavicle, acromion and spine of the scapula.
rest|Deltoid fascia.destino: It continues with the pectoral, infraspinous and brachial fasciae.

rest|Diaphragmatic fascia.descripcion: Fascia lining the abdominal (inferior) surface of the diaphragm, part of the endoabdominal fascia.
rest|Diaphragmatic fascia.territorio: Inferior surface of the diaphragm; continuous with the transversalis fascia.
rest|Diaphragmatic fascia.funcion: Covers the diaphragm and separates its musculature from the extraperitoneal space.

rest|Dorsal fascia of hand.descripcion: Thin fascia of the dorsum of the hand, continuation of the extensor retinaculum.
rest|Dorsal fascia of hand.destino: Metacarpals and extensor expansions of the fingers.
rest|Dorsal fascia of hand.territorio: Covers the extensor tendons and the dorsal interossei muscles.
rest|Dorsal fascia of hand.funcion: Contains the extensor tendons on the dorsum of the hand.

rest|Epicranial aponeurosis.descripcion: Strong tendinous sheet covering the cranial vault, uniting the frontal and occipital bellies of the occipitofrontalis.
rest|Epicranial aponeurosis.origen: Occipital bellies and supreme nuchal line.
rest|Epicranial aponeurosis.destino: Frontal bellies; laterally the temporal fascia.
rest|Epicranial aponeurosis.territorio: Intermediate layer of the scalp, over the loose subaponeurotic areolar tissue.
rest|Epicranial aponeurosis.funcion: Transmits the traction of the occipitofrontalis to raise the eyebrows and move the scalp.
rest|Epicranial aponeurosis.clinica: Wounds that sever it gape widely; hematomas and subgaleal infections accumulate beneath it.

rest|Extensor retinaculum of wrist.descripcion: Oblique fibrous band on the dorsum of the wrist that forms six compartments for the extensor tendons.
rest|Extensor retinaculum of wrist.origen: Anterolateral border of the distal end of the radius.
rest|Extensor retinaculum of wrist.destino: Pisiform, triquetrum and ulnar styloid (without attaching to the ulna).
rest|Extensor retinaculum of wrist.territorio: Six osteofibrous tunnels for the extensor tendons and abductor pollicis longus.
rest|Extensor retinaculum of wrist.funcion: Prevents bowstringing of the extensor tendons during wrist extension.
rest|Extensor retinaculum of wrist.clinica: De Quervain's tenosynovitis occurs in the first compartment.

rest|Fascia lata.descripcion: Thick deep fascia that encloses the thigh; laterally it thickens forming the iliotibial tract.
rest|Fascia lata.origen: Inguinal ligament, iliac crest, sacrum, coccyx, sacrotuberous ligament, pubis and ischium.
rest|Fascia lata.destino: Patella, tibial condyles and head of the fibula; it continues with the crural fascia.
rest|Fascia lata.territorio: By means of intermuscular septa it forms the anterior, medial and posterior compartments of the thigh.
rest|Fascia lata.funcion: Contains the thigh musculature, limits its expansion and promotes venous return.
rest|Fascia lata.clinica: Its saphenous hiatus allows passage of the great saphenous vein; site of femoral hernias and fascial grafts.

rest|Flexor retinaculum of ankle.descripcion: Fibrous band between the medial malleolus and the calcaneus that closes the tarsal tunnel.
rest|Flexor retinaculum of ankle.destino: Medial surface of the calcaneus and plantar aponeurosis.
rest|Flexor retinaculum of ankle.territorio: Tendons of tibialis posterior, flexor digitorum longus and flexor hallucis longus, posterior tibial neurovascular bundle and tibial nerve.
rest|Flexor retinaculum of ankle.funcion: Keeps the flexor tendons in their medial retromalleolar position.
rest|Flexor retinaculum of ankle.clinica: Its compression of the tibial nerve causes tarsal tunnel syndrome.

rest|Flexor retinaculum of wrist.descripcion: Transverse fibrous band that converts the carpal groove into the carpal tunnel.
rest|Flexor retinaculum of wrist.origen: Pisiform and hook of the hamate.
rest|Flexor retinaculum of wrist.destino: Tubercles of the scaphoid and trapezium.
rest|Flexor retinaculum of wrist.territorio: Carpal tunnel: median nerve and tendons of flexor digitorum superficialis, profundus and flexor pollicis longus.
rest|Flexor retinaculum of wrist.funcion: Keeps the flexor tendons against the carpus and gives origin to the thenar and hypothenar muscles.
rest|Flexor retinaculum of wrist.clinica: Its surgical division is the treatment of carpal tunnel syndrome.

rest|Iliopectineal bursa.descripcion: Large bursa located between the iliopsoas tendon and the iliopubic eminence and hip capsule.
rest|Iliopectineal bursa.territorio: Separates the iliopsoas from the anterior capsule of the hip; it often communicates with the joint.
rest|Iliopectineal bursa.funcion: Reduces friction of the iliopsoas over the pelvis and hip.
rest|Iliopectineal bursa.clinica: Its bursitis causes groin pain and may be associated with internal snapping hip.

rest|Iliopsoas fascia.descripcion: Fascia that lines the psoas major and iliacus muscles, from the lumbar region to the thigh.
rest|Iliopsoas fascia.origen: Lumbar vertebral bodies, iliac crest and arcuate line.
rest|Iliopsoas fascia.destino: Inguinal ligament and lesser trochanter; iliopectineal arch.
rest|Iliopsoas fascia.territorio: Psoas major and iliacus and the femoral nerve, which runs beneath it.
rest|Iliopsoas fascia.funcion: Encloses the iliopsoas and separates the muscular lacuna from the vascular lacuna.
rest|Iliopsoas fascia.clinica: Psoas abscesses spread within it to the groin; basis of the fascia iliaca block.

rest|Iliotibial tract.descripcion: Lateral thickening of the fascia lata that extends from the iliac crest to the tibia.
rest|Iliotibial tract.origen: Tubercle of the iliac crest; it receives the tensor fasciae latae and gluteus maximus.
rest|Iliotibial tract.destino: Gerdy's tubercle on the lateral condyle of the tibia.
rest|Iliotibial tract.territorio: Lateral surface of the thigh and knee.
rest|Iliotibial tract.funcion: Stabilizes the hip and the knee laterally in extension during gait.
rest|Iliotibial tract.clinica: Its friction over the lateral femoral epicondyle produces runner's iliotibial band syndrome.

rest|Inferior extensor retinaculum of an.descripcion: Y-shaped fibrous band on the dorsum of the ankle and tarsus.
rest|Inferior extensor retinaculum of an.origen: Superior surface of the calcaneus (sinus tarsi).
rest|Inferior extensor retinaculum of an.destino: Medial malleolus and medial plantar aponeurosis.
rest|Inferior extensor retinaculum of an.territorio: Tendons of tibialis anterior, extensor hallucis longus, extensor digitorum longus, fibularis tertius and deep fibular nerve.
rest|Inferior extensor retinaculum of an.funcion: Keeps the extensor tendons applied to the ankle during dorsiflexion.
rest|Inferior extensor retinaculum of an.clinica: The deep fibular nerve may be compressed beneath it (anterior tarsal tunnel syndrome).

rest|Inferior fibular retinaculum.descripcion: Fibrous band on the lateral surface of the calcaneus that holds the fibular tendons.
rest|Inferior fibular retinaculum.origen: Inferior extensor retinaculum and lateral surface of the calcaneus.
rest|Inferior fibular retinaculum.destino: Lateral surface of the calcaneus and fibular trochlea.
rest|Inferior fibular retinaculum.territorio: Tendons of fibularis longus and brevis, separated by the fibular trochlea.
rest|Inferior fibular retinaculum.funcion: Keeps the fibular tendons against the calcaneus.

rest|Inferior subtendinous bursa of bice.es: Inferior subtendinous bursa of biceps femoris muscle
rest|Inferior subtendinous bursa of bice.la: Bursa subtendinea musculi bicipitis femoris inferior
rest|Inferior subtendinous bursa of bice.descripcion: Bursa located between the distal tendon of the biceps femoris and the fibular collateral ligament.
rest|Inferior subtendinous bursa of bice.territorio: Separates the biceps femoris tendon from the fibular collateral ligament.
rest|Inferior subtendinous bursa of bice.funcion: Reduces friction of the biceps tendon over the lateral collateral ligament.
rest|Inferior subtendinous bursa of bice.clinica: Its bursitis causes lateral knee pain that may be mistaken for collateral ligament injury.

rest|Intermuscular gluteal bursae.descripcion: Bursae located between the gluteus maximus tendon and the origin of the vastus lateralis, next to the linea aspera.
rest|Intermuscular gluteal bursae.territorio: Tendon of the gluteus maximus and vastus lateralis.
rest|Intermuscular gluteal bursae.funcion: Reduce friction between the gluteus maximus and the femur or the vastus lateralis.

rest|Investing abdominal fascia.descripcion: Thin deep fascia that covers the external surface of the external oblique and its aponeurosis.
rest|Investing abdominal fascia.territorio: Muscles of the anterolateral abdominal wall.
rest|Investing abdominal fascia.funcion: Envelops the abdominal musculature; it continues with the external spermatic fascia.

rest|Lateral femoral intermuscular septu.descripcion: Strong fibrous lamina extending from the fascia lata to the lateral lip of the linea aspera.
rest|Lateral femoral intermuscular septu.origen: Deep surface of the fascia lata and iliotibial tract.
rest|Lateral femoral intermuscular septu.destino: Lateral lip of the linea aspera and lateral supracondylar line.
rest|Lateral femoral intermuscular septu.territorio: Separates the anterior compartment (vastus lateralis) from the posterior compartment (biceps femoris).
rest|Lateral femoral intermuscular septu.funcion: Delimits compartments and gives origin to fibers of the vastus lateralis and biceps femoris.
rest|Lateral femoral intermuscular septu.clinica: Landmark in the lateral approach to the femur, where the perforating arteries are ligated.

rest|Lateral intermuscular septum of arm.descripcion: Fibrous lamina extending from the brachial fascia to the lateral border of the humerus.
rest|Lateral intermuscular septum of arm.origen: Insertion of the deltoid and brachial fascia.
rest|Lateral intermuscular septum of arm.destino: Lateral supracondylar ridge and lateral epicondyle of the humerus.
rest|Lateral intermuscular septum of arm.territorio: Separates the anterior and posterior compartments; it is pierced by the radial nerve and the radial collateral artery.
rest|Lateral intermuscular septum of arm.funcion: Delimits compartments and gives insertion to brachialis, brachioradialis, extensor carpi radialis longus and triceps.
rest|Lateral intermuscular septum of arm.clinica: The radial nerve becomes fixed as it pierces it and is vulnerable in distal humeral shaft fractures.

rest|Lateral patellar retinaculum.descripcion: Fibrous expansion of the vastus lateralis and the iliotibial band that connects the patella to the lateral tibia and femur.
rest|Lateral patellar retinaculum.origen: Vastus lateralis, iliotibial tract and lateral border of the patella.
rest|Lateral patellar retinaculum.destino: Lateral condyle of the tibia and lateral femoral epicondyle.
rest|Lateral patellar retinaculum.territorio: Anterolateral aspect of the knee capsule.
rest|Lateral patellar retinaculum.funcion: Stabilizes the patella and reinforces the anterolateral joint capsule.
rest|Lateral patellar retinaculum.clinica: Excessive tension causes lateral patellar compression syndrome; it can be released surgically.

rest|Lateral subtendinous bursa of gastr.es: Lateral subtendinous bursa of gastrocnemius muscle
rest|Lateral subtendinous bursa of gastr.descripcion: Bursa located beneath the origin of the lateral head of the gastrocnemius, over the knee capsule.
rest|Lateral subtendinous bursa of gastr.territorio: Lateral head of the gastrocnemius and posterolateral knee capsule.
rest|Lateral subtendinous bursa of gastr.funcion: Reduces friction between the lateral head of the gastrocnemius and the joint capsule.

rest|Masseteric fascia.descripcion: Fascia covering the masseter muscle, a continuation of the superficial layer of the cervical fascia.
rest|Masseteric fascia.destino: Inferior border and ramus of the mandible; continuous with the parotid fascia.
rest|Masseteric fascia.territorio: Masseter muscle; together with the parotid fascia it forms the parotideomasseteric fascia.
rest|Masseteric fascia.funcion: Encloses the masseter and delimits the masseteric space.
rest|Masseteric fascia.clinica: It delimits the masseteric space, which is involved in odontogenic abscesses of the lower molars.

rest|Medial femoral intermuscular septum.descripcion: Fibrous lamina between the fascia lata and the medial lip of the linea aspera.
rest|Medial femoral intermuscular septum.origen: Deep surface of the fascia lata.
rest|Medial femoral intermuscular septum.destino: Medial lip of the linea aspera.
rest|Medial femoral intermuscular septum.territorio: Separates the anterior compartment (vastus medialis) from the medial compartment (adductors).
rest|Medial femoral intermuscular septum.funcion: Delimits compartments and gives origin to fibers of the vastus medialis.

rest|Medial intermuscular septum of arm.descripcion: Resistant fibrous lamina between the brachial fascia and the medial border of the humerus.
rest|Medial intermuscular septum of arm.origen: Insertion of the coracobrachialis and brachial fascia.
rest|Medial intermuscular septum of arm.destino: Medial supracondylar ridge and medial epicondyle of the humerus.
rest|Medial intermuscular septum of arm.territorio: Separates the anterior and posterior compartments; it is pierced by the ulnar nerve and the superior ulnar collateral artery.
rest|Medial intermuscular septum of arm.funcion: Delimits compartments and gives insertion to brachialis and triceps.
rest|Medial intermuscular septum of arm.clinica: Its distal border (arcade of Struthers) can compress the ulnar nerve after its transposition.

rest|Medial patellar retinaculum.descripcion: Fibrous expansion of the vastus medialis that connects the medial border of the patella to the medial tibia and femur.
rest|Medial patellar retinaculum.origen: Vastus medialis and medial border of the patella.
rest|Medial patellar retinaculum.destino: Medial condyle of the tibia and medial femoral epicondyle.
rest|Medial patellar retinaculum.territorio: Anteromedial aspect of the knee capsule; includes the medial patellofemoral ligament.
rest|Medial patellar retinaculum.funcion: Medially stabilizes the patella and reinforces the anteromedial capsule.
rest|Medial patellar retinaculum.clinica: Injured in lateral patellar dislocation; its reconstruction (MPFL) prevents recurrence.

rest|Medial subtendinous bursa of gastro.es: Medial subtendinous bursa of gastrocnemius muscle
rest|Medial subtendinous bursa of gastro.descripcion: Bursa located beneath the medial head of the gastrocnemius, often communicating with the semimembranosus bursa.
rest|Medial subtendinous bursa of gastro.territorio: Medial head of the gastrocnemius and posteromedial knee capsule.
rest|Medial subtendinous bursa of gastro.funcion: Reduces friction between the medial head of the gastrocnemius and the capsule.
rest|Medial subtendinous bursa of gastro.clinica: Its distension together with that of the semimembranosus bursa forms the Baker popliteal cyst.

rest|Middle layer of thoracolumbar fasci.descripcion: Layer located between the erector spinae and the quadratus lumborum.
rest|Middle layer of thoracolumbar fasci.origen: Tips of the lumbar transverse processes and intertransverse ligaments.
rest|Middle layer of thoracolumbar fasci.destino: Iliac crest and 12th rib; laterally, origin of the transversus abdominis.
rest|Middle layer of thoracolumbar fasci.territorio: Separates the erector spinae muscles from the quadratus lumborum.
rest|Middle layer of thoracolumbar fasci.funcion: Together with the posterior layer it encloses the erector spinae and transmits tension from the transversus abdominis.

rest|Palmar aponeurosis.descripcion: Triangular fibrous lamina in the palm, a continuation of the palmaris longus tendon.
rest|Palmar aponeurosis.origen: Flexor retinaculum and palmaris longus tendon.
rest|Palmar aponeurosis.destino: Digital fibrous sheaths, transverse metacarpal ligaments and skin of the palmar creases.
rest|Palmar aponeurosis.territorio: Covers the long flexor tendons, the palmar arches and the digital nerves.
rest|Palmar aponeurosis.funcion: Protects the deep palmar structures and anchors the palmar skin for gripping.
rest|Palmar aponeurosis.clinica: Its fibrosis and contracture constitute Dupuytren disease.

rest|Pectoral fascia.descripcion: Thin fascia covering the pectoralis major.
rest|Pectoral fascia.destino: Continuous with the axillary, deltoid and abdominal fasciae.
rest|Pectoral fascia.territorio: Pectoralis major muscle; the mammary gland rests upon it.
rest|Pectoral fascia.funcion: Encloses the pectoralis major and forms the retromammary plane.
rest|Pectoral fascia.clinica: Fixation of a breast cancer to it indicates deep infiltration; it is resected in mastectomy.

rest|Piriformis fascia.descripcion: Fascia covering the piriformis muscle on the posterior wall of the lesser pelvis, part of the parietal pelvic fascia.
rest|Piriformis fascia.territorio: Piriformis muscle and the sacral plexus, which runs over it.
rest|Piriformis fascia.funcion: Lines the piriformis and forms part of the parietal pelvic fascia.

rest|Plantar aponeurosis.descripcion: Thick fibrous lamina of the sole of the foot, from the calcaneus to the toes.
rest|Plantar aponeurosis.origen: Medial tubercle of the calcaneal tuberosity.
rest|Plantar aponeurosis.destino: Five slips to the digital fibrous sheaths, plantar plates and skin at the base of the toes.
rest|Plantar aponeurosis.territorio: Covers the intrinsic plantar musculature and separates the medial, central and lateral compartments.
rest|Plantar aponeurosis.funcion: Supports the longitudinal arch of the foot (windlass mechanism) and protects the plantar structures.
rest|Plantar aponeurosis.clinica: Its inflammation at the calcaneus (plantar fasciitis) is the most frequent cause of heel pain.

rest|Plantar tendon sheath of fibularis.es: Plantar tendon sheath of fibularis longus muscle
rest|Plantar tendon sheath of fibularis.la: Vagina plantaris tendinis musculi fibularis longi
rest|Plantar tendon sheath of fibularis.descripcion: Synovial sheath enclosing the fibularis longus tendon along its course through the groove of the cuboid on the sole.
rest|Plantar tendon sheath of fibularis.territorio: Fibularis longus tendon in the sole of the foot.
rest|Plantar tendon sheath of fibularis.funcion: Allows the fibularis longus tendon to glide beneath the cuboid toward the first metatarsal.
rest|Plantar tendon sheath of fibularis.clinica: The os peroneum may cause lateral plantar pain in this area.

rest|Popliteal fascia.descripcion: Portion of the deep fascia covering the popliteal fossa, between the fascia lata and the crural fascia.
rest|Popliteal fascia.territorio: Roof of the popliteal fossa: popliteal vessels, tibial and common fibular nerves; the small saphenous vein pierces it.
rest|Popliteal fascia.funcion: Covers and protects the contents of the popliteal fossa.
rest|Popliteal fascia.clinica: Its rigidity makes popliteal masses (aneurysms, cysts) painful and causes them to compress neurovascular structures.

rest|Posterior intermuscular septum of l.descripcion: Fibrous lamina between the crural fascia and the posterior border of the fibula.
rest|Posterior intermuscular septum of l.origen: Deep surface of the crural fascia.
rest|Posterior intermuscular septum of l.territorio: Separates the lateral (fibular) compartment from the posterior (flexor) compartment of the leg.
rest|Posterior intermuscular septum of l.funcion: Delimits compartments and gives origin to fibers of the fibularis muscles and the soleus.

rest|Posterior layer of thoracolumbar fa.descripcion: Thick, superficial layer covering the erector spinae muscles in the thoracic and lumbar regions.
rest|Posterior layer of thoracolumbar fa.origen: Thoracic, lumbar and sacral spinous processes, and supraspinous ligaments.
rest|Posterior layer of thoracolumbar fa.destino: Costal angles, iliac crest; laterally it joins the middle layer.
rest|Posterior layer of thoracolumbar fa.territorio: Covers the erector spinae; gives origin to the latissimus dorsi and serratus posterior inferior.
rest|Posterior layer of thoracolumbar fa.funcion: Contains the erector spinae and transmits forces between the upper limbs, trunk and pelvis.
rest|Posterior layer of thoracolumbar fa.clinica: Implicated in nonspecific low back pain through altered gliding and sensitization.

rest|Sciatic bursa of gluteus maximus mu.es: Sciatic bursa of gluteus maximus muscle
rest|Sciatic bursa of gluteus maximus mu.descripcion: Bursa located between the gluteus maximus and the ischial tuberosity.
rest|Sciatic bursa of gluteus maximus mu.territorio: Separates the gluteus maximus from the ischial tuberosity.
rest|Sciatic bursa of gluteus maximus mu.funcion: Reduces friction of the gluteus maximus over the ischium.
rest|Sciatic bursa of gluteus maximus mu.clinica: Its bursitis (weaver's or tailor's bottom) causes pain when sitting on hard surfaces.

rest|Sciatic bursa of obturator internus.descripcion: Bursa located between the obturator internus tendon and the posterior surface of the ischium, in the lesser sciatic notch.
rest|Sciatic bursa of obturator internus.territorio: Obturator internus tendon where it turns over the ischium.
rest|Sciatic bursa of obturator internus.funcion: Reduces friction of the obturator internus tendon over the lesser sciatic notch.

rest|Semimembranosus bursa.descripcion: Bursa located between the semimembranosus tendon, the medial head of the gastrocnemius and the medial tibial condyle.
rest|Semimembranosus bursa.territorio: Semimembranosus tendon; it often communicates with the medial gastrocnemius bursa and the joint.
rest|Semimembranosus bursa.funcion: Reduces friction of the semimembranosus tendon.
rest|Semimembranosus bursa.clinica: Its distension together with the gastrocnemio-semimembranosus bursa constitutes Baker cyst.

rest|Subacromial bursa.descripcion: Bursa located between the acromion and coracoacromial ligament and the supraspinatus tendon; it usually communicates with the subdeltoid bursa.
rest|Subacromial bursa.territorio: Separates the coracoacromial arch from the rotator cuff.
rest|Subacromial bursa.funcion: Facilitates gliding of the rotator cuff beneath the acromial arch during abduction.
rest|Subacromial bursa.clinica: Its bursitis is part of subacromial syndrome; usual site for corticosteroid injections.

rest|Subcutaneous acromial bursa.descripcion: Bursa located between the skin and the superior surface of the acromion.
rest|Subcutaneous acromial bursa.funcion: Allows the skin to glide over the acromion.

rest|Subcutaneous bursa of lateral malle.descripcion: Bursa located between the skin and the lateral malleolus.
rest|Subcutaneous bursa of lateral malle.funcion: Reduces friction of the skin over the lateral malleolus.
rest|Subcutaneous bursa of lateral malle.clinica: It may become inflamed from shoe rubbing or from sitting with the legs crossed.

rest|Subcutaneous bursa of medial malleo.descripcion: Bursa located between the skin and the medial malleolus.
rest|Subcutaneous bursa of medial malleo.funcion: Reduces friction of the skin over the medial malleolus.
rest|Subcutaneous bursa of medial malleo.clinica: It may become inflamed from rubbing by shoes or skating boots.

rest|Subcutaneous bursa of tuberosity of.descripcion: Bursa located between the skin and the tuberosity of the tibia.
rest|Subcutaneous bursa of tuberosity of.funcion: Allows the skin to glide over the tibial tuberosity when kneeling.
rest|Subcutaneous bursa of tuberosity of.clinica: Its inflammation from kneeling is known as clergyman's knee.

rest|Subcutaneous calcaneal bursa.descripcion: Bursa located between the skin and the calcaneal tendon, near its insertion.
rest|Subcutaneous calcaneal bursa.territorio: Skin posterior to the calcaneal tendon.
rest|Subcutaneous calcaneal bursa.funcion: Reduces friction between the skin and the calcaneal tendon.
rest|Subcutaneous calcaneal bursa.clinica: Its inflammation from the heel counter of footwear produces superficial retro-Achilles bursitis (Haglund deformity).

rest|Subcutaneous infrapatellar bursa.descripcion: Bursa located between the skin and the patellar ligament or the lower part of the patella.
rest|Subcutaneous infrapatellar bursa.funcion: Allows the skin to glide over the patellar ligament.
rest|Subcutaneous infrapatellar bursa.clinica: Its bursitis occurs from kneeling in an upright position (clergyman's knee).

rest|Subcutaneous prepatellar bursa.descripcion: Bursa located between the skin and the anterior surface of the patella.
rest|Subcutaneous prepatellar bursa.funcion: Allows free movement of the skin over the patella during knee flexion.
rest|Subcutaneous prepatellar bursa.clinica: Its bursitis is housemaid's knee; it can become infected (septic bursitis).

rest|Subcutaneous trochanteric bursa.descripcion: Bursa located between the skin and the greater trochanter.
rest|Subcutaneous trochanteric bursa.funcion: Reduces friction of the skin over the greater trochanter.

rest|Subdeltoid bursa.descripcion: Bursa located between the deltoid and the shoulder capsule and greater tuberosity; it usually continues with the subacromial bursa.
rest|Subdeltoid bursa.territorio: Separates the deltoid from the rotator cuff and greater tubercle.
rest|Subdeltoid bursa.funcion: Facilitates gliding of the deltoid over the rotator cuff.
rest|Subdeltoid bursa.clinica: Its bursitis, often with calcifications of the supraspinatus, causes intense pain in abduction.

rest|Subfacial prepatellar bursa.descripcion: Inconstant bursa located between the superficial fascia and the deep fascia in front of the patella.
rest|Subfacial prepatellar bursa.territorio: Anterior surface of the patella, between fascial planes.
rest|Subfacial prepatellar bursa.funcion: Facilitates gliding between prepatellar fascial layers.

rest|Subtendinous bursa of iliacus muscl.descripcion: Bursa located between the iliopsoas tendon and the lesser trochanter.
rest|Subtendinous bursa of iliacus muscl.territorio: Insertion of the iliopsoas on the lesser trochanter.
rest|Subtendinous bursa of iliacus muscl.funcion: Reduces friction of the iliopsoas tendon at its insertion.

rest|Subtendinous bursa of infraspinatus.descripcion: Bursa located between the infraspinatus tendon and the capsule of the shoulder joint.
rest|Subtendinous bursa of infraspinatus.territorio: Infraspinatus tendon and posterior glenohumeral capsule.
rest|Subtendinous bursa of infraspinatus.funcion: Reduces friction of the infraspinatus tendon over the capsule.

rest|Subtendinous bursa of obturator int.descripcion: Bursa located between the obturator internus tendon and the capsule of the hip joint.
rest|Subtendinous bursa of obturator int.territorio: Obturator internus tendon and posterior coxofemoral capsule.
rest|Subtendinous bursa of obturator int.funcion: Reduces friction of the obturator internus tendon over the hip capsule.

rest|Subtendinous bursa of sartorius mus.descripcion: Bursae located between the sartorius tendon and the tendons of the gracilis and semitendinosus, in the pes anserinus.
rest|Subtendinous bursa of sartorius mus.territorio: Sartorius tendon at its medial tibial insertion.
rest|Subtendinous bursa of sartorius mus.funcion: Reduce friction between the tendons of the pes anserinus.

rest|Subtendinous bursa of teres major m.es: Subtendinous bursa of teres major muscle
rest|Subtendinous bursa of teres major m.descripcion: Bursa located between the teres major tendon and the humerus, near the crest of the lesser tubercle.
rest|Subtendinous bursa of teres major m.territorio: Teres major tendon at its humeral insertion.
rest|Subtendinous bursa of teres major m.funcion: Reduces friction of the teres major tendon over the humerus.

rest|Subtendinous bursa of tibialis ante.es: Subtendinous bursa of tibialis anterior muscle
rest|Subtendinous bursa of tibialis ante.descripcion: Bursa located between the tibialis anterior tendon and the medial surface of the medial cuneiform and base of the first metatarsal.
rest|Subtendinous bursa of tibialis ante.territorio: Tibialis anterior tendon at its insertion.
rest|Subtendinous bursa of tibialis ante.funcion: Reduces friction of the tibialis anterior tendon at its insertion.

rest|Subtendinous bursa of trapezius mus.descripcion: Bursa located between the ascending fibers of the trapezius and the medial end of the spine of the scapula.
rest|Subtendinous bursa of trapezius mus.territorio: Ascending part of the trapezius over the scapular spine.
rest|Subtendinous bursa of trapezius mus.funcion: Reduces friction of the trapezius over the spine of the scapula.
rest|Subtendinous bursa of trapezius mus.clinica: It may contribute to painful scapulothoracic crepitus.

rest|Subtendinous bursa of triceps brach.es: Subtendinous bursa of triceps brachii muscle
rest|Subtendinous bursa of triceps brach.descripcion: Bursa located between the triceps tendon and the olecranon or the posterior elbow capsule.
rest|Subtendinous bursa of triceps brach.territorio: Triceps brachii tendon at its olecranon insertion.
rest|Subtendinous bursa of triceps brach.funcion: Reduces friction of the triceps tendon over the olecranon.

rest|Subtendinous calcaneal bursa.descripcion: Retrocalcaneal bursa located between the calcaneal tendon and the upper part of the posterior surface of the calcaneus.
rest|Subtendinous calcaneal bursa.territorio: Separates the Achilles tendon from the calcaneus.
rest|Subtendinous calcaneal bursa.funcion: Reduces friction of the calcaneal tendon over the calcaneus during dorsiflexion.
rest|Subtendinous calcaneal bursa.clinica: Retrocalcaneal bursitis is associated with Haglund deformity and insertional Achilles tendinopathy.

rest|Subtendinous prepatellar bursa.descripcion: Inconstant bursa located between the expansion of the quadriceps tendon and the periosteum of the patella.
rest|Subtendinous prepatellar bursa.territorio: Anterior surface of the patella beneath the quadriceps fibers.
rest|Subtendinous prepatellar bursa.funcion: Facilitates gliding of the quadriceps tendon over the patella.

rest|Superficial investing cervical fasc.descripcion: Investing fascia that surrounds the neck and splits to enclose the sternocleidomastoid and trapezius.
rest|Superficial investing cervical fasc.origen: Superior nuchal line, mastoid, zygomatic arch and mandible.
rest|Superficial investing cervical fasc.destino: Manubrium of the sternum, clavicle, acromion and spine of the scapula.
rest|Superficial investing cervical fasc.territorio: Encloses the sternocleidomastoid, trapezius, and the submandibular and parotid glands.
rest|Superficial investing cervical fasc.funcion: Contains the superficial cervical structures and forms the roof of the triangles of the neck.
rest|Superficial investing cervical fasc.clinica: Limits the superficial spread of infections; abscesses may lodge in the suprasternal space.

rest|Superficial layer of temporal fasci.descripcion: Outer layer of the temporal fascia that inserts on the lateral border of the zygomatic arch.
rest|Superficial layer of temporal fasci.destino: Superior lateral border of the zygomatic arch.
rest|Superficial layer of temporal fasci.territorio: Covers the temporalis muscle; between the two layers lie fat and temporal vessels.
rest|Superficial layer of temporal fasci.funcion: Encloses the temporalis muscle and resists the traction of the masseter on the zygomatic arch.
rest|Superficial layer of temporal fasci.clinica: Reference plane in the Gillies approach for reducing zygomatic arch fractures.

rest|Superior bursa of biceps femoris mu.es: Superior bursa of biceps femoris muscle
rest|Superior bursa of biceps femoris mu.descripcion: Bursa located at the origin of the long head of the biceps femoris, between it and the semitendinosus or the ischial tuberosity.
rest|Superior bursa of biceps femoris mu.territorio: Origin of the long head of the biceps femoris at the ischial tuberosity.
rest|Superior bursa of biceps femoris mu.funcion: Reduces friction at the proximal origin of the hamstrings.

rest|Superior extensor retinaculum of an.descripcion: Transverse fibrous band in the distal part of the anterior surface of the leg, above the malleoli.
rest|Superior extensor retinaculum of an.territorio: Tendons of tibialis anterior, long extensors and fibularis tertius, anterior tibial vessels and deep fibular nerve.
rest|Superior extensor retinaculum of an.funcion: Holds the extensor tendons against the tibia and fibula.

rest|Superior fibular retinaculum.descripcion: Fibrous band between the lateral malleolus and the calcaneus that holds the fibular tendons in the retromalleolar groove.
rest|Superior fibular retinaculum.origen: Posterior surface of the lateral malleolus.
rest|Superior fibular retinaculum.territorio: Tendons of the fibularis longus and brevis muscles and their common sheath.
rest|Superior fibular retinaculum.funcion: Prevents anterior dislocation of the fibular tendons.
rest|Superior fibular retinaculum.clinica: Its rupture or detachment causes dislocation of the fibular tendons, common in skiers.

rest|Suprapatellar bursa.descripcion: Large bursa located between the quadriceps tendon and the femur, usually communicating with the knee joint cavity.
rest|Suprapatellar bursa.territorio: Separates the quadriceps tendon from the anterior surface of the distal femur.
rest|Suprapatellar bursa.funcion: Allows the quadriceps to glide over the femur; the articularis genus muscle tenses it.
rest|Suprapatellar bursa.clinica: Accumulates knee joint effusion; site of aspiration and of the patellar tap (ballottement) sign.

rest|Synovial sheaths of digits of hand.es: Synovial sheaths of digits of hand
rest|Synovial sheaths of digits of hand.descripcion: Synovial sheaths that enclose the flexor tendons within the osteofibrous canals of the fingers.
rest|Synovial sheaths of digits of hand.territorio: Tendons of the flexor digitorum superficialis and profundus (and flexor pollicis longus).
rest|Synovial sheaths of digits of hand.funcion: Lubricate and nourish the flexor tendons, facilitating their gliding beneath the pulleys.
rest|Synovial sheaths of digits of hand.clinica: Infectious tenosynovitis is recognized by Kanavel signs and is a surgical emergency.

rest|Tendon sheath - abd. pollicis longu.es: Tendon sheath of abductor pollicis longus and extensor pollicis brevis
rest|Tendon sheath - abd. pollicis longu.la: Vagina tendinum musculorum abductoris longi et extensoris pollicis brevis
rest|Tendon sheath - abd. pollicis longu.descripcion: Synovial sheath of the first extensor compartment, over the styloid process of the radius.
rest|Tendon sheath - abd. pollicis longu.territorio: Tendons of the abductor pollicis longus and extensor pollicis brevis.
rest|Tendon sheath - abd. pollicis longu.funcion: Allows these tendons to glide beneath the extensor retinaculum.
rest|Tendon sheath - abd. pollicis longu.clinica: Its stenosis is De Quervain tenosynovitis (positive Finkelstein test).

rest|Tendon sheath of extensor digitorum.es: Tendon sheath of extensor digitorum and extensor indicis
rest|Tendon sheath of extensor digitorum.la: Vagina tendinum musculorum extensoris digitorum et extensoris indicis
rest|Tendon sheath of extensor digitorum.descripcion: Synovial sheath of the fourth extensor compartment on the dorsum of the wrist.
rest|Tendon sheath of extensor digitorum.territorio: Tendons of the extensor digitorum and extensor indicis; posterior interosseous nerve on its floor.
rest|Tendon sheath of extensor digitorum.funcion: Facilitates gliding of the extensor tendons beneath the retinaculum.
rest|Tendon sheath of extensor digitorum.clinica: Frequent site of synovitis in rheumatoid arthritis, with risk of tendon rupture.

rest|Tendon sheath of extensor digitorum.es: Tendon sheath of extensor digitorum longus muscle
rest|Tendon sheath of extensor digitorum.la: Vagina tendinum musculi extensoris digitorum longi pedis
rest|Tendon sheath of extensor digitorum.descripcion: Synovial sheath enclosing the tendons of the extensor digitorum longus and fibularis tertius beneath the extensor retinacula.
rest|Tendon sheath of extensor digitorum.territorio: Tendons of the extensor digitorum longus and fibularis tertius.
rest|Tendon sheath of extensor digitorum.funcion: Allows their gliding on the anterior surface of the ankle.
rest|Tendon sheath of extensor digitorum.clinica: May become inflamed from tight footwear or laces.

rest|Tendon sheath of extensors carpi ra.es: Tendon sheath of extensors carpi radialis
rest|Tendon sheath of extensors carpi ra.la: Vagina tendinum musculorum extensorum carpi radialium
rest|Tendon sheath of extensors carpi ra.descripcion: Synovial sheath of the second extensor compartment of the wrist.
rest|Tendon sheath of extensors carpi ra.territorio: Tendons of the extensor carpi radialis longus and extensor carpi radialis brevis.
rest|Tendon sheath of extensors carpi ra.funcion: Facilitates gliding of the radial extensors beneath the extensor retinaculum.
rest|Tendon sheath of extensors carpi ra.clinica: Intersection syndrome occurs at the crossing with the first compartment.

rest|Tendon sheath of flexor digitorum l.es: Tendon sheath of flexor digitorum longus muscle
rest|Tendon sheath of flexor digitorum l.la: Vagina tendinum musculi flexoris digitorum longi pedis
rest|Tendon sheath of flexor digitorum l.descripcion: Synovial sheath of the flexor digitorum longus tendon behind the medial malleolus, beneath the flexor retinaculum.
rest|Tendon sheath of flexor digitorum l.territorio: Flexor digitorum longus tendon in the tarsal tunnel.
rest|Tendon sheath of flexor digitorum l.funcion: Allows the tendon to glide in the medial retromalleolar groove.

rest|Tendon sheath of flexor hallucis lo.es: Tendon sheath of flexor hallucis longus
rest|Tendon sheath of flexor hallucis lo.la: Vagina tendinis musculi flexoris hallucis longi
rest|Tendon sheath of flexor hallucis lo.descripcion: Synovial sheath of the flexor hallucis longus tendon in the groove of the talus and beneath the sustentaculum tali of the calcaneus.
rest|Tendon sheath of flexor hallucis lo.funcion: Facilitates gliding of the tendon in its retrotalar osteofibrous canal.
rest|Tendon sheath of flexor hallucis lo.clinica: Its stenosing tenosynovitis is typical of ballet dancers (en pointe position).

rest|Tendon sheath of tibialis anterior.descripcion: Synovial sheath of the tibialis anterior tendon beneath the superior and inferior extensor retinacula.
rest|Tendon sheath of tibialis anterior.funcion: Allows the tendon to glide on the anterior surface of the ankle.
rest|Tendon sheath of tibialis anterior.clinica: Tenosynovitis of the tibialis anterior causes anterior pain on resisted dorsiflexion.

rest|Tendon sheath of tibialis posterior.es: Tendon sheath of tibialis posterior muscle
rest|Tendon sheath of tibialis posterior.descripcion: Synovial sheath of the tibialis posterior tendon in the medial retromalleolar groove.
rest|Tendon sheath of tibialis posterior.funcion: Facilitates gliding of the tendon around the medial malleolus.
rest|Tendon sheath of tibialis posterior.clinica: Its tenosynovitis and degeneration lead to posterior tibial tendon dysfunction and adult acquired flatfoot.

rest|Tensor fasciae latae.descripcion: Muscle of the anterolateral gluteal region enclosed in a split of the fascia lata.
rest|Tensor fasciae latae.origen: Anterior superior iliac spine and anterior part of the iliac crest.
rest|Tensor fasciae latae.destino: Iliotibial tract, to the Gerdy tubercle of the tibia.
rest|Tensor fasciae latae.funcion: Tenses the fascia lata; flexes, abducts and medially rotates the hip; stabilizes the knee in extension.
rest|Tensor fasciae latae.clinica: Its shortening contributes to iliotibial band syndrome and external snapping hip.

rest|Transversalis fascia.descripcion: Fascia lining the deep surface of the transversus abdominis muscle, part of the endoabdominal fascia.
rest|Transversalis fascia.territorio: Anterolateral abdominal wall; forms the deep inguinal ring and the internal spermatic fascia.
rest|Transversalis fascia.funcion: Forms the posterior wall of the inguinal canal and separates the musculature from the extraperitoneal space.
rest|Transversalis fascia.clinica: Its weakness in the Hesselbach triangle gives rise to direct inguinal hernias.

rest|Transverse intermuscular septum of.descripcion: Deep fascial lamina between the superficial and deep posterior muscles of the leg.
rest|Transverse intermuscular septum of.territorio: Separates the superficial posterior compartment (triceps surae) from the deep one (long flexors, tibialis posterior, posterior tibial vessels).
rest|Transverse intermuscular septum of.funcion: Delimits the posterior compartments and contains the posterior tibial neurovascular bundle.
rest|Transverse intermuscular septum of.clinica: It must be opened in fasciotomy to decompress the deep posterior compartment.

rest|Trochanteric bursa of gluteus maxim.es: Trochanteric bursa of gluteus maximus muscle
rest|Trochanteric bursa of gluteus maxim.descripcion: Large bursa located between the gluteus maximus and iliotibial tract and the lateral surface of the greater trochanter.
rest|Trochanteric bursa of gluteus maxim.territorio: Separates the gluteus maximus and iliotibial band from the greater trochanter.
rest|Trochanteric bursa of gluteus maxim.funcion: Reduces friction of the gluteus maximus over the greater trochanter.
rest|Trochanteric bursa of gluteus maxim.clinica: Classically implicated in greater trochanteric pain syndrome, now attributed mainly to gluteal tendinopathy.

rest|Trochanteric bursa of gluteus mediu.es: Trochanteric bursae of gluteus medius muscle
rest|Trochanteric bursa of gluteus mediu.descripcion: Bursae located between the gluteus medius tendon and the lateral surface of the greater trochanter.
rest|Trochanteric bursa of gluteus mediu.territorio: Gluteus medius tendon at its trochanteric insertion.
rest|Trochanteric bursa of gluteus mediu.funcion: Reduce friction of the gluteus medius tendon over the trochanter.
rest|Trochanteric bursa of gluteus mediu.clinica: Involved in greater trochanteric pain syndrome together with gluteus medius tendinopathy.

rest|Trochanteric bursa of gluteus minim.es: Trochanteric bursa of gluteus minimus muscle
rest|Trochanteric bursa of gluteus minim.descripcion: Bursa located between the gluteus minimus tendon and the anterior surface of the greater trochanter.
rest|Trochanteric bursa of gluteus minim.territorio: Gluteus minimus tendon at its insertion.
rest|Trochanteric bursa of gluteus minim.funcion: Reduces friction of the gluteus minimus tendon over the trochanter.

rest|Anterior layer of rectus sheath.la: Lamina anterior vaginae musculi recti abdominis
rest|Anterior layer of rectus sheath.descripcion: Aponeurotic lamina covering the rectus abdominis anteriorly. Above the arcuate line it is formed by the external oblique aponeurosis and the anterior layer of the internal oblique aponeurosis; below, by the aponeuroses of the three flat muscles (external oblique, internal oblique and transversus). In the midline they interlace to form the linea alba.
rest|Anterior layer of rectus sheath.origen: Aponeuroses of the external oblique, internal oblique and (below the arcuate line) transversus abdominis muscles
rest|Anterior layer of rectus sheath.territorio: Adheres to the tendinous intersections of the rectus, which is therefore divided into visible bellies ("six-pack").
rest|Anterior layer of rectus sheath.funcion: Contains the rectus abdominis, transmits the traction of the flat muscles toward the linea alba and reinforces the anterior abdominal wall.
rest|Anterior layer of rectus sheath.clinica: Paramedian incisions and diastasis recti (separation of the recti due to thinning of the linea alba, common after pregnancy) affect this sheath; weakness of the semilunar line gives rise to Spigelian hernia.

rest|Posterior layer of rectus sheath.la: Lamina posterior vaginae musculi recti abdominis
rest|Posterior layer of rectus sheath.descripcion: Aponeurotic lamina located behind the rectus abdominis, formed by the posterior layer of the internal oblique aponeurosis and the transversus aponeurosis.
