It exists only above the arcuate line (about 3–5 cm below the umbilicus); below it, the rectus rests directly on the transversalis fascia.
rest|Posterior layer of rectus sheath.origen: Aponeurosis of the internal oblique (posterior layer) and of the transversus abdominis
rest|Posterior layer of rectus sheath.territorio: The inferior epigastric vessels run behind it as they enter the sheath at the level of the arcuate line.
rest|Posterior layer of rectus sheath.funcion: Closes the rectus sheath posteriorly and separates the muscle from the abdominal contents.
rest|Posterior layer of rectus sheath.clinica: The arcuate line marks the inferior limit of this layer: below it, the wall is weaker, which matters in hernias and surgical approaches.

rest|Rectum.descripcion: Final portion of the large intestine (12–15 cm) that follows the concavity of the sacrum and coccyx. Its dilated lower part is the rectal ampulla. It lacks taeniae, haustra and epiploic appendages. Its upper third is covered by peritoneum anteriorly; the rest is subperitoneal.
rest|Rectum.origen: Sigmoid colon, at the level of S3.
rest|Rectum.destino: Anal canal, as it passes through the pelvic diaphragm (puborectalis sling).
rest|Rectum.territorio: Superior (inferior mesenteric), middle (internal iliac) and inferior (internal pudendal) rectal arteries; portal and systemic venous drainage (portocaval anastomosis).
rest|Rectum.funcion: Stores feces until defecation; its distension triggers the rectoanal reflex.
rest|Rectum.clinica: Examined by digital rectal examination. In women, the rectouterine pouch (of Douglas) lies anteriorly: it is the most dependent point of the peritoneal cavity. Rectocele is its prolapse into the posterior wall of the vagina.

rest|Anal canal.descripcion: Last segment of the digestive tract (about 3–4 cm), from the anorectal junction to the anus. The pectinate line separates the upper half (endodermal, with anal columns) from the lower (ectodermal, sensitive).
rest|Anal canal.origen: Rectum, at the level of the anorectal junction (puborectalis sling, angle of about 90°).
rest|Anal canal.territorio: Middle and inferior rectal arteries; inferior rectal nerves (pudendal) below the pectinate line.
rest|Anal canal.funcion: Fecal continence thanks to the internal (smooth, involuntary) and external (striated, voluntary) sphincters and the puborectalis muscle.
rest|Anal canal.clinica: Internal hemorrhoids (above the pectinate line) are painless; external ones and anal fissures are very painful. Third- and fourth-degree perineal tears during childbirth injure its sphincters.

rest|Anterior leaflet of left atrioventr.descripcion: Anterior (aortic) leaflet of the mitral valve: taller and narrower at its attachment than the posterior one, it occupies about one third of the annulus and is in fibrous continuity with the aortic valve (mitral-aortic continuity), between the inflow orifice and the outflow tract of the left ventricle. Its chordae tendineae go to both papillary muscles. In the model it was built schematically, because the original atlas did not include it, with the chordae tendineae included in the same structure.
rest|Anterior leaflet of left atrioventr.funcion: Closes the left atrioventricular orifice in systole by coapting with the posterior leaflet; in diastole it separates inflow from outflow.
rest|Anterior leaflet of left atrioventr.clinica: Its prolapse or chordal rupture produces mitral regurgitation; in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy it may be displaced toward the septum in systole (systolic anterior motion) and obstruct ventricular outflow.

rest|Anterior leaflet of right atriovent.descripcion: The largest of the three leaflets of the tricuspid valve, between the infundibulum and the anterolateral wall of the right ventricle. Its chordae tendineae go mainly to the anterior papillary muscle. Built schematically in the model, because the original atlas did not include it.
rest|Anterior leaflet of right atriovent.funcion: Closes the right atrioventricular orifice in systole together with the inferior (posterior) and septal leaflets.
rest|Anterior leaflet of right atriovent.clinica: Dilation of the right ventricle stretches the annulus and produces functional tricuspid regurgitation; tricuspid endocarditis is typical of intravenous drug users.

rest|Anterior papillary muscle of left v.es: Anterior (anterolateral) papillary muscle of left ventricle
rest|Anterior papillary muscle of left v.descripcion: The larger of the two papillary muscles of the left ventricle, in the anterolateral wall beneath the anterolateral commissure of the mitral valve; it sends chordae tendineae to both leaflets. In the model it was obtained by rotating the atlas posterior papillary muscle around the long axis of the ventricle, so its shape is approximate.
rest|Anterior papillary muscle of left v.funcion: Contracts in systole and tenses the chordae tendineae to prevent the leaflets from everting into the atrium.
rest|Anterior papillary muscle of left v.clinica: It has a dual blood supply (anterior descending and circumflex), so it ruptures less often in infarction than the posterior one, which depends on a single artery.

fem|Vagina.descripcion: Distensible fibromuscular canal of 7–9 cm that runs upward and backward from the vulvar vestibule to the cervix. Its upper end surrounds the vaginal part of the cervix, forming the anterior, posterior and lateral fornices.
fem|Vagina.territorio: Blood supply: vaginal artery and vaginal branches of the uterine, middle rectal and internal pudendal arteries; vaginal venous plexus → internal iliac vein. Lymph: upper third to iliac nodes, lower third to superficial inguinal nodes. Innervation: uterovaginal plexus in its upper 3/4 (no somatic pain sensation) and pudendal nerve in the lower part.
fem|Vagina.funcion: Organ of copulation, birth canal and outflow tract for menstrual flow.
fem|Vagina.clinica: The posterior fornix contacts the rectouterine pouch (of Douglas), which allows culdocentesis; weakness of the pelvic floor produces cystocele or rectocele through prolapse of its walls.

fem|Cervicovaginal junction.descripcion: Circular line of attachment of the vaginal wall to the cervix, dividing it into the supravaginal part and the vaginal part (ectocervix) and delimiting the vaginal fornices.
fem|Cervicovaginal junction.territorio: Blood supply: cervicovaginal branch of the uterine artery and vaginal artery. Innervation: uterovaginal plexus.
fem|Cervicovaginal junction.funcion: Anchors the cervix to the vagina and forms the roof of the vaginal fornices.
fem|Cervicovaginal junction.clinica: Not to be confused with the squamocolumnar junction (transformation zone) at the external os, site of origin of most HPV-related cervical carcinomas.

fem|Ampulla of uterine tube.descripcion: Longest and widest portion of the uterine tube (more than half its length), located between the infundibulum and the isthmus, with a thin wall and a mucosa with highly branched folds.
fem|Ampulla of uterine tube.territorio: Blood supply: tubal branches of the uterine and ovarian arteries (anastomotic arcade in the mesosalpinx); corresponding veins. Lymph: lumbar (para-aortic) nodes. Innervation: ovarian and uterine plexuses (visceral afferents to T10–L1).
fem|Ampulla of uterine tube.funcion: Usual site of fertilization; transport of the oocyte and early embryo by cilia and peristalsis.
fem|Ampulla of uterine tube.clinica: It is the most frequent location of ectopic pregnancy (≈70–80% of tubal ones).

fem|Isthmus of uterine tube.descripcion: Medial, narrow segment with a thick muscular wall of the uterine tube, which continues with the uterine (intramural) part at the horn of the uterus.
fem|Isthmus of uterine tube.destino: Uterine part of the tube (uterine horn)
fem|Isthmus of uterine tube.territorio: Blood supply: tubal branches of the uterine and ovarian arteries (anastomotic arcade in the mesosalpinx); corresponding veins. Lymph: lumbar (para-aortic) nodes. Innervation: ovarian and uterine plexuses (visceral afferents to T10–L1).
fem|Isthmus of uterine tube.funcion: Transport of gametes and the embryo toward the uterine cavity; temporary reservoir of sperm.
fem|Isthmus of uterine tube.clinica: Usual site of tubal ligation (sterilization); isthmic ectopic pregnancies tend to rupture early.

fem|Fimbriae of uterine tube.descripcion: Finger-like projections of the free border of the infundibulum; one of them, longer (ovarian fimbria), attaches to the tubal pole of the ovary.
fem|Fimbriae of uterine tube.territorio: Blood supply: tubal branches of the uterine and ovarian arteries (anastomotic arcade in the mesosalpinx); corresponding veins. Lymph: lumbar (para-aortic) nodes. Innervation: ovarian and uterine plexuses (visceral afferents to T10–L1).
fem|Fimbriae of uterine tube.funcion: Capture the oocyte-cumulus complex released at ovulation and direct it into the tube.
fem|Fimbriae of uterine tube.clinica: The fimbriae are the probable origin of many high-grade serous "ovarian" carcinomas, which justifies opportunistic salpingectomy.

fem|Infundibulum of uterine tube.descripcion: Funnel-shaped lateral end of the uterine tube, open to the peritoneal cavity through the abdominal ostium and surrounded by fimbriae.
fem|Infundibulum of uterine tube.origen: Abdominal ostium of the tube (peritoneal cavity)
fem|Infundibulum of uterine tube.territorio: Blood supply: tubal branches of the uterine and ovarian arteries (anastomotic arcade in the mesosalpinx); corresponding veins. Lymph: lumbar (para-aortic) nodes. Innervation: ovarian and uterine plexuses (visceral afferents to T10–L1).
fem|Infundibulum of uterine tube.funcion: Collects the oocyte from the ovarian surface.
fem|Infundibulum of uterine tube.clinica: It connects the genital tract with the peritoneal cavity: route of spread of pelvic inflammatory disease (e.g., Fitz-Hugh–Curtis perihepatitis).

fem|Abdominal ostium of uterine tube.descripcion: Orifice of 2–3 mm at the bottom of the infundibulum that connects the tubal lumen with the peritoneal cavity.
fem|Abdominal ostium of uterine tube.territorio: Blood supply: tubal branches of the uterine and ovarian arteries (anastomotic arcade in the mesosalpinx); corresponding veins. Lymph: lumbar (para-aortic) nodes. Innervation: ovarian and uterine plexuses (visceral afferents to T10–L1).
fem|Abdominal ostium of uterine tube.funcion: Allows the oocyte to enter the tube.
fem|Abdominal ostium of uterine tube.clinica: Its obstruction (e.g., hydrosalpinx) causes infertility; patency is checked by hysterosalpingography (passage of contrast into the peritoneum).

fem|Vesico-uterine pouch.descripcion: Shallow peritoneal pouch between the anterior surface of the uterus (at the level of the isthmus) and the superior surface of the urinary bladder.
fem|Vesico-uterine pouch.funcion: Allows independent distension of the bladder and the uterus.
fem|Vesico-uterine pouch.clinica: It is incised in lower-segment cesarean section to reflect the bladder; it is a frequent location of endometriosis implants.

fem|Round ligament of uterus.descripcion: Fibromuscular cord, remnant of the caudal part of the gubernaculum, that runs through the broad ligament and the inguinal canal.
fem|Round ligament of uterus.origen: Lateral angle of the uterus (horn), anteroinferior to the uterine tube
fem|Round ligament of uterus.destino: Subcutaneous tissue of the labium majus, after crossing the inguinal canal
fem|Round ligament of uterus.territorio: Blood supply: artery of the round ligament (branch of the inferior epigastric). Lymph: some vessels from the uterine horn follow it to the superficial inguinal nodes. Innervation: genital branch of the genitofemoral nerve.
fem|Round ligament of uterus.funcion: Helps maintain anteversion of the uterus.
fem|Round ligament of uterus.clinica: Its stretching in pregnancy produces inguinal pain; persistence of the processus vaginalis (canal of Nuck) gives hydroceles or inguinal hernias in women.

fem|Uterosacral ligament.descripcion: Band of fibrous tissue and smooth muscle that encircles the rectum laterally and forms the rectouterine folds that bound the rectouterine pouch; it contains fibers of the inferior hypogastric plexus.
fem|Uterosacral ligament.origen: Posterolateral surface of the cervix and posterior vaginal fornix
fem|Uterosacral ligament.territorio: Innervation: contains autonomic fibers of the inferior hypogastric plexus (pelvic splanchnic nerves S2–S4).
fem|Uterosacral ligament.funcion: Apical support (DeLancey level I): keeps the cervix backward and upward, in anteversion.
fem|Uterosacral ligament.clinica: Used for apical suspension in prolapse surgery; frequent site of deep endometriosis (dyspareunia).

fem|Cardinal ligament.descripcion: Condensation of connective tissue and smooth muscle at the base of the broad ligament that accompanies the uterine vessels (parametrium/paracolpium).
fem|Cardinal ligament.origen: Lateral borders of the cervix and of the upper part of the vagina
fem|Cardinal ligament.destino: Lateral pelvic wall (fascia of the obturator internus and sheath of the internal iliac vessels)
fem|Cardinal ligament.territorio: Contains the uterine artery and veins, lymphatics and fibers of the uterovaginal plexus.
fem|Cardinal ligament.funcion: Main support of the cervix and vaginal vault against descent (DeLancey level I).
fem|Cardinal ligament.clinica: The ureter passes beneath the uterine artery about 1.5–2 cm from the cervix ("water under the bridge"): risk of ureteral injury in hysterectomy.

fem|Suspensory ligament of ovary.descripcion: Peritoneal fold (infundibulopelvic ligament) that contains the ovarian vessels, lymphatics and nerves of the ovary.
fem|Suspensory ligament of ovary.destino: Lateral pelvic wall, over the external iliac vessels
fem|Suspensory ligament of ovary.territorio: Contains the ovarian artery and vein, lymphatics to the lumbar nodes and the ovarian plexus.
fem|Suspensory ligament of ovary.funcion: Anchors the ovary to the pelvic wall and carries its vascular pedicle.
fem|Suspensory ligament of ovary.clinica: In oophorectomy the ovarian vessels are ligated here; the ureter crosses very close and may be injured.

fem|Ligament of ovary.descripcion: Fibromuscular cord within the thickness of the broad ligament, remnant of the cranial part of the gubernaculum.
fem|Ligament of ovary.destino: Lateral angle of the uterus, posteroinferior to the uterine tube
fem|Ligament of ovary.territorio: Accompanied by the ovarian branch of the uterine artery.
fem|Ligament of ovary.funcion: Connects the ovary to the uterus and limits its displacement.
fem|Ligament of ovary.clinica: Together with the suspensory ligament it forms the axis around which the adnexa rotates in ovarian torsion.

fem|Broad ligament of uterus.descripcion: Double peritoneal fold that extends from the lateral borders of the uterus to the lateral walls and floor of the pelvis; it is divided into mesometrium, mesosalpinx and mesovarium.
fem|Broad ligament of uterus.destino: Lateral walls and floor of the pelvis
fem|Broad ligament of uterus.territorio: Contains the uterine and ovarian arteries, their veins, lymphatics and nerves; the ureter runs along its base.
fem|Broad ligament of uterus.funcion: Keeps the uterus, tubes and ovaries in relative position and carries their neurovascular bundle.
fem|Broad ligament of uterus.clinica: It can harbor hematomas after childbirth or surgery and paraovarian cysts; its defects can give rise to internal hernias.

fem|Mesosalpinx.descripcion: Portion of the broad ligament located between the uterine tube and the mesovarium; it contains the tubal vascular arcade and embryonic remnants (epoophoron, paroophoron).
fem|Mesosalpinx.destino: Broad ligament (above the attachment of the mesovarium)
fem|Mesosalpinx.territorio: Contains the anastomosis between tubal branches of the uterine and ovarian arteries.
fem|Mesosalpinx.funcion: Suspends the tube and carries its vessels and nerves.
fem|Mesosalpinx.clinica: Site of paratubal cysts (e.g., hydatid of Morgagni), which can undergo torsion.

fem|Mesovarium.descripcion: Short fold of the posterior layer of the broad ligament that attaches to the mesovarial border of the ovary at its hilum.
fem|Mesovarium.origen: Posterior layer of the broad ligament
fem|Mesovarium.territorio: The ovarian vessels, lymphatics and nerves enter and leave the ovary through it.
fem|Mesovarium.funcion: Anchors the ovary to the broad ligament and carries its neurovascular pedicle.
fem|Mesovarium.clinica: The ovary is not covered by peritoneum but by surface epithelium, so the oocyte is released directly into the peritoneal cavity.

fem|Ovary.descripcion: Paired, ovoid female gonad (≈3 × 2 × 1 cm in reproductive age), located in the ovarian fossa of the lateral pelvic wall; it consists of a cortex with follicles and a vascular medulla.
fem|Ovary.territorio: Blood supply: ovarian artery (branch of the abdominal aorta, ~L2) and ovarian branch of the uterine. Veins: the right drains into the inferior vena cava and the left into the left renal vein. Lymph: lumbar (para-aortic) nodes. Innervation: ovarian plexus (afferents T10–T11).
fem|Ovary.funcion: Oogenesis and production of estrogens, progesterone and inhibin.
fem|Ovary.clinica: Irritation of the obturator nerve, adjacent to the ovarian fossa, can refer pain to the medial thigh.

fem|Body of uterus.descripcion: Upper two thirds of the uterus, between the fundus and the isthmus, housing the triangular uterine cavity; its wall consists of endometrium, myometrium and perimetrium and in most women it is anteverted and anteflexed.
fem|Body of uterus.territorio: Blood supply: uterine artery (branch of the internal iliac) anastomosed with the ovarian; veins to the uterine venous plexus → internal iliac vein. Lymph: external and internal iliac nodes (from the fundus also lumbar). Innervation: uterovaginal plexus (sympathetic T10–L1, parasympathetic S2–S4).
fem|Body of uterus.funcion: Implantation and development of the embryo; contraction of the myometrium expels the fetus at birth.
fem|Body of uterus.clinica: Usual site of leiomyomas (fibroids), a frequent cause of heavy menstrual bleeding and pelvic pain.

fem|Fundus of uterus.descripcion: Rounded portion of the uterine body located above the openings of the uterine tubes.
fem|Fundus of uterus.territorio: Blood supply: uterine artery (branch of the internal iliac) anastomosed with the ovarian; veins to the uterine venous plexus → internal iliac vein. Lymph: external and internal iliac nodes (from the fundus also lumbar). Innervation: uterovaginal plexus (sympathetic T10–L1, parasympathetic S2–S4). Part of the lymph from the fundus reaches the lumbar nodes.
fem|Fundus of uterus.funcion: Preferred site of placental implantation; its coordinated contraction initiates fetal expulsion.
fem|Fundus of uterus.clinica: The height of the uterine fundus estimates gestational age (at the level of the umbilicus ≈20 weeks).

fem|Uterine horn.descripcion: Superolateral angle of the uterus where the intramural part of the tube opens and the round ligament and ligament of the ovary attach.
fem|Uterine horn.territorio: Blood supply: uterine artery (branch of the internal iliac) anastomosed with the ovarian; veins to the uterine venous plexus → internal iliac vein. Lymph: external and internal iliac nodes (from the fundus also lumbar). Innervation: uterovaginal plexus (sympathetic T10–L1, parasympathetic S2–S4). Some lymphatics follow the round ligament to the superficial inguinal nodes.
fem|Uterine horn.funcion: Connects the uterine cavity with the tubal lumen.
fem|Uterine horn.clinica: Interstitial (cornual) pregnancy carries a high risk of rupture and severe hemorrhage.

fem|Lower uterine segment.descripcion: Narrow portion of ≈1 cm between the body and the cervix of the uterus that, at the end of pregnancy, thins and expands to form the lower uterine segment.
fem|Lower uterine segment.territorio: Blood supply: uterine artery (branch of the internal iliac) anastomosed with the ovarian; veins to the uterine venous plexus → internal iliac vein. Lymph: external and internal iliac nodes (from the fundus also lumbar). Innervation: uterovaginal plexus (sympathetic T10–L1, parasympathetic S2–S4).
fem|Lower uterine segment.funcion: It is incorporated into the uterine cavity in the third trimester and is passive during labor.
fem|Lower uterine segment.clinica: Site of the transverse hysterotomy in cesarean section (less bleeding and lower risk of rupture in later pregnancies); placenta previa implants here.

fem|Posterior wall of uterus.descripcion: Dorsal wall of the uterine body (intestinal surface), convex and covered with peritoneum that descends to the rectouterine pouch.
fem|Posterior wall of uterus.territorio: Blood supply: uterine artery (branch of the internal iliac) anastomosed with the ovarian; veins to the uterine venous plexus → internal iliac vein. Lymph: external and internal iliac nodes (from the fundus also lumbar). Innervation: uterovaginal plexus (sympathetic T10–L1, parasympathetic S2–S4).
fem|Posterior wall of uterus.funcion: Delimits the uterine cavity; related to the sigmoid colon, ileal loops and the rectum.
fem|Posterior wall of uterus.clinica: In retroverted uteri, the posterior wall occupies the pouch of Douglas and can cause dyspareunia or low back pain.

fem|Anterior wall of uterus.descripcion: Ventral wall of the uterine body (vesical surface), flattened, resting on the superior surface of the urinary bladder separated by the vesicouterine pouch.
fem|Anterior wall of uterus.territorio: Blood supply: uterine artery (branch of the internal iliac) anastomosed with the ovarian; veins to the uterine venous plexus → internal iliac vein. Lymph: external and internal iliac nodes (from the fundus also lumbar). Innervation: uterovaginal plexus (sympathetic T10–L1, parasympathetic S2–S4).
fem|Anterior wall of uterus.funcion: Delimits the uterine cavity; related to the bladder.
fem|Anterior wall of uterus.clinica: Growth of anterior fibroids compresses the bladder and produces urinary frequency.

fem|Cervix of uterus.descripcion: Cylindrical, predominantly fibrous lower third of the uterus (≈2.5–3 cm), with a supravaginal part and a vaginal part; its cervical canal extends between the internal and external os.
fem|Cervix of uterus.territorio: Blood supply: cervicovaginal branch of the uterine artery. Lymph: internal and external iliac, obturator and sacral nodes. Innervation: uterovaginal plexus; the pain of dilation travels with the pelvic splanchnic nerves (S2–S4).
fem|Cervix of uterus.funcion: Barrier against infections (cervical mucus), retention of the pregnancy and, in labor, effacement and dilation.
fem|Cervix of uterus.clinica: Cervical cancer screening (cytology and HPV testing) samples the transformation zone of the ectocervix.

fem|Internal os of uterus.descripcion: Superior orifice of the cervical canal, at the junction with the uterine isthmus.
fem|Internal os of uterus.territorio: Cervicovaginal branch of the uterine artery; uterovaginal plexus.
fem|Internal os of uterus.funcion: Keeps the uterus closed during gestation.
fem|Internal os of uterus.clinica: Its incompetence (cervical insufficiency) causes second-trimester pregnancy losses and can be treated with cerclage.

fem|External os of uterus.descripcion: Inferior orifice of the cervical canal, at the center of the vaginal part of the cervix: circular in nulliparous women and a transverse slit after vaginal delivery.
fem|External os of uterus.territorio: Cervicovaginal branch of the uterine artery; uterovaginal plexus.
fem|External os of uterus.funcion: Connects the cervical canal with the vagina; route for menstrual outflow and passage of the fetus.
fem|External os of uterus.clinica: Its proximity to the transformation zone makes it the site of sampling in cervicovaginal cytology.

fem|Fat of breast.descripcion: Subcutaneous, interlobular and retromammary adipose tissue that determines most of the volume and shape of the non-lactating breast.
fem|Fat of breast.territorio: Blood supply: medial perforating branches of the internal thoracic artery, lateral thoracic artery, pectoral branches of the thoracoacromial and branches of the posterior intercostals. Lymph: ~75% to axillary nodes, the rest to parasternal. Innervation: anterior and lateral cutaneous branches of intercostal nerves 2–6.
fem|Fat of breast.funcion: Gives shape and volume to the breast and supports the glandular parenchyma.
fem|Fat of breast.clinica: The fat/fibroglandular tissue ratio determines mammographic density: dense breasts reduce the sensitivity of mammography; fat necrosis can mimic a tumor.

fem|Areolar tubercles.descripcion: Small elevations of the areola produced by the areolar glands, modified sebaceous glands.
fem|Areolar tubercles.territorio: Blood supply: medial perforating branches of the internal thoracic artery, lateral thoracic artery, pectoral branches of the thoracoacromial and branches of the posterior intercostals. Lymph: ~75% to axillary nodes, the rest to parasternal. Innervation: anterior and lateral cutaneous branches of intercostal nerves 2–6.
fem|Areolar tubercles.funcion: Secrete a lubricating and protective substance for the areola and nipple during lactation.
fem|Areolar tubercles.clinica: They enlarge in the first weeks of pregnancy (early sign); they may form small cysts.

fem|Nipple.descripcion: Conical or cylindrical projection at the center of the areola, with circular and longitudinal smooth muscle, where 15–20 lactiferous ducts open.
fem|Nipple.territorio: Sensory innervation: lateral cutaneous branch of the 4th intercostal nerve (dermatome T4). Blood supply and lymph: those of the breast (subareolar lymphatic plexus).
fem|Nipple.funcion: Outlet for milk; its erection facilitates suckling by the infant.
fem|Nipple.clinica: A new-onset retraction or bloody discharge requires ruling out carcinoma; Paget disease of the nipple is eczematoid.

fem|Areola.descripcion: Circular area of pigmented skin around the nipple, with areolar, sebaceous and sweat glands and smooth muscle fibers.
fem|Areola.territorio: Blood supply: medial perforating branches of the internal thoracic artery, lateral thoracic artery, pectoral branches of the thoracoacromial and branches of the posterior intercostals. Lymph: ~75% to axillary nodes, the rest to parasternal. Innervation: anterior and lateral cutaneous branches of intercostal nerves 2–6. The subareolar lymphatic plexus lies beneath it.
fem|Areola.funcion: Lubricates and protects the areola-nipple complex and guides the infant during breastfeeding.
fem|Areola.clinica: It darkens in pregnancy; in lactation the infant must take in a good part of the areola for effective latching and to avoid cracks.

fem|Lobes of mammary gland.descripcion: 15–20 lobes of tubuloalveolar gland arranged radially around the nipple, each formed by lobules (terminal duct-lobular units) and drained by a lactiferous duct.
fem|Lobes of mammary gland.territorio: Blood supply: medial perforating branches of the internal thoracic artery, lateral thoracic artery, pectoral branches of the thoracoacromial and branches of the posterior intercostals. Lymph: ~75% to axillary nodes, the rest to parasternal. Innervation: anterior and lateral cutaneous branches of intercostal nerves 2–6.
fem|Lobes of mammary gland.funcion: Milk production (prolactin) and ejection by myoepithelial contraction (oxytocin).
fem|Lobes of mammary gland.clinica: Most carcinomas originate in the terminal duct-lobular unit; the upper outer quadrant, with the axillary tail, is the most affected.

fem|Lactiferous ducts.descripcion: Main excretory ducts, one per lobe, which converge radially toward the nipple and open at its apex.
fem|Lactiferous ducts.territorio: Blood supply: medial perforating branches of the internal thoracic artery, lateral thoracic artery, pectoral branches of the thoracoacromial and branches of the posterior intercostals. Lymph: ~75% to axillary nodes, the rest to parasternal. Innervation: anterior and lateral cutaneous branches of intercostal nerves 2–6.
fem|Lactiferous ducts.funcion: Conduct milk from the lobes to the nipple.
fem|Lactiferous ducts.clinica: Intraductal papilloma is the most frequent cause of unilateral single-duct nipple discharge.

fem|Lactiferous sinuses.descripcion: Fusiform dilations of the lactiferous ducts beneath the areola, classically described as reservoirs; ultrasound during lactation shows that they are not permanent reservoirs but ducts that dilate during ejection.
fem|Lactiferous sinuses.territorio: Blood supply: medial perforating branches of the internal thoracic artery, lateral thoracic artery, pectoral branches of the thoracoacromial and branches of the posterior intercostals. Lymph: ~75% to axillary nodes, the rest to parasternal. Innervation: anterior and lateral cutaneous branches of intercostal nerves 2–6.
fem|Lactiferous sinuses.funcion: Conduction (and transient storage) of milk during the ejection reflex.
fem|Lactiferous sinuses.clinica: Site of ductal ectasia and subareolar abscesses, more frequent in smokers.

fem|Suspensory ligaments of breast.descripcion: Fibrous septa that cross the breast tissue, compartmentalizing it, from the deep fascia to the dermis.
fem|Suspensory ligaments of breast.origen: Pectoral fascia (deep layer of the superficial fascia)
fem|Suspensory ligaments of breast.funcion: Support the breast and anchor the skin to the parenchyma.
fem|Suspensory ligaments of breast.clinica: Their shortening by tumor infiltration produces skin retraction (dimpling), a sign suspicious for carcinoma.

fem|Mammary gland.descripcion: Modified apocrine sweat gland of the subcutaneous tissue of the anterior chest wall, extending from the 2nd to the 6th rib and from the sternal border to the midaxillary line, resting on the fascia of the pectoralis major (≈2/3) and serratus anterior (≈1/3), with an axillary tail.
fem|Mammary gland.territorio: Blood supply: medial perforating branches of the internal thoracic artery, lateral thoracic artery, pectoral branches of the thoracoacromial and branches of the posterior intercostals. Lymph: ~75% to axillary nodes, the rest to parasternal. Innervation: anterior and lateral cutaneous branches of intercostal nerves 2–6. Veins: internal thoracic, axillary and intercostal.
fem|Mammary gland.funcion: Production and secretion of milk; secondary sex characteristic.
fem|Mammary gland.clinica: Axillary lymphadenectomy can cause lymphedema of the upper limb and injure the long thoracic nerve (winged scapula), targets of physiotherapy after breast cancer.

fem|Hip bone.descripcion: Paired bone formed by the fusion of the ilium, ischium and pubis at the acetabulum (triradiate cartilage, ossified at about 15–17 years). In women it shows more flared iliac wings, a wider greater sciatic notch (≈90°), a subpubic angle of ≈80–90° (≈50–60° in men), smaller and more widely separated acetabula, and a more triangular obturator foramen.
fem|Hip bone.territorio: Blood supply: branches of the internal iliac artery (iliolumbar, gluteal, obturator), deep circumflex iliac and femoral circumflex arteries.
fem|Hip bone.funcion: Transmits the weight of the trunk to the lower limbs, provides muscle attachments and protects the pelvic viscera.
fem|Hip bone.clinica: Fractures of the pelvic ring can cause severe hemorrhage through injury to the presacral venous plexuses and to branches of the internal iliac artery.

fem|Ilium.descripcion: Superior and largest part of the hip bone, with a body (≈2/5 of the acetabulum) and an ala, iliac crest, iliac spines, iliac fossa and auricular surface. In women the ala is lower and more flared, the greater sciatic notch wider and the preauricular sulcus more frequent.
fem|Ilium.territorio: Blood supply: iliolumbar, deep circumflex iliac and superior gluteal arteries.
fem|Ilium.funcion: Attachment of the abdominal muscles, iliacus, gluteal muscles, tensor fasciae latae, sartorius (ASIS) and rectus femoris (AIIS); sacroiliac joint.
fem|Ilium.clinica: The line joining the iliac crests crosses the spinous process of L4, a landmark for lumbar puncture; the crest is a donor site for bone grafts.

fem|Ischium.descripcion: Posteroinferior part of the hip bone, with a body (≈2/5 of the acetabulum) and a ramus, ischial spine and ischial tuberosity. In women the spines are less prominent (interspinous diameter ≈10–11 cm) and the tuberosities are more widely separated and everted.
fem|Ischium.territorio: Blood supply: obturator, inferior gluteal and medial circumflex femoral arteries.
fem|Ischium.funcion: Weight bearing in sitting (tuberosity) and attachment of the hamstrings, adductor magnus and gemelli; the spine gives attachment to the sacrospinous ligament and the coccygeus muscle.
fem|Ischium.clinica: The ischial spine is a landmark for pudendal nerve block and for the station of the fetal presentation (plane 0); the tuberosity suffers avulsions from the hamstrings.

fem|Pubis.descripcion: Anteromedial part of the hip bone, with a body, superior ramus and inferior ramus; it articulates with its counterpart at the pubic symphysis and contributes ≈1/5 of the acetabulum. In women the body is longer and wider, the inferior rami more slender and everted, and the subpubic angle measures ≈80–90° (≈50–60° in men).
fem|Pubis.territorio: Blood supply: obturator artery and pubic branches of the inferior epigastric artery.
fem|Pubis.funcion: Attachment of the rectus abdominis, pyramidalis, adductors, gracilis and pectineus; closes the pelvic ring anteriorly.
fem|Pubis.clinica: In pregnancy relaxin increases laxity of the symphysis and can cause pubic symphysis dysfunction / pelvic girdle pain.

fem|Sacrum.descripcion: Triangular bone formed by the fusion of five sacral vertebrae, wedged between the hip bones; it has a promontory, sacral foramina, auricular surfaces and sacral hiatus. In women it is shorter, wider and less curved, with alae proportionally wider relative to the body of S1.
fem|Sacrum.territorio: Blood supply: lateral sacral and median sacral arteries. The rami of the sacral nerves S1–S5 exit through its foramina.
fem|Sacrum.funcion: Transmits the weight of the trunk to the pelvis through the sacroiliac joints and forms the posterior wall of the pelvis.
fem|Sacrum.clinica: Nutation and counternutation movements change the pelvic diameters during childbirth; the sacral hiatus gives access for caudal anesthesia.

fem|Coccyx.descripcion: Small bone formed by 3–5 (usually 4) fused coccygeal vertebrae, articulated with the apex of the sacrum. In women it is more mobile and less curved forward.
fem|Coccyx.territorio: Blood supply: median sacral artery and branches of the lateral sacral arteries. Innervation: coccygeal plexus.
fem|Coccyx.funcion: Attachment of the gluteus maximus, coccygeus, iliococcygeus (levator ani) and anococcygeal ligament; support of the pelvic floor.
fem|Coccyx.clinica: Its posterior displacement during childbirth enlarges the anteroposterior diameter of the pelvic outlet; coccydynia is more frequent in women.

fem|Female pelvis.descripcion: Bony ring formed by the two hip bones, the sacrum and the coccyx, joined by the pubic symphysis and the sacroiliac joints; the terminal line separates the greater (false) pelvis from the lesser (true) pelvis. Compared with the male pelvis it has a rounded or transversely oval pelvic inlet (gynecoid), a wider and shallower cavity, a subpubic angle of ≈80–90° (≈50–60° in men), less prominent ischial spines and more widely separated tuberosities.
fem|Female pelvis.territorio: Blood supply: internal and external iliac arteries; innervation of its contents by the lumbar, sacral and inferior hypogastric plexuses.
fem|Female pelvis.funcion: Transmits weight to the lower limb, protects the pelvic viscera, supports the pelvic floor and forms the bony birth canal.
fem|Female pelvis.clinica: Reference obstetric diameters: obstetric conjugate ≥10 cm, transverse diameter of the pelvic inlet ≈13 cm and interspinous diameter ≈10 cm; narrowing can cause dystocia.

fem|Labium majus.descripcion: Paired, rounded skin fold extending from the mons pubis to the perineum (about 7–12 cm, mean 9.3 cm; Lloyd et al., 2005). It contains adipose tissue, smooth muscle (dartos) and the termination of the round ligament of the uterus.
fem|Labium majus.destino: Posterior commissure, in front of the perineum
fem|Labium majus.territorio: External and internal pudendal arteries (labial branches); ilioinguinal, genitofemoral (genital branch) and pudendal (posterior labial) nerves; lymph to the superficial inguinal nodes.
fem|Labium majus.funcion: Protects the vestibule; homologue of the scrotum.
fem|Labium majus.clinica: Its cysts and abscesses usually arise from the Bartholin gland, located in its posterior and deep third.

fem|Labium minus.descripcion: Thin, fat-free mucocutaneous fold located medial to the labium majus that bounds the vestibule. Anteriorly it splits into the prepuce and frenulum of the clitoris; posteriorly it joins at the fourchette. Highly variable size (2–10 cm in length and 0.5–6 cm in width).
fem|Labium minus.origen: Prepuce and frenulum of the clitoris
fem|Labium minus.territorio: Labial arteries (from the internal pudendal); pudendal nerve; highly vascularized with abundant sensory nerve endings.
fem|Labium minus.funcion: Closes the vestibule and protects the urethral and vaginal orifices.
fem|Labium minus.clinica: The wide normal variability in size and shape should be recognized so as not to pathologize it (labiaplasty).

fem|Prepuce of clitoris.descripcion: Skin hood formed by the anterior union of the labia minora, covering the glans of the clitoris.
fem|Prepuce of clitoris.clinica: Adhesions of the prepuce can hide the glans on examination.

fem|Glans of clitoris.descripcion: Free, visible end of the body of the clitoris beneath the prepuce. Mean diameter about 5.5 mm (3–10 mm; Lloyd et al., 2005). It is the area with the highest density of nerve endings in the body.
fem|Glans of clitoris.territorio: Dorsal nerve of the clitoris (pudendal, S2–S4); dorsal artery of the clitoris (internal pudendal).
fem|Glans of clitoris.funcion: Sensory erectile organ of the sexual response.
fem|Glans of clitoris.clinica: The dorsal nerve must be preserved in vulvar surgery; female genital mutilation injures it.

fem|Body of clitoris.descripcion: Formed by the two fused corpora cavernosa, 2–4 cm long, which ascends from the glans and bends beneath the pubic symphysis, where it is fixed by the suspensory ligament; there it divides into the two crura.
fem|Body of clitoris.origen: Union of the crura beneath the pubic symphysis
fem|Body of clitoris.territorio: Deep and dorsal arteries of the clitoris (internal pudendal); dorsal nerve of the clitoris.
fem|Body of clitoris.funcion: Erectile tissue: becomes engorged during arousal.
fem|Body of clitoris.clinica: The whole clitoris measures 9–11 cm including crura and bulbs; the visible part is only a fraction.

fem|Crus of clitoris.descripcion: Posterior extension of each corpus cavernosum (5–9 cm) attached to the border of the ischiopubic ramus and covered by the ischiocavernosus muscle.
fem|Crus of clitoris.territorio: Deep artery of the clitoris (internal pudendal).
fem|Crus of clitoris.funcion: Root of the clitoris; erectile tissue.
fem|Crus of clitoris.clinica: Relevant in surgery of the perineal region and in trauma to the symphysis.

fem|Bulb of vestibule.descripcion: Paired mass of erectile tissue (about 3–4 cm) located on each side of the vaginal orifice, beneath the labia, covered by the bulbospongiosus muscle; anteriorly it joins the body of the clitoris.
fem|Bulb of vestibule.destino: Body and glans of clitoris (commissure of the bulbs)
fem|Bulb of vestibule.territorio: Artery of the bulb of the vestibule (internal pudendal); pudendal nerve.
fem|Bulb of vestibule.funcion: Homologue of the bulb of the penis; increases in volume during arousal.
fem|Bulb of vestibule.clinica: Its injury in childbirth or surgery can cause significant vulvar hematomas.

fem|Greater vestibular gland.descripcion: Paired pea-sized gland (~1 cm) located at the posterior end of the bulb of the vestibule, beneath the bulbospongiosus muscle; its duct (~2 cm) opens into the vestibule between the hymen and the labium minus, at the 5 and 7 o'clock positions.
fem|Greater vestibular gland.territorio: Internal pudendal artery (perineal branches); pudendal nerve.
fem|Greater vestibular gland.funcion: Secretes mucus that lubricates the vestibule; homologue of the bulbourethral gland.
fem|Greater vestibular gland.clinica: Obstruction of the duct produces a Bartholin cyst or abscess, which is common and painful.

fem|Vestibule of vagina.descripcion: Space between the labia minora into which the urethra, the vagina and the ducts of the greater and lesser vestibular glands open.
fem|Vestibule of vagina.funcion: Receives the urethral and vaginal orifices.
fem|Vestibule of vagina.clinica: Vestibulodynia (vestibular pain) is a frequent cause of dyspareunia.

fem|External urethral orifice.descripcion: Urethral opening in the vestibule, 2–3 cm behind the glans and in front of the vaginal orifice; the paraurethral glands (Skene's glands) open on both sides.
fem|External urethral orifice.clinica: Landmark for bladder catheterization in women.

fem|Vaginal orifice.descripcion: Opening of the vagina in the posterior part of the vestibule, surrounded by the hymen or its remnants (hymenal caruncles).
fem|Vaginal orifice.territorio: Pudendal nerve; vaginal and internal pudendal arteries.
fem|Vaginal orifice.funcion: Entrance to the vagina; birth canal.
fem|Vaginal orifice.clinica: Its posterior border (fourchette) and the perineal body tear in childbirth (perineal tears).

fem|Vaginal canal (lower part).descripcion: Lower third of the vagina, which crosses the urogenital diaphragm and opens into the vestibule; it is surrounded by the bulbospongiosus and puborectalis muscles.
fem|Vaginal canal (lower part).territorio: Internal pudendal artery; pudendal nerve (somatic sensation).
fem|Vaginal canal (lower part).funcion: Birth canal and canal of copulation.
fem|Vaginal canal (lower part).clinica: The lower third has somatic sensation (pudendal), unlike the upper thirds (autonomic).

fem|Female urethra.descripcion: Duct of about 4 cm that runs from the bladder neck to the vestibule, in front of the vagina, passing through the external urethral sphincter.
fem|Female urethra.territorio: Inferior vesical and internal pudendal arteries; pudendal nerve (external sphincter).
fem|Female urethra.funcion: Conveys urine; continence by the sphincters.
fem|Female urethra.clinica: Its short length explains the higher frequency of urinary tract infections in women.

fem|Ischiocavernosus muscle.descripcion: Paired muscle of the superficial perineal space that covers each crus of the clitoris.
fem|Ischiocavernosus muscle.destino: Crus of clitoris (inferior and medial surface)
fem|Ischiocavernosus muscle.funcion: Compresses the crus and maintains erection of the clitoris.

fem|Bulbospongiosus muscle.descripcion: Paired muscle that, in women, surrounds the vaginal orifice, covering the bulb of the vestibule and Bartholin's gland; unlike in men, its two halves are separated by the vagina.
fem|Bulbospongiosus muscle.destino: Body of clitoris and perineal membrane
fem|Bulbospongiosus muscle.funcion: Constricts the vaginal orifice, compresses the bulb and the vestibular gland, and assists erection of the clitoris.
fem|Bulbospongiosus muscle.clinica: It is injured in tears and in episiotomy; its repair is key to pelvic floor function.

fem|Superficial transverse perineal musc.descripcion: Thin muscular band of the superficial perineal space that crosses the perineum transversely.
fem|Superficial transverse perineal musc.origen: Inner surface of the ischial tuberosity
fem|Superficial transverse perineal musc.funcion: Fixes and stabilizes the perineal body.
fem|Superficial transverse perineal musc.clinica: Involved in the repair of second-degree perineal tears.

fem|Perineal body.es: Perineal body (central tendon of the perineum)
fem|Perineal body.descripcion: Fibromuscular node between the vaginal orifice and the anus where the bulbospongiosus, the transverse perineal muscles, the external anal sphincter and fibers of the levator ani converge. Perineal distance in women: about 3 cm (1.5–5.5 cm).
fem|Perineal body.funcion: Central support of the pelvic floor and of the posterior wall of the vagina.
fem|Perineal body.clinica: Its tearing in childbirth weakens the pelvic floor and favors prolapse; episiotomy cuts it in a controlled manner.

fem|Skin of breast.descripcion: Thin skin covering the mammary gland; centrally it presents the pigmented areola with the Montgomery tubercles and the nipple.
fem|Skin of breast.territorio: Cutaneous branches of the internal thoracic and lateral thoracic arteries; 4th–6th intercostal nerves; lymph mainly to the axillary nodes.
fem|Skin of breast.funcion: Protection and sensory function; the nipple-areola complex takes part in lactation.
fem|Skin of breast.clinica: Skin or nipple retraction and peau d'orange are warning signs of breast cancer.

mus|Tendinous intersection of rectus abd.origen: Anterior surface of the rectus abdominis
mus|Tendinous intersection of rectus abd.insercion: Adherent to the anterior layer of the rectus sheath
mus|Tendinous intersection of rectus abd.accion: Transverse fibrous bands (usually three: at the xiphoid, at the umbilicus and halfway between) that divide the rectus into bellies and adhere to the anterior layer of its sheath; they reinforce the muscle and form the abdominal “six-pack”.
mus|Tendinous intersection of rectus abd.clinica: Their adherence to the anterior sheath limits the spread of rectus sheath haematomas. They are visible landmarks on examination and on abdominal wall ultrasound.

mus|Tensor fasciae latae.origen: Anterior superior iliac spine and anterior part of the outer lip of the iliac crest
mus|Tensor fasciae latae.insercion: Iliotibial tract, which reaches Gerdy's tubercle of the tibia
mus|Tensor fasciae latae.irrigacion: Lateral circumflex femoral a. (ascending branch) and superior gluteal a.
mus|Tensor fasciae latae.accion: Hip flexion, abduction and medial rotation; tenses the iliotibial tract and stabilises the extended knee
mus|Tensor fasciae latae.clinica: Shortening of the muscle and the iliotibial tract is associated with iliotibial band friction syndrome in runners and cyclists (Ober test). It compensates for gluteus medius weakness.
mus|Tensor fasciae latae.prueba: Supine: hip flexion, abduction and medial rotation with the knee extended; resistance toward extension and adduction (Daniels).
mus|Tensor fasciae latae.biomecanica: Sagittal plane (flexion, frontal axis) and frontal plane (abduction, sagittal axis); medial rotation in the transverse plane (longitudinal axis).

rest|Tendinous arch of levator ani.descripcion: Linear thickening of the obturator internus fascia running from the posterior surface of the pubis to the ischial spine.
rest|Tendinous arch of levator ani.origen: Posterior surface of the body of the pubis
rest|Tendinous arch of levator ani.funcion: Origin of the iliococcygeus and pubococcygeus fibres of the levator ani; anchors the pelvic floor laterally.
rest|Tendinous arch of levator ani.clinica: Its detachment (levator avulsion) after vaginal birth favours prolapse; it is the anchor point of some pelvic floor repair techniques.
